name: abnormality of body height
abnormality of body height
HP:0000002.def: Deviation from the norm of height with respect to that which is expected according to age and gender norms.

name: multicystic kidney dysplasia
multicystic kidney dysplasia
HP:0000003.def: Multicystic dysplasia of the kidney is characterized by multiple cysts of varying size in the kidney and the absence of a normal pelvicaliceal system. The condition is associated with ureteral or ureteropelvic atresia, and the affected kidney is nonfunctional.

name: mode of inheritance
mode of inheritance
HP:0000005.def: The pattern in which a particular genetic trait or disorder is passed from one generation to the next.

name: autosomal dominant inheritance
autosomal dominant inheritance
HP:0000006.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on one of the autosomes (i.e., the human chromosomes 1-22) in which a trait manifests in heterozygotes. In the context of medical genetics, an autosomal dominant disorder is caused when a single copy of the mutant allele is present. Males and females are affected equally, and can both transmit the disorder with a risk of 50% for each child of inheriting the mutant allele.

name: autosomal recessive inheritance
autosomal recessive inheritance
HP:0000007.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on one of the autosomes (i.e., the human chromosomes 1-22) in which a trait manifests in individuals with two pathogenic alleles, either homozygotes (two copies of the same mutant allele) or compound heterozygotes (whereby each copy of a gene has a distinct mutant allele).

name: abnormal morphology of female internal genitalia
abnormal morphology of female internal genitalia
HP:0000008.def: An abnormality of the female internal genitalia.

name: recurrent urinary tract infections
recurrent urinary tract infection
HP:0000010.def: Repeated infections of the urinary tract.

name: neurogenic bladder
neurogenic bladder
HP:0000011.def: A type of bladder dysfunction caused by neurologic damage. Neurogenic bladder can be flaccid or spastic. Common manifestatios of neurogenic bladder are overflow incontinence, frequency, urgency, urge incontinence, and retention.
synonym: lack of bladder control due to nervous system injury
lack of bladder control due to nervous system injury

name: urinary urgency
urinary urgency
HP:0000012.def: Urge incontinence is the strong, sudden need to urinate.

name: abnormality of the bladder
abnormality of the bladder
HP:0000014.def: An abnormality of the urinary bladder.

name: bladder diverticulum
bladder diverticulum
HP:0000015.def: Diverticulum (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urinary bladder.

name: urinary retention
urinary retention
HP:0000016.def: Inability to completely empty the urinary bladder during the process of urination.
synonym: increased post - void residual urine volume
increase post - void residual urine volume

name: nocturia
nocturia
HP:0000017.def: Abnormally increased production of urine during the night leading to an unusually frequent need to urinate.

name: urinary hesitancy
urinary hesitancy
HP:0000019.def: Difficulty in beginning the process of urination.

name: urinary incontinence
urinary incontinence
HP:0000020.def: Loss of the ability to control the urinary bladder leading to involuntary urination.

name: abnormal male internal genitalia morphology
abnormal male internal genitalia morphology
HP:0000022.def: An abnormality of the male internal genitalia.

name: inguinal hernia
inguinal hernia
HP:0000023.def: Protrusion of the contents of the abdominal cavity through the inguinal canal.

name: prostatitis
prostatitis
HP:0000024.def: The presence of inflammation of the prostate.

name: functional abnormality of male internal genitalia
functional abnormality of male internal genitalia
male hypogonadism
male hypogonadism
HP:0000026.def: Decreased functionality of the male gonad, i.e., of the testis, with reduced spermatogenesis or testosterone synthesis.

name: azoospermia
azoospermia
HP:0000027.def: Absence of any measurable level of sperm,whereby spermatozoa cannot be observed even after centrifugation of the semen pellet.

name: cryptorchidism
cryptorchidism
HP:0000028.def: Testis in inguinal canal. That is, absence of one or both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

name: testicular atrophy
testicular atrophy
HP:0000029.def: Wasting (atrophy) of the testicle (the male gonad) manifested by a decrease in size and potentially by a loss of fertility.

name: testicular gonadoblastoma
testicular gonadoblastoma
HP:0000030.def: The presence of a gonadoblastoma of the testis.

name: epididymitis
epididymitis
HP:0000031.def: The presence of inflammation of the epididymis.

name: abnormality of male external genitalia
abnormality of male external genitalia
HP:0000032.def: An abnormality of male external genitalia.

name: ambiguous genitalia , male
ambiguous genitalia , male
HP:0000033.def: Ambiguous genitalia in an individual with XY genetic gender.

name: hydrocele testis
hydrocele testis
HP:0000034.def: Accumulation of clear fluid in the between the layers of membrane (tunica vaginalis) surrounding the testis.

name: abnormal testis morphology
abnormal testis morphology
HP:0000035.def: An anomaly of the testicle (the male gonad).

name: abnormal penis morphology
abnormal penis morphology
HP:0000036.def: Abnormality of the male external sex organ.

name: male pseudohermaphroditism
male pseudohermaphroditism
HP:0000037.def: Hermaphroditism refers to a discrepancy between the morphology of the gonads and that of the external genitalia. In male pseudohermaphroditism, the genotype is male (XY) and the external genitalia are imcompletely virilized, ambiguous, or complete female. If gonads are present, they are testes.

name: epispadias
epispadias
HP:0000039.def: Epispadias is a urogenital malformation characterized by the failure of the urethral tube to tubularize on the dorsal aspect. Unlike in hypospadias, where the meatus is on the ventral aspect, children with epispadias have a wide-open urethral plate on the dorsum. It is commonly seen as a component in the spectrum of bladder exstrophy-epispadias-complex. Isolated epispadias constitutes less than 10 percent of the total cases of epispadias.

name: long penis
long penis
HP:0000040.def: Penile length more than 2 SD above the mean for age.

name: chordee
chordee
HP:0000041.def: Ventral, lateral, or ventrolateral bowing of the shaft and glans penis of more than 30 degrees.

name: absent external genitalia
absent external genitalia
HP:0000042.def: Lack of external genitalia in a male or female individual.

name: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
HP:0000044.def: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism is characterized by reduced function of the gonads (testes in males or ovaries in females) and results from the absence of the gonadal stimulating pituitary hormones: follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

name: small scrotum
small scrotum
synonym: smaller than typical growth of scrotum
small than typical growth of scrotum

name: hypospadias
hypospadias
HP:0000047.def: Abnormal position of urethral meatus on the ventral penile shaft (underside) characterized by displacement of the urethral meatus from the tip of the glans penis to the ventral surface of the penis, scrotum, or perineum.

name: bifid scrotum
bifid scrotum
HP:0000048.def: Midline indentation or cleft of the scrotum.

name: shawl scrotum
shawl scrotum
HP:0000049.def: Superior margin of the scrotum superior to the base of the penis.

name: hypoplastic male external genitalia
hypoplastic male external genitalia
HP:0000050.def: Underdevelopment of part or all of the male external reproductive organs (which include the penis, the scrotum and the urethra).

name: perineal hypospadias
perineal hypospadias
HP:0000051.def: Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the perineal region.

name: urethral atresia , male
urethral atresia , male
HP:0000052.def: Congenital anomaly characterized by closure or failure to develop an opening in the urethra in males.

name: macroorchidism
macroorchidism
HP:0000053.def: The presence of abnormally large testes.

name: micropenis
micropenis
HP:0000054.def: Abnormally small penis. At birth, the normal penis is about 3 cm (stretched length from pubic tubercle to tip of penis) with micropenis less than 2.0-2.5 cm.

name: abnormality of female external genitalia
abnormality of female external genitalia
HP:0000055.def: An abnormality of the female external genitalia.

name: abnormal labia morphology
abnormal labium morphology
HP:0000058.def: An anomaly of the labia, the externally visible portions of the vulva.

name: ambiguous genitalia , female
ambiguous genitalia , female
HP:0000061.def: Ambiguous genitalia in an individual with XX genetic gender.

name: ambiguous genitalia
ambiguous genitalia
HP:0000062.def: A genital phenotype that is not clearly assignable to a single gender. Ambiguous genitalia can be evaluated using the Prader scale: Prader 0: Normal female external genitalia. Prader 1: Female external genitalia with clitoromegaly. Prader 2: Clitoromegaly with partial labial fusion forming a funnel-shaped urogenital sinus. Prader 3: Increased phallic enlargement. Complete labioscrotal fusion forming a urogenital sinus with a single opening. Prader 4: Complete scrotal fusion with urogenital opening at the base or on the shaft of the phallus. Prader 5: Normal male external genitalia. The diagnosis of ambiguous genitalia is made for Prader 1-4.

name: fused labia minora
fuse labium minora
HP:0000063.def: Fusion of the labia minora as a result of labial adhesions resulting in vaginal obstruction.

name: urethral atresia , female
urethral atresia , female
HP:0000067.def: Congenital anomaly characterized by closure or failure to develop an opening in the urethra in females.

name: urethral atresia
urethral atresia
HP:0000068.def: Congenital anomaly characterized by closure or failure to develop an opening in the urethra.

name: abnormality of the ureter
abnormality of the ureter
HP:0000069.def: An abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

name: ureterocele
ureterocele
HP:0000070.def: A ureterocele is a congenital saccular dilatation of the distal segment of the ureter.

name: ureteral stenosis
ureteral stenosis
HP:0000071.def: The presence of a stenotic, i.e., constricted ureter.

name: hydroureter
hydroureter
HP:0000072.def: The distention of the ureter with urine.

name: ureteral duplication
ureteral duplication
HP:0000073.def: A developmental anomaly characterized by the presence of two, instead of one, ureter connecting a kidney to the bladder.

name: ureteropelvic junction obstruction
ureteropelvic junction obstruction
HP:0000074.def: Blockage of urine flow from the renal pelvis to the proximal ureter.

name: renal duplication
renal duplication
HP:0000075.def: A congenital anomaly of the urinary tract, in which the kidney is duplicated and is drained via two separate renal pelves and ureters.

name: vesicoureteral reflux
vesicoureteral reflux
HP:0000076.def: Abnormal (retrograde) movement of urine from the bladder into ureters or kidneys related to inadequacy of the valvular mechanism at the ureterovesicular junction or other causes.

name: abnormality of the genital system
abnormality of the genital system
HP:0000078.def: An abnormality of the genital system.

name: abnormality of the urinary system
abnormality of the urinary system
HP:0000079.def: An abnormality of the urinary system.

name: abnormality of reproductive system physiology
abnormality of reproductive system physiology
HP:0000080.def: An abnormal functionality of the genital system.

name: duplicated collecting system
duplicate collecting system
HP:0000081.def: A duplication of the collecting system of the kidney, defined as a kidney with two (instead of, normally, one) pyelocaliceal systems. The pyelocaliceal system is comprised of the renal pelvis and calices. The duplicated renal collecting system can be associated with a single ureter or with double ureters. In the latter case, the two ureters empty separately into the bladder or fuse to form a single ureteral orifice.
synonym: double urinary collecting systems on intravenous pyelography
double urinary collect system on intravenous pyelography

name: renal insufficiency
renal insufficiency
HP:0000083.def: A reduction in the level of performance of the kidneys in areas of function comprising the concentration of urine, removal of wastes, the maintenance of electrolyte balance, homeostasis of blood pressure, and calcium metabolism.

name: horseshoe kidney
horseshoe kidney
HP:0000085.def: A connection of the right and left kidney by an isthmus of functioning renal parenchyma or fibrous tissue that crosses the midline.

name: ectopic kidney
ectopic kidney
HP:0000086.def: A developmental defect in which a kidney is located in an abnormal anatomic position.

name: nephronophthisis
nephronophthisis
HP:0000090.def: Presence of cysts at the corticomedullary junction of the kidney in combination with tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

name: abnormal renal tubule morphology
abnormal renal tubule morphology
HP:0000091.def: An abnormality of the renal tubules.
synonym: morphologic abnormality of the renal tubules
morphologic abnormality of the renal tubule

name: renal tubular atrophy
renal tubular atrophy
HP:0000092.def: The presence of renal tubules with thick redundant basement membranes, or a reduction of greater than 50% in tubular diameter compared to surrounding non-atrophic tubules.

name: proteinuria
proteinuria
HP:0000093.def: Increased levels of protein in the urine.

name: abnormal renal glomerulus morphology
abnormal renal glomerulus morphology
HP:0000095.def: A structural anomaly of the glomerulus.
synonym: morphologic abnormality of the renal glomerulus
morphologic abnormality of the renal glomerulus

name: glomerular sclerosis
glomerular sclerosis
HP:0000096.def: Accumulation of scar tissue within the glomerulus.

name: focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
HP:0000097.def: Segmental accumulation of scar tissue in individual (but not all) glomeruli.

name: tall stature
tall stature
HP:0000098.def: A height above that which is expected according to age and gender norms.

name: nephrotic syndrome
nephrotic syndrome
HP:0000100.def: Nephrotic syndrome is a collection of findings resulting from glomerular dysfunction with an increase in glomerular capillary wall permeability associated with pronounced proteinuria. Nephrotic syndrome refers to the constellation of clinical findings that result from severe renal loss of protein, with Proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia.

name: polyuria
polyuria
HP:0000103.def: An increased rate of urine production.

name: renal agenesis
renal agenesis
HP:0000104.def: Agenesis, that is, failure of the kidney to develop during embryogenesis and development.

name: enlarged kidney
enlarge kidney
HP:0000105.def: An abnormal increase in the size of the kidney.

name: renal cyst
renal cyst
HP:0000107.def: A fluid filled sac in the kidney.

name: renal corticomedullary cysts
renal corticomedullary cyst
HP:0000108.def: The presence of multiple cysts at the border between the renal cortex and medulla.

name: renal dysplasia
renal dysplasia
HP:0000110.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.

name: renal juxtaglomerular cell hypertrophy / hyperplasia
renal juxtaglomerular cell hypertrophy / hyperplasia
HP:0000111.def: Increased number and size of the juxtaglomerular cells.

name: nephropathy
nephropathy
HP:0000112.def: A nonspecific term referring to disease or damage of the kidneys.

name: polycystic kidney dysplasia
polycystic kidney dysplasia
HP:0000113.def: The presence of multiple cysts in both kidneys.

name: proximal tubulopathy
proximal tubulopathy
HP:0000114.def: Dysfunction of the proximal tubule, which is the portion of the duct system of the nephron of the kidney which leads from Bowman's capsule to the loop of Henle.

name: renal phosphate wasting
renal phosphate wasting
HP:0000117.def: High urine phosphate in the presence of hypophosphatemia.
synonym: decreased tubular maximum for phosphate reabsorption per glomerular filtration rate
decrease tubular maximum for phosphate reabsorption per glomerular filtration rate

name: abnormality of the genitourinary system
abnormality of the genitourinary system
HP:0000119.def: The presence of any abnormality of the genitourinary system.

name: nephrocalcinosis
nephrocalcinosis
HP:0000121.def: Nephrocalcinosis is the deposition of calcium salts in renal parenchyma.
synonym: too much calcium deposited in kidneys
too much calcium deposit in kidney

name: unilateral renal agenesis
unilateral renal agenesis
HP:0000122.def: A unilateral form of agenesis of the kidney.

name: nephritis
nephritis
HP:0000123.def: The presence of inflammation affecting the kidney.

name: renal tubular dysfunction
renal tubular dysfunction
HP:0000124.def: Abnormal function of the renal tubule. The basic functional unit of the kidney, the nephron, consists of a renal corpuscle attached to a renal tubule, with roughly 0.8 to 1.5 nephrons per adult kidney. The functions of the renal tubule include reabsorption of water, electrolytes, glucose, and amino acids and secretion of substances such as uric acid.
synonym: abnormal function of filtrating structures in kidney
abnormal function of filtrate structure in kidney

name: pelvic kidney
pelvic kidney
HP:0000125.def: A developmental defect in which a kidney is located in an abnormal anatomic position within the pelvis.

name: hydronephrosis
hydronephrosis
HP:0000126.def: Severe distention of the kidney with dilation of the renal pelvis and calices.

name: renal salt wasting
renal salt waste
HP:0000127.def: A high concentration of one or more electrolytes in the urine in the presence of low serum concentrations of the electrolyte(s).

name: renal potassium wasting
renal potassium wasting
HP:0000128.def: High urine potassium in the presence of hypokalemia.

name: uterine leiomyoma
uterine leiomyoma
HP:0000131.def: The presence of a leiomyoma of the uterus.

name: menorrhagia
menorrhagia
HP:0000132.def: Prolonged and excessive menses at regular intervals in excess of 80 mL or lasting longer than 7 days.

name: female hypogonadism
female hypogonadism
HP:0000134.def: Decreased functionality of the female gonads, i.e., of the ovary.

name: hypogonadism
hypogonadism
HP:0000135.def: A decreased functionality of the gonad.

name: bifid uterus
bifid uterus
HP:0000136.def: The presence of a bifid uterus.

name: ovarian cyst
ovarian cyst
HP:0000138.def: The presence of one or more cysts of the ovary.

name: uterine prolapse
uterine prolapse
HP:0000139.def: The presence of prolapse of the uterus.

name: abnormality of the menstrual cycle
abnormality of the menstrual cycle
HP:0000140.def: An abnormality of the ovulation cycle.

name: amenorrhea
amenorrhea
HP:0000141.def: Absence of menses for an interval of time equivalent to a total of more than (or equal to) 3 previous cycles or 6 months.

name: abnormal vagina morphology
abnormal vagina morphology
HP:0000142.def: Any structural abnormality of the vagina.

name: rectovaginal fistula
rectovaginal fistula
HP:0000143.def: The presence of a fistula between the vagina and the rectum.
synonym: abnormal connection between rectum and vagina
abnormal connection between rectum and vagina

name: vaginal atresia
vaginal atresia
HP:0000148.def: Congenital occlusion of the vagina or adhesion of the walls of the vagina causing occlusion.

name: ovarian gonadoblastoma
ovarian gonadoblastoma
HP:0000149.def: The presence of a gonadoblastoma of the ovary.

name: gonadoblastoma
gonadoblastoma
HP:0000150.def: The presence of a gonadoblastoma, a neoplasm of a gonad that consists of aggregates of germ cells and sex cord elements.

name: abnormality of head or neck
abnormality of head or neck
HP:0000152.def: An abnormality of head and neck.

name: wide mouth
wide mouth
HP:0000154.def: Distance between the oral commissures more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased width of the oral aperture (subjective).

name: oral ulcer
oral ulcer
HP:0000155.def: Erosion of the mucous mebrane of the mouth with local excavation of the surface, resulting from the sloughing of inflammatory necrotic tissue.

name: macroglossia
macroglossia
HP:0000158.def: Increased length and width of the tongue.

name: narrow mouth
narrow mouth
HP:0000160.def: Distance between the commissures of the mouth more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased width of the oral aperture (subjective).

name: median cleft lip
median cleft lip
HP:0000161.def: A type of cleft lip presenting as a midline (median) gap in the upper lip.

name: glossoptosis
glossoptosis
HP:0000162.def: Posterior displacement of the tongue into the pharynx, i.e., a tongue that is mislocalised posteriorly.

name: abnormal oral cavity morphology
abnormal oral cavity morphology
HP:0000163.def: Abnormality of the oral cavity, i.e., the opening or hollow part of the mouth.

name: abnormality of the gingiva
abnormality of the gingiva
HP:0000168.def: Any abnormality of the gingiva (also known as gums).

name: gingival fibromatosis
gingival fibromatosis
HP:0000169.def: The presence of fibrosis of the gingiva.

name: microglossia
microglossia
HP:0000171.def: Decreased length and width of the tongue.

name: abnormal uvula morphology
abnormal uvula morphology
HP:0000172.def: Abnormality of the uvula, the conic projection from the posterior edge of the middle of the soft palate.

name: abnormal palate morphology
abnormal palate morphology
HP:0000174.def: Any abnormality of the palate, i.e., of roof of the mouth.
synonym: abnormality of the roof of the mouth
abnormality of the roof of the mouth

name: cleft palate
cleft palate
HP:0000175.def: Cleft palate is a developmental defect of the palate resulting from a failure of fusion of the palatine processes and manifesting as a separation of the roof of the mouth (soft and hard palate).
synonym: cleft of hard and soft palate
cleft of hard and soft palate

name: submucous cleft hard palate
submucous cleft hard palate
HP:0000176.def: Hard-palate submucous clefts are characterized by bony defects in the midline of the bony palate that are covered by the mucous membrane of the roof of the mouth. It may be possible to detect a submucous cleft hard palate upon palpation as a notch in the bony palate.

name: abnormal upper lip morphology
abnormal upper lip morphology
HP:0000177.def: An abnormality of the upper lip.

name: abnormal lower lip morphology
abnormal low lip morphology
HP:0000178.def: An abnormality of the lower lip.

name: thick lower lip vermilion
thick low lip vermilion
HP:0000179.def: Increased thickness of the lower lip, leading to a prominent appearance of the lower lip. The height of the vermilion of the lower lip in the midline is more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased height of the vermilion of the lower lip in the frontal view (subjective).
synonym: increased height of lower lip vermilion
increase height of low lip vermilion
increased volume of lower lip vermilion
increased volume of low lip vermilion
thick red part of the lower lip
thick red part of the low lip
thick vermilion border of lower lip
thick vermilion border of low lip

name: lobulated tongue
lobulated tongue
HP:0000180.def: Multiple indentations and/or elevations on the edge and/or surface of the tongue producing an irregular surface contour.

name: cleft soft palate
cleft soft palate
HP:0000185.def: Cleft of the soft palate (also known as the velum, or muscular palate) as a result of a developmental defect occurring between the 7th and 12th week of pregnancy. Cleft soft palate can cause functional abnormalities of the Eustachian tube with resulting middle ear anomalies and hearing difficulties, as well as speech problems associated with hypernasal speech due to velopharyngeal insufficiency.

name: short upper lip
short upper lip
HP:0000188.def: Decreased width of the upper lip.
synonym: decreased vertical length of upper lip
decreased vertical length of upper lip

name: narrow palate
narrow palate
HP:0000189.def: Width of the palate more than 2 SD below the mean (objective) or apparently decreased palatal width (subjective).

name: abnormal oral frenulum morphology
abnormal oral frenulum morphology
HP:0000190.def: An abnormality of the lingual frenulum, that is of the small fold of mucous membrane that attaches the tongue to the floor of the mouth, or the presence of accessory frenula in the oral cavity.

name: accessory oral frenulum
accessory oral frenulum
HP:0000191.def: Extra fold of tissue extending from the alveolar ridge to the inner surface of the upper or lower lip.

name: bifid uvula
bifid uvula
HP:0000193.def: Uvula separated into two parts most easily seen at the tip.

name: open mouth
open mouth
HP:0000194.def: A facial appearance characterized by a permanently or nearly permanently opened mouth.

name: lower lip pit
low lip pit
HP:0000196.def: Depression located on the vermilion of the lower lip, usually paramedian.

name: abnormal parotid gland morphology
abnormal parotid gland morphology
HP:0000197.def: Any abnormality of the parotid glands, which are the salivary glands that are located in the subcutaneous tissues of the face overlying the mandibular ramus and anterior and inferior to the external ear.

name: absence of stensen duct
absence of stensen duct
synonym: failure of development of parotid duct
failure of development of parotid duct
failure of development of stensen duct
failure of development of stensen duct

name: short lingual frenulum
short lingual frenulum
HP:0000200.def: The presence of an abnormally short lingual frenulum.

name: pierre - robin sequence
pierre - robin sequence
HP:0000201.def: Pierre Robin malformation is a sequence of developmental malformations characterized by micrognathia (mandibular hypoplasia), glossoptosis and cleft palate.

name: orofacial cleft
orofacial cleft
HP:0000202.def: The presence of a cleft in the oral cavity, the two main types of which are cleft lip and cleft palate. In cleft lip, there is the congenital failure of the maxillary and median nasal processes to fuse, forming a groove or fissure in the lip. In cleft palate, there is a congenital failure of the palate to fuse properly, forming a grooved depression or fissure in the roof of the mouth. Clefts of the lip and palate can occur individually or together. It is preferable to code each defect separately.

name: cleft upper lip
cleft upper lip
HP:0000204.def: A gap in the upper lip. This is a congenital defect resulting from nonfusion of tissues of the lip during embryonal development.

name: pursed lips
purse lip
HP:0000205.def: An abnormality of the appearance of the face caused by constant contraction of the lips leading to a puckered or pursed appearance.

name: triangular mouth
triangular mouth
HP:0000207.def: The presence of a triangular form of the mouth.

name: trismus
trismus
HP:0000211.def: Limitation in the ability to open the mouth.

name: gingival overgrowth
gingival overgrowth
HP:0000212.def: Hyperplasia of the gingiva (that is, a thickening of the soft tissue overlying the alveolar ridge. The degree of thickening ranges from involvement of the interdental papillae alone to gingival overgrowth covering the entire tooth crown.

name: lip telangiectasia
lip telangiectasia
HP:0000214.def: Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the lips.

name: thick upper lip vermilion
thick upper lip vermilion
HP:0000215.def: Height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the midline more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the frontal view (subjective).
synonym: increased height of upper lip vermilion
increase height of upper lip vermilion
increased volume of upper lip vermilion
increased volume of upper lip vermilion
thick red part of the upper lip
thick red part of the upper lip
thick vermilion border of upper lip
thick vermilion border of upper lip

name: xerostomia
xerostomia
HP:0000217.def: Dryness of the mouth due to salivary gland dysfunction.

name: high palate
high palate
HP:0000218.def: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

name: thin upper lip vermilion
thin upper lip vermilion
HP:0000219.def: Height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the midline more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the frontal view (subjective).
synonym: decreased height of upper lip vermilion
decreased height of upper lip vermilion
decreased volume of upper lip vermilion
decreased volume of upper lip vermilion
thin red part of the upper lip
thin red part of the upper lip
thin vermilion border of upper lip
thin vermilion border of upper lip

name: velopharyngeal insufficiency
velopharyngeal insufficiency
HP:0000220.def: Inability of velopharyngeal sphincter to sufficiently separate the nasal cavity from the oral cavity during speech.

name: furrowed tongue
furrow tongue
HP:0000221.def: Accentuation of the grooves on the dorsal surface of the tongue.

name: hypogeusia
hypogeusia
HP:0000224.def: A decreased ability to perceive flavor.

name: tongue telangiectasia
tongue telangiectasia
HP:0000227.def: Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the tongue.

name: oral cavity telangiectasia
oral cavity telangiectasia
HP:0000228.def: Presence of telangiectases in the oral cavity.
synonym: spider veins of the oral cavity
spider vein of the oral cavity

name: everted lower lip vermilion
evert low lip vermilion
HP:0000232.def: An abnormal configuration of the lower lip such that it is turned outward i.e., everted, with the Inner aspect of the lower lip vermilion (normally opposing the teeth) being visible in a frontal view.

name: thin vermilion border
thin vermilion border
HP:0000233.def: Height of the vermilion of the medial part of the lip more than 2 SD below the mean, or apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the lip in the frontal view. The vermilion is the red part of the lips (and confusingly, the vermilion itself is also often referred to as being equivalent the lips).

name: abnormality of the fontanelles or cranial sutures
abnormality of the fontanelle or cranial suture
HP:0000235.def: Any abnormality of the fontanelles (the regions covered by a thick membrane that normally ossify in the first two years of life) or the cranial sutures (the fibrous joints in which the articulating bones or cartilages of the skull are connected by sutural ligaments).

name: abnormality of the anterior fontanelle
abnormality of the anterior fontanelle
HP:0000236.def: An abnormality of the anterior fontanelle, i.e., the cranial fontanelle that is located at the intersection of the coronal and sagittal sutures.
synonym: abnormality of the forehead soft spot
abnormality of the forehead soft spot

name: small anterior fontanelle
small anterior fontanelle
HP:0000237.def: Abnormally decreased size of the anterior fontanelle with respect to age-dependent norms.

name: hydrocephalus
hydrocephalus
HP:0000238.def: Hydrocephalus is an active distension of the ventricular system of the brain resulting from inadequate passage of CSF from its point of production within the cerebral ventricles to its point of absorption into the systemic circulation.
synonym: too much cerebrospinal fluid in the brain
too much cerebrospinal fluid in the brain

name: large fontanelles
large fontanelle
HP:0000239.def: In newborns, the two frontal bones, two parietal bones, and one occipital bone are joined by fibrous sutures, which form a small posterior fontanelle, and a larger, diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle. These regions allow for the skull to pass the birth canal and for later growth. The fontanelles gradually ossify, whereby the posterior fontanelle usually closes by eight weeks and the anterior fontanelle by the 9th to 16th month of age. Large fontanelles are diagnosed if the fontanelles are larger than age-dependent norms.

name: abnormality of skull size
abnormality of skull size
HP:0000240.def: Any abnormality of the size of the skull.

name: parietal bossing
parietal bossing
HP:0000242.def: Parietal bossing is a marked prominence in the parietal region.

name: trigonocephaly
trigonocephaly
HP:0000243.def: Wedge-shaped, or triangular head, with the apex of the triangle at the midline of the forehead and the base of the triangle at the occiput.

name: brachyturricephaly
brachyturricephaly
HP:0000244.def: Abnormal vertical height of the skull and a shortening of its anterior-posterior length, frequently combined with malformations of the occipital region.

name: abnormal paranasal sinus morphology
abnormal paranasal sinus morphology
HP:0000245.def: Abnormality of the paranasal (cranial) sinuses, which are air-filled spaces that are located within the bones of the skull and face and communicate with the nasal cavity. They comprise the maxillary sinuses, the frontal sinuses, the ethmoid sinuses, and the sphenoid sinuses.
synonym: abnormality of the sinuses of the head
abnormality of the sinus of the head

name: sinusitis
sinusitis
HP:0000246.def: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses owing to a viral, bacterial, or fungal infection, allergy, or an autoimmune reaction.

name: brachycephaly
brachycephaly
HP:0000248.def: An abnormality of skull shape characterized by a decreased anterior-posterior diameter. That is, a cephalic index greater than 81%. Alternatively, an apparently shortened anteroposterior dimension (length) of the head compared to width.

name: dense calvaria
dense calvaria
HP:0000250.def: An abnormal increase of density of the bones making up the calvaria.

name: microcephaly
microcephaly
HP:0000252.def: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender.

name: progressive microcephaly
progressive microcephaly
HP:0000253.def: Progressive microcephaly is diagnosed when the head circumference falls progressively behind age- and gender-dependent norms.

name: macrocephaly
macrocephaly
HP:0000256.def: Occipitofrontal (head) circumference greater than 97th centile compared to appropriate, age matched, sex-matched normal standards. Alternatively, a apparently increased size of the cranium.

name: wide anterior fontanel
wide anterior fontanel
HP:0000260.def: Enlargement of the anterior fontanelle with respect to age-dependent norms.
synonym: wider - than - typical soft spot of skull
wide - than - typical soft spot of skull

name: turricephaly
turricephaly
HP:0000262.def: Tall head relative to width and length.

name: oxycephaly
oxycephaly
HP:0000263.def: Oxycephaly (from Greek oxus, sharp, and kephalos, head) refers to a conical or pointed shape of the skull.

name: abnormal mastoid morphology
abnormal mastoid morphology
HP:0000264.def: An abnormality of the mastoid process, which is the conical prominence projecting from the undersurface of the mastoid portion of the temporal bone.
synonym: abnormality of mastoid process of temporal bone
abnormality of mastoid process of temporal bone

name: cranial asymmetry
cranial asymmetry
HP:0000267.def: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull.

name: dolichocephaly
dolichocephaly
HP:0000268.def: An abnormality of skull shape characterized by a increased anterior-posterior diameter, i.e., an increased antero-posterior dimension of the skull. Cephalic index less than 76%. Alternatively, an apparently increased antero-posterior length of the head compared to width. Often due to premature closure of the sagittal suture.

name: prominent occiput
prominent occiput
HP:0000269.def: Increased convexity of the occiput (posterior part of the skull).

name: delayed cranial suture closure
delay cranial suture closure
HP:0000270.def: Infants normally have two fontanels at birth, the diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle at the junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures, and the posterior fontanelle at the intersection of the occipital and parietal bones. The posterior fontanelle usually closes by the 8th week of life, and the anterior fontanel closes by the 18th month of life on average. This term applies if there is delay of closure of the fontanelles beyond the normal age.

name: malar flattening
malar flattening
HP:0000272.def: Underdevelopment of the malar prominence of the jugal bone (zygomatic bone in mammals), appreciated in profile, frontal view, and/or by palpation.

name: small face
small face
HP:0000274.def: A face that is short and narrow.

name: narrow face
narrow face
HP:0000275.def: Bizygomatic (upper face) and bigonial (lower face) width are both more than 2 standard deviations below the mean (objective); or, an apparent reduction in the width of the upper and lower face (subjective).

name: long face
long face
HP:0000276.def: Facial height (length) is more than 2 standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, an apparent increase in the height (length) of the face (subjective).

name: abnormal mandible morphology
abnormal mandible morphology
HP:0000277.def: Any abnormality of the mandible, the bone of the lower jaw.
synonym: abnormality of the lower jaw bone
abnormality of the low jaw bone
deformity of the lower jaw bone
deformity of the low jaw bone
malformation of the lower jaw bone
malformation of the low jaw bone

name: retrognathia
retrognathia
HP:0000278.def: An abnormality in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

name: coarse facial features
coarse facial feature
HP:0000280.def: Absence of fine and sharp appearance of brows, nose, lips, mouth, and chin, usually because of rounded and heavy features or thickened skin with or without thickening of subcutaneous and bony tissues.
synonym: thickened facial skin with coarse facial features
thicken facial skin with coarse facial feature

name: broad face
broad face
HP:0000283.def: Bizygomatic (upper face) and bigonial (lower face) width greater than 2 standard deviations above the mean (objective); or an apparent increase in the width of the face (subjective).

name: obsolete abnormality of the ocular region
obsolete abnormality of the ocular region
epicanthus
epicanthus
HP:0000286.def: A fold of skin starting above the medial aspect of the upper eyelid and arching downward to cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.

name: increased facial adipose tissue
increase facial adipose tissue
HP:0000287.def: An increased amount of subcutaneous fat tissue in the face.
synonym: increased amount of facial adipose tissue
increased amount of facial adipose tissue
increased volume of facial adipose tissue
increased volume of facial adipose tissue

name: broad philtrum
broad philtrum
HP:0000289.def: Distance between the philtral ridges, measured just above the vermilion border, more than 2 standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased distance between the ridges of the philtrum.

name: abnormality of the forehead
abnormality of the forehead
synonym: abnormality of the frontal region of the face
abnormality of the frontal region of the face

name: loss of facial adipose tissue
loss of facial adipose tissue
HP:0000292.def: Loss of normal subcutaneous fat tissue in the face.
synonym: decreased amount of facial adipose tissue
decreased amount of facial adipose tissue
decreased volume of facial adipose tissue
decreased volume of facial adipose tissue
loss of facial subcutaneous adipose tissue
loss of facial subcutaneous adipose tissue
loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face
loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face

name: full cheeks
full cheek
HP:0000293.def: Increased prominence or roundness of soft tissues between zygomata and mandible.

name: low anterior hairline
low anterior hairline
HP:0000294.def: Distance between the hairline (trichion) and the glabella (the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose), in the midline, more than two SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased distance between the hairline and the glabella.

name: doll - like facies
doll - like facies
HP:0000295.def: A characteristic facial appearance with a round facial form, full cheeks, a short nose, and a relatively small chin.

name: facial hypotonia
facial hypotonia
HP:0000297.def: Reduced muscle tone of a muscle that is innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

name: mask - like facies
mask - like facies
HP:0000298.def: A lack of facial expression often with staring eyes and a slightly open mouth.

name: oval face
oval face
HP:0000300.def: A face with a rounded and slightly elongated outline.

name: abnormality of facial musculature
abnormality of facial musculature
HP:0000301.def: An anomaly of a muscle that is innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

name: mandibular prognathia
mandibular prognathia
HP:0000303.def: Abnormal prominence of the chin related to increased length of the mandible.

name: abnormality of the chin
abnormality of the chin
HP:0000306.def: An abnormality of the chin, i.e., of the inferior portion of the face lying inferior to the lower lip and including the central prominence of the lower jaw.

name: pointed chin
point chin
HP:0000307.def: A marked tapering of the lower face to the chin.

name: microretrognathia
microretrognathia
HP:0000308.def: A form of developmental hypoplasia of the mandible in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

name: abnormal midface morphology
abnormal midface morphology
HP:0000309.def: An anomaly of the midface, which is a region and not an anatomical term. It extends, superiorly, from the inferior orbital margin to, inferiorly, the level of nasal base. It is formed by the maxilla (upper jaw) and zygoma and cheeks and malar region. Traditionally, the nose and premaxilla are not included in the midface.

name: round face
round face
HP:0000311.def: The facial appearance is more circular than usual as viewed from the front.

name: abnormality of the orbital region
abnormality of the orbital region
synonym: abnormality of the region around the eyes
abnormality of the region around the eye
anomaly of the orbital region of the face
anomaly of the orbital region of the face
deformity of the orbital region of the face
deformity of the orbital region of the face
malformation of the orbital region of the face
malformation of the orbital region of the face

name: hypertelorism
hypertelorism
HP:0000316.def: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

name: facial myokymia
facial myokymia
HP:0000317.def: Facial myokymia is a fine fibrillary activity of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

name: smooth philtrum
smooth philtrum
HP:0000319.def: Flat skin surface, with no ridge formation in the central region of the upper lip between the nasal base and upper vermilion border.

name: square face
square face
HP:0000321.def: Facial contours, as viewed from the front, show a broad upper face/cranium and lower face/mandible, creating a square appearance.

name: short philtrum
short philtrum
HP:0000322.def: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

name: facial asymmetry
facial asymmetry
HP:0000324.def: An abnormal difference between the left and right sides of the face.
synonym: asymmetry of right and left side of face
asymmetry of right and leave side of face

name: triangular face
triangular face
HP:0000325.def: Facial contour, as viewed from the front, triangular in shape, with breadth at the temples and tapering to a narrow chin.
synonym: face with broad temples and narrow chin
face with broad temple and narrow chin

name: abnormal maxilla morphology
abnormal maxilla morphology
HP:0000326.def: An abnormality of the Maxilla (upper jaw bone).
synonym: abnormality of the upper jaw bone
abnormality of the upper jaw bone
abnormality of the upper jaw bones
abnormality of the upper jaw bone
deformity of the upper jaw bones
deformity of the upper jaw bone
malformation of the upper jaw bones
malformation of the upper jaw bone

name: hypoplasia of the maxilla
hypoplasia of the maxilla
HP:0000327.def: Abnormally small dimension of the Maxilla. Usually creating a malocclusion or malalignment between the upper and lower teeth or resulting in a deficient amount of projection of the base of the nose and lower midface region.

name: facial hemangioma
facial hemangioma
HP:0000329.def: Hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, occurring in the face.

name: short chin
short chin
HP:0000331.def: Decreased vertical distance from the vermilion border of the lower lip to the inferior-most point of the chin.

name: prominent supraorbital ridges
prominent supraorbital ridge
HP:0000336.def: Greater than average forward and/or lateral protrusion of the supraorbital portion of the frontal bones.

name: broad forehead
broad forehead
HP:0000337.def: Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or apparently increased distance between the two sides of the forehead.

name: hypomimic face
hypomimic face
HP:0000338.def: A reduced degree of motion of the muscles beneath the skin of the face, often associated with reduced facial crease formation.

name: pugilistic facies
pugilistic facies
HP:0000339.def: Coarse facial features reminiscent of those of a boxer.

name: sloping forehead
slop forehead
HP:0000340.def: Inclination of the anterior surface of the forehead from the vertical more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or apparently excessive posterior sloping of the forehead in a lateral view.

name: narrow forehead
narrow forehead
HP:0000341.def: Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations below the mean (objective); or apparently narrow intertemporal region (subjective).

name: long philtrum
long philtrum
HP:0000343.def: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

name: whistling appearance
whistle appearance
HP:0000346.def: An abnormality of facial morphology characterized by a small mouth opening and constant contraction of the lips as if the patient were whistling.

name: high forehead
high forehead
HP:0000348.def: An abnormally increased height of the forehead.

name: widow 's peak
widow 's peak
HP:0000349.def: Frontal hairline with bilateral arcs to a low point in the midline of the forehead.
synonym: pointed hairline at front of head
point hairline at front of head

name: small forehead
small forehead
HP:0000350.def: The presence of a forehead that is abnormally small.
synonym: decreased size of frontal region of face
decreased size of frontal region of face

name: abnormality of the outer ear
abnormality of the outer ear
HP:0000356.def: An abnormality of the external ear.

name: posteriorly rotated ears
posteriorly rotate ear
HP:0000358.def: A type of abnormal location of the ears in which the position of the ears is characterized by posterior rotation (the superior part of the ears is rotated towards the back of the head, and the inferior part of the ears towards the front).
synonym: ears rotated toward back of head
ear rotate toward back of head

name: abnormality of the inner ear
abnormality of the inner ear
HP:0000359.def: An abnormality of the inner ear.

name: tinnitus
tinnitus
HP:0000360.def: Tinnitus is an auditory perception that can be described as the experience of sound, in the ear or in the head, in the absence of external acoustic stimulation.

name: otosclerosis
otosclerosis
HP:0000362.def: In otosclerosis, a callus of bone accumulates on the stapes creating a partial fixation. This limits the movement of the stapes bone, which results in hearing loss.

name: abnormal earlobe morphology
abnormal earlobe morphology
HP:0000363.def: An abnormality of the lobule of pinna.

name: hearing abnormality
hearing abnormality
HP:0000364.def: An abnormality of the sensory perception of sound.

name: hearing impairment
hearing impairment
HP:0000365.def: A decreased magnitude of the sensory perception of sound.

name: low - set , posteriorly rotated ears
low - set , posteriorly rotate ear
HP:0000368.def: Ears that are low-set and posteriorly rotated.

name: low - set ears
low - set ear
HP:0000369.def: Upper insertion of the ear to the scalp below an imaginary horizontal line drawn between the inner canthi of the eye and extending posteriorly to the ear.

name: abnormality of the middle ear
abnormality of the middle ear
HP:0000370.def: An abnormality of the middle ear.

name: acute otitis media
acute otitis medium
HP:0000371.def: Acute otitis media is a short and generally painful infection of the middle ear.

name: abnormality of the auditory canal
abnormality of the auditory canal
HP:0000372.def: An abnormality of the External acoustic tube (also known as the auditory canal).

name: incomplete partition of the cochlea type ii
incomplete partition of the cochlea type ii
HP:0000376.def: With incomplete partition II, the cochlea consists of 1.5 turns; the apical and middle cochlea turns are undifferentiated and form a cystic apex. The vestibule is normal while the vestibular aqueduct is always enlarged. Developmental arrest occurs at the seventh week of gestation.

name: abnormal pinna morphology
abnormal pinna morphology
HP:0000377.def: An abnormality of the pinna, which is also referred to as the auricle or external ear.

name: cupped ear
cup ear
HP:0000378.def: Laterally protruding ear that lacks antihelical folding (including absence of inferior and superior crura).

name: stapes ankylosis
stapes ankylosis
HP:0000381.def: Stapes ankylosis refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the stapes (the stirrup-shaped small bone or ossicle in the middle ear), which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism (the external auditory canal, tympanic membrane, and/or middle-ear ossicles).

name: abnormal periauricular region morphology
abnormal periauricular region morphology
synonym: abnormality of the region around the ear
abnormality of the region around the ear

name: preauricular skin tag
preauricular skin tag
HP:0000384.def: A rudimentary tag of skin often containing ear tissue including a core of cartilage and located just anterior to the auricle (outer part of the ear).
synonym: skin tag in front of the ear
skin tag in front of the ear
skin tag on the posterior cheek
skin tag on the posterior cheek

name: absent earlobe
absent earlobe
HP:0000387.def: Absence of fleshy non-cartilaginous tissue inferior to the tragus and incisura.

name: otitis media
otitis medium
HP:0000388.def: Inflammation or infection of the middle ear.

name: chronic otitis media
chronic otitis medium
HP:0000389.def: Chronic otitis media refers to fluid, swelling, or infection of the middle ear that does not heal and may cause permanent damage to the ear.
synonym: chronic infections of the middle ear
chronic infection of the middle ear

name: thickened helices
thicken helix
HP:0000391.def: Increased thickness of the helix of the ear.

name: lop ear
lop ear
HP:0000394.def: Anterior and inferior folding of the upper portion of the ear that obliterates triangular fossa and scapha.

name: prominent antihelix
prominent antihelix
HP:0000395.def: The presence of an abnormally prominent antihelix.

name: overfolded helix
overfolded helix
HP:0000396.def: A condition in which the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal. That is, excessive curling of the helix edge, whereby the free edge is parallel to the plane of the ear.

name: prelingual sensorineural hearing impairment
prelingual sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000399.def: A form of sensorineural deafness with either congenital onset or infantile onset, i.e., before the acquisition of speech.

name: macrotia
macrotia
HP:0000400.def: Median longitudinal ear length greater than two standard deviations above the mean and median ear width greater than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, apparent increase in length and width of the pinna (subjective).

name: stenosis of the external auditory canal
stenosis of the external auditory canal
HP:0000402.def: An abnormal narrowing of the external auditory canal.
synonym: narrowing of passageway from outer ear to middle ear
narrowing of passageway from out ear to middle ear

name: recurrent otitis media
recurrent otitis medium
HP:0000403.def: Increased susceptibility to otitis media, as manifested by recurrent episodes of otitis media.

name: conductive hearing impairment
conductive hearing impairment
HP:0000405.def: An abnormality of vibrational conductance of sound to the inner ear leading to impairment of sensory perception of sound.

name: sensorineural hearing impairment
sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000407.def: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

name: progressive sensorineural hearing impairment
progressive sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000408.def: A progressive form of sensorineural hearing impairment.

name: mixed hearing impairment
mixed hearing impairment
HP:0000410.def: A type of hearing loss resulting from a combination of conductive hearing impairment and sensorineural hearing impairment.

name: protruding ear
protrude ear
HP:0000411.def: Angle formed by the plane of the ear and the mastoid bone greater than the 97th centile for age (objective); or, outer edge of the helix more than 2 cm from the mastoid at the point of maximum distance (objective).

name: atresia of the external auditory canal
atresia of the external auditory canal
HP:0000413.def: Absence or failure to form of the external auditory canal.
synonym: atresia of the external auditory canals
atresia of the external auditory canal

name: bulbous nose
bulbous nose
HP:0000414.def: Increased volume and globular shape of the anteroinferior aspect of the nose.

name: abnormality of the choanae
abnormality of the choanae
HP:0000415.def: Abnormality of the choanae (the posterior nasal apertures).

name: narrow nasal ridge
narrow nasal ridge
HP:0000418.def: Decreased width of the nasal ridge.
synonym: decreased width of dorsum of nose
decrease width of dorsum of nose

name: abnormal nasal septum morphology
abnormal nasal septum morphology
HP:0000419.def: An abnormality of the nasal septum.

name: short nasal septum
short nasal septum
HP:0000420.def: Reduced superior to inferior length of the nasal septum.
synonym: decreased length of septum of nose
decreased length of septum of nose

name: epistaxis
epistaxis
HP:0000421.def: Epistaxis, or nosebleed, refers to a hemorrhage localized in the nose.

name: abnormal nasal bridge morphology
abnormal nasal bridge morphology
HP:0000422.def: Abnormality of the nasal bridge, which is the saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose. It lies between the glabella and the inferior boundary of the nasal bone, and extends laterally to the inner canthi.
synonym: abnormality of the bridge of the nose
abnormality of the bridge of the nose
deformity of the bridge of the nose
deformity of the bridge of the nose
malformation of the bridge of the nose
malformation of the bridge of the nose

name: prominent nasal bridge
prominent nasal bridge
HP:0000426.def: Anterior positioning of the nasal root in comparison to the usual positioning for age.

name: abnormal morphology of the nasal alae
abnormal morphology of the nasal ala
HP:0000429.def: An abnormality of the Ala of nose.
synonym: abnormality of the nasal alar cartilage
abnormality of the nasal alar cartilage
deformity of the nasal alar cartilage
deformity of the nasal alar cartilage
malformation of the nasal alar cartilage
malformation of the nasal alar cartilage

name: underdeveloped nasal alae
underdeveloped nasal ala
HP:0000430.def: Thinned, deficient, or excessively arched ala nasi.

name: wide nasal bridge
wide nasal bridge
HP:0000431.def: Increased breadth of the nasal bridge (and with it, the nasal root).
synonym: increased breadth of bridge of nose
increase breadth of bridge of nose
increased width of bridge of nose
increase width of bridge of nose

name: abnormal nasal mucosa morphology
abnormal nasal mucosa morphology
synonym: abnormality of mucous membrane of nose
abnormality of mucous membrane of nose

name: nasal mucosa telangiectasia
nasal mucosa telangiectasia
synonym: angioectasia of mucous membrane of nose
angioectasia of mucous membrane of nose
spider veins of mucosa of nose
spider vein of mucosa of nose
spider veins of mucous membrane of nose
spider vein of mucous membrane of nose
spider veins of nasal mucous membrane
spider vein of nasal mucous membrane
telangiectasia of mucous membrane of nose
telangiectasia of mucous membrane of nose

name: abnormal nasal tip morphology
abnormal nasal tip morphology
HP:0000436.def: An abnormality of the nasal tip.

name: depressed nasal tip
depress nasal tip
HP:0000437.def: Decreased distance from the nasal tip to the nasal base.

name: convex nasal ridge
convex nasal ridge
HP:0000444.def: Nasal ridge curving anteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip. The nose appears often also prominent, and the columella low.

name: wide nose
wide nose
HP:0000445.def: Interalar distance more than two standard deviations above the mean for age, i.e., an apparently increased width of the nasal base and alae.

name: narrow nasal bridge
narrow nasal bridge
HP:0000446.def: Decreased width of the bony bridge of the nose.

name: prominent nose
prominent nose
HP:0000448.def: Distance between subnasale and pronasale more than two standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased anterior protrusion of the nasal tip.

name: choanal stenosis
choanal stenosis
HP:0000452.def: Abnormal narrowing of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture).
synonym: narrowing of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
narrowing of the rear opening of the nasal cavity

name: choanal atresia
choanal atresia
HP:0000453.def: Absence or abnormal closure of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture). Most embryologists believe that posterior choanal atresia results from a failure of rupture between the 35th and 38th day of fetal life of the partition which separates the bucconasal or buccopharyngeal membranes. The resultant choanal atresia may be unilateral or bilateral, bony or membranous, complete or incomplete. In over 90 per cent of cases the obstruction is bony, while in the remainder it is membranous. The bony type of atresia is commonly located 1-2 mm. anterior to the posterior edge of the hard palate, and the osseous septum varies in thickness from 1 to 10 mm. In the membranous form of choanal atresia the obstruction usually occurs further posteriorly. In approximately one third of cases the atresia is bilateral.
synonym: blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity

name: broad nasal tip
broad nasal tip
HP:0000455.def: Increase in width of the nasal tip.
synonym: increased breadth of tip of nose
increase breadth of tip of nose
increased width of tip of nose
increase width of tip of nose

name: bifid nasal tip
bifid nasal tip
HP:0000456.def: A splitting of the nasal tip. Visually assessable vertical indentation, cleft, or depression of the nasal tip.

name: depressed nasal ridge
depress nasal ridge
HP:0000457.def: Lack of prominence of the nose resulting from a posteriorly-placed nasal ridge.

name: anosmia
anosmia
HP:0000458.def: An inability to perceive odors. This is a general term describing inability to smell arising in any part of the process of smelling from absorption of odorants into the nasal mucous overlying the olfactory epithelium, diffusion to the cilia, binding to olfactory receptor sites, generation of action potentials in olfactory neurons, and perception of a smell.

name: narrow nose
narrow nose
HP:0000460.def: Interalar distance more than 2 SD below the mean for age, or alternatively, an apparently decreased width of the nasal base and alae.

name: anteverted nares
anteverted naris
HP:0000463.def: Anteriorly-facing nostrils viewed with the head in the Frankfurt horizontal and the eyes of the observer level with the eyes of the subject. This gives the appearance of an upturned nose (upturned nasal tip).

name: webbed neck
web neck
HP:0000465.def: Pterygium colli is a congenital skin fold that runs along the sides of the neck down to the shoulders. It involves an ectopic fibrotic facial band superficial to the trapezius muscle. Excess hair-bearing skin is also present and extends down the cervical region well beyond the normal hairline.

name: neck muscle weakness
neck muscle weakness
HP:0000467.def: Decreased strength of the neck musculature.

name: increased adipose tissue around the neck
increase adipose tissue around the neck
HP:0000468.def: An increased amount of subcutaneous fat tissue around the neck.

name: gastrointestinal angiodysplasia
gastrointestinal angiodysplasia
HP:0000471.def: Dysplasia affecting the vasculature of the gastrointestinal tract.

name: long neck
long neck
HP:0000472.def: Increased inferior-superior length of the neck.

name: torticollis
torticollis
HP:0000473.def: Involuntary contractions of the neck musculature resulting in an abnormal posture of or abnormal movements of the head.

name: thickened nuchal skin fold
thicken nuchal skin fold
HP:0000474.def: A thickening of the skin thickness in the posterior aspect of the fetal neck. A nuchal fold (NF) measurement is obtained in a transverse section of the fetal head at the level of the cavum septum pellucidum and thalami, angled posteriorly to include the cerebellum. The measurement is taken from the outer edge of the occiput bone to the outer skin limit directly in the midline. An NF measurement greater than 5 mm at 14 to 17+6 weeks of gestation, or 6 mm at 18 to 28 weeks has been associated with a markedly increased risk for Down syndrome.

name: broad neck
broad neck
HP:0000475.def: Increased side-to-side width of the neck.

name: cystic hygroma
cystic hygroma
HP:0000476.def: A cystic lymphatic lesion of the neck.

name: abnormality of the eye
abnormality of the eye
HP:0000478.def: Any abnormality of the eye, including location, spacing, and intraocular abnormalities.

name: abnormal retinal morphology
abnormal retinal morphology
HP:0000479.def: A structural abnormality of the retina.

name: retinal coloboma
retinal coloboma
HP:0000480.def: A notch or cleft of the retina.
synonym: hole in the back of the eye
hole in the back of the eye

name: abnormal cornea morphology
abnormal cornea morphology
HP:0000481.def: Any abnormality of the cornea, which is the transparent tissue at the front of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

name: microcornea
microcornea
HP:0000482.def: A congenital abnormality of the cornea in which the cornea and the anterior segment of the eye are smaller than normal. The horizontal diameter of the cornea does not reach 10 mm even in adulthood.
synonym: cornea of eye less than 10mm in diameter
cornea of eye less than 10mm in diameter

name: astigmatism
astigmatism
HP:0000483.def: A type of astigmatism associated with abnormal curvatures on the anterior and/or posterior surface of the cornea.
synonym: abnormal curving of the cornea or lens of the eye
abnormal curving of the cornea or lens of the eye

name: hyperopic astigmatism
hyperopic astigmatism
HP:0000484.def: A form of astigmatism in which one meridian is hyperopic while the one at a right angle to it has no refractive error.

name: megalocornea
megalocornea
HP:0000485.def: An enlargement of the cornea with normal clarity and function. Megalocornea is diagnosed with a horizontal corneal diameter of 12 mm or more at birth or 13 mm or more after two years of age.

name: strabismus
strabismus
HP:0000486.def: A misalignment of the eyes so that the visual axes deviate from bifoveal fixation. The classification of strabismus may be based on a number of features including the relative position of the eyes, whether the deviation is latent or manifest, intermittent or constant, concomitant or otherwise and according to the age of onset and the relevance of any associated refractive error.

name: retinopathy
retinopathy
HP:0000488.def: Any noninflammatory disease of the retina. This nonspecific term is retained here because of its wide use in the literature, but if possible new annotations should indicate the precise type of retinal abnormality.

name: obsolete abnormality of globe location or size
obsolete abnormality of globe location or size
deeply set eye
deeply set eye
HP:0000490.def: An eye that is more deeply recessed into the plane of the face than is typical.

name: abnormal foveal morphology
abnormal foveal morphology
HP:0000493.def: An abnormality of the fovea centralis, the central area of the macula that mediates central, high resolution vision and contains the largest concentration of cone cells in the retina.

name: downslanted palpebral fissures
downslanted palpebral fissure
HP:0000494.def: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations below the mean.
synonym: downward slanting of the opening between the eyelids
downward slanting of the opening between the eyelid

name: recurrent corneal erosions
recurrent corneal erosion
HP:0000495.def: The presence of recurrent corneal epithelial erosions. Although most corneal epithelial defects heal quickly, some may show recurrent ulcerations.
synonym: recurrent breakdown of clear protective layer of eye
recurrent breakdown of clear protective layer of eye

name: abnormality of eye movement
abnormality of eye movement
HP:0000496.def: An abnormality in voluntary or involuntary eye movements or their control.
synonym: abnormal motility of the globe of the eye
abnormal motility of the globe of the eye
abnormal movement of the globe of the eye
abnormal movement of the globe of the eye

name: globe retraction and deviation on abduction
globe retraction and deviation on abduction
glaucoma
glaucoma
HP:0000501.def: Glaucoma refers loss of retinal ganglion cells in a characteristic pattern of optic neuropathy usually associated with increased intraocular pressure.

name: tortuosity of conjunctival vessels
tortuosity of conjunctival vessel
HP:0000503.def: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the conjunctival blood vessels.

name: visual impairment
visual impairment
HP:0000505.def: Visual impairment (or vision impairment) is vision loss (of a person) to such a degree as to qualify as an additional support need through a significant limitation of visual capability resulting from either disease, trauma, or congenital or degenerative conditions that cannot be corrected by conventional means, such as refractive correction, medication, or surgery.

name: telecanthus
telecanthus
HP:0000506.def: Distance between the inner canthi more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, apparently increased distance between the inner canthi.

name: ptosis
ptosis
HP:0000508.def: The upper eyelid margin is positioned 3 mm or more lower than usual and covers the superior portion of the iris (objective); or, the upper lid margin obscures at least part of the pupil (subjective).

name: rod - cone dystrophy
rod - cone dystrophy
HP:0000510.def: An inherited retinal disease subtype in which the rod photoreceptors appear to be more severely affected than the cone photoreceptors. Typical presentation is with nyctalopia (due to rod dysfunction) followed by loss of mid-peripheral field of vision, which gradually extends and leaves many patients with a small central island of vision due to the preservation of macular cones.

name: vertical supranuclear gaze palsy
vertical supranuclear gaze palsy
HP:0000511.def: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a vertical direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.

name: abnormal electroretinogram
abnormal electroretinogram
HP:0000512.def: Any abnormality of the electrical responses of various cell types in the retina as measured by electroretinography.

name: slow saccadic eye movements
slow saccadic eye movement
HP:0000514.def: An abnormally slow velocity of the saccadic eye movements.

name: cataract
cataract
HP:0000518.def: A cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the crystalline lens of the eye or in its capsule.
synonym: clouding of the lens of the eye
clouding of the lens of the eye

name: developmental cataract
developmental cataract
HP:0000519.def: A cataract that occurs congenitally as the result of a developmental defect, in contrast to the majority of cataracts that occur in adulthood as the result of degenerative changes of the lens.
synonym: clouding of the lens of the eye at birth
clouding of the lens of the eye at birth

name: proptosis
proptosis
HP:0000520.def: An eye that is protruding anterior to the plane of the face to a greater extent than is typical.
synonym: anterior bulging of the globe of eye
anterior bulging of the globe of eye

name: alacrima
alacrima
synonym: absence of tears in the eyes
absence of tear in the eye

name: subcapsular cataract
subcapsular cataract
HP:0000523.def: A cataract that affects the region of the lens directly beneath the capsule of the lens.

name: conjunctival telangiectasia
conjunctival telangiectasia
HP:0000524.def: The presence of small (ca. 0.5-1.0 mm) dilated blood vessels near the surface of the mucous membranes of the conjunctiva.
synonym: small dilated blood vessels near membrane covering front of eye and eyelids
small dilate blood vessel near membrane cover front of eye and eyelid

name: abnormality iris morphology
abnormality iris morphology
HP:0000525.def: An abnormality of the iris, which is the pigmented muscular tissue between the cornea and the lens, that is perforated by an opening called the pupil.

name: aniridia
aniridia
HP:0000526.def: Abnormality of the iris characterized by, typically bilateral, complete or partial iris hypoplasia. The phenotype ranges from mild defects of anterior iris stroma only to almost complete absence of the iris.

name: long eyelashes
long eyelash
HP:0000527.def: Mid upper eyelash length >10 mm or increased length of the eyelashes (subjective).

name: anophthalmia
anophthalmia
HP:0000528.def: Absence of the globe or eyeball.

name: progressive visual loss
progressive visual loss
HP:0000529.def: A reduction of previously attained ability to see.

name: abnormal chorioretinal morphology
abnormal chorioretinal morphology
HP:0000532.def: An abnormality of the choroid and retina.

name: chorioretinal atrophy
chorioretinal atrophy
HP:0000533.def: Atrophy of the choroid and retinal layers of the fundus.

name: epicanthus inversus
epicanthus inversus
HP:0000537.def: A fold of skin starting at or just below the medial aspect of the lower lid and arching upward to cover, extend in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.

name: pseudopapilledema
pseudopapilledema
HP:0000538.def: Apparent optic disc swelling in the absence of increased intracranial pressure.

name: abnormality of refraction
abnormality of refraction
HP:0000539.def: An abnormality in the process of focusing of light by the eye in order to produce a sharp image on the retina.

name: hypermetropia
hypermetropia
HP:0000540.def: An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects in the distance clearly, while objects nearby appear blurry.

name: retinal detachment
retinal detachment
HP:0000541.def: Separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium.

name: impaired ocular adduction
impaired ocular adduction
HP:0000542.def: Reduced ability to move the eye in the direction of the nose.

name: optic disc pallor
optic disc pallor
HP:0000543.def: A pale yellow discoloration of the optic disk (the area of the optic nerve head in the retina). The optic disc normally has a pinkish hue with a central yellowish depression.

name: external ophthalmoplegia
external ophthalmoplegia
HP:0000544.def: Paralysis of the external ocular muscles.
synonym: paralysis or weakness of muscles within or surrounding outer part of eye
paralysis or weakness of muscle within or surround out part of eye
progressive paralysis or weakness of muscles of eye motility
progressive paralysis or weakness of muscle of eye motility
progressive paralysis or weakness of muscles of eye movement
progressive paralysis or weakness of muscle of eye movement

name: myopia
myopia
HP:0000545.def: An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects nearby clearly, while objects in the distance appear blurry.

name: retinal degeneration
retinal degeneration
HP:0000546.def: A nonspecific term denoting degeneration of the retinal pigment epithelium and/or retinal photoreceptor cells.

name: abnormal conjugate eye movement
abnormal conjugate eye movement
HP:0000549.def: Any deviation from the normal motor coordination of the eyes that allows for bilateral fixation on a single object.

name: undetectable electroretinogram
undetectable electroretinogram
HP:0000550.def: Lack of any response to stimulation upon electroretinography.
synonym: no light - evoked response on electroretinogram
no light - evoked response on electroretinogram

name: color vision defect
color vision defect
HP:0000551.def: An anomaly in the ability to discriminate between or recognize colors.

name: tritanomaly
tritanomaly
HP:0000552.def: Difficulty distinguishing between yellow and blue, possible related to dysfunction of the S photopigment.

name: abnormal uvea morphology
abnormal uvea morphology
HP:0000553.def: An abnormality of the uvea, the vascular layer of the eyeball.

name: uveitis
uveitis
HP:0000554.def: Inflammation of one or all portions of the uveal tract.

name: leukocoria
leukocoria
HP:0000555.def: An abnormal white reflection from the pupil rather than the usual black reflection.

name: retinal dystrophy
retinal dystrophy
HP:0000556.def: Retinal dystrophy is an abnormality of the retina associated with a hereditary process. Retinal dystrophies are defined by their predominantly monogenic inheritance and they are frequently associated with loss or dysfunction of photoreceptor cells as a primary or secondary event.
synonym: breakdown of light - sensitive cells in back of eye
breakdown of light - sensitive cell in back of eye

name: buphthalmos
buphthalmos
HP:0000557.def: Diffusely large eye (with megalocornea) associated with glaucoma.

name: rieger anomaly
rieger anomaly
HP:0000558.def: A congenital malformation of the anterior segment characterized by iridicorneal malformation, glaucoma, iris stroma hypoplasia, posterior embryotoxon, and corneal opacities.

name: keratoconus
keratoconus
HP:0000563.def: A cone-shaped deformity of the cornea characterized by the presence of corneal distortion secondary to thinning of the apex.

name: lacrimal duct atresia
lacrimal duct atresia
HP:0000564.def: A developmental disorder of the lacrimal drainage system that most often affects the lacrimal ostium and resulting in non-opening of the nasolacrimal duct. It usually results from a non-canalization of the nasolacrimal duct.

name: esotropia
esotropia
HP:0000565.def: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes turned inward ('crossed') to a relatively severe degree, usually defined as 10 diopters or more.

name: chorioretinal coloboma
chorioretinal coloboma
HP:0000567.def: Absence of a region of the retina, retinal pigment epithelium, and choroid.
synonym: birth defect that causes a hole in the innermost layer at the back of the eye
birth defect that cause a hole in the innermost layer at the back of the eye

name: microphthalmia
microphthalmia
HP:0000568.def: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one or both eyes.
synonym: decreased size of globe of eye
decreased size of globe of eye

name: abnormal saccadic eye movements
abnormal saccadic eye movement
HP:0000570.def: An abnormality of eye movement characterized by impairment of fast (saccadic) eye movements.

name: hypometric saccades
hypometric saccade
HP:0000571.def: Saccadic undershoot, i.e., a saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

name: visual loss
visual loss
HP:0000572.def: Loss of visual acuity (implying that vision was better at a certain time point in life). Otherwise the term reduced visual acuity should be used (or a subclass of that).

name: thick eyebrow
thick eyebrow
HP:0000574.def: Increased density/number and/or increased diameter of eyebrow hairs.

name: scotoma
scotoma
HP:0000575.def: A regional and pathological increase of the light detection threshold in any region of the visual field surrounded by a field of normal or relatively well-preserved vision.

name: centrocecal scotoma
centrocecal scotoma
HP:0000576.def: A scotoma (area of diminished vision within the visual field) located between the central point of fixation and the blind spot with a roughly horizontal oval shape.

name: exotropia
exotropia
HP:0000577.def: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes deviated outward.

name: pigmentary retinopathy
pigmentary retinopathy
HP:0000580.def: An abnormality of the retina characterized by pigment deposition. It is typically associated with migration and proliferation of macrophages or retinal pigment epithelial cells into the retina; melanin from these cells causes the pigmentary changes. Pigmentary retinopathy is a common final pathway of many retinal conditions and is often associated with visual loss.

name: blepharophimosis
blepharophimosis
HP:0000581.def: A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures.

name: upslanted palpebral fissure
upslanted palpebral fissure
HP:0000582.def: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, the inclination of the palpebral fissure is greater than typical for age.
synonym: upward slanting of the opening between the eyelids
upward slanting of the opening between the eyelid

name: band keratopathy
band keratopathy
HP:0000585.def: An abnormality of the cornea characterized by the deposition of calcium in a band across the central cornea, leading to decreased vision, foreign body sensation, and ocular irritation.

name: shallow orbits
shallow orbit
HP:0000586.def: Reduced depth of the orbits associated with prominent-appearing ocular globes.

name: optic disc coloboma
optic disc coloboma
HP:0000588.def: A cleft of the optic nerve that extends inferiorly.

name: coloboma
coloboma
HP:0000589.def: A developmental defect characterized by a cleft of some portion of the eye or ocular adnexa.

name: progressive external ophthalmoplegia
progressive external ophthalmoplegia
