HP:0000590.def: Initial bilateral ptosis followed by limitation of eye movements in all directions and slowing of saccades.

name: abnormal sclera morphology
abnormal sclera morphology
synonym: abnormality of the outer white part of eyeball
abnormality of the outer white part of eyeball

name: blue sclerae
blue sclerae
HP:0000592.def: An abnormal bluish coloration of the sclera.
synonym: blue outer white part of eyeball
blue out white part of eyeball
whites of eyes are a bluish - gray color
white of eye be a bluish - gray color
whites of eyes are a bluish - gray colour
white of eye be a bluish - gray colour

name: abnormal anterior chamber morphology
abnormal anterior chamber morphology
HP:0000593.def: Abnormality of the anterior chamber, which is the space in the eye that is behind the cornea and in front of the iris.

name: shallow anterior chamber
shallow anterior chamber
HP:0000594.def: Reduced depth of the anterior chamber, i.e., the anteroposterior distance between the cornea and the iris is decreased.

name: ophthalmoparesis
ophthalmoparesis
HP:0000597.def: Ophthalmoplegia is a paralysis or weakness of one or more of the muscles that control eye movement.
synonym: weakness of muscles controlling eye movement
weakness of muscle control eye movement

name: abnormality of the frontal hairline
abnormality of the frontal hairline
HP:0000599.def: An anomaly in the placement or shape of the hairline (trichion) on the forehead, that is, the border between skin on the forehead that has head hair and that does not.
synonym: abnormality of hairline at front of head
abnormality of hairline at front of head

name: abnormality of the pharynx
abnormality of the pharynx
HP:0000600.def: An anomaly of the pharynx, i.e., of the tubular structure extending from the base of the skull superiorly to the esophageal inlet inferiorly.

name: hypotelorism
hypotelorism
HP:0000601.def: Interpupillary distance less than 2 SD below the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an decreased interpupillary distance or closely spaced eyes).

name: ophthalmoplegia
ophthalmoplegia
HP:0000602.def: Paralysis of one or more extraocular muscles that are responsible for eye movements.

name: central scotoma
central scotoma
HP:0000603.def: An area of depressed vision located at the point of fixation and that interferes with central vision.
synonym: blind spot located at fixation point
blind spot locate at fixation point

name: supranuclear gaze palsy
supranuclear gaze palsy
HP:0000605.def: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a particular direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.

name: abnormality of the periorbital region
abnormality of the periorbital region
HP:0000606.def: An abnormality of the region situated around the orbit of the eye.
synonym: abnormality of the region around the eye
abnormality of the region around the eye
abnormality of the region around the eye socket
abnormality of the region around the eye socket

name: macular degeneration
macular degeneration
HP:0000608.def: A nonspecific term denoting degeneration of the retinal pigment epithelium and/or retinal photoreceptor cells of the macula lutea.

name: abnormal choroid morphology
abnormal choroid morphology
HP:0000610.def: Any structural abnormality of the choroid.

name: photophobia
photophobia
HP:0000613.def: Excessive sensitivity to light with the sensation of discomfort or pain in the eyes due to exposure to bright light.
synonym: extreme sensitivity of the eyes to light
extreme sensitivity of the eye to light

name: abnormal nasolacrimal system morphology
abnormal nasolacrimal system morphology
HP:0000614.def: An abnormality of the nasolacrimal drainage system, which serves as a conduit for tear flow from the external eye to the nasal cavity.

name: abnormality of ocular smooth pursuit
abnormality of ocular smooth pursuit
HP:0000617.def: An abnormality of eye movement characterized by impaired smooth-pursuit eye movements.

name: blindness
blindness
HP:0000618.def: Blindness is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as visual perception below 3/60 and/or a visual field of no greater than 10 degrees in radius around central fixation.

name: impaired convergence
impaired convergence
HP:0000619.def: Reduced ability to turn the eyes inward in order to focus on a nearby object.

name: entropion
entropion
HP:0000621.def: An abnormal inversion (turning inward) of the eyelid (usually the lower) towards the globe. Entropion is usually acquired as a result of involutional or cicatricial processes but may occasionally be congenital.

name: blurred vision
blur vision
HP:0000622.def: Lack of sharpness of vision resulting in the inability to see fine detail.

name: supranuclear ophthalmoplegia
supranuclear ophthalmoplegia
HP:0000623.def: A vertical gaze palsy with inability to direct the gaze of the eyes downwards.

name: eyelid coloboma
eyelid coloboma
HP:0000625.def: A short discontinuity of the margin of the lower or upper eyelid.
synonym: full thickness defect of the eyelid
full thickness defect of the eyelid

name: posterior embryotoxon
posterior embryotoxon
HP:0000627.def: A posterior embryotoxon is the presence of a prominent and anteriorly displaced line of Schwalbe.

name: retinal arterial tortuosity
retinal arterial tortuosity
HP:0000631.def: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the retinal artery.

name: decreased lacrimation
decrease lacrimation
HP:0000633.def: Abnormally decreased lacrimation, that is, reduced ability to produce tears.

name: impaired ocular abduction
impaired ocular abduction
HP:0000634.def: An impaired ability of the eye to move in the outward direction (towards the side of the head).

name: blue irides
blue iris
HP:0000635.def: A markedly blue coloration of the iris.

name: upper eyelid coloboma
upper eyelid coloboma
HP:0000636.def: A short discontinuity of the margin of the upper eyelid.
synonym: full thickness defect of the upper eyelid
full thickness defect of the upper eyelid

name: long palpebral fissure
long palpebral fissure
HP:0000637.def: Distance between medial and lateral canthi is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, apparently increased length of the palpebral fissures.

name: nystagmus
nystagmus
HP:0000639.def: Rhythmic, involuntary oscillations of one or both eyes related to abnormality in fixation, conjugate gaze, or vestibular mechanisms.

name: gaze - evoked nystagmus
gaze - evoke nystagmus
HP:0000640.def: Nystagmus made apparent by looking to the right or to the left.

name: dysmetric saccades
dysmetric saccade
HP:0000641.def: The controller signal for saccadic eye movements has two components: the pulse that moves the eye rapidly from one point to the next, and the step that holds the eye in the new position. When both the pulse and the step are not the correct size, a dysmetric refixation eye movement results.

name: red - green dyschromatopsia
red - green dyschromatopsia
HP:0000642.def: Difficulty with discriminating red and green hues.

name: blepharospasm
blepharospasm
HP:0000643.def: A focal dystonia that affects the muscles of the eyelids and brow, associated with involuntary recurrent spasm of both eyelids.

name: amblyopia
amblyopia
HP:0000646.def: Reduced visual acuity that is uncorrectable by lenses in the absence of detectable anatomic defects in the eye or visual pathways.

name: sclerocornea
sclerocornea
HP:0000647.def: A congenital anomaly in which a part or the whole of the cornea acquires the characteristics of sclera, resulting in clouding of the cornea.
synonym: hardening of skin and connective tissue
hardening of skin and connective tissue

name: optic atrophy
optic atrophy
HP:0000648.def: Atrophy of the optic nerve. Optic atrophy results from the death of the retinal ganglion cell axons that comprise the optic nerve and manifesting as a pale optic nerve on fundoscopy.

name: abnormality of visual evoked potentials
abnormality of visual evoked potential
HP:0000649.def: An anomaly of visually evoked potentials (VEP), which are electrical potentials, initiated by brief visual stimuli, which are recorded from the scalp overlying the visual cortex.

name: abnormal amplitude of pattern reversal visual evoked potentials
abnormal amplitude of pattern reversal visual evoke potential
diplopia
diplopia
HP:0000651.def: Diplopia is a condition in which a single object is perceived as two images, it is also known as double vision.

name: lower eyelid coloboma
low eyelid coloboma
HP:0000652.def: A short discontinuity of the margin of the lower eyelid.
synonym: full thickness defect of the lower eyelid
full thickness defect of the low eyelid

name: decreased light - and dark - adapted electroretinogram amplitude
decrease light - and dark - adapted electroretinogram amplitude
HP:0000654.def: Descreased amplitude of eletrical response upon electroretinography.
synonym: decreased amplitudes on flash visual electroretinogram
decrease amplitude on flash visual electroretinogram

name: ectropion
ectropion
HP:0000656.def: An outward turning (eversion) or rotation of the eyelid margin.

name: oculomotor apraxia
oculomotor apraxia
HP:0000657.def: Ocular motor apraxia is a deficiency in voluntary, horizontal, lateral, fast eye movements (saccades) with retention of slow pursuit movements. The inability to follow objects visually is often compensated by head movements. There may be decreased smooth pursuit, and cancellation of the vestibulo-ocular reflex.
synonym: defective or absent horizontal voluntary eye movements
defective or absent horizontal voluntary eye movement

name: peters anomaly
peter anomaly
HP:0000659.def: A form of anterior segment dysgenesis in which abnormal cleavage of the anterior chamber occurs. Peters anomaly is characterized by central, paracentral, or complete corneal opacity.

name: lipemia retinalis
lipemia retinalis
HP:0000660.def: A creamy appearance of the retinal blood vessels that occurs when the concentration of lipids in the blood are extremely increased, with pale pink to milky white retinal vessels and altered pale reflexes from choroidal vasculature.

name: nyctalopia
nyctalopia
HP:0000662.def: Inability to see well at night or in poor light.

name: synophrys
synophrys
HP:0000664.def: Meeting of the medial eyebrows in the midline.

name: horizontal nystagmus
horizontal nystagmus
HP:0000666.def: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements.

name: phthisis bulbi
phthisis bulbi
HP:0000667.def: Atrophy of the eyeball with blindness and decreased intraocular pressure due to end-stage intraocular disease.

name: hypodontia
hypodontia
HP:0000668.def: The absence of five or less teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop.
synonym: failure of development of between one and six teeth
failure of development of between one and six teeth
missing between one and six teeth
miss between one and six teeth

name: carious teeth
carious teeth
HP:0000670.def: Caries is a multifactorial bacterial infection affecting the structure of the tooth. This term has been used to describe the presence of more than expected dental caries.

name: anodontia
anodontia
HP:0000674.def: The absence of all teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop.
synonym: failure of development of all teeth
failure of development of all teeth

name: macrodontia of permanent maxillary central incisor
macrodontia of permanent maxillary central incisor
HP:0000675.def: Increased size of the maxillary central secondary incisor tooth.
synonym: hyperplasia of permanent maxillary central incisor
hyperplasia of permanent maxillary central incisor
hypertrophy of permanent maxillary central incisor
hypertrophy of permanent maxillary central incisor
increased size of permanent maxillary central incisor
increase size of permanent maxillary central incisor
increased size of permanent upper central incisor
increase size of permanent upper central incisor
increased width of permanent maxillary central incisor
increase width of permanent maxillary central incisor
increased width of permanent upper central incisor
increase width of permanent upper central incisor

name: abnormality of the incisor
abnormality of the incisor
HP:0000676.def: An abnormality of the Incisor tooth.

name: oligodontia
oligodontia
HP:0000677.def: The absence of six or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop.
synonym: failure of development of more than six teeth
failure of development of more than six teeth
number of teeth decreased by more than six
number of teeth decrease by more than six

name: dental crowding
dental crowding
HP:0000678.def: Changes in alignment of teeth in the dental arch
synonym: inadequate arch length for tooth size
inadequate arch length for tooth size

name: taurodontia
taurodontia
HP:0000679.def: Increased volume of dental pulp of permanent molar characterized by a crown body-root ratio equal or larger than 1:1 or an elongated pulp chambers and apical displacement of the bifurcation or trifurcation of the roots.

name: delayed eruption of primary teeth
delay eruption of primary teeth
HP:0000680.def: Delayed tooth eruption affecting the primary dentition.

name: abnormal dental enamel morphology
abnormal dental enamel morphology
HP:0000682.def: An abnormality of the dental enamel.

name: grayish enamel
grayish enamel
HP:0000683.def: A grey discoloration of the dental enamel.

name: delayed eruption of teeth
delay eruption of teeth
HP:0000684.def: Delayed tooth eruption, which can be defined as tooth eruption more than 2 SD beyond the mean eruption age.

name: widely spaced teeth
widely space teeth
HP:0000687.def: Increased spaces (diastemata) between most of the teeth in the same dental arch.

name: dental malocclusion
dental malocclusion
HP:0000689.def: Dental malocclusion refers to an abnormality of the occlusion, or alignment, of the teeth and the way the upper and lower teeth fit together, resulting in overcrowding of teeth or in abnormal bite patterns.
synonym: incorrect relation between upper and lower dental arches
incorrect relation between upper and low dental arch
malalignment of upper and lower dental arches
malalignment of upper and low dental arch
misalignment of upper and lower dental arches
misalignment of upper and low dental arch

name: agenesis of maxillary lateral incisor
agenesis of maxillary lateral incisor
HP:0000690.def: Agenesis of one or more maxillary lateral incisor, comprising the maxillary lateral primary incisor and maxillary lateral secondary incisor.
synonym: failure of development of maxillary lateral incisor
failure of development of maxillary lateral incisor

name: microdontia
microdontia
HP:0000691.def: Decreased size of the teeth, which can be defined as a mesiodistal tooth diameter (width) more than 2 SD below mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased maximum width of tooth.

name: tooth malposition
tooth malposition
HP:0000692.def: Abnormal alignment, positioning, or spacing of the teeth, i.e., misaligned teeth.

name: odontodysplasia
odontodysplasia
HP:0000694.def: The diagnosis odontodysplasia requires clinical and radiological exams, in which unusually large pulp chambers and large pulp room chambers with thin enamel and dentin are visible. It may affect either a single tooth or several teeth. The term regional odontodysplasia is used if several teeth are affected. It affects the deciduous and permanent dentitions in the maxilla, the mandible or both, although the maxilla is more frequently involved. A type of dental dysplasia occurring in dentinogenesis imperfecta in which the pulp chambers are enlarged and there is a reduced amount of coronal dentin.
synonym: teeth with thin dentin and large pulp chambers
teeth with thin dentin and large pulp chamber
teeth with type iii dentinogenesis imperfecta
teeth with type iii dentinogenesis imperfecta

name: natal tooth
natal tooth
HP:0000695.def: A tooth present at birth or erupting within the first month of life.

name: delayed eruption of permanent teeth
delay eruption of permanent teeth
HP:0000696.def: Delayed tooth eruption affecting the secondary dentition.

name: conical tooth
conical tooth
HP:0000698.def: An abnormal conical form of the teeth, that is, a tooth whose sides converge or taper together incisally.

name: diastema
diastema
HP:0000699.def: Increased space between two adjacent teeth in the same dental arch.

name: periapical bone loss
periapical bone loss
HP:0000700.def: Radiolucency (reflecting a reduction in the bony substance) around the apex (the tip of the dental root).
synonym: dark spot around tooth root on x - ray
dark spot around tooth root on x - ray

name: amelogenesis imperfecta
amelogenesis imperfecta
HP:0000705.def: A developmental dysplasia of the dental enamel.

name: eruption failure
eruption failure
HP:0000706.def: A tooth which does not erupt within the teeth eruption timeline and after the loss of eruption potential.

name: abnormality of the nervous system
abnormality of the nervous system
HP:0000707.def: An abnormality of the nervous system.
synonym: brain and / or spinal cord issue
brain and / or spinal cord issue

name: atypical behavior
atypical behavior
HP:0000708.def: Atypical behavior is an abnormality in a person's actions, which can be controlled or modulated by the will of the individual. While abnormal behaviors can be difficult to control, they are distinct from other abnormal actions that cannot be affected by the individual's will.

name: psychosis
psychosis
HP:0000709.def: A condition characterized by changes in personality and thought patterns, often accompanied by hallucinations and delusional beliefs, is known as psychosis.

name: hyperorality
hyperorality
HP:0000710.def: Hyperorality is a condition characterized by an excessive preoccupation with oral sensations and behaviors, such as chewing, sucking, biting, swallowing, and excessive mouthing of objects.

name: restlessness
restlessness
HP:0000711.def: A state of unease is characterized by diffuse motor activity or motion, which is subject to limited control, nonproductive, or disorganized behavior.

name: emotional lability
emotional lability
HP:0000712.def: Unstable emotional experiences and frequent mood changes; emotions that are easily aroused, intense, and/or disproportionate to events and circumstances.

name: agitation
agitation
HP:0000713.def: A state of extreme restlessness and excessive motor activity is associated with mental distress or a feeling of inner tension.

name: depression
depression
HP:0000716.def: Frequently experiencing feelings of being down, miserable, and/or hopeless; struggling to recover from these moods; having a pessimistic outlook on the future; feeling a pervasive sense of shame; having a low self-worth; experiencing thoughts of suicide and engaging in suicidal behavior.

name: autism
autism
HP:0000717.def: Autism is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social interaction and communication, and by restricted and repetitive behavior. Autism begins in childhood. It is marked by the presence of markedly abnormal or impaired development in social interaction and communication and a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest. Manifestations of the disorder vary greatly depending on the developmental level and chronological age of the individual (DSM-IV).

name: aggressive behavior
aggressive behavior
HP:0000718.def: Behavior or an act aimed at harming a person, animal, or physical property (e.g., acts of physical violence; shouting, swearing, and using harsh language; slashing someone's tires).

name: inappropriate behavior
inappropriate behavior
HP:0000719.def: An explicit or perceived action, demonstration, conduct, or language (verbal and written) that is contrary to generally accepted norms, rules, procedures, or unacceptable within the context in which it is carried out. Inappropriate behaviors could take place in a sexual or social context and could be aggressive, violent, impulsive, intimidating, or threatening in nature.

name: compulsive behaviors
compulsive behavior
HP:0000722.def: Behavior that consists of repetitive acts, characterized by the feeling that one \"has to\

name: restrictive behavior
restrictive behavior
HP:0000723.def: Behavior characterized by an abnormal limitation to a few interests and activities.

name: psychotic episodes
psychotic episode
HP:0000725.def: Periods of time during which an individual experiences significant disturbances in their thoughts, perceptions, emotions, and behavior, resulting in a loss of touch with reality. These episodes are hallmark features of psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and certain forms of bipolar disorder.

name: dementia
dementia
HP:0000726.def: A loss of global cognitive ability of sufficient amount to interfere with normal social or occupational function. Dementia represents a loss of previously present cognitive abilities, generally in adults, and can affect memory, thinking, language, judgment, and behavior.

name: impaired ability to form peer relationships
impaired ability to form peer relationship
autistic behavior
autistic behavior
HP:0000729.def: Persistent deficits in social interaction and communication and interaction as well as a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest as well as repetitive patterns of behavior.

name: inflexible adherence to routines
inflexible adherence to routines
HP:0000732.def: A need to strictly adhere to repetitive routines or patterns of behavior which are created by the environment. One becomes upset or distressed when their routines are disrupted or altered.

name: abnormal repetitive mannerisms
abnormal repetitive mannerism
HP:0000733.def: Use of the same abnormal action in response to certain triggers or at random. They may be used as a way to regulate one's internal state but must otherwise have no apparent functional purpose.

name: disinhibition
disinhibition
HP:0000734.def: Reduced ability to control, or a failure to resist a temptation, urge, or impulse. Examples include disregard for social conventions, general impulsivity, and poor risk assessment.

name: impaired social interactions
impaired social interaction
HP:0000735.def: Difficulty interacting with others through emotional, physical, or verbal communication.

name: short attention span
short attention span
HP:0000736.def: Reduced attention span characterized by distractibility and impulsivity.

name: irritability
irritability
HP:0000737.def: A proneness to anger, i.e., a tendency to become easily bothered or annoyed.

name: hallucinations
hallucination
HP:0000738.def: Perceptions in a conscious and awake state that, in the absence of external stimuli, have qualities of real perception. These perceptions are vivid, substantial, and located in external objective space.

name: anxiety
anxiety
HP:0000739.def: Intense feelings of nervousness, tension, or panic often arise in response to interpersonal stresses. There is worry about the negative effects of past unpleasant experiences and future negative possibilities. Individuals may feel fearful, apprehensive, or threatened by uncertainty, and they may also have fears of falling apart or losing control.

name: episodic paroxysmal anxiety
episodic paroxysmal anxiety
HP:0000740.def: Recurrent attacks of severe anxiety, which occur without restriction to any particular situation or set of circumstances, are therefore unpredictable.

name: apathy
apathy
HP:0000741.def: Apathy is a quantitative reduction of motivation and the initiation and persistence of goal-directed behavior, where the accompanying emotions, thoughts, and social interactions are also suppressed.
synonym: lack of feeling , emotion , interest , motivation , initiation
lack of feeling , emotion , interest , motivation , initiation

name: self - mutilation
self - mutilation
HP:0000742.def: Deliberate harm to one's body resulting in tissue damage, without a conscious intent to die.

name: frontal release signs
frontal release sign
HP:0000743.def: Primitive reflexes traditionally held to be a sign of disorders that affect the frontal lobes.

name: low frustration tolerance
low frustration tolerance
HP:0000744.def: The feeling of frustration can be defined as an emotional reaction that occurs when a desired goal is not achieved. Frustration intolerance is defined as an age-inappropriate response to frustration, characterized by crying or temper tantrums in children, or aggressive or other undesirable behaviors.

name: diminished motivation
diminish motivation
HP:0000745.def: A reduction in goal-directed behavior, that is, motivation, is the determinant of behavior and adaptation that allows individuals to get started, be energized to perform a sustained and directed action.

name: delusion
delusion
HP:0000746.def: A delusion is a fixed false belief held despite evidence to the contrary. The term delusion broadly encompasses all false judgments that possess the following external characteristics to a significant, albeit unspecified, extent: (1) they are held with an exceptional level of conviction, accompanied by an unparalleled subjective certainty; (2) there is an inability to consider alternative experiences or compelling counter-arguments; (3) the content of the belief is impossible.

name: inappropriate laughter
inappropriate laughter
HP:0000748.def: Laughing that may be excessive and/or inappropriate in context (e.g., laughing at a funeral while others are crying).

name: delayed speech and language development
delay speech and language development
HP:0000750.def: A degree of language development that is significantly below the norm for a child of a specified age.

name: personality changes
personality change
HP:0000751.def: An abnormal shift in patterns of thinking, acting, or feeling.

name: hyperactivity
hyperactivity
HP:0000752.def: Hyperactivity is a condition characterized by constant and unusually high levels of activity, even in situations where it is deemed inappropriate.

name: agoraphobia
agoraphobia
HP:0000756.def: A type of anxiety disorder characterized by the avoidance of public places, especially where crowds gather.

name: lack of insight
lack of insight
HP:0000757.def: Lack of insight (Anosognosia) is a neurological condition in which an individual is unaware of his or her own neurological deficit or psychiatric condition. Anosognosia can be associated with mental illness, dementia, and structural brain lesions and can affect an indviduals's conscious awareness of deficits involving judgment, emotions, memory, executive function, language skills, and motor ability.

name: abnormal nonverbal communicative behavior
abnormal nonverbal communicative behavior
HP:0000758.def: Abnormalities in eye contact, communicative facial expressions, gesture use, or the use of others' bodies to communicate convey shared meanings within a culture that replace or supplement verbal communication.

name: abnormal peripheral nervous system morphology
abnormal peripheral nervous system morphology
HP:0000759.def: A structural abnormality of the peripheral nervous system, which is composed of the nerves that lead to or branch off from the central nervous system. This includes the cranial nerves (olfactory and optic nerves are technically part of the central nervous system).

name: decreased nerve conduction velocity
decrease nerve conduction velocity
HP:0000762.def: A reduction in the speed at which electrical signals propagate along the axon of a neuron.

name: sensory neuropathy
sensory neuropathy
HP:0000763.def: Peripheral neuropathy affecting the sensory nerves.
synonym: damage to nerves that sense feeling
damage to nerve that sense feel

name: abnormal thorax morphology
abnormal thorax morphology
HP:0000765.def: Any abnormality of the thorax (the region of the body formed by the sternum, the thoracic vertebrae and the ribs).
synonym: structural abnormality of the chest wall
structural abnormality of the chest wall

name: abnormal sternum morphology
abnormal sternum morphology
HP:0000766.def: An anomaly of the sternum, also known as the breastbone.

name: pectus excavatum
pectus excavatum
HP:0000767.def: A defect of the chest wall characterized by a depression of the sternum, giving the chest (\"pectus\") a caved-in (\"excavatum\") appearance.

name: pectus carinatum
pectus carinatum
HP:0000768.def: A deformity of the chest caused by overgrowth of the ribs and characterized by protrusion of the sternum.

name: gynecomastia
gynecomastia
HP:0000771.def: Abnormal development of large mammary glands in males resulting in breast enlargement.

name: narrow chest
narrow chest
HP:0000774.def: Reduced width of the chest from side to side, associated with a reduced distance from the sternal notch to the tip of the shoulder.

name: abnormality of the diaphragm
abnormality of the diaphragm
HP:0000775.def: Any abnormality of the diaphragm, the sheet of skeletal muscle that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity.

name: congenital diaphragmatic hernia
congenital diaphragmatic hernia
HP:0000776.def: The presence of a hernia of the diaphragm present at birth.

name: abnormal thymus morphology
abnormal thymus morphology
HP:0000777.def: Abnormality of the thymus, an organ located in the upper anterior portion of the chest cavity just behind the sternum and whose main function is to provide an environment for T lymphocyte maturation.

name: abnormal scapula morphology
abnormal scapula morphology
HP:0000782.def: Any abnormality of the scapula, also known as the shoulder blade.

name: nephrolithiasis
nephrolithiasis
HP:0000787.def: The presence of calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

name: hematuria
hematuria
HP:0000790.def: The presence of blood in the urine. Hematuria may be gross hematuria (visible to the naked eye) or microscopic hematuria (detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine).

name: uric acid nephrolithiasis
uric acid nephrolithiasis
HP:0000791.def: The presence of uric acid-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

name: membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
HP:0000793.def: A type of glomerulonephritis characterized by diffuse mesangial cell proliferation and the thickening of capillary walls due to subendothelial extension of the mesangium. The term membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis is often employed to denote a general pattern of glomerular injury seen in a variety of disease processes that share a common pathogenetic mechanism, rather than to describe a single disease entity

name: iga deposition in the glomerulus
iga deposition in the glomerulus
HP:0000794.def: The presence of immunoglobulin A deposits in the glomerulus.

name: abnormality of the urethra
abnormality of the urethra
HP:0000795.def: An abnormality of the urethra, i.e., of the tube which connects the urinary bladder to the outside of the body.

name: urethral obstruction
urethral obstruction
HP:0000796.def: Obstruction of the flow of urine through the urethra.

name: oligozoospermia
oligozoospermia
HP:0000798.def: Reduced count of spermatozoa in the semen, defined as a sperm count below 20 million per milliliter semen.

name: renal steatosis
renal steatosis
HP:0000799.def: Abnormal fat accumulation in the kidneys.

name: impotence
impotence
HP:0000802.def: Inability to develop or maintain an erection of the penis.

name: renal cortical cysts
renal cortical cyst
HP:0000803.def: Cysts of the cortex of the kidney.

name: xanthine nephrolithiasis
xanthine nephrolithiasis
HP:0000804.def: The presence of xanthine-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.

name: enuresis
enuresis
HP:0000805.def: Lack of the ability to control the urinary bladder leading to involuntary urination at an age where control of the bladder should already be possible.

name: penoscrotal hypospadias
penoscrotal hypospadias
HP:0000808.def: A severe form of hypospadias in which the urethral opening is located at the junction of the penis and scrotum.

name: urinary tract atresia
urinary tract atresia
HP:0000809.def: Congenital absence of the normal opening of a structure of the urinary tract.

name: abnormal internal genitalia
abnormal internal genitalia
HP:0000812.def: An anomaly of the adnexa, uterus, and vagina (in female) or seminal tract and prostate (in male).

name: bicornuate uterus
bicornuate uterus
HP:0000813.def: The presence of a bicornuate uterus.

name: hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
HP:0000815.def: Reduced function of the gonads (testes in males or ovaries in females) associated with excess pituitary gonadotropin secretion and resulting in delayed sexual development and growth delay.

name: abnormality of krebs cycle metabolism
abnormality of krebs cycle metabolism
HP:0000816.def: An abnormality of the tricarboxylic acid cycle.

name: reduced eye contact
reduce eye contact
HP:0000817.def: A reduced frequency or duration of eye contact.

name: abnormality of the endocrine system
abnormality of the endocrine system
HP:0000818.def: An abnormality of the endocrine system.

name: diabetes mellitus
diabetes mellitus
HP:0000819.def: A group of abnormalities characterized by hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance.

name: abnormality of the thyroid gland
abnormality of the thyroid gland
HP:0000820.def: An abnormality of the thyroid gland.

name: hypertension
hypertension
HP:0000822.def: The presence of chronic increased pressure in the systemic arterial system.

name: delayed puberty
delay puberty
HP:0000823.def: Passing the age when puberty normally occurs with no physical or hormonal signs of the onset of puberty.

name: decreased response to growth hormone stimulation test
decrease response to growth hormone stimulation test
HP:0000824.def: Insufficient responses to growth hormone (GH) provocation tests. GH deficiency is defined as a serum peak GH concentration less than 10 ng/mL on provocation with a combination of at least two separate stimulation tests.

name: hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia
hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia
HP:0000825.def: An increased concentration of insulin combined with a decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

name: precocious puberty
precocious puberty
HP:0000826.def: The onset of secondary sexual characteristics before a normal age. Although it is difficult to define normal age ranges because of the marked variation with which puberty begins in normal children, precocious puberty can be defined as the onset of puberty before the age of 8 years in girls or 9 years in boys.

name: abnormality of the parathyroid gland
abnormality of the parathyroid gland
HP:0000828.def: An abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

name: hypoparathyroidism
hypoparathyroidism
HP:0000829.def: A condition caused by a deficiency of parathyroid hormone characterized by hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia.

name: anterior hypopituitarism
anterior hypopituitarism
HP:0000830.def: A condition of reduced function of the anterior pituitary gland characterized by decreased secretion of one or more of the pituitary hormones growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotropic hormone, prolactin, luteinizing hormone, and follicle-stimulating hormone.

name: insulin - resistant diabetes mellitus
insulin - resistant diabetes mellitus
HP:0000831.def: A type of diabetes mellitus related not to lack of insulin but rather to lack of response to insulin on the part of the target tissues of insulin such as muscle, fat, and liver cells. This type of diabetes is typically associated with increases both in blood glucose concentrations as well as in fasting and postprandial serum insulin levels.

name: primary hypothyroidism
primary hypothyroidism
HP:0000832.def: A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in the thyroid gland.

name: abnormality of the adrenal glands
abnormality of the adrenal gland
HP:0000834.def: Abnormality of the adrenal glands, i.e., of the endocrine glands located at the top of the kindneys.

name: adrenal hypoplasia
adrenal hypoplasia
HP:0000835.def: Developmental hypoplasia of the adrenal glands.

name: hyperthyroidism
hyperthyroidism
HP:0000836.def: An abnormality of thyroid physiology characterized by excessive secretion of the thyroid hormones thyroxine (i.e., T4) and/or 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine zwitterion (i.e., triiodothyronine or T3).

name: increased circulating gonadotropin level
increase circulate gonadotropin level
HP:0000837.def: Overproduction of gonadotropins (FSH, LH) by the anterior pituitary gland.

name: pituitary dwarfism
pituitary dwarfism
HP:0000839.def: A type of reduced stature with normal proportions related to dysfunction of the pituitary gland related to either an isolated defect in the secretion of growth hormone or to panhypopituitarism, i.e., a deficit of all the anterior pituitary hormones.

name: adrenogenital syndrome
adrenogenital syndrome
HP:0000840.def: Adrenogenital syndrome is also known as congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which results from disorders of steroid hormone production in the adrenal glands leading to a deficiency of cortisol. The pituitary gland reacts by increased secretion of corticotropin, which in turn causes the adrenal glands to overproduce certain intermediary hormones which have testosterone-like effects.

name: hyperactive renin - angiotensin system
hyperactive renin - angiotensin system
HP:0000841.def: An abnormally increased activity of the renin-angiotensin system, causing hypertension by a combination of volume excess and vasoconstrictor mechanisms.

name: hyperinsulinemia
hyperinsulinemia
HP:0000842.def: An increased concentration of insulin in the blood.

name: hyperparathyroidism
hyperparathyroidism
HP:0000843.def: Excessive production of parathyroid hormone (PTH) by the parathyroid glands.

name: elevated circulating growth hormone concentration
elevate circulate growth hormone concentration
HP:0000845.def: Acromegaly is a condition resulting from overproduction of growth hormone by the pituitary gland in persons with closed epiphyses, and consists chiefly in the enlargement of the distal parts of the body. The circumference of the skull increases, the nose becomes broad, the tongue becomes enlarged, the facial features become coarsened, the mandible grows excessively, and the teeth become separated. The fingers and toes grow chiefly in thickness.

name: adrenal insufficiency
adrenal insufficiency
HP:0000846.def: Insufficient production of steroid hormones (primarily cortisol) by the adrenal glands.

name: abnormality of renin - angiotensin system
abnormality of renin - angiotensin system
HP:0000847.def: An abnormality of the renin-angiotensin system.
synonym: abnormality of the renin - aldosterone axis
abnormality of the renin - aldosterone axis

name: increased circulating renin level
increase circulate renin level
HP:0000848.def: An increased level of renin in the blood.

name: congenital hypothyroidism
congenital hypothyroidism
HP:0000851.def: A type of hypothyroidism with congenital onset.

name: pseudohypoparathyroidism
pseudohypoparathyroidism
HP:0000852.def: A condition characterized by resistance to the action of parathyroid hormone, in which there is hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and (appropriately) high levels of parathyroid hormone.

name: goiter
goiter
HP:0000853.def: An enlargement of the thyroid gland.

name: thyroid adenoma
thyroid adenoma
HP:0000854.def: The presence of a adenoma of the thyroid gland.

name: insulin resistance
insulin resistance
HP:0000855.def: Increased resistance towards insulin, that is, diminished effectiveness of insulin in reducing blood glucose levels.
synonym: body fails to respond to insulin
body fail to respond to insulin

name: irregular menstruation
irregular menstruation
HP:0000858.def: Abnormally high variation in the amount of time between periods.

name: hyperaldosteronism
hyperaldosteronism
HP:0000859.def: Overproduction of the mineralocorticoid aldosterone by the adrenal cortex.

name: parathyroid hypoplasia
parathyroid hypoplasia
HP:0000860.def: Developmental hypoplasia of the parathyroid gland.

name: central diabetes insipidus
central diabetes insipidus
HP:0000863.def: A form of diabetes insipidus related to a failure of vasopressin (AVP) release from the hypothalamus.

name: abnormality of the hypothalamus - pituitary axis
abnormality of the hypothalamus - pituitary axis
HP:0000864.def: Abnormality of the pituitary gland (also known as hypophysis), which is an endocrine gland that protrudes from the bottom of the hypothalamus at the base of the brain. The pituitary gland secretes the hormones ACTH, TSH, PRL, GH, endorphins, FSH, LH, oxytocin, and antidiuretic hormone. The secretion of hormones from the anterior pituitary is under the strict control of hypothalamic hormones, and the posterior pituitary is essentially an extension of the hypothalamus, so that hypothalamus and pituitary gland may be regarded as a functional unit.

name: secondary hyperparathyroidism
secondary hyperparathyroidism
HP:0000867.def: Secondary hyperparathyroidism refers to the production of higher than normal levels of parathyroid hormone in the presence of hypocalcemia.

name: increased circulating prolactin concentration
increase circulate prolactin concentration
HP:0000870.def: The presence of abnormally increased levels of prolactin in the blood. Prolactin is a peptide hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland that plays a role in breast development and lactation during pregnancy.

name: panhypopituitarism
panhypopituitarism
HP:0000871.def: A pituitary functional deficit affecting all the anterior pituitary hormones (growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, adrenocorticotropic hormone, and prolactin).

name: hashimoto thyroiditis
hashimoto thyroiditis
HP:0000872.def: A chronic, autoimmune type of thyroiditis associated with hypothyroidism.

name: diabetes insipidus
diabetes insipidus
HP:0000873.def: A state of excessive water intake and hypotonic (dilute) polyuria. Diabetes insipidus may be due to failure of vasopressin (AVP) release (central or neurogenic diabetes insipidus) or to a failure of the kidney to respond to AVP (nephrogenic diabetes insipidus).

name: oligomenorrhea
oligomenorrhea
HP:0000876.def: Infrequent menses (less than 6 per year or more than 35 days between cycles).

name: insulin - resistant diabetes mellitus at puberty
insulin - resistant diabetes mellitus at puberty
synonym: insulin - resistant diabetes mellitus at puberty
insulin - resistant diabetes mellitus at puberty

name: 11 pairs of ribs
11 pair of rib
HP:0000878.def: Presence of only 11 pairs of ribs.

name: short sternum
short sternum
HP:0000879.def: Decreased inferosuperior length of the sternum.

name: horizontal ribs
horizontal rib
HP:0000888.def: A horizontal (flat) conformation of the ribs, the long curved bones that form the rib cage and normally progressively oblique (slanted) from ribs 1 through 9, then less slanted through rib 12.

name: abnormal clavicle morphology
abnormal clavicle morphology
HP:0000889.def: Any abnormality of the clavicles (collar bones).

name: bifid ribs
bifid rib
HP:0000892.def: A bifid rib refers to cleavage of the sternal end of a rib, usually unilateral. Bifid ribs are usually asymptomatic, and are often discovered incidentally by chest x-ray.

name: bulging of the costochondral junction
bulging of the costochondral junction
HP:0000893.def: Abnormal outward curving (protuberance) of the junction of ribs and costal cartilage.

name: lateral clavicle hook
lateral clavicle hook
HP:0000895.def: An excessive upward convexity of the lateral clavicle.

name: rib exostoses
rib exostosis
HP:0000896.def: Multiple circumscribed bony excrescences located in the ribs.

name: rachitic rosary
rachitic rosary
HP:0000897.def: A row of beadlike prominences at the junction of a rib and its cartilage (i.e., enlarged costochondral joints), resembling a rosary.

name: rib fusion
rib fusion
HP:0000902.def: Complete or partial merging of adjacent ribs.

name: flaring of rib cage
flaring of rib cage
HP:0000904.def: The presence of wide, concave anterior rib ends.

name: progressive clavicular acroosteolysis
progressive clavicular acroosteolysis
HP:0000905.def: Progressive bone resorption in the distal part of the clavicle.

name: flat glenoid fossa
flat glenoid fossa
HP:0000911.def: Abnormally flat configuration of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.

name: sprengel anomaly
sprengel anomaly
HP:0000912.def: A congenital skeletal deformity characterized by the elevation of one scapula (thus, one scapula is located superior to the other).
synonym: congenital , upward displacement of the scapula
congenital , upward displacement of the scapula

name: posterior rib fusion
posterior rib fusion
HP:0000913.def: Complete or partial merging of the posterior part of adjacent ribs.

name: pectus excavatum of inferior sternum
pectus excavatum of inferior sternum
HP:0000915.def: Pectus excavatum (defect of the chest wall characterized by depression of the sternum) affecting primarily the inferior region of the sternum.

name: broad clavicles
broad clavicle
HP:0000916.def: Increased width (cross-sectional diameter) of the clavicles.

name: superior pectus carinatum
superior pectus carinatum
HP:0000917.def: Pectus carinatum affecting primarily the superior part of the sternum.

name: scapular exostoses
scapular exostosis
HP:0000918.def: The presence of multiple exostoses on the scapula. An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage.

name: abnormality of the costochondral junction
abnormality of the costochondral junction
HP:0000919.def: Any anomaly of the costochondral junction. The costochondral junctions are located between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.

name: enlargement of the costochondral junction
enlargement of the costochondral junction
HP:0000920.def: Abnormally increased size of the costochondral junctions, which are located between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.

name: missing ribs
miss rib
HP:0000921.def: A developmental anomaly with absence of one or more ribs.

name: beaded ribs
bead rib
HP:0000923.def: The presence of a row of multiple rounded expansions (beadlike prominences) at the junction of a rib and its cartilage.

name: abnormality of the skeletal system
abnormality of the skeletal system
HP:0000924.def: An abnormality of the skeletal system.

name: abnormality of the vertebral column
abnormality of the vertebral column
HP:0000925.def: Any abnormality of the vertebral column.

name: platyspondyly
platyspondyly
HP:0000926.def: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates.

name: abnormality of skeletal maturation
abnormality of skeletal maturation
HP:0000927.def: The bones of the skeleton undergo a series of characteristic changes in size, shape, and calcification from fetal life until puberty. An abnormality of this process can include delayed or accelerated skeletal maturation, or deviation of some, but not all bones from the expected patterns of maturation.

name: abnormal skull morphology
abnormal skull morphology
HP:0000929.def: An abnormality of the skull, the bony framework of the head which is comprised of the neurocranium (with eight cranial bones) and the viscerocranium (facial skeleton) that comprises fourteen facial bones with the mandible as its largest bone.

name: elevated imprint of the transverse sinuses
elevate imprint of the transverse sinus
synonym: elevated imprint of occipital bone over the transverse sinuses
elevate imprint of occipital bone over the transverse sinus
elevated imprint of posterior skull bones over the transverse sinuses
elevate imprint of posterior skull bone over the transverse sinus
thinning and bulging of occipital bone over the transverse sinuses
thinning and bulging of occipital bone over the transverse sinus
thinning and bulging of posterior skull bones over the transverse sinuses
thinning and bulging of posterior skull bone over the transverse sinus

name: thinning and bulging of the posterior fossa bones
thinning and bulging of the posterior fossa bone
synonym: thinning and bulging of occipital bone of skull
thinning and bulging of occipital bone of skull
thinning and bulging of posterior fossa bones
thinning and bulging of posterior fossa bone
thinning and bulging of posterior skull bones
thinning and bulging of posterior skull bone

name: abnormal posterior cranial fossa morphology
abnormal posterior cranial fossa morphology
HP:0000932.def: An abnormality of the fossa cranii posterior (the posterior fossa), which is made up primarily of the occipital bone and which surrounds to the foramen magnum.
synonym: abnormality of the posterior cranial fossa
abnormality of the posterior cranial fossa

name: posterior fossa cyst at the fourth ventricle
posterior fossa cyst at the fourth ventricle
chondrocalcinosis
chondrocalcinosis
HP:0000934.def: Radiographic evidence of articular calcification that represent calcium pyrophosphate depositions in soft tissue surrounding joints and at the insertions of tendons near joints (Entheses/Sharpey fibers) .

name: thickened cortex of long bones
thicken cortex of long bone
HP:0000935.def: Abnormal thickening of the cortex of long bones.
synonym: cortical thickening of the long bones
cortical thickening of the long bone

name: osteopenia
osteopenia
HP:0000938.def: Osteopenia is a term to define bone density that is not normal but also not as low as osteoporosis. By definition from the World Health Organization osteopenia is defined by bone densitometry as a T score -1 to -2.5.

name: osteoporosis
osteoporosis
HP:0000939.def: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease characterized by low bone density and microarchitectural deterioration of bone tissue with a consequent increase in bone fragility. According to the WHO criteria, osteoporosis is defined as a BMD that lies 2.5 standard deviations or more below the average value for young healthy adults (a T-score below -2.5 SD).

name: abnormal diaphysis morphology
abnormal diaphysis morphology
HP:0000940.def: An abnormality of the structure or form of the diaphysis, i.e., of the main or mid-section (shaft) of a long bone.
synonym: abnormal shape of shaft of long bone
abnormal shape of shaft of long bone
abnormality involving the diaphyses of the limbs
abnormality involve the diaphysis of the limb
abnormality of shaft of long bone of the limbs
abnormality of shaft of long bone of the limb
anomaly of the limb diaphyses morphology
anomaly of the limb diaphyses morphology

name: abnormal metaphysis morphology
abnormal metaphysis morphology
HP:0000944.def: An abnormality of one or more metaphysis, i.e., of the somewhat wider portion of a long bone that is adjacent to the epiphyseal growth plate and grows during childhood.
synonym: abnormality of the wide portion of a long bone
abnormality of the wide portion of a long bone

name: hypoplastic ilia
hypoplastic ilium
synonym: small wings of the pelvic girdle
small wing of the pelvic girdle

name: dumbbell - shaped long bone
dumbbell - shape long bone
HP:0000947.def: An abnormal appearance of the long bones with resemblance to a dumbbell, a short bar with a weight at each end. That is, the long bone is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.
synonym: dumbbell widening of long bone metaphyses
dumbbell widening of long bone metaphyses

name: jaundice
jaundice
HP:0000952.def: Yellow pigmentation of the skin due to bilirubin, which in turn is the result of increased bilirubin concentration in the bloodstream.

name: hyperpigmentation of the skin
hyperpigmentation of the skin
HP:0000953.def: A darkening of the skin related to an increase in melanin production and deposition.

name: single transverse palmar crease
single transverse palmar crease
HP:0000954.def: The distal and proximal transverse palmar creases are merged into a single transverse palmar crease.

name: acanthosis nigricans
acanthosis nigricans
HP:0000956.def: A dermatosis characterized by thickened, hyperpigmented plaques, typically on the intertriginous surfaces and neck.

name: cafe - au - lait spot
cafe - au - lait spot
HP:0000957.def: Cafe-au-lait spots are hyperpigmented lesions that can vary in color from light brown to dark brown with smooth borders and having a size of 1.5 cm or more in adults and 0.5 cm or more in children.
synonym: flat light - brown mark on skin
flat light - brown mark on skin

name: dry skin
dry skin
HP:0000958.def: Skin characterized by the lack of natural or normal moisture.

name: sacral dimple
sacral dimple
HP:0000960.def: A cutaneous indentation resulting from tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) of the intergluteal cleft.

name: cyanosis
cyanosis
HP:0000961.def: Bluish discoloration of the skin and mucosa due to poor circulation or inadequate oxygenation of arterial or capillary blood.

name: hyperkeratosis
hyperkeratosis
HP:0000962.def: Hyperkeratosis is thickening of the outer layer of the skin, the stratum corneum, which is composed of large, polyhedral, plate-like envelopes filled with keratin which are the dead cells that have migrated up from the stratum granulosum.

name: thin skin
thin skin
HP:0000963.def: Reduction in thickness of the skin, generally associated with a loss of suppleness and elasticity of the skin.

name: eczema
eczema
HP:0000964.def: Eczema is a form of dermatitis. The term eczema is broadly applied to a range of persistent skin conditions and can be related to a number of underlying conditions. Manifestations of eczema can include dryness and recurring skin rashes with redness, skin edema, itching and dryness, crusting, flaking, blistering, cracking, oozing, or bleeding.

name: cutis marmorata
cutis marmorata
HP:0000965.def: A reticular discoloration of the skin with cyanotic (reddish-blue appearing) areas surrounding pale central areas due to dilation of capillary blood vessels and stagnation of blood within the vessels. Cutis marmorata generally occurs on the legs, arms and trunk and is often more severe in cold weather.

name: petechiae
petechia
HP:0000967.def: Petechiae are pinpoint-sized reddish/purple spots, resembling a rash, that appear just under the skin or a mucous membrane when capillaries have ruptured and some superficial bleeding into the skin has happened. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to developing petechiae.

name: ectodermal dysplasia
ectodermal dysplasia
HP:0000968.def: Ectodermal dysplasia is a group of conditions in which there is abnormal development of the skin, hair, nails, teeth, or sweat glands.

name: edema
edema
HP:0000969.def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.

name: abnormal sweat gland morphology
abnormal sweat gland morphology
HP:0000971.def: Any structural abnormality of the sweat gland.

name: palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
HP:0000972.def: Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.
synonym: hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles
hyperkeratosis of the palm and sol
thickening of the outer layer of the skin of the palms and soles
thickening of the outer layer of the skin of the palm and sol

name: cutis laxa
cutis laxa
HP:0000973.def: Wrinkled, redundant, inelastic and sagging skin.

name: hyperextensible skin
hyperextensible skin
HP:0000974.def: A condition in which the skin can be stretched beyond normal, and then returns to its initial position.

name: hyperhidrosis
hyperhidrosis
HP:0000975.def: Abnormal excessive perspiration (sweating) despite the lack of appropriate stimuli like hot and humid weather.

name: soft skin
soft skin
HP:0000977.def: Subjective impression of increased softness upon palpation of the skin.

name: bruising susceptibility
bruise susceptibility
HP:0000978.def: An ecchymosis (bruise) refers to the skin discoloration caused by the escape of blood into the tissues from ruptured blood vessels. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to bruising. The corresponding phenotypic abnormality is generally elicited on medical history as a report of frequent ecchymoses or bruising without adequate trauma.

name: purpura
purpura
HP:0000979.def: Purpura (from Latin: purpura, meaning \"purple\") is the appearance of red or purple discolorations on the skin that do not blanch on applying pressure. They are caused by bleeding underneath the skin. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to developing purpura. Purpura are larger than petechiae.
synonym: red or purple spots on the skin
red or purple spot on the skin

name: palmoplantar keratoderma
palmoplantar keratoderma
HP:0000982.def: Abnormal thickening of the skin of the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet.

name: skin rash
skin rash
HP:0000988.def: A red eruption of the skin.

name: pruritus
pruritus
HP:0000989.def: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased disposition to experience pruritus.

name: xanthomatosis
xanthomatosis
HP:0000991.def: The presence of multiple xanthomas (xanthomata) in the skin. Xanthomas are yellowish, firm, lipid-laden nodules in the skin.
synonym: yellow bumps of fatty deposits on skin
yellow bump of fatty deposit on skin

name: cutaneous photosensitivity
cutaneous photosensitivity
HP:0000992.def: An increased sensitivity of the skin to light. Photosensitivity may result in a rash upon exposure to the sun (which is known as photodermatosis). Photosensitivity can be diagnosed by phototests in which light is shone on small areas of skin.

name: molluscoid pseudotumors
molluscoid pseudotumors
HP:0000993.def: Bluish-grey, spongy nodules associated with scars over pressure points and easily traumatized areas like the elbows and knees.

name: melanocytic nevus
melanocytic nevus
HP:0000995.def: A oval and round, colored (usually medium-to dark brown, reddish brown, or flesh colored) lesion. Typically, a melanocytic nevus is less than 6 mm in diameter, but may be much smaller or larger.

name: facial capillary hemangioma
facial capillary hemangioma
HP:0000996.def: Hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells with small endothelial spaces, occurring in the face.

name: axillary freckling
axillary freckling
HP:0000997.def: The presence in the axillary region (armpit) of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

name: hypertrichosis
hypertrichosis
HP:0000998.def: Hypertrichosis is increased hair growth that is abnormal in quantity or location.

name: pyoderma
pyoderma
HP:0000999.def: Any manifestation of a skin disease associated with the production of pus.

name: abnormality of skin pigmentation
abnormality of skin pigmentation
HP:0001000.def: An abnormality of the pigmentation of the skin.

name: abnormality of subcutaneous fat tissue
abnormality of subcutaneous fat tissue
synonym: abnormality of fatty tissue below the skin
abnormality of fatty tissue below the skin

name: multiple lentigines
multiple lentigo
HP:0001003.def: Presence of an unusually high number of lentigines (singular: lentigo), which are flat, tan to brown oval spots.

name: lymphedema
lymphedema
HP:0001004.def: Localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
synonym: swelling caused by excess lymph fluid under skin
swell cause by excess lymph fluid under skin

name: hirsutism
hirsutism
HP:0001007.def: Abnormally increased hair growth referring to a male pattern of body hair (androgenic hair).

name: telangiectasia
telangiectasia
HP:0001009.def: Telangiectasias refer to small dilated blood vessels located near the surface of the skin or mucous membranes, measuring between 0.5 and 1 millimeter in diameter. Telangiectasia are located especially on the tongue, lips, palate, fingers, face, conjunctiva, trunk, nail beds, and fingertips.

name: hypopigmentation of the skin
hypopigmentation of the skin
HP:0001010.def: A reduction of skin color related to a decrease in melanin production and deposition.

name: multiple lipomas
multiple lipoma
HP:0001012.def: The presence of multiple lipomas (a type of benign tissue made of fatty tissue).

name: eruptive xanthomas
eruptive xanthoma
HP:0001013.def: Eruptive xanthomas are yellow-orange-to-red-brown papules that are often surrounded by an erythematous halo. They appear in crops on the buttocks, extensor surfaces of the extremities, and flexural creases. Acutely, variable amounts of pruritus and pain occur.

name: angiokeratoma
angiokeratoma
HP:0001014.def: Angiokeratomas are hyperkeratotic papules that are characterized histologically by superficial ectatic (i.e., dilated) blood vessels with epidermal proliferation. Clinically, angiokeratoma presents as a small, raised, dark-red spot.

name: prominent superficial veins
prominent superficial vein
HP:0001015.def: A condition in which superficial veins (i.e., veins just under the skin) are more conspicuous or noticable than normal.

name: anemic pallor
anemic pallor
HP:0001017.def: A type of pallor that is secondary to the presence of anemia.

name: abnormal palmar dermatoglyphics
abnormal palmar dermatoglyphic
HP:0001018.def: An abnormality of the dermatoglyphs, i.e., an abnormality of the patterns of ridges of the skin of palm of hand.

name: erythroderma
erythroderma
HP:0001019.def: An inflammatory exfoliative dermatosis involving nearly all of the surface of the skin. Erythroderma develops suddenly. A patchy erythema may generalize and spread to affect most of the skin. Scaling may appear in 2-6 days and be accompanied by hot, red, dry skin, malaise, and fever.
synonym: red scaly skin caused by inflammatory skin disease
red scaly skin cause by inflammatory skin disease

name: albinism
albinism
HP:0001022.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of pigmentation (reduced or absent) of skin, hair and eye (iris and retina).

name: skin dimple over apex of long bone angulation
skin dimple over apex of long bone angulation
urticaria
urticaria
HP:0001025.def: Raised, well-circumscribed areas of erythema and edema involving the dermis and epidermis. Urticaria is intensely pruritic, and blanches completely with pressure.

name: soft , doughy skin
soft , doughy skin
HP:0001027.def: A skin texture that is unusually soft (and may feel silky), and has a malleable consistency resembling that of dough.

name: hemangioma
hemangioma
HP:0001028.def: A hemangioma is a benign tumor characterized by blood-filled spaces lined by benign endothelial cells. A hemangioma characterized by large endothelial spaces (caverns) is called a cavernous hemangioma (in contrast to a hemangioma with small endothelial spaces, which is called capillary hemangioma).

name: poikiloderma
poikiloderma
HP:0001029.def: Poikiloderma refers to a patch of skin with (1) reticulated hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation, (2) wrinkling secondary to epidermal atrophy, and (3) telangiectasias.

name: fragile skin
fragile skin
HP:0001030.def: Skin that splits easily with minimal injury.

name: absent distal interphalangeal creases
absent distal interphalangeal crease
HP:0001032.def: Absence of the distal interphalangeal flexion creases of the fingers.
synonym: absence of skin creases over distal interphalangeal joints
absence of skin crease over distal interphalangeal joint
aplasia of the distal interphalangeal creases
aplasia of the distal interphalangeal crease

name: hypermelanotic macule
hypermelanotic macule
HP:0001034.def: A hyperpigmented circumscribed area of change in normal skin color without elevation or depression of any size.

name: parakeratosis
parakeratosis
HP:0001036.def: Abnormal formation of the keratinocytes of the epidermis characterized by persistence of nuclei, incomplete formation of keratin, and moistness and swelling of the keratinocytes.

name: facial erythema
facial erythema
HP:0001041.def: Redness of the skin of the face, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

name: intermittent jaundice
intermittent jaundice
HP:0001046.def: Jaundice that is sometimes present, sometimes not.

name: atopic dermatitis
atopic dermatitis
HP:0001047.def: Atopic dermatitis (AD) or atopic eczema is an itchy, inflammatory skin condition with a predilection for the skin flexures. It is characterized by poorly defined erythema with edema, vesicles, and weeping in the acute stage and skin thickening (lichenification) in the chronic stage.

name: cavernous hemangioma
cavernous hemangioma
HP:0001048.def: The presence of a cavernous hemangioma. A hemangioma characterized by large endothelial spaces (caverns) is called a cavernous hemangioma.
synonym: collection of dilated blood vessels that forms mass
collection of dilated blood vessel that form mass

name: absent dorsal skin creases over affected joints
absent dorsal skin crease over affected joint
seborrheic dermatitis
seborrheic dermatitis
HP:0001051.def: Seborrheic dermatitis is a form of eczema which is closely related to dandruff. It causes dry or greasy peeling of the scalp, eyebrows, and face, and sometimes trunk.

name: nevus flammeus
nevus flammeus
HP:0001052.def: A congenital vascular malformation consisting of superficial and deep dilated capillaries in the skin which produce a reddish to purplish discolouration of the skin.

name: erysipelas
erysipelas
HP:0001055.def: Increased susceptibility to erysipelas, as manifested by a medical history of repeated episodes of erysipelas, which is a superficial infection of the skin, typically involving the lymphatic system.

name: milia
milium
HP:0001056.def: Presence of multiple small cysts containing keratin (skin protein) and presenting as tiny pearly-white bumps just under the surface of the skin.

name: aplasia cutis congenita
aplasia cutis congenita
HP:0001057.def: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin in multiple or solitary non-inflammatory, well-demarcated, oval or circular ulcers with a diameter of about 1 to 2 cm. Aplasia cutis congenita most commonly occurs on the scalp, but may present in the face, trunk, or limbs.
synonym: absence of part of skin at birth
absence of part of skin at birth

name: poor wound healing
poor wind heal
HP:0001058.def: A reduced ability to heal cutaneous wounds.

name: pterygium
pterygium
HP:0001059.def: Pterygia are 'winglike' triangular membranes occurring in the neck, eyes, knees, elbows, ankles or digits.

name: axillary pterygium
axillary pterygium
HP:0001060.def: Presence of a cutaneous membrane (flap) in the armpit.

name: acne
acne
HP:0001061.def: A skin condition in which there is an increase in sebum secretion by the pilosebaceous apparatus associated with open comedones (blackheads), closed comedones (whiteheads), and pustular nodules (papules, pustules, and cysts).

name: atypical nevus
atypical nevus
HP:0001062.def: A large pigmented lesion measuring 5-15 mm in diameter with irregular, notched, and ill defined border and with color that may range from tan to dark brown to pink.

name: acrocyanosis
acrocyanosis
HP:0001063.def: Bluish discoloration of the skin of the hands or feet.
synonym: persistent blue color of hands or feet
persistent blue color of hand or foot
persistent blue colour of hands or feet
persistent blue colour of hand or foot

name: striae distensae
stria distensae
HP:0001065.def: Thinned, erythematous, depressed bands of atrophic skin. Initially, striae appear as flattened and thinned, pinkish linear regions of the skin. Striae tend to enlarge in length and become reddish or purplish. Later, striae tend to appear as white, depressed bands that are parallel to the lines of skin tension. Striae distensae occur most often in areas that have been subject to distension such as the lower back, buttocks, thighs, breast, abdomen, and shoulders.

name: neurofibroma
neurofibroma
HP:0001067.def: A benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor that generally appears as a soft, skin-colored papule or small subcutaneous nodule. Individuals with neurofibromatosis can have numerous neurofibromas.

name: episodic hyperhidrosis
episodic hyperhidrosis
HP:0001069.def: Intermittent episodes of abnormally increased perspiration.

name: angiokeratoma corporis diffusum
angiokeratoma corporis diffusum
HP:0001071.def: Angiokeratoma corporis diffusum (ACD) is typically characterized by innumerable small red to black papules which occur in clusters and are situated symmetrically in the bathing trunks area. The number of lesions and the extension of the body increase steadily with time so that generalization and mucosal involvement are common. The single lesion begins with a minute reddish papule which enlarges to up to 10 mm in diameter, becomes dark red to black with a discrete keratotic overgrowth. Histologically, the papules are characterized by superficial dilated capillaries in papillary dermis with epidermal proliferation.

name: atypical nevi in non - sun exposed areas
atypical nevus in non - sun expose area
atrophic scars
atrophic scar
HP:0001075.def: Scars that form a depression compared to the level of the surrounding skin because of damage to the collagen, fat or other tissues below the skin.
synonym: sunken or indented skin due to damage
sunken or indent skin due to damage

name: biliary tract abnormality
biliary tract abnormality
HP:0001080.def: An abnormality of the biliary tree.

name: cholelithiasis
cholelithiasis
HP:0001081.def: Hard, pebble-like deposits that form within the gallbladder.

name: cholecystitis
cholecystitis
HP:0001082.def: The presence of inflammatory changes in the gallbladder.

name: ectopia lentis
ectopia lentis
HP:0001083.def: Dislocation or malposition of the crystalline lens of the eye. A partial displacement (or dislocation) of the lens is described as a subluxation of the lens, while a complete displacement is termed luxation of the lens. A complete displacement occurs if the lens is completely outside the patellar fossa of the lens, either in the anterior chamber, in the vitreous, or directly on the retina. If the lens is partially displaced but still contained within the lens space, then it is termed subluxation.

name: corneal arcus
corneal arcus
HP:0001084.def: A hazy, grayish-white ring about 2 mm in width located close to but separated from the limbus (the corneoscleral junction). Corneal arcus generally occurs bilaterally, and is related to lipid deposition in the cornea. Corneal arcus can occur in elderly persons as a part of the aging process but may be associated with hypercholesterolemia in people under the age of 50 years.

name: papilledema
papilledema
HP:0001085.def: Papilledema refers to edema (swelling) of the optic disc secondary to any factor which increases cerebral spinal fluid pressure.

name: developmental glaucoma
developmental glaucoma
HP:0001087.def: Glaucoma which forms during the early years of a child's life is called developmental or congenital glaucoma.

name: brushfield spots
brushfield spot
HP:0001088.def: The presence of whitish spots in a ring-like arrangement at the periphery of the iris.

name: abnormally large globe
abnormally large globe
HP:0001090.def: Diffusely large eye (with megalocornea) without glaucoma.

name: absent lacrimal punctum
absent lacrimal punctum
HP:0001092.def: No identifiable superior and/or inferior lacrimal punctum.

name: optic nerve dysplasia
optic nerve dysplasia
HP:0001093.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the optic nerve.

name: iridocyclitis
iridocyclitis
HP:0001094.def: A type of anterior uveitis, in which there is Inflammation of the iris and the ciliary body.

name: keratoconjunctivitis
keratoconjunctivitis
HP:0001096.def: Inflammation of the cornea and conjunctiva.

name: keratoconjunctivitis sicca
keratoconjunctivitis sicca
HP:0001097.def: Dryness of the eye related to deficiency of the tear film components (aqueous, mucin, or lipid), lid surface abnormalities, or epithelial abnormalities. Keratoconjunctivitis sicca often results in a scratchy or sandy sensation (foreign body sensation) in the eyes, and may also be associated with itching, inability to produce tears, photosensitivity, redness, pain, and difficulty in moving the eyelids.

name: abnormal fundus morphology
abnormal fundus morphology
HP:0001098.def: Any structural abnormality of the fundus of the eye.

name: heterochromia iridis
heterochromia iridis
HP:0001100.def: Heterochromia iridis is a difference in the color of the iris in the two eyes.

name: angioid streaks of the fundus
angioid streak of the fundus
HP:0001102.def: Irregular lines in the deep retina that are typically configured in a radiating fashion and emanate from the optic disc. Angioid streaks are crack-like dehiscences in abnormally thickened and calcified Bruch's membrane, resulting in atrophy of the overlying retinal pigment epithelium. They may be associated with a number of endocrine, metabolic, and connective tissue abnormalities but are frequently idiopathic.

name: abnormal macular morphology
abnormal macular morphology
HP:0001103.def: A structural abnormality of the macula lutea, which is an oval-shaped highly pigmented yellow spot near the center of the retina.

name: retinal atrophy
retinal atrophy
HP:0001105.def: Well-demarcated area(s) of partial or complete depigmentation in the fundus, reflecting atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium with associated retinal photoreceptor loss.

name: periorbital hyperpigmentation
periorbital hyperpigmentation
HP:0001106.def: Increased pigmentation of the skin in the region surrounding the orbit of the eye.
synonym: idiopathic cutaneous hyperchromia at the orbital region
idiopathic cutaneous hyperchromia at the orbital region

name: ocular albinism
ocular albinism
HP:0001107.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of pigmentation (reduced or absent) of the iris and retina.

name: leber optic atrophy
leber optic atrophy
HP:0001112.def: Degeneration of retinal ganglion cells and their axons.

name: xanthelasma
xanthelasma
HP:0001114.def: The presence of xanthomata in the skin of the eyelid.
synonym: fatty deposits in skin around the eyes
fatty deposit in skin around the eye

name: posterior polar cataract
posterior polar cataract
HP:0001115.def: A polar cataract that affects the posterior pole of the lens.

name: macular coloboma
macular coloboma
HP:0001116.def: A congenital defect of the macula distinct from coloboma associated with optic fissure closure defects. Macular coloboma is characterized by a sharply defined, rather large defect in the central area of the fundus that is oval or round, and coarsely pigmented.

name: sudden loss of visual acuity
sudden loss of visual acuity
HP:0001117.def: Severe loss of visual acuity within hours or days. This is characteristic of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy.

name: juvenile cataract
juvenile cataract
HP:0001118.def: A type of cataract that is not apparent at birth but that arises in childhood or adolescence.

name: keratoglobus
keratoglobus
HP:0001119.def: Limbus-to-limbus corneal thinning, often greatest in the periphery, with globular protrusion of the cornea.

name: abnormality of corneal size
abnormality of corneal size
HP:0001120.def: Any abnormality of the size or morphology of the cornea.

name: obsolete aplasia / hypoplasia of the choroid
obsolete aplasia / hypoplasia of the choroid
visual field defect
visual field defect
synonym: partial loss of field of vision
partial loss of field of vision

name: transient unilateral blurring of vision
transient unilateral blurring of vision
HP:0001125.def: Transient blurring of vision associated with the aura phase of migraine.

name: cryptophthalmos
cryptophthalmos
HP:0001126.def: Cryptophthalmos is a condition of total absence of eyelids and the skin of forehead is continuous with that of cheek, in which the eyeball is completely concealed by the skin, which is stretched over the orbital cavity.

name: trichiasis
trichiasis
HP:0001128.def: Inversion and rubbing of the eyelashes against the globe of the eye.

name: large central visual field defect
large central visual field defect
synonym: large central loss of field of vision
large central loss of field of vision

name: corneal dystrophy
corneal dystrophy
HP:0001131.def: The term corneal dystrophy embraces a heterogenous group of bilateral genetically determined non-inflammatory corneal diseases that are restricted to the cornea.

name: lens subluxation
lens subluxation
HP:0001132.def: Partial dislocation of the lens of the eye.

name: constriction of peripheral visual field
constriction of peripheral visual field
HP:0001133.def: An absolute or relative decrease in retinal sensitivity extending from edge (periphery) of the visual field in a concentric pattern. The visual field is the area that is perceived simultaneously by a fixating eye.

name: anterior polar cataract
anterior polar cataract
HP:0001134.def: A polar cataract that affects the anterior pole of the lens.

name: retinal arteriolar tortuosity
retinal arteriolar tortuosity
HP:0001136.def: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the retinal arterioles.

name: alternating esotropia
alternate esotropia
HP:0001137.def: Esotropia in which either eye may be used for fixation.

name: limbal dermoid
limbal dermoid
HP:0001140.def: A benign tumor typically found at the junction of the cornea and sclera (limbal epibullar dermoid).

name: severely reduced visual acuity
severely reduce visual acuity
HP:0001141.def: Severe reduction of the ability to see defined as visual acuity less than 6/60 (20/200 in US notation; 0.1 in decimal notation) but at least 3/60 (20/400 in US notation; 0.05 in decimal notation).

name: lenticonus
lenticonus
HP:0001142.def: A conical projection of the anterior or posterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.

name: orbital cyst
orbital cyst
HP:0001144.def: Presence of a cyst in the region of the periorbital tissues. Orbital cysts can be derived from epithelial or glandular tissue within or surrounding the orbit (lacrimal glands, salivary glands, conjunctival, oral, nasal, or sinus epithelium).

name: retinal exudate
retinal exudate
HP:0001147.def: Fluid which has escaped from retinal blood vessels with a high concentration of lipid, protein, and cellular debris with a typically bright, reflective, white or cream colored appearance on the surface of the retina.

name: lattice corneal dystrophy
lattice corneal dystrophy
HP:0001149.def: The presence of fine, branching linear opacities in Bowman's layer in the central area that may spread to the periphery in the clinical course. The deep corneal stroma may be involved but the process does not reach Descemet's membrane. Recurrent corneal erosion may occur. Histologic examination reveals amyloid deposits in the collagen fibers of the cornea.

name: impaired horizontal smooth pursuit
impaired horizontal smooth pursuit
HP:0001151.def: An abnormality of ocular smooth pursuit characterized by an impairment of the ability to track horizontally moving objects.

name: saccadic smooth pursuit
saccadic smooth pursuit
HP:0001152.def: An abnormality of tracking eye movements in which smooth pursuit is interrupted by an abnormally high number of saccadic movements.

name: septate vagina
septate vagina
