HP:0001153.def: The presence of a vaginal septum, thereby creating a vaginal duplication. The septum is longitudinal in the majority of cases.

name: abnormality of the hand
abnormality of the hand
HP:0001155.def: An abnormality affecting one or both hands.

name: brachydactyly
brachydactyly
HP:0001156.def: Digits that appear disproportionately short compared to the hand/foot. The word brachydactyly is used here to describe a series distinct patterns of shortened digits (brachydactyly types A-E). This is the sense used here.

name: syndactyly
syndactyly
HP:0001159.def: Webbing or fusion of the fingers or toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as \"bony\

name: hand polydactyly
hand polydactyly
HP:0001161.def: A kind of polydactyly characterized by the presence of a supernumerary finger or fingers.

name: postaxial hand polydactyly
postaxial hand polydactyly
HP:0001162.def: Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand (that is, on the side with the fifth finger).

name: arachnodactyly
arachnodactyly
HP:0001166.def: Abnormally long and slender fingers (\"spider fingers\").

name: broad palm
broad palm
HP:0001169.def: For children from birth to 4 years of age the palm width is more than 2 SD above the mean; for children from 4 to 16 years of age the palm width is above the 95th centile; or, the width of the palm appears disproportionately wide for the length.

name: split hand
split hand
HP:0001171.def: A condition in which middle parts of the hand (fingers and metacarpals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic middle fingers over absent middel fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands.

name: abnormal thumb morphology
abnormal thumb morphology
HP:0001172.def: An abnormal structure of the first digit of the hand.

name: preaxial hand polydactyly
preaxial hand polydactyly
HP:0001177.def: Supernumerary digits located at the radial side of the hand. Polydactyly (supernumerary digits) involving the thumb occurs in many distinct forms of high variability and severity. Ranging from fleshy nubbins over varying degrees of partial duplication/splitting to completely duplicated or even triplicated thumbs or preaxial (on the radial side of the hand) supernumerary digits.

name: ulnar claw
ulnar claw
HP:0001178.def: An abnormal hand position characterized by hyperextension of the fourth and fifth fingers at the metacarpophalangeal joints and flexion of the interphalangeal joints of the same fingers such that they are curled towards the palm.

name: hand oligodactyly
hand oligodactyly
HP:0001180.def: A developmental defect resulting in the presence of fewer than the normal number of fingers.

name: adducted thumb
adduct thumb
HP:0001181.def: In the resting position, the tip of the thumb is on, or near, the palm, close to the base of the fourth or fifth finger.

name: tapered finger
taper finger
HP:0001182.def: The gradual reduction in girth of the finger from proximal to distal.

name: hyperextensibility of the finger joints
hyperextensibility of the finger joint
HP:0001187.def: The ability of the finger joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

name: hand clenching
hand clench
HP:0001188.def: An abnormal hand posture in which the hands are clenched to fists. All digits held completely flexed at the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. In prenatal sonography of the fetal clenched hand, the index finger overlaps a clenched fist formed by the other digits. The proximal interphalangeal articulation of the index finger is flexed and ulnarly deviated, and the thumb is adducted.

name: abnormal carpal morphology
abnormal carpal morphology
HP:0001191.def: An abnormality affecting the carpal bones of the wrist (scaphoid, lunate, triquetral, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

name: ulnar deviation of the hand or of fingers of the hand
ulnar deviation of the hand or of finger of the hand
abnormalities of placenta or umbilical cord
abnormality of placenta or umbilical cord
HP:0001194.def: An abnormality of the placenta (the organ that connects the developing fetus to the uterine wall) or of the umbilical cord (the cord that connects the fetus to the placenta).
synonym: abnormalities of placenta or umbilical cord
abnormality of placenta or umbilical cord

name: single umbilical artery
single umbilical artery
HP:0001195.def: Single umbilical artery (SUA) is the absence of one of the two umbilical arteries surrounding the fetal bladder and in the fetal umbilical cord.
synonym: only one artery in umbilical cord instead of two
only one artery in umbilical cord instead of two

name: short umbilical cord
short umbilical cord
HP:0001196.def: Decreased length of the umbilical cord.

name: abnormality of prenatal development or birth
abnormality of prenatal development or birth
HP:0001197.def: An abnormality of the fetus or the birth of the fetus, excluding structural abnormalities.
synonym: abnormality of prenatal development or birth
abnormality of prenatal development or birth

name: triphalangeal thumb
triphalangeal thumb
HP:0001199.def: A thumb with three phalanges in a single, proximo-distal axis. Thus, this term applies if the thumb has an accessory phalanx, leading to a digit like appearance of the thumb.

name: distal symphalangism of hands
distal symphalangism of hand
HP:0001204.def: The term distal symphalangism refers to a bony fusion of the distal and middle phalanges of the digits of the hand, in other words the distal interphalangeal joint (DIJ) is missing which can be seen either on x-rays or as an absence of the distal interphalangeal finger creases.
synonym: symphalangism affecting the distal phalanges of the hand
symphalangism affect the distal phalanx of the hand

name: abnormal fingertip morphology
abnormal fingertip morphology
HP:0001211.def: An abnormal structure of the tip (end) of a finger.

name: prominent fingertip pads
prominent fingertip pad
HP:0001212.def: A soft tissue prominence of the ventral aspects of the fingertips. The term \"persistent fetal fingertip pads\

name: camptodactyly of 2nd - 5th fingers
camptodactyly of 2nd - 5th finger
HP:0001215.def: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the second to fifth fingers cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.

name: delayed ossification of carpal bones
delay ossification of carpal bone
HP:0001216.def: Ossification of carpal bones occurs later than age-adjusted norms.

name: clubbing
club
HP:0001217.def: Broadening of the soft tissues (non-edematous swelling of soft tissues) of the digital tips in all dimensions associated with an increased longitudinal and lateral curvature of the nails.

name: autoamputation
autoamputation
HP:0001218.def: Auto-amputation is the spontaneous detachment of an appendage from the body due to long standing pathology.

name: interphalangeal joint contracture of finger
interphalangeal joint contracture of finger
HP:0001220.def: Chronic loss of joint motion in an interphalangeal joint of a finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

name: pointed proximal second through fifth metacarpals
point proximal second through fifth metacarpal
HP:0001223.def: All of the metacarpal bones of the hand have a pointed proximal appearance.

name: obsolete acral ulceration and osteomyelitis leading to autoamputation of digits
obsolete acral ulceration and osteomyelitis lead to autoamputation of digit
abnormality of the thenar eminence
abnormality of the thenar eminence
HP:0001227.def: An abnormality of the thenar eminence, i.e., of the muscle on the palm of the human hand just beneath the thumb.

name: nail bed telangiectasia
nail bed telangiectasia
HP:0001232.def: Telangiectases in the area of the nails.

name: 2 - 3 finger syndactyly
2 - 3 finger syndactyly
HP:0001233.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers two and three.

name: hitchhiker thumb
hitchhiker thumb
HP:0001234.def: With the hand relaxed and the thumb in the plane of the palm, the axis of the thumb forms an angle of at least 90 degrees with the long axis of the hand.

name: slender finger
slender finger
HP:0001238.def: Fingers that are disproportionately narrow (reduced girth) for the hand/foot size or build of the individual.

name: wrist flexion contracture
wrist flexion contracture
HP:0001239.def: A chronic loss of wrist joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevent normal movement of the joints of the wrist.

name: small thenar eminence
small thenar eminence
HP:0001245.def: Underdevelopment of the thenar eminence with reduced palmar soft tissue mass surrounding the base of the thumb.

name: short tubular bones of the hand
short tubular bone of the hand
HP:0001248.def: Decreased length of the tubular bones of the hand, that is, the phalanges and metacarpals.
synonym: shortened short tubular bones of the hand
shorten short tubular bone of the hand

name: intellectual disability
intellectual disability
HP:0001249.def: Intellectual disability, previously referred to as mental retardation, is characterized by subnormal intellectual functioning that occurs during the developmental period. It is defined by an IQ score below 70.

name: seizure
seizure
HP:0001250.def: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterised by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

name: ataxia
ataxia
HP:0001251.def: Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. This causes a variety of elementary neurological deficits including asynergy (lack of coordination between muscles, limbs and joints), dysmetria (lack of ability to judge distances that can lead to under- or overshoot in grasping movements), and dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid movements requiring antagonizing muscle groups to be switched on and off repeatedly).

name: hypotonia
hypotonia
HP:0001252.def: Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia is not the same as muscle weakness, although the two conditions can co-exist.

name: lethargy
lethargy
HP:0001254.def: A state of disinterest, listlessness, and indifference, resulting in difficulty performing simple tasks or concentrating.

name: intellectual disability , mild
intellectual disability , mild
HP:0001256.def: Mild intellectual disability is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 50-69.

name: spasticity
spasticity
HP:0001257.def: A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone, exaggerated (hyperexcitable) tendon reflexes.
synonym: involuntary muscle stiffness , contraction , or spasm
involuntary muscle stiffness , contraction , or spasm

name: spastic paraplegia
spastic paraplegia
HP:0001258.def: Spasticity and weakness of the leg and hip muscles.

name: coma
coma
HP:0001259.def: The complete absence of wakefulness and consciousness, which is evident through a lack of response to any form of external stimuli.

name: dysarthria
dysarthria
HP:0001260.def: Dysarthric speech is a general description referring to a neurological speech disorder characterized by poor articulation. Depending on the involved neurological structures, dysarthria may be further classified as spastic, flaccid, ataxic, hyperkinetic and hypokinetic, or mixed.

name: excessive daytime somnolence
excessive daytime somnolence
HP:0001262.def: A state of abnormally strong desire for sleep during the daytime.
synonym: more than typical sleepiness during day
more than typical sleepiness during day

name: global developmental delay
global developmental delay
HP:0001263.def: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

name: spastic diplegia
spastic diplegia
HP:0001264.def: Spasticity (neuromuscular hypertonia) primarily in the muscles of the legs, hips, and pelvis.

name: hyporeflexia
hyporeflexia
HP:0001265.def: Reduction of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

name: choreoathetosis
choreoathetosis
HP:0001266.def: Involuntary movements characterized by both athetosis (inability to sustain muscles in a fixed position) and chorea (widespread jerky arrhythmic movements).

name: mental deterioration
mental deterioration
HP:0001268.def: Loss of previously present mental abilities, generally in adults.

name: hemiparesis
hemiparesis
HP:0001269.def: Loss of strength in the arm, leg, and sometimes face on one side of the body. Hemiplegia refers to a complete loss of strength, whereas hemiparesis refers to an incomplete loss of strength.
synonym: weakness of one side of body
weakness of one side of body

name: motor delay
motor delay
HP:0001270.def: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.

name: polyneuropathy
polyneuropathy
HP:0001271.def: A generalized disorder of peripheral nerves.

name: cerebellar atrophy
cerebellar atrophy
HP:0001272.def: Cerebellar atrophy is defined as a cerebellum with initially normal structures, in a posterior fossa with normal size, which displays enlarged fissures (interfolial spaces) in comparison to the foliae secondary to loss of tissue. Cerebellar atrophy implies irreversible loss of tissue and result from an ongoing progressive disease until a final stage is reached or a single injury, e.g. an intoxication or infectious event.

name: agenesis of corpus callosum
agenesis of corpus callosum
HP:0001274.def: Absence of the corpus callosum as a result of the failure of the corpus callosum to develop, which can be the result of a failure in any one of the multiple steps of callosal development including cellular proliferation and migration, axonal growth or glial patterning at the midline.

name: hypertonia
hypertonia
HP:0001276.def: A condition in which there is increased muscle tone so that arms or legs, for example, are stiff and difficult to move.

name: orthostatic hypotension
orthostatic hypotension
HP:0001278.def: A form of hypotension characterized by a sudden fall in blood pressure that occurs when a person assumes a standing position.
synonym: decrease in blood pressure upon standing up
decrease in blood pressure upon stand up

name: syncope
syncope
HP:0001279.def: Syncope refers to a generalized weakness of muscles with loss of postural tone, inability to stand upright, and loss of consciousness. Once the patient is in a horizontal position, blood flow to the brain is no longer hindered by gravitation and consciousness is regained. Unconsciousness usually lasts for seconds to minutes. Headache and drowsiness (which usually follow seizures) do not follow a syncopal attack. Syncope results from a sudden impairment of brain metabolism usually due to a reduction in cerebral blood flow.

name: tetany
tetany
HP:0001281.def: A condition characterized by intermittent involuntary contraction of muscles (spasms) related to hypocalcemia or occasionally magnesium deficiency.

name: bulbar palsy
bulbar palsy
HP:0001283.def: Bulbar weakness (or bulbar palsy) refers to bilateral impairment of function of the lower cranial nerves IX, X, XI and XII, which occurs due to lower motor neuron lesion either at nuclear or fascicular level in the medulla or from bilateral lesions of the lower cranial nerves outside the brain-stem. Bulbar weakness is often associated with difficulty in chewing, weakness of the facial muscles, dysarthria, palatal weakness and regurgitation of fluids, dysphagia, and dysphonia.

name: areflexia
areflexia
HP:0001284.def: Absence of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

name: spastic tetraparesis
spastic tetraparesis
HP:0001285.def: Spastic weakness affecting all four limbs.

name: gait disturbance
gait disturbance
HP:0001288.def: The term gait disturbance can refer to any disruption of the ability to walk. In general, this can refer to neurological diseases but also fractures or other sources of pain that is triggered upon walking. However, in the current context gait disturbance refers to difficulty walking on the basis of a neurological or muscular disease.

name: confusion
confusion
HP:0001289.def: Lack of clarity and coherence of thought, perception, understanding, or action.

name: generalized hypotonia
generalize hypotonia
HP:0001290.def: Generalized muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone).

name: abnormal cranial nerve morphology
abnormal cranial nerve morphology
HP:0001291.def: Structural abnormality affecting one or more of the cranial nerves, which emerge directly from the brain stem.

name: stroke
stroke
HP:0001297.def: Sudden impairment of blood flow to a part of the brain due to occlusion or rupture of an artery to the brain.

name: encephalopathy
encephalopathy
HP:0001298.def: Encephalopathy is a term that means brain disease, damage, or malfunction. In general, encephalopathy is manifested by an altered mental state.

name: parkinsonism
parkinsonism
HP:0001300.def: Characteristic neurologic anomaly resulting from degeneration of dopamine-generating cells in the substantia nigra, a region of the midbrain, characterized clinically by shaking, rigidity, slowness of movement and difficulty with walking and gait.

name: pachygyria
pachygyria
HP:0001302.def: Pachygyria is a malformation of cortical development with abnormally wide gyri with sulci 1,5-3 cm apart and abnormally thick cortex measuring more than 5 mm (radiological definition). See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.
synonym: fewer and broader ridges in brain
few and broad ridge in brain

name: torsion dystonia
torsion dystonia
HP:0001304.def: Sustained involuntary muscle contractions that produce twisting and repetitive movements of the body.

name: dandy - walker malformation
dandy - walker malformation
HP:0001305.def: A congenital brain malformation typically characterized by incomplete formation of the cerebellar vermis, dilation of the fourth ventricle, and enlargement of the posterior fossa. In layman's terms, Dandy Walker malformation is a cyst in the cerebellum (typically symmetrical) that is involved with the fourth ventricle. This may interfere with the ability to drain cerebrospinal fluid from the brain, resulting in hydrocephalus. Dandy Walker cysts are formed during early embryonic development, while the brain forms. The cyst in the cerebellum typically has several blood vessels running through it connecting to the brain, thereby prohibiting surgical removal.

name: tongue fasciculations
tongue fasciculation
HP:0001308.def: Fasciculations or fibrillation affecting the tongue muscle.

name: dysmetria
dysmetria
HP:0001310.def: A type of ataxia characterized by the inability to carry out movements with the correct range and motion across the plane of more than one joint related to incorrect estimation of the distances required for targeted movements.

name: abnormal nervous system electrophysiology
abnormal nervous system electrophysiology
HP:0001311.def: An abnormality of the function of the electrical signals with which nerve cells communicate with each other or with muscles as measured by electrophysiological investigations.

name: giant somatosensory evoked potentials
giant somatosensory evoke potential
HP:0001312.def: An abnormal enlargement (i.e. increase in measured voltage) of somatosensory evoked potentials.

name: reduced tendon reflexes
reduce tendon reflex
HP:0001315.def: Diminution of tendon reflexes, which is an invariable sign of peripheral nerve disease.
synonym: absent or decreased deep tendon reflexes
absent or decrease deep tendon reflex
decreased to absent deep tendon reflexes
decrease to absent deep tendon reflex
diminished or absent deep tendon reflexes
diminish or absent deep tendon reflex
hypoactive to absent deep tendon reflexes
hypoactive to absent deep tendon reflex
weak or absent deep tendon reflexes
weak or absent deep tendon reflex

name: abnormal cerebellum morphology
abnormal cerebellum morphology
HP:0001317.def: Any structural abnormality of the cerebellum.

name: neonatal hypotonia
neonatal hypotonia
HP:0001319.def: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) manifesting in the neonatal period.
synonym: low muscle tone , in neonatal onset
low muscle tone , in neonatal onset

name: cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
HP:0001320.def: Underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: cerebellar hypoplasia
cerebellar hypoplasia
HP:0001321.def: Cerebellar hypoplasia is a descriptive term implying a cerebellum with a reduced volume, but a normal shape and is stable over time.

name: hypoglycemic coma
hypoglycemic coma
HP:0001325.def: Coma induced by low blood sugar.
synonym: coma caused by low blood sugar
coma cause by low blood sugar
loss of consciousness due to hypoglycemia
loss of consciousness due to hypoglycemia

name: eeg with irregular generalized spike and wave complexes
eeg with irregular generalize spike and wave complex
HP:0001326.def: EEG shows spikes (<80 ms) and waves, which are recorded over the entire scalp and do not have a specific frequency.
synonym: eeg with irregular generalised spike and wave complexes
eeg with irregular generalise spike and wave complex

name: photosensitive myoclonic seizure
photosensitive myoclonic seizure
HP:0001327.def: Generalised myoclonic seizure provoked by flashing or flickering light.

name: specific learning disability
specific learn disability
HP:0001328.def: Impairment of certain skills such as reading or writing, coordination, self-control, or attention that interfere with the ability to learn. The impairment is not related to a global deficiency of intelligence.

name: absent septum pellucidum
absent septum pellucidum
HP:0001331.def: Absence of the septum pellucidum (meaning translucent wall in Latin - SP), also known as the ventricle of Sylvius. The septum pellucidum is a thin, triangular double membrane separating the frontal horns of the right and left lateral ventricles of the brain. It extends between the anterior portion of the corpus callosum, and the body of the fornix and its width varies from 1.5 to 3.0 mm.

name: dystonia
dystonia
HP:0001332.def: An abnormally increased muscular tone that causes fixed abnormal postures. There is a slow, intermittent twisting motion that leads to exaggerated turning and posture of the extremities and trunk.

name: communicating hydrocephalus
communicate hydrocephalus
HP:0001334.def: A form of hydrocephalus in which there is no visible obstruction to the flow of the cerebrospinal fluid between the ventricles and subarachnoid space.

name: bimanual synkinesia
bimanual synkinesia
HP:0001335.def: Involuntary movements of one hand that accompany and mirror intentional movements of the opposite hand.

name: myoclonus
myoclonus
HP:0001336.def: Very brief, involuntary random muscular contractions occurring at rest, in response to sensory stimuli, or accompanying voluntary movements.

name: tremor
tremor
HP:0001337.def: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.

name: partial agenesis of the corpus callosum
partial agenesis of the corpus callosum
HP:0001338.def: A partial failure of the development of the corpus callosum.
synonym: partial or complete agenesis of corpus callosum
partial or complete agenesis of corpus callosum
partial or complete agenesis of the corpus callosum
partial or complete agenesis of the corpus callosum
partial to complete agenesis of corpus callosum
partial to complete agenesis of corpus callosum
partial - total agenesis of corpus callosum
partial - total agenesis of corpus callosum

name: lissencephaly
lissencephaly
HP:0001339.def: A spectrum of malformations of cortical development caused by insufficient neuronal migration that subsumes the terms agyria, pachygyria and subcortical band heterotopia. See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.
synonym: fewer or absent grooves in brain
few or absent groove in brain

name: enhancement of the c - reflex
enhancement of the c - reflex
HP:0001340.def: Increase in amplitude of a long-loop response upon somatosensory evoked potential testing, representing an electrically evoked myoclonic response.

name: cerebral hemorrhage
cerebral hemorrhage
HP:0001342.def: Hemorrhage into the parenchyma of the brain.

name: kernicterus
kernicterus
HP:0001343.def: Damage to cerebral nuclei caused in infants by highly increased levels of unconjugated bilirubin. The basal ganglia and brainstem nuclei could be shown to have a yellow staining historically in infants who died of kernicterus, that is, kernicterus is strictly speaking a pathological diagnosis. The presence of kernicterus may be inferred in infants with characteristic acute or chronic bilirubin-induced neurological dysfunction.

name: absent speech
absent speech
HP:0001344.def: Complete lack of development of speech and language abilities.

name: psychotic mentation
psychotic mentation
HP:0001345.def: A pattern of thinking and perceiving characterized by a loss of contact with reality, leading to significant changes in thoughts, perceptions, and behaviors.

name: hyperreflexia
hyperreflexia
HP:0001347.def: Hyperreflexia is the presence of hyperactive stretch reflexes of the muscles.

name: brisk reflexes
brisk reflex
HP:0001348.def: Tendon reflexes that are noticeably more active than usual (conventionally denoted 3+ on clinical examination). Brisk reflexes may or may not indicate a neurological lesion. They are distinguished from hyperreflexia by the fact that hyerreflexia is characterized by hyperactive repeating (clonic) reflexes, which are considered to be always abnormal.

name: facial diplegia
facial diplegia
HP:0001349.def: Facial diplegia refers to bilateral facial palsy (bilateral facial palsy is much rarer than unilateral facial palsy).

name: slurred speech
slur speech
HP:0001350.def: Abnormal coordination of muscles involved in speech.

name: jerk - locked premyoclonus spikes
jerk - lock premyoclonus spike
HP:0001351.def: Jerk-locked averaging (JLA) is used to record the timing and distribution of brain activity preceding brisk involuntary movements such as those observed in patients with myoclonus. JLA is capable of revealing a premyoclonus spike in the absence of paroxysmal activity in the routine EEG.

name: megalencephaly
megalencephaly
HP:0001355.def: Diffuse enlargement of the entire cerebral hemispheres leading to macrocephaly (with or without overlying cortical dysplasia).

name: plagiocephaly
plagiocephaly
HP:0001357.def: Asymmetric head shape, which is usually a combination of unilateral occipital flattening with ipsilateral frontal prominence, leading to rhomboid cranial shape.

name: holoprosencephaly
holoprosencephaly
HP:0001360.def: Holoprosencephaly is a structural anomaly of the brain in which the developing forebrain fails to divide into two separate hemispheres and ventricles.

name: nystagmus - induced head nodding
nystagmus - induced head nod
HP:0001361.def: Head movements associated with nystagmus, that may represent an attempt to compensate for the involuntary eye movements and to improve vision.

name: calvarial skull defect
calvarial skull defect
HP:0001362.def: A localized defect in the bone of the skull resulting from abnormal embryological development. The defect is covered by normal skin. In some cases, skull x-rays have shown underlying lytic bone lesions which have closed before the age of one year.

name: craniosynostosis
craniosynostosis
HP:0001363.def: Craniosynostosis refers to the premature closure of the cranial sutures. Primary craniosynostosis refers to the closure of one or more sutures due to abnormalities in skull development, and secondary craniosynostosis results from failure of brain growth.

name: abnormal joint morphology
abnormal joint morphology
HP:0001367.def: An abnormal structure or form of the joints, i.e., one or more of the articulations where two bones join.

name: rheumatoid arthritis
rheumatoid arthritis
HP:0001370.def: Inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures with widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, as well as atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures.

name: flexion contracture
flexion contracture
HP:0001371.def: A flexion contracture is a bent (flexed) joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.
synonym: flexed joint that can not be straightened
flexed joint that can not be straighten

name: limitation of joint mobility
limitation of joint mobility
HP:0001376.def: A reduction in the freedom of movement of one or more joints.

name: limited elbow extension
limited elbow extension
HP:0001377.def: Limited ability to straighten the arm at the elbow joint.

name: joint hypermobility
joint hypermobility
HP:0001382.def: The ability of a joint to move beyond its normal range of motion.

name: abnormal hip joint morphology
abnormal hip joint morphology
HP:0001384.def: An abnormality of the hip joint.

name: hip dysplasia
hip dysplasia
HP:0001385.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the hip.

name: joint stiffness
joint stiffness
HP:0001387.def: Joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in a joint or joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity. Joint stiffness typically subsides over time.

name: joint laxity
joint laxity
HP:0001388.def: Lack of stability of a joint.

name: cirrhosis
cirrhosis
HP:0001394.def: A chronic disorder of the liver in which liver tissue becomes scarred and is partially replaced by regenerative nodules and fibrotic tissue resulting in loss of liver function.
synonym: scar tissue replaces healthy tissue in the liver
scar tissue replace healthy tissue in the liver

name: hepatic fibrosis
hepatic fibrosis
HP:0001395.def: The presence of excessive fibrous connective tissue in the liver. Fibrosis is a reparative or reactive process.

name: cholestasis
cholestasis
HP:0001396.def: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in bile ducts.
synonym: slowed or blocked flow of bile from liver
slow or block flow of bile from liver

name: hepatic steatosis
hepatic steatosis
HP:0001397.def: Steatosis is a term used to denote lipid accumulation within hepatocytes.

name: obsolete hepatic abscesses due to immunodeficiency
obsolete hepatic abscess due to immunodeficiency
hepatocellular carcinoma
hepatocellular carcinoma
HP:0001402.def: A kind of neoplasm of the liver that originates in hepatocytes and presents macroscopically as a soft and hemorrhagic tan mass in the liver.

name: macrovesicular hepatic steatosis
macrovesicular hepatic steatosis
HP:0001403.def: A form of hepatic steatosis characterized by the presence of large, lipid-laden vesicles in the affected hepatocytes.

name: periportal fibrosis
periportal fibrosis
HP:0001405.def: The presence of fibrosis affecting the interlobular stroma of liver.

name: intrahepatic cholestasis
intrahepatic cholestasis
HP:0001406.def: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in the small bile ducts within the liver.
synonym: impaired release of bile from liver
impaired release of bile from liver

name: bile duct proliferation
bile duct proliferation
HP:0001408.def: Proliferative changes of the bile ducts.

name: portal hypertension
portal hypertension
HP:0001409.def: Increased pressure in the portal vein.

name: decreased liver function
decrease liver function
HP:0001410.def: Reduced ability of the liver to perform its functions.

name: enteroviral hepatitis
enteroviral hepatitis
HP:0001412.def: Inflammation of the liver due to infection with enterovirus.

name: micronodular cirrhosis
micronodular cirrhosis
HP:0001413.def: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of small regenerative nodules.

name: microvesicular hepatic steatosis
microvesicular hepatic steatosis
HP:0001414.def: A form of hepatic steatosis characterized by the presence of small, lipid-laden vesicles in the affected hepatocytes.

name: x - linked inheritance
x - link inheritance
HP:0001417.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome.

name: x - linked recessive inheritance
x - link recessive inheritance
HP:0001419.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for recessive traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome. In the context of medical genetics, X-linked recessive disorders manifest in males (who have one copy of the X chromosome and are thus hemizygotes), but generally not in female heterozygotes who have one mutant and one normal allele.

name: abnormality of the musculature of the hand
abnormality of the musculature of the hand
x - linked dominant inheritance
x - link dominant inheritance
HP:0001423.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for dominant traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome. In the context of medical genetics, X-linked dominant disorders tend to manifest very severely in affected males. The severity of manifestation in females may depend on the degree of skewed X inactivation.

name: non - mendelian inheritance
non - mendelian inheritance
HP:0001426.def: A mode of inheritance that depends on genetic determinants in more than one gene.

name: mitochondrial inheritance
mitochondrial inheritance
HP:0001427.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the mitochondrial genome. Because the mitochondrial genome is essentially always maternally inherited, a mitochondrial condition can only be transmitted by females, although the condition can affect both sexes. The proportion of mutant mitochondria can vary (heteroplasmy).

name: hepatosplenomegaly
hepatosplenomegaly
HP:0001433.def: Simultaneous enlargement of the liver and spleen.

name: abnormality of the shoulder girdle musculature
abnormality of the shoulder girdle musculature
abnormality of the foot musculature
abnormality of the foot musculature
HP:0001436.def: An anomaly of the musculature of foot.

name: abnormality of the musculature of the lower limbs
abnormality of the musculature of the low limb
abnormal abdomen morphology
abnormal abdomen morphology
HP:0001438.def: A structural abnormality of the abdomen ('belly'), that is, the part of the body between the pelvis and the thorax.

name: metatarsal synostosis
metatarsal synostosis
synonym: fusion of the long bones of the feet
fusion of the long bone of the foot

name: abnormality of the musculature of the thigh
abnormality of the musculature of the thigh
typified by somatic mosaicism
typify by somatic mosaicism
HP:0001442.def: Description of conditions in which affected individuals typically display somatic mosaicism, i.e., genetically distinct populations of somatic cells in a given organism caused by DNA mutations, epigenetic alterations of DNA, chromosomal abnormalities or the spontaneous reversion of inherited mutations. In many conditions typified by somatic mosaicism, constitutive mutation is lethal and cases are exclusively or predominantly mosaic.

name: obsolete autosomal dominant somatic cell mutation
obsolete autosomal dominant somatic cell mutation
abnormality of the hip - girdle musculature
abnormality of the hip - girdle musculature
abnormality of the musculature of the upper limbs
abnormality of the musculature of the upper limb
duplication of metatarsal bones
duplication of metatarsal bone
synonym: duplication of long bones of foot
duplication of long bone of foot

name: y - linked inheritance
y - link inheritance
HP:0001450.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the Y chromosome.

name: obsolete autosomal dominant contiguous gene syndrome
obsolete autosomal dominant contiguous gene syndrome
abnormality of the musculature of the upper arm
abnormality of the musculature of the upper arm
1 - 3 toe syndactyly
1 - 3 toe syndactyly
HP:0001459.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to three.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia involving the skeletal musculature
aplasia / hypoplasia involve the skeletal musculature
HP:0001460.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the musculature.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia involving the shoulder musculature
aplasia / hypoplasia involve the shoulder musculature
HP:0001464.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the muscles of the shoulder.

name: contiguous gene syndrome
contiguous gene syndrome
HP:0001466.def: A syndrome caused by the effects of abnormality (typically a deletion or duplication) of 2 or more adjacent genes

name: aplasia / hypoplasia involving the musculature of the upper limbs
aplasia / hypoplasia involve the musculature of the upper limb
HP:0001467.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the musculature of the upper limbs.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia involving the musculature of the upper arm
aplasia / hypoplasia involve the musculature of the upper arm
HP:0001468.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the muscles of the upper arm.

name: abnormal morphology of the pelvis musculature
abnormal morphology of the pelvis musculature
synonym: abnormality of the musculature of the pelvis
abnormality of the musculature of the pelvis

name: sex - limited expression
sex - limited expression
HP:0001470.def: Sex limitation is used to refer to a monogenic trait linked to an autosomal locus in which the phenotypic effects of allelic differences are expressed only in one sex.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
aplasia / hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
sclerotic scapulae
sclerotic scapula
HP:0001474.def: Increased density of the bony tissue of the scapula.

name: male - limited expression
male - limited expression
HP:0001475.def: Used to refer to a monogenic trait linked to an autosomal locus in which the phenotypic effects of allelic differences are expressed only in the male sex.

name: delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle
delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle
HP:0001476.def: A delay in closure (ossification) of the anterior fontanelle, which generally undergoes closure around the 18th month of life.
synonym: delayed closure of the bregma sutures
delayed closure of the bregma suture
delayed closure of the soft spot on the skull
delayed closure of the soft spot on the skull
late closure of large anterior fontanel
late closure of large anterior fontanel
late closure of soft spot on the skull
late closure of soft spot on the skull
late closure of the bregma sutures
late closure of the bregma suture
later than typical closing of soft spot of skull
later than typical closing of soft spot of skull

name: compensatory chin elevation
compensatory chin elevation
HP:0001477.def: A tendency to hold the chin elevated by about 20 to 30 degrees to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

name: freckling
freckle
HP:0001480.def: The presence of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

name: subcutaneous nodule
subcutaneous nodule
HP:0001482.def: Slightly elevated lesions on or in the skin with a diameter of over 5 mm.
synonym: growth of abnormal tissue under the skin
growth of abnormal tissue under the skin

name: eye poking
eye poking
HP:0001483.def: Repetitive pressing, poking, and/or rubbing in the eyes.

name: posterior vitreous detachment
posterior vitreous detachment
HP:0001489.def: Separation of the vitreous humor from the retina.

name: congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles
congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscle
HP:0001491.def: Congenital non-progressive ophthalmoplegia with multiple extraocular muscle restrictions. Typically, there is ptosis and variable degrees of restriction of horizontal and vertical eye movements.
synonym: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscle

name: axenfeld anomaly
axenfeld anomaly
HP:0001492.def: Axenfeld's anomaly is a bilateral disorder characterized by a prominent, anteriorly displaced Schwalbe's line (posterior embryotoxon) and peripheral iris strands which span the anterior chamber angle to attach to Schwalbe's line.

name: falciform retinal fold
falciform retinal fold
HP:0001493.def: An area of the retina that is buckled so that a sector-shaped sheet of retina lies in front of the normal retina. This feature is of congenital onset.

name: carpal bone hypoplasia
carpal bone hypoplasia
HP:0001498.def: Underdevelopment of one or more carpal bones.

name: broad finger
broad finger
HP:0001500.def: Increased width of a non-thumb digit of the hand.

name: failure to thrive
failure to thrive
HP:0001508.def: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

name: growth delay
growth delay
HP:0001510.def: A deficiency or slowing down of growth pre- and postnatally.

name: intrauterine growth retardation
intrauterine growth retardation
HP:0001511.def: An abnormal restriction of fetal growth with fetal weight below the tenth percentile for gestational age.

name: obesity
obesity
HP:0001513.def: Accumulation of substantial excess body fat.

name: small for gestational age
small for gestational age
HP:0001518.def: Smaller than normal size according to sex and gestational age related norms, defined as a weight below the 10th percentile for the gestational age.

name: disproportionate tall stature
disproportionate tall stature
HP:0001519.def: A tall and slim body build with increased arm span to height ratio (>1.05) and a reduced upper-to-lower segment ratio (<0.85), i.e., unusually long arms and legs. The extremities as well as the hands and feet are unusually slim.

name: large for gestational age
large for gestational age
HP:0001520.def: The term large for gestational age applies to babies whose birth weight lies above the 90th percentile for that gestational age.

name: death in infancy
death in infancy
HP:0001522.def: Death within the first 24 months of life.

name: hemihypertrophy
hemihypertrophy
HP:0001528.def: Overgrowth of only one side of the body.

name: mild postnatal growth retardation
mild postnatal growth retardation
HP:0001530.def: A mild degree of slow or limited growth after birth, being between two and three standard deviations below age- and sex-related norms.
synonym: postnatal onset of mild growth retardation
postnatal onset of mild growth retardation

name: failure to thrive in infancy
failure to thrive in infancy
synonym: failure to thrive in first year of life
failure to thrive in first year of life

name: slender build
slender build
HP:0001533.def: Asthenic habitus refers to a slender build with long limbs, an angular profile, and prominent muscles or bones.

name: umbilical hernia
umbilical hernia
HP:0001537.def: Protrusion of abdominal contents through a defect in the abdominal wall musculature around the umbilicus. Skin and subcutaneous tissue overlie the defect.

name: protuberant abdomen
protuberant abdomen
HP:0001538.def: A thrusting or bulging out of the abdomen.

name: omphalocele
omphalocele
HP:0001539.def: A midline anterior incomplete closure of the abdominal wall in which there is herniation of the abdominal viscera into the base of the abdominal cord.

name: diastasis recti
diastasis rectus
HP:0001540.def: A separation of the rectus abdominis muscle into right and left halves (which are normally joined at the midline at the linea alba).
synonym: gap between large left and right abdominal muscles
gap between large left and right abdominal muscle

name: ascites
ascites
HP:0001541.def: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity.
synonym: accumulation of fluid in the abdomen
accumulation of fluid in the abdomen

name: gastroschisis
gastroschisis
HP:0001543.def: A type of congenital ventral incomplete closure of the abdominal wall in which the intestines and sometimes other organs extend freely into the amniotic fluid space through a small opening in the abdomen, usually to the right of the umbilicus.

name: abnormal rib cage morphology
abnormal rib cage morphology
HP:0001547.def: A morphological anomaly of the rib cage.

name: overgrowth
overgrowth
HP:0001548.def: Excessive postnatal growth which may comprise increased weight, increased length, and/or increased head circumference.

name: abnormal umbilicus morphology
abnormal umbilicus morphology
HP:0001551.def: An abnormality of the structure or appearance of the umbilicus.

name: barrel - shaped chest
barrel - shape chest
HP:0001552.def: A rounded, bulging chest that resembles the shape of a barrel. That is, there is an increased anteroposterior diameter and usually some degree of kyphosis.

name: asymmetry of the thorax
asymmetry of the thorax
HP:0001555.def: Lack of symmetry between the left and right halves of the thorax.

name: decreased fetal movement
decrease fetal movement
HP:0001558.def: An abnormal reduction in quantity or strength of fetal movements.
synonym: less than 10 fetal movements in 12 hours
less than 10 fetal movement in 12 hour
less than 10 foetal movements in 12 hours
less than 10 foetal movement in 12 hour

name: abnormality of the amniotic fluid
abnormality of the amniotic fluid
HP:0001560.def: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid, which is the fluid contained in the amniotic sac surrounding the developing fetus.

name: polyhydramnios
polyhydramnios
HP:0001561.def: The presence of excess amniotic fluid in the uterus during pregnancy.

name: oligohydramnios
oligohydramnios
HP:0001562.def: Diminished amniotic fluid volume in pregnancy.

name: fetal polyuria
fetal polyuria
HP:0001563.def: Abnormally increased production of urine by the fetus resulting in polyhydramnios.

name: widely - spaced maxillary central incisors
widely - space maxillary central incisor
HP:0001566.def: Increased distance between the maxillary central permanent incisor tooth.
synonym: wide gap between upper central incisors
wide gap between upper central incisor

name: multiple impacted teeth
multiple impacted teeth
HP:0001571.def: The presence of multiple impacted teeth.

name: macrodontia
macrodontia
HP:0001572.def: Increased size of the teeth, which can be defined as a mesiodistal tooth diameter (width) more than 2 SD above mean for age. Alternatively, an apparently increased maximum width of the tooth.

name: abnormality of the integument
abnormality of the integument
HP:0001574.def: An abnormality of the integument, which consists of the skin and the superficial fascia.

name: primary hypercortisolism
primary hypercortisolism
HP:0001579.def: Hypercortisolemia associated with a primary defect of the adrenal gland leading to overproduction of cortisol.

name: recurrent skin infections
recurrent skin infection
HP:0001581.def: Infections of the skin that happen multiple times.

name: redundant skin
redundant skin
HP:0001582.def: Loose and sagging skin often associated with loss of skin elasticity.

name: rotary nystagmus
rotary nystagmus
HP:0001583.def: A form of nystagmus in which the eyeball makes rotary motions around the axis.

name: vesicovaginal fistula
vesicovaginal fistula
HP:0001586.def: The presence of a fistula connecting the urinary bladder to the vagina.

name: bell - shaped thorax
bell - shape thorax
HP:0001591.def: The rib cage has the shape of a wide mouthed bell. That is, the superior portion of the rib cage is constricted, followed by a convex region, and the inferior portion of the rib cage expands again to have a large diameter.

name: selective tooth agenesis
selective tooth agenesis
HP:0001592.def: Agenesis specifically affecting one of the classes incisor, premolar, or molar.
synonym: failure of development of a tooth
failure of development of a tooth

name: maxillary lateral incisor microdontia
maxillary lateral incisor microdontia
HP:0001593.def: Decreased size of the maxillary permanent incisor.
synonym: decreased size of maxillary lateral incisor
decreased size of maxillary lateral incisor
decreased size of upper lateral incisor
decreased size of upper lateral incisor
decreased width of upper lateral incisor
decrease width of upper lateral incisor

name: alopecia
alopecia
HP:0001596.def: A noncongenital process of hair loss, which may progress to partial or complete baldness.

name: concave nail
concave nail
HP:0001598.def: The natural longitudinal (posterodistal) convex arch is not present or is inverted.

name: laryngomalacia
laryngomalacia
HP:0001601.def: Laryngomalacia is a congenital abnormality of the laryngeal cartilage in which the cartilage is floppy and prolapses over the larynx during inspiration.

name: laryngeal stenosis
laryngeal stenosis
HP:0001602.def: Stricture or narrowing of the larynx that may be associated with symptoms of respiratory difficulty depending on the degree of laryngeal narrowing.

name: vocal cord paresis
vocal cord paresis
HP:0001604.def: Decreased strength of the vocal folds.
synonym: hoarse voice due to vocal cord paresis
hoarse voice due to vocal cord paresis
vocal cord paresis in severe cases
vocal cord paresis in severe case

name: vocal cord paralysis
vocal cord paralysis
HP:0001605.def: A loss of the ability to move the vocal folds.

name: obsolete vocal cord paralysis ( caused by tumor impingement )
obsolete vocal cord paralysis ( cause by tumor impingement )
hoarse voice
hoarse voice
HP:0001609.def: Hoarseness refers to a change in the pitch or quality of the voice, with the voice sounding weak, very breathy, scratchy, or husky.

name: hypernasal speech
hypernasal speech
HP:0001611.def: A type of speech characterized by the presence of an abnormally increased nasal airflow during speech associated with structural abnormality of the nasal passages.

name: obsolete hoarse voice ( caused by tumor impingement )
obsolete hoarse voice ( cause by tumor impingement )
dysphonia
dysphonia
HP:0001618.def: Difficulty in speaking due to a physical disorder of the mouth, tongue, throat, or vocal cords. Associated with a known physical or neurological cause.

name: high pitched voice
high pitch voice
HP:0001620.def: An abnormal increase in the pitch (frequency) of the voice.

name: premature birth
premature birth
HP:0001622.def: The birth of a baby of less than 37 weeks of gestational age.

name: breech presentation
breech presentation
HP:0001623.def: A position of the fetus at delivery in which the fetus enters the birth canal with the buttocks or feet first.
synonym: feet or buttocks of fetus positioned near opening of uterus
foot or buttock of fetus position near opening of uterus
feet or buttocks of foetus positioned near opening of uterus
foot or buttock of foetus position near opening of uterus

name: abnormality of the cardiovascular system
abnormality of the cardiovascular system
HP:0001626.def: Any abnormality of the cardiovascular system.

name: abnormal heart morphology
abnormal heart morphology
HP:0001627.def: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

name: ventricular septal defect
ventricular septal defect
HP:0001629.def: A hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.
synonym: hole in heart wall separating two lower heart chambers
hole in heart wall separate two low heart chamber

name: atrial septal defect
atrial septal defect
HP:0001631.def: Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum.
synonym: an opening in the wall separating the top two chambers of the heart
an opening in the wall separate the top two chamber of the heart
hole in heart wall separating two upper heart chambers
hole in heart wall separate two upper heart chamber

name: abnormal mitral valve morphology
abnormal mitral valve morphology
HP:0001633.def: Any structural anomaly of the mitral valve.

name: mitral valve prolapse
mitral valve prolapse
HP:0001634.def: One or both of the leaflets (cusps) of the mitral valve bulges back into the left atrium upon contraction of the left ventricle.

name: congestive heart failure
congestive heart failure
HP:0001635.def: The presence of an abnormality of cardiac function that is responsible for the failure of the heart to pump blood at a rate that is commensurate with the needs of the tissues or a state in which abnormally elevated filling pressures are required for the heart to do so. Heart failure is frequently related to a defect in myocardial contraction.

name: tetralogy of fallot
tetralogy of fallot
HP:0001636.def: A congenital cardiac malformation comprising pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy. The diagnosis of TOF is made if at least three of the four above mentioned features are present.

name: abnormal myocardium morphology
abnormal myocardium morphology
HP:0001637.def: A structural anomaly of the muscle layer of the heart wall.

name: cardiomyopathy
cardiomyopathy
HP:0001638.def: A myocardial disorder in which the heart muscle is structurally and functionally abnormal, in the absence of coronary artery disease, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital heart disease sufficient to cause the observed myocardial abnormality.

name: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
HP:0001639.def: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is defined by the presence of increased ventricular wall thickness or mass in the absence of loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) sufficient to cause the observed abnormality.

name: cardiomegaly
cardiomegaly
HP:0001640.def: Increased size of the heart, clinically defined as an increased transverse diameter of the cardiac silhouette that is greater than or equal to 50% of the transverse diameter of the chest (increased cardiothoracic ratio) on a posterior-anterior projection of a chest radiograph or a computed tomography.

name: abnormal pulmonary valve morphology
abnormal pulmonary valve morphology
HP:0001641.def: Any structural abnormality of the pulmonary valve.

name: pulmonic stenosis
pulmonic stenosis
HP:0001642.def: A narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract that can occur at the pulmonary valve (valvular stenosis), below the pulmonary valve (infundibular stenosis), or above the pulmonary valve (supravalvar stenosis).

name: patent ductus arteriosus
patent ductus arteriosus
HP:0001643.def: In utero, the ductus arteriosus (DA) serves to divert ventricular output away from the lungs and toward the placenta by connecting the main pulmonary artery to the descending aorta. A patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the first 3 days of life is a physiologic shunt in healthy term and preterm newborn infants, and normally is substantially closed within about 24 hours after bith and completely closed after about three weeks. Failure of physiologcal closure is referred to a persistent or patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Depending on the degree of left-to-right shunting, PDA can have clinical consequences.

name: dilated cardiomyopathy
dilate cardiomyopathy
HP:0001644.def: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is defined by the presence of left ventricular dilatation and left ventricular systolic dysfunction in the absence of abnormal loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) or coronary artery disease sufficient to cause global systolic impairment. Right ventricular dilation and dysfunction may be present but are not necessary for the diagnosis.

name: sudden cardiac death
sudden cardiac death
HP:0001645.def: The heart suddenly and unexpectedly stops beating resulting in death within a short time period (generally within 1 h of symptom onset).

name: abnormal aortic valve morphology
abnormal aortic valve morphology
HP:0001646.def: Any abnormality of the aortic valve.

name: bicuspid aortic valve
bicuspid aortic valve
HP:0001647.def: The presence of an aortic valve with two instead of the normal three cusps (flaps). Bicuspid aortic valvue is a malformation of a commissure (small space between the attachment of each cusp to the aortic wall) and the adjacent parts of the two corresponding cusps forming a raphe (the fused area of the two underdeveloped cusps turning into a malformed commissure between both cusps; the raphe is a fibrous ridge that extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps).
synonym: aortic valve has two leaflets rather than three
aortic valve have two leaflet rather than three

name: cor pulmonale
cor pulmonale
HP:0001648.def: Right-sided heart failure resulting from chronic hypertension in the pulmonary arteries and right ventricle.

name: tachycardia
tachycardia
HP:0001649.def: A rapid heartrate that exceeds the range of the normal resting heartrate for age.

name: aortic valve stenosis
aortic valve stenosis
HP:0001650.def: The presence of a stenosis (narrowing) of the aortic valve.

name: dextrocardia
dextrocardia
HP:0001651.def: The heart is located in the right hand sided hemithorax. That is, there is a left-right reversal (or \"mirror reflection\") of the anatomical location of the heart in which the heart is locate on the right side instead of the left.
synonym: heart tip and four chambers point towards right side of body
heart tip and four chamber point towards right side of body

name: mitral regurgitation
mitral regurgitation
HP:0001653.def: An abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by insufficiency or incompetence of the mitral valve resulting in retrograde leaking of blood through the mitral valve upon ventricular contraction.

name: abnormal heart valve morphology
abnormal heart valve morphology
HP:0001654.def: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac valve.

name: patent foramen ovale
patent foramen ovale
HP:0001655.def: Failure of the foramen ovale to seal postnatally, leaving a potential conduit between the left and right cardiac atria.

name: prolonged qt interval
prolonged qt interval
HP:0001657.def: Increased time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).

name: myocardial infarction
myocardial infarction
HP:0001658.def: Necrosis of the myocardium caused by an obstruction of the blood supply to the heart and often associated with chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, and anxiety as well as characteristic EKG findings and elevation of serum markers including creatine kinase-MB fraction and troponin.

name: aortic regurgitation
aortic regurgitation
HP:0001659.def: An insufficiency of the aortic valve, leading to regurgitation (backward flow) of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle.

name: truncus arteriosus
truncus arteriosus
HP:0001660.def: A single arterial trunk arises from the cardiac mass. The pulmonary arteries, aorta and coronary arteries arise from this single trunk with no evidence of another outflow tract.

name: bradycardia
bradycardia
HP:0001662.def: A slower than normal heart rate (in adults, slower than 60 beats per minute).

name: ventricular fibrillation
ventricular fibrillation
HP:0001663.def: Uncontrolled contractions of muscles fibers in the left ventricle not producing contraction of the left ventricle. Ventricular fibrillation usually begins with a ventricular premature contraction and a short run of rapid ventricular tachycardia degenerating into uncoordinating ventricular fibrillations.

name: torsade de pointes
torsade de pointes
HP:0001664.def: A type of ventricular tachycardia characterized by polymorphioc QRS complexes that change in amplitue and cycle length, and thus have the appearance of oscillating around the baseline in the EKG.

name: right ventricular hypertrophy
right ventricular hypertrophy
HP:0001667.def: In this case the right ventricle is more muscular than normal, causing a characteristic boot-shaped (coeur-en-sabot) appearance as seen on anterior- posterior chest x-rays. Right ventricular hypertrophy is commonly associated with any form of right ventricular outflow obstruction or pulmonary hypertension, which may in turn owe its origin to left-sided disease. The echocardiographic signs are thickening of the anterior right ventricular wall and the septum. Cavity size is usually normal, or slightly enlarged. In many cases there is associated volume overload present due to tricuspid regurgitation, in the absence of this, septal motion is normal.

name: transposition of the great arteries
transposition of the great artery
HP:0001669.def: A complex congenital heart defect in which the aorta arises from the morphologic right ventricle and the pulmonary artery arises from the morphologic left ventricle.

name: asymmetric septal hypertrophy
asymmetric septal hypertrophy
HP:0001670.def: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an asymmetrical pattern of hypertrophy, with a predilection for the interventricular septum and myocyte disarray.

name: abnormal cardiac septum morphology
abnormal cardiac septum morphology
HP:0001671.def: An anomaly of the intra-atrial or intraventricular septum.

name: complete atrioventricular canal defect
complete atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0001674.def: A congenital heart defect characterized by a specific combination of heart defects with a common atrioventricular valve, primum atrial septal defect and inlet ventricular septal defect.

name: obsolete rhythm disturbances associated with pheochromocytoma
obsolete rhythm disturbance associate with pheochromocytoma
coronary artery atherosclerosis
coronary artery atherosclerosis
HP:0001677.def: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries, which increases the risk of myocardial ischemia.
synonym: plaque build - up in arteries supplying blood to heart
plaque build - up in artery supply blood to heart

name: atrioventricular block
atrioventricular block
HP:0001678.def: Delayed or lack of conduction of atrial depolarizations through the atrioventricular node to the ventricles.
synonym: interruption of electrical communication between upper and lower chambers of heart
interruption of electrical communication between upper and low chamber of heart

name: coarctation of aorta
coarctation of aorta
HP:0001680.def: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the aorta.

name: angina pectoris
angina pectoris
HP:0001681.def: Paroxysmal chest pain that occurs with exertion or stress and is related to myocardial ischemia.

name: subvalvular aortic stenosis
subvalvular aortic stenosis
HP:0001682.def: A fixed form of obstruction to blood flow across the left-ventricular outflow tract related to stenosis (narrowing) below the level of the aortic valve.
synonym: narrowing of blood vessel below aortic heart valve
narrowing of blood vessel below aortic heart valve

name: ectopia cordis
ectopia cordis
HP:0001683.def: Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and through the defect in the ventral wall.

name: secundum atrial septal defect
secundum atrial septal defect
HP:0001684.def: A kind of atrial septum defect arising from an enlarged foramen ovale, inadequate growth of the septum secundum, or excessive absorption of the septum primum.
synonym: atrial septal defect , ostium secundum type
atrial septal defect , ostium secundum type

name: myocardial fibrosis
myocardial fibrosis
HP:0001685.def: Myocardial fibrosis is characterized by dysregulated collagen turnover (increased synthesis predominates over unchanged or decreased degradation) and excessive diffuse collagen accumulation in the interstitial and perivascular spaces as well as by phenotypically transformed fibroblasts, termed myofibroblasts.

name: sinus bradycardia
sinus bradycardia
HP:0001688.def: Bradycardia related to a mean resting sinus rate of less than 50 beats per minute.

name: muscular subvalvular aortic stenosis
muscular subvalvular aortic stenosis
HP:0001691.def: A type of subvalvular aortic stenosis resulting from thickening of the musculature of the interventricular septum, which results in obstruction to blood flow through the left-ventricular outflow tract.

name: atrial arrhythmia
atrial arrhythmia
HP:0001692.def: A type of supraventricular tachycardia in which the atria are the principal site of electrophysiologic disturbance.

name: cardiac shunt
cardiac shunt
HP:0001693.def: Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system.

name: right - to - left shunt
right - to - left shunt
HP:0001694.def: Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from the right side of the heart to the left.

name: cardiac arrest
cardiac arrest
HP:0001695.def: An abrupt loss of heart function.

name: situs inversus totalis
situs inversus totalis
HP:0001696.def: A left-right reversal (or \"mirror reflection\") of the anatomical location of the major thoracic and abdominal organs.
synonym: all organs on wrong side of body
all organ on wrong side of body

name: abnormal pericardium morphology
abnormal pericardium morphology
HP:0001697.def: An abnormality of the pericardium, i.e., of the fluid filled sac that surrounds the heart and the proximal ends of the aorta, vena cava, and the pulmonary artery.

name: pericardial effusion
pericardial effusion
HP:0001698.def: Accumulation of fluid within the pericardium.

name: myocardial necrosis
myocardial necrosis
HP:0001700.def: Irreversible damage to heart tissue (myocardium) due to lack of oxygen after a heart attack (myocardial infarction).

name: pericarditis
pericarditis
HP:0001701.def: Inflammation of the sac-like covering around the heart (pericardium).
synonym: swelling or irritation of membrane around heart
swell or irritation of membrane around heart

name: abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
HP:0001702.def: Any structural anomaly of the tricuspid valve.

name: tricuspid valve prolapse
tricuspid valve prolapse
HP:0001704.def: One or more of the leaflets (cusps) of the tricuspid valve bulges back into the right atrium upon contraction of the right ventricle.

name: right ventricular outlet tract obstruction
right ventricular outlet tract obstruction
HP:0001705.def: An obstruction to the forward flow of blood in the outflow tract of the right ventricle.

name: endocardial fibroelastosis
endocardial fibroelastosis
HP:0001706.def: Diffuse thickening of the ventricular endocardium and by associated myocardial dysfunction

name: abnormal right ventricle morphology
abnormal right ventricle morphology
HP:0001707.def: An abnormality of the right ventricle of the heart.

name: right ventricular failure
right ventricular failure
HP:0001708.def: Reduced ability of the right ventricle to perform its function (to receive blood from the right atrium and to eject blood into the pulmonary artery), often leading to pitting peripheral edema, ascites, and hepatomegaly.

name: third degree atrioventricular block
third degree atrioventricular block
HP:0001709.def: Third-degree atrioventricular (AV) block (also referred to as complete heart block) is the complete dissociation of the atria and the ventricles. Third-degree AV block exists when more P waves than QRS complexes exist and no relationship (no conduction) exists between them.

name: conotruncal defect
conotruncal defect
HP:0001710.def: A congenital malformation of the outflow tract of the heart. Conotruncal defects are thought to result from a disturbance of the outflow tract of the embryonic heart, and comprise truncus arteriosus, tetralogy of Fallot, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of the great arteries, and double outlet right ventricle.

name: abnormal left ventricle morphology
abnormal leave ventricle morphology
HP:0001711.def: Any structural abnormality of the left ventricle of the heart.

name: left ventricular hypertrophy
leave ventricular hypertrophy
HP:0001712.def: Enlargement or increased size of the heart left ventricle.

name: abnormal cardiac ventricle morphology
abnormal cardiac ventricle morphology
HP:0001713.def: An abnormality of a cardiac ventricle.

name: ventricular hypertrophy
ventricular hypertrophy
HP:0001714.def: Enlargement of the cardiac ventricular muscle tissue with increase in the width of the wall of the ventricle and loss of elasticity. Ventricular hypertrophy is clinically differentiated into left and right ventricular hypertrophy.

name: wolff - parkinson - white syndrome
wolff - parkinson - white syndrome
HP:0001716.def: A disorder of the cardiac conduction system of the heart characterized by ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of an abnormal accessory atrioventricular electrical conduction pathway.

name: coronary artery calcification
coronary artery calcification
HP:0001717.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a coronary artery.

name: mitral stenosis
mitral stenosis
HP:0001718.def: An abnormal narrowing of the orifice of the mitral valve.

name: double outlet right ventricle
double outlet right ventricle
HP:0001719.def: Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) is a type of ventriculoarterial connection in which both great vessels arise entirely or predominantly from the right ventricle.

name: high - output congestive heart failure
high - output congestive heart failure
HP:0001722.def: A form of heart failure characterized by elevated cardiac output. This may be seen in patients with heart failure and hyperthyroidism, anemia, pregnancy, arteriovenous fistulae, and others.

name: restrictive cardiomyopathy
restrictive cardiomyopathy
HP:0001723.def: Restrictive left ventricular physiology is characterized by a pattern of ventricular filling in which increased stiffness of the myocardium causes ventricular pressure to rise precipitously with only small increases in volume, defined as restrictive ventricular physiology in the presence of normal or reduced diastolic volumes (of one or both ventricles), normal or reduced systolic volumes, and normal ventricular wall thickness.

name: obsolete increased prevalence of valvular disease
obsolete increase prevalence of valvular disease
thromboembolic stroke
thromboembolic stroke
HP:0001727.def: A cerebrovascular accident (stroke) that occurs because of thromboembolism.

name: progressive hearing impairment
progressive hearing impairment
HP:0001730.def: A progressive form of hearing impairment.

name: pancreatitis
pancreatitis
HP:0001733.def: The presence of inflammation in the pancreas.

name: annular pancreas
annular pancreas
HP:0001734.def: A congenital anomaly in which the pancreas completely (or sometimes incompletely) encircles the second portion of duodenum and occasionally obstructs the more proximal duodenum.

name: pancreatic cysts
pancreatic cyst
HP:0001737.def: A cyst of the pancreas that possess a lining of mucous epithelium.

name: exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
HP:0001738.def: Impaired function of the exocrine pancreas associated with a reduced ability to digest foods because of lack of digestive enzymes.
synonym: inability to properly digest food due to lack of pancreatic digestive enzymes
inability to properly digest food due to lack of pancreatic digestive enzyme

name: abnormal nasopharynx morphology
abnormal nasopharynx morphology
HP:0001739.def: A structural anomaly of the nasopharynx.

name: phimosis
phimosis
HP:0001741.def: The male foreskin cannot be fully retracted from the head of the penis.

name: nasal congestion
nasal congestion
HP:0001742.def: Reduced ability to pass air through the nasal cavity often leading to mouth breathing.

name: splenomegaly
splenomegaly
HP:0001744.def: Abnormal increased size of the spleen.

name: accessory spleen
accessory spleen
HP:0001747.def: An accessory spleen is a round, iso-echogenic, homogenic and smooth structure and is seen as a normal variant mostly on the medial contour of the spleen, near the hilus or around the lower pole. This has no pathogenic relevance.

name: polysplenia
polysplenia
HP:0001748.def: Polysplenia is a congenital disease manifested by multiple small accessory spleens.

name: single ventricle
single ventricle
HP:0001750.def: The presence of only one working lower chamber in the heart, usually with a virtual absence of the ventricular septum and usually present in conjunction with double inlet left or right ventricle.

name: abnormal vestibular function
abnormal vestibular function
HP:0001751.def: An abnormality of the functioning of the vestibular apparatus.

name: vestibular hypofunction
vestibular hypofunction
HP:0001756.def: A general descriptive term that describes impaired functioning of the vestibular apparatus that leads to manifestations such as dizziness or postural imbalance

name: high - frequency sensorineural hearing impairment
high - frequency sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0001757.def: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects primarily the higher frequencies.

name: abnormal foot morphology
abnormal foot morphology
HP:0001760.def: An abnormality of the skeleton of foot.

name: pes cavus
pe cavus
HP:0001761.def: An increase in height of the medial longitudinal arch of the foot that does not flatten on weight bearing (i.e., a distinctly hollow form of the sole of the foot when it is bearing weight).

name: talipes equinovarus
talipes equinovarus
HP:0001762.def: Talipes equinovarus (also called clubfoot) typically has four main components: inversion and adduction of the forefoot; inversion of the heel and hindfoot; equinus (limitation of extension) of the ankle and subtalar joint; and internal rotation of the leg.

name: pes planus
pe planus
HP:0001763.def: A foot where the longitudinal arch of the foot is in contact with the ground or floor when the individual is standing; or, in a patient lying supine, a foot where the arch is in contact with the surface of a flat board pressed against the sole of the foot by the examiner with a pressure similar to that expected from weight bearing; or, the height of the arch is reduced.

name: hammertoe
hammertoe
HP:0001765.def: Hyperextension of the metatarsal-phalangeal joint with hyperflexion of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint.

name: broad foot
broad foot
HP:0001769.def: A foot for which the measured width is above the 95th centile for age; or, a foot that appears disproportionately wide for its length.

name: toe syndactyly
toe syndactyly
HP:0001770.def: Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as \"bony\

name: achilles tendon contracture
achilles tendon contracture
HP:0001771.def: A contracture of the Achilles tendon.

name: talipes equinovalgus
talipes equinovalgus
HP:0001772.def: A deformity of foot and ankle in which the foot is bent down and outwards.

name: short foot
short foot
HP:0001773.def: A measured foot length that is more than 2 SD below the mean for a newborn of 27 - 41 weeks gestation, or foot that is less than the 3rd centile for individuals from birth to 16 years of age (objective). Alternatively, a foot that appears disproportionately short (subjective).

name: bulbous tips of toes
bulbous tip of toe
HP:0001782.def: An abnormality of the morphology of the toes, such that the tips of the toes are prominent and bulbous.

name: broad metatarsal
broad metatarsal
HP:0001783.def: Increased side-to-side width of a metatarsal bone.

name: narrow foot
narrow foot
HP:0001786.def: A foot for which the measured width is below the 5th centile for age; or, a foot that appears disproportionately narrow for its length.

name: abnormal delivery
abnormal delivery
HP:0001787.def: An abnormality of the birth process.

name: premature rupture of membranes
premature rupture of membrane
HP:0001788.def: Premature rupture of membranes (PROM) is a condition which occurs in pregnancy when the amniotic sac ruptures more than an hour before the onset of labor.

name: hydrops fetalis
hydrops fetalis
HP:0001789.def: The abnormal accumulation of fluid in two or more fetal compartments, including ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and skin edema.

name: nonimmune hydrops fetalis
nonimmune hydrops fetalis
HP:0001790.def: A type of hydrops fetalis in which there is no identifiable circulating antibody to red blood cell antigens .

name: fetal ascites
fetal ascites
HP:0001791.def: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity during the fetal period.

name: small nail
small nail
HP:0001792.def: A nail that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail.

name: hyperconvex nail
hyperconvex nail
HP:0001795.def: When viewed on end (with the digit tip pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the nail forms a tighter curve of convexity.

name: nail pits
nail pit
HP:0001803.def: Small (typically about 1 mm or less in size) depressions on the dorsal nail surface.

name: onychogryposis
onychogryposis
HP:0001805.def: Nail that appears thick when viewed on end.

name: onycholysis
onycholysis
HP:0001806.def: Detachment of the nail from the nail bed.

name: ridged nail
ridge nail
HP:0001807.def: Longitudinal, linear prominences in the nail plate.

name: split nail
split nail
HP:0001809.def: A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation and the two sections of the nail share the same lateral radius of curvature.

name: dystrophic toenail
dystrophic toenail
HP:0001810.def: Toenail changes apart from changes of the color of the toenail (nail dyschromia) that involve partial or complete disruption of the various keratinous layers of the nail plate.

name: hyperconvex fingernails
hyperconvex fingernail
HP:0001812.def: When viewed on end (with the finger tip pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the fingernail forms a tighter curve of convexity.

name: thin nail
thin nail
HP:0001816.def: Nail that appears thin when viewed on end.

name: paronychia
paronychia
HP:0001818.def: The nail disease paronychia is an often-tender bacterial or fungal hand infection or foot infection where the nail and skin meet at the side or the base of a finger or toenail. The infection can start suddenly (acute paronychia) or gradually (chronic paronychia).

name: hallux valgus
hallux valgus
HP:0001822.def: Lateral deviation of the great toe (i.e., in the direction of the little toe).

name: genital tract atresia
genital tract atresia
HP:0001827.def: Congenital occlusion of a tube in the genital tract.

name: foot polydactyly
foot polydactyly
HP:0001829.def: A kind of polydactyly characterized by the presence of a supernumerary toe or toes.
synonym: duplication of bones of the toes
duplication of bone of the toe

name: postaxial foot polydactyly
postaxial foot polydactyly
HP:0001830.def: Polydactyly of the foot most commonly refers to the presence of six toes on one foot. Postaxial polydactyly affects the lateral ray and the duplication may range from a well-formed articulated digit to a rudimentary digit.
synonym: extra toe attached near the little toe
extra toe attach near the little toe

name: short toe
short toe
HP:0001831.def: A toe that appears disproportionately short compared to the foot.

name: abnormal metatarsal morphology
abnormal metatarsal morphology
