HP:0001832.def: Abnormalities of the metatarsal bones (i.e. of five tubular bones located between the tarsal bones of the hind- and mid-foot and the phalanges of the toes).
synonym: abnormality of the long bone of foot
abnormality of the long bone of foot

name: long foot
long foot
HP:0001833.def: Increased back to front length of the foot.

name: camptodactyly of toe
camptodactyly of toe
HP:0001836.def: Camptodactyly is a painless flexion contracture of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint that is usually gradually progressive. This term refers to camptodactyly of one or more toes.

name: broad toe
broad toe
HP:0001837.def: Visible increase in width of the non-hallux digit without an increase in the dorso-ventral dimension.

name: rocker bottom foot
rocker bottom foot
HP:0001838.def: The presence of both a prominent heel and a convex contour of the sole.

name: split foot
split foot
HP:0001839.def: A condition in which middle parts of the foot (toes and metatarsals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic 3rd toe over absent 2nd or 3rd toes as far as oligo- or monodactyl feet.

name: metatarsus adductus
metatarsus adductus
HP:0001840.def: The metatarsals are deviated medially (tibially), that is, the bones in the front half of the foot bend or turn in toward the body.
synonym: front half of foot turns inward
front half of foot turn inward

name: preaxial foot polydactyly
preaxial foot polydactyly
HP:0001841.def: Duplication of all or part of the first ray.
synonym: partial / complete duplication of the phalanges of the big toe
partial / complete duplication of the phalanx of the big toe

name: abnormal hallux morphology
abnormal hallux morphology
HP:0001844.def: This term applies for all abnormalities of the big toe, also called hallux.

name: overlapping toe
overlap toe
HP:0001845.def: Describes a foot digit resting on the dorsal surface of an adjacent digit when the foot is at rest. Initially clawing may be dynamic and only noticeable on walking. Over time the plantar plate tears, subluxation occurs at the metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ), and the deformity becomes permanent.

name: long hallux
long hallux
HP:0001847.def: Increased length of the big toe.

name: calcaneovalgus deformity
calcaneovalgus deformity
HP:0001848.def: This is a postural deformity in which the foot is positioned up against the tibia. The heel (calcaneus) is positioned downward (that is, the ankle is flexed upward), and the heel is turned outward (valgus).
synonym: foot and ankle bend up toward shin of leg
foot and ankle bend up toward shin of leg

name: foot oligodactyly
foot oligodactyly
HP:0001849.def: A developmental defect resulting in the presence of fewer than the normal number of toes.

name: abnormality of the tarsal bones
abnormality of the tarsal bone
HP:0001850.def: An abnormality of the tarsus are the cluster of seven bones in the foot between the tibia and fibula and the metatarsus, including the calcaneus (heel) bone and the talus (ankle) bone.

name: sandal gap
sandal gap
HP:0001852.def: A widely spaced gap between the first toe (the great toe) and the second toe.
synonym: gap between first and second toe
gap between first and second toe
increased space between first and second toes
increase space between first and second toe
sandal gap between first and second toes
sandal gap between first and second toe
space between great toe and second toe
space between great toe and second toe
wide space between first and second toes
wide space between first and second toe
widely spaced first and second toes
widely space first and second toe
widened gap first and second toe
widen gap first and second toe

name: podagra
podagra
HP:0001854.def: Gout affecting the Metatarsophalangeal joint of big toe.

name: short distal phalanx of toe
short distal phalanx of toe
HP:0001857.def: Short distance from the end of the toe to the most distal interphalangeal crease or distal interphalangeal joint flexion point, i.e., abnormally short distal phalanx of toe.

name: obsolete acral ulceration and osteomyelitis leading to autoamputation of the digits ( feet )
obsolete acral ulceration and osteomyelitis lead to autoamputation of the digit ( foot )
toe clinodactyly
toe clinodactyly
HP:0001863.def: Bending or curvature of a toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

name: clinodactyly of the 5th toe
clinodactyly of the 5th toe
HP:0001864.def: Bending or curvature of a fifth toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

name: autoamputation of foot
autoamputation of foot
HP:0001868.def: The spontaneous detachment of a foot from the body due to long standing pathology.

name: deep plantar creases
deep plantar crease
HP:0001869.def: The presence of unusually deep creases (ridges/wrinkles) on the skin of sole of foot.
synonym: deep wrinkles in soles of feet
deep wrinkle in sol of foot

name: acroosteolysis of distal phalanges ( feet )
acroosteolysis of distal phalanx ( foot )
synonym: acroosteolysis of distal phalanges of feet
acroosteolysis of distal phalanx of foot

name: abnormality of blood and blood - forming tissues
abnormality of blood and blood - forming tissue
HP:0001871.def: An abnormality of the hematopoietic system.
synonym: abnormality of blood and blood - forming tissues
abnormality of blood and blood - forming tissue

name: thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia
HP:0001873.def: A reduction in the number of circulating thrombocytes.

name: neutropenia
neutropenia
HP:0001875.def: An abnormally low number of neutrophils in the peripheral blood.

name: pancytopenia
pancytopenia
HP:0001876.def: An abnormal reduction in numbers of all blood cell types (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets).

name: abnormal erythrocyte morphology
abnormal erythrocyte morphology
HP:0001877.def: Any structural abnormality of erythrocytes (red-blood cells).

name: hemolytic anemia
hemolytic anemia
HP:0001878.def: A type of anemia caused by premature destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis).

name: abnormal eosinophil morphology
abnormal eosinophil morphology
HP:0001879.def: An abnormal count or structure of eosinophils.

name: eosinophilia
eosinophilia
HP:0001880.def: Increased count of eosinophils in the blood.

name: leukopenia
leukopenia
HP:0001882.def: An abnormal decreased number of leukocytes in the blood.

name: talipes
talipes
HP:0001883.def: A deformity of foot and ankle that has different subtypes that are talipes equinovarus, talipes equinovalgus, talipes calcaneovarus and talipes calcaneovalgus.

name: talipes calcaneovalgus
talipes calcaneovalgus
HP:0001884.def: Talipes calcaneovalgus is a flexible foot deformity (as opposed to a rigid congenital vertical talus foot deformity) that can either present as a positional or structural foot deformity depending on severity and/or causality. The axis of calcaneovalgus deformity is in the tibiotalar joint, where the foot is positioned in extreme hyperextension. On inspection, the foot has an \"up and out\

name: foot osteomyelitis
foot osteomyelitis
HP:0001886.def: An infection of bone of the foot.

name: lymphopenia
lymphopenia
HP:0001888.def: A reduced number of lymphocytes in the blood.

name: megaloblastic anemia
megaloblastic anemia
HP:0001889.def: Anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal (megaloblasts).

name: autoimmune hemolytic anemia
autoimmune hemolytic anemia
HP:0001890.def: An autoimmune form of hemolytic anemia.

name: abnormal bleeding
abnormal bleeding
HP:0001892.def: An abnormal susceptibility to bleeding, often referred to as a bleeding diathesis. A bleeding diathesis may be related to vascular, platelet and coagulation defects.

name: thrombocytosis
thrombocytosis
HP:0001894.def: Increased numbers of platelets in the peripheral blood.
synonym: increased number of platelets in blood
increased number of platelet in blood

name: reticulocytopenia
reticulocytopenia
HP:0001896.def: A reduced number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood.

name: normocytic anemia
normocytic anemia
HP:0001897.def: A kind of anemia in which the volume of the red blood cells is normal.

name: increased red blood cell mass
increase red blood cell mass
HP:0001898.def: The presence of an increased mass of red blood cells in the circulation.

name: increased hematocrit
increase hematocrit
HP:0001899.def: An elevation above the normal ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

name: polycythemia
polycythemia
HP:0001901.def: Polycythemia is diagnosed if the red blood cell count, the hemoglobin level, and the red blood cell volume all exceed the upper limits of normal.

name: giant platelets
giant platelet
HP:0001902.def: Giant platelets are larger than 7 micrometers and usually 10 to 20 micrometers. The term giant platelet is used when the platelet is larger than the size of the average red cell in the field. (Description adapted from College of American Pathologists, Hematology Manual, 1998).

name: anemia
anemia
HP:0001903.def: A reduction in erythrocytes volume or hemoglobin concentration.
synonym: low number of red blood cells or haemoglobin
low number of red blood cell or haemoglobin
low number of red blood cells or hemoglobin
low number of red blood cell or hemoglobin

name: neutropenia in presence of anti - neutropil antibodies
neutropenia in presence of anti - neutropil antibody
HP:0001904.def: A type of neutropenia that is observed in the presence of granulocyte-specific antibodies.

name: thromboembolism
thromboembolism
HP:0001907.def: The formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel that subsequently travels through the blood stream from the site where it formed to another location in the body, generally leading to vascular occlusion at the distant site.

name: hypoplastic anemia
hypoplastic anemia
HP:0001908.def: Anemia with varying degrees of erythrocytic hypoplasia without leukopenia or thrombocytopenia.

name: leukemia
leukemia
HP:0001909.def: A cancer of the blood and bone marrow characterized by an abnormal proliferation of leukocytes.

name: abnormal granulocyte morphology
abnormal granulocyte morphology
HP:0001911.def: Any structural abnormality or abnormal count of granulocytes.

name: abnormal basophil morphology
abnormal basophil morphology
HP:0001912.def: Any structural abnormality or abnormal count of basophils.

name: granulocytopenia
granulocytopenia
HP:0001913.def: An abnormally reduced number of granulocytes in the blood.

name: aplastic anemia
aplastic anemia
HP:0001915.def: Aplastic anemia is defined as pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow.

name: renal amyloidosis
renal amyloidosis
HP:0001917.def: A form of amyloidosis that affects the kidney. On hematoxylin and eosin stain, amyloid is identified as extracellular amorphous material that is lightly eosinophilic. These deposits often stain weakly for periodic acid Schiff (PAS), demonstrate a blue-to-gray hue on the trichrome stain and are typically negative on the Jones methenamine silver (JMS) stain. These tinctorial properties contrast with the histologic appearance of collagen, a major component of basement membranes, mesangial matrix and areas of sclerosis, which demonstrates strong positivity for PAS and JMS (See Figure 1 of PMID:25852856).

name: acute kidney injury
acute kidney injury
HP:0001919.def: Sudden loss of renal function, as manifested by decreased urine production, and a rise in serum creatinine or blood urea nitrogen concentration (azotemia).

name: renal artery stenosis
renal artery stenosis
HP:0001920.def: The presence of stenosis of the renal artery.

name: vacuolated lymphocytes
vacuolated lymphocyte
HP:0001922.def: The presence of clear, sharply defined vacuoles in the lymphocyte cytoplasm.

name: reticulocytosis
reticulocytosis
HP:0001923.def: An elevation in the number of reticulocytes (immature erythrocytes) in the peripheral blood circulation.
synonym: increased number of immature red blood cells
increased number of immature red blood cell

name: sideroblastic anemia
sideroblastic anemia
HP:0001924.def: Sideroblastic anemia results from a defect in the incorporation of iron into the heme molecule. A sideroblast is an erythroblast that has stainable deposits of iron in cytoplasm (this can be demonstrated by Prussian blue staining).

name: acanthocytosis
acanthocytosis
HP:0001927.def: Acanthocytosis is a type of poikilocytosis characterized by the presence of spikes on the cell surface. The cells have an irregular shape resembling many-pointed stars.

name: abnormality of coagulation
abnormality of coagulation
HP:0001928.def: An abnormality of the process of blood coagulation. That is, altered ability or inability of the blood to clot.

name: reduced factor xi activity
reduce factor xi activity
HP:0001929.def: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XI. Factor XI, also known as plasma thromboplastin antecedent, is a serine proteinase that activates factor IX.

name: hypochromic anemia
hypochromic anemia
HP:0001931.def: A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes.

name: subcutaneous hemorrhage
subcutaneous hemorrhage
HP:0001933.def: This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to bruising (purpura, petechiae, or ecchymoses).

name: microcytic anemia
microcytic anemia
HP:0001935.def: A kind of anemia in which the volume of the red blood cells is reduced.

name: acidosis
acidosis
HP:0001941.def: Abnormal acid accumulation or depletion of base.

name: metabolic acidosis
metabolic acidosis
HP:0001942.def: Metabolic acidosis (MA) is characterized by a fall in blood pH due to a reduction of serum bicarbonate concentration. This can occur as a result of either the accumulation of acids (high anion gap MA) or the loss of bicarbonate from the gastrointestinal tract or the kidney (hyperchloremic MA). By definition, MA is not due to a respirary cause.

name: hypoglycemia
hypoglycemia
HP:0001943.def: A decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

name: fever
fever
HP:0001945.def: Body temperature elevated above the normal range.

name: ketosis
ketosis
HP:0001946.def: Presence of elevated levels of ketone bodies in the body.

name: renal tubular acidosis
renal tubular acidosis
HP:0001947.def: Acidosis owing to malfunction of the kidney tubules with accumulation of metabolic acids and hyperchloremia, potentially leading to complications including hypokalemia, hypercalcinuria, nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis.
synonym: accumulation of acid in body due to kidney problem
accumulation of acid in body due to kidney problem

name: alkalosis
alkalosis
HP:0001948.def: Depletion of acid or accumulation base in the body fluids.

name: respiratory alkalosis
respiratory alkalosis
HP:0001950.def: Alkalosis due to excess loss of carbon dioxide from the body.

name: glucose intolerance
glucose intolerance
HP:0001952.def: Glucose intolerance (GI) can be defined as dysglycemia that comprises both prediabetes and diabetes. It includes the conditions of impaired fasting glucose (IFG) and impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) and diabetes mellitus (DM).

name: diabetic ketoacidosis
diabetic ketoacidosis
HP:0001953.def: A type of diabetic metabolic abnormality with an accumulation of ketone bodies.

name: recurrent fever
recurrent fever
HP:0001954.def: Periodic (episodic or recurrent) bouts of fever.

name: unexplained fevers
unexplained fever
HP:0001955.def: Episodes of fever for which no infectious cause can be identified.

name: truncal obesity
truncal obesity
HP:0001956.def: Obesity located preferentially in the trunk of the body as opposed to the extremities.

name: polydipsia
polydipsia
HP:0001959.def: Excessive thirst manifested by excessive fluid intake.

name: palpitations
palpitation
HP:0001962.def: A sensation that the heart is pounding or racing, which is a non-specific sign but may be a manifestation of arrhythmia.

name: abnormal speech discrimination
abnormal speech discrimination
HP:0001963.def: A type of hearing impairment prominently characterized by a difficulty in understanding speech, rather than an inability to hear speech. Poor speech discrimination is a very common symptom of high frequency hearing loss.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of metatarsal bones
aplasia / hypoplasia of metatarsal bone
HP:0001964.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the metatarsal bones.
synonym: absent / small long bone of foot
absent / small long bone of foot
absent / underdeveloped long bone of foot
absent / underdevelop long bone of foot

name: abnormal scalp morphology
abnormal scalp morphology
HP:0001965.def: Any anomaly of the scalp, the skin an subcutaneous tissue of the head on which head hair grows.

name: abnormal glomerular mesangium morphology
abnormal glomerular mesangium morphology
HP:0001966.def: An abnormality of the mesangium, i.e., of the central part of the renal glomerulus between capillaries.

name: diffuse mesangial sclerosis
diffuse mesangial sclerosis
HP:0001967.def: Diffuse sclerosis of the mesangium, as manifestated by diffuse mesangial matrix expansion.

name: abnormal tubulointerstitial morphology
abnormal tubulointerstitial morphology
HP:0001969.def: An abnormality that involves the tubules and interstitial tissue of the kidney.

name: tubulointerstitial nephritis
tubulointerstitial nephritis
HP:0001970.def: A form of inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

name: hypersplenism
hypersplenism
HP:0001971.def: A malfunctioning of the spleen in which it prematurely destroys red blood cells.

name: macrocytic anemia
macrocytic anemia
HP:0001972.def: A type of anemia characterized by increased size of erythrocytes with increased mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH).

name: autoimmune thrombocytopenia
autoimmune thrombocytopenia
HP:0001973.def: The presence of thrombocytopenia in combination with detection of antiplatelet antibodies.

name: leukocytosis
leukocytosis
HP:0001974.def: An abnormal increase in the number of leukocytes in the blood.

name: decreased platelet glycoprotein iib - iiia
decrease platelet glycoprotein iib - iiia
HP:0001975.def: Decreased cell membrane concentration of glycoprotein IIb-IIIa.
synonym: reduced level of platelet glycoprotein iib / iiia complex
reduce level of platelet glycoprotein iib / iiia complex

name: reduced antithrombin iii activity
reduce antithrombin iii activity
HP:0001976.def: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of antithrombin-III.

name: abnormal thrombosis
abnormal thrombosis
HP:0001977.def: Venous or arterial thrombosis (formation of blood clots) of spontaneous nature and which cannot be fully explained by acquired risk (e.g. atherosclerosis).

name: extramedullary hematopoiesis
extramedullary hematopoiesis
HP:0001978.def: The process of hematopoiesis occurring outside of the bone marrow (in the liver, thymus, and spleen) in the postnatal organisms.

name: megaloblastic bone marrow
megaloblastic bone marrow
HP:0001980.def: Abnormal increased number of megaloblasts in the bone marrow.

name: schistocytosis
schistocytosis
HP:0001981.def: The presence of an abnormal number of fragmented red blood cells (schistocytes) in the blood.

name: sea - blue histiocytosis
sea - blue histiocytosis
HP:0001982.def: An abnormality of histiocytes, in which the cells take on a sea blue appearance due to abnormally increased lipid content. Histiocytes are a type of macrophage. Sea-blue histiocytes are typically large macrophages from 20 to 60 micrometers in diameter with a single eccentric nucleus whose cytoplasm if packed with sea-blue or blue-green granules when stained with Wright-Giemsa.

name: reduced lymphocyte surface expression of cd43
reduce lymphocyte surface expression of cd43
HP:0001983.def: A reduction in the expression of CD43 on the cell surface of lymphocytes.
synonym: cd43 defectively expressed on surface of blood cells
cd43 defectively express on surface of blood cell
reduced lymphocyte surface expression of sialophorin
reduce lymphocyte surface expression of sialophorin

name: hypoketotic hypoglycemia
hypoketotic hypoglycemia
HP:0001985.def: A decreased concentration of glucose in the blood associated with a reduced concentration of ketone bodies.

name: hyperammonemia
hyperammonemia
HP:0001987.def: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood.

name: recurrent hypoglycemia
recurrent hypoglycemia
HP:0001988.def: Recurrent episodes of decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

name: fetal akinesia sequence
fetal akinesia sequence
HP:0001989.def: Decreased fetal activity associated with multiple joint contractures, facial anomalies and pulmonary hypoplasia. Ultrasound examination may reveal polyhydramnios, ankylosis, scalp edema, and decreased chest movements (reflecting pulmonary hypoplasia).

name: organic aciduria
organic aciduria
HP:0001992.def: Excretion of non-amino organic acids in urine.

name: ketoacidosis
ketoacidosis
HP:0001993.def: Acidosis resulting from accumulation of ketone bodies.

name: renal fanconi syndrome
renal fanconi syndrome
HP:0001994.def: An inability of the tubules in the kidney to reabsorb small molecules, causing increased urinary loss of electrolytes (sodium, potassium, bicarbonate), minerals, glucose, amino acids, and water.

name: hyperchloremic acidosis
hyperchloremic acidosis
HP:0001995.def: Acidosis (pH less than 7.35) that develops with an increase in ionic chloride.

name: gout
gout
HP:0001997.def: Recurrent attacks of acute inflammatory arthritis of a joint or set of joints caused by elevated levels of uric acid in the blood which crystallize and are deposited in joints, tendons, and surrounding tissues.

name: abnormal facial shape
abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.def: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

name: short columella
short columella
HP:0002000.def: Reduced distance from the anterior border of the naris to the subnasale.

name: deep philtrum
deep philtrum
HP:0002002.def: Accentuated, prominent philtral ridges giving rise to an exaggerated groove in the midline between the nasal base and upper vermillion border.

name: large forehead
large forehead
synonym: increased size of frontal region of face
increase size of frontal region of face

name: facial cleft
facial cleft
HP:0002006.def: A congenital malformation with a cleft (gap or opening) in the face.

name: frontal bossing
frontal bossing
HP:0002007.def: Bilateral bulging of the lateral frontal bone prominences with relative sparing of the midline.

name: potter facies
potter facies
HP:0002009.def: A facial appearance characteristic of a fetus or neonate due to oligohydramnios experienced in the womb, comprising ocular hypertelorism, low-set ears, receding chin, and flattening of the nose.

name: narrow maxilla
narrow maxilla
synonym: decreased breadth of upper jaw bones
decrease breadth of upper jaw bone
decreased width of upper jaw bones
decrease width of upper jaw bone

name: morphological central nervous system abnormality
morphological central nervous system abnormality
HP:0002011.def: A structural abnormality of the central nervous system.
synonym: abnormality of the central nervous system
abnormality of the central nervous system
morphological abnormality of the central nervous system
morphological abnormality of the central nervous system

name: abnormality of the abdominal organs
abnormality of the abdominal organ
HP:0002012.def: An abnormality of the viscera of the abdomen.

name: vomiting
vomit
HP:0002013.def: Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.

name: diarrhea
diarrhea
HP:0002014.def: Abnormally increased frequency (usually defined as three or more) loose or watery bowel movements a day.

name: nausea and vomiting
nausea and vomiting
HP:0002017.def: Nausea is a commonly encountered symptom that has been defined as an unpleasant painless subjective feeling that one will imminently vomit. Vomiting has been defined as the forceful expulsion of the contents of the stomach, duodenum, or jejunum through the oral cavity. While nausea and vomiting are often thought to exist on a temporal continuum, this is not always the case. There are situations when severe nausea may be present without emesis and less frequently, when emesis may be present without preceding nausea.

name: nausea
nausea
HP:0002018.def: A sensation of unease in the stomach together with an urge to vomit.

name: constipation
constipation
HP:0002019.def: Infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces.

name: gastroesophageal reflux
gastroesophageal reflux
HP:0002020.def: A condition in which the stomach contents leak backwards from the stomach into the esophagus through the lower esophageal sphincter.

name: pyloric stenosis
pyloric stenosis
HP:0002021.def: Pyloric stenosis, also known as infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, is an uncommon condition in infants characterized by abnormal thickening of the pylorus muscles in the stomach leading to gastric outlet obstruction. Clinically infants are well at birth. Then, at 3 to 6 weeks of age, the infants present with projectile vomiting, potentially leading to dehydration and weight loss.

name: anal atresia
anal atresia
HP:0002023.def: Congenital absence of the anus, i.e., the opening at the bottom end of the intestinal tract.

name: malabsorption
malabsorption
HP:0002024.def: Impaired ability to absorb one or more nutrients from the intestine.

name: anal stenosis
anal stenosis
HP:0002025.def: Abnormal narrowing of the anal opening.

name: abdominal pain
abdominal pain
HP:0002027.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the abdomen.

name: chronic diarrhea
chronic diarrhea
HP:0002028.def: The presence of chronic diarrhea, which is usually taken to mean diarrhea that has persisted for over 4 weeks.

name: abnormal esophagus morphology
abnormal esophagus morphology
HP:0002031.def: A structural abnormality of the esophagus.

name: esophageal atresia
esophageal atresia
HP:0002032.def: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the esophagus such that the esophagus ends in a blind pouch rather than connecting to the stomach.
synonym: birth defect in which part of esophagus did not develop
birth defect in which part of esophagus do not develop
birth defect in which part of oesophagus did not develop
birth defect in which part of oesophagus do not develop

name: poor suck
poor suck
HP:0002033.def: An inadequate sucking reflex, resulting in the difficult of newborns to be breast-fed.

name: abnormal rectum morphology
abnormal rectum morphology
HP:0002034.def: An abnormaltiy of the rectum, the final segment of the large intestine that stores solid waste until it passes through the anus.

name: rectal prolapse
rectal prolapse
HP:0002035.def: Protrusion of the rectal mucous membrane through the anus.

name: hiatus hernia
hiatus hernia
HP:0002036.def: The presence of a hernia in which the upper part of the stomach, i.e., mainly the gastric cardia protrudes through the diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus.

name: inflammation of the large intestine
inflammation of the large intestine
HP:0002037.def: Inflammation, or an inflammatory state in the large intestine.

name: anorexia
anorexia
HP:0002039.def: Anorexia, or the loss of appetite for food, is a medical condition.

name: esophageal varix
esophageal varix
HP:0002040.def: Extreme dilation of the submucusoal veins in the lower portion of the esophagus.

name: esophageal stricture
esophageal stricture
HP:0002043.def: A pathological narrowing of the esophagus that is caused by the development of a ring of scar tissue that constricts the esophageal lumen.
synonym: narrowing of esophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue
narrowing of esophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue
narrowing of oesophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue
narrowing of oesophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue

name: zollinger - ellison syndrome
zollinger - ellison syndrome
HP:0002044.def: A condition in which there is increased production of gastrin by a gastrin-secreting tumor (usually located in the pancreas, duodenum, or abdominal lymph nodes) that stimulates the gastric mucosa to maximal activity, with consequent gastrointestinal mucosal ulceration.

name: hypothermia
hypothermia
HP:0002045.def: Reduced body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.

name: heat intolerance
heat intolerance
HP:0002046.def: The inability to maintain a comfortable body temperature in warm or hot weather.

name: malignant hyperthermia
malignant hyperthermia
HP:0002047.def: Malignant hyperthermia is characterized by a rapid increase in temperature to 39-42 degrees C. Malignant hyperthermia may occur in response to either inhalational anesthetics such as halothane, to muscle relaxants such as succinylcholine, or to exercise.

name: renal cortical atrophy
renal cortical atrophy
HP:0002048.def: Atrophy of the cortex of the kidney.

name: proximal renal tubular acidosis
proximal renal tubular acidosis
HP:0002049.def: A type of renal tubular acidosis characterized by a failure of the proximal tubular cells to reabsorb bicarbonate, leading to urinary bicarbonate wasting and subsequent acidemia.

name: curved linear dimple below the lower lip
curve linear dimple below the low lip
abnormality of the glabella
abnormality of the glabella
synonym: abnormality of the area between the eyebrows
abnormality of the area between the eyebrow
deformity of the area between the eyebrows
deformity of the area between the eyebrow
malformation of the area between the eyebrows
malformation of the area between the eyebrow

name: myopathic facies
myopathic facies
HP:0002058.def: A facial appearance characteristic of myopathic conditions. The face appears expressionless with sunken cheeks, bilateral ptosis, and inability to elevate the corners of the mouth, due to muscle weakness.

name: cerebral atrophy
cerebral atrophy
HP:0002059.def: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the cerebrum.

name: abnormal cerebral morphology
abnormal cerebral morphology
HP:0002060.def: Any structural abnormality of the telencephalon, which is also known as the cerebrum.

name: lower limb spasticity
low limb spasticity
HP:0002061.def: Spasticity (velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone and hyperexcitable tendon reflexes) in the muscles of the lower limbs, hips, and pelvis

name: abnormal pyramidal tract morphology
abnormal pyramidal tract morphology
HP:0002062.def: Any structural abnormality of the pyramidal tract, whose chief element, the corticospinal tract, is the only direct connection between the brain and the spinal cord. In addition to the corticospinal tract, the pyramidal system includes the corticobulbar, corticomesencephalic, and corticopontine tracts.
synonym: morphological abnormality of the pyramidal tract
morphological abnormality of the pyramidal tract

name: rigidity
rigidity
HP:0002063.def: Continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity.

name: spastic gait
spastic gait
HP:0002064.def: Spasticity is manifested by increased stretch reflex which is intensified with movement velocity. This results in excessive and inappropriate muscle activation which can contribute to muscle hypertonia. Spastic gait is characterized by manifestations such as muscle hypertonia, stiff knee, and circumduction of the leg.

name: gait ataxia
gait ataxia
HP:0002066.def: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to coordinate the movements required for normal walking. Gait ataxia is characteirzed by a wide-based staggering gait with a tendency to fall.
synonym: inability to coordinate movements when walking
inability to coordinate movement when walk

name: bradykinesia
bradykinesia
HP:0002067.def: Bradykinesia literally means slow movement, and is used clinically to denote a slowness in the execution of movement (in contrast to hypokinesia, which is used to refer to slowness in the initiation of movement).

name: bilateral tonic - clonic seizure
bilateral tonic - clonic seizure
HP:0002069.def: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure is a seizure defined by a tonic (bilateral increased tone, lasting seconds to minutes) and then a clonic (bilateral sustained rhythmic jerking) phase.
synonym: generalised tonic - clonic seizure ( without specification of onset )
generalise tonic - clonic seizure ( without specification of onset )
generalized tonic - clonic seizure ( without specification of onset )
generalize tonic - clonic seizure ( without specification of onset )

name: limb ataxia
limb ataxia
HP:0002070.def: A kind of ataxia that affects movements of the extremities.

name: abnormality of extrapyramidal motor function
abnormality of extrapyramidal motor function
HP:0002071.def: A neurological condition related to lesions of the basal ganglia leading to typical abnormalities including akinesia (inability to initiate changes in activity and perform volitional movements rapidly and easily), muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement), chorea (widespread arrhythmic movements of a forcible, rapid, jerky, and restless nature), athetosis (inability to sustain the muscles of the fingers, toes, or other group of muscles in a fixed position), and akathisia (inability to remain motionless).

name: chorea
chorea
HP:0002072.def: Chorea (Greek for 'dance') refers to widespread arrhythmic involuntary movements of a forcible, jerky and restless fashion. It is a random-appearing sequence of one or more discrete involuntary movements or movement fragments. Movements appear random because of variability in timing, duration or location. Each movement may have a distinct start and end. However, movements may be strung together and thus may appear to flow randomly from one muscle group to another. Chorea can involve the trunk, neck, face, tongue, and extremities.

name: increased neuronal autofluorescent lipopigment
increase neuronal autofluorescent lipopigment
HP:0002074.def: Lipofuscin, a generic term applied to autofluorescent lipopigment, is a mixture of protein and lipid that accumulates in most aging cells, particularly those involved in high lipid turnover (e.g., the adrenal medulla) or phagocytosis of other cell types (e g., the retinal pigment epithelium or RPE; macrophage). This term pertains if there is an increase in the neuronal accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.

name: dysdiadochokinesis
dysdiadochokinesis
HP:0002075.def: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to perform rapidly alternating movements, such as pronating and supinating his or her hand on the dorsum of the other hand as rapidly as possible.
synonym: difficulty performing quick and alternating movements
difficulty perform quick and alternate movement

name: migraine
migraine
HP:0002076.def: Migraine is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by episodic attacks of headache and associated symptoms.

name: migraine with aura
migraine with aura
HP:0002077.def: A type of migraine in which there is an aura characterized by focal neurological phenomena that usually proceed, but may accompany or occur in the absence of, the headache. The symptoms of an aura may include fully reversible visual, sensory, and speech symptoms but not motor weakness. Visual symptoms may include flickering lights, spots and lines and/or loss of vision and/or unilateral sensory symptoms such as paresthesias or numbness. At least one of the symptoms of an aura develops gradually over 5 or more minutes and/or different symptoms occur in succession.

name: truncal ataxia
truncal ataxia
HP:0002078.def: Truncal ataxia is a sign of ataxia characterized by instability of the trunk. It usually occurs during sitting.
synonym: instability or lack of coordination of central trunk muscles
instability or lack of coordination of central trunk muscle

name: hypoplasia of the corpus callosum
hypoplasia of the corpus callosum
synonym: underdevelopment of part of brain called corpus callosum
underdevelopment of part of brain call corpus callosum

name: intention tremor
intention tremor
HP:0002080.def: A type of kinetic tremor that occurs during target directed movement is called intention tremor. That is, an oscillatory cerebellar ataxia that tends to be absent when the limbs are inactive and during the first part of voluntary movement but worsening as the movement continues and greater precision is required (e.g., in touching a target such as the patient's nose or a physician's finger).

name: migraine without aura
migraine without aura
HP:0002083.def: Repeated headache attacks lasting 4-72 h fulfilling at least two of the following criteria: 1) unilateral location, 2) pulsating quality, 3) moderate or severe pain intensity, and 4) aggravation by or causing avoidance of routine physical activity such as climbing stairs. Headache attacks are commonly accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia, or phonophobia.

name: encephalocele
encephalocele
HP:0002084.def: A neural tube defect characterized by sac-like protrusions of the brain and the membranes that cover it through openings in the skull.

name: occipital encephalocele
occipital encephalocele
HP:0002085.def: A type of encephalocele (that is, a a protrusion of part of the cranial contents including brain tissue through a congenital opening in the cranium, typically covered with skin or mucous membrane) in the occipital region of the skull. Occipital encephalocele presents as a midline swelling over the occipital bone. It is usually covered with normal full-thickness scalp.
synonym: brain tissue sticks out through back of skull
brain tissue stick out through back of skull

name: abnormality of the respiratory system
abnormality of the respiratory system
HP:0002086.def: An abnormality of the respiratory system, which include the airways, lungs, and the respiratory muscles.

name: abnormality of the upper respiratory tract
abnormality of the upper respiratory tract
HP:0002087.def: An abnormality of the upper respiratory tract.
synonym: abnormality of the upper respiratory tract
abnormality of the upper respiratory tract

name: abnormal lung morphology
abnormal lung morphology
HP:0002088.def: Any structural anomaly of the lung.

name: pneumonia
pneumonia
HP:0002090.def: Inflammation of any part of the lung parenchyma.

name: restrictive ventilatory defect
restrictive ventilatory defect
HP:0002091.def: A functional defect characterized by reduced total lung capacity (TLC) not associated with abnormalities of expiratory airflow or airway resistance. Spirometrically, a restrictive defect is defined as FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in 1 second) and FVC (forced vital capacity) less than 80 per cent. Restrictive lung disease may be caused by alterations in lung parenchyma or because of a disease of the pleura, chest wall, or neuromuscular apparatus.
synonym: restrictive deficit on pulmonary function testing
restrictive deficit on pulmonary function test
restrictive deficit on pulmonary function tests
restrictive deficit on pulmonary function test
stiff lung or chest wall causing decreased lung volume
stiff lung or chest wall causing decrease lung volume

name: pulmonary arterial hypertension
pulmonary arterial hypertension
HP:0002092.def: Pulmonary hypertension is defined mean pulmonary artery pressure of 25mmHg or more and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 15mmHg or less when measured by right heart catheterisation at rest and in a supine position.
synonym: increased blood pressure in blood vessels of lungs
increase blood pressure in blood vessel of lung

name: dyspnea
dyspnea
HP:0002094.def: Difficult or labored breathing. Dyspnea is a subjective feeling only the patient can rate, e.g., on a Borg scale.

name: respiratory distress
respiratory distress
HP:0002098.def: Respiratory distress is objectively observable as the physical or emotional consequences from the experience of dyspnea. The physical presentation of respiratory distress is generally referred to as labored breathing, while the sensation of respiratory distress is called shortness of breath or dyspnea.

name: asthma
asthma
HP:0002099.def: Asthma is characterized by increased responsiveness of the tracheobronchial tree to multiple stimuli, leading to narrowing of the air passages with resultant dyspnea, cough, and wheezing.

name: recurrent aspiration pneumonia
recurrent aspiration pneumonia
HP:0002100.def: Increased susceptibility to aspiration pneumonia, defined as pneumonia due to breathing in foreign material, as manifested by a medical history of repeated episodes of aspiration pneumonia.

name: abnormal lung lobation
abnormal lung lobation
HP:0002101.def: A developmental defect in the formation of pulmonary lobes.

name: pleuritis
pleuritis
synonym: inflammation of tissues lining lungs and chest
inflammation of tissue line lung and chest

name: abnormal pleura morphology
abnormal pleura morphology
HP:0002103.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary pleura, the thin, transparent membrane which covers the lungs and lines the inside of the chest walls.

name: apnea
apnea
HP:0002104.def: Lack of breathing with no movement of the respiratory muscles and no exchange of air in the lungs. This term refers to a disposition to have recurrent episodes of apnea rather than to a single event.

name: hemoptysis
hemoptysis
HP:0002105.def: Coughing up (expectoration) of blood or blood-streaked sputum from the larynx, trachea, bronchi, or lungs.
synonym: coughing up blood or blood - stained mucus
cough up blood or blood - stain mucus

name: pneumothorax
pneumothorax
HP:0002107.def: Accumulation of air in the pleural cavity leading to a partially or completely collapsed lung.

name: spontaneous pneumothorax
spontaneous pneumothorax
HP:0002108.def: Pneumothorax occurring without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

name: bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis
HP:0002110.def: Persistent abnormal dilatation of the bronchi owing to localized and irreversible destruction and widening of the large airways.
synonym: permanent enlargement of the airways of the lungs
permanent enlargement of the airway of the lung

name: obsolete restrictive deficit on pulmonary function testing
obsolete restrictive deficit on pulmonary function test
abnormal cerebral ventricle morphology
abnormal cerebral ventricle morphology
HP:0002118.def: Any structural abnormality of the cerebral ventricles.

name: ventriculomegaly
ventriculomegaly
HP:0002119.def: An increase in size of the ventricular system of the brain.

name: cerebral cortical atrophy
cerebral cortical atrophy
HP:0002120.def: Atrophy of the cortex of the cerebrum.
synonym: decrease in size of the outer layer of the brain due to loss of brain cells
decrease in size of the outer layer of the brain due to loss of brain cell

name: generalized non - motor ( absence ) seizure
generalize non - motor ( absence ) seizure
HP:0002121.def: A generalized non-motor (absence) seizure is a type of a type of dialeptic seizure that is of electrographically generalized onset. It is a generalized seizure characterised by an interruption of activities, a blank stare, and usually the person will be unresponsive when spoken to. Any ictal motor phenomena are minor in comparison to these non-motor features.

name: generalized myoclonic seizure
generalize myoclonic seizure
HP:0002123.def: A generalized myoclonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterised by bilateral, sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction of muscles or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.

name: polymicrogyria
polymicrogyria
HP:0002126.def: Polymicrogyria is a congenital malformation of the cerebral cortex characterized by abnormal cortical layering (lamination) and an excessive number of small gyri (folds).

name: abnormal upper motor neuron morphology
abnormal upper motor neuron morphology
HP:0002127.def: Any structural anomaly that affects the upper motor neuron.
synonym: abnormal shape of upper motor neuron
abnormal shape of upper motor neuron

name: episodic ataxia
episodic ataxia
HP:0002131.def: Periodic spells of incoordination and imbalance, that is, episodes of ataxia typically lasting from 10 minutes to several hours or days.

name: porencephalic cyst
porencephalic cyst
HP:0002132.def: A cavity within the cerebral hemisphere, filled with cerebrospinal fluid, that communicates directly with the ventricular system.

name: status epilepticus
status epilepticus
HP:0002133.def: Status epilepticus is a type of prolonged seizure resulting either from the failure of the mechanisms responsible for seizure termination or from the initiation of mechanisms which lead to abnormally prolonged seizures (after time point t1). It is a condition that can have long-term consequences (after time point t2), including neuronal death, neuronal injury, and alteration of neuronal networks, depending on the type and duration of seizures.
synonym: repeated seizures without recovery between them
repeat seizure without recovery between them

name: basal ganglia calcification
basal ganglion calcification
HP:0002135.def: The presence of calcium deposition affecting one or more structures of the basal ganglia.

name: broad - based gait
broad - base gait
HP:0002136.def: An abnormal gait pattern in which persons stand and walk with their feet spaced widely apart. This is often a component of cerebellar ataxia.

name: subarachnoid hemorrhage
subarachnoid hemorrhage
HP:0002138.def: Hemorrhage occurring between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater.

name: arrhinencephaly
arrhinencephaly
HP:0002139.def: A defect of development of the brain characterized by congenital absence of the part of the brain that includes the olfactory bulbs, tracts, and other structures associated with the sense of smell.

name: ischemic stroke
ischemic stroke
HP:0002140.def: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is defined by the sudden loss of blood flow to an area of the brain with the resulting loss of neurologic function. It is caused by thrombosis or embolism that occludes a cerebral vessel supplying a specific area of the brain. During a vessel occlusion, there is a core area where damage to the brain is irreversible and an area of penumbra where the brain has lost function owing to decreased blood flow but is not irreversibly injured.

name: abnormal spinal cord morphology
abnormal spinal cord morphology
HP:0002143.def: A structural abnormality of the spinal cord (myelon).

name: tethered cord
tether cord
HP:0002144.def: During normal embryological development, the spinal cord first occupies the entire length of the vertebral column but goes on to assume a position at the level of L1 due to differential growth of the conus medullaris and the vertebral column. The filum terminale is a slender, threadlike structure that remains after the normal regression of the distal embryonic spinal cord and attaches the spinal cord to the coccyx. A tethered cord results if there is a thickened rope-like filum terminale which anchors the cord at the level of L2 or below, potentially causing neurologic signs owing to abnormal tension on the spinal cord.

name: frontotemporal dementia
frontotemporal dementia
HP:0002145.def: A dementia associated with degeneration of the frontotemporal lobe and clinically associated with personality and behavioral changes such as disinhibition, apathy, and lack of insight. The hallmark feature of frontotemporal dementia is the presentation with focal syndromes such as progressive language dysfunction, or aphasia, or behavioral changes characteristic of frontal lobe disorders.

name: hypophosphatemia
hypophosphatemia
HP:0002148.def: An abnormally decreased phosphate concentration in the blood.

name: hyperuricemia
hyperuricemia
HP:0002149.def: An abnormally high level of uric acid in the blood.

name: increased serum lactate
increase serum lactate
HP:0002151.def: Abnormally increased level of blood lactate (2-hydroxypropanoic acid). Lactate is produced from pyruvate by lactate dehydrogenase during normal metabolism. The terms lactate and lactic acid are often used interchangeably but lactate (the component measured in blood) is strictly a weak base whereas lactic acid is the corresponding acid. Lactic acidosis is often used clinically to describe elevated lactate but should be reserved for cases where there is a corresponding acidosis (pH below 7.35).
synonym: higher than normal levels of lactate in blood
high than normal level of lactate in blood

name: hyperproteinemia
hyperproteinemia
HP:0002152.def: An increased concentration of proteins in the blood.

name: hyperkalemia
hyperkalemia
HP:0002153.def: An abnormally increased potassium concentration in the blood.

name: hyperglycinemia
hyperglycinemia
HP:0002154.def: An elevated concentration of glycine in the blood.

name: hypertriglyceridemia
hypertriglyceridemia
HP:0002155.def: An abnormal increase in the level of triglycerides in the blood.

name: homocystinuria
homocystinuria
HP:0002156.def: An increased concentration of homocystine in the urine.

name: azotemia
azotemia
HP:0002157.def: An increased concentration of nitrogen compounds in the blood.

name: heparan sulfate excretion in urine
heparan sulfate excretion in urine
HP:0002159.def: An increased concentration of heparan sulfates in the urine.

name: hyperhomocystinemia
hyperhomocystinemia
HP:0002160.def: An increased concentration of homocystine in the blood.

name: hyperlysinemia
hyperlysinemia
HP:0002161.def: An increased concentration of lysine in the blood.

name: low posterior hairline
low posterior hairline
HP:0002162.def: Hair on the neck extends more inferiorly than usual.
synonym: low hairline at back of neck
low hairline at back of neck

name: nail dysplasia
nail dysplasia
HP:0002164.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the nail.

name: pterygium of nails
pterygium of nail
HP:0002165.def: Inward advance of skin over the nail plate.

name: impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs
impaired vibration sensation in the low limb
HP:0002166.def: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the legs.
synonym: decreased vibratory sense in lower limbs
decreased vibratory sense in low limb
decreased vibratory sense in the lower extremities
decreased vibratory sense in the low extremity
decreased vibratory sense in the lower limbs
decreased vibratory sense in the low limb
diminished vibratory sensation in the legs
diminished vibratory sensation in the leg
distal sensory loss , especially vibratory sense
distal sensory loss , especially vibratory sense
distal vibratory impairment of the lower limbs
distal vibratory impairment of the low limb
impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs
impaired vibration sensation in the low limb

name: abnormality of speech or vocalization
abnormality of speech or vocalization
HP:0002167.def: Abnormalities in the sound of a person's speech or vocalization are not necessarily associated with a known physical cause or due to stuttering or stammering.

name: scanning speech
scan speech
HP:0002168.def: An abnormal pattern of speech in which the words are as if measured or scanned; there is a pause after every syllable, and the syllables themselves are pronounced slowly.

name: clonus
clonus
HP:0002169.def: A series of rhythmic and involuntary muscle contractions (at a frequency of about 5 to 7 Hz) that occur in response to an abruptly applied and sustained stretch.
synonym: involuntary rhythmic muscular contractions and relaxations
involuntary rhythmic muscular contraction and relaxation

name: gliosis
gliosis
HP:0002171.def: Gliosis is the focal proliferation of glial cells in the central nervous system.

name: postural instability
postural instability
HP:0002172.def: A tendency to fall or the inability to keep oneself from falling; imbalance. The retropulsion test is widely regarded as the gold standard to evaluate postural instability, Use of the retropulsion test includes a rapid balance perturbation in the backward direction, and the number of balance correcting steps (or total absence thereof) is used to rate the degree of postural instability. Healthy subjects correct such perturbations with either one or two large steps, or without taking any steps, hinging rapidly at the hips while swinging the arms forward as a counterweight. In patients with balance impairment, balance correcting steps are often too small, forcing patients to take more than two steps. Taking three or more steps is generally considered to be abnormal, and taking more than five steps is regarded as being clearly abnormal. Markedly affected patients continue to step backward without ever regaining their balance and must be caught by the examiner (this would be called true retropulsion). Even more severely affected patients fail to correct entirely, and fall backward like a pushed toy soldier, without taking any corrective steps.

name: postural tremor
postural tremor
HP:0002174.def: A type of tremors that is triggered by holding a limb in a fixed position.

name: spinal cord compression
spinal cord compression
HP:0002176.def: External mechanical compression of the spinal cord.

name: neurodegeneration
neurodegeneration
HP:0002180.def: Progressive loss of neural cells and tissue.

name: cerebral edema
cerebral edema
HP:0002181.def: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in the brain.

name: phonophobia
phonophobia
HP:0002183.def: An abnormally heightened sensitivity to loud sounds.

name: neurofibrillary tangles
neurofibrillary tangle
HP:0002185.def: Pathological protein aggregates formed by hyperphosphorylation of a microtubule-associated protein known as tau, causing it to aggregate in an insoluble form.
synonym: neurofibrillary tangles composed of disordered microtubules in neurons
neurofibrillary tangle compose of disordered microtubule in neuron

name: apraxia
apraxia
HP:0002186.def: A defect in the understanding of complex motor commands and in the execution of certain learned movements, i.e., deficits in the cognitive components of learned movements.

name: intellectual disability , profound
intellectual disability , profound
HP:0002187.def: Profound mental retardation is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) below 20.

name: delayed cns myelination
delay cns myelination
HP:0002188.def: Delayed myelination in the central nervous system.
synonym: delay in central nervous system myelination
delay in central nervous system myelination

name: choroid plexus cyst
choroid plexus cyst
HP:0002190.def: A cyst occurring within the choroid plexus within a cerebral ventricle.

name: progressive spasticity
progressive spasticity
HP:0002191.def: Spasticity that increases in degree with time.

name: pseudobulbar behavioral symptoms
pseudobulbar behavioral symptom
HP:0002193.def: Individuals with Pseudobulbar signs often also demonstrate abnormal behavioral symptoms such as inappropriate emotional outbursts of uncontrolled laughter or weeping etc.

name: delayed gross motor development
delay gross motor development
HP:0002194.def: A type of motor delay characterized by a delay in acquiring the ability to control the large muscles of the body for walking, running, sitting, and crawling.

name: dysgenesis of the cerebellar vermis
dysgenesis of the cerebellar vermis
HP:0002195.def: Defective development of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: generalized - onset seizure
generalize - onset seizure
HP:0002197.def: A generalized-onset seizure is a type of seizure originating at some point within, and rapidly engaging, bilaterally distributed networks. The networks may include cortical and subcortical structures but not necessarily the entire cortex.

name: dilated fourth ventricle
dilate fourth ventricle
HP:0002198.def: An abnormal dilatation of the fourth cerebral ventricle.

name: pseudobulbar signs
pseudobulbar sign
HP:0002200.def: Pseudobulbar signs result from injury to an upper motor neuron lesion to the corticobulbar pathways in the pyramidal tract. Patients have difficulty chewing, swallowing and demonstrate slurred speech (often initial presentation) as well as abnormal behavioral symptoms such as inappropriate emotional outbursts of uncontrolled laughter or weeping etc.

name: pleural effusion
pleural effusion
HP:0002202.def: The presence of an excessive amount of fluid in the pleural cavity.

name: respiratory paralysis
respiratory paralysis
HP:0002203.def: Inability to move the muscles of respiration.

name: pulmonary embolism
pulmonary embolism
HP:0002204.def: An embolus (that is, an abnormal particle circulating in the blood) located in the pulmonary artery and thereby blocking blood circulation to the lung. Usually the embolus is a blood clot that has developed in an extremity (for instance, a deep venous thrombosis), detached, and traveled through the circulation before becoming trapped in the pulmonary artery.
synonym: blood clot in artery of lung
blood clot in artery of lung

name: recurrent respiratory infections
recurrent respiratory infection
HP:0002205.def: An increased susceptibility to respiratory infections as manifested by a history of recurrent respiratory infections.

name: pulmonary fibrosis
pulmonary fibrosis
HP:0002206.def: Replacement of normal lung tissues by fibroblasts and collagen.

name: diffuse reticular or finely nodular infiltrations
diffuse reticular or finely nodular infiltration
coarse hair
coarse hair
HP:0002208.def: Hair shafts are rough in texture.

name: sparse scalp hair
sparse scalp hair
HP:0002209.def: Decreased number of hairs per unit area of skin of the scalp.
synonym: reduced / lack of hair on scalp
reduce / lack of hair on scalp
reduction in the number of scalp follicles
reduction in the number of scalp follicle

name: white forelock
white forelock
HP:0002211.def: A triangular depigmented region of white hairs located in the anterior midline of the scalp.
synonym: white part of hair above forehead
white part of hair above forehead

name: fine hair
fine hair
HP:0002213.def: Hair that is fine or thin to the touch.

name: sparse axillary hair
sparse axillary hair
HP:0002215.def: Reduced number or density of axillary hair.
synonym: sparse scalp , axillary , and pubic hair
sparse scalp , axillary , and pubic hair

name: premature graying of hair
premature graying of hair
HP:0002216.def: Development of gray hair at a younger than normal age.

name: slow - growing hair
slow - grow hair
HP:0002217.def: Hair whose growth is slower than normal.

name: facial hypertrichosis
facial hypertrichosis
HP:0002219.def: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the facial region.

name: melanin pigment aggregation in hair shafts
melanin pigment aggregation in hair shaft
woolly hair
woolly hair
HP:0002224.def: The term woolly hair refers to an abnormal variant of hair that is fine, with tightly coiled curls, and often hypopigmented. Optical microscopy may reveal the presence of tight spirals and a clear diameter reduction as compared with normal hair. Electron microscopy may show flat, oval hair shafts with reduced transversal diameter.

name: sparse pubic hair
sparse pubic hair
HP:0002225.def: Reduced number or density of pubic hair.

name: white eyebrow
white eyebrow
HP:0002226.def: White color (lack of pigmentation) of the eyebrow.

name: white eyelashes
white eyelash
HP:0002227.def: White color (lack of pigmentation) of the eyelashes.

name: generalized hirsutism
generalize hirsutism
HP:0002230.def: Abnormally increased hair growth over much of the entire body.

name: patchy alopecia
patchy alopecia
HP:0002232.def: Transient, non-scarring hair loss and preservation of the hair follicle located in in well-defined patches.

name: early balding
early balding
HP:0002234.def: Loss of scalp hair at an earlier than normal age.

name: pili canaliculi
pili canaliculus
HP:0002235.def: A characteristic triangular, kidney- or heat-shaped diameter of hair shafts with typical longitudinal canalicular deformation as observable by scanning electron microscopy.

name: frontal upsweep of hair
frontal upsweep of hair
HP:0002236.def: Upward and/or sideward growth of anterior hair.

name: hepatomegaly
hepatomegaly
HP:0002240.def: Abnormally increased size of the liver.

name: abnormal intestine morphology
abnormal intestine morphology
HP:0002242.def: An abnormality of the intestine. The closely related term enteropathy is used to refer to any disease of the intestine.

name: protein - losing enteropathy
protein - losing enteropathy
HP:0002243.def: Abnormal loss of protein from the digestive tract related to excessive leakage of plasma proteins into the lumen of the gastrointestinal tract.

name: abnormal small intestine morphology
abnormal small intestine morphology
HP:0002244.def: A structural abnormality of the small intestine.

name: meckel diverticulum
meckel diverticulum
HP:0002245.def: Meckel's diverticulum is a congenital diverticulum located in the distal ileum.

name: abnormal duodenum morphology
abnormal duodenum morphology
HP:0002246.def: An abnormality of the duodenum, i.e., the first section of the small intestine.

name: duodenal atresia
duodenal atresia
HP:0002247.def: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the duodenal lumen, that is, an abnormal closure of the duodenum.
synonym: absence or narrowing of first part of small bowel
absence or narrowing of first part of small bowel

name: melena
melena
HP:0002249.def: The passage of blackish, tarry feces associated with gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Melena occurs if the blood remains in the colon long enough for it to be broken down by colonic bacteria. One degradation product, hematin, imbues the stool with a blackish color. Thus, melena generally occurs with bleeding from the upper gastrointestinal tract (e.g., stomach ulcers or duodenal ulcers), since the blood usually remains in the gut for a longer period of time than with lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

name: abnormal large intestine morphology
abnormal large intestine morphology
HP:0002250.def: Any abnormality of the large intestine.

name: aganglionic megacolon
aganglionic megacolon
HP:0002251.def: An abnormality resulting from a lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) that results in bowel obstruction with enlargement of the colon.

name: colonic diverticula
colonic diverticulum
HP:0002253.def: The presence of multiple diverticula of the colon.

name: intermittent diarrhea
intermittent diarrhea
HP:0002254.def: Repeated episodes of diarrhea separated by periods without diarrhea.

name: chronic rhinitis
chronic rhinitis
HP:0002257.def: Chronic inflammation of the nasal mucosa.

name: exaggerated cupid 's bow
exaggerated cupid 's bow
HP:0002263.def: More pronounced paramedian peaks and median notch of the Cupid's bow.
synonym: prominent cupid - bow of upper lip
prominent cupid - bow of upper lip

name: focal clonic seizure
focal clonic seizure
HP:0002266.def: A focal clonic seizure is a type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking, that is regularly repetitive.

name: exaggerated startle response
exaggerated startle response
HP:0002267.def: An exaggerated startle reaction in response to a sudden unexpected visual or acoustic stimulus, or a quick movement near the face.

name: paroxysmal dystonia
paroxysmal dystonia
HP:0002268.def: A form of dystonia characterized by episodes of dystonia (often hemidystonia or generalized) lasting from minutes to hours. There are no dystonic symptoms between episodes.

name: abnormality of neuronal migration
abnormality of neuronal migration
HP:0002269.def: An abnormality resulting from an anomaly of neuronal migration, i.e., of the process by which neurons travel from their origin to their final position in the brain.

name: abnormality of the autonomic nervous system
abnormality of the autonomic nervous system
HP:0002270.def: An abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.

name: horner syndrome
horner syndrome
HP:0002277.def: An abnormality resulting from a lesion of the sympathetic nervous system characterized by a combination of unilateral ptosis, miosis, and often ipsilateral hypohidrosis and conjunctival injection.

name: enlarged cisterna magna
enlarge cisterna magna
HP:0002280.def: Increase in size of the cisterna magna, one of three principal openings in the subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia mater, located between the cerebellum and the dorsal surface of the medulla oblongata.

name: gray matter heterotopia
gray matter heterotopia
HP:0002282.def: Heterotopia or neuronal heterotopia are macroscopic clusters of misplaced neurons (gray matter), most often situated along the ventricular walls or within the subcortical white matter.

name: global brain atrophy
global brain atrophy
HP:0002283.def: Unlocalized atrophy of the brain with decreased total brain matter volume and increased ventricular size.

name: fair hair
fair hair
HP:0002286.def: A lesser degree of hair pigmentation than would otherwise be expected.

name: alopecia universalis
alopecia universalis
HP:0002289.def: Loss of all hair on the entire body.

name: poliosis
poliosis
HP:0002290.def: Circumscribed depigmentation of the hair of the head or the eyelashes.

name: frontal balding
frontal balding
HP:0002292.def: Absence of hair in the anterior midline and/or parietal areas.

name: progressive hypotrichosis
progressive hypotrichosis
HP:0002296.def: Progressively reduced or lacking hair growth.

name: brittle hair
brittle hair
HP:0002299.def: Fragile, easily breakable hair, i.e., with reduced tensile strength.

name: mutism
mutism
HP:0002300.def: Inability to speak or communicate verbally past the age of typical language development.

name: hemiplegia
hemiplegia
HP:0002301.def: Paralysis (complete loss of muscle function) in the arm, leg, and in some cases the face on one side of the body.
synonym: paralysis on one side of body
paralysis on one side of body

name: akinesia
akinesia
HP:0002304.def: Inability to initiate changes in activity or movement and to perform ordinary volitional movements rapidly and easily.

name: athetosis
athetosis
HP:0002305.def: A slow, continuous, involuntary writhing movement that prevents maintenance of a stable posture. Athetosis involves continuous smooth movements that appear random and are not composed of recognizable sub-movements or movement fragments. In contrast to chorea, in athetosis, the same regions of the body are repeatedly involved. Athetosis may worsen with attempts at movement of posture, but athetosis can also occur at rest.
synonym: involuntary writhing movements in fingers , hands , toes , and feet
involuntary writhe movement in finger , hand , toe , and foot

name: drooling
drool
HP:0002307.def: Habitual flow of saliva out of the mouth.

name: chiari malformation
chiari malformation
HP:0002308.def: Chiari malformation consists of a downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils and the medulla through the foramen magnum, sometimes causing hydrocephalus as a result of obstruction of CSF outflow.

name: clumsiness
clumsiness
HP:0002312.def: Lack of physical coordination resulting in an abnormal tendency to drop items or bump into objects.

name: degeneration of the lateral corticospinal tracts
degeneration of the lateral corticospinal tract
HP:0002314.def: Deterioration of the tissues of the lateral corticospinal tracts.

name: headache
headache
HP:0002315.def: Cephalgia, or pain sensed in various parts of the head, not confined to the area of distribution of any nerve.

name: vertigo
vertigo
HP:0002321.def: An abnormal sensation of spinning while the body is actually stationary.

name: resting tremor
rest tremor
HP:0002322.def: A resting tremor occurs when muscles are at rest and becomes less noticeable or disappears when the affected muscles are moved. Resting tremors are often slow and coarse.

name: anencephaly
anencephaly
HP:0002323.def: Anencephaly is a developmental anomaly characterized by a fetus that has no calvarium, with a lack of most or all of the fetus' brain tissue. Anencephaly belongs to a collective group known as neural tube defects (NTD) and is a result of the neural tube failing to close in its rostral end during fetal development.

name: hydranencephaly
hydranencephaly
HP:0002324.def: A defect of development of the brain characterized by replacement of greater portions of the cerebral hemispheres and the corpus striatum by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and glial tissue.

name: drowsiness
drowsiness
HP:0002329.def: Abnormal feeling of sleepiness or difficulty staying awake.

name: paroxysmal drowsiness
paroxysmal drowsiness
HP:0002330.def: A neurological disorder marked by a sudden recurrent uncontrollable compulsion to sleep
synonym: a neurological disorder marked by a sudden recurrent uncontrollable compulsion to sleep
a neurological disorder mark by a sudden recurrent uncontrollable compulsion to sleep

name: recurrent paroxysmal headache
recurrent paroxysmal headache
HP:0002331.def: Repeated episodes of headache with rapid onset, reaching a peak within minutes and of short duration (less than one hour) with pain that is throbbing, pulsating, or bursting in quality.

name: lack of peer relationships
lack of peer relationship
HP:0002332.def: The state of not having relationships with peers outside of school or organized activity appropriate to developmental level. This may be caused by behavioral or physical barriers.

name: motor deterioration
motor deterioration
HP:0002333.def: Loss of previously present motor (i.e., movement) abilities.

name: abnormal cerebellar vermis morphology
abnormal cerebellar vermis morphology
HP:0002334.def: An anomaly of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: agenesis of cerebellar vermis
agenesis of cerebellar vermis
HP:0002335.def: Congenital absence of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: abnormal caudate nucleus morphology
abnormal caudate nucleus morphology
HP:0002339.def: Any structural abnormality of the caudate nucleus.

name: cervical cord compression
cervical cord compression
HP:0002341.def: Compression of the spinal cord in the cervical region, generally manifested by paresthesias and numbness, weakness, difficulty walking, abnormalities of coordination, and neck pain or stiffness.

name: intellectual disability , moderate
intellectual disability , moderate
HP:0002342.def: Moderate mental retardation is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 35-49.

name: normal pressure hydrocephalus
normal pressure hydrocephalus
HP:0002343.def: A form of hydrocephalus characterized by enlarged cerebral ventricles and normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pressure upon lumbar puncture.

name: action tremor
action tremor
HP:0002345.def: A tremor present when the limbs are active, either when outstretched in a certain position or throughout a voluntary movement.

name: head tremor
head tremor
HP:0002346.def: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting head movement.

name: focal aware seizure
focal aware seizure
HP:0002349.def: A type of focal-onset seizure in which awareness is preserved. Awareness during a seizure is defined as the patient being fully aware of themself and their environment throughout the seizure, even if immobile.
synonym: focal seizure without impairment of awareness
focal seizure without impairment of awareness
focal seizure without impairment of consciousness or awareness
focal seizure without impairment of consciousness or awareness
focal seizures without impairment of consciousness or awareness
focal seizure without impairment of consciousness or awareness
partial seizure without impairment of awareness
partial seizure without impairment of awareness

name: leukoencephalopathy
leukoencephalopathy
HP:0002352.def: This term describes abnormality of the white matter of the cerebrum resulting from damage to the myelin sheaths of nerve cells.

name: eeg abnormality
eeg abnormality
HP:0002353.def: Abnormality observed by electroencephalogram (EEG), which is used to record of the brain's spontaneous electrical activity from multiple electrodes placed on the scalp.

name: memory impairment
memory impairment
HP:0002354.def: An impairment of memory as manifested by a reduced ability to remember things such as dates and names, and increased forgetfulness.

name: writer 's cramp
writer 's cramp
HP:0002356.def: A focal dystonia of the fingers, hand, and/or forearm that appears when the affected person attempts to do a task that requires fine motor movements such as writing or playing a musical instrument.

name: sleep abnormality
sleep abnormality
HP:0002360.def: An abnormal pattern in the quality, quantity, or characteristics of sleep.

name: psychomotor deterioration
psychomotor deterioration
HP:0002361.def: Loss of previously present mental and motor abilities.

name: shuffling gait
shuffle gait
HP:0002362.def: A type of gait (walking) characterized by by dragging one's feet along or without lifting the feet fully from the ground.

name: abnormal lower motor neuron morphology
abnormal low motor neuron morphology
HP:0002366.def: Any structural anomaly of the lower motor neuron.

name: visual hallucination
visual hallucination
HP:0002367.def: Visual perception in the absence of a visual stimulus.

name: normal interictal eeg
normal interictal eeg
HP:0002372.def: Lack of observable abnormal electroencephalographic (EEG) patterns in an individual with a history of seizures. About half of individuals with epilepsy show interictal epileptiform discharges upon the first investigation. The yield can be increased by repeated studies, sleep studies, or by ambulatory EEG recordings over 24 hours. Normal interictal EEG is a sign that can be useful in the differential diagnosis.

name: febrile seizure ( within the age range of 3 months to 6 years )
febrile seizure ( within the age range of 3 month to 6 year )
HP:0002373.def: A febrile seizure is any type of seizure (most often a generalized tonic-clonic seizure) occurring with fever (at least 38 degrees Celsius) but in the absence of central nervous system infection, severe metabolic disturbance or other alternative precipitant in children between the ages of 3 months and 6 years.

name: hypokinesia
hypokinesia
HP:0002375.def: Abnormally diminished motor activity. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.

name: developmental regression
developmental regression
HP:0002376.def: Loss of developmental skills, as manifested by loss of developmental milestones.

name: obsolete paraganglioma - related cranial nerve palsy
obsolete paraganglioma - relate cranial nerve palsy
hand tremor
hand tremor
HP:0002378.def: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the hand.

name: fasciculations
fasciculation
HP:0002380.def: Fasciculations are observed as small, local, involuntary muscle contractions (twitching) visible under the skin. Fasciculations result from increased irritability of an axon (which in turn is often a manifestation of disease of a motor neuron). This leads to sporadic discharges of all the muscle fibers controlled by the axon in isolation from other motor units.

name: aphasia
aphasia
HP:0002381.def: An acquired language impairment of some or all of the abilities to produce or comprehend speech and to read or write.

name: infectious encephalitis
infectious encephalitis
HP:0002383.def: A disorder of the brain caused by an infectious agent that presents with fever, headache, and an altered level of consciousness. There may also be focal or multifocal neurologic deficits, and focal or generalized seizure activity.

name: focal impaired awareness seizure
focal impair awareness seizure
HP:0002384.def: Focal impaired awareness seizure (or focal seizure with impaired or lost awareness) is a type of focal-onset seizure characterized by some degree (which may be partial) of impairment of the person's awareness of themselves or their surroundings at any point during the seizure.
synonym: focal seizure with impairment of awareness
focal seizure with impairment of awareness
focal seizure with loss of awareness
focal seizure with loss of awareness
focal seizures with impairment of consciousness or awareness
focal seizure with impairment of consciousness or awareness
localised seizure with loss of awareness
localised seizure with loss of awareness
localized seizure with loss of awareness
localized seizure with loss of awareness
partial seizure with impairment of awareness
partial seizure with impairment of awareness
partial seizure with loss of awareness
partial seizure with loss of awareness

name: paraparesis
paraparesis
HP:0002385.def: Weakness or partial paralysis in the lower limbs.

name: cavum septum pellucidum
cavum septum pellucidum
HP:0002389.def: If the two laminae of the septum pellucidum are not fused then a fluid-filled space or cavum is present. The cavum septum pellucidum is present at birth but usually obliterates by the age of 3 to 6 months. It is up to 1cm in width and the walls are parallel. It is an enclosed space and is not part of the ventricular system or connected with the subarachnoid space.

name: eeg with polyspike wave complexes
eeg with polyspike wave complex
HP:0002392.def: The presence of complexes of repetitive spikes and waves in EEG.
synonym: eeg : spike and multispike waves , 3 - 4 hz
eeg : spike and multispike wave , 3 - 4 hz

name: lower limb hyperreflexia
low limb hyperreflexia
synonym: increased deep tendon reflexes in the lower limbs
increase deep tendon reflex in the low limb

name: cogwheel rigidity
cogwheel rigidity
HP:0002396.def: A type of rigidity in which a muscle responds with cogwheellike jerks to the use of constant force in bending the limb (i.e., it gives way in little, repeated jerks when the muscle is passively stretched).

name: degeneration of anterior horn cells
degeneration of anterior horn cell
synonym: degeneration of alpha - motor neurons in anterior horn cells of the spinal cord
degeneration of alpha - motor neuron in anterior horn cell of the spinal cord
degeneration of spinal cord anterior horn cells
degeneration of spinal cord anterior horn cell
loss of spinal cord anterior horn cells
loss of spinal cord anterior horn cell
progressive loss of anterior horn cells
progressive loss of anterior horn cell
spinal cord anterior horn cell degeneration
spinal cord anterior horn cell degeneration

name: stroke - like episode
stroke - like episode
HP:0002401.def: No consensus exists on what a stroke-like episode is, but these episodes can be functionally defined as a new neurological deficit, occurring with or without the context of seizures, which last longer than 24 hours.

name: positive romberg sign
positive romberg sign
HP:0002403.def: The patient stands with the feet placed together and balance and is asked to close his or her eyes. A loss of balance upon eye closure is a positive Romberg sign and is interpreted as indicating a deficit in proprioception.

name: thickened superior cerebellar peduncle
thicken superior cerebellar peduncle
HP:0002404.def: Increased width of the superior cerebellar peduncle.

name: limb dysmetria
limb dysmetria
HP:0002406.def: A type of dysmetria involving the limbs.
