name: cerebral arteriovenous malformation
cerebral arteriovenous malformation
HP:0002408.def: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the brain.

name: aqueductal stenosis
aqueductal stenosis
HP:0002410.def: Stenosis of the cerebral aqueduct (also known as the mesencephalic duct, aqueductus mesencephali, or aqueduct of Sylvius), which connects the third cerebral ventricle in the diencephalon to the fourth ventricle, which is between the pons and cerebellum.

name: myokymia
myokymia
HP:0002411.def: Myokymia consists of involuntary, fine, continuous, undulating contractions that spread across the affected striated muscle.

name: spina bifida
spina bifida
HP:0002414.def: Incomplete closure of the embryonic neural tube, whereby some vertebral arches remain unfused and open. The mildest form is spina bifida occulta, followed by meningocele and meningomyelocele.

name: leukodystrophy
leukodystrophy
HP:0002415.def: Leukodystrophy refers to deterioration of white matter of the brain resulting from degeneration of myelin sheaths in the CNS. Their basic defect is directly related to the synthesis and maintenance of myelin membranes. Symmetric white matter involvement at MRI is a typical finding in patients with leukodystrophies.
synonym: degeneration of white matter of brain
degeneration of white matter of brain

name: subependymal cysts
subependymal cyst
HP:0002416.def: Cerebral cysts, usually located in the wall of the caudate nucleus or in the caudothalamic groove. They are found in up to 5.2% of all neonates, using transfontanellar ultrasound in the first days of life.

name: abnormal midbrain morphology
abnormal midbrain morphology
HP:0002418.def: An abnormality of the midbrain, which has as its parts the tectum, cerebral peduncle, midbrain tegmentum and cerebral aqueduct.

name: molar tooth sign on mri
molar tooth sign on mri
HP:0002419.def: An abnormal appearance of the midbrain in axial magnetic resonance imaging in which the elongated superior cerebellar peduncles give the midbrain an appearance reminiscent of a molar or wisdom tooth.
synonym: molar tooth sign on brain imaging
molar tooth sign on brain imaging

name: poor head control
poor head control
HP:0002421.def: Difficulty to maintain correct position of the head while standing or sitting.

name: long - tract signs
long - tract sign
HP:0002423.def: Long-tract signs refer to symptoms that are attributable to the involvement of the long fiber tracts in the spinal cord, which connect the spinal cord to the brain and mediate spinal and motor functions.

name: anarthria
anarthria
HP:0002425.def: A defect in the motor ability that enables speech.

name: expressive aphasia
expressive aphasia
HP:0002427.def: Impairment of expressive language and relative preservation of receptive language abilities. That is, the patient understands language (speech, writing) but cannot express it.

name: meningocele
meningocele
HP:0002435.def: Protrusion of the meninges through a defect of the skull or vertebral column.

name: occipital meningocele
occipital meningocele
HP:0002436.def: A herniation of meninges through a congenital bone defect in the skull in the occipital region.

name: dyscalculia
dyscalculia
HP:0002442.def: A specific learning disability involving mathematics and arithmetic.

name: hypothalamic hamartoma
hypothalamic hamartoma
HP:0002444.def: The presence of a hamartoma of the hypothalamus.

name: tetraplegia
tetraplegia
HP:0002445.def: Paralysis of all four limbs, and trunk of the body below the level of an associated injury to the spinal cord. The etiology of quadriplegia is similar to that of paraplegia except that the lesion is in the cervical spinal cord rather than in the thoracic or lumbar segments of the spinal cord.

name: astrocytosis
astrocytosis
HP:0002446.def: Proliferation of astrocytes in the area of a lesion of the central nervous system.

name: abnormal motor neuron morphology
abnormal motor neuron morphology
HP:0002450.def: Any structural anomaly that affects the motor neuron.

name: limb dystonia
limb dystonia
HP:0002451.def: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the limbs.

name: abnormal globus pallidus morphology
abnormal globus pallidus morphology
HP:0002453.def: An abnormality of the globus pallidus.

name: eye of the tiger anomaly of globus pallidus
eye of the tiger anomaly of globus pallidus
HP:0002454.def: The presence, on T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, of markedly low signal intensity of the globus pallidus that surrounds a central region of high signal intensity in the anteromedial globus pallidus, producing an eye-of-the-tiger appearance. The sign is thought to represent iron accumulation in the globus pallidus.

name: distal muscle weakness
distal muscle weakness
HP:0002460.def: Reduced strength of the musculature of the distal extremities.
synonym: distal limb muscle weakness due to peripheral neuropathy
distal limb muscle weakness due to peripheral neuropathy
muscle weakness , distal limbs , due to neuronopathy
muscle weakness , distal limb , due to neuronopathy

name: dense calcifications in the cerebellar dentate nucleus
dense calcification in the cerebellar dentate nucleus
language impairment
language impairment
HP:0002463.def: Language impairment is a deficit in comprehension or production of language that includes reduced vocabulary, limited sentence structure, or impairments in written or spoken communication. Language abilities are substantially and quantifiably below age expectations.

name: spastic dysarthria
spastic dysarthria
HP:0002464.def: A type of dysarthria related to bilateral damage of the upper motor neuron tracts of the pyramidal and extra- pyramidal tracts. Speech of affected individuals is slow, effortful, and has a harsh vocal quality.

name: small cerebral cortex
small cerebral cortex
HP:0002472.def: Reduced size of the cerebral cortex.

name: expressive language delay
expressive language delay
HP:0002474.def: A delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

name: myelomeningocele
myelomeningocele
HP:0002475.def: Protrusion of the meninges and portions of the spinal cord through a defect of the vertebral column.

name: primitive reflex
primitive reflex
HP:0002476.def: The primitive reflexes are a group of behavioural motor responses which are found in normal early development, are subsequently inhibited, but may be released from inhibition by cerebral, usually frontal, damage. They are thus part of a broader group of reflexes which reflect release phenomena, such as exaggerated stretch reflexes and extensor plantars. They do however involve more complex motor responses than such simple stretch reflexes, and are often a normal feature in the neonate or infant.

name: hepatic encephalopathy
hepatic encephalopathy
HP:0002480.def: Central nervous system dysfunction in association with liver failure and characterized clinically (depending on degree of severity) by lethargy, confusion, nystagmus, decorticate posturing, spasticity, and bilateral Babinski reflexes.

name: myotonia
myotonia
HP:0002486.def: An involuntary and painless delay in the relaxation of skeletal muscle following contraction or electrical stimulation.
synonym: delayed relaxation of muscle fibers after contraction
delay relaxation of muscle fiber after contraction
delayed relaxation of muscle fibres after contraction
delay relaxation of muscle fibre after contraction

name: hyperkinetic movements
hyperkinetic movement
HP:0002487.def: Motor hyperactivity with excessive movement of muscles of the body as a whole.

name: acute leukemia
acute leukemia
HP:0002488.def: A clonal (malignant) hematopoietic disorder with an acute onset, affecting the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. The malignant cells show minimal differentiation and are called blasts, either myeloid blasts (myeloblasts) or lymphoid blasts (lymphoblasts).

name: increased csf lactate
increase csf lactate
HP:0002490.def: Increased concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: spasticity of facial muscles
spasticity of facial muscle
HP:0002491.def: Spasticity of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve.

name: abnormal corticospinal tract morphology
abnormal corticospinal tract morphology
HP:0002492.def: Abnormality of the corticospinal tract, which is the chief element of the pyramidal system (the principle motor tract) and is the only direct connection between the cerebrum and the spinal cord.
synonym: morphological abnormality of the corticospinal tract
morphological abnormality of the corticospinal tract

name: upper motor neuron dysfunction
upper motor neuron dysfunction
HP:0002493.def: A functional anomaly of the upper motor neuron. The upper motor neurons are neurons of the primary motor cortex which project to the brainstem and spinal chord via the corticonuclear, corticobulbar and corticospinal (pyramidal) tracts. They are involved in control of voluntary movements. Dysfunction leads to weakness, impairment of fine motor movements, spasticity, hyperreflexia and abnormal pyramidal signs.

name: abnormal rapid eye movement sleep
abnormal rapid eye movement sleep
HP:0002494.def: Abnormality of REM Sleep are phases of REM sleep are characterized by desynchronized EEG patterns, increases in heart rate and blood pressure, sympathetic activation, and a profound loss of muscle tone except for the eye and middle-ear muscles. There are also phases of rapid eye movements.

name: impaired vibratory sensation
impaired vibratory sensation
HP:0002495.def: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to bony prominences such as the malleoli at the ankles or the metacarpal-phalangeal joints. There is a slow decay of vibration from the tuning fork. The degree of vibratory sense loss can be crudely estimated by counting the number of seconds that the examiner can perceive the vibration longer than the patient.

name: abnormal cerebral white matter morphology
abnormal cerebral white matter morphology
HP:0002500.def: An abnormality of the cerebral white matter.
synonym: abnormality of the cerebral white matter
abnormality of the cerebral white matter
cortical white matter abnormalities seen on mri
cortical white matter abnormality see on mri

name: calcification of the small brain vessels
calcification of the small brain vessel
HP:0002504.def: Deposition of calcium salts within small blood vessels of the brain.

name: loss of ambulation
loss of ambulation
HP:0002505.def: Inability to walk in a person who previous had the ability to walk.

name: diffuse cerebral atrophy
diffuse cerebral atrophy
HP:0002506.def: Diffuse unlocalised atrophy affecting the cerebrum.

name: semilobar holoprosencephaly
semilobar holoprosencephaly
HP:0002507.def: A type of holoprosencephaly in which the left and right frontal and parietal lobes are fused and the interhemispheric fissure is only present posteriorly.

name: brainstem dysplasia
brainstem dysplasia
HP:0002508.def: A developmental structural anomaly of the stalk-like part of the brain that comprises the midbrain (aka mesencephalon), the pons (aka pons Varolii), and the medulla oblongata, and connects the cerebral hemispheres with the cervical spinal cord.

name: limb hypertonia
limb hypertonia
synonym: increased muscle tone of arm or leg
increased muscle tone of arm or leg

name: spastic tetraplegia
spastic tetraplegia
HP:0002510.def: Spastic paralysis affecting all four limbs.

name: alzheimer disease
alzheimer disease
HP:0002511.def: A degenerative disease of the brain characterized by the insidious onset of dementia. Impairment of memory, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe apraxia and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathologically by severe cortical atrophy and the triad of senile plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, and neuropil threads.
synonym: late - onset form of familial alzheimer disease
late - onset form of familial alzheimer disease

name: cerebral calcification
cerebral calcification
HP:0002514.def: The presence of calcium deposition within brain structures.
synonym: abnormal deposits of calcium in the brain
abnormal deposit of calcium in the brain

name: waddling gait
waddle gait
HP:0002515.def: Weakness of the hip girdle and upper thigh muscles, for instance in myopathies, leads to an instability of the pelvis on standing and walking. If the muscles extending the hip joint are affected, the posture in that joint becomes flexed and lumbar lordosis increases. The patients usually have difficulties standing up from a sitting position. Due to weakness in the gluteus medius muscle, the hip on the side of the swinging leg drops with each step (referred to as Trendelenburg sign). The gait appears waddling. The patients frequently attempt to counteract the dropping of the hip on the swinging side by bending the trunk towards the side which is in the stance phase (in the German language literature this is referred to as Duchenne sign). Similar gait patterns can be caused by orthopedic conditions when the origin and the insertion site of the gluteus medius muscle are closer to each other than normal, for instance due to a posttraumatic elevation of the trochanter or pseudarthrosis of the femoral neck.

name: increased intracranial pressure
increase intracranial pressure
HP:0002516.def: An increase of the pressure inside the cranium (skull) and thereby in the brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid.

name: abnormal periventricular white matter morphology
abnormal periventricular white matter morphology
HP:0002518.def: A structural abnormality of the myelinated axons (white matter) located near the cerebral ventricles.
synonym: abnormality of the periventricular white matter
abnormality of the periventricular white matter

name: hypnagogic hallucination
hypnagogic hallucination
HP:0002519.def: Hypnagogic hallucinations are brief hallucinations that occur as you are falling asleep.

name: hypsarrhythmia
hypsarrhythmia
HP:0002521.def: Hypsarrhythmia is abnormal interictal high amplitude waves and a background of irregular spikes. There is continuous (during wakefulness), high-amplitude (>200 Hz), generalized polymorphic slowing with no organized background and multifocal spikes demonstrated by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: areflexia of lower limbs
areflexia of low limb
HP:0002522.def: Inability to elicit tendon reflexes in the lower limbs.

name: cataplexy
cataplexy
HP:0002524.def: A sudden and transient episode of bilateral loss of muscle tone, often triggered by emotions.

name: deficit in nonword repetition
deficit in nonword repetition
HP:0002526.def: Impaired ability to repeat non-word sounds. Nonword repetition (NWR) is a measure of short-term phonological memory.

name: granulovacuolar degeneration
granulovacuolar degeneration
HP:0002528.def: Electron-dense granules within double membrane-bound cytoplasmic vacuoles.

name: neuronal loss in central nervous system
neuronal loss in central nervous system
axial dystonia
axial dystonia
HP:0002530.def: A type of dystonia that affects the midline muscles, i.e., the chest, abdominal, and back muscles.

name: abnormal posturing
abnormal posturing
HP:0002533.def: Involuntary flexion or extension of the arms and legs.

name: abnormal cortical gyration
abnormal cortical gyration
HP:0002536.def: An abnormality of the gyri (i.e., the ridges) of the cerebral cortex of the brain.

name: abnormal cerebral cortex morphology
abnormal cerebral cortex morphology
HP:0002538.def: Any structural abnormality of the cerebral cortex.

name: cortical dysplasia
cortical dysplasia
HP:0002539.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cerebral cortex.

name: olivopontocerebellar atrophy
olivopontocerebellar atrophy
HP:0002542.def: Neuronal degeneration in the cerebellum, pontine nuclei, and inferior olivary nucleus.

name: retrocollis
retrocollis
HP:0002544.def: A form of torticollis in which the head is drawn back, either due to a permanent contractures of neck extensor muscles, or to a spasmodic contracture.

name: patchy demyelination of subcortical white matter
patchy demyelination of subcortical white matter
HP:0002545.def: Patchy loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

name: parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication
parkinsonism with favorable response to dopaminergic medication
HP:0002548.def: Parkinsonism is a clinical syndrome that is a feature of a number of different diseases, including Parkinson disease itself, other neurodegenerative diseases such as progressive supranuclear palsy, and as a side-effect of some neuroleptic medications. Some but not all individuals with Parkinsonism show responsiveness to dopaminergic medication defined as a substantial reduction of amelioration of the component signs of Parkinsonism (including mainly tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, and postural instability) upon administration of dopaminergic medication.
synonym: parkinsonism with favourable response to dopaminergic medication
parkinsonism with favourable response to dopaminergic medication

name: deficit in phonologic short - term memory
deficit in phonologic short - term memory
HP:0002549.def: Impaired ability to repeat non-word sounds. The test for nonword repetition involves the repetition of nonsensical words of increasing length and complexity and is regarded as a measure of phonological (speech sound) processing and short-term memory

name: highly arched eyebrow
highly arch eyebrow
HP:0002553.def: Increased height of the central portion of the eyebrow, forming a crescent, semicircular, or inverted U shape.

name: supernumerary nipple
supernumerary nipple
HP:0002558.def: Presence of more than two nipples.

name: absent nipple
absent nipple
HP:0002561.def: Congenital failure to develop, and absence of, the nipple.

name: low - set nipples
low - set nipple
HP:0002562.def: Placement of the nipples at a lower than normal location.

name: constrictive pericarditis
constrictive pericarditis
HP:0002563.def: Presence of a thickened, fibrotic pericardium that forms a non-compliant shell around the heart, and resulting from chronic inflammation of the pericardium.

name: obsolete malformation of the heart and great vessels
obsolete malformation of the heart and great vessel
intestinal malrotation
intestinal malrotation
HP:0002566.def: An abnormality of the intestinal rotation and fixation that normally occurs during the development of the gut. This can lead to volvulus, or twisting of the intestine that causes obstruction and necrosis.

name: steatorrhea
steatorrhea
HP:0002570.def: Greater than normal amounts of fat in the feces. This is a result of malabsorption of lipids in the small intestine and results in frothy foul-smelling fecal matter that floats.

name: achalasia
achalasia
HP:0002571.def: A disorder of esophageal motility characterized by the inability of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax during swallowing and by inadequate or lacking peristalsis in the lower half of the body of the esophagus.

name: hematochezia
hematochezia
HP:0002573.def: The passage of fresh (red) blood per anus, usually in or with stools. Most rectal bleeding comes from the colon, rectum, or anus.

name: episodic abdominal pain
episodic abdominal pain
HP:0002574.def: An intermittent form of abdominal pain.

name: tracheoesophageal fistula
tracheoesophageal fistula
HP:0002575.def: An abnormal connection (fistula) between the esophagus and the trachea.
synonym: abnormal connection between trachea and esophagus
abnormal connection between trachea and esophagus
abnormal connection between trachea and oesophagus
abnormal connection between trachea and oesophagus

name: intussusception
intussusception
HP:0002576.def: An abnormality of the intestine in which part of the intestine invaginates (telescopes) into another part of the intestine.

name: gastroparesis
gastroparesis
HP:0002578.def: Decreased strength of the muscle layer of stomach, which leads to a decreased ability to empty the contents of the stomach despite the absence of obstruction.

name: gastrointestinal dysmotility
gastrointestinal dysmotility
HP:0002579.def: Abnormal intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis, related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.

name: volvulus
volvulus
HP:0002580.def: Abnormal twisting of a portion of intestine around itself or around a stalk of mesentery tissue.

name: atrophic gastritis
atrophic gastritis
HP:0002582.def: Atrophic gastritis (AG) is a histopathological entity that is characterized by chronic inflammation of the gastric mucosa with loss of gastric glandular cells and replacement by intestinal-type epithelium, pyloric-type glands, and fibrous tissue.

name: colitis
colitis
HP:0002583.def: Colitis refers to an inflammation of the colon and is often used to describe an inflammation of the large intestine (colon, cecum and rectum). Colitides may be acute and self-limited or chronic, and broadly fit into the category of digestive diseases.

name: projectile vomiting
projectile vomit
HP:0002587.def: Vomiting that ejects the gastric contents with great force.

name: duodenal ulcer
duodenal ulcer
HP:0002588.def: An erosion of the mucous membrane in a portion of the duodenum.

name: polyphagia
polyphagia
HP:0002591.def: A neurological anomaly with gross overeating associated with an abnormally strong desire or need to eat.

name: gastric ulcer
gastric ulcer
HP:0002592.def: An ulcer, that is, an erosion of an area of the gastric mucous membrane.

name: intestinal lymphangiectasia
intestinal lymphangiectasia
HP:0002593.def: Angiectasia of lymph vessels (i.e., dilatation of lymphatic vessels) in the intestines.

name: ileus
ileus
HP:0002595.def: Acute obstruction of the intestines preventing passage of the contents of the intestines.

name: head titubation
head titubation
HP:0002599.def: A head tremor of moderate speed (3 to 4 Hz) in the anterior-posterior direction.

name: hyporeflexia of lower limbs
hyporeflexia of low limb
HP:0002600.def: Reduced intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in the lower limbs. Reflexes are elicited by stretching the tendon of a muscle, e.g., by tapping.

name: paresis of extensor muscles of the big toe
paresis of extensor muscle of the big toe
gastrointestinal telangiectasia
gastrointestinal telangiectasia
synonym: small , enlarged blood vessels near skin
small , enlarge blood vessel near skin

name: hepatic necrosis
hepatic necrosis
HP:0002605.def: The presence of cell death (necrosis) affecting the liver.

name: bowel incontinence
bowel incontinence
HP:0002607.def: Involuntary fecal soiling in adults and children who have usually already been toilet trained.

name: celiac disease
celiac disease
HP:0002608.def: Celiac disease (CD) is an autoimmune condition affecting the small intestine, triggered by the ingestion of gluten, the protein fraction of wheat, barley, and rye. Clinical manifestations of CD are highly variable and include both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal features. The hallmark of CD is an immune-mediated enteropathy. This term is included because the occurence of CD is seen as a feature of a number of other diseases.

name: congenital hepatic fibrosis
congenital hepatic fibrosis
HP:0002612.def: The presence of fibrosis of that part of the liver with congenital onset.
synonym: excessive buildup of connective tissue and scarring of liver at birth
excessive buildup of connective tissue and scarring of liver at birth

name: biliary cirrhosis
biliary cirrhosis
HP:0002613.def: Progressive destruction of the small-to-medium bile ducts of the intrahepatic biliary tree, which leads to progressive cholestasis and often end-stage liver disease.

name: hepatic periportal necrosis
hepatic periportal necrosis
HP:0002614.def: A type of hepatic necrosis that is concentrated around the necrosis of hepatocytes localized around the intrahepatic branch of portal vein.

name: aortic root aneurysm
aortic root aneurysm
HP:0002616.def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic root.
synonym: bulge in wall of root of large artery that carries blood away from heart
bulge in wall of root of large artery that carry blood away from heart

name: vascular dilatation
vascular dilatation
HP:0002617.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of an atery, vein or the heart.
synonym: wider than typical opening or gap
wide than typical opening or gap

name: atherosclerosis
atherosclerosis
HP:0002621.def: A condition characterized by patchy atheromas or atherosclerotic plaques which develop in the walls of medium-sized and large arteries and can lead to arterial stenosis with reduced or blocked blood flow.

name: overriding aorta
override aorta
HP:0002623.def: An overriding aorta is a congenital heart defect where the aorta is positioned directly over a ventricular septal defect, instead of over the left ventricle. The result is that the aorta receives some blood from the right ventricle, which reduces the amount of oxygen in the blood. It is one of the four conditions of the Tetralogy of Fallot. The aortic root can be displaced toward the front (anteriorly) or directly above the septal defect, but it is always abnormally located to the right of the root of the pulmonary artery. The degree of override is quite variable, with 5-95% of the valve being connected to the right ventricle.

name: deep venous thrombosis
deep venous thrombosis
HP:0002625.def: Formation of a blot clot in a deep vein. The clot often blocks blood flow, causing swelling and pain. The deep veins of the leg are most often affected.
synonym: blood clot in a deep vein
blood clot in a deep vein

name: venous varicosities of celiac and mesenteric vessels
venous varicosity of celiac and mesenteric vessel
HP:0002626.def: Elongated and tortuous mesenteric veins, which comprise the inferior mesenteric vein and the superior mesenteric vein.
synonym: venous varicosities of coeliac and mesenteric vessels
venous varicosity of coeliac and mesenteric vessel

name: right aortic arch with mirror image branching
right aortic arch with mirror image branching
HP:0002627.def: The aortic arch crosses the right mainstem bronchus and not the left mainstem bronchus, but does not result in the creation of a vascular ring. The first branch is the left brachiocephalic artery which divides into the left carotid artery and left subclavian artery, the second branch is the right carotid artery, the third branch is the right subclavian artery.

name: gastrointestinal arteriovenous malformation
gastrointestinal arteriovenous malformation
HP:0002629.def: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the gastrointestinal tract.

name: fat malabsorption
fat malabsorption
HP:0002630.def: Abnormality of the absorption of fat from the gastrointestinal tract.

name: arteriosclerosis
arteriosclerosis
HP:0002634.def: Sclerosis (hardening) of the arteries with increased thickness of the wall of arteries as well as increased stiffness and a loss of elasticity.

name: type iv atherosclerotic lesion
type iv atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0002635.def: In type IV atherosclerotic lesions a dense accumulation of extracellular lipid occupies an extensive but well-defined region of the intima. This type of extracellular lipid accumulation is known as the lipid core. A fibrous tissue increase is not a feature, and complications such as defects of the lesion surface and thrombosis are not present. The type IV lesion is also known as atheroma. Type IV is the first lesion considered advanced in this classification because of the severe intimal disorganization caused by the lipid core. The characteristic core appears to develop from an increase and the consequent confluence of the small isolated pools of extracellular lipid that characterize type III lesions. The increase in lipid is believed to result from continued insudation from the plasma. Type IV lesions, when they first appear in younger people, are found in the same locations as adaptive intimal thickenings of the eccentric type. Thus, atheroma is, at least initially, an eccentric lesion.

name: budd - chiari syndrome
budd - chiari syndrome
HP:0002639.def: Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) is caused by obstruction of hepatic venous outflow at any level from the small hepatic veins to the junction of the inferior vena cava (IVC) with the right atrium, 1 and occurs in 1/100,000 of the general population worldwide. The most common presentation is with ascites, but can range from fulminant hepatic failure (FHF) to asymptomatic forms. Obstruction of hepatic venous outflow is mainly caused by primary intravascular thrombosis, which can occur suddenly or be repeated over time, accompanied by some revascularization, accounting for the variable parenchymal hepatic damage and histologic presentation. Budd-Chiari syndrome is thus a disease, but since it occurs as a manifestation of several other diseases, this term is kept for the present for convenience.

name: rickets
rickets
HP:0002748.def: Rickets is divided into two major categories including calcipenic and phosphopenic. Hypophosphatemia is described as a common manifestation of both categories. Hypophosphatemic rickets is the most common type of rickets that is characterized by low levels of serum phosphate, resistance to ultraviolet radiation or vitamin D intake. There are several issues involved in hypophosphatemic rickets such as calcium, vitamin D, phosphorus deficiencies. Moreover, other disorder can be associated with its occurrence such as absorption defects due to pancreatic, intestinal, gastric, and renal disorders and hepatobiliary disease. Symptoms are usually seen in childhood and can be varied in severity. Severe forms may be linked to bowing of the legs, poor bone growth, and short stature as well as joint and bone pain. Hypophosphatemic rickets are associated with renal excretion of phosphate, hypophosphatemia, and mineral defects in bones. The familial type of the disease is the most common type of rickets.

name: obstructive sleep apnea
obstructive sleep apnea
HP:0002870.def: Obstructive Sleep Apnea is a condition characterized by the obstruction of the airway and pauses in breathing during sleep, which occur multiple times throughout the night. It is related to the relaxation of muscle tone that typically happens during sleep, leading to a partial collapse of the soft tissues in the airway and causing airflow obstruction.

name: central apnea
central apnea
HP:0002871.def: Apnea resulting from depression of the respiratory centers in the medulla oblongata. There is a lack of respiratory effort rather than obstruction of airflow.

name: apneic episodes precipitated by illness , fatigue , stress
apneic episode precipitate by illness , fatigue , stress
HP:0002872.def: Recurrent episodes of apnea that are precipitated by factors such as illness, fatigue, or stress.
synonym: episodic apnea induced by febrile illness or stress
episodic apnea induce by febrile illness or stress

name: exertional dyspnea
exertional dyspnea
HP:0002875.def: Perceived difficulty to breathe that occurs with exercise or exertion and improves with rest.
synonym: shortness of breathing upon physical activity
shortness of breathe upon physical activity

name: nocturnal hypoventilation
nocturnal hypoventilation
HP:0002877.def: An abnormal reduction in alveolar ventilation occuring during sleep. This is characterized by a rise in arterial carbon dioxide.

name: respiratory failure
respiratory failure
HP:0002878.def: A severe form of respiratory insufficiency characterized by inadequate gas exchange such that the levels of oxygen or carbon dioxide cannot be maintained within normal limits.

name: anisospondyly
anisospondyly
HP:0002879.def: Abnormally increased variability of the size of the vertebral bodies.

name: sudden episodic apnea
sudden episodic apnea
HP:0002882.def: Recurrent bouts of sudden, severe apnea that may be life-threatening.

name: hyperventilation
hyperventilation
HP:0002883.def: Hyperventilation refers to an increased pulmonary ventilation rate that is faster than necessary for the exchange of gases. Hyperventilation can result from increased frequency of breathing, an increased tidal volume, or both, and leads to an excess intake of oxygen and the blowing off of carbon dioxide.

name: hepatoblastoma
hepatoblastoma
HP:0002884.def: A kind of neoplasm of the liver that originates from immature liver precursor cells and macroscopically is composed of tissue resembling fetal or mature liver cells or bile ducts.

name: medulloblastoma
medulloblastoma
HP:0002885.def: A rapidly growing embryonic tumor arising in the posterior part of the cerebellar vermis and neuroepithelial roof of the fourth ventricle in children. More rarely, medulloblastoma arises in the cerebellum in adults.

name: vagal paraganglioma
vagal paraganglioma
HP:0002886.def: A tumor that develops in the retrostyloid compartment of the parapharyngeal space, arising from an island of paraganglion tissue derived from the neural crest that is located on the vagus nerve.

name: ependymoma
ependymoma
HP:0002888.def: The presence of an ependymoma of the central nervous system.

name: thyroid carcinoma
thyroid carcinoma
HP:0002890.def: The presence of a carcinoma of the thyroid gland.

name: uterine leiomyosarcoma
uterine leiomyosarcoma
HP:0002891.def: The presence of a leiomyosarcoma of the uterus.

name: pituitary adenoma
pituitary adenoma
HP:0002893.def: A benign epithelial tumor derived from intrinsic cells of the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary).

name: neoplasm of the pancreas
neoplasm of the pancreas
HP:0002894.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the pancreas.

name: papillary thyroid carcinoma
papillary thyroid carcinoma
HP:0002895.def: The presence of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland.

name: neoplasm of the liver
neoplasm of the liver
HP:0002896.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the liver.

name: parathyroid adenoma
parathyroid adenoma
HP:0002897.def: A benign tumor of the parathyroid gland that can cause hyperparathyroidism.

name: hypokalemia
hypokalemia
HP:0002900.def: An abnormally decreased potassium concentration in the blood.

name: hypocalcemia
hypocalcemia
HP:0002901.def: An abnormally decreased calcium concentration in the blood.

name: hyponatremia
hyponatremia
HP:0002902.def: An abnormally decreased sodium concentration in the blood.

name: hyperbilirubinemia
hyperbilirubinemia
HP:0002904.def: An increased amount of bilirubin in the blood.

name: hyperphosphatemia
hyperphosphatemia
HP:0002905.def: An abnormally increased phosphate concentration in the blood.

name: microscopic hematuria
microscopic hematuria
HP:0002907.def: Microscopic hematuria detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine.
synonym: small amount of blood in urine
small amount of blood in urine

name: generalized aminoaciduria
generalize aminoaciduria
HP:0002909.def: An increased concentration of all types of amino acid in the urine.

name: elevated hepatic transaminase
elevate hepatic transaminase
HP:0002910.def: Elevations of the levels of SGOT and SGPT in the serum. SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) are transaminases primarily found in the liver and heart and are released into the bloodstream as the result of liver or heart damage. SGOT and SGPT are used clinically mainly as markers of liver damage.

name: methylmalonic acidemia
methylmalonic acidemia
HP:0002912.def: Increased concentration of methylmalonic acid in the blood.

name: myoglobinuria
myoglobinuria
HP:0002913.def: Presence of myoglobin in the urine.

name: hyperchloriduria
hyperchloriduria
HP:0002914.def: An increased concentration of chloride in the urine.

name: hypomagnesemia
hypomagnesemia
HP:0002917.def: An abnormally decreased magnesium concentration in the blood.

name: hypermagnesemia
hypermagnesemia
HP:0002918.def: An abnormally increased magnesium concentration in the blood.

name: ketonuria
ketonuria
HP:0002919.def: High levels of ketone bodies (acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, and acetone) in the urine. Ketone bodies are insignificant in the blood and urine of normal individuals in the postprandial or overnight-fasted state.

name: decreased circulating acth concentration
decrease circulate acth concentration
HP:0002920.def: The concentration of corticotropin, also known as adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), is below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal cerebrospinal fluid morphology
abnormal cerebrospinal fluid morphology
HP:0002921.def: An abnormality of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: increased csf protein concentration
increase csf protein concentration
HP:0002922.def: Increased concentration of protein in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: rheumatoid factor positive
rheumatoid factor positive
HP:0002923.def: The presence in the serum of an autoantibody directed against the Fc portion of IgG.

name: elevated circulating thyroid - stimulating hormone concentration
elevate circulate thyroid - stimulate hormone concentration
HP:0002925.def: Increased concentration of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood circulation.

name: abnormality of thyroid physiology
abnormality of thyroid physiology
HP:0002926.def: An abnormal functionality of the thyroid gland.

name: histidinuria
histidinuria
HP:0002927.def: An increased concentration of histidine in the urine.

name: decreased activity of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
decreased activity of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
synonym: decreased activity of the pdh complex
decreased activity of the pdh complex

name: impaired sensitivity to thyroid hormone
impaired sensitivity to thyroid hormone
HP:0002930.def: Reduced sensitivity of end organs to thyroid hormone characterized by elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed thyroid stimulating hormone.
synonym: elevated serum levels of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed tsh
elevate serum level of free thyroid hormone with nonsuppressed tsh
end - organ unresponsiveness to thyroid hormone
end - organ unresponsiveness to thyroid hormone

name: aldehyde oxidase deficiency
aldehyde oxidase deficiency
HP:0002932.def: A reduction in aldehyde oxidase level.

name: ventral hernia
ventral hernia
HP:0002933.def: Ventral hernia refers to a condition in which abdominal contents protrude through a weakened portion of the abdominal wall.

name: distal sensory impairment
distal sensory impairment
HP:0002936.def: An abnormal reduction in sensation in the distal portions of the extremities.
synonym: distal sensory impairment in lower limbs
distal sensory impairment in low limb
distal sensory impairment of the lower extremities
distal sensory impairment of the low extremity
distal sensory loss , upper and lower limbs
distal sensory loss , upper and low limb

name: hemivertebrae
hemivertebrae
HP:0002937.def: Absence of one half of the vertebral body.

name: lumbar hyperlordosis
lumbar hyperlordosis
HP:0002938.def: An abnormal accentuation of the inward curvature of the spine in the lumbar region.
synonym: excessive inward curvature of lower spine
excessive inward curvature of low spine

name: thoracic kyphosis
thoracic kyphosis
HP:0002942.def: Over curvature of the thoracic region, leading to a round back or if sever to a hump.

name: intervertebral space narrowing
intervertebral space narrowing
HP:0002945.def: Decreased height of the intervertebral disk.

name: cervical kyphosis
cervical kyphosis
HP:0002947.def: Exaggerated convexity of the cervical vertebral column, causing the cervical spine to bow outwards and take on a rounded appearance.

name: vertebral fusion
vertebral fusion
HP:0002948.def: A developmental defect leading to the union of two adjacent vertebrae.

name: fused cervical vertebrae
fused cervical vertebra
HP:0002949.def: A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more cervical vertebral bodies with one another.

name: partial absence of cerebellar vermis
partial absence of cerebellar vermis
HP:0002951.def: Congenital absence of a part of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: vertebral compression fracture
vertebral compression fracture
synonym: compression fracture of a vertebral body
compression fracture of a vertebral body

name: granulomatosis
granulomatosis
HP:0002955.def: A granulomatous inflammation leading to multiple granuloma formation, which is a specific type of inflammation. A granuloma is a focal compact collection of inflammatory cells, mononuclear cells predominating, usually as a result of the persistence of a non-degradable product and of active cell mediated hypersensitivity.

name: immune dysregulation
immune dysregulation
HP:0002958.def: Altered immune function characterized by lymphoid proliferation, immune activation, and excessive autoreactivity often leading to autoimmune/inflammatory complications.

name: impaired ig class switch recombination
impaired ig class switch recombination
HP:0002959.def: An impairment of the class-switch recombination process that normally leads B lymphocytes to produce IgG, IgA, or IgE.

name: autoimmunity
autoimmunity
HP:0002960.def: The occurrence of an immune reaction against the organism's own cells or tissues.

name: dysgammaglobulinemia
dysgammaglobulinemia
HP:0002961.def: Selective deficiency of one or more, but not all, classes of immunoglobulins.

name: abnormal delayed hypersensitivity skin test
abnormal delay hypersensitivity skin test
HP:0002963.def: Delay in cutaneous immune reaction to specific antigens mediated not by antibodies but by cells. The delayed hypersensitivity test is an immune function test measuring the presence of activated T cells that recognize a specific antigen and is performed by injecting a small amount of the antigen into the skin. The area of the injection is examined 48-72 hours thereafter.

name: cutaneous anergy
cutaneous anergy
HP:0002965.def: Inability to react to a delayed hypersensitivity skin test.
synonym: absence of delayed hypersensitivity skin test
absence of delayed hypersensitivity skin test
lack of delayed skin hypersensitivity reaction
lack of delayed skin hypersensitivity reaction

name: cubitus valgus
cubitus valgus
HP:0002967.def: Abnormal positioning in which the elbows are turned out.

name: genu varum
genu varum
HP:0002970.def: A positional abnormality marked by outward bowing of the legs in which the knees stay wide apart when a person stands with the feet and ankles together.

name: absent microvilli on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes
absent microvilli on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocyte
HP:0002971.def: Absence of the fingerlike protrusive, actin-dependent structures found on the surface of peripheral blood lymphocytes.

name: reduced delayed hypersensitivity
reduce delayed hypersensitivity
HP:0002972.def: Decreased ability to react to a delayed hypersensitivity skin test.
synonym: decreased reactivity to skin test antigens
decrease reactivity to skin test antigen

name: abnormal forearm morphology
abnormal forearm morphology
HP:0002973.def: An abnormality of the lower arm.

name: radioulnar synostosis
radioulnar synostosis
HP:0002974.def: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the radius and the ulna.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia involving the central nervous system
aplasia / hypoplasia involve the central nervous system
HP:0002977.def: Absence or underdevelopment of tissue in the central nervous system.
synonym: absent / underdeveloped central nervous system tissue
absent / underdeveloped central nervous system tissue

name: bowing of the legs
bowing of the leg
HP:0002979.def: A bending or abnormal curvature affecting a long bone of the leg.

name: abnormality of the calf
abnormality of the calf
HP:0002981.def: An abnormality of the calf, i.e. of the posterior part of the lower leg.

name: tibial bowing
tibial bowing
HP:0002982.def: A bending or abnormal curvature of the tibia.

name: micromelia
micromelia
HP:0002983.def: The presence of abnormally small extremities.
synonym: smaller or shorter than typical limbs
small or short than typical limb

name: radial bowing
radial bowing
HP:0002986.def: A bending or abnormal curvature of the radius.
synonym: bowing of outer large bone of the forearm
bowing of out large bone of the forearm
bowing of radius bone of the forearm
bowing of radius bone of the forearm

name: elbow flexion contracture
elbow flexion contracture
HP:0002987.def: An elbow contracture that limits the ability of the elbow joint to be extended (straightened), meaning that the elbow is fixed in an flexed (bent) position.
synonym: fixed flexion at the elbow joint
fix flexion at the elbow joint

name: abnormal fibula morphology
abnormal fibula morphology
HP:0002991.def: An anomaly of the calf bone (fibula), one of the two bones of the calf.

name: patellar dislocation
patellar dislocation
HP:0002999.def: The kneecap normally is located within the groove termed trochlea on the distal femur and can slide up and down in it. Patellar dislocation occurs if the patella fully dislocates out of the groove.

name: breast carcinoma
breast carcinoma
HP:0003002.def: The presence of a carcinoma of the breast.

name: ganglioneuroma
ganglioneuroma
HP:0003005.def: A benign neoplasm that usually arises from the sympathetic trunk in the mediastinum, representing a tumor of the sympathetic nerve fibers arising from neural crest cells.

name: neuroblastoma
neuroblastoma
HP:0003006.def: Neuroblastoma is a solid tumor that originate in neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Most neuroblastomas originate in the abdomen, and most abdominal neuroblastomas originate in the adrenal gland. Neuroblastomas can also originate in the thorax, usually in the posterior mediastinum.

name: prolonged bleeding time
prolong bleeding time
HP:0003010.def: Prolongation of the time taken for a standardized skin cut of fixed depth and length to stop bleeding.

name: abnormality of the musculature
abnormality of the musculature
HP:0003011.def: Abnormality originating in one or more muscles, i.e., of the set of muscles of body.

name: bulging epiphyses
bulging epiphysis
HP:0003013.def: A morphological abnormality of epiphyses whereby they are abnormally outwardly curving (protuberant).

name: flared metaphysis
flare metaphysis
HP:0003015.def: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones.
synonym: flared wide portion of long bone
flare wide portion of long bone
marked metaphyseal flaring of long bones
mark metaphyseal flaring of long bone

name: metaphyseal widening
metaphyseal widening
HP:0003016.def: Abnormal widening of the metaphyseal regions of long bones.
synonym: broad wide portion of long bone
broad wide portion of long bone

name: abnormality of the wrist
abnormality of the wrist
HP:0003019.def: Abnormality of the wrist, the structure connecting the hand and the forearm.

name: metaphyseal cupping
metaphyseal cup
HP:0003021.def: Metaphyseal cupping refers to an inward bulging of the metaphyseal profile giving the metaphysis a cup-like appearance.

name: bowing of limbs due to multiple fractures
bowing of limb due to multiple fracture
HP:0003023.def: Curvature of the shafts of the long bones due to multiple fractures.
synonym: bowed limbs due to multiple fractures
bow limb due to multiple fracture

name: metaphyseal irregularity
metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0003025.def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphyses.
synonym: irregular wide portion of a long bone
irregular wide portion of a long bone

name: short long bone
short long bone
HP:0003026.def: One or more abnormally short long bone.

name: mesomelia
mesomelia
HP:0003027.def: Shortening of the middle parts of the limbs (forearm and lower leg) in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
synonym: disproportionately short middle portion of limb
disproportionately short middle portion of limb

name: abnormality of the ankle
abnormality of the ankle
HP:0003028.def: An anomaly of the joint that connects the foot with the leg.

name: ulnar bowing
ulnar bowing
HP:0003031.def: Bending of the diaphysis (shaft) of the ulna.

name: diaphyseal sclerosis
diaphyseal sclerosis
HP:0003034.def: An elevation in bone density in one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
synonym: increased bone density in shaft of long bone
increase bone density in shaft of long bone

name: enlarged joints
enlarged joint
HP:0003037.def: Increase in size of one or more joints.

name: humeroradial synostosis
humeroradial synostosis
HP:0003041.def: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the radius and the humerus.
synonym: fusion of upper and lower arm bones
fusion of upper and low arm bone

name: elbow dislocation
elbow dislocation
HP:0003042.def: Dislocation of the distal humerus out of the elbow joint, where the radius, ulna, and humerus meet.

name: abnormal shoulder morphology
abnormal shoulder morphology
HP:0003043.def: An abnormality of the shoulder, which is defined as the structures surrounding the shoulder joint where the humerus attaches to the scapula.

name: shoulder flexion contracture
shoulder flexion contracture
HP:0003044.def: Chronic reduction in active and passive mobility of the shoulder joint due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.

name: radial head subluxation
radial head subluxation
HP:0003048.def: Partial dislocation of the head of the radius.

name: enlarged metaphyses
enlarge metaphyses
HP:0003051.def: Abnormal increase in size of one or more metaphyses.
synonym: enlarged wide portion of a long bone
enlarge wide portion of a long bone

name: abnormality of the humerus
abnormality of the humerus
HP:0003063.def: An abnormality of the humerus (i.e., upper arm bone).

name: limited knee extension
limited knee extension
HP:0003066.def: Reduced ability to extend (straighten) the knee joint.

name: madelung deformity
madelung deformity
HP:0003067.def: An anomaly related to partial closure, or failure of development of the ulnar side of the distal radial growth plate, which results in an arrest of epiphyseal growth of the medial and volar portions of the distal radius. This leads to shortening of the radius and relative overgrowth of the ulna.

name: hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia
HP:0003072.def: An abnormally increased calcium concentration in the blood.

name: hypoalbuminemia
hypoalbuminemia
HP:0003073.def: Reduction in the concentration of albumin in the blood.

name: hyperglycemia
hyperglycemia
HP:0003074.def: An increased concentration of glucose in the blood.

name: hypoproteinemia
hypoproteinemia
HP:0003075.def: A decreased concentration of protein in the blood.

name: glycosuria
glycosuria
HP:0003076.def: An increased concentration of glucose in the urine.

name: hyperlipidemia
hyperlipidemia
HP:0003077.def: An elevated lipid concentration in the blood.

name: defective dna repair after ultraviolet radiation damage
defective dna repair after ultraviolet radiation damage
hydroxyprolinuria
hydroxyprolinuria
HP:0003080.def: An increased concentration of 4-hydroxy-L-proline in the urine.

name: increased urinary potassium
increase urinary potassium
HP:0003081.def: An increased concentration of potassium(1+) in the urine.

name: dislocated radial head
dislocate radial head
HP:0003083.def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint.

name: fractures of the long bones
fracture of the long bone
HP:0003084.def: An increased tendency to fractures of the long bones (Mainly, the femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius, and ulna).

name: hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
HP:0003090.def: Underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
synonym: underdevelopment of the innermost thighbone end part
underdevelopment of the innermost thighbone end part

name: trophic limb changes
trophic limb change
HP:0003091.def: Trophic changes occurring in a limb.

name: limited hip extension
limited hip extension
HP:0003093.def: Limitation of the extension of the hip, i.e., decreased ability to straighten the hip joint and thereby increase the angle between torso and thigh; moving the thigh or top of the pelvis backward.

name: short femur
short femur
HP:0003097.def: An abnormal shortening of the femur.

name: fibular overgrowth
fibular overgrowth
HP:0003099.def: Relatively increased growth of the fibula compared to that of the tibia.

name: slender long bone
slender long bone
HP:0003100.def: Reduced diameter of a long bone.

name: increased carrying angle
increase carry angle
HP:0003102.def: An abnormal increase in the carrying angle, which is the angle he long axis of the extended forearm as it lies lateral to the long axis of the arm.

name: abnormal cortical bone morphology
abnormal cortical bone morphology
HP:0003103.def: An abnormality of compact bone (also known as cortical bone), which forms the dense surface of bones.

name: protuberances at ends of long bones
protuberance at end of long bone
HP:0003105.def: The presence of multiple protuberances (bulges, or knobs) at the ends of the long bones.
synonym: protuberances at ends of long bones
protuberance at end of long bone

name: subperiosteal bone resorption
subperiosteal bone resorption
HP:0003106.def: Loss of bone mass occurring beneath the periosteum (the periosteum is the connective-tissue membrane that surrounds all bones except at the articular surfaces). This process may create a serrated and lace-like appearance in periosteal cortical bone.

name: abnormal circulating cholesterol concentration
abnormal circulate cholesterol concentration
HP:0003107.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of cholesterol in the blood circulation.

name: hyperglycinuria
hyperglycinuria
HP:0003108.def: An increased concentration of glycine in the urine.

name: hyperphosphaturia
hyperphosphaturia
HP:0003109.def: An increased excretion of phosphates in the urine.

name: abnormality of urine homeostasis
abnormality of urine homeostasis
HP:0003110.def: An abnormality of the composition of urine or the levels of its components.

name: abnormal blood ion concentration
abnormal blood ion concentration
HP:0003111.def: Abnormality of the homeostasis (concentration) of a monoatomic ion.

name: abnormal circulating amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate amino acid concentration
HP:0003112.def: The presence of an abnormal decrease or increase of one or more amino acids in the blood circulation.
synonym: abnormality of serum amino acid level
abnormality of serum amino acid level
abnormality of serum amino acid levels
abnormality of serum amino acid level

name: hypochloremia
hypochloremia
HP:0003113.def: An abnormally decreased chloride concentration in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating hormone concentration
abnormal circulate hormone concentration
HP:0003117.def: Concentration of a hormone in the blood circulation outside of normal limits.

name: increased circulating cortisol level
increase circulate cortisol level
HP:0003118.def: Overproduction of the hormone of cortisol by the adrenal cortex, resulting in a characteristic combination of clinical symptoms termed Cushing syndrome, with truncal obesity, a round, full face, striae atrophicae and acne, muscle weakness, and other features.

name: abnormal circulating lipid concentration
abnormal circulate lipid concentration
HP:0003119.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a lipid in the blood circulation.

name: limb joint contracture
limb joint contracture
HP:0003121.def: A contracture (chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin) that prevent normal movement of one or more joints of the limbs.

name: hypercholesterolemia
hypercholesterolemia
HP:0003124.def: An increased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.

name: reduced factor viii activity
reduce factor viii activity
HP:0003125.def: Reduced activity of coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.

name: low - molecular - weight proteinuria
low - molecular - weight proteinuria
HP:0003126.def: Excretion in urine of proteins of a size smaller than albumin (molecular weight 69 kD).

name: hypocalciuria
hypocalciuria
HP:0003127.def: An abnormally decreased calcium concentration in the urine.

name: lactic acidosis
lactic acidosis
HP:0003128.def: An abnormal buildup of lactic acid in the body, leading to acidification of the blood and other bodily fluids.

name: abnormal peripheral myelination
abnormal peripheral myelination
HP:0003130.def: An abnormality of the myelination of motor and sensory peripheral nerves. These are axons for motor nerves and dendrites for sensory nerves in the strict anatomic sense.

name: cystinuria
cystinuria
HP:0003131.def: An increased concentration of cystine in the urine.

name: abnormality of the spinocerebellar tracts
abnormality of the spinocerebellar tract
HP:0003133.def: An abnormality of the spinocerebellar tracts, a set of axonal fibers originating in the spinal cord and terminating in the ipsilateral cerebellum. The spinocerebellar tract convey information to the cerebellum about limb and joint position (proprioception). They comprise the ventral spinocerebellar tract, the anterior spinocerebellar tract, and the posterior spinocerebellar tract.

name: abnormality of peripheral nerve conduction
abnormality of peripheral nerve conduction
HP:0003134.def: An abnormality of the conduction of electrical impulses by peripheral (motor or sensory) nerves. This finding is elicited by a nerve conduction study (NCS).
synonym: sensory and motor nerve conduction abnormalities
sensory and motor nerve conduction abnormality

name: prolinuria
prolinuria
HP:0003137.def: Level of proline in the urine anove the upper limit of normal.

name: increased blood urea nitrogen
increase blood urea nitrogen
HP:0003138.def: An increased amount of nitrogen in the form of urea in the blood.

name: panhypogammaglobulinemia
panhypogammaglobulinemia
HP:0003139.def: A reduction in the circulating levels of all the major classes of immunoglobulin. is characterized by profound decreases in all classes of immunoglobulin with an absence of circulating B lymphocytes.

name: t - wave inversion in the right precordial leads
t - wave inversion in the right precordial lead
increased ldl cholesterol concentration
increase ldl cholesterol concentration
HP:0003141.def: An elevated concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
synonym: increased circulating low - density lipoprotein cholesterol
increase circulate low - density lipoprotein cholesterol
increased circulating low - density lipoprotein levels
increase circulate low - density lipoprotein level

name: increased serum serotonin
increase serum serotonin
HP:0003144.def: A increased concentration of serotonin in the blood.

name: decreased adenosylcobalamin
decrease adenosylcobalamin
HP:0003145.def: Decreased concentration of adenosylcobalamin. Adenosylcobalamin is one of the active forms of vitamin B12.

name: hypocholesterolemia
hypocholesterolemia
HP:0003146.def: An decreased concentration of cholesterol in the blood.

name: hyperuricosuria
hyperuricosuria
HP:0003149.def: An abnormally high level of uric acid in the urine.

name: glutaric aciduria
glutaric aciduria
HP:0003150.def: The concentration of glutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: cystathioninuria
cystathioninuria
HP:0003153.def: An elevated urinary concentration of cystathionine.

name: increased circulating acth level
increase circulate acth level
HP:0003154.def: An abnormal increased in the concentration of corticotropin, also known as adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), in the blood.

name: elevated circulating alkaline phosphatase concentration
elevate circulate alkaline phosphatase concentration
HP:0003155.def: Abnormally increased serum levels of alkaline phosphatase activity.

name: hyposthenuria
hyposthenuria
HP:0003158.def: An abnormally low urinary specific gravity, i.e., reduced concentration of solutes in the urine.

name: hyperoxaluria
hyperoxaluria
HP:0003159.def: Increased excretion of oxalates in the urine.
synonym: increased level of oxalate in urine
increase level of oxalate in urine

name: abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin
abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin
HP:0003160.def: Glycosylated transferrin concentrations can be measured in serum as a marker of N-linked glycosylation fidelity. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II. These terms are retained for historical reasons but for new annotations the precise glycosylation defect should be recorded.

name: 4 - hydroxyphenylpyruvic aciduria
4 - hydroxyphenylpyruvic aciduria
HP:0003161.def: Increased relative concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvic acid in the urine.

name: elevated urinary delta - aminolevulinic acid
elevate urinary delta - aminolevulinic acid
HP:0003163.def: An increased concentration of 5-aminolevulinic acid (CHEBI:17549) in the urine.

name: elevated circulating parathyroid hormone level
elevate circulate parathyroid hormone level
HP:0003165.def: An abnormal increased concentration of parathyroid hormone.

name: increased urinary taurine
increase urinary taurine
HP:0003166.def: Increased concentration of taurine in the urine.

name: carnosinuria
carnosinuria
HP:0003167.def: An increased concentration of carnosine in the urine.

name: dibasicaminoaciduria
dibasicaminoaciduria
HP:0003168.def: An increased level of a dibasic amino acid in the urine. Dibasic amino acids are usually refered to simply as basic aminoacids because they contain basic side chains at neutral pH. These are arginine (Arg), lysine (Lys), and histidine (His).

name: abnormal acetabulum morphology
abnormal acetabulum morphology
HP:0003170.def: An abnormality of the acetabulum, i.e., the Acetabular part of hip bone, which together with the head of the femur forms the hip joint.

name: abnormal pubic bone morphology
abnormal pubic bone morphology
HP:0003172.def: An anomaly of the the pubic bone, i.e., of the ventral and anterior of the three principal components (pubis, ilium, ischium) of the hip bone.

name: hypoplastic pubic bone
hypoplastic pubic bone
HP:0003173.def: Underdevelopment of the pubis, which together with the ilium and the ischium, is one of the three bones that make up the hip bone.

name: abnormal ischium morphology
abnormal ischium morphology
HP:0003174.def: An anomaly of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.

name: hypoplastic ischia
hypoplastic ischia
HP:0003175.def: Underdevelopment of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.

name: squared iliac bones
square iliac bone
HP:0003177.def: A shift from the normally round (convex) appearance of the iliac wing towards a square-like appearance.

name: protrusio acetabuli
protrusio acetabuli
HP:0003179.def: Intrapelvic bulging of the medial acetabular wall.

name: flat acetabular roof
flat acetabular roof
HP:0003180.def: Flattening of the superior part of the acetabulum, which is a cup-shaped cavity at the base of the hipbone into which the ball-shaped head of the femur fits. The acetabular roof thereby appears horizontal rather than arched, as it normally does.

name: wide pubic symphysis
wide pubic symphysis
HP:0003183.def: Abnormally increased width of the pubic symphysis is the midline cartilaginous joint uniting the superior rami of the left and right pubic bones.

name: decreased hip abduction
decrease hip abduction
HP:0003184.def: Reduced ability to move the femur outward to the side.

name: short greater sciatic notch
short great sciatic notch
HP:0003185.def: The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a reduction in the height of the notch.

name: inverted nipples
inverted nipple
HP:0003186.def: The presence of nipples that instead of pointing outward are retracted inwards.

name: long nose
long nose
HP:0003189.def: Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased length from the nasal root to the nasal base.

name: cleft ala nasi
cleft ala nasi
HP:0003191.def: The presence of a notch in the margin of the ala nasi.

name: allergic rhinitis
allergic rhinitis
HP:0003193.def: It is characterized by one or more symptoms including sneezing, itching, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea.

name: short nasal bridge
short nasal bridge
HP:0003194.def: Decreased superior-inferior length of the nasal bridge, which is the saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose.
synonym: decreased length of bridge of nose
decreased length of bridge of nose

name: short nose
short nose
HP:0003196.def: Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations below the mean, or alternatively, an apparently decreased length from the nasal root to the nasal tip.

name: myopathy
myopathy
HP:0003198.def: A disorder of muscle unrelated to impairment of innervation or neuromuscular junction.

name: ragged - red muscle fibers
rag - red muscle fiber
HP:0003200.def: An abnormal appearance of muscle fibers observed on muscle biopsy. Ragged red fibers can be visualized with Gomori trichrome staining as irregular and intensely red subsarcolemmal zones, whereas the normal myofibrils are green. The margins of affect fibers appear red and ragged. The ragged-red is due to the accumulation of abnormal mitochondria below the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to the appearance of a red rim and speckled sarcoplasm.

name: rhabdomyolysis
rhabdomyolysis
HP:0003201.def: Breakdown of muscle fibers that leads to the release of muscle fiber contents (myoglobin) into the bloodstream.

name: skeletal muscle atrophy
skeletal muscle atrophy
HP:0003202.def: The presence of skeletal muscular atrophy (which is also known as amyotrophy).
synonym: neurogenic muscle atrophy , especially in the lower limbs
neurogenic muscle atrophy , especially in the low limb

name: impaired oxidative burst
impaired oxidative burst

If this test is negative (i.e., no blue color is produced), then this indicates a defect in superoxide-generating NADPH oxidase activity with inability to efficiently kill phagocytized bacteria.

name: intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0003204.def: The intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent storage material.

curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material

intracellular curvilinear profile on ultrastructural analysis

name: arterial calcification
arterial calcification

fingerprint intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material

abnormality of the coagulation cascade
HP:0003256.def: An abnormality of the coagulation cascade, which is comprised of the contact activation pathway (also known as the intrinsic pathway) and the tissue factor pathway (also known as the extrinsic pathway) as well as cofactors and regulators.

hydroxyprolinemia

smooth muscle antibody positivity

argininuria

abnormal hip bone morphology
HP:0003272.def: An abnormality of the hip bone.

hip contracture

narrow pelvis bone

pelvic bone exostosis
HP:0003276.def: A benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface of the pelvis. Exostoses are capped by cartilage, and arise from a bone that develops from cartilage.

name: square pelvis bone
square pelvis bone
HP:0003278.def: An abnormally squared appearance of the bony pelvis, a normally rounded or basin-shaped structure.

HP:0003301.def: An irregular surface of the vertebral end plates, which are normally relatively smooth.

displacement of one backbone compare to another

name: spondylolysis
spondylolysis

block vertebra

cervical subluxation

abnormal form of the vertebral body
butterfly vertebrae
butterfly vertebra

The name is based on the appearance of the two hemivertebrae emerging as butterfly wings from the central cleft on x-ray.

abnormality of the cervical spine

name: c1 - c2 subluxation
c1 - c2 subluxation
HP:0003320.def: A partial dislocation of the atlantoaxial joints.

generalize muscle weakness
HP:0003324.def: Generalized weakness or decreased strength of the muscles, affecting both distal and proximal musculature.

name: limb - girdle muscle weakness
limb - girdle muscle weakness
HP:0003325.def: Weakness of the limb-girdle muscles (also known as the pelvic and shoulder girdles), that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders and the pelvis.

name: axial muscle weakness
axial muscle weakness
HP:0003327.def: Reduced strength of the axial musculature (i.e., of the muscles of the head and neck, spine, and ribs).

abnormal hairshaft morphology
HP:0003328.def: An abnormal structure of the hairshaft, i.e., of the nongrowing portion of a hair that protrudes from the skin.

abnormal bone structure

name: abnormal enchondral ossification
abnormal enchondral ossification
HP:0003336.def: An abnormality of the process of endochondral ossification, which is a type of replacement ossification in which bone tissue replaces cartilage.

reduce prothrombin consumption

subepidermal blister with cleavage in the lamina lucida

reduce glutathione synthetase level

3 - methylglutaric aciduria

elevate urinary norepinephrine level

impaired lymphocyte transformation with phytohemagglutinin

low cholesterol esterification rate

gowers sign

thenar muscle atrophy
