name: atlantoaxial abnormality
atlantoaxial abnormality
HP:0003413.def: An anomaly of the atlantoaxial joint, i.e., of the joint between the first (atlas) and second (axis) cervical vertebrae.

name: atlantoaxial dislocation
atlantoaxial dislocation
HP:0003414.def: Partial dislocation of the atlantoaxial joint.

name: spinal canal stenosis
spinal canal stenosis
HP:0003416.def: An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal.

name: coronal cleft vertebrae
coronal cleft vertebra
HP:0003417.def: Frontal schisis (cleft or cleavage) of vertebral bodies.

name: back pain
back pain
HP:0003418.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back.

name: low back pain
low back pain
HP:0003419.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the lower back.

name: vertebral segmentation defect
vertebral segmentation defect
HP:0003422.def: An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation during development.

name: cns hypomyelination
cns hypomyelination
HP:0003429.def: Reduced amount of myelin in the central nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis.

name: decreased motor nerve conduction velocity
decrease motor nerve conduction velocity
HP:0003431.def: A type of decreased nerve conduction velocity that affects the motor neuron.

name: prolonged miniature endplate currents
prolonged miniature endplate current
HP:0003436.def: An abnormal prolongation of the miniature endplate potentials, i.e. the postsynaptic response to transmitter released from an individual vesicle at the neuromuscular junction.

name: absent achilles reflex
absent achilles reflex
HP:0003438.def: Absence of the Achilles reflex (also known as the ankle jerk reflex), which can normally be elicited by tapping the tendon is tapped while the foot is dorsiflexed.

name: decreased size of nerve terminals
decreased size of nerve terminal
HP:0003443.def: A reduction in the size of nerve terminals.

name: emg : chronic denervation signs
emg : chronic denervation sign
HP:0003444.def: Evidence of chronic denervation on electromyography.

name: emg : neuropathic changes
emg : neuropathic change
HP:0003445.def: The presence of characteristic findings of denervation on electromyography (fibrillations, positive sharp waves, and giant motor unit potentials).

name: axonal loss
axonal loss
HP:0003447.def: A reduction in the number of axons in the peripheral nervous system.

name: decreased sensory nerve conduction velocity
decreased sensory nerve conduction velocity
HP:0003448.def: Reduced speed of conduction of the action potential along a sensory nerve.

name: cold - induced muscle cramps
cold - induced muscle cramp
HP:0003449.def: Sudden and involuntary contractions of one or more muscles brought on by exposure to cold temperatures.

name: axonal regeneration
axonal regeneration
HP:0003450.def: The presence of axonal regeneration following a previous axonal lesion.

name: increased rate of premature chromosome condensation
increased rate of premature chromosome condensation
HP:0003451.def: An increased rate of premature chromosome condensation.

name: antineutrophil antibody positivity
antineutrophil antibody positivity
HP:0003453.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against neutrophils.

name: platelet antibody positive
platelet antibody positive
HP:0003454.def: The presence in the serum of autoantibodies directed against thrombocytes.

name: elevated circulating long chain fatty acid concentration
elevate circulate long chain fatty acid concentration
HP:0003455.def: Increased concentration of long-chain fatty acids in the blood circulation.
synonym: elevated serum long - chain fatty acids
elevate serum long - chain fatty acid
increased serum long - chain fatty acids
increase serum long - chain fatty acid

name: low urinary cyclic amp response to pth administration
low urinary cyclic amp response to pth administration
emg abnormality
emg abnormality
HP:0003457.def: Abnormal results of investigations using electromyography (EMG).

name: emg : myopathic abnormalities
emg : myopathic abnormality
HP:0003458.def: The presence of abnormal electromyographic patterns indicative of myopathy, such as small-short polyphasic motor unit potentials.

name: polyclonal elevation of igm
polyclonal elevation of igm
HP:0003459.def: A heterogeneous increase in IgM immunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.

name: decreased circulating total iga
decrease circulate total iga
HP:0003460.def: Undetectable serum immunoglobulin A level at a value < 5 mg/dL (0.05 g/L).

name: increased urinary o - linked sialopeptides
increase urinary o - link sialopeptides
HP:0003461.def: Excretion of peptides conjugated to sialic acid in the urine.

name: increased extraneuronal autofluorescent lipopigment
increase extraneuronal autofluorescent lipopigment
HP:0003463.def: Lipofuscin, a generic term applied to autofluorescent lipopigment, is a mixture of protein and lipid that accumulates in most aging cells, particularly those involved in high lipid turnover (e.g., the adrenal medulla) or phagocytosis of other cell types (e g., the retinal pigment epithelium or RPE; macrophage). This term pertains if there is an increase in the extraneuronal accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.

name: paradoxical increased cortisol secretion on dexamethasone suppression test
paradoxical increase cortisol secretion on dexamethasone suppression test
atlantoaxial instability
atlantoaxial instability
HP:0003467.def: Abnormally increased movement at the junction between the first cervical (atlas) and the second cervical (axis) vertebrae as a result of either a bony or ligamentous anomaly.

name: abnormal vertebral morphology
abnormal vertebral morphology
HP:0003468.def: An abnormality of one or more of the vertebrae.

name: peripheral dysmyelination
peripheral dysmyelination
HP:0003469.def: Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths. Dysmyelination is distinguished from demyleination where there is destruction or damage of previously normal myelination.

name: paralysis
paralysis
HP:0003470.def: Paralysis of voluntary muscles means loss of contraction due to interruption of one or more motor pathways from the brain to the muscle fibers. Although the word paralysis is often used interchangeably to mean either complete or partial loss of muscle strength, it is preferable to use paralysis or plegia for complete or severe loss of muscle strength, and paresis for partial or slight loss. Motor paralysis results from deficits of the upper motor neurons (corticospinal, corticobulbar, or subcorticospinal). Motor paralysis is often accompanied by an impairment in the facility of movement.

name: hypocalcemic tetany
hypocalcemic tetany
HP:0003472.def: Hyperexcitability of the neuromuscular system related to abnormally low level of calcium in the blood, resulting in carpopedal or generalized spasms.

name: fatigable weakness
fatigable weakness
HP:0003473.def: A type of weakness that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.
synonym: generalised muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
generalise muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
generalized muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
generalize muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
proximal muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction
proximal muscle weakness due to defect at the neuromuscular junction

name: somatic sensory dysfunction
somatic sensory dysfunction
HP:0003474.def: An abnormality of the primary sensation that is mediated by peripheral nerves (pain, temperature, touch, vibration, joint position). The word hypoesthesia (or hypesthesia) refers to a reduction in cutaneous sensation to a specific type of testing.

name: peripheral axonal neuropathy
peripheral axonal neuropathy
HP:0003477.def: An abnormality characterized by disruption of the normal functioning of peripheral axons.

name: segmental peripheral demyelination / remyelination
segmental peripheral demyelination / remyelination
HP:0003481.def: A segmental pattern of demyelination and regeneration (remyelination) affecting peripheral nerves.

name: emg : axonal abnormality
emg : axonal abnormality
HP:0003482.def: Electromyographic (EMG) findings characteristic of axonal neuropathy, with normal or slightly decreased nerve conduction velocities, normal or slightly prolonged distal latencies, but significantly reduced motor potentials and sensory amplitudes. There may be spontaneous activity upon needle EMG studies, such as increased insertional activity, positive sharp waves, and fibrillation potentials.

name: upper limb muscle weakness
upper limb muscle weakness
HP:0003484.def: Weakness of the muscles of the arms.

name: babinski sign
babinski sign
HP:0003487.def: Upturning of the big toe (and sometimes fanning of the other toes) in response to stimulation of the sole of the foot. If the Babinski sign is present it can indicate damage to the corticospinal tract.

name: obsolete defective dehydrogenation of isovaleryl coa and butyryl coa
obsolete defective dehydrogenation of isovaleryl coa and butyryl coa
elevated urine pyrophosphate
elevate urine pyrophosphate
HP:0003491.def: An abnormally increased diphosphate(4-) concentration in the urine. Diphosphate(4-), as ester with two phosphate groups, is also known as pyrophosphate.

name: high urinary gonadotropin level
high urinary gonadotropin level
HP:0003492.def: An elevated concentration of a gonadotropin hormone (stimulating hormone or luteinizing hormone) in the urine, consistent with the diagnosis of primary hypogonadism.

name: antinuclear antibody positivity
antinuclear antibody positivity
HP:0003493.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against nuclei or nuclear components.

name: obsolete loss of heterozygosity , multiple chromosomes
obsolete loss of heterozygosity , multiple chromosome
increased circulating igm level
increase circulate igm level
HP:0003496.def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin M in blood.

name: disproportionate short stature
disproportionate short stature
HP:0003498.def: A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to differing extents.

name: mild short stature
mild short stature
HP:0003502.def: A mild degree of short stature, more than -2 SD but not more than -3 SD from mean corrected for age and sex.

name: proportionate short stature
proportionate short stature
HP:0003508.def: A kind of short stature in which different regions of the body are shortened to a comparable extent.

name: severe short stature
severe short stature
HP:0003510.def: A severe degree of short stature, more than -4 SD from the mean corrected for age and sex.

name: reduced ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
reduce ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
HP:0003513.def: A reduction of the ratio of renal calcium clearance to creatinine clearance to below 0.01.
synonym: reduced ration of kidney calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
reduce ration of kidney calcium clearance to creatinine clearance
reduced ration of renal ca clearance to creatinine clearance
reduce ration of renal ca clearance to creatinine clearance
reduced ration of renal ca2+ to creatinine clearance
reduce ration of renal ca2+ to creatinine clearance

name: deficiency or absence of cytochrome b ( - 245 )
deficiency or absence of cytochrome b ( - 245 )
synonym: deficiency or absence of cytochrome b
deficiency or absence of cytochrome b

name: disproportionate short - trunk short stature
disproportionate short - trunk short stature
HP:0003521.def: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs.

name: decreased methionine synthase activity
decrease methionine synthase activity
HP:0003524.def: A reduction in methionine synthase activity.

name: orotic acid crystalluria
orotic acid crystalluria
HP:0003526.def: Formation of crystals owing to an increased concentration of orotic acid in the urine.

name: hyperprostaglandinuria
hyperprostaglandinuria
HP:0003527.def: An increased concentration of prostaglandin in the urine.

name: elevated circulating calcitonin concentration
elevate circulate calcitonin concentration
HP:0003528.def: Concentration of calcitonin, a 32-amino acid polypeptide hormone that is produced primarily by the parafollicular cells of the thyroid, in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: parathormone - independent increased renal tubular calcium reabsorption
parathormone - independent increase renal tubular calcium reabsorption
HP:0003529.def: An increase in the reabsorption of calcium by the renal tubulus that is not associated with increased parathormone levels.
synonym: parathormone - independent increased renal tubular ca reabsorption
parathormone - independent increase renal tubular ca reabsorption
parathormone - independent increased renal tubular ca2+ reabsorption
parathormone - independent increase renal tubular ca2+ reabsorption

name: elevated circulating glutaric acid concentration
elevate circulate glutaric acid concentration
HP:0003530.def: An increased concentration of glutaric acid in the blood.

name: ornithinuria
ornithinuria
HP:0003532.def: Level of ornithine in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

name: reduced acetaldehyde dehydrogenase level
reduce acetaldehyde dehydrogenase level
HP:0003533.def: Decreased level of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH). ALDH and alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) are the primary enzymes involved in alcohol metabolism.

name: reduced xanthine dehydrogenase level
reduce xanthine dehydrogenase level
HP:0003534.def: An abnormal reduction in xanthine dehydrogenase level.

name: 3 - methylglutaconic aciduria
3 - methylglutaconic aciduria
HP:0003535.def: An increased amount of 3-methylglutaconic acid in the urine.

name: decreased fumarate hydratase activity
decrease fumarate hydratase activity
HP:0003536.def: An abnormality of Krebs cycle metabolism that is characterized by a decreased rate of fumarate hydratase activity.

name: hypouricemia
hypouricemia
HP:0003537.def: An abnormally low level of uric acid in the blood.

name: increased iduronate sulfatase level
increase iduronate sulfatase level
HP:0003538.def: An increased level of iduronate-2-sulfatase activity in the blood.

name: impaired platelet aggregation
impaired platelet aggregation
HP:0003540.def: An impairment in the rate and degree to which platelets aggregate after the addition of an agonist that stimulates platelet clumping. Platelet aggregation is measured using aggregometer to measure the optical density of platelet-rich plasma, whereby platelet aggregation causes the plasma to become more transparent.

name: urinary glycosaminoglycan excretion
urinary glycosaminoglycan excretion
HP:0003541.def: Excretion of glycosaminoglycan in the urine. Glycosaminoglycans are long unbranched polysaccharides consisting of a repeating disaccharide unit.

name: increased serum pyruvate
increase serum pyruvate
HP:0003542.def: An increased concentration of pyruvate in the blood.

name: exercise intolerance
exercise intolerance
HP:0003546.def: A functional motor deficit where individuals whose responses to the challenges of exercise fail to achieve levels considered normal for their age and gender.

name: shoulder girdle muscle weakness
shoulder girdle muscle weakness
HP:0003547.def: The shoulder, or pectoral, girdle is composed of the clavicles and the scapulae. Shoulder-girdle weakness refers to lack of strength of the muscles attaching to these bones, that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders.

name: subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormally shaped mitochondria
subsarcolemmal accumulation of abnormally shape mitochondrion
HP:0003548.def: An abnormally increased number of mitochondria in the cytoplasma adjacent to the sarcolemma (muscle cell membrane), whereby the mitochondria also possess an abnormal morphology.

name: abnormality of connective tissue
abnormality of connective tissue
HP:0003549.def: Any abnormality of the soft tissues, including both connective tissue (tendons, ligaments, fascia, fibrous tissues, and fat).

name: predominantly lower limb lymphedema
predominantly low limb lymphedema
HP:0003550.def: Localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system, affecting mainly the legs.

name: muscle stiffness
muscle stiffness
HP:0003552.def: A condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm.

name: type 2 muscle fiber atrophy
type 2 muscle fiber atrophy
HP:0003554.def: Atrophy (wasting) affecting primary type 2 muscle fibers. This feature in general can only be observed on muscle biopsy.

name: muscle fiber splitting
muscle fiber splitting
HP:0003555.def: Fiber splitting or branching is a common finding in human and rat skeletal muscle pathology. Fiber splitting refers to longitudinal halving of the complete fiber, while branching originates from a regenerating end of a necrotic fiber as invaginations of the sarcolemma. In fiber branching, one end of the fiber remains intact as a single entity, while the other end has several branches.

name: increased variability in muscle fiber diameter
increase variability in muscle fiber diameter
HP:0003557.def: An abnormally high degree of muscle fiber size variation. This phenotypic feature can be observed upon muscle biopsy.
synonym: increased variability in muscle fiber size
increase variability in muscle fiber size
increased variability in muscle fibre diameter
increase variability in muscle fibre diameter
increased variability in muscle fibre size
increase variability in muscle fibre size
increased variation in muscle fiber size
increase variation in muscle fiber size
increased variation in muscle fibre size
increase variation in muscle fibre size

name: viral infection - induced rhabdomyolysis
viral infection - induced rhabdomyolysis
HP:0003558.def: Rhabdomyolysis induced by a viral infection.

name: muscular dystrophy
muscular dystrophy
HP:0003560.def: The term dystrophy means abnormal growth. However, muscular dystrophy is used to describe primary myopathies with a genetic basis and a progressive course characterized by progressive skeletal muscle weakness and wasting, defects in muscle proteins, and histological features of muscle fiber degeneration (necrosis) and regeneration. If possible, it is preferred to use other HPO terms to describe the precise phenotypic abnormalities.

name: decreased ldl cholesterol concentration
decrease ldl cholesterol concentration
HP:0003563.def: An decreased concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
synonym: decreased circulating low - density lipoprotein levels
decrease circulate low - density lipoprotein level

name: folate - dependent fragile site at xq28
folate - dependent fragile site at xq28
HP:0003564.def: The presence of a folate sensitive fragile site at chromosome Xq28.

name: elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
elevate erythrocyte sedimentation rate
HP:0003565.def: An increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The ESR is a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen.

name: increased serum prostaglandin e2
increase serum prostaglandin e2
HP:0003566.def: An increased concentration of prostaglandin E2 in the blood.

name: decreased glucosephosphate isomerase level
decrease glucosephosphate isomerase level
HP:0003568.def: A decreased level of glucose-6-phosphate isomerase.

name: molybdenum cofactor deficiency
molybdenum cofactor deficiency
HP:0003570.def: Absence of molybdenum cofactor(2-), a cofactor for enzymes including sulfite oxidase, xanthine oxidoreductase, and aldehyde oxidase.

name: propionic acidemia
propionic acidemia
HP:0003571.def: Increased concentration of proprionic acid in the blood circulation.

name: low plasma citrulline
low plasma citrulline
HP:0003572.def: A decreased concentration of citrulline in the blood.

name: increased total bilirubin
increase total bilirubin
HP:0003573.def: Increased concentration of total (conjugated and unconjugated) bilirubin in the blood.

name: positive regitine blocking test
positive regitine block test
HP:0003574.def: A positive response to the regitine blocking test consisting of a substantial reduction in blood pressure following administration of regitine, indicative of the presence of increased levels of epinephrine and norepinephrine in the circulation, which is seen in pheochromocytoma-associated hypertension.

name: increased intracellular sodium
increase intracellular sodium
HP:0003575.def: An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the cytosol.

name: congenital onset
congenital onset
HP:0003577.def: A phenotypic abnormality that is present at birth.

name: adult onset
adult onset
HP:0003581.def: Onset of disease manifestations in adulthood, defined here as at the age of 16 years or later.

name: late onset
late onset
HP:0003584.def: A type of adult onset with onset of symptoms after the age of 60 years.

name: insidious onset
insidious onset
HP:0003587.def: Gradual, very slow onset of disease manifestations.

name: infantile onset
infantile onset
HP:0003593.def: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease between 28 days to one year of life.
synonym: onset in first year of life
onset in first year of life

name: middle age onset
middle age onset
HP:0003596.def: A type of adult onset with onset of symptoms at the age of 40 to 60 years.

name: absent urinary urothione
absent urinary urothione
HP:0003606.def: Lack of urothione (the urinary metabolite of molybdenum cofactor) in the urine.

name: 4 - hydroxyphenylacetic aciduria
4 - hydroxyphenylacetic aciduria
HP:0003607.def: Increased concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid in the urine.

name: foam cells with lamellar inclusion bodies
foam cell with lamellar inclusion body
HP:0003609.def: The presence of foam cells that contain lamellar inclusion bodies.

name: fibroblast metachromasia
fibroblast metachromasia
HP:0003610.def: Increased cytoplasmic staining of fibroblasts with toluidine blue.

name: positive ferric chloride test
positive ferric chloride test
HP:0003612.def: If positive, the ferric chloride test indicates an increased concentration of phenols in the urine or blood.

name: antiphospholipid antibody positivity
antiphospholipid antibody positivity
HP:0003613.def: The presence of circulating autoantibodies to phospholipids.

name: trimethylaminuria
trimethylaminuria
HP:0003614.def: Increased concentration of trimethylamine in the urine.

name: juvenile onset
juvenile onset
HP:0003621.def: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease between the age of 5 and 15 years.
synonym: signs and symptoms begin before 15 years of age
sign and symptom begin before 15 year of age

name: neonatal onset
neonatal onset
HP:0003623.def: Onset of signs or symptoms of disease within the first 28 days of life.
synonym: onset in first weeks of life
onset in first week of life

name: amyoplasia
amyoplasia
HP:0003634.def: Congenital lack of development of the muscles, which are then replaced by a mixture of dense fat and fibrous tissue.

name: loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs
loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limb
HP:0003635.def: Loss (disappearance) of previously present subcutaneous fat tissue in arm or leg.
synonym: loss of fat tissue below the skin in limbs
loss of fat tissue below the skin in limb
loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from extremities
loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from extremity

name: reduced 4 - hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase level
reduce 4 - hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase level
HP:0003637.def: An abnormal reduction in 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase level.

name: elevated urinary epinephrine level
elevate urinary epinephrine level
HP:0003639.def: The concentration of epinephrine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: cns foam cells
cns foam cell
HP:0003640.def: The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, in the central nervous system.

name: hemoglobinuria
hemoglobinuria
HP:0003641.def: The presence of free hemoglobin in the urine.

name: type i transferrin isoform profile
type i transferrin isoform profile
HP:0003642.def: Abnormal transferrin isoform profile consistent with a type I congenital disorder of glycosylation. In the traditional nomenclature for congenital disorders of glycosylation, absence of entire glycans was designated type I, and loss of one or more monosaccharides as type II.
synonym: abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin , type i pattern
abnormal isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin , type i pattern
isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin consistent with cdg type i
isoelectric focusing of serum transferrin consistent with cdg type i

name: prolonged partial thromboplastin time
prolong partial thromboplastin time
HP:0003645.def: Increased time to coagulation in the partial thromboplastin time (PTT) test, a measure of the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Phospholipid, and activator, and calcium are mixed into an anticoagulated plasma sample, and the time is measured until a thrombus forms.

name: bicarbonaturia
bicarbonaturia
HP:0003646.def: Abnormally increased concentration of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.

name: electron transfer flavoprotein - ubiquinone oxidoreductase defect
electron transfer flavoprotein - ubiquinone oxidoreductase defect
HP:0003647.def: A deficiency of the electron transfer flavoprotein-ubiquinone oxidoreductase.

name: lacticaciduria
lacticaciduria
HP:0003648.def: An increased concentration of lactic acid in the urine.

name: foam cells
foam cell
HP:0003651.def: The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, where they ingest low-density lipoproteins and become laden with lipids, giving them a foamy appearance.

name: recurrent myoglobinuria
recurrent myoglobinuria
HP:0003652.def: Recurring episodes of myoglobinuria, i.e., of the presence of myoglobin in the urine. This is usually a consequence of rhabdomyolysis, i.e., of the destruction of muscle tissue.

name: cellular metachromasia
cellular metachromasia
HP:0003653.def: Metachromasia (also known as metachromacy) is a characteristic color change which certain aniline dyes exhibit when bound to particular substances or when concentrated in solution. For example, the basic dye toluidine blue becomes distinctly pink when bound to cartilage matrix. In the sense used here, the metachromasia refers to a change in color not observed with normal tissues, anomalous staining with the cationic dyes toluidine blue O and Alcian blue resulting from excessive amounts of the polyanionic glycosaminoglycans.

name: reduced dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase level
reduce dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase level
HP:0003654.def: An abnormal reduction in dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (NADP+) level.

name: reduced level of n - acetylglucosaminyltransferase ii
reduce level of n - acetylglucosaminyltransferase ii
HP:0003655.def: An abnormality of glycoprotein metabolism related to a decreased level of alpha-1,6-mannosylglycoprotein 2-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity.

name: decreased beta - glucocerebrosidase level
decrease beta - glucocerebrosidase level
HP:0003656.def: Reduced level of the enzyme beta-glucosidase, an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of glucosylceramide into ceramide and glucose.

name: vascular granular osmiophilic material deposition
vascular granular osmiophilic material deposition
HP:0003657.def: Accumulation of granular osmiophilic material in blood vessel walls. Osmiophilic material becomes black upon staining with osmium tetroxide. Deposition of granular osmiophilic material (GOM) is the vascular pathological hallmark of CADASIL, which is the most prevalent hereditary small vessel disease and is caused by missense mutations in the NOTCH3 gene. GOM have been shown to contain NOTCH3 ectodomain (NOTCH3ECD) and extracellular matrix proteins, and can be visualized ultrastructurally in the tunica media of small arteries and capillaries. These electron dense GOM deposits are located in the basement membrane of mural cells, i.e. vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. In both manifest and pre-manifest CADASIL patients, GOM deposits are present not only in brain vessels, but also in vessels of other organs, such as the skin.
synonym: granular osmiophilic deposits ( grod ) in cells
granular osmiophilic deposit ( grod ) in cell

name: hypomethioninemia
hypomethioninemia
HP:0003658.def: A decreased concentration of methionine in the blood.

name: amyotrophy of the musculature of the pelvis
amyotrophy of the musculature of the pelvis
HP:0003665.def: Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles of the pelvis.

name: onset
onset
HP:0003674.def: The age group in which disease manifestations appear.

name: progressive
progressive
HP:0003676.def: Applies to a disease manifestation that increases in scope or severity over the course of time, i.e., that worsens with age.

name: slowly progressive
slowly progressive
HP:0003677.def: Applies to a disease manifestation that only slowly increases in scope or severity over the course of time.
synonym: signs and symptoms worsen slowly with time
sign and symptom worsen slowly with time

name: rapidly progressive
rapidly progressive
HP:0003678.def: Applies to a disease manifestation that quickly increases in scope or severity over the course of time.

name: nonprogressive
nonprogressive
HP:0003680.def: Applies to a disease manifestation that does not increase in scope or severity over the course of time, i.e., that does not worsen with age.

name: variable progression rate
variable progression rate
HP:0003682.def: Applies to a disease manifestation that quickly increases in scope or severity with a rate that varies. For instance, progression may be slow in one time period and rapid in another.

name: centrally nucleated skeletal muscle fibers
centrally nucleated skeletal muscle fiber
HP:0003687.def: An abnormality in which the nuclei of sarcomeres take on an abnormally central localization (or in which this feature is found in an increased proportion of muscle cells).

name: cytochrome c oxidase - negative muscle fibers
cytochrome c oxidase - negative muscle fiber
HP:0003688.def: An abnormally reduced activity of the enzyme cytochrome C oxidase in muscle tissue.
synonym: cytochrome c oxidase deficiency in skeletal muscle
cytochrome c oxidase deficiency in skeletal muscle
cytochrome c oxidase - negative muscle fibres
cytochrome c oxidase - negative muscle fibre
decreased activity of cytochrome c oxidase in muscle tissue
decreased activity of cytochrome c oxidase in muscle tissue
decreased skeletal muscle cytochrome c oxidase activity
decrease skeletal muscle cytochrome c oxidase activity

name: multiple mitochondrial dna deletions
multiple mitochondrial dna deletion
HP:0003689.def: The presence of multiple deletions of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).

name: limb muscle weakness
limb muscle weakness
HP:0003690.def: Reduced strength and weakness of the muscles of the arms and legs.

name: scapular winging
scapular winging
HP:0003691.def: Abnormal protrusion of the scapula away from the surface of the back.

name: distal amyotrophy
distal amyotrophy
HP:0003693.def: Muscular atrophy affecting muscles in the distal portions of the extremities.
synonym: distal amyotrophy , especially of the hands and feet
distal amyotrophy , especially of the hand and foot
distal muscle atrophy , upper and lower limbs
distal muscle atrophy , upper and low limb

name: late - onset proximal muscle weakness
late - onset proximal muscle weakness
HP:0003694.def: Lack of strength of the proximal musculature occurring late in the clinical course.

name: absent epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
absent epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger
HP:0003696.def: Absence of the epiphysis located at the proximal end of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger.

absent end part of the outermost bone of the little finger

Changes may affect all bones of the organism, just certain bones or only parts of bones and include decreased mineralisation as may be seen in osteoporosis or increased mineralisation and or ossification as in osteopetrosis, exostoses or any kind of atopic calicfications of different origin and distribution. The overall amount of mineralization of the bone-organ can be measured as the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones, usually measured by densitometry of the lumbar spine or hip. The measurements are usually reported as g/cm3 or as a Z-score (the number of standard deviations above or below the mean for the patient's age and sex). Note that measurement with this method does not reflect local changes in other bones, and as such might not be correct with regard the hole bone-organ.
synonym: abnormality of bone mineralisation and ossification
abnormality of bone mineralisation and ossification

name: reduced bone mineral density
reduce bone mineral density

decrease bone mineral density z score
low solidness and mass of the bones
low solidness and mass of the bone

name: abnormal circulating purine concentration

name: abnormal circulating pyrimidine concentration
abnormal circulate pyrimidine concentration

name: abnormal circulating carboxylic acid concentration
abnormal circulate carboxylic acid concentration

name: abnormal circulating leucine concentration
abnormal circulate leucine concentration
HP:0004357.def: Any deviation from the normal circulation of leucine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating fatty - acid concentration
abnormal circulate fatty - acid concentration

abnormality of acid - base homeostasis

name: abnormal circulating leptin concentration
abnormal circulate leptin concentration
HP:0004361.def: An abnormal concentration of leptin in the blood.

name: abnormal enteric ganglion morphology
abnormal enteric ganglion morphology
HP:0004362.def: An abnormality of the enteric nervous system, which comprises two types of ganglia, the myenteric (Auerbach's) and submucosal (Meissner's) plexuses. The enteric nervous system functions to control gut movement, fluid exchange between the gut and its lumen, and local blood flow.

name: abnormal circulating calcium concentration
abnormal circulate calcium concentration
HP:0004363.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of calcium in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating nitrogen compound concentration
abnormal circulate nitrogen compound concentration
HP:0004364.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a nitrogen compound in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating tryptophan concentration
abnormal circulate tryptophan concentration
HP:0004365.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of tryptophan in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating purine concentration
increase circulate purine concentration
HP:0004368.def: Abnormally elevated concentration of a purine compound. Purine compounds are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring.

name: decreased circulating purine concentration
decrease circulate purine concentration
HP:0004369.def: Abnormally reduced concentration of a purine compound. Purine compounds are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring.

name: reduced consciousness
reduce consciousness
HP:0004372.def: Abnormally diminished level of attention, responsiveness, or wakefulness.

name: focal dystonia
focal dystonia
HP:0004373.def: A type of dystonia that is localized to a specific part of the body.

name: hemiplegia / hemiparesis
hemiplegia / hemiparesis
HP:0004374.def: Loss of strength in the arm, leg, and sometimes face on one side of the body. Hemiplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas hemiparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.
synonym: paralysis or weakness of one side of body
paralysis or weakness of one side of body

name: neoplasm of the nervous system
neoplasm of the nervous system
HP:0004375.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the nervous system.

name: neuroblastic tumor
neuroblastic tumor

name: hematological neoplasm
hematological neoplasm
HP:0004377.def: Neoplasms located in the blood and blood-forming tissue (the bone marrow and lymphatic tissue).

name: abnormality of alkaline phosphatase level
abnormality of alkaline phosphatase level
HP:0004379.def: An abnormality of alkaline phosphatase level.

name: aortic valve calcification
aortic valve calcification
HP:0004380.def: Deposition of calcium salts in the aortic valve.

name: supravalvular aortic stenosis
supravalvular aortic stenosis

name: mitral valve calcification
mitral valve calcification
HP:0004382.def: Abnormal calcification of the mitral valve.

name: hypoplastic left heart
hypoplastic leave heart

name: type i truncus arteriosus
type i truncus arteriosus
HP:0004384.def: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with a short pulmonary trunk arises from the truncus arteriosus, giving rise to both pulmonary arteries.

name: gastrointestinal inflammation
gastrointestinal inflammation
HP:0004386.def: Inflammation of the alimentary part of the gastrointestinal system.

enterocolitis

name: microcolon
microcolon

hamartomatous polyposis

prune belly

name: malnutrition
malnutrition

name: ectopic anus
ectopic anus
HP:0004397.def: Abnormal displacement or malposition of the anus.

name: peptic ulcer
peptic ulcer

Peptic ulcers are usually located in the stomach or proximal duodenum, but they can also be found in the oesophagus or Meckel's diverticulum. Infection with Helicobacter pylori and the use of non steroidal antiinflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or aspirin are the main risk factors of both gastric and duodenal peptic ulcers.

sore in the lining of gastrointestinal tract

name: meconium ileus
meconium ileus

name: hyposmia
hyposmia

deviate nasal septum

name: abnormality of the pulmonary artery
abnormality of the pulmonary artery

precocious atherosclerosis

intermittent claudication

arterial thrombosis

name: elevated systolic blood pressure

HP:0004421.def: Abnormal increase in systolic blood pressure.

name: biparietal narrowing

name: cranium bifidum occultum
cranium bifidum occultum
HP:0004423.def: Cranium bifidum occultum, also known as Catlin mark, is a congenital midline skull defect presenting as an enlarged posterior fontanelle in the upper posterior angle of the parietal bone close to the intersection of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures.1, 2, 3 Cranium bifidum occultum occurs due to a defect in intramembranous ossification, a process through which skull bones (frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and occipital bones superior to the mendosal suture) ossify under a vascularized membrane toward the midline to cover the brain.1, 4, 5 Unlike cranium bifidum cysticum, cranium bifidum occultum does not have herniation of intracranial contents. As the skull grows, the midline cranium bifidum occultum defect is separated into bilateral enlarged parietal foramina (EPF) by a midline osseous bridge.

name: abnormal cheek morphology
abnormal cheek morphology
HP:0004426.def: An abnormality of the cheek- one of two bilateral soft tissue facial structures in the region of the face inferior to the eyes and between the nose and the ear. \"Buccal\

elfin facies

Because of the imprecision in this definition it is preferable to describe these features precisely. This term is retained because it was often used in the past, but it should not be used for new annotations.

name: recurrent viral infections
recurrent viral infection

name: severe combined immunodeficiency
severe combine immunodeficiency
HP:0004430.def: A type of primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.

name: complement deficiency
complement deficiency

distal ulnar hypoplasia

shortening of all phalanx of the toe

unilateral ulnar hypoplasia

proximal humeral metaphyseal irregularity

name: diaphyseal cortical sclerosis
diaphyseal cortical sclerosis

name: anterolateral radial head dislocation
anterolateral radial head dislocation

fragment , irregular epiphysis

proximal fibular overgrowth

name: proximal radial head dislocation
proximal radial head dislocation

name: hyperextensibility at wrists
hyperextensibility at wrist
HP:0005072.def: The ability of the wrist joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

name: anterior radial head dislocation
anterior radial head dislocation

name: limited knee flexion / extension
limited knee flexion / extension
HP:0005085.def: A limited ability of the knee joint to perform extension and flexion.

name: abnormal metaphyseal trabeculation
abnormal metaphyseal trabeculation
HP:0005089.def: An abnormality of the pattern of trabecula (small interconnecting rods of bone) in a metaphyseal region of bone.

name: lateral femoral bowing
lateral femoral bowing
HP:0005090.def: A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.

name: streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
HP:0005092.def: The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
synonym: streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone
streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone

name: absent proximal radial epiphyses
absent proximal radial epiphysis
HP:0005093.def: Absence of the proximal radial epiphysis.

name: distal femoral bowing
distal femoral bowing
HP:0005096.def: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the femur.

name: premature birth following premature rupture of fetal membranes
premature birth follow premature rupture of fetal membrane
synonym: premature birth following premature rupture of foetal membranes
premature birth follow premature rupture of foetal membrane

name: high - frequency hearing impairment
high - frequency hearing impairment
HP:0005101.def: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).

name: cochlear degeneration
cochlear degeneration
HP:0005102.def: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the cochlea.

name: calcification of the auricular cartilage
calcification of the auricular cartilage
HP:0005103.def: Ossification affecting the external ear cartilage.

name: hypoplastic nasal septum
hypoplastic nasal septum
synonym: decreased size of septum of nose
decreased size of septum of nose

name: abnormality of the vertebral endplates
abnormality of the vertebral endplate
HP:0005106.def: Any abnormality of the vertebral end plates, which are the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral discs.

name: abnormal sacrum morphology
abnormal sacrum morphology
HP:0005107.def: An abnormality of the sacral bone.

name: abnormal intervertebral disk morphology
abnormal intervertebral disk morphology
HP:0005108.def: Any structural abnormality of the intervertebral disk.

name: abnormality of the achilles tendon
abnormality of the achilles tendon
HP:0005109.def: An abnormality of the Achilles tendon.

name: atrial fibrillation
atrial fibrillation
HP:0005110.def: An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.
synonym: quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat
quiver upper heart chamber result in irregular heartbeat

name: obsolete dilatation of the ascending aorta
obsolete dilatation of the ascending aorta
abdominal aortic aneurysm
abdominal aortic aneurysm
HP:0005112.def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta.

name: aortic arch aneurysm
aortic arch aneurysm
HP:0005113.def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch.

name: obsolete abnormalities of the peripheral arteries
obsolete abnormality of the peripheral artery
supraventricular arrhythmia
supraventricular arrhythmia
HP:0005115.def: A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.

name: arterial tortuosity
arterial tortuosity
HP:0005116.def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.

name: elevated diastolic blood pressure
elevate diastolic blood pressure
HP:0005117.def: Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.

name: abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
HP:0005120.def: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.

name: posterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
posterior scalloping of vertebral body
HP:0005121.def: An excessive concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.

name: pericardial constriction
pericardial constriction
HP:0005132.def: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.

name: right ventricular dilatation
right ventricular dilatation
HP:0005133.def: Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle.

name: absence of the pulmonary valve
absence of the pulmonary valve
HP:0005134.def: Refers to the specific combination of defects with a severely dysplastic pulmonary valve and massively dilated branch pulmonary arteries.

name: abnormal t - wave
abnormal t - wave
HP:0005135.def: An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.

name: mitral annular calcification
mitral annular calcification
HP:0005136.def: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.

name: anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascend aorta
HP:0005143.def: The right pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

name: ventricular septal hypertrophy
ventricular septal hypertrophy
HP:0005144.def: The dividing wall between left and right sides of the heart, thickens and bulges into the left ventricle.

name: coronary artery stenosis
coronary artery stenosis
HP:0005145.def: Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.

name: cardiac valve calcification
cardiac valve calcification
HP:0005146.def: Abnormal calcification of a cardiac valve.

name: pulmonary valve defects
pulmonary valve defect
HP:0005148.def: Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.

name: abnormal atrioventricular conduction
abnormal atrioventricular conduction
HP:0005150.def: An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.

name: preductal coarctation of the aorta
preductal coarctation of the aorta
HP:0005151.def: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized proximal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the preductal region of aortic arch.

name: histiocytoid cardiomyopathy
histiocytoid cardiomyopathy
HP:0005152.def: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized pathologically by hamartomatous lesions of cardiac Purkinje cells.

name: ventricular escape rhythm
ventricular escape rhythm
HP:0005155.def: A ventricular escape rhythm occurs whenever higher-lever pacemakers in AV junction or sinus node fail to control ventricular activation. Escape rate is usually 20-40 bpm, often associated with broad QRS complexes (at least 120 ms).

name: concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
HP:0005157.def: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

name: total anomalous pulmonary venous return
total anomalous pulmonary venous return
HP:0005160.def: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return refers to a congenital malformation in which all four pulmonary veins do not connect normally to the left atrium, but instead drain abnormally to the right atrium.

name: abnormal left ventricular function
abnormal leave ventricular function
HP:0005162.def: Inability of the left ventricle to perform its normal physiologic function. Failure is either due to an inability to contract the left ventricle or the inability to relax completely and fill with blood during diastole.

name: dysplastic pulmonary valve
dysplastic pulmonary valve
HP:0005164.def: A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

name: shortened pr interval
shorten pr interval
HP:0005165.def: Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

name: elevated right atrial pressure
elevate right atrial pressure
HP:0005168.def: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.

name: complete heart block with broad qrs complexes
complete heart block with broad qrs complex
HP:0005170.def: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at a relatively low part of the conduction system (below the atrioventricular node), which produces a wide QRS complex.

name: left posterior fascicular block
leave posterior fascicular block
HP:0005172.def: Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

name: membranous subvalvular aortic stenosis
membranous subvalvular aortic stenosis
HP:0005174.def: Subvalvular stenosis is caused by a diaphragm-like membrane. The stenosis is clinically manifested like any other form of aortic stenosis but is often associated with some aortic insufficiency.

name: dysplastic aortic valve
dysplastic aortic valve
HP:0005176.def: A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

name: premature arteriosclerosis
premature arteriosclerosis
HP:0005177.def: Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.

name: complete heart block with narrow qrs complexes
complete heart block with narrow qrs complex
HP:0005178.def: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at the atrioventricular node, which produces a narrow QRS complex.

name: tricuspid regurgitation
tricuspid regurgitation
HP:0005180.def: Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.

name: premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
HP:0005181.def: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.

name: bicuspid pulmonary valve
bicuspid pulmonary valve
HP:0005182.def: The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.

name: pericardial lymphangiectasia
pericardial lymphangiectasia
HP:0005183.def: An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

name: prolonged qtc interval
prolonged qtc interval
HP:0005184.def: A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

name: global systolic dysfunction
global systolic dysfunction
HP:0005185.def: A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.

name: synovial lining hyperplasia
synovial lining hyperplasia
HP:0005186.def: Synovial hyperplasia involves proliferation of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and leads to synovial thickening, which can be observed radiographically.

name: flattened metatarsal heads
flatten metatarsal head
HP:0005194.def: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.
synonym: flattened head of long bone of foot
flatten head of long bone of foot

name: generalized morning stiffness
generalize morning stiffness
HP:0005197.def: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.

name: stiff interphalangeal joints
stiff interphalangeal joint
HP:0005198.def: Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

name: aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
helicobacter pylori infection
helicobacter pylorus infection
HP:0005202.def: A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.

name: spontaneous esophageal perforation
spontaneous esophageal perforation
HP:0005203.def: The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.

name: pancreatic pseudocyst
pancreatic pseudocyst
HP:0005206.def: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.

name: secretory diarrhea
secretory diarrhea
HP:0005208.def: Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

name: intrahepatic bile duct cysts
intrahepatic bile duct cyst
HP:0005209.def: The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.

name: anal mucosal leukoplakia
anal mucosal leukoplakia
HP:0005212.def: Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.

name: pancreatic calcification
pancreatic calcification
HP:0005213.def: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.

name: intestinal obstruction
intestinal obstruction
HP:0005214.def: Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.

name: frequent giardia lamblia infestation
frequent giardia lamblia infestation
HP:0005215.def: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.

name: impaired mastication
impaired mastication
HP:0005216.def: An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.

name: anoperineal fistula
anoperineal fistula
HP:0005218.def: The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.

name: absence of intrinsic factor
absence of intrinsic factor
HP:0005219.def: Absence of gastric intrinsic factor, which is normally produced by the parietal cells of the stomach, and is required for the absorption of vitamin B12.
synonym: intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice
intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice

name: bowel diverticulosis
bowel diverticulosis
HP:0005222.def: The presence of multiple diverticula of the intestine.

name: rectal abscess
rectal abscess
HP:0005224.def: A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.

name: intestinal edema
intestinal edema
HP:0005225.def: Accumulation of cell free, noninflammatony fluid within the wall of the intestinal tract producing uniform thickening of the mucosal folds.

name: adenomatous colonic polyposis
adenomatous colonic polyposis
HP:0005227.def: Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.

name: pancreatic dysplasia
pancreatic dysplasia
HP:0005232.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the pancreas.

name: hypoplasia of the gallbladder
hypoplasia of the gallbladder
HP:0005233.def: The presence of a hypoplastic gallbladder.

name: jejunal atresia
jejunal atresia
HP:0005235.def: A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.

name: chronic calcifying pancreatitis
chronic calcifying pancreatitis
HP:0005236.def: A form of chronic pancreatitis that is characterized by calcification.

name: degenerative liver disease
degenerative liver disease
HP:0005237.def: The presence of degenerative changes of the liver.

name: total intestinal aganglionosis
total intestinal aganglionosis
HP:0005241.def: A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.

name: extrahepatic biliary duct atresia
extrahepatic biliary duct atresia
HP:0005242.def: Atresia in the extrahepatic bile duct.

name: partial abdominal muscle agenesis
partial abdominal muscle agenesis
HP:0005243.def: Failure to form of portions of the abdominal musculature.

name: gastrointestinal infarctions
gastrointestinal infarction
synonym: death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply
death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply

name: giant hypertrophic gastritis
giant hypertrophic gastritis
HP:0005246.def: A type of gastritis characterized by excessive proliferation of the gastric mucosa and diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal folds.

name: hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
intrahepatic biliary atresia
intrahepatic biliary atresia
HP:0005248.def: Atresia in the intrahepatic bile duct.

name: absence of pectoralis minor muscle

unilateral absence of pectoralis major muscle
HP:0005256.def: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.
