name: diverticulosis of trachea
diverticulosis of trachea
HP:0006509.def: Tracheal diverticula are blind-ended outpouchings arising from the trachea. They are usually an incidental finding. Occasionally they can mimic pneumomediastinum. Tracheal diverticula are either congenital or acquired, in the latter case the most common causes are prolonged increased intraluminal pressure, e.g. chronic cough, COPD, tracheomalacia, and iatrogenic (e.g. post-surgical).

name: chronic pulmonary obstruction
chronic pulmonary obstruction
HP:0006510.def: An anomaly that is characterized progressive airflow obstruction that is only partly reversible, inflammation in the airways, and systemic effects or comorbities.

name: laryngeal stridor
laryngeal stridor
HP:0006511.def: An abnormal high-pitched noisy sound, occurring during inhalation or exhalation caused by the incomplete obstruction in the throat.

name: hypersensitivity pneumonitis
hypersensitivity pneumonitis
HP:0006516.def: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis involves inhalation of an antigen. This leads to an exaggerated immune response and a following inflammation of the alveoli within the lungs. The main feature of chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis on lung biopsies is expansion of the interstitium by lymphocytes accompanied by an occasional multinucleated giant cell or loose granuloma. After exposure to the provoking antigen, following symptoms can be seen: fever, chills, malaise, cough, hemoptysis, chest tightness, dyspnea, rash, swelling and headache and can be completely reversible, based on the duration of the illness, categorized as acute (HP:0011009), subacute (HP:0011011), and chronic (HP:0011010).

name: intraalveolar phospholipid accumulation
intraalveolar phospholipid accumulation
HP:0006517.def: Accumulation of amorphous PAS-positive material in the space betweem alveolar macrophages, sometimes as condensed form (oval bodies) are typically found in alveolar proteinosis.
synonym: detection of pas - positive extracellular material in broncho - alveolar lavage
detection of pas - positive extracellular material in broncho - alveolar lavage

name: pulmonary venous occlusion
pulmonary venous occlusion
HP:0006518.def: Substantial narrowing or blockage of small pulmonary veins as a result of disorganized smooth muscle hypertrophy and collagen matrix deposition.

name: pulmonary lymphangiectasia
pulmonary lymphangiectasia
HP:0006521.def: Abnormal dilatation of the pulmonary lymphatic vessels. Lymphatic fluid in the lung is derived from normal leakage of fluid out of the blood capillaries in the lung. In pulmonary lymphangiectasia, the pulmonary lymphatics are not properly connected and become dilated with fluid.

name: lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia
HP:0006527.def: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis is a benign lymphoproliferative disorder of the lung that is characterized by the presence of a dense, predominantly lymphocytic interstitial infiltrate (lymphocytes, plasma cells, other elements of the lymphoreticular system) that expands the alveolar septa.

name: chronic lung disease
chronic lung disease
HP:0006528.def: According to the definitions of the American and British Thoracic Societies, including pulmonary functional tests, X-rays, and CT scans for items such as fibrosis, bronchiectasis, bullae, emphysema, nodular or lymphomatous abnormalities.

name: abnormal pulmonary lymphatics
abnormal pulmonary lymphatics
HP:0006529.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary lymphatic chain.

name: abnormal pulmonary interstitial morphology
abnormal pulmonary interstitial morphology
HP:0006530.def: Abnormality of the lung parenchyma extending to the pulmonary interstitium and leading to diffuse pulmonary fibrosis.
synonym: abnormality in area between air sacs in lung
abnormality in area between air sac in lung

name: recurrent pneumonia
recurrent pneumonia
HP:0006532.def: An increased susceptibility to pneumonia as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of pneumonia.

name: recurrent intrapulmonary hemorrhage
recurrent intrapulmonary hemorrhage
HP:0006535.def: A recurrent hemorrhage occurring within the lung.

name: airway obstruction
airway obstruction
HP:0006536.def: Obstruction of conducting airways of the lung.

name: recurrent bronchopulmonary infections
recurrent bronchopulmonary infection
HP:0006538.def: An increased susceptibility to bronchopulmonary infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bronchopulmonary infections.
synonym: recurrent infections in bronchi and lungs
recurrent infection in bronchus and lung

name: obsolete chronic obstructive airway disease from birth
obsolete chronic obstructive airway disease from birth
extrapulmonary sequestrum
extrapulmonary sequestrum
HP:0006544.def: A type of pulmonary sequestration that is completely enclosed in its own pleural sac, occurring above, within, or below the diaphragm, and without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.

name: pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
pulmonary arteriovenous malformation
HP:0006548.def: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformation, a condition most commonly associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, is an abnormal communication between the pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary communication. HRCT images usually show a coarse spidery appearance of the peripheral vascular markings in the lungs. More specific findings are obtained in the pulmonary angiogram where the normally invisible capillary phase is replaced by irregular vascular channels bridging the peripheral branches of pulmonary arteries and veins.

name: acute hepatic failure
acute hepatic failure
HP:0006554.def: Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as acute if there is onset of encephalopathy within 8 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.

name: diffuse hepatic steatosis
diffuse hepatic steatosis
HP:0006555.def: A diffuse form of hepatic steatosis.

name: decreased mitochondrial complex iii activity in liver tissue
decreased mitochondrial complex iii activity in liver tissue
HP:0006558.def: Decreased activity of complex III of the mitochondrion in the liver.

name: hepatic calcification
hepatic calcification
HP:0006559.def: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition in the liver.

name: biliary hyperplasia
biliary hyperplasia
HP:0006560.def: Hyperplasia of the biliary tree, as manifested by increased size of bile ducts, dilated lumen, and histologically by an increased number of epithelial cells or hyperplasia.

name: viral hepatitis
viral hepatitis
HP:0006562.def: Inflammation of the liver due to infection with a virus.

name: malformation of the hepatic ductal plate
malformation of the hepatic ductal plate
fluctuating hepatomegaly
fluctuate hepatomegaly
HP:0006564.def: Intermittently increased size of the liver.

name: increased hepatocellular lipid droplets
increase hepatocellular lipid droplet
HP:0006565.def: An abnormal increase in the amount of intracellular lipid droplets in hepatocytes.

name: increased hepatic glycogen content
increase hepatic glycogen content
HP:0006568.def: An increase in the amount of glycogen stored in hepatocytes compared to normal.

name: reduced number of intrahepatic bile ducts
reduced number of intrahepatic bile duct
HP:0006571.def: The presence of reduced numbers of intrahepatic bile duct than normal.

name: acute hepatic steatosis
acute hepatic steatosis
HP:0006573.def: An acute form of hepatic steatosis.

name: macronodular cirrhosis
macronodular cirrhosis
HP:0006577.def: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of large regenerative nodules.

name: prolonged neonatal jaundice
prolonged neonatal jaundice
HP:0006579.def: Neonatal jaundice refers to a yellowing of the skin and other tissues of a newborn infant as a result of increased concentrations of bilirubin in the blood. Neonatal jaundice affects over half of all newborns to some extent in the first week of life. Prolonged neonatal jaundice is said to be present if the jaundice persists for longer than 14 days in term infants and 21 days in preterm infants.
synonym: prolonged yellowing of skin in newborn
prolonged yellowing of skin in newborn

name: portal fibrosis
portal fibrosis
HP:0006580.def: Fibroblast proliferation and fiber expansion from the portal areas to the lobule.

name: depletion of mitochondrial dna in liver
depletion of mitochondrial dna in liver
HP:0006581.def: An abnormal reduction in the number of mitochondria in hepatocytes.

name: reye syndrome - like episodes
reye syndrome - like episode
HP:0006582.def: Repeated occurrences of acute noninflammatory encephalopathy and fatty degenerative liver failure.

name: congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle
congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle
HP:0006585.def: The two portions of the clavicle (corresponding to the two primary ossification centers of the clavicle) are connected by a fibrous bridge that is contiguous with the periosteum, and a synovial membrane develops, resulting in a clavicle with a bipartite appearance radiographically. Congenital pseudarthrosis of the clavicle generally presents as a painless mass or swelling over the clavicle.

name: straight clavicles
straight clavicle
HP:0006587.def: An abnormally straight configuration of the clavicle, a tubular bone which normally is doubly curved .

name: absent glenoid fossa
absent glenoid fossa
HP:0006591.def: Lack of development of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.

name: scapulohumeral synostosis
scapulohumeral synostosis
HP:0006595.def: Bony fusion between the humerus and scapula, leading to an impairment in mobility of the affected shoulder joint.
synonym: fusion of shoulder blade to long bone in upper arm
fusion of shoulder blade to long bone in upper arm

name: diaphragmatic paralysis
diaphragmatic paralysis
HP:0006597.def: The presence of a paralyzed diaphragm.

name: irregular ossification at anterior rib ends
irregular ossification at anterior rib end
irregular chondrocostal junctions
irregular chondrocostal junction
HP:0006606.def: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth border between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.

name: precocious costochondral ossification
precocious costochondral ossification
HP:0006607.def: Early ossification of the costochondral junction, which is the joint between the ribs and costal cartilage in the front of the rib cage.

name: midclavicular hypoplasia
midclavicular hypoplasia
HP:0006608.def: Underdevelopment of the middle portion of the clavicle.
synonym: underdeveloped middle portion of the collarbone
underdeveloped middle portion of the collarbone

name: wide intermamillary distance
wide intermamillary distance
HP:0006610.def: A larger than usual distance between the left and right nipple.

name: decreased number of sternal ossification centers
decreased number of sternal ossification center
HP:0006611.def: A less than normal number of sternal ossification centers. The sternum is initially formed from bilateral sternal plates that chondrify and begin to fuse with ribs at 10 weeks gestational age. Ossification starts in the manubrium and upper part of the sternal body at the 6th month, in the middle of the sternal body at the 7th month, in the lower part of the body during the 1st postnatal year and in the xiphoid process between years 5 and 18. The number of ossification centers vary up to six, and it is the ossification centers that are visualized by prenatal ultrasound. This term describes a reduction in the number of ossification centers compared with age-related norms.
synonym: decreased number of sternal ossification centres
decreased number of sternal ossification centre

name: absent in utero rib ossification
absent in utero rib ossification
HP:0006615.def: Lack of formation and mineralization of the ribs in utero.

name: anterior rib punctate calcifications
anterior rib punctate calcification
HP:0006619.def: Deposition of calcium salts in point-like foci within the anterior portion of one or more ribs.

name: costochondral joint sclerosis
costochondral joint sclerosis
HP:0006623.def: Abnormal increase in density of the tissue at the costochondral junctions.

name: multifocal breast carcinoma
multifocal breast carcinoma
HP:0006625.def: Breast carcinoma that is bilateral or otherwise multifocal.

name: absent sternal ossification
absent sternal ossification
HP:0006628.def: Lack of formation of mineralized bony tissue of the sternum.

name: hypoplastic distal segments of scapulae
hypoplastic distal segment of scapula
synonym: small distal segments of the shoulder blade
small distal segment of the shoulder blade
small outermost segments of shoulder blade
small outermost segment of shoulder blade
underdeveloped outermost segments of shoulder blade
underdeveloped outermost segment of shoulder blade

name: glenoid fossa hypoplasia
glenoid fossa hypoplasia
HP:0006633.def: Underdevelopment of the glenoid fossa, which is the cavity in the lateral part of the scapula which articulates with the head of the humerus.

name: osteosclerosis of ribs
osteosclerosis of rib
HP:0006634.def: Osteosclerosis of ribs (increased density related to increased bone mass).

name: midclavicular aplasia
midclavicular aplasia
HP:0006638.def: Developmental defect resulting in congenital absence of the middle portion of the clavicle.

name: multiple rib fractures
multiple rib fracture
HP:0006640.def: More than one fracture of the ribs.

name: thin clavicles
thin clavicle
HP:0006645.def: Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles.

name: costal cartilage calcification
costal cartilage calcification
HP:0006646.def: Calcification of the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage found at the anterior ends of the ribs which serve to prolong the ribs forward and contribute to the elasticity of the walls of the thorax.

name: costochondral pain
costochondral pain
HP:0006649.def: Chest wall pain in the area of the costochondral junctions.

name: thickening of the lateral border of the scapula
thickening of the lateral border of the scapula
synonym: thickening of the lateral border of the shoulder blade
thickening of the lateral border of the shoulder blade

name: aplastic clavicle
aplastic clavicle
HP:0006660.def: Absence of the clavicles as a developmental defect.

name: coat hanger sign of ribs
coat hanger sign of rib
HP:0006665.def: An abnormal morphology of the ribs consisting of shorted, abnormally curved ribs. On posteroanterior chest radiography, the ribs show a curvature resembling that of a coat hanger (clothes hanger).

name: prolonged qrs complex
prolonged qrs complex
HP:0006677.def: Increased time for the complex comprised of the Q wave, R wave, and S wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).. In adults, normal values are 0.06 - 0.10 sec.

name: granulomatous coronary arteritis
granulomatous coronary arteritis
HP:0006679.def: Inflammation of the coronary arteries involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.

name: premature ventricular contraction
premature ventricular contraction
HP:0006682.def: Premature ventricular contractions (PVC) or ventricular extrasystoles are premature contractions of the heart that arise in response to an impulse in the ventricles rather than the normal impulse from the sinoatrial (SA) node.

name: abnormal ventricular filling
abnormal ventricular filling
HP:0006683.def: An abnormality of filling of a ventricle with blood during diastole.

name: ventricular preexcitation with multiple accessory pathways
ventricular preexcitation with multiple accessory pathway
HP:0006684.def: A form of ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of multiple accessory pathways for cardiac conduction.

name: endocardial fibrosis
endocardial fibrosis
HP:0006685.def: The presence of excessive connective tissue in the endocardium.

name: aortic tortuosity
aortic tortuosity
HP:0006687.def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the aorta.

name: bacterial endocarditis
bacterial endocarditis
HP:0006689.def: A bacterial infection of the endocardium, the inner layer of the heart, which usually involves the heart valves.

name: pulmonic valve myxoma
pulmonic valve myxoma
HP:0006691.def: A benign tumor of connective tissue containing mucous or gelatinous material (myxoma) localized in the pumonic valve.

name: short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
HP:0006692.def: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve.

name: early progressive calcific cardiac valvular disease
early progressive calcific cardiac valvular disease
atrioventricular canal defect
atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0006695.def: A defect of the atrioventricular septum of the heart.

name: dilatation of the ventricular cavity
dilatation of the ventricular cavity
HP:0006698.def: A localized outpouching of ventricular cavity that is generally associated with dyskinesia and paradoxical expansion during systole.

name: premature atrial contractions
premature atrial contraction
HP:0006699.def: A type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature atrial contractions or beats caused by signals originating from ectopic atrial sites.

name: coronary artery dissection
coronary artery dissection
HP:0006702.def: Acute occurrence of a dissection (tear within the tunica intima and entry of blood into the tunica media) of a coronary artery.

name: abnormal coronary artery morphology
abnormal coronary artery morphology
HP:0006704.def: Any structural abnormality of the coronary arteries.

name: abnormal atrioventricular valve morphology
abnormal atrioventricular valve morphology
HP:0006705.def: An abnormality of an atrioventricular valve.

name: abnormality of the hepatic vasculature
abnormality of the hepatic vasculature
HP:0006707.def: An abnormality of the hepatic vasculature.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the clavicles
aplasia / hypoplasia of the clavicle
HP:0006710.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the clavicles (collar bones).

name: aplasia / hypoplasia involving bones of the thorax
aplasia / hypoplasia involve bone of the thorax
acute lymphoblastic leukemia
acute lymphoblastic leukemia
HP:0006721.def: A form of acute leukemia characterized by excess lympoblasts.

name: pancreatic adenocarcinoma
pancreatic adenocarcinoma
HP:0006725.def: The presence of an adenocarcinoma of the pancreas.

name: t - cell acute lymphoblastic leukemias
t - cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
HP:0006727.def: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia of T-cell origin. It comprises about 15% of childhood cases and 25% of adult cases. It is more common in males than females.

name: follicular thyroid carcinoma
follicular thyroid carcinoma
HP:0006731.def: The presence of an follicular adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland.

name: papillary renal cell carcinoma type 2
papillary renal cell carcinoma type 2
HP:0006732.def: A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma in which the papillae are covered by large eosinophilic cells with pleomorphic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and nuclear pseudostratification.

name: acute megakaryocytic leukemia
acute megakaryocytic leukemia
HP:0006733.def: A rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia evolving from primitive megakaryoblasts.

name: renal cortical adenoma
renal cortical adenoma
HP:0006735.def: The presence of an adenoma in the cortex of the kidney.

name: extraadrenal pheochromocytoma
extraadrenal pheochromocytoma
HP:0006737.def: Pheochromocytoma not originating from the adrenal medulla but from another source such as from chromaffin cells in or about sympathetic ganglia.

name: squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
HP:0006739.def: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is a malignant tumor of squamous epithelium.

name: transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
HP:0006740.def: The presence of a carcinoma of the urinary bladder with origin in a transitional epithelial cell.

name: adrenocortical carcinoma
adrenocortical carcinoma
HP:0006744.def: A malignant neoplasm of the adrenal cortex that may produce hormones such as cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen, or testosterone.

name: adrenal pheochromocytoma
adrenal pheochromocytoma
HP:0006748.def: Pheochromocytoma originating from the adrenal medulla.

name: paraspinal neurofibroma
paraspinal neurofibroma
HP:0006751.def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized adjacent to the spine.

name: neoplasm of the stomach
neoplasm of the stomach
HP:0006753.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the stomach.

name: cutaneous leiomyosarcoma
cutaneous leiomyosarcoma
HP:0006755.def: The presence of leiomyosarcoma of the skin.

name: malignant genitourinary tract tumor
malignant genitourinary tract tumor
HP:0006758.def: The presence of a malignant neoplasm of the genital system.

name: renal pelvic carcinoma
renal pelvic carcinoma
HP:0006762.def: The presence of a carcinoma in the renal pelvis.

name: chondrosarcoma
chondrosarcoma
HP:0006765.def: A slowly growing malignant neoplasm derived from cartilage cells.

name: papillary renal cell carcinoma
papillary renal cell carcinoma
HP:0006766.def: The presence of renal cell carcinoma in the renal papilla.

name: pituitary prolactin cell adenoma
pituitary prolactin cell adenoma
HP:0006767.def: A type of pituitary adenoma originating in prolactin secreting cells. This kind of adenoma is characterized by overproduction of prolactin, and may cause loss of menstrual periods and breast milk production in women.

name: clear cell renal cell carcinoma
clear cell renal cell carcinoma
HP:0006770.def: A subtype of renal cell carcinoma thought to originate from mature renal tubular cells in the proximal tubule of the nehpron.

name: duodenal adenocarcinoma
duodenal adenocarcinoma
HP:0006771.def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the duodenum.

name: renal angiomyolipoma
renal angiomyolipoma
HP:0006772.def: A benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.

name: ovarian papillary adenocarcinoma
ovarian papillary adenocarcinoma
HP:0006774.def: The presence of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the ovary.

name: multiple myeloma
multiple myeloma
HP:0006775.def: A malignant plasma cell tumor growing within soft tissue or within the skeleton.

name: benign genitourinary tract neoplasm
benign genitourinary tract neoplasm
HP:0006778.def: A non-malignant neoplasm of the genitourinary system.

name: parathyroid carcinoma
parathyroid carcinoma
HP:0006780.def: A malignancy of the parathyroid glands. Parathyroid carcinoma usually secretes parathyroid hormone, leading to hyperparathyroidism.

name: hurthle cell thyroid adenoma
hurthle cell thyroid adenoma
HP:0006781.def: A kind of thyroid adenoma characterized by the presence of oxyphil cells.

name: limb - girdle muscular dystrophy
limb - girdle muscular dystrophy
HP:0006785.def: Muscular dystrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle (the hips and shoulders).

name: loss of ability to walk in first decade
loss of ability to walk in first decade
synonym: loss of ability to walk in first decade
loss of ability to walk in first decade

name: basal ganglia cysts
basal ganglion cyst
synonym: cystic lesions in the basal ganglia
cystic lesion in the basal ganglion

name: abnormal anterior horn cell morphology
abnormal anterior horn cell morphology
HP:0006802.def: Any anomaly of the anterior horn cell.
synonym: abnormality of the anterior horn cell
abnormality of the anterior horn cell
abnormality of the anterior horn cells
abnormality of the anterior horn cell
anomaly of the anterior horn cells
anomaly of the anterior horn cell

name: vivid hallucination
vivid hallucination
HP:0006803.def: Perceptual experiences that are vivid, intense, and sensory in nature occur in the absence of corresponding stimuli from the external environment.

name: cerebral hypomyelination
cerebral hypomyelination
HP:0006808.def: Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the white matter of the central nervous system.

name: white mater abnormalities in the posterior periventricular region
white mater abnormality in the posterior periventricular region
focal hemiclonic seizure
focal hemiclonic seizure
HP:0006813.def: A type of focal clonic seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking rapidly involves one side of the body at seizure onset.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis
aplasia / hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis
HP:0006817.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: 4 - layered lissencephaly
4 - layer lissencephaly
HP:0006818.def: A form of lissencephaly in which the cortex is thickened and has four more or less disorganized layers rather than six normal layers resulting from incomplete neuronal migration during brain development. At neuropathological examination, a 4-layered cortex consists of an upper molecular layer, a second thin cellular layer containing pyramidal neurons usually observed in layer V, a third pale poorly cellular layer and a fourth thick deep layer made up of neurons which had failed to migrate. Radiologocally would manifest as agyria or pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm.

name: frontal polymicrogyria
frontal polymicrogyria
HP:0006821.def: A type of polymicrogyria with a gradient of severity (anterior more severe than posterior) extending from frontal poles posteriorly to precentral gyrus and inferiorly to frontal operculum.

name: pallor of dorsal columns of the spinal cord
pallor of dorsal column of the spinal cord
HP:0006825.def: An abnormally pale appearance of the dorsal portion of the gray substance of the spinal cord. This finding can be observed by histological examination.

name: severe muscular hypotonia
severe muscular hypotonia
HP:0006829.def: A severe degree of muscular hypotonia characterized by markedly reduced muscle tone.

name: obsolete severe neonatal hypotonia in males
obsolete severe neonatal hypotonia in male
developmental stagnation at onset of seizures
developmental stagnation at onset of seizure
HP:0006834.def: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills, following the onset of epilepsy.

name: congenital horner syndrome
congenital horner syndrome
HP:0006837.def: A type of Horner syndrome with congenital onset.

name: absent patellar reflexes
absent patellar reflex
HP:0006844.def: Absence of the knee jerk reflex, which can normally be elicited by tapping the patellar tendon with a reflex hammer just below the patella.

name: hypodysplasia of the corpus callosum
hypodysplasia of the corpus callosum
HP:0006849.def: Developmental defect characterized by a small and malformed corpus callosum.

name: hypoplasia of the ventral pons
hypoplasia of the ventral pons
HP:0006850.def: Underdevelopment of the ventral portion of the pons.

name: symmetric spinal nerve root neurofibromas
symmetric spinal nerve root neurofibroma
HP:0006851.def: Multiple neurofibromas of the spinal nerve roots with a symmetric distribution.
synonym: spinal nerve root neurofibromas , symmetric , multiple
spinal nerve root neurofibroma , symmetric , multiple

name: episodic generalized hypotonia
episodic generalize hypotonia
HP:0006852.def: The occurrence of repeated episodes of generalized muscular hypotonia.

name: cerebellar vermis atrophy
cerebellar vermis atrophy
HP:0006855.def: Wasting (atrophy) of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: impaired distal proprioception
impaired distal proprioception
HP:0006858.def: A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position occuring at distal joints.

name: severe expressive language delay
severe expressive language delay
HP:0006863.def: A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

name: sensorimotor polyneuropathy affecting arms more than legs
sensorimotor polyneuropathy affect arm more than leg
lobar holoprosencephaly
lobar holoprosencephaly
HP:0006870.def: A type of holoprosencephaly in which most of the right and left cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles are separated but the most rostral aspect of the telencephalon, the frontal lobes, are fused, especially ventrally.

name: symmetrical progressive peripheral demyelination
symmetrical progressive peripheral demyelination
HP:0006873.def: A symmetric and progressive loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

name: pontocerebellar atrophy
pontocerebellar atrophy
HP:0006879.def: Atrophy affecting the pons and the cerebellum.

name: diffuse peripheral demyelination
diffuse peripheral demyelination
HP:0006881.def: A diffuse loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

name: impaired distal vibration sensation
impaired distal vibration sensation
HP:0006886.def: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the distal portions of the limbs.

name: intellectual disability , progressive
intellectual disability , progressive
HP:0006887.def: The term progressive intellectual disability should be used if intelligence decreases/deteriorates over time.

name: intellectual disability , borderline
intellectual disability , borderline
HP:0006889.def: Borderline intellectual disability is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 70-85.

name: frontotemporal cerebral atrophy
frontotemporal cerebral atrophy
HP:0006892.def: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the frontotemporal cerebrum.

name: hypnopompic hallucination
hypnopompic hallucination
HP:0006896.def: Brief hallucinations that occur as you wake up in the morning, in a state that falls somewhere between dreaming and being fully awake.

name: abducens palsy
abducens palsy
HP:0006897.def: Malfunction of the abducens nerve as manifested by impairment of the ability of the affected eye to be moved outward. Patients who develop abducens nerve palsy often present with binocular horizontal diplopia, which is a double vision when looking at objects side by side. There will be a notable weakness of the ipsilateral lateral rectus muscle leading to a deficit in of eye abduction on the affected side. Some patients may present with a constant head turning movement to maintain binocular fusion and to lessen the degree of diplopia.

name: congenital intracerebral calcification
congenital intracerebral calcification
HP:0006906.def: The presence of calcium deposition within brain structures that is present already at the time of birth.

name: inability to walk by childhood / adolescence
inability to walk by childhood / adolescence
synonym: inability to walk by childhood / adolescence
inability to walk by childhood / adolescence

name: intraaxonal accumulation of curvilinear autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
intraaxonal accumulation of curvilinear autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
HP:0006916.def: Curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material within axons.

name: abnormal aggressive , impulsive or violent behavior
abnormal aggressive , impulsive or violent behavior
synonym: abnormal aggressive , impulsive or violent behaviour
abnormal aggressive , impulsive or violent behaviour

name: axial muscle stiffness
axial muscle stiffness
HP:0006921.def: Stiffness (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) of the axial musculature.

name: unilateral polymicrogyria
unilateral polymicrogyria
HP:0006927.def: Excessive number of small gyri (convolutions) on the surface of one side of the brain.

name: hypoglycemic encephalopathy
hypoglycemic encephalopathy
HP:0006929.def: Brain damage related to a lowering of blood glucose below a critical level (around 30 mg/dl), which may lead to confusion, lethargy and delirium followed by seizures and coma. Prolonged hypoglycemia may lead to irreversible brain damage.

name: frontoparietal cortical dysplasia
frontoparietal cortical dysplasia
HP:0006930.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cortex of frontal lobe and the cortex of parietal lobe.

name: pericallosal lipoma
pericallosal lipoma
HP:0006931.def: Pericallosal lipomas are congenital soft masses of adipose cells encapsulated by a thin layer of fibrous tissue, appearing adjacent to the corpus callosum of the brain.

name: transient psychotic episodes
transient psychotic episode
HP:0006932.def: Relatively short-lived periods of psychosis are characterized by the sudden onset of severe disturbances in perception, thinking, and behavior. These episodes typically last for a brief duration, generally ranging from a few days to a few weeks, and are often triggered by a significant stressor or traumatic event.

name: congenital nystagmus
congenital nystagmus
HP:0006934.def: Nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

name: impaired distal tactile sensation
impaired distal tactile sensation
HP:0006937.def: A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation) on the skin of the distal limbs. This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.

name: impaired vibration sensation at ankles
impaired vibration sensation at ankle
HP:0006938.def: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration at the ankles. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to the malleoli of the ankles.

name: abolished vibration sense
abolish vibration sense
HP:0006944.def: A complete loss of the ability to perceive vibration.

name: recurrent meningitis
recurrent meningitis
HP:0006946.def: An increased susceptibility to meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of meningitis.

name: olivopontocerebellar hypoplasia
olivopontocerebellar hypoplasia
HP:0006955.def: Hypoplasia of the cerebellum, pontine nuclei, and inferior olivary nucleus.

name: obsolete loss of ability to walk
obsolete loss of ability to walk
abnormal auditory evoked potentials
abnormal auditory evoke potential
HP:0006958.def: An abnormality of the auditory evoked potentials, which are used to trace the signal generated by a sound, from the cochlear nerve, through the lateral lemniscus, to the medial geniculate nucleus, and to the cortex.

name: proximal spinal muscular atrophy
proximal spinal muscular atrophy
HP:0006959.def: Proximal spinal muscular atrophy, i.e., muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

name: choroid plexus calcification
choroid plexus calcification
HP:0006960.def: The presence of calcium deposition in the choroid plexus.

name: gait instability , worse in the dark
gait instability , bad in the dark
synonym: unstable walking , worse in the dark
unstable walking , bad in the dark

name: periventricular leukomalacia
periventricular leukomalacia
HP:0006970.def: Periventricular leukomalacia is characterized by diffuse injury of deep cerebral white matter, accompanied in its most severe form by focal necrosis. The neuropathologic hallmarks of PVL are microglial activation and focal and diffuse periventricular depletion of premyelinating oligodendroglia.

name: necrotizing encephalopathy
necrotizing encephalopathy
HP:0006976.def: A type of encephalopathy (brain disease, damage, or malfunction accompanied by an altered mental state) that is characterized by evidence of necrosis of brain tissue.

name: deficit in grammar
deficit in grammar
HP:0006977.def: Deficit in grammar, including syntax and morphology.

name: sleep - wake cycle disturbance
sleep - wake cycle disturbance
HP:0006979.def: Any abnormality of an individual's circadian rhythm that affects the timing of sleeping and being awake is referred to as a sleep-wake disorder.

name: progressive leukoencephalopathy
progressive leukoencephalopathy
HP:0006980.def: Leukoencephalopathy that gets more severe with time.

name: obsolete distal sensory loss of all modalities
obsolete distal sensory loss of all modality
alobar holoprosencephaly
alobar holoprosencephaly
HP:0006988.def: A type of holoprosencephaly characterized by the presence of a single ventricle and no separation of the cerebral hemisphere. The single midline ventricle is often greatly enlarged.

name: dysplastic corpus callosum
dysplastic corpus callosum
HP:0006989.def: Dysplasia and dysgenesis of the corpus callosum are nonspecific descriptions that imply defective development of the corpus callosum. The term dysplasia is applied when the morphology of the corpus callosum is altered as a congenital trait. For instance, the corpus callosum may be hump-shaped, kinked, or a striped corpus callosum that lacks an anatomically distinct genu and splenium.

name: myelin - dependent gliosis
myelin - dependent gliosis
HP:0006990.def: A type of gliosis that occurs in the vicinity of injured neurons.

name: basal ganglia gliosis
basal ganglion gliosis
HP:0006999.def: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the basal ganglia.

name: loss of purkinje cells in the cerebellar vermis
loss of purkinje cell in the cerebellar vermis
motor axonal neuropathy
motor axonal neuropathy
HP:0007002.def: Progressive impairment of function of motor axons with muscle weakness, atrophy, and cramps. The deficits are length-dependent, meaning that muscles innervated by the longest nerves are affected first, so that for instance the arms are affected at a later age than the onset of deficits involving the lower leg.

name: cavitation of the basal ganglia
cavitation of the basal ganglion
HP:0007007.def: The formation of small cavities in the tissue of the basal ganglia.

name: poor fine motor coordination
poor fine motor coordination
HP:0007010.def: An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of small muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Fine motor skills are required to mediate movements of the wrists, hands, fingers, feet, and toes.

name: fourth cranial nerve palsy
fourth cranial nerve palsy
HP:0007011.def: Paralysis of the fourth cranial (trochlear) nerve manifested as weakness of the superior oblique muscle which causes vertical diplopia that is maximal when the affected eye is adducted and directed inferiorly.

name: poor gross motor coordination
poor gross motor coordination
HP:0007015.def: An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of large muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Gross motor skills are required to mediate movements of the arms, legs, and other large body parts.

name: attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
HP:0007018.def: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. The main symptoms are distractibility, impulsivity, hyperactivity, and often trouble organizing tasks and projects, difficulty going to sleep, and social problems from being aggressive, loud, or impatient.

name: antenatal intracerebral hemorrhage
antenatal intracerebral hemorrhage
HP:0007023.def: Cerebral hemorrhage that occurs before birth.

name: pseudobulbar paralysis
pseudobulbar paralysis
HP:0007024.def: Bilateral impairment of the function of the cranial nerves 9-12, which control musculature involved in eating, swallowing, and speech. Pseudobulbar paralysis is characterized clinically by dysarthria, dysphonia, and dysphagia with bifacial paralysis, and may be accompanied by Pseudobulbar behavioral symptoms such as enforced crying and laughing.

name: poorly formed metencephalon
poorly form metencephalon
HP:0007027.def: A morphological abnormality of the metencephalon.

name: cerebral berry aneurysm
cerebral berry aneurysm
HP:0007029.def: A small, sac-like aneurysm (outpouching) of a cerebral blood vessel.

name: cerebellar dysplasia
cerebellar dysplasia
HP:0007033.def: Cerebellar dysplasia (abnormal growth or development) is defined by abnormal cerebellar foliation, white matter arborization, and gray-white matter junction. Cerebellar dysplasia is a neuroimaging finding that describes abnormalities of both the cerebellar cortex and white matter and is associated with variable neurodevelopmental outcome. Dysplasia may globally involve the cerebellum or affect only one cerebellar hemisphere. In addition, cerebellar dysplasia may be associated with cortical/subcortical cysts.

name: symmetric lesions of the basal ganglia
symmetric lesion of the basal ganglion
chronic lymphocytic meningitis
chronic lymphocytic meningitis
HP:0007041.def: Meningitis that persists for more than 4 weeks, and lymphocytes are present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: atrophy of the dentate nucleus
atrophy of the dentate nucleus
HP:0007047.def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of dentate nucleus.

name: large basal ganglia
large basal ganglion
HP:0007048.def: Increased size of the basal ganglia.

name: proximal hyperreflexia
proximal hyperreflexia
HP:0007054.def: Hyperactive stretch reflexes of muscles that move proximal joints (elbow, knee).

name: generalized cerebral atrophy / hypoplasia
generalize cerebral atrophy / hypoplasia
HP:0007058.def: Generalized atrophy or hypoplasia of the cerebrum.

name: aplasia of the inferior half of the cerebellar vermis
aplasia of the inferior half of the cerebellar vermis
synonym: absent inferior half of the cerebellar vermis
absent inferior half of the cerebellar vermis

name: progressive language deterioration
progressive language deterioration
HP:0007064.def: Progressive loss of previously present language abilities.

name: disorganization of the anterior cerebellar vermis
disorganization of the anterior cerebellar vermis
synonym: disorganisation of the anterior cerebellar vermis
disorganisation of the anterior cerebellar vermis

name: proximal limb muscle stiffness
proximal limb muscle stiffness
HP:0007066.def: Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in the proximal limb muscle.

name: distal peripheral sensory neuropathy
distal peripheral sensory neuropathy
HP:0007067.def: Peripheral sensory neuropathy affecting primarily distal sensation.

name: inferior cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
inferior cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
HP:0007068.def: Underdevelopment of the inferior portion of the vermis of cerebellum.

name: thick corpus callosum
thick corpus callosum
HP:0007074.def: Increased vertical dimension of the corpus callosum. This feature can be visualized by sagittal sections on magnetic resonance tomography imaging of the brain.

name: extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
HP:0007076.def: Muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).

name: decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials
decrease amplitude of sensory action potential
HP:0007078.def: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

name: dilated third ventricle
dilated third ventricle
HP:0007082.def: An increase in size of the third ventricle.

name: facial - lingual fasciculations
facial - lingual fasciculation
HP:0007089.def: Fasciculations affecting the tongue muscle and the musculature of the face.

name: paroxysmal choreoathetosis
paroxysmal choreoathetosis
HP:0007098.def: Episodes of choreoathetosis that can occur following triggers such as quick voluntary movements.

name: chiari type i malformation
chiari type i malformation
HP:0007099.def: Arnold-Chiari type I malformation refers to a relatively mild degree of herniation of the posteroinferior region of the cerebellum (the cerebellar tonsils) into the cervical canal with little or no displacement of the fourth ventricle. It is characterized by one or both pointed (not rounded) cerebellar tonsils that project 5 mm below the foramen magnum, measured by a line drawn from the basion to the opisthion (McRae Line)

name: hypointensity of cerebral white matter on mri
hypointensity of cerebral white matter on mri
HP:0007103.def: A darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter.

name: infantile encephalopathy
infantile encephalopathy
HP:0007105.def: Encephalopathy with onset in the infantile period.

name: segmental peripheral demyelination
segmental peripheral demyelination
HP:0007107.def: A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers from segments of the peripheral nervous system.

name: demyelinating peripheral neuropathy
demyelinate peripheral neuropathy
HP:0007108.def: Demyelinating neuropathy is characterized by slow nerve conduction velocities with reduced amplitudes of sensory/motor nerve conduction and prolonged distal latencies.

name: subcortical dementia
subcortical dementia
HP:0007123.def: A particular type of dementia characterized by a pattern of mental defects consisting prominently of forgetfulness, slowness of thought processes, and personality or mood change.

name: proximal amyotrophy
proximal amyotrophy
HP:0007126.def: Amyotrophy (muscular atrophy) affecting the proximal musculature.
synonym: wasting of muscles near the body
wasting of muscle near the body

name: acute demyelinating polyneuropathy
acute demyelinate polyneuropathy
HP:0007131.def: Acute progressive areflexic weakness and mild sensory changes resulting from myelin breakdown and axonal degeneration.

name: pallidal degeneration
pallidal degeneration
HP:0007132.def: Neurodegeneration involving the globus pallidus,a part of the basal ganglia that is involved in the regulation of voluntary movement.

name: sensorimotor neuropathy
sensorimotor neuropathy
synonym: nerve damage causing decreased feeling and movement
nerve damage cause decrease feeling and movement

name: distal upper limb amyotrophy
distal upper limb amyotrophy
HP:0007149.def: Muscular atrophy of distal arm muscles.

name: asymmetric limb muscle stiffness
asymmetric limb muscle stiffness
HP:0007156.def: Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in an asymmetric pattern.

name: progressive extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
progressive extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
HP:0007158.def: A progressive degree of muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).

name: fluctuations in consciousness
fluctuation in consciousness
HP:0007159.def: Changes in one's level of awareness and responsiveness to their environment.

name: diffuse demyelination of the cerebral white matter
diffuse demyelination of the cerebral white matter
HP:0007162.def: A diffuse loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

name: obsolete corticospinal tract disease in lower limbs
obsolete corticospinal tract disease in low limb
periventricular heterotopia
periventricular heterotopia
HP:0007165.def: A form of gray matter heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is typically located periventricularly, also sometimes called subependymal heterotopia. Periventricular means beside the ventricles. This is by far the most common location for heterotopia. Subependymal heterotopia present in a wide array of variations. There can be a small single node or a large number of nodes, can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, can be small or large, single or multiple, and can form a small node or a large wavy or curved mass.

name: paroxysmal dyskinesia
paroxysmal dyskinesia
HP:0007166.def: Episodic bouts of involuntary movements with dystonic, choreic, ballistic movements, or a combination thereof. There is no loss of consciousness during the attacks.

name: absent smooth pursuit
absent smooth pursuit
HP:0007179.def: A complete lack of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.

name: interosseus muscle atrophy
interosseus muscle atrophy
HP:0007181.def: Atrophy of the interosseus muscles (including the palmar interossei that lie on the anterior aspect of the metacarpals, the dorsal interosseus muscles of the hand, which lie between the intercarpals, the plantar interosseus muscles, which lie underneath the metatarsal bones, and the dorsal interossei, which are located between the metatarsal bones.

name: peripheral hypomyelination
peripheral hypomyelination
HP:0007182.def: Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the peripheral nervous system.

name: focal t2 hyperintense basal ganglia lesion
focal t2 hyperintense basal ganglion lesion
HP:0007183.def: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the basal ganglia.
synonym: hyperintense lesions in the basal ganglia on mri
hyperintense lesion in the basal ganglion on mri

name: loss of consciousness
loss of consciousness
HP:0007185.def: Loss of alertness and orientation to place and time.

name: focal lissencephaly
focal lissencephaly
HP:0007187.def: A congenital absence of the convolutions of the cerebral cortex and a poorly formed sylvian fissure that affects a particular part of the cortex.

name: congenital facial diplegia
congenital facial diplegia
HP:0007188.def: Facial diplegia (that is, bilateral facial palsy) with congenital onset.

name: neuronal loss in the cerebral cortex
neuronal loss in the cerebral cortex
bilateral tonic - clonic seizure on awakening
bilateral tonic - clonic seizure on awaken
HP:0007193.def: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure of either generalized or focal onset occurring on or soon after wakening (typically within 90 minutes of waking, regardless of the time of day).
synonym: generalised tonic - clonic seizures on awakening
generalise tonic - clonic seizure on awaken
generalized tonic - clonic seizures on awakening
generalize tonic - clonic seizure on awaken

name: episodic hypersomnia
episodic hypersomnia
HP:0007200.def: Recurrent episodes of severe hypersomnia are accompanied by cognitive and behavioral disturbances, including confusion, derealization, apathy, compulsive eating, and hypersexuality.

name: cerebral artery atherosclerosis
cerebral artery atherosclerosis
HP:0007201.def: The formation of the formation of fibrofatty lesions in the wall of an artery located in the brain.
synonym: plaque build - up in cerebral artery
plaque build - up in cerebral artery

name: hemimegalencephaly
hemimegalencephaly
HP:0007206.def: Enlargement of all or parts of one cerebral hemisphere.

name: photosensitive tonic - clonic seizure
photosensitive tonic - clonic seizure
HP:0007207.def: Generalized-onset tonic-clonic seizures that are provoked by flashing or flickering light.

name: irregular myelin loops
irregular myelin loop
HP:0007208.def: Presence of irregular redundant loops of focally folded myelin in a peripheral nerve.

name: facial paralysis
facial paralysis
HP:0007209.def: Complete loss of ability to move facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (i.e., the seventh cranial nerve).

name: lower limb amyotrophy
low limb amyotrophy
HP:0007210.def: Muscular atrophy affecting the lower limb.

name: periodic hyperkalemic paralysis
periodic hyperkalemic paralysis
HP:0007215.def: Episodes of muscle weakness associated with elevated levels of potassium in the blood.

name: macrogyria
macrogyria
HP:0007227.def: Increased size of cerebral gyri, often associated with a moderate reduction in the number of sulci of the cerebrum.

name: intracerebral periventricular calcifications
intracerebral periventricular calcification
HP:0007229.def: The presence of calcium deposition in the cerebral white matter surrounding the cerebral ventricles.

name: decreased distal sensory nerve action potential
decrease distal sensory nerve action potential
HP:0007230.def: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential in distal nerve segments. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

name: spinocerebellar tract disease in lower limbs
spinocerebellar tract disease in low limb
clusters of axonal regeneration
cluster of axonal regeneration
HP:0007233.def: Groups of small caliber axons in peripheral nerve biospies indicative of axonal regeneration.

name: progressive gait ataxia
progressive gait ataxia
HP:0007240.def: A type of gait ataxia displaying progression of clinical severity.

name: decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fiber
synonym: decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibres
decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibre

name: recurrent external ophthalmoplegia
recurrent external ophthalmoplegia
HP:0007250.def: Alternating and recurrent weakness of the external ocular muscles.

name: abnormal pyramidal sign
abnormal pyramidal sign
HP:0007256.def: Functional neurological abnormalities related to dysfunction of the pyramidal tract.

name: severe demyelination of the white matter
severe demyelination of the white matter
HP:0007258.def: A severe loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

name: type ii lissencephaly
type ii lissencephaly
HP:0007260.def: A form of lissencephaly characterized by an uneven cortical surface with a so called 'cobblestone' appearace. There are no distinguishable cortical layers.

name: symmetric peripheral demyelination
symmetric peripheral demyelination
HP:0007262.def: A symmetric loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

name: spinocerebellar atrophy
spinocerebellar atrophy
HP:0007263.def: Atrophy affecting the cerebellum and the spinocerebellar tracts of the spinal cord.

name: cerebral dysmyelination
cerebral dysmyelination
HP:0007266.def: Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths of the white matter of the brain.

name: chronic axonal neuropathy
chronic axonal neuropathy
HP:0007267.def: An abnormality characterized by chronic impairment of the normal functioning of the axons.

name: spinal muscular atrophy
spinal muscular atrophy
HP:0007269.def: Muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

name: atypical absence seizure
atypical absence seizure
HP:0007270.def: An atypical absence seizure is a type of generalised non-motor (absence) seizure characterised by interruption of ongoing activities and reduced responsiveness. In comparison to a typical absence seizure, changes in tone may be more pronounced, onset and/or cessation may be less abrupt, and the duration of the ictus and post-ictal recovery may be longer. Although not always available, an EEG often demonstrates slow (<3 Hz), irregular, generalized spike-wave activity.

name: recurrent bacterial meningitis
recurrent bacterial meningitis
HP:0007274.def: An increased susceptibility to bacterial meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of bacterial meningitis.

name: paucity of anterior horn motor neurons
paucity of anterior horn motor neuron
developmental stagnation
developmental stagnation
HP:0007281.def: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills.

name: facial palsy secondary to cranial hyperostosis
facial palsy secondary to cranial hyperostosis
HP:0007285.def: Paralysis of the facial nerves on the basis of overgrowth of the cranial bones causing impingement upon the seventh cranial nerve.
synonym: facial palsy caused by enlargement of cranial bones
facial palsy cause by enlargement of cranial bone
facial palsy caused by excessive growth of facial bones
facial palsy cause by excessive growth of facial bone
facial palsy caused by overgrowth of cranial bones
facial palsy cause by overgrowth of cranial bone
facial palsy secondary to hypertrophy of cranial bones
facial palsy secondary to hypertrophy of cranial bone

name: horizontal jerk nystagmus
horizontal jerk nystagmus
HP:0007286.def: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.

name: limb fasciculations
limb fasciculation
HP:0007289.def: Fasciculations affecting the musculature of the arms and legs.

name: posterior fossa cyst
posterior fossa cyst
HP:0007291.def: A discrete posterior fossa cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collection that does not communicate directly with the fourth ventricle.

name: oromotor apraxia
oromotor apraxia
HP:0007301.def: Oral-motor apraxia is the inability to volitionally sequence oral movements of the speech structure for nonspeech tasks in the absence of neuromuscular deficits such as paralysis or muscle weakness. Oral-motor apraxia is diagnosed when, despite intact sensory motor function an individual is unable to use these effector systems under voluntary control.

name: bipolar affective disorder
bipolar affective disorder
HP:0007302.def: Bipolar disorder is an illness of mood characterized by alternating episodes of elevated and depressed moods, which are interspersed with euthymic periods.

name: cns demyelination
cns demyelination
HP:0007305.def: A loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

name: deep white matter hypodensities
deep white matter hypodensities
HP:0007321.def: Multiple areas of darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the deep cerebral white matter.

name: generalized dystonia
generalize dystonia
HP:0007325.def: A type of dystonia that affects all or most of the body.

name: impaired pain sensation
impaired pain sensation
HP:0007328.def: Reduced ability to perceive painful stimuli.

name: focal hemifacial clonic seizure
focal hemifacial clonic seizure
HP:0007332.def: Focal seizure characterized at onset by clonic movements affecting half of the face.

name: hypoplasia of the frontal lobes
hypoplasia of the frontal lobe
HP:0007333.def: Underdevelopment of the frontal lobe of the cerebrum.

name: bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
HP:0007334.def: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset is a focal-onset seizure which progresses into a bilateral tonic-clonic phase.
synonym: focal to bilateral tonic - clonic seizure
focal to bilateral tonic - clonic seizure
generalised tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
generalise tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
generalised tonic - clonic seizure with partial onset
generalise tonic - clonic seizure with partial onset
generalised tonic - clonic seizures with focal onset
generalise tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
generalized tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
generalize tonic - clonic seizure with focal onset
