HP:0010530.def: Palatal tremor (PT) is an involuntary, rhythmic and oscillatory movement of the soft palate. PT is a rare type of tremor involving the soft palate. It can be unilateral or bilateral.

name: spinal myoclonus
spinal myoclonus
HP:0010531.def: Spinal myoclonus is generally due to a tumor, infection, injury, or degenerative process of the spinal cord, and is characterized by involuntary rhythmic muscle contractions, usually at a rate of more than one per second. Myoclonus occurs synchronously in several muscles and can be increased in severity and frequency by fatigue or stress, but is usually unaffected by sensory stimuli. Spinal myoclonus ceases during sleep or anesthesia.

name: spasmus nutans
spasmus nutans
HP:0010533.def: The combination of pendular nystagmus, head nodding, and torticollis.

name: transient global amnesia
transient global amnesia
HP:0010534.def: A paroxysmal, transient loss of memory function with preservation of immediate recall and remote memory but with a severe impairment of memory for recent events and ability to retain new information.

name: sleep apnea
sleep apnea
HP:0010535.def: An intermittent cessation of airflow at the mouth and nose during sleep is known as sleep apnea. Apneas that last at least 10 seconds are considered significant, but individuals with sleep apnea may experience apneas lasting from 20 seconds up to 2 or 3 minutes. Patients may have up to 15 events per hour of sleep.

name: central sleep apnea
central sleep apnea
HP:0010536.def: Sleep apnea results from a temporary loss of the central drive to the muscles responsible for breathing.

name: wide cranial sutures
wide cranial suture
HP:0010537.def: An abnormally increased width of the cranial sutures for age-related norms (generally resulting from delayed closure).

name: thin calvarium
thin calvarium
HP:0010539.def: The presence of an abnormally thin calvarium.

name: advanced pneumatization of cranial sinuses
advanced pneumatization of cranial sinus
HP:0010540.def: A degree of pneumatization that is increased compared to age-related norms.

name: cutis gyrata of scalp
cutis gyrata of scalp
HP:0010541.def: The presence of convoluted folds and furrows formed from thickened skin of the scalp, resembling cerebriform pattern. The scalp has convoluted and elevated folds, 1 to 2 cm in thickness. The convolutions generally cannot be flattened by traction.
synonym: furrows in thickened skin on top of scalp
furrow in thickened skin on top of scalp
thickened folds on top of scalp
thicken fold on top of scalp

name: vestibular nystagmus
vestibular nystagmus
HP:0010542.def: Nystagmus due to disturbance of the vestibular system; eye movements are rhythmic, with slow and fast components.

name: opsoclonus
opsoclonus
HP:0010543.def: Bursts of large-amplitude multidirectional saccades without intersaccadic interval

name: vertical nystagmus
vertical nystagmus
HP:0010544.def: Vertical nystagmus may present with either up-beating or down-beating eye movements or both. When present in the straight-ahead position of gaze it is referred to as upbeat nystagmus or downbeat nystagmus.

name: downbeat nystagmus
downbeat nystagmus
HP:0010545.def: Downbeat nystagmus is a type of fixation nystagmus with the fast phase beating in a downward direction. It generally increases when looking to the side and down and when lying prone.

name: muscle fibrillation
muscle fibrillation
HP:0010546.def: Fine, rapid twitching of individual muscle fibers with little or no movement of the muscle as a whole. If a motor neuron or its axon is destroyed, the muscle fibers it innervates undergo denervation atrophy. This leads to hypersensitivity of individual muscle fibers to acetyl choline so that they may contract spontaneously. Isolated activity of individual muscle fibers is generally so fine it cannot be seen through the intact skin, although it can be recorded as a short-duration spike in the EMG.

name: muscle flaccidity
muscle flaccidity
HP:0010547.def: A type of paralysis in which a muscle becomes soft and yields to passive stretching, which results from loss of all or practically all peripheral motor nerves that innervated the muscle. Muscle tone is reduced and the affected muscles undergo extreme atrophy within months of the loss of innervation.

name: percussion myotonia
percussion myotonia
HP:0010548.def: A localized myotonic contraction in a muscle in reaction to percussion (tapping with the examiner's finger, a rubber percussion hammer, or a similar object).
synonym: transient swelling of muscle induced by percussion
transient swelling of muscle induce by percussion

name: weakness due to upper motor neuron dysfunction
weakness due to upper motor neuron dysfunction
HP:0010549.def: Paralysis of voluntary muscles means loss of contraction due to interruption of one or more motor pathways from the brain to the muscle fibers. Although the word paralysis is often used interchangeably to mean either complete or partial loss of muscle strength, it is preferable to use paralysis or plegia for complete or severe loss of muscle strength, and paresis for partial or slight loss. Paralysis due to lesions of the principle motor tracts is related to a lesion in the corticospinal, corticobulbar or brainstem descending (subcorticospinal) neurons.
synonym: paralysis due to lesions of the principle motor tracts
paralysis due to lesion of the principle motor tract

name: paraplegia
paraplegia
HP:0010550.def: Severe or complete weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities.

name: paraplegia / paraparesis
paraplegia / paraparesis
HP:0010551.def: Weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities. Paraplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas paraparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.

name: oculogyric crisis
oculogyric crisis
HP:0010553.def: An acute dystonic reaction with blepharospasm, periorbital twitches, and protracted fixed staring episodes. There may be a maximal upward deviation of the eyes in the sustained fashion. Oculogyric crisis can be triggered by a number of factors including neuroleptic medications.

name: cutaneous finger syndactyly
cutaneous finger syndactyly
HP:0010554.def: A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints, or a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two fingers that lies significantly distal to the flexion crease that overlies the metacarpophalangeal joint of the adjacent fingers.

name: overlapping fingers
overlap finger
HP:0010557.def: A finger resting on the dorsal surface of an adjacent digit when the hand is at rest.

name: abnormality of the clivus
abnormality of the clivus
HP:0010558.def: An abnormality of the clivus, which is the inclined bony region of the posterior cranial fossa located between the sella turcica and the foramen magnum.

name: vertical clivus
vertical clivus
HP:0010559.def: An abnormal vertical orientation of the clivus (which normally forms a kind of slope from the sella turcica down to the region of the foramen magnum).

name: undulate clavicles
undulate clavicle
HP:0010560.def: An abnormally wavy surface or edge of the clavicles.

name: undulate ribs
undulate rib
HP:0010561.def: An abnormally wavy surface or edge of the ribs.

name: bifid epiglottis
bifid epiglottis
HP:0010564.def: A midline anterior-posterior cleft of the epiglottis that involves at least two-thirds of the epiglottic leaf. It is a useful feature for clinical diagnosis because it appears to be very rare in syndromes other than Pallister-Hall-Syndrome and is also rare as an isolated malformation.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the epiglottis
aplasia / hypoplasia of the epiglottis
HP:0010565.def: This term applies if the Epiglottis is absent or hypoplastic.

name: hamartoma
hamartoma
HP:0010566.def: A disordered proliferation of mature tissues that is native to the site of origin, e.g., exostoses, nevi and soft tissue hamartomas. Although most hamartomas are benign, some histologic subtypes, e.g., neuromuscular hamartoma, may proliferate aggressively such as mesenchymal cystic hamartoma, Sclerosing epithelial hamartoma, Sclerosing metanephric hamartoma.

name: y - shaped metatarsals
y - shape metatarsal
HP:0010567.def: Y-shaped metatarsals are the result of a partial fusion of two metatarsal bones, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Y-shaped metatarsals may be seen in combination with polydactyly.
synonym: y - shaped long bone of foot
y - shape long bone of foot

name: hamartoma of the eye
hamartoma of the eye
HP:0010568.def: A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) which can originate from any tissue of the eye.

name: elevated circulating 7 - dehydrocholesterol concentration
elevate circulate 7 - dehydrocholesterol concentration
HP:0010569.def: Concentration of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: elevated levels of cholesta - 5,7 - dien - 3beta - ol
elevated level of cholesta - 5,7 - dien - 3beta - ol

name: low maternal circulating alpha - fetoprotein concentration
low maternal circulating alpha - fetoprotein concentration
HP:0010570.def: An abnormally low concentration of serum alpha-fetoprotein as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

name: elevated circulating phytanic acid concentration
elevate circulate phytanic acid concentration
HP:0010571.def: An abnormal elevation of phytanic acid.

name: abnormality of the epiphysis of the femoral head
abnormality of the epiphysis of the femoral head
HP:0010574.def: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
synonym: abnormality of the end part of the innermost thighbone
abnormality of the end part of the innermost thighbone
abnormality of the proximal femoral epiphysis
abnormality of the proximal femoral epiphysis

name: dysplasia of the femoral head
dysplasia of the femoral head
HP:0010575.def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the femoral head.

name: intracranial cystic lesion
intracranial cystic lesion
HP:0010576.def: A cystic lesion originating within the brain.

name: bracket epiphyses
bracket epiphysis
synonym: bracket shaped end part of long bone
bracket shape end part of long bone

name: cone - shaped epiphysis
cone - shaped epiphysis
HP:0010579.def: Cone-shaped epiphyses (also known as coned epiphyses) are epiphyses that invaginate into cupped metaphyses. That is, the epiphysis has a cone-shaped distal extension resulting from increased growth of the central portion of the epiphysis relative to its periphery.
synonym: cone - shaped end part of bone
cone - shaped end part of bone

name: irregular epiphyses
irregular epiphysis
HP:0010582.def: An alteration of the normally smooth contour of the epiphysis leading to an irregular appearance.
synonym: irregular end part of long bone
irregular end part of long bone

name: ivory epiphyses
ivory epiphysis
HP:0010583.def: Sclerosis of the epiphyses, leading to an increased degree of radiopacity (white or ivory appearance) in X-rays.
synonym: increased bone density in end part of bone
increase bone density in end part of bone

name: small epiphyses
small epiphysis
HP:0010585.def: Reduction in the size or volume of epiphyses.

name: premature epimetaphyseal fusion
premature epimetaphyseal fusion
HP:0010588.def: Stop of growth at the epiphyseal plate the hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at each end of a long bone, at an earlier than normal age, resulting in growth arrest and shortening of the involved bone.

name: abnormality of the distal femoral epiphysis
abnormality of the distal femoral epiphysis
HP:0010590.def: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the femur.
synonym: abnormality of the end part of the outermost thighbone
abnormality of the end part of the outermost thighbone

name: abnormality of the proximal tibial epiphysis
abnormality of the proximal tibial epiphysis
HP:0010591.def: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia.
synonym: abnormality of the end part of innermost shankbone
abnormality of the end part of innermost shankbone
abnormality of the end part of innermost shinbone
abnormality of the end part of innermost shinbone

name: abnormality of the distal tibial epiphysis
abnormality of the distal tibial epiphysis
synonym: abnormality of the end part of outermost shankbone
abnormality of the end part of outermost shankbone
abnormality of the end part of outermost shinbone
abnormality of the end part of outermost shinbone

name: abnormal fibular epiphysis morphology
abnormal fibular epiphysis morphology
synonym: abnormality of the end part of the calf bone
abnormality of the end part of the calf bone

name: abnormality of the proximal fibular epiphysis
abnormality of the proximal fibular epiphysis
HP:0010594.def: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the fibula.
synonym: abnormality of the innermost end part of calf bone
abnormality of the innermost end part of calf bone

name: abnormality of the distal fibular epiphysis
abnormality of the distal fibular epiphysis
HP:0010595.def: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the fibula.
synonym: abnormality of the outermost end part of calf bone
abnormality of the outermost end part of calf bone

name: abnormality of the proximal radial epiphysis
abnormality of the proximal radial epiphysis
HP:0010596.def: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.

name: abnormality of the distal radial epiphysis
abnormality of the distal radial epiphysis
HP:0010597.def: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the radius.

name: abnormality of the proximal humeral epiphysis
abnormality of the proximal humeral epiphysis
HP:0010598.def: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the humerus.
synonym: abnormality of the end part of the innermost long bone in upper arm
abnormality of the end part of the innermost long bone in upper arm

name: abnormality of the distal humeral epiphysis
abnormality of the distal humeral epiphysis
HP:0010599.def: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the humerus.
synonym: abnormality of the end part of the outermost long bone in upper arm
abnormality of the end part of the outermost long bone in upper arm

name: abnormal distal ulnar epiphysis morphology
abnormal distal ulnar epiphysis morphology
HP:0010600.def: Any abnormality of the distal epiphysis of the ulna.
synonym: abnormality of the distal ulnar epiphysis
abnormality of the distal ulnar epiphysis

name: abnormal proximal ulnar epiphysis morphology
abnormal proximal ulnar epiphysis morphology
HP:0010601.def: Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the ulna.
synonym: abnormality of the proximal ulnar epiphysis
abnormality of the proximal ulnar epiphysis

name: type 2 muscle fiber predominance
type 2 muscle fiber predominance
HP:0010602.def: An abnormal predominance of type II muscle fibers (in general, this feature can only be observed on muscle biopsy).

name: odontogenic keratocysts of the jaw
odontogenic keratocysts of the jaw
HP:0010603.def: A benign uni- or multicystic, intraosseous tumor of odontogenic origin, with a characteristic lining of parakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium and potential for aggressive, infiltrative behaviour.

name: chalazion
chalazion
HP:0010605.def: A chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland. A chalazion or meibomian cyst appears as a painless tuberous swelling in the upper lid without loss of eyelashes.

name: hordeolum
hordeolum
HP:0010606.def: An acute purulent infection of the sebaceous glands of Zeis at the base of the eyelashes, of the apocrine sweat glands of Moll or the meibomian sebacious glands often caused by staphylococcus infections. Hordeola can either occur as Hordeola externa affecting the sebaceous glands of Zeis or the apocrine sweat glands of Moll or as Hordeola interna affecting the meibomian sebacious glands. In contrast to chalazia, hordeola are extremely painful and can cause extreme local swelling.

name: hordeolum externum
hordeolum externum
HP:0010607.def: Hordeola externa are acute purulent infections affecting the sebaceous glands of Zeis or the apocrine sweat glands of Moll, often caused by staphylococcus infections. In contrast to chalazia, hordeola are extremely painfull and can cause extreme local swelling.

name: hordeolum internum
hordeolum internum
HP:0010608.def: Hordeola interna are acute purulent infections affecting the meibomian sebacious glands, often caused by staphylococcus infections. In contrast to chalazia (chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland), hordeola are extremely painfull and can cause extreme local swelling.

name: skin tags
skin tag
HP:0010609.def: Cutaneous skin tags also known as acrochorda or fibroepithelial polyps are small benign tumors that may either form secondarily over time primarily in areas where the skin forms creases, such as the neck, armpit or groin or may also be present at birth, in which case they usually occur in the periauricular region.

name: plantar pits
plantar pit
HP:0010612.def: The presence of multiple pits (small, pinpoint-large indentations on the surface of the skin) located on the skin of sole of foot.

name: fibroma
fibroma
HP:0010614.def: Benign tumors that are composed of fibrous or connective tissue. They can grow in all organs, arising from mesenchyme tissue. The term \"fibroblastic\

name: angiofibromas
angiofibromas
HP:0010615.def: Angiofibroma consist of many often dilated vessels.

name: lung fibroma
lung fibroma
HP:0010616.def: The presence of a lung fibroma, a benign neoplasm that can present as a mass causing airway obstruction, cough, and hemoptysis, or present without symptoms as a solitary pulmonary nodule.

name: ovarian fibroma
ovarian fibroma
HP:0010618.def: The presence of a fibroma of the ovary.

name: fibroadenoma of the breast
fibroadenoma of the breast
HP:0010619.def: A benign biphasic tumor of the breast with epithelial and stromal components.

name: malar prominence
malar prominence
HP:0010620.def: Prominence of the malar process of the maxilla and infraorbital area appreciated in profile and from in front of the face.

name: cutaneous syndactyly of toes
cutaneous syndactyly of toe
HP:0010621.def: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between adjacent foot digits that involves at least half of the proximodistal length of one of the two involved digits; or, a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits of the foot that does not meet the prior objective criteria.

name: neoplasm of the skeletal system
neoplasm of the skeletal system
HP:0010622.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the skeleton.

name: aplastic / hypoplastic toenail
aplastic / hypoplastic toenail
HP:0010624.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the toenail.

name: anterior pituitary dysgenesis
anterior pituitary dysgenesis
HP:0010625.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis.

name: anterior pituitary agenesis
anterior pituitary agenesis
HP:0010626.def: Absence of the anterior pituitary gland resulting from a developmental defect.

name: anterior pituitary hypoplasia
anterior pituitary hypoplasia
HP:0010627.def: Underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland.

name: facial palsy
facial palsy
HP:0010628.def: Facial nerve palsy is a dysfunction of cranial nerve VII (the facial nerve) that results in inability to control facial muscles on the affected side with weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure. This can either be present in unilateral or bilateral form.
synonym: facial muscle weakness of muscles innervated by cn vii
facial muscle weakness of muscle innervate by cn vii

name: abnormal morphology of the cortex of the humerus
abnormal morphology of the cortex of the humerus
HP:0010629.def: Any abnormality affecting the cortex of the humerus.

name: abnormal metatarsal epiphysis morphology
abnormal metatarsal epiphysis morphology
HP:0010630.def: Any abnormality of a metatarsal bone epiphysis.
synonym: abnormality of end part of long bone of foot
abnormality of end part of long bone of foot
abnormality of the epiphyses of the metatarsals
abnormality of the epiphysis of the metatarsal

name: abnormality of the epiphyses of the feet
abnormality of the epiphysis of the foot
HP:0010631.def: Any abnormality of the epiphyses of the feet.
synonym: abnormality of the end part of the foot bone
abnormality of the end part of the foot bone

name: total anosmia
total anosmia
HP:0010632.def: Inability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.

name: partial anosmia
partial anosmia
HP:0010633.def: Inability to perceive certain odorants (implies that the sense of smell is maintained for other classes of odorants).

name: total hyposmia
total hyposmia
HP:0010634.def: Reduced ability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.

name: partial hyposmia
partial hyposmia
HP:0010635.def: Reduced ability to perceive certain odorants (implies that the sense of smell is maintained for other classes of odorants).

name: schizencephaly
schizencephaly
HP:0010636.def: The presence of a cleft in the cerebral cortex unilaterally or bilaterally, usually located in the frontal area.

name: conjunctival amyloidosis
conjunctival amyloidosis
HP:0010637.def: A form of amyloidosis that affects the conjunctiva.

name: elevated alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
elevate alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
HP:0010638.def: An abnormally increased level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

name: elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
elevate alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
HP:0010639.def: An abnormally increased level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
synonym: elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
elevate alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
increased serum bone - specific alkaline phosphatase
increase serum bone - specific alkaline phosphatase

name: abnormality of the nasal cavity
abnormality of the nasal cavity
HP:0010640.def: Abnormality of the nasal cavity (the cavity includes and starts at the nares and reaches all the way through to the and includes the choanae, the posterior nasal apertures).

name: abnormality of the midnasal cavity
abnormality of the midnasal cavity
HP:0010641.def: Abnormality of the midnasal cavity which includes the cavity between the nares and the choanae.

name: midnasal atresia
midnasal atresia
HP:0010643.def: Absence or abnormal closure of the midnasal cavity.

name: midnasal stenosis
midnasal stenosis
HP:0010644.def: Abnormal narrowing (stenosis) of the midnasal cavity, i.e., of the middle nasal meatus, which in neonates can cause respiratory distress.

name: aplasia of the distal phalanges of the toes
aplasia of the distal phalanx of the toe
HP:0010645.def: Absence of the distal phalanges of the toes.
synonym: absent outermost bone of the toes
absent outermost bone of the toe

name: cervical spine instability
cervical spine instability
HP:0010646.def: An abnormal lack of stability of the cervical spine.

name: abnormal elasticity of skin
abnormal elasticity of skin
HP:0010647.def: Any abnormal increase or reduction in skin elasticity.

name: dermal translucency
dermal translucency
HP:0010648.def: An abnormally increased ability of the skin to permit light to pass through (translucency) such that subcutaneous structures such as veins display an increased degree of visibility.

name: flat nasal alae
flat nasal ala
HP:0010649.def: An abnormal degree of flatness of the Ala of nose, which can be defined as a reduced nasal elevation index (lateral depth of the nose from the tip of the nose to the insertion of the nasal ala in the cheek x 100 divided by the side-to-side breadth of the nasal alae).

name: hypoplasia of the premaxilla
hypoplasia of the premaxilla
HP:0010650.def: An abnormality of the premaxilla (the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla) causing it to appear relatively small in size compared to the other parts of the maxilla or other facial structures.
synonym: decreased size of the primary palate bone
decreased size of the primary palate bone
hypoplasia of the primary palate bone
hypoplasia of the primary palate bone
underdevelopment of the primary palate bone
underdevelopment of the primary palate bone

name: abnormal meningeal morphology
abnormal meningeal morphology
HP:0010651.def: An abnormality of the Meninges, including any abnormality of the Dura mater, the Arachnoid mater, and the Pia mater.

name: abnormal dura mater morphology
abnormal dura mater morphology
HP:0010652.def: An abnormality of the Dura mater.

name: abnormality of the falx cerebri
abnormality of the falx cerebri
HP:0010653.def: An abnormality of the Falx cerebri.

name: aplasia of the falx cerebri
aplasia of the falx cerebri
HP:0010654.def: A developmental defect characterized by aplasia of the Falx cerebri.

name: epiphyseal stippling
epiphyseal stipple
HP:0010655.def: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more epiphyses.
synonym: speckled calcifications in end part of bone
speckled calcification in end part of bone

name: abnormal epiphyseal ossification
abnormal epiphyseal ossification
HP:0010656.def: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of an epiphysis.
synonym: abnormal maturation of the end part of a bone
abnormal maturation of the end part of a bone
abnormality of the mineralisation or ossification of the epiphyses
abnormality of the mineralisation or ossification of the epiphysis

name: patchy reduction of bone mineral density
patchy reduction of bone mineral density
HP:0010657.def: Patchy (irregular) reduction in bone density. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.

name: patchy changes of bone mineral density
patchy change of bone mineral density
HP:0010658.def: Patchy (irregular) changes in bone mineral density. These changes can either be patchy reduction or increase of mineral density as seen on x-rays. Depending on the pathomechanism and the underlying disease, these changes can either appear solely as reduction or increase or as a combination of both (patches of bone showing an increased density while others are affected by reduction of mineral density).

name: patchy variation in bone mineral density
patchy variation in bone mineral density
HP:0010659.def: Patchy (irregular) changes in bone mineral density with patches of bone showing an increased density side to side with patches that are affected by reduction of mineral density. This is sometimes referred to as a moth-eaten appearance on x-rays.
synonym: patchy increased and decreased bone mineral density
patchy increase and decrease bone mineral density

name: abnormal hand bone ossification
abnormal hand bone ossification
HP:0010660.def: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the skeleton of hand.
synonym: abnormal maturation of the hand bones
abnormal maturation of the hand bone
abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bones of the hand
abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bone of the hand

name: absence of the third cerebral ventricle
absence of the third cerebral ventricle
HP:0010661.def: A developmental defect characterized by the absence of the third ventricle.

name: abnormality of the diencephalon
abnormality of the diencephalon
HP:0010662.def: An abnormality of the Diencephalon, which together with the cerebrum (telencephalon) makes up the forebrain.

name: fusion of the left and right thalami
fusion of the left and right thalamus
HP:0010664.def: A developmental defect characterized by fusion of the left and right halves of the thalamus.

name: bilateral coxa valga
bilateral coxa valga
HP:0010665.def: The presence of bilateral coxa valga.

name: hypoplasia of the anterior nasal spine
hypoplasia of the anterior nasal spine
HP:0010666.def: Underdevelopment of the anterior nasal spine of maxilla.
synonym: decreased length of anterior nasal spine
decreased length of anterior nasal spine
decreased projection of anterior nasal spine
decreased projection of anterior nasal spine
decreased size of anterior nasal spine
decreased size of anterior nasal spine

name: aplasia of the maxilla
aplasia of the maxilla
HP:0010667.def: A congenital defect characterized by absence of the Maxilla.
synonym: aplasia of the upper jaw bones
aplasia of the upper jaw bone
failure of development of upper jaw bones
failure of development of upper jaw bone

name: abnormal zygomatic bone morphology
abnormal zygomatic bone morphology
HP:0010668.def: An abnormality of the zygomatic bone.

name: hypoplasia of the zygomatic bone
hypoplasia of the zygomatic bone
HP:0010669.def: Underdevelopment of the zygomatic bone. That is, a reduction in size of the zygomatic bone, including the zygomatic process of the temporal bone of the skull, which forms part of the zygomatic arch.

name: abnormality of the third metatarsal bone
abnormality of the third metatarsal bone
HP:0010672.def: An abnormality of the third metatarsal bone.
synonym: abnormality of the 3rd long bone of foot
abnormality of the 3rd long bone of foot

name: abnormal curvature of the vertebral column
abnormal curvature of the vertebral column
HP:0010674.def: The presence of an abnormal curvature of the vertebral column.
synonym: abnormality of the curvature of the vertebral column
abnormality of the curvature of the vertebral column

name: abnormal foot bone ossification
abnormal foot bone ossification
HP:0010675.def: An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of any bone of the skeleton of foot.
synonym: abnormal ossification involving bones of the feet
abnormal ossification involve bone of the foot
abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bones of the feet
abnormality of the mineralisation and ossification of bone of the foot

name: enuresis diurna
enuresis diurna
HP:0010678.def: Enuresis occurring during waking hours of the day.

name: elevated tissue non - specific alkaline phosphatase
elevate tissue non - specific alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010679.def: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
synonym: elevated alkaline phosphatase , liver / bone / kidney
elevate alkaline phosphatase , liver / bone / kidney

name: elevated alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
elevate alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
HP:0010680.def: An abnormally increased level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

name: elevated intestinal alkaline phosphatase
elevate intestinal alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010681.def: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.

name: elevated placental alkaline phosphatase
elevate placental alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010682.def: An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.

name: low tissue non - specific alkaline phosphatase
low tissue non - specific alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010683.def: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.

name: low alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
low alkaline phosphatase of bone origin
HP:0010684.def: An abnormally reduced level of bone isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

name: low alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
low alkaline phosphatase of renal origin
HP:0010685.def: An abnormally reduced level of kidney isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

name: low alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
low alkaline phosphatase of hepatic origin
HP:0010686.def: An abnormally reduced level of liver isoforms of alkaline phosphatase in the blood.

name: low intestinal alkaline phosphatase
low intestinal alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010687.def: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, intestinal type in the blood.

name: low placental alkaline phosphatase
low placental alkaline phosphatase
HP:0010688.def: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase, placental type in the blood.

name: mirror image polydactyly
mirror image polydactyly
HP:0010689.def: A hand or foot with more than five digits that has a recognizable A/P axis of symmetry. The axis can lie within a normally formed or partially duplicated digit resembling a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe, or hallux. Alternatively, the axis can be in an interdigital space with a flanking pair of digits that resemble a middle finger, index finger, thumb, toe or hallux. The most lateral digits on each side of the hand/foot typically resemble fifth fingers/toes.

name: mirror image hand polydactyly
mirror image hand polydactyly
HP:0010690.def: Mirror image duplication of digits affecting the hands only.

name: mirror image foot polydactyly
mirror image foot polydactyly
HP:0010691.def: Mirror image duplication of digits affecting the feet.

name: 2 - 5 finger syndactyly
2 - 5 finger syndactyly
HP:0010692.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers two to five.
synonym: webbed index , middle and little finger
webbed index , middle and little finger
webbed index , middle and pinkie finger
webbed index , middle and pinkie finger
webbed index , middle and pinky finger
webbed index , middle and pinky finger

name: pulverulent cataract
pulverulent cataract
HP:0010693.def: A kind of congenital cataract that is characterized by a hollow sphere of punctate opacities involving the fetal nucleus and that usually occurs bilaterally.

name: lamellar pulverulent cataract
lamellar pulverulent cataract
HP:0010694.def: A Lamellar cataract with a pulverulent (punctate, \"dust-like\

name: sutural cataract
sutural cataract
HP:0010695.def: A type of congenital cataract in which the opacity follows the anterior or posterior Y suture.

name: polar cataract
polar cataract
HP:0010696.def: A type of Congenital cataract in which the opacities occupy the subcapsular cortex at the anterior or posterior pole of the lens.

name: anterior pyramidal cataract
anterior pyramidal cataract
HP:0010697.def: A type of anterior polar cataract which projects as a conical opacity into the anterior chamber.

name: nuclear pulverulent cataract
nuclear pulverulent cataract
HP:0010698.def: A type of nuclear cataract involving congenital dust-like (pulverulent) opacity of the embryonal and fetal nucleus.

name: triangular nuclear cataract
triangular nuclear cataract
HP:0010699.def: A nuclear cataract with a triangular form.

name: abnormal immunoglobulin level
abnormal immunoglobulin level
HP:0010701.def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of immunoglobulins in blood.

name: increased circulating antibody level
increase circulate antibody level
HP:0010702.def: An increased level of gamma globulin (immunoglobulin) in the blood.

name: 1 - 2 finger syndactyly
1 - 2 finger syndactyly
HP:0010704.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one and two.

name: 4 - 5 finger syndactyly
4 - 5 finger syndactyly
HP:0010705.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers four and five.

name: 1 - 3 finger syndactyly
1 - 3 finger syndactyly
HP:0010706.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one to three.

name: 1 - 4 finger syndactyly
1 - 4 finger syndactyly
HP:0010707.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one to four.

name: 1 - 5 finger syndactyly
1 - 5 finger syndactyly
HP:0010708.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers one to five (complete syndactyly of all fingers of the hand).

name: 2 - 4 finger syndactyly
2 - 4 finger syndactyly
HP:0010709.def: Syndactyly with fusion of the fingers two to four.
synonym: syndactyly of second to fourth fingers
syndactyly of second to fourth finger

name: 3 - 5 finger syndactyly
3 - 5 finger syndactyly
HP:0010710.def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers three to five.
synonym: webbed third , fourth and fifth toes
webbed third , fourth and fifth toe

name: 1 - 2 toe syndactyly
1 - 2 toe syndactyly
HP:0010711.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one and two.

name: 1 - 4 toe syndactyly
1 - 4 toe syndactyly
HP:0010712.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to four.

name: 1 - 5 toe syndactyly
1 - 5 toe syndactyly
HP:0010713.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to five (complete syndactyly of all toes of the foot).

name: 2 - 4 toe syndactyly
2 - 4 toe syndactyly
HP:0010714.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to four.

name: 2 - 5 toe syndactyly
2 - 5 toe syndactyly
HP:0010715.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to five.

name: 3 - 5 toe syndactyly
3 - 5 toe syndactyly
HP:0010716.def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes three to five.

name: osseous syndactyly of toes
osseous syndactyly of toe
HP:0010717.def: Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts and including fusion of individual bones of the toes. Bony fusions are referred to as \"bony\

name: abnormality of hair texture
abnormality of hair texture
HP:0010719.def: An abnormality of the texture of the hair.

name: abnormal hair pattern
abnormal hair pattern
HP:0010720.def: An abnormality of the distribution of hair growth.

name: abnormal hair whorl
abnormal hair whorl
HP:0010721.def: An abnormal hair whorl (that is, a patch of hair growing in the opposite direction of the rest of the hair).

name: asymmetry of the ears
asymmetry of the ear
HP:0010722.def: An asymmetriy, i.e., difference in size, shape or position between the left and right ear.

name: advanced pneumatization of the mastoid process
advanced pneumatization of the mastoid process
HP:0010724.def: An abnormally advanced degree of pneumatization (i.e., formation of air cells) in the mastoid process with respect to age-dependent norms.

name: prominent corneal nerve fibers
prominent corneal nerve fiber
HP:0010726.def: Abnormal prominence of the corneal nerve fibers.

name: spontaneous rupture of the globe
spontaneous rupture of the globe
HP:0010727.def: Rupture of the eyeball not due to trauma.

name: aplasia of the retina
aplasia of the retina
HP:0010728.def: A developmental defect characterized by absence of the retina.

name: cherry red spot of the macula
cherry red spot of the macula
HP:0010729.def: Pallor of the perifoveal macula of the retina with appearance of a small circular reddish choroid shape as seen through the fovea centralis due to relative transparancy of the macula.

name: double eyebrow
double eyebrow
HP:0010730.def: This may present as a partial or complete duplication of the eyebrows.

name: extension of eyebrows towards upper eyelid
extension of eyebrow towards upper eyelid
HP:0010731.def: The eyebrows extend towards - or even all the way down to - the margin of the upper eyelid.
synonym: extension of eyebrows towards upper eyelid
extension of eyebrow towards upper eyelid

name: nodular changes affecting the eyelids
nodular change affect the eyelid
HP:0010732.def: Nodular changes affecting the eyelids may have many different causes such as cystic lesions (chalaziae, hordeolae), lipogranulomas, melanomas, infectious diseases (Molluscum contagiosum) and many more.

name: naevus flammeus of the eyelid
naevus flammeus of the eyelid
HP:0010733.def: Naevus flammeus localised in the skin of the eyelid.

name: fibrous dysplasia of the bones
fibrous dysplasia of the bone
HP:0010734.def: Tumor-like growths that consist of replacement of the medullary bone with fibrous tissue, causing the expansion and weakening of the areas of bone involved. Especially when involving the skull or facial bones, the lesions can cause externally visible deformities. The skull is often, but not necessarily, affected, and any other bone or bones may be involved. Fibrous dysplasia can either effect isolated bones (Monostotic fibrous dysplasia) or also generalized all bones of the body (Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia).

name: polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
HP:0010735.def: Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in many bones throughout of the body. Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia is a cardinal feature of McCune-Albright syndrome.

name: monostotic fibrous dysplasia
monostotic fibrous dysplasia
HP:0010736.def: Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in only one bone.

name: osteopoikilosis
osteopoikilosis
HP:0010739.def: Osteopoikilosis is a benign, asymptomatic sclerotic dysplasia of the bones. It affects both male and female and may be seen at any age. Radiographically sclerotic circular or ovoid lesions are usually symmetrically distributed in a periarticular location. Lesions can increase or decrease in size and number in serial radiographs or even disappear and do not have increased bone radiotracer uptake.

name: osteopathia striata
osteopathia striata
HP:0010740.def: A lamellar pattern visible on radiographs and mainly localized at the metaphyses of the long tubular bones. Pathologic-anatomical studies revealed that these benign signs on x-rays are the result of a juvenile metaphyseal bone necrosis. Calcifications in the necrotic marrow lead to this lamellar or lattice-like appearance.

name: pedal edema
pedal edema
HP:0010741.def: An abnormal accumulation of excess fluid in the lower extremity resulting in swelling of the feet and extending upward to the lower leg.

name: edema of the upper limbs
edema of the upper limb
HP:0010742.def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin of the arms.

name: short metatarsal
short metatarsal
HP:0010743.def: Diminished length of a metatarsal bone, with resultant proximal displacement of the associated toe.

name: absent metatarsal bone
absent metatarsal bone
HP:0010744.def: A developmental abnormality characterized by the absence (aplasia) of a metatarsal bone.

name: aplasia of the phalanges of the toes
aplasia of the phalanx of the toe
HP:0010745.def: Absence of a digit or of one or more phalanges of a toe.

name: hypoplasia of the phalanges of the toes
hypoplasia of the phalanx of the toe
medial flaring of the eyebrow
medial flaring of the eyebrow
HP:0010747.def: An abnormal distribution of eyebrow hair growth in the medial direction.

name: ectopic lacrimal punctum
ectopic lacrimal punctum
HP:0010748.def: Positioning of a lacrimal punctum other than at the medial margins of the eyelid.
synonym: abnormal position of the lacrimal punctum
abnormal position of the lacrimal punctum

name: blepharochalasis
blepharochalasis
HP:0010749.def: Blepharochalasis is characterized by recurrent, non-painful, nonerythematous episodes of eyelid edema. It has been divided into hypertrophic and atrophic forms. In the hypertrophic form recurrent edema results in orbital fat herniation through a weakened orbital septum. Most patients who have blepharochalasis present in an atrophic condition with atrophy of redundant eyelid skin and superior nasal fat pads.

name: dermatochalasis
dermatochalasis
HP:0010750.def: Loss of elasticity of the upper and lower eyelids causing the skin to sag and bulge.

name: dimple chin
dimple chin
HP:0010751.def: A persistent midline depression of the skin over the fat pad of the chin.

name: cleft mandible
cleft mandible
HP:0010752.def: Midline deficiency of the mandible and some or all overlying tissues.

name: abnormality of the temporomandibular joint
abnormality of the temporomandibular joint
HP:0010754.def: An anomaly of the temporomandibular joint.

name: asymmetry of the maxilla
asymmetry of the maxilla
HP:0010755.def: Asymmetry between the left and right sides of the maxilla.
synonym: asymmetry of right and left side of the maxilla
asymmetry of right and leave side of the maxilla

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the premaxilla
aplasia / hypoplasia of the premaxilla
HP:0010756.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the premaxilla.
synonym: aplasia / hypoplasia of the intermaxillary bone
aplasia / hypoplasia of the intermaxillary bone
aplasia / hypoplasia of the primary palate bone
aplasia / hypoplasia of the primary palate bone

name: aplasia of the premaxilla
aplasia of the premaxilla
HP:0010757.def: Absence of the premaxilla, which is the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla.
synonym: absence of the primary palate bone
absence of the primary palate bone
aplasia of the primary palate bone
aplasia of the primary palate bone
failure of development of the primary palate bone
failure of development of the primary palate bone

name: abnormality of the premaxilla
abnormality of the premaxilla
HP:0010758.def: An abnormality of the premaxilla, the most anterior part of the maxilla that usually bears the central and lateral incisors and includes the anterior nasal spine and inferior aspect of the piriform rim. The premaxilla contains the bone and teeth of the primary palate.
synonym: abnormality of the intermaxillary segment of the maxilla
abnormality of the intermaxillary segment of the maxilla
abnormality of the primary palate bone
abnormality of the primary palate bone

name: prominence of the premaxilla
prominence of the premaxilla
HP:0010759.def: Prominent positioning of the premaxilla in relation to the rest of the maxilla, the facial skeleton, or mandible. Not necessarily caused by an increase in size (hypertrophy of) the premaxilla.
synonym: anterior position of the primary palate bone
anterior position of the primary palate bone
prominence of the primary palate bone
prominence of the primary palate bone

name: absent toe
absent toe
HP:0010760.def: Aplasia of a toe. That is, absence of all phalanges of a non-hallux digit of the foot and the associated soft tissues.

name: chordoma
chordoma
HP:0010762.def: A chordoma is a tumor that arises from embryonic remnants of the notochord along the length of the neuraxis. Chordomas generally occur in the sacrum, intracranially at the clivus, or along the spinal axis.

name: low insertion of columella
low insertion of columella
HP:0010763.def: Insertion of the posterior columella below the nasal base.

name: palmar hyperkeratosis
palmar hyperkeratosis
HP:0010765.def: Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand.

name: ectopic calcification
ectopic calcification
HP:0010766.def: Deposition of calcium salts in a tissue or location in which calcification does not normally occur.

name: sacrococcygeal pilonidal abnormality
sacrococcygeal pilonidal abnormality
HP:0010767.def: The presence of a cyst, fistula, or abscess in the sacrococcygeal region (gluteal crease) characteristically accompanied by hair and skin folds.

name: pilonidal sinus
pilonidal sinus
HP:0010769.def: A sinus in the coccygeal region (the region of the intergluteal cleft). A pilonidal sinus often contains hair and skin debris.

name: pilonidal abscess
pilonidal abscess
HP:0010771.def: A hair-containing cyst or sinus usually in the coccygeal region.

name: anomalous pulmonary venous return
anomalous pulmonary venous return
HP:0010772.def: A developmental defect characterized by abnormal connection of one or more pulmonary veins to the superior or inferior vena cava, the right atrium, or the coronary sinus, resulting in a left-to-right shunt of oxygenated blood.

name: partial anomalous pulmonary venous return
partial anomalous pulmonary venous return
HP:0010773.def: A form of anomalous pulmonary venous return in which not all pulmonary veins drain abnormally. Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return frequently involves one or both of the veins from one lung.

name: cor triatriatum
cor triatriatum
HP:0010774.def: The presence of an additional membrane in the left or right cardiac atrium which results in the subdivision of the affected atrium (and thus in total three atria, whence the name).

name: vascular ring
vascular ring
HP:0010775.def: A developmental defect of the aortic arch system in which the trachea and esophagus are completely encircled by connected segments of the aortic arch and its branches. This occurs if the normal process of regression and persistence of the bilateral embryonic aortic arches fails.

name: tracheobronchmegaly
tracheobronchmegaly
HP:0010776.def: Marked widening of the trachea and major bronchi that may be predispose to chronic respiratory tract infection.

name: bronchomegaly
bronchomegaly
HP:0010777.def: Marked widening of the major bronchi that may be predispose to chronic respiratory tract infection.

name: large pelvis bone
large pelvis bone
HP:0010779.def: The presence of an abnormally large pelvis.

name: hyperacusis
hyperacusis
HP:0010780.def: Over-sensitivity to certain frequency ranges of sound.

name: skin dimple
skin dimple
HP:0010781.def: Skin dimples are cutaneous indentations that are the result of tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) causing an indentation.

name: shoulder dimple
shoulder dimple
HP:0010782.def: A subtype of skin dimples occurring in the shoulder region.

name: erythema
erythema
HP:0010783.def: Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
synonym: redness of skin or mucous membrane
redness of skin or mucous membrane

name: uterine neoplasm
uterine neoplasm
HP:0010784.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the uterus.

name: gonadal neoplasm
gonadal neoplasm
HP:0010785.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of a gonad.

name: urinary tract neoplasm
urinary tract neoplasm
HP:0010786.def: The presence of a neoplasm of the urinary system.

name: genital neoplasm
genital neoplasm
HP:0010787.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the genital system.

name: testicular neoplasm
testicular neoplasm
HP:0010788.def: The presence of a neoplasm of the testis.

name: hypoplasia of the leydig cells
hypoplasia of the leydig cell
HP:0010790.def: Underdevelopment of the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis. These cells produce testosterone.

name: hyperplasia of the leydig cells
hyperplasia of the leydig cell
HP:0010791.def: Hypertrophy or overdevelopment of the interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis. These cells produce testosterone.

name: bifid nail
bifid nail
HP:0010793.def: A digit with two nails, with at least some soft tissue between them.

name: impaired visuospatial constructive cognition
impaired visuospatial constructive cognition
HP:0010794.def: Reduced ability affecting mainly visuospatial cognition which may be tested using pattern construction (for example by Differential Ability Scales, which test a person's strengths and weaknesses across a range of intellectual abilities).

name: hemangioblastoma
hemangioblastoma
HP:0010797.def: A hemangioblastoma is a benign vascular neoplasm that arises almost exclusively in the central nervous system. Hemangioblastomas consist of a tightly packed cluster of small blood vessels forming a mass of up to 1 or 2 cm in diameter.

name: lip freckle
lip freckle
HP:0010798.def: Increased focal pigmentation of the vermilion of the lips.

name: pinealoma
pinealoma
HP:0010799.def: A neoplasm of the pineal gland.

name: absent cupid 's bow
absent cupid 's bow
HP:0010800.def: Lack of paramedian peaks and median notch of the upper lip vermilion.
synonym: failure of development of cupid 's bow
failure of development of cupid 's bow

name: underdeveloped nasolabial fold
underdeveloped nasolabial fold
HP:0010801.def: Reduced bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion or commissure).

name: perioral hyperpigmentation
perioral hyperpigmentation
HP:0010802.def: Increased pigmentation, either focal or generalized, of the skin surrounding the vermilion of the lips.
synonym: darkening of skin around the mouth
darkening of skin around the mouth

name: everted upper lip vermilion
evert upper lip vermilion
HP:0010803.def: Inner aspect of the upper lip vermilion (normally apposing the teeth) visible in a frontal view, i.e., the presence of an everted upper lip.

name: tented upper lip vermilion
tent upper lip vermilion
HP:0010804.def: Triangular appearance of the oral aperture with the apex in the midpoint of the upper vermilion and the lower vermilion forming the base.

name: upturned corners of mouth
upturned corner of mouth
HP:0010805.def: Oral commissures positioned superior to the midline labial fissure.

name: u - shaped upper lip vermilion
u - shape upper lip vermilion
HP:0010806.def: Gentle upward curve of the upper lip vermilion such that the center is placed well superior to the commissures.

name: open bite
open bite
HP:0010807.def: Visible space between the dental arches in occlusion.
synonym: absence of overlap of upper and lower teeth
absence of overlap of upper and low teeth
open bite between upper and lower teeth
open bite between upper and low teeth

name: protruding tongue
protrude tongue
HP:0010808.def: Tongue extending beyond the alveolar ridges or teeth at rest.

name: broad uvula
broad uvula
HP:0010809.def: Increased width of the uvula (subjective finding).

name: abnormal number of hair whorls
abnormal number of hair whorl
HP:0010813.def: More than two clockwise hair whorls.

name: abnormal position of hair whorl
abnormal position of hair whorl
HP:0010814.def: Hair growth from a single point on the scalp in any location other than lateral to the midline and close to the vertex of the skull.

name: nevus sebaceous
nevus sebaceous
HP:0010815.def: A congenital, hairless plaque consisting of overgrown epidermis, sebaceous glands, hair follicles, apocrine glands and connective tissue. They are a variant of epidermal naevi. Sebaceous naevi most often appear on the scalp, but they may also arise on the face, neck or forehead. At birth, a sevaceous nevus typically appears as a solitary, smooth, yellow-orange hairless patch. Sebaceous naevi become more pronounced around adolescence, often appearing bumpy, warty or scaly.

name: epidermal nevus
epidermal nevus
HP:0010816.def: Epidermal naevi are due to an overgrowth of the epidermis and may be present at birth (50%) or develop during childhood.

name: linear nevus sebaceous
linear nevus sebaceous
HP:0010817.def: A type of nevus sebaceous with a linear form, raised borders and yellowish color.

name: generalized tonic seizure
generalize tonic seizure
HP:0010818.def: A generalized tonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterised by bilateral limb stiffening or elevation, often with neck stiffening without a subsequent clonic phase. The tonic activity can be a sustained abnormal posture, either in extension or flexion, sometimes accompanied by tremor of the extremities.

name: atonic seizure
atonic seizure
HP:0010819.def: Atonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by a sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic event lasting about 1 to 2 seconds, involving head, trunk, jaw, or limb musculature.

name: focal emotional seizure with crying
focal emotional seizure with cry
HP:0010820.def: Focal emotional seizure with crying (dacrystic) is characterized by the presence of stereotyped crying, this may be accompanied by lacrimation, sad facial expression and sobbing. The subjective emotion of sadness may or may not be present.

name: focal emotional seizure with laughing
focal emotional seizure with laugh
HP:0010821.def: Focal emotional seizure with laughing (gelastic) is characterized by bursts of laughter or giggling, usually without appropriate related emotion of happiness, and described as 'mirthless'.

name: scintillating scotoma
scintillate scotoma
HP:0010822.def: A scintillating scotoma is a common visual aura that can preced a migraine, whereby a spot of flickering light near the center of the visual fields occurs. The spot prevents vision, and is thus termed scotoma. The scotoma can extend into one or more shimmering arcs of white or colored flashing lights.

name: ridged cranial sutures
ridge cranial suture
HP:0010823.def: An overlap of the bony plates of the skull in an infant, with or without early closure.

name: abnormal fifth cranial nerve morphology
abnormal fifth cranial nerve morphology
HP:0010824.def: Any structural abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve.
synonym: abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve
abnormality of the fifth cranial nerve

name: abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve
abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve
HP:0010825.def: Abnormality of the eleventh cranial nerve.

name: abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve
abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve
HP:0010826.def: Abnormality of the twelfth cranial nerve.

name: abnormality of the seventh cranial nerve
abnormality of the seventh cranial nerve
HP:0010827.def: Abnormality of the seventh cranial nerve sometimes also referred to as the facial nerve.

name: hemifacial spasm
hemifacial spasm
HP:0010828.def: Intermittent clonic or tonic contraction of muscles supplied by facial nerve. Muscles are relaxed in between contractions.
synonym: spasms on one side of the face
spasm on one side of the face

name: impaired temperature sensation
impaired temperature sensation
HP:0010829.def: A reduced ability to discriminate between different temperatures.

name: impaired tactile sensation
impaired tactile sensation
HP:0010830.def: A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation). This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.

name: impaired proprioception
impaired proprioception
HP:0010831.def: A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position.

name: abnormality of pain sensation
abnormality of pain sensation
HP:0010832.def: Pain is an unpleasant sensation that can range from mild, localized discomfort to agony, whereby the physical part of pain results from nerve stimulation and is often accompanied by an emotional component. This term groups abnormalities in pain sensation presumed to result from abnormalities related to the specific nerve fibers that carry the pain impulses to the brain.

name: spontaneous pain sensation
spontaneous pain sensation
HP:0010833.def: Spontaneous pain is a kind of neuropathic pain which occurs without an identifiable trigger.

name: trophic changes related to pain
trophic change relate to pain
HP:0010834.def: Trophic changes is a term used to describe abnormalities in the area of pain that include primarily wasting away of the skin, tissues, or muscle, thinning of the bones, and changes in how the hair or nails grow, including thickening or thinning of hair or brittle nails.

name: dissociated sensory loss
dissociated sensory loss
HP:0010835.def: A pattern of sensory loss with selective loss of touch sensation and proprioception without loss of pain and temperature, or vice-versa.

name: decreased circulating ceruloplasmin concentration
decrease circulate ceruloplasmin concentration
HP:0010837.def: Decreased concentration of ceruloplasmin in the blood.

name: high nonceruloplasmin - bound serum copper
high nonceruloplasmin - bound serum copper
HP:0010838.def: An increased concentration of non ceruloplasmin bound copper in the blood.

name: increased urinary copper concentration
increase urinary copper concentration
HP:0010839.def: An increased concentration of copper in the urine.

name: multifocal epileptiform discharges
multifocal epileptiform discharge
HP:0010841.def: An abnormality in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG) and being identified at multiple locations (foci).

name: eeg with focal slow activity
eeg with focal slow activity
HP:0010843.def: Focal (localized) slow activity reflects focal dysfunction, not diffuse dysfunction (i.e., encephalopathy).

name: eeg with multifocal slow activity
eeg with multifocal slow activity
HP:0010844.def: Multifocal slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: eeg with generalized slow activity
eeg with generalized slow activity
HP:0010845.def: Diffuse slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: eeg with persistent abnormal rhythmic activity
eeg with persistent abnormal rhythmic activity
eeg with spike - wave complexes ( < 2.5 hz )
eeg with spike - wave complex ( < 2.5 hz )
HP:0010847.def: The presence of complexes of slow spikes and slow waves (<2.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).
synonym: electroencephalogram demonstrated spike - slow wave discharges
electroencephalogram demonstrate spike - slow wave discharge

name: eeg with spike - wave complexes ( 2.5 - 3.5 hz )
eeg with spike - wave complex ( 2.5 - 3.5 hz )
HP:0010848.def: The presence of complexes of spikes and waves (2.5-3.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).

name: eeg with spike - wave complexes ( > 3.5 hz )
eeg with spike - wave complex ( > 3.5 hz )
HP:0010849.def: The presence of complexes of spikes and waves (>3.5 Hz) in electroencephalography (EEG).

name: eeg with spike - wave complexes
eeg with spike - wave complex
HP:0010850.def: Complexes of spikes (<70 ms) and sharp waves (70-200 ms), which are sharp transient waves that have a strong association with epilepsy, in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: eeg with burst suppression
eeg with burst suppression
HP:0010851.def: The burst suppression pattern in electroencephalography refers to a characteristic periodic pattern of low voltage (<10 microvolts) suppressed background and a relatively shorter pattern of higher amplitude slow, sharp, and spiking complexes.

name: eeg with photoparoxysmal response
eeg with photoparoxysmal response
HP:0010852.def: EEG abnormalities (epileptiform discharges) evoked by flashing lights or black and white striped patterns.

name: eeg with periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges
eeg with periodic lateralize epileptiform discharge
HP:0010853.def: Periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs)are periodic, lateralized, and epileptiform. PLEDs show a relatively constant interval between discharges (0.5 to 3 seconds).

name: eeg with generalized low amplitude activity
eeg with generalized low amplitude activity
HP:0010854.def: An abnormal generalized reduction in amplitude of the cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
synonym: eeg with generalised low amplitude activity
eeg with generalised low amplitude activity

name: eeg with localized low amplitude activity
eeg with localized low amplitude activity
HP:0010855.def: An abnormal localized reduction in amplitude of the cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
synonym: eeg with localised low amplitude activity
eeg with localised low amplitude activity

name: eeg with periodic abnormalities
eeg with periodic abnormality
HP:0010857.def: Periodically recurring abnormalities in the EEG.

name: eeg with hyperventilation - induced epileptiform discharges
eeg with hyperventilation - induced epileptiform discharge
HP:0010858.def: Epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: frank breech presentation
frank breech presentation
HP:0010859.def: A kind of breech presentation in which the hips are flexed and the knees are extended.

name: complete breech presentation
complete breech presentation
HP:0010860.def: A kind of breech presentation in which the hips are flexed and the knees are flexed.

name: incomplete breech presentation
incomplete breech presentation
HP:0010861.def: A kind of breech presentation in which one or both hips are extended and one or both of the fetus' feet are pointing down and entering the birth canal.

name: delayed fine motor development
delay fine motor development
HP:0010862.def: A type of motor delay characterized by a delay in acquiring the ability to control the fingers and hands.

name: receptive language delay
receptive language delay
HP:0010863.def: A delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

name: intellectual disability , severe
intellectual disability , severe
HP:0010864.def: Severe mental retardation is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 20-34.

name: oppositional defiant disorder
oppositional defiant disorder
HP:0010865.def: An enduring pattern of uncooperative, defiant, and hostile behavior towards authority figures that does not involve major antisocial violations, is not accounted for by the child's developmental stage, and results in significant functional impairment. A certain level of oppositional behavior is common in children and adolescents.

name: abdominal wall defect
abdominal wall defect
HP:0010866.def: An incomplete closure of the abdominal wall.

name: dyssynergia
dyssynergia
HP:0010867.def: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to smoothly perform the elements of a voluntary movement in the appropriate order and speed. With dyssynergia, a voluntary movement appears broken down into its component parts.

name: ocular dyssynergia
ocular dyssynergia
HP:0010868.def: A type of dyssynergia affecting eye movements and characterized by the inability to smoothly follow a visual target across the visual field.

name: asynergia
asynergia
HP:0010869.def: A type of dyssynergy characterized by the lack of the ability to smoothly perform the elements of a voluntary movement in the appropriate order and speed.

name: sensory ataxia
sensory ataxia
HP:0010871.def: Incoordination of movement caused by a deficit in the sensory nervous system. Sensory ataxia can be distinguished from cerebellar ataxia by asking the patient to close his or her eyes. Persons with cerebellar ataxia show only a minimal worsening of symptoms, whereas persons with sensory ataxia show a marked worsening of symptoms.

name: t - wave inversion
t - wave inversion
HP:0010872.def: An inversion of the T-wave (which is normally positive).

name: cervical spinal cord atrophy
cervical spinal cord atrophy
HP:0010873.def: Atrophy of the cervical segment of the spinal cord.

name: tendon xanthomatosis
tendon xanthomatosis
HP:0010874.def: The presence of xanthomas (intra-and extra-cellular accumulations of cholesterol) extensor tendons (typically over knuckles, Achilles tendon, knee, and elbows).

name: chaddock reflex
chaddock reflex
HP:0010875.def: A diagnostic reflex elicited by stimulation of the skin over the surface of the lateral malleolus of the foot. The Chaddock refelx is present if there is extension of one or more or all of the toes with or without fanning of them when the external inframalleolar skin is stimulated. The Chaddock sign, similar to the Babinski sign, is taken to be an indication of disease of the spinocortical (pyramidal) tract.

name: abnormal circulating protein concentration
abnormal circulate protein concentration
HP:0010876.def: An abnormal level of a circulating protein in the blood.

name: monocular strabismus
monocular strabismus
HP:0010877.def: A type of strabismus in which the fixating eye is always the same one, while the other eye is constantly deviated. Monocular strabismus is to be distinguished from alternating strabismus, in which either of the eyes 'squints' at different times.

name: fetal cystic hygroma
fetal cystic hygroma
HP:0010878.def: The presence during the prenatal period of a cystic mass with multiple septa with multiple, asymmetric, thin-walled cysts near the posterior aspect of the neck. Fetal cystic hygroma can be defined as nuchal translucency with or without septations measuring greater than 3.0 mm. Increased NT refers to a measurement above the 95th centile, and the term is used irrespective of whether the collection of fluid is septated or not, and whether it is confined to the neck or envelopes the whole fetus. After 14 weeks, increased NT usually resolves, but in some cases it evolves into nuchal edema or cystic hygromas.

name: increased nuchal translucency
increase nuchal translucency
HP:0010880.def: Nuchal translucency is the sonographic appearance of subcutaneous accumulation of liquid in the back of the fetal neck in the first trimester of pregnancy (11-14 gestational weeks of pregnancy).

name: abnormality of the umbilical cord
abnormality of the umbilical cord
HP:0010881.def: An abnormality of the umbilical cord, which is the cord connecting the developing embryo or fetus to the placenta.

name: pulmonary valve atresia
pulmonary valve atresia
HP:0010882.def: A congenital disorder of the pulmonary valve in which the orifice of the valve fails to develop.

name: aortic valve atresia
aortic valve atresia
HP:0010883.def: A congenital disorder of the aortic valve in which the orifice of the valve fails to develop.

name: acromelia
acromelia
HP:0010884.def: Shortening of the extremities affecting primarily the distal parts of the limbs (hands and feet) in relation to the other segments of the limbs.

name: avascular necrosis
avascular necrosis
HP:0010885.def: A disease where there is cellular death (necrosis) of bone components due to interruption of the blood supply.
synonym: death of bone due to decreased blood supply
death of bone due to decreased blood supply

name: osteochondritis dissecans
osteochondritis dissecans
HP:0010886.def: A joint disorder caused by blood deprivation in the subchondral bone causing the subchondral bone to die in a process called avascular necrosis. The bone is then reabsorbed by the body, leaving the articular cartilage it supported prone to damage. The result is fragmentation (dissection) of both cartilage and bone, and the free movement of these osteochondral fragments within the joint space, causing pain and further damage.

name: morbus koehler
morbus koehler
HP:0010888.def: Morbus Koehler is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Os naviculare pedis.

name: morbus kienboeck
morbus kienboeck
HP:0010889.def: Morbus Kienboeck is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Os lunatum.

name: morbus osgood - schlatter
morbus osgood - schlatter
HP:0010890.def: Morbus Osgood-Schlatter is a Juvenile aseptic necrosis affecting the Tuberositas tibiae.

name: morbus scheuermann
morbus scheuermann
HP:0010891.def: A developmental growth retardation of the vertebral end plates that may lead to secondary destruction of the vertebral end plates and protrusion of the nucleus pulposus into the vertebral body (so called Schmorl's nodes as seen on x-rays).

name: abnormal circulating branched chain amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate branch chain amino acid concentration
HP:0010892.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a branched chain family amino acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating phenylalanine concentration
abnormal circulate phenylalanine concentration
HP:0010893.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of phenylalanine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating serine family amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate serine family amino acid concentration
HP:0010894.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a serine family amino acid in the blood circulation.
synonym: abnormality of serine family amino acid metabolism
abnormality of serine family amino acid metabolism

name: abnormal circulating glycine concentration
abnormal circulate glycine concentration
HP:0010895.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glycine in the blood circulation.

name: hypersarcosinemia
hypersarcosinemia
HP:0010896.def: An elevated plasma concentration of sarcosine.

name: hypersarcosinuria
hypersarcosinuria
HP:0010897.def: An elevated urinary concentration of sarcosine.

name: abnormal circulating sarcosine concentration
abnormal circulate sarcosine concentration
HP:0010898.def: An deviation from the normal concentration of sarcosine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating aspartate family amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate aspartate family amino acid concentration
HP:0010899.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of an aspartate family amino acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating threonine concentration
abnormal circulate threonine concentration
HP:0010900.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of threonine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating methionine concentration
abnormal circulate methionine concentration
HP:0010901.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of methionine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating glutamine family amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate glutamine family amino acid concentration
HP:0010902.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a glutamine family amino acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating glutamine concentration
abnormal circulate glutamine concentration
HP:0010903.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glutamine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating histidine concentration
abnormal circulate histidine concentration
HP:0010904.def: An abnormality of a histidine metabolic process.

name: hyperhistidinemia
hyperhistidinemia
HP:0010906.def: An increased concentration of histidine in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating proline concentration
abnormal circulate proline concentration
HP:0010907.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of proline or a proline metabolite in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating lysine concentration
abnormal circulate lysine concentration
HP:0010908.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of lysine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating arginine concentration
abnormal circulate arginine concentration
HP:0010909.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of arginine in the blood circulation.

name: hypervalinemia
hypervalinemia
HP:0010910.def: An increased concentration of valine in the blood.

name: hyperleucinemia
hyperleucinemia
HP:0010911.def: An increased concentration of leucine in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating isoleucine concentration
abnormal circulate isoleucine concentration
HP:0010912.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of isoleucine in the blood circulation.

name: hyperisoleucinemia
hyperisoleucinemia
HP:0010913.def: An increased concentration of isoleucine in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating valine concentration
abnormal circulate valine concentration
HP:0010914.def: Any deviation from the normal circulation of valine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating pyruvate family amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate pyruvate family amino acid concentration
HP:0010915.def: An abnormality of a pyruvate family amino acid metabolic process.
synonym: abnormality of pyruvate family amino acid metabolism
abnormality of pyruvate family amino acid metabolism

name: abnormal circulating alanine concentration
abnormal circulate alanine concentration
HP:0010916.def: An abnormality of an alanine metabolic process.

name: abnormal circulating tyrosine concentration
abnormal circulate tyrosine concentration
HP:0010917.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of tyrosine in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating cysteine concentration
abnormal circulate cysteine concentration
HP:0010918.def: An abnormality of a cysteine metabolic process.

name: abnormal circulating homocysteine concentration
abnormal circulate homocysteine concentration
HP:0010919.def: An abnormality of a homocysteine metabolic process.

name: zonular cataract
zonular cataract
HP:0010920.def: Zonular cataracts are defined to be cataracts that affect specific regions of the lens.

name: coralliform cataract
coralliform cataract
HP:0010921.def: A 'coral-like' pattern of opacity in the lens of the eye. That is, a cataract with an irregular, stellate form.

name: membranous cataract
membranous cataract
HP:0010922.def: A form of cataract in which the lens substance has shrunk, leaving a collapsed, flattened capsule with little or no cortex or epithelium on the lens.

name: anterior subcapsular cataract
anterior subcapsular cataract
HP:0010923.def: A type of cataract affecting the anterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to ('beneath') the lens capsule.

name: posterior cortical cataract
posterior cortical cataract
HP:0010924.def: A cataract that affects the posterior part of the cortex of the lens.

name: aculeiform cataract
aculeiform cataract
HP:0010926.def: A kind of nuclear cataract characterized by fiberglasslike or needlelike crystals projecting in different directions, through or close to the axial region of the lens.

name: abnormal blood inorganic cation concentration
abnormal blood inorganic cation concentration
HP:0010927.def: An abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis.
synonym: abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis
abnormality of divalent inorganic cation homeostasis

name: obsolete increased urinary orotic acid concentration
obsolete increase urinary orotic acid concentration
abnormal blood monovalent inorganic cation concentration
abnormal blood monovalent inorganic cation concentration
HP:0010930.def: An abnormality of monovalent inorganic cation homeostasis.
synonym: abnormality of monovalent inorganic cation homeostasis
abnormality of monovalent inorganic cation homeostasis

name: abnormal circulating nucleobase concentration
abnormal circulate nucleobase concentration
HP:0010932.def: An abnormality of a nucleobase metabolic process.

name: hyperxanthinemia
hyperxanthinemia
HP:0010933.def: An increased level of xanthine in the blood circulation.

name: xanthinuria
xanthinuria
HP:0010934.def: An increased concentration of xanthine in the urine.

name: abnormality of the upper urinary tract
abnormality of the upper urinary tract
HP:0010935.def: An abnormality of the upper urinary tract.
synonym: abnormality of the upper urinary tract
abnormality of the upper urinary tract

name: abnormality of the lower urinary tract
abnormality of the low urinary tract
HP:0010936.def: An abnormality of the lower urinary tract.

name: abnormal nasal skeleton morphology
abnormal nasal skeleton morphology
HP:0010937.def: An abnormality of the nasal skeleton.
synonym: deformity of the bones of the nose
deformity of the bone of the nose
distortion of the bones of the nose
distortion of the bone of the nose
malformation of the bones of the nose
malformation of the bone of the nose

name: abnormal external nose morphology
abnormal external nose morphology
HP:0010938.def: An abnormality of the external nose.

name: abnormal nasal bone morphology
abnormal nasal bone morphology
HP:0010939.def: An abnormality of the nasal bone, comprising the left nasal bone and the right nasal bone.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the nasal bone
aplasia / hypoplasia of the nasal bone
HP:0010940.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the nasal bone.

name: aplasia of the nasal bone
aplasia of the nasal bone
synonym: failure of development of the nasal bone
failure of development of the nasal bone
lack of development of the nasal bone
lack of development of the nasal bone

name: echogenic intracardiac focus
echogenic intracardiac focus
HP:0010942.def: A finding of a focus of increased echogenicity upon prenatal ultrasound examination of the fetus. The foci may be present in one or both ventricles. Echogenic intracardiac focus (EICF) is defined as a focus of echogenicity comparable to bone, in the region of the papillary muscle in either or both ventricles of the fetal heart.

name: echogenic fetal bowel
echogenic fetal bowel
HP:0010943.def: Echogenic bowel is defined as fetal bowel with homogenous areas of echogenicity that are equal to or greater than that of surrounding bone.

name: abnormal renal pelvis morphology
abnormal renal pelvis morphology
