HP:0010944.def: An abnormality of the renal pelvis.

name: fetal pyelectasis
fetal pyelectasis
HP:0010945.def: Mild pyelectasis is defined as a hypoechoic spherical or elliptical space within the renal pelvis that measures at least 5mm and not more than 10 mm. The measurement is taken on a transverse section through the fetal renal pelvis using the maximum anterior-to-posterior measurement.

name: dilatation of the renal pelvis
dilatation of the renal pelvis
HP:0010946.def: The presence of dilatation of the renal pelvis.

name: abnormality of ductus venosus blood flow
abnormality of ductus venosus blood flow
HP:0010947.def: A first-trimester prenatal ultrasound finding of abnormal blood flow in the ductus venosus.

name: abnormal fetal cardiovascular morphology
abnormal fetal cardiovascular morphology
HP:0010948.def: A structural abnormality of the fetal circulation system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.
synonym: abnormality of the fetal cardiovascular system
abnormality of the fetal cardiovascular system
abnormality of the fetal circulation system
abnormality of the fetal circulation system
abnormality of the foetal cardiovascular system
abnormality of the foetal cardiovascular system
abnormality of the foetal circulation system
abnormality of the foetal circulation system

name: abnormality of umbilical vein blood flow
abnormality of umbilical vein blood flow
HP:0010949.def: A first-trimester prenatal ultrasound finding of abnormal blood flow in the umbilical vein.

name: abnormal fourth ventricle morphology
abnormal fourth ventricle morphology
HP:0010950.def: An abnormality of the fourth ventricle.

name: abnormal third ventricle morphology
abnormal third ventricle morphology
HP:0010951.def: An abnormality of the third ventricle.

name: mild fetal ventriculomegaly
mild fetal ventriculomegaly
HP:0010952.def: A kind of ventriculomegaly occurring in the fetal period and usually diagnosed by prenatal ultrasound. Cerebral ventriculomegaly is defined by atrial measurements 10 mm or more. Mild ventriculomegaly (MVM) is defined as measurements between 10 and 15 mm. Measurements are obtained from an axial plane at the level of the thalamic nuclei just below the standard image to measure the BPD (PMID:16100637).

name: noncommunicating hydrocephalus
noncommunicating hydrocephalus
HP:0010953.def: A form of hydrocephalus in which the flow of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) within the cerebral ventricular system or in the outlets of the CSF to the arachnoid space is obstructed.

name: hypoplastic right heart
hypoplastic right heart
HP:0010954.def: Underdevelopment of the right-sided structures of the heart.

name: dilatation of the bladder
dilatation of the bladder
HP:0010955.def: The presence of a dilated urinary bladder.

name: fetal megacystis
fetal megacystis
HP:0010956.def: Fetal megacystis is an abnormally enlarged bladder identified at any gestational age.

name: congenital posterior urethral valve
congenital posterior urethral valve
HP:0010957.def: A developmental defect resulting in an obstructing membrane in the posterior male urethra.

name: bilateral renal agenesis
bilateral renal agenesis
HP:0010958.def: A bilateral form of agenesis of the kidney.

name: congenital pulmonary airway malformation
congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP:0010959.def: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) - previously known as congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM) - is a relatively rare developmental malformation of the lower respiratory tract. It is a hamartomatous, dysplastic developmental abnormality of the lung characterized by abnormal airway patterning during lung branching morphogenesis and is formed by abnormal branching of the immature bronchioles.
synonym: congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung
congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung
congenital cystic disease of the lung
congenital cystic disease of the lung

name: bronchopulmonary sequestration
bronchopulmonary sequestration
HP:0010960.def: The presence of microscopic cystic masses of nonfunctioning pulmonary tissue that lack an obvious communication with the tracheobronchial tree.

name: intralobar sequestration
intralobar sequestration
HP:0010961.def: A kind of bronchopulmonary sequestration that is incorporated into the normal surrounding lung.

name: extralobar sequestration
extralobar sequestration
HP:0010962.def: A kind of bronchopulmonary sequestration that is completely discrete from the normal lung and is surrounded by separate pleura.

name: absence of stomach bubble on fetal sonography
absence of stomach bubble on fetal sonography
HP:0010963.def: By the 14th week of gestation it is nearly always possible to visualized the fluid-filled fetal stomach bubble on prenatal sonography. This term refers to the absence of a normal fetal stomach bubble on fetal ultrasonography performed at around 16 to 20 weeks' gestation.
synonym: absence of stomach bubble on foetal sonography
absence of stomach bubble on foetal sonography
non - visualisation of the fetal stomach
non - visualisation of the fetal stomach
non - visualisation of the foetal stomach
non - visualisation of the foetal stomach

name: abnormal circulating long - chain fatty - acid concentration
abnormal circulate long - chain fatty - acid concentration
HP:0010964.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a long-chain fatty acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating phytanic acid concentration
abnormal circulate phytanic acid concentration
HP:0010965.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of phytanic acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating fatty - acid anion concentration
abnormal circulate fatty - acid anion concentration
HP:0010966.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a fatty acid anion in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating carnitine concentration
abnormal circulate carnitine concentration
HP:0010967.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation.

name: blood group antigen abnormality
blood group antigen abnormality
HP:0010970.def: An abnormality of an erythrocyte cell surface molecule.

name: absence of lutheran antigen on erythrocytes
absence of lutheran antigen on erythrocyte
HP:0010971.def: Absence of the Lutheran antigen (a type I integral membrane glycoprotein) from the surface of red blood cells.

name: anemia of inadequate production
anemia of inadequate production
HP:0010972.def: A kind of anemia characterized by inadequate production of erythrocytes.

name: abnormal b cell count
abnormal b cell count
HP:0010975.def: A deviation from the normal count of B cells, i.e., the cells that are formed in the bone marrow, migrate to the peripheral lymphatic system, and mature into plasma cells or memory cells.

name: b lymphocytopenia
b lymphocytopenia
HP:0010976.def: An abnormal decrease from the normal count of B cells.

name: abnormal phagocytosis
abnormal phagocytosis
HP:0010977.def: An abnormal functioning of phagocytosis. Phagocytosis is an elegant but complex process for the ingestion and elimination of pathogens, but it is also important for the elimination of apoptotic cells and hence fundamental for tissue homeostasis. Phagocytosis can be divided into four main steps: (i) recognition of the target particle, (ii) signaling to activate the internalization machinery, (iii) phagosome formation, and (iv) phagolysosome maturation.

name: abnormality of immune system physiology
abnormality of immune system physiology
HP:0010978.def: A functional abnormality of the immune system.

name: abnormality of lipoprotein cholesterol concentration

name: hyperlipoproteinemia
hyperlipoproteinemia
HP:0010980.def: An abnormal increase in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

name: hypolipoproteinemia
hypolipoproteinemia
HP:0010981.def: An abnormal decrease in the level of lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

name: polygenic inheritance
polygenic inheritance
HP:0010982.def: A mode of inheritance that depends on a mixture of major and minor genetic determinants possibly together with environmental factors. Diseases inherited in this manner are termed complex diseases.

name: oligogenic inheritance
oligogenic inheritance
HP:0010983.def: A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of a few gene loci. It is recommended this term be used for traits governed by three loci, although it is noted that usage of this term in the literature is not uniform.

name: digenic inheritance
digenic inheritance
HP:0010984.def: A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of two gene loci.

name: abnormal cellular immune system morphology

name: abnormality of the extrinsic pathway

name: abnormality of the intrinsic pathway
abnormality of the intrinsic pathway

name: abnormality of the common coagulation pathway

name: abnormal morphology of the abdominal musculature

name: stress urinary incontinence

name: abnormal corpus striatum morphology

name: abnormal circulating dicarboxylic acid concentration

name: abnormal circulating monocarboxylic acid concentration

synonym: chromosomal breakage induced by ionising radiation
chromosomal breakage induce by ionise radiation

name: increased susceptibility to spontaneous sister chromatid exchange
increase susceptibility to spontaneous sister chromatid exchange
HP:0010998.def: An increase in the number of spontaneous sister chromatid exchanges observed in cell culture of lymphocytes or other cells.

aplasia / hypoplasia of the optic tract
increased bone mineral density
increase bone mineral density
HP:0011001.def: An abnormal increase of bone mineral density, that is, of the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones which is often referred to as osteosclerosis. Osteosclerosis can be detected on radiological examination as an increased whiteness (density) of affected bones.

name: osteopetrosis
osteopetrosis
HP:0011002.def: Abnormally increased formation of dense trabecular bone tissue. Despite the increased density of bone tissue, osteopetrotic bones tend to be more fracture-prone than normal.

name: high myopia
high myopia
HP:0011003.def: A severe form of myopia with greater than -6.00 diopters.

name: mixed cirrhosis
mixed cirrhosis

name: subacute

HP:0011034.def: The presence of amyloid deposition in one or more tissues. Amyloidosis may be defined as the extracellular deposition of amyloid in one or more sites of the body.

name: abnormal renal cortex morphology

name: abnormal helix morphology
abnormal helix morphology
HP:0011039.def: An abnormality of the helix. The helix is the outer rim of the ear that extends from the insertion of the ear on the scalp (root) to the termination of the cartilage at the earlobe.

name: abnormal intrahepatic bile duct morphology
abnormal intrahepatic bile duct morphology
HP:0011040.def: An abnormality of the intrahepatic bile duct.

HP:0011041.def: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the cervical vertebral column.

abnormal number of permanent teeth

dentinogenesis imperfecta limit to primary teeth
HP:0011060.def: Developmental dysplasia of dentin affecting only the primary dentition.

HP:0011061.def: An abnormality of the structure or composition of the teeth.

name: abnormal incisor morphology
abnormal incisor morphology
HP:0011063.def: An abnormality of morphology of the incisor tooth.

name: abnormal number of incisors
abnormal number of incisor

name: conical incisor
conical incisor
HP:0011065.def: An abnormal conical morphology of the incisor tooth.

name: mesiodens
mesiodens
HP:0011067.def: A supernumerary tooth in the midline between the maxillary central incisors.

name: supernumerary tooth
supernumerary tooth
HP:0011069.def: The presence of one or more teeth additional to the normal number.

name: abnormal molar morphology
abnormal molar morphology
HP:0011070.def: An abnormality of morphology of molar tooth.

name: abnormal permanent molar morphology
abnormal permanent molar morphology
HP:0011071.def: An abnormality of morphology of permanent molar.
synonym: abnormality of shape of adult molar

abnormality of shape of permanent molar

name: rootless teeth
rootless teeth
synonym: tooth with dentin dysplasia type i
tooth with dentin dysplasia type i

name: abnormality of dental color
abnormality of dental color
HP:0011073.def: A developmental defect of tooth color.

name: localized hypoplasia of dental enamel
localized hypoplasia of dental enamel
HP:0011074.def: A localized form of developmental hypoplasia of the dental enamel.

name: impacted tooth
impact tooth
HP:0011079.def: A tooth that has not erupted because of local impediments (overcrowding or fibrous gum overgrowth).

name: abnormal premolar morphology
abnormal premolar morphology
HP:0011080.def: An abnormality of morphology of premolar tooth.

name: incisor macrodontia
incisor macrodontia
HP:0011081.def: Increased size of the incisor tooth.

name: conical primary incisor
conical primary incisor
HP:0011082.def: An abnormal conical morphology of the primary incisor.

name: conical maxillary incisor
conical maxillary incisor
HP:0011083.def: An abnormal conical morphology of either maxillary primary incisor tooth or maxillary permanent incisor tooth or both.

name: hypocalcification of dental enamel
hypocalcification of dental enamel
HP:0011084.def: A form of hypomineralization of enamel characterized by reduced calcification.

name: hypomature dental enamel
hypomature dental enamel
HP:0011085.def: A form of hypomineralization of enamel characterized by a chalky appearance of the enamel with orange, brown, or white color.

name: dentinogenesis imperfecta of primary and permanent teeth
dentinogenesis imperfecta of primary and permanent teeth
HP:0011086.def: Developmental dysplasia of dentin or both the primary dentition and the permanent dentition.
synonym: dentinogenesis imperfecta of adult and baby teeth
dentinogenesis imperfecta of adult and baby teeth
dentinogenesis imperfecta of both sets of teeth
dentinogenesis imperfecta of both set of teeth

name: talon cusp
talon cusp
HP:0011087.def: Talon cusp is an accessory cusp located near the cingulum (the portion of the lingual or palatal aspect of the tooth that forms a convex protuberance at the cervical third of the anatomic crown).
synonym: extra cusp on inside of front tooth
extra cusp on inside of front tooth

name: dens in dente
den in dente
HP:0011088.def: An abnormality of the incisor characterized by invagination of the enamel, giving a radiographic appearance that suggests a tooth within a tooth.

name: fused teeth
fuse teeth
HP:0011090.def: The union of two separately developing tooth germs typically leading to one less tooth than normal in the affected dental arch.

name: gemination
gemination
HP:0011091.def: The development of two teeth from a single tooth bud, leading to a larger fused tooth.

name: mulberry molar
mulberry molar
HP:0011092.def: Mulberry molars are irregular teeth generally affecting the first molars and are characterized by a grossly deformed crown imitating, as the name implies, the surface of a mulberry.

name: molarization of premolar
molarization of premolar
HP:0011093.def: Increased size and molar morphology of premolar tooth.

name: increased overbite
increase overbite
HP:0011094.def: Maxillary teeth cover the mandibular teeth when biting to an increased degree. The feature is defined as a vertical overlap of the maxillary incisors over the mandibular incisors that exceeds 2 mm.
synonym: increased overlap of upper and lower incisors
increase overlap of upper and low incisor

name: overjet
overjet
HP:0011095.def: An abnormal anteroposterior extension of the maxillary teeth beyond the plane of the mandibular teeth upon jaw closure.
synonym: protrusion of upper teeth in front of lower teeth
protrusion of upper teeth in front of low teeth

name: peripheral demyelination
peripheral demyelination
HP:0011096.def: A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

name: epileptic spasm
epileptic spasm
HP:0011097.def: A sudden flexion, extension, or mixed extension-flexion of predominantly proximal and truncal muscles that is usually more sustained than a myoclonic movement but not as sustained as a tonic seizure. Limited forms may occur: Grimacing, head nodding, or subtle eye movements. Epileptic spasms frequently occur in clusters. Infantile spasms are the best known form, but spasms can occur at all ages

name: speech apraxia
speech apraxia
HP:0011098.def: A type of apraxia that is characterized by difficulty or inability to execute speech movements because of problems with coordination and motor problems, leading to incorrect articulation. An increase of errors with increasing word and phrase length may occur.

name: spastic hemiparesis
spastic hemiparesis
HP:0011099.def: Unilateral paresis (weakness) with spasticity of the affected muscles and increased tendon reflexes.

name: intestinal atresia
intestinal atresia
HP:0011100.def: An abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the intestine.

name: ileal atresia
ileal atresia
HP:0011102.def: An abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the ileum.

name: abnormal left ventricular outflow tract morphology
abnormal leave ventricular outflow tract morphology
HP:0011103.def: An abnormality of the outflow tract of the left ventricle.
synonym: abnormality of the left ventricular outflow tract
abnormality of the left ventricular outflow tract

name: abnormality of blood volume homeostasis
abnormality of blood volume homeostasis
HP:0011104.def: An abnormality in the amount of volume occupied by intravascular blood.

name: hypervolemia
hypervolemia
HP:0011105.def: An increase in the amount of intravascular fluid, particularly in the volume of the circulating blood.

name: hypovolemia
hypovolemia
HP:0011106.def: An decrease in the amount of intravascular fluid, particularly in the volume of the circulating blood.

name: recurrent aphthous stomatitis
recurrent aphthous stomatitis
HP:0011107.def: Recurrent episodes of ulceration of the oral mucosa, typically presenting as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a hyperemic border.

name: recurrent tonsillitis
recurrent tonsillitis
HP:0011110.def: Inflammation of the tonsils that has occurred repeatedly. The definition of recurrent may vary somewhat, but the criteria used recently as a measure of severity were five or more episodes of true tonsillitis per year, symptoms recurring for at least a year, and episodes that are disabling and that prevent normal functioning. In some cases recurrent tonsillitis may be related to immunosusceptibility. Evidence exists for a genetic predisposition for recurrent tonsillitis.

name: abnormality of immune serum protein physiology
abnormality of immune serum protein physiology
HP:0011111.def: An abnormality of the concentration or function of circulating immune proteins.

name: abnormality of serum cytokine level
abnormality of serum cytokine level
HP:0011112.def: Abnormality of the cytokine levels in the blood, i.e., an abnormality of any of the non-antibody proteins made by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells that affect the behavior of other cells.

name: abnormality of cytokine secretion
abnormality of cytokine secretion
HP:0011113.def: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of a cytokine (i.e., any of the non-antibody proteins made by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells that affect the behavior of other cells).

name: defective production of nfkb1 - dependent cytokines
defective production of nfkb1 - dependent cytokine
HP:0011114.def: An impairment in the production by leukocytes of NFKB1-dependent cytokines such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interferon-alpha.

name: abnormality of chemokine secretion
abnormality of chemokine secretion
HP:0011115.def: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of a chemokine (a class of cytokines).

name: abnormality of interferon secretion
abnormality of interferon secretion
HP:0011116.def: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of interferons (a class of cytokines).

name: abnormality of interleukin secretion
abnormality of interleukin secretion
HP:0011117.def: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of interleukins (a class of cytokines).

name: abnormality of tumor necrosis factor secretion
abnormality of tumor necrosis factor secretion
HP:0011118.def: An abnormality in the production or cellular release of tumor necrosis factor.
synonym: abnormality of tumour necrosis factor secretion
abnormality of tumour necrosis factor secretion

name: abnormal nasal dorsum morphology
abnormal nasal dorsum morphology
HP:0011119.def: An abnormality of the nasal dorsum, also known as the nasal ridge.
synonym: abnormal morphology of dorsum of nose
abnormal morphology of dorsum of nose
abnormality of the dorsum of nose
abnormality of the dorsum of nose
deformity of the dorsum of the nose
deformity of the dorsum of the nose
malformation of the dorsum of nose
malformation of the dorsum of nose

name: concave nasal ridge
concave nasal ridge
HP:0011120.def: Nasal ridge curving posteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip.

name: abnormal skin morphology
abnormal skin morphology
HP:0011121.def: Any morphological abnormality of the skin.

name: abnormality of skin physiology
abnormality of skin physiology
HP:0011122.def: Any abnormality of the physiological function of the skin.

name: inflammatory abnormality of the skin
inflammatory abnormality of the skin
HP:0011123.def: The presence of inflammation of the skin. That is, an abnormality of the skin resulting from the local accumulation of fluid, plasma proteins, and leukocytes.
synonym: abnormal tendency to infections of the skin
abnormal tendency to infection of the skin

name: abnormal epidermal morphology
abnormal epidermal morphology
HP:0011124.def: An abnormality of the morphology of the epidermis.

name: abnormality of dermal melanosomes
abnormality of dermal melanosomes
HP:0011125.def: An abnormality of the melanosomes, i.e., of the cellular organelles in which melanin pigments are synthesized and stored within melanocytes (the cells that produce pigment in the dermis).

name: nephroptosis
nephroptosis
HP:0011126.def: A significant descent of the kidney as the patient moves from the supine to the erect position.

name: perioral eczema
perioral eczema
HP:0011127.def: A type of eczema that occurs in the lips and perioral area.

name: acute esophageal necrosis
acute esophageal necrosis
HP:0011128.def: A condition characterized by necrosis of the mucosal and submucosal layers of the esophagus not related to ingestion of caustic or other injurious agents. Endoscopically, there is a dark lesion ('black esophagus') distributed in a circumferential manner in the distal one-third of the esophagus with or without exudates. There is involvement of the distal esophagus ending sharply at the gastroesophageal junction.

name: bilateral fetal pyelectasis
bilateral fetal pyelectasis
HP:0011129.def: A bilateral form of fetal pyelectasis.

name: abnormal renal calyx morphology
abnormal renal calyx morphology
HP:0011130.def: Any abnormality of the morphology of the major calices or minor calices of the kidney.

name: perianal dermatitis
perianal dermatitis
HP:0011131.def: The presence of a rash (change of color and texture) of the perianal skin.

name: chronic furunculosis
chronic furunculosis
HP:0011132.def: A furuncle (boil) is a skin infection involving an entire hair follicle and nearby skin tissue. Chronic furunculosis refers to recurrent episodes of furuncles, often caused by recurrent staphylococcus infection.

name: increased sensitivity to ionizing radiation
increase sensitivity to ionize radiation
HP:0011133.def: An abnormally increased sensitivity to the effects of ionizing radiation.

name: low - grade fever
low - grade fever
HP:0011134.def: Mild fever that does not exceed 38.5 degrees centigrade.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the sweat glands
aplasia / hypoplasia of the sweat gland
HP:0011135.def: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the sweat glands.

name: non - pruritic urticaria
non - pruritic urticaria
HP:0011137.def: Pale reddish slightly elevated papules and plaques of 0.5-3 cm in diameter and not accompanied by pruritus.

name: abnormal skin adnexa morphology
abnormal skin adnexa morphology
HP:0011138.def: An abnormality of the skin adnexa (skin appendages), which are specialized skin structures located within the dermis and focally within the subcutaneous fatty tissue, comprising three histologically distinct structures: (1) the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle and sebaceous glands); (2) the eccrine sweat glands; and (3) the apocrine glands.

name: gastric duplication
gastric duplication
HP:0011139.def: Gastric duplication is a usually cystic malformation of gastrointestinal tract, usually attached to the greater curvature of the stomach and has no communication with the stomach.

name: gastrointestinal duplication
gastrointestinal duplication
HP:0011140.def: A spherical hollow structure with a smooth muscle coat, lined by a mucous membrane, and attached to any part of the gastrointestinal tract, from the base of the tongue to the anus.

name: age - related cataract
age - relate cataract
HP:0011141.def: A type of cataract (opacification of the lens) that forms during the course of aging.
synonym: clouding of the lens of the eye with age
clouding of the lens of the eye with age

name: age - related nuclear cataract
age - related nuclear cataract
HP:0011142.def: A type of age-related cataract that primarily affects the nucleus of the lens.

name: age - related cortical cataract
age - related cortical cataract
HP:0011143.def: A type of age-related cataract that primarily affects the cortex of the lens.

name: age - related posterior subcapsular cataract
age - related posterior subcapsular cataract
HP:0011144.def: A type of age-related cataract consisting of granular opacities occurring mainly in the central posterior cortex just under the posterior capsule.

name: symptomatic seizures
symptomatic seizure
HP:0011145.def: A seizure that occurs in the context of a brain insult (systemic, toxic, or metabolic) and may not recur when the underlying cause has been removed or the acute phase has elapsed.

name: dialeptic seizure
dialeptic seizure
HP:0011146.def: A dialeptic seizure is a type of seizure characterised predominantly by reduced responsiveness or awareness and with subsequent at least partial amnesia of the event.
synonym: behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness irrespective of onset
unknown onset behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness
unknown onset behavioral arrest seizure with impairment of awareness
unknown onset behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness
unknown onset behavioural arrest seizure with impairment of awareness

name: typical absence seizure
typical absence seizure
HP:0011147.def: A typical absence seizure is a type of generalised non-motor (absence) seizure characterised by its sudden onset, interruption of ongoing activities, a blank stare, possibly a brief upward deviation of the eyes. Usually the patient will be unresponsive when spoken to. Duration is a few seconds to half a minute with very rapid recovery. Although not always available, an EEG would usually show 3 Hz generalized epileptiform discharges during the event.

name: obsolete absence seizures with special features
obsolete absence seizure with special feature
absence seizure with eyelid myoclonia
absence seizure with eyelid myoclonia
HP:0011149.def: An absence with eyelid myoclonia seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterised by forced upward jerking of the eyelids during an absence seizure.

name: myoclonic absence seizure
myoclonic absence seizure
HP:0011150.def: Myoclonic absence seizure is a type of generalized non-motor (absence) seizure characterised by an interruption of ongoing activities, a blank stare and rhythmic three-per-second myoclonic movements, causing ratcheting abduction of the upper limbs leading to progressive arm elevation, and associated with 3 Hz generalized spike-wave discharges on the electroencephalogram. Duration is typically 10-60 s. Whilst impairment of consciousness may not be obvious the ILAE classified this seizure as a generalized non-motor seizure in 2017.

name: atypical absence status epilepticus
atypical absence status epilepticus
HP:0011151.def: Atypical absence status epilepticus is a type of generalized non-convulsive status epilepticus without coma that is semiologically a prolonged atypical absence seizure.

name: early onset absence seizures
early onset absence seizure
HP:0011152.def: Typical absence seizures starting before the age of 4 years.

name: focal motor seizure
focal motor seizure
HP:0011153.def: A type of focal-onset seizure characterized by a motor sign as its initial semiological manifestation.

name: focal autonomic seizure
focal autonomic seizure
HP:0011154.def: An autonomic seizure is a type of focal non-motor seizure characterized by alteration of autonomic nervous system function as the initial semiological feature.

name: obsolete focal autonomic seizures with altered responsiveness
obsolete focal autonomic seizure with altered responsiveness
obsolete focal autonomic seizures without altered responsiveness
obsolete focal autonomic seizure without altered responsiveness
focal sensory seizure
focal sensory seizure
HP:0011157.def: A focal sensory seizure is a type seizure beginning with a subjective sensation.

name: focal sensory seizure with auditory features
focal sensory seizure with auditory feature
HP:0011158.def: A seizure characterized by elementary auditory phenomena including buzzing, ringing, drumming or single tones as its first clinical manifestation.

name: focal autonomic seizure with epigastric sensation / nausea / vomiting / other gastrointestinal phenomena
focal autonomic seizure with epigastric sensation / nausea / vomiting / other gastrointestinal phenomenon
HP:0011159.def: A type of focal autonomic seizure characterised by symptoms or signs pertaining to the gastrointestinal system as the initial semiological feature.

name: focal sensory seizure with gustatory features
focal sensory seizure with gustatory feature
HP:0011160.def: A seizure characterized by taste phenomena including acidic, bitter, salty, sweet, or metallic tastes as its first clinical manifestation.

name: focal sensory seizure with olfactory features
focal sensory seizure with olfactory feature
HP:0011161.def: Seizures characterized by olfactory phenomena as its first clinical manifestation.

name: focal sensory seizure with somatosensory features
focal sensory seizure with somatosensory feature
HP:0011163.def: A seizure characterized by sensory phenomena including tingling, numbness, electric-shock like sensation, pain, sense of movement, or desire to move as its first clinical manifestation.

name: focal sensory seizure with visual features
focal sensory seizure with visual feature
HP:0011165.def: A seizure characterized by elementary visual hallucinations such as flashing or flickering lights/colours, or other shapes, simple patterns, scotomata, or amaurosis as its first clinical manifestation.

name: focal myoclonic seizure
focal myoclonic seizure
HP:0011166.def: A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction(s) of muscles(s) or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.

name: focal tonic seizure
focal tonic seizure
HP:0011167.def: A type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained increase in muscle contraction, lasting a few seconds to minutes.

name: focal seizure with eyelid myoclonia
focal seizure with eyelid myoclonia
HP:0011168.def: Focal seizure with eyelid myoclonia, not eyelid myoclonias in the context of absence seizures.

name: generalized clonic seizure
generalize clonic seizure
HP:0011169.def: Generalized clonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterised by sustained bilateral jerking, either symmetric or asymmetric, that is regularly repetitive and involves the same muscle groups.

name: generalized myoclonic - atonic seizure
generalize myoclonic - atonic seizure
HP:0011170.def: A generalized myoclonic-atonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by a myoclonic jerk followed by an atonic motor component.

name: simple febrile seizure
simple febrile seizure
HP:0011171.def: A short generalized seizure, of a duration of <15 min, not recurring within 24 h, occurring during a febrile episode not caused by an acute disease of the nervous system intracranial infection or severe metabolic disturbance.

name: complex febrile seizure
complex febrile seizure
HP:0011172.def: A febrile seizure that has any of the following features: focal semiology (or associated with post-ictal neurologic abnormalities beyond drowsiness, such as a Todd's paresis), prolonged seizure beyond 15 minutes, or recurring (occurring more than once) in a 24 hour period.

name: focal behavior arrest seizure
focal behavior arrest seizure
HP:0011173.def: A type of focal non-motor seizure characterized by an arrest or pause of activities, freezing, or immobilization as the predominant semiological feature throughout the seizure.

name: focal hyperkinetic seizure
focal hyperkinetic seizure
HP:0011174.def: A focal seizure characterized at onset by predominantly proximal limb or axial muscles producing irregular sequential ballistic movements, such as pedaling, pelvic thrusting, thrashing, rocking movements.

name: focal motor seizure with version
focal motor seizure with version
HP:0011175.def: A type of focal motor seizure characterised by sustained, forced conjugate ocular, cephalic, and/or truncal rotation or lateral deviation from the midline as the initial semiological manifestation.

name: eeg with constitutional variants
eeg with constitutional variant
HP:0011176.def: An EEG with constitutional variants contains waves that are rare or unusual but not generally pathologic.

name: beta - eeg
beta - eeg
HP:0011179.def: EEG dominated by diffuse beta-waves (>13 Hz).

name: partial beta - eeg
partial beta - eeg
HP:0011180.def: EEG dominated by diffuse beta waves (>13 Hz) with occipitally localized alpha waves (8-13 Hz).

name: low voltage eeg
low voltage eeg
HP:0011181.def: EEG with an amplitude less than 30 microvolts without observable occipital alpha rhythm (8-13 Hz).

name: interictal epileptiform activity
interictal epileptiform activity
HP:0011182.def: Epileptiform activity refers to distinctive EEG waves or complexes distinguished from background activity found in in a proportion of human subjects with epilepsy, but which can also be found in subjects without seizures. Interictal epileptiform activity refers to such activity that occurs in the absence of a clinical or subclinical seizure.

name: eeg with hyperventilation - induced focal epileptiform discharges
eeg with hyperventilation - induced focal epileptiform discharge
HP:0011183.def: Focal epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: eeg with hyperventilation - induced generalized epileptiform discharges
eeg with hyperventilation - induced generalized epileptiform discharge
HP:0011184.def: Generalized epileptiform discharges induced by hyperventilation (overbreathing) in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).
synonym: eeg with hyperventilation - induced generalised epileptiform discharges
eeg with hyperventilation - induce generalised epileptiform discharge

name: eeg with focal epileptiform discharges
eeg with focal epileptiform discharge
HP:0011185.def: EEG discharges recorded in particular areas of a localized (focal) abnormality in cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography (EEG).

name: focal epileptiform discharges with limited propagation to contralateral hemisphere
focal epileptiform discharge with limited propagation to contralateral hemisphere
HP:0011186.def: Focal epileptiform discharges with spreading to contralateral hemisphere but without secondary generalization.

name: focal eeg discharges with propagation to ipsilateral hemisphere
focal eeg discharge with propagation to ipsilateral hemisphere
HP:0011187.def: Focal epileptiform discharges with spreading to the hemisphere on the same side of the brain.

name: focal eeg discharges with secondary generalization
focal eeg discharge with secondary generalization
HP:0011188.def: Focal EEG discharges that secondarily spread to both hemispheres and can then be recorded over the entire scalp.
synonym: focal eeg discharges with secondary generalisation
focal eeg discharge with secondary generalisation

name: bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharge
HP:0011189.def: Epileptiform discharges being identified at multiple locations in both hemispheres.

name: uni - and bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
uni - and bilateral multifocal epileptiform discharge
HP:0011190.def: Epileptiform discharges identified at multiple locations temporarily in both hemispheres and temporarily in one hemisphere.

name: unilateral multifocal epileptiform discharges
unilateral multifocal epileptiform discharge
HP:0011191.def: Epileptiform discharges being identified at multiple locations in one hemisphere.

name: polymorphic focal epileptiform discharges
polymorphic focal epileptiform discharge
HP:0011192.def: Focal epileptiform discharges of different shapes and frequencies.

name: eeg with focal spikes
eeg with focal spike
HP:0011193.def: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec.

name: eeg with series of focal spikes
eeg with series of focal spike
HP:0011194.def: Focal spikes occurring for several seconds.

name: eeg with focal sharp slow waves
eeg with focal sharp slow wave
HP:0011195.def: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with focal sharp waves
eeg with focal sharp wave
HP:0011196.def: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

name: eeg with focal spike waves
eeg with focal spike wave
HP:0011197.def: EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with generalized epileptiform discharges
eeg with generalized epileptiform discharge
HP:0011198.def: EEG discharges recorded on the entire scalp typically seen in persons with epilepsy.

name: eeg with generalized sharp slow waves
eeg with generalized sharp slow wave
HP:0011199.def: EEG with generalized sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.
synonym: eeg with generalised sharp slow waves
eeg with generalised sharp slow wave

name: eeg with generalized polymorphic epileptiform discharges
eeg with generalized polymorphic epileptiform discharge
HP:0011200.def: Generalized epileptiform discharges of different shapes and frequencies.
synonym: eeg with generalised polymorphic epileptiform discharges
eeg with generalised polymorphic epileptiform discharge

name: eeg with continuous slow activity
eeg with continuous slow activity
HP:0011204.def: EEG showing diffuse slowing without interruption.

name: eeg with intermittent slow activity
eeg with intermittent slow activity
HP:0011205.def: Non-continuous diffuse slowing of electroencephalographic patterns.

name: eeg with generalized slow activity grade 1
eeg with generalized slow activity grade 1
HP:0011206.def: Slowing at frequencies between 7.5 and 8.5 Hz.
synonym: eeg with generalised slow activity grade 1
eeg with generalised slow activity grade 1

name: eeg with generalized slow activity grade 2
eeg with generalized slow activity grade 2
HP:0011207.def: Generalized slowing of EEG activity at frequencies between 4-7 Hz.
synonym: eeg with generalised slow activity grade 2
eeg with generalised slow activity grade 2

name: eeg with generalized slow activity grade 3
eeg with generalized slow activity grade 3
HP:0011208.def: Generalized slowing of EEG activity at frequencies between 0.5-3 Hz.
synonym: eeg with generalised slow activity grade 3
eeg with generalised slow activity grade 3

name: eeg with generalized slow activity grade 4
eeg with generalized slow activity grade 4
synonym: eeg with generalised slow activity grade 4
eeg with generalised slow activity grade 4

name: eeg with occipital slowing
eeg with occipital slow
HP:0011210.def: Slowing in occipital areas of the scalp EEG.

name: eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade i
eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade i
HP:0011211.def: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital regions during photic stimulation.

name: eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade ii
eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade ii
HP:0011212.def: Occurence of epileptiform discharges in occipital and central regions during photic stimulation.

name: eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade iii
eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade iii
HP:0011213.def: Occurrence of epileptiform discharges in occipital, central, temporal and parietal regions during photic stimulation.

name: eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade iv
eeg with photoparoxysmal response grade iv
HP:0011214.def: Occurrence of generalized epileptiform discharges during photic stimulation.

name: abnormal shape of the occiput
abnormal shape of the occiput
synonym: abnormal shape of the back of the head
abnormal shape of the back of the head
abnormal shape of the back of the skull
abnormal shape of the back of the skull

name: abnormal shape of the frontal region
abnormal shape of the frontal region
HP:0011218.def: An abnormal shape of the frontal part of the head.
synonym: abnormal morphology of the frontal region
abnormal morphology of the frontal region

name: short face
short face
HP:0011219.def: Facial height (length) is more than two standard deviations below the mean (objective); or an apparent decrease in the height (length) of the face (subjective).

name: prominent forehead
prominent forehead
HP:0011220.def: Forward prominence of the entire forehead, due to protrusion of the frontal bone.

name: vertical forehead creases
vertical forehead crease
HP:0011221.def: Vertical soft tissue creases in the midline of the forehead, often extending from the hairline to the brow, and seen with facial expression or when the face is at rest.

name: depressed glabella
depressed glabella
HP:0011222.def: Posterior positioning of the glabella, i.e., of the midline forehead between the supraorbital ridges.

name: metopic depression
metopic depression
HP:0011223.def: Linear vertical groove in the midline of the forehead, extending from hairline to glabella.

name: epiblepharon
epiblepharon
HP:0011225.def: Redundant eyelid skin pressing the eyelashes against the cornea and/or conjunctiva.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the eyelid
aplasia / hypoplasia of the eyelid
HP:0011226.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the eyelid.

name: elevated circulating c - reactive protein concentration
elevate circulate c - reactive protein concentration
HP:0011227.def: An abnormal elevation of the C-reactive protein level in the blood circulation.

name: horizontal eyebrow
horizontal eyebrow
HP:0011228.def: An eyebrow that extends straight across the brow, without curve.

name: broad eyebrow
broad eyebrow
HP:0011229.def: Regional increase in the width (height) of the eyebrow.

name: laterally extended eyebrow
laterally extend eyebrow
HP:0011230.def: An eyebrow that extends laterally beyond the orbital rim rather than turning gently downward at that location.

name: prominent eyelashes
prominent eyelash
HP:0011231.def: Eyelashes that draw the attention of the viewer due to increased density and/or length and/or curl without meeting the criteria of trichomegaly.

name: infra - orbital fold
infra - orbital fold
HP:0011232.def: Elevated ridge(s) of skin starting well below the medial aspect of the lower lid that curves gradually upward toward and/or across the nasal bridge.

name: antihelical shelf
antihelical shelf
HP:0011233.def: Antihelix protrusion directed more anteriorly than laterally, forming a shelf overlying the posterior concha.

name: absent antihelix
absent antihelix
HP:0011234.def: No discernible ridge between concha and triangular fossa and helix.

name: additional crus of antihelix
additional crus of antihelix
HP:0011235.def: Supernumerary ridge or crus of the ear arising from the antihelix.

name: angulated antihelix
angulate antihelix
HP:0011236.def: Antihelical ridge that forms an acute angle between the antitragus and its bifurcation (stem) instead of a gently curving arc.

name: broad inferior crus of antihelix
broad inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011237.def: Increased width of the inferred cross-section of the inferior crus.

name: prominent inferior crus of antihelix
prominent inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011238.def: Increased protrusion of the inferior crus relative to the prominence of the antihelix stem.

name: underdeveloped inferior crus of antihelix
underdeveloped inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011239.def: Decreased protrusion of the inferior crus relative to the prominence of the antihelix stem.

name: prominent stem of antihelix
prominent stem of antihelix
HP:0011240.def: Increased protrusion of the antihelical ridge, proximal to its bifurcation, relative to the prominence of the helix.

name: serpiginous stem of antihelix
serpiginous stem of antihelix
HP:0011241.def: Posterior curving of the antihelix from its origin at the antitragus, traveling initially almost perpendicular to the descending helix and obscuring some of the concha.

name: underdeveloped stem of antihelix
underdeveloped stem of antihelix
HP:0011242.def: Decreased protrusion of the antihelical ridge, proximal to its bifurcation, relative to the prominence of a normal helix.

name: abnormality of inferior crus of antihelix
abnormality of inferior crus of antihelix
HP:0011243.def: An abnormality of the inferior crus of the antihelix is the lower cartilaginous ridge arising at the bifurcation of the antihelix that ends beneath the fold of the ascending helix, and separates the concha from the triangular fossa.
synonym: abnormality of anterior crus of antihelix
abnormality of anterior crus of antihelix

name: abnormality of stem of antihelix
abnormality of stem of antihelix
HP:0011244.def: An abnormality of the stem of the antihelix, which is the part below the bifurcation of the antihelix into the inferior and superior crura.

name: abnormality of superior crus of antihelix
abnormality of superior crus of antihelix
HP:0011245.def: An abnormality of the superior crus of the antihelix is the upper cartilaginous ridge arising at the bifurcation of the antihelix that ends beneath the fold of the ascending helix, and separates the concha from the triangular fossa.
synonym: abnormality of posterior crus of antihelix
abnormality of posterior crus of antihelix

name: underdeveloped superior crus of antihelix
underdeveloped superior crus of antihelix
HP:0011246.def: Decreased protrusion of the superior crus relative to the prominence of a normal antihelix stem.

name: prominent superior crus of antihelix
prominent superior crus of antihelix
HP:0011247.def: Increased protrusion of the superior crus relative to the prominence of a normal antihelix stem.

name: everted antitragus
evert antitragus
HP:0011248.def: Positioning of the antitragus at an angle perpendicular to the plane of the ear (oriented away from the plane of the ear).

name: absent antitragus
absent antitragus
HP:0011249.def: Absence of the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.

name: bifid antitragus
bifid antitragus
HP:0011250.def: Double rather than single peak of the antitragus.

name: underdeveloped antitragus
underdeveloped antitragus
HP:0011251.def: Reduction in the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.

name: cryptotia
cryptotia
HP:0011252.def: Invagination of the superior part of the auricle under a fold of temporal skin.

name: type i cryptotia
type i cryptotia
HP:0011253.def: A type of cryptotia associated with reduction in size of the antihelix and superior crus.

name: type ii cryptotia
type ii cryptotia
HP:0011254.def: A type of cryptotia associated with reduction in size of the antihelix and inferior crus that are affected.

name: absent crus of helix
absent crus of helix
HP:0011255.def: Continuum between the tragus and ascending helix, without any evidence of a posterior extension (crus) towards the concha.

name: crus of helix connected to antihelix
crus of helix connect to antihelix
HP:0011256.def: Extension of the ridge of the crus helix across the ear and connection of the crus to the antihelix.

name: serpiginous crus of helix
serpiginous crus of helix
HP:0011257.def: Curving course of the crus of the helix, approaching or joining the antitragus.

name: tragal bridge of crus of helix
tragal bridge of crus of helix
HP:0011258.def: The anterior origin of the crus encompasses the superior margin of the tragus, the crus overrides the upper portion of the conchal cavum and ends at the antihelix.

name: expanded terminal portion of crus of helix
expand terminal portion of crus of helix
HP:0011259.def: Widening, rather than tapering, of the crus at its posterior border near the antihelix.

name: darwin notch of helix
darwin notch of helix
HP:0011260.def: Small defect of the helical fold that lies at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix.

name: darwin tubercle of helix
darwin tubercle of helix
HP:0011261.def: Small expansion of the helical fold at the junction of the superior and descending portions of the helix.

name: crimped helix
crimped helix
HP:0011262.def: Linear, circumferential indentation in the convexity of the outer surface of the helix.

name: forward facing earlobe
forward face earlobe
HP:0011263.def: Positioning of the anterior surface of the ear lobe in a more coronal plane than the remainder of the ear.

name: discontinuous ascending root of helix
discontinuous ascend root of helix
HP:0011264.def: Interruption between the ascending helix and the crus helix, allowing the ascending helix to be attached directly to the mastoid.

name: cleft earlobe
cleft earlobe
HP:0011265.def: Discontinuity in the convexity of the inferior margin of the lobe.

name: microtia , first degree
microtia , first degree
HP:0011266.def: Presence of all the normal ear components and the median longitudinal length more than two standard deviations below the mean.

name: microtia , third degree
microtia , third degree
HP:0011267.def: Presence of some auricular structures, but none of these structures conform to recognized ear components.

name: absent tragus
absent tragus
HP:0011268.def: Lack of convexity or prominence of the contour of the ridge between the bottom of the incisura and the confluence of the ascending helix and crus helix.

name: bifid tragus
bifid tragus
HP:0011269.def: Increased height of the tragal ridge with a shallow indentation at the apex, giving the appearance of a double peak.

name: duplicated tragus
duplicate tragus
HP:0011270.def: A complete or partial duplication of the tragus; expected to lie anterior to the normal tragus.

name: prominent tragus
prominent tragus
HP:0011271.def: Increase posterolateral protrusion of the tragus.

name: underdeveloped tragus
underdeveloped tragus
HP:0011272.def: Decreased posterolateral protrusion of the tragus.

name: anisocytosis
anisocytosis
HP:0011273.def: Abnormally increased variability in the size of erythrocytes.
synonym: unequal size of red blood cells
unequal size of red blood cell

name: recurrent mycobacterial infections
recurrent mycobacterial infection
HP:0011274.def: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of mycobacterial infection.

name: recurrent mycobacterium avium complex infections
recurrent mycobacterium avium complex infection
HP:0011275.def: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial avium complex infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of mycobacterial infection.

name: abnormality of the urinary system physiology
abnormality of the urinary system physiology
intrapulmonary sequestration
intrapulmonary sequestration
HP:0011278.def: A type of pulmonary sequestration that occurs within the visceral pleura of normal lung tissue, usually without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.

name: abnormality of urine bicarbonate level
abnormality of urine bicarbonate level
HP:0011279.def: An abnormal amount of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.

name: abnormality of urine calcium concentration
abnormality of urine calcium concentration
HP:0011280.def: An abnormality of calcium concentration in the urine.

name: abnormality of urine catecholamine level
abnormality of urine catecholamine level
HP:0011281.def: An abnormal amount of urinary catecholamine concentration.

name: abnormal hindbrain morphology
abnormal hindbrain morphology
HP:0011282.def: An abnormality of the hindbrain, also known as the rhombencephalon.

name: abnormal metencephalon morphology
abnormal metencephalon morphology
HP:0011283.def: An abnormality of the metencephalon. The metencephalon is the part of the hindbrain that consists of the pons and the cerebellum.

name: short - segment aganglionic megacolon
short - segment aganglionic megacolon
HP:0011284.def: A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment does not extend beyond the upper sigmoid.

name: long - segment aganglionic megacolon
long - segment aganglionic megacolon
HP:0011285.def: A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment extends proximal to the sigmoid.

name: total colonic aganglionosis
total colonic aganglionosis
HP:0011286.def: A type of aganglionic megacolon in which the aganglionic segment comprises the entire colon.

name: eeg with occipital sharp slow waves
eeg with occipital sharp slow wave
HP:0011287.def: EEG with sharp slow waves in the occipital region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with parietal sharp slow waves
eeg with parietal sharp slow wave
HP:0011288.def: EEG with sharp slow waves in the parietal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with temporal sharp slow waves
eeg with temporal sharp slow wave
HP:0011289.def: EEG with sharp slow waves in the temporal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with frontal sharp slow waves
eeg with frontal sharp slow wave
HP:0011290.def: EEG with sharp slow waves in the frontal region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with central sharp slow waves
eeg with central sharp slow wave
HP:0011291.def: EEG with sharp slow waves in the central region. Sharp slow waves are focal sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec followed by a slow wave.

name: eeg with occipital sharp waves
eeg with occipital sharp wave
HP:0011292.def: EEG with sharp waves in the occipital region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

name: eeg with central sharp waves
eeg with central sharp wave
HP:0011293.def: EEG with sharp waves in the central region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

name: eeg with frontal sharp waves
eeg with frontal sharp wave
HP:0011294.def: EEG with sharp waves in the frontal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

name: eeg with parietal sharp waves
eeg with parietal sharp wave
HP:0011295.def: EEG with sharp waves in the parietal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

name: eeg with temporal sharp waves
eeg with temporal sharp wave
HP:0011296.def: EEG with sharp waves in the temporal region, i.e., sharp transient waves of a duration between 80 and 200 msec.

name: abnormal digit morphology
abnormal digit morphology
HP:0011297.def: A morphological abnormality of a digit, i.e., of a finger or toe.

name: prominent digit pad
prominent digit pad
HP:0011298.def: A soft tissue prominence of the ventral aspects of the fingertips or toe tips.

name: partial absence of finger
partial absence of finger
HP:0011299.def: The absence of a phalangeal segment of a finger.

name: broad fingertip
broad fingertip
HP:0011300.def: Increased width of the distal segment of a finger.

name: absent foot
absent foot
HP:0011301.def: The total absence of the foot, with no bony elements distal to the tibia or fibula.

name: long palm
long palm
HP:0011302.def: For children from birth to 16 years of age the length of the palm is more than the 97th centile; or, the length of the palm appears relatively long compared to the finger length or the limb length.

name: convex contour of sole
convex contour of sole
HP:0011303.def: The contour of the foot in lateral profile has a convex shape.

name: broad thumb
broad thumb
HP:0011304.def: Increased thumb width without increased dorso-ventral dimension.

name: partial absence of toe
partial absence of toe
HP:0011305.def: The absence of a phalangeal segment of a toe or hallux.

name: splayed toes
splay toe
HP:0011307.def: Divergence of digits along the anteroposterior axis (in the plane of the sole).

name: slender toe
slender toe
HP:0011308.def: Toes that are disproportionately narrow (reduced girth) for the hand/foot size or build of the individual.

name: tapered toe
taper toe
HP:0011309.def: The gradual reduction in girth of the toe from proximal to distal.

name: bridged palmar crease
bridge palmar crease
HP:0011310.def: A crease that connects the proximal and distal transverse palmar creases.

name: sydney crease
sydney crease
HP:0011311.def: Extension of the proximal transverse crease (five finger crease) to the ulnar edge of the palm.

name: fused nails
fuse nail
HP:0011312.def: A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation with partially separated nails, each with a separate lateral radius of curvature.

name: abnormal long bone morphology
abnormal long bone morphology

unicoronal synostosis

leave unicoronal synostosis
HP:0011316.def: Synostosis affecting only the left coronal suture.

right unicoronal synostosis
HP:0011317.def: Unicoronal synostosis affecting only the right coronal suture.

name: bicoronal synostosis
bicoronal synostosis

bilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011319.def: Premature synostosis of both lambdoid sutures.

name: unilambdoid synostosis
unilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011320.def: Premature synostosis of only one lambdoid suture.

leave unilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011321.def: Premature synostosis of only the left lambdoid suture.

name: right unilambdoid synostosis
right unilambdoid synostosis
HP:0011322.def: Premature synostosis of only the right lambdoid suture.

name: cleft of chin
cleft of chin
HP:0011323.def: Incomplete fusion of the chin, resulting from a developmental defect and manifesting as a midline cleft or fissure of the chin.

name: multiple suture craniosynostosis
multiple suture craniosynostosis
HP:0011324.def: Craniosynostosis involving at least 2 cranial sutures, where the exact pattern of sutures fused has not been precisely specified.

name: anterior plagiocephaly
anterior plagiocephaly
HP:0011326.def: Asymmetry of the anterior part of the skull.

name: posterior plagiocephaly
posterior plagiocephaly
HP:0011327.def: Asymmetry of the posterior part of the skull.

name: abnormality of cranial sutures
abnormality of cranial suture
HP:0011329.def: Any anomaly of a cranial suture, that is one of the six membrane-covered openings in the incompletely ossified skull of the fetus or newborn infant.

name: metopic synostosis
metopic synostosis
HP:0011330.def: Premature fusion of the metopic suture.

name: hemifacial atrophy
hemifacial atrophy
HP:0011331.def: Unilateral atrophy of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.
synonym: atrophy of one side of the face
atrophy of one side of the face

name: hemifacial hypoplasia
hemifacial hypoplasia
HP:0011332.def: Unilateral underdevelopment of the facial tissues, including muscles and bones.

shrinking of one side of the face

hypoplasia of depressor angula oris muscle

name: frontal hirsutism
frontal hirsutism
HP:0011335.def: Excessive amount of hair growth on forehead.

name: bitemporal forceps marks
bitemporal forceps mark
HP:0011336.def: Bilateral temporal scarlike defects, which are said to resemble forceps marks.
synonym: congenital ectodermal dysplasia of the face
congenital ectodermal dysplasia of the face

name: abnormality of mouth shape
abnormality of mouth shape
HP:0011338.def: An abnormality of the outline, configuration, or contour of the mouth.

name: abnormality of upper lip vermillion
abnormality of upper lip vermillion
HP:0011339.def: An abnormality of the vermilion border, the sharp demarcation between the lip (red colored) and the adjacent normal skin.

incomplete cleft of the upper lip
HP:0011340.def: A subtle unilateral cleft of the upper lip, which may appear as a small indentation.

long upper lip

name: mild global developmental delay
mild global developmental delay

moderate global developmental delay

name: severe global developmental delay
severe global developmental delay

name: moderate expressive language delay
moderate expressive language delay
HP:0011345.def: A moderate delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

name: mild expressive language delay
mild expressive language delay
HP:0011346.def: A mild delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

name: abnormality of ocular abduction
abnormality of ocular abduction
HP:0011347.def: An abnormality involving the movement of the eye outwards.

name: abnormal sixth cranial nerve morphology
abnormal sixth cranial nerve morphology
HP:0011348.def: Any structural abnormality of the abducens nerve.
synonym: abnormality of the sixth cranial nerve
abnormality of the sixth cranial nerve

name: mild receptive language delay
mild receptive language delay
HP:0011350.def: A mild delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

name: moderate receptive language delay
moderate receptive language delay
HP:0011351.def: A moderate delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

name: severe receptive language delay
severe receptive language delay
HP:0011352.def: A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to understand the speech of others.

name: arterial intimal fibrosis
arterial intimal fibrosis
HP:0011353.def: Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries.

name: generalized abnormality of skin
generalize abnormality of skin
HP:0011354.def: An abnormality of the skin that is not localized to any one particular region.

name: localized skin lesion
localize skin lesion
HP:0011355.def: A lesion of the skin that is located in a specific region rather than being generalized.

name: regional abnormality of skin
regional abnormality of skin
HP:0011356.def: An abnormality of the skin that is restricted to a particular body region.

name: dry hair
dry hair
HP:0011359.def: Hair that lacks the lustre (shine or gleam) of normal hair.

name: acquired abnormal hair pattern
acquire abnormal hair pattern
HP:0011360.def: An abnormality of the distribution of hair growth that is acquired during the course of life.

name: congenital abnormal hair pattern
congenital abnormal hair pattern
HP:0011361.def: A congenital abnormality of the distribution of hair growth.

name: abnormality of hair growth rate
abnormality of hair growth rate
HP:0011363.def: Hair whose growth rate deviates from the norm.

abnormality of pace of hair growth
abnormality of speed of hair growth
abnormality of speed of hair growth

name: patchy hypopigmentation of hair
patchy hypopigmentation of hair
HP:0011365.def: Reduced pigmentation of hair in patches.

name: epidermal thickening
epidermal thickening
HP:0011368.def: Thickening of the epidermal layer of the skin.

name: mongolian blue spot
mongolian blue spot
HP:0011369.def: Congenital deep dermal melanosis in the sacral area.

name: recurrent cutaneous fungal infections
recurrent cutaneous fungal infection
HP:0011370.def: Increased susceptibility to cutaneous fungal infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of cutaneous fungal infections.

name: recurrent viral skin infections
recurrent viral skin infection
HP:0011371.def: Increased susceptibility to viral skin infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral skin infections.

name: aplasia of the inner ear
aplasia of the inner ear
HP:0011372.def: Absence of the inner ear due to a developmental defect.

name: incomplete partition of the cochlea
incomplete partition of the cochlea
HP:0011373.def: Incomplete formation of the cochlear partition. The scala vestibuli and scala tympani separated by the cochlear partition, except in the apical turn where the two scalae are in continuity via the helicotrema.

name: incomplete partition of the cochlea type i
incomplete partition of the cochlea type i
HP:0011374.def: Incomplete partition I is also known as cystic cochleovestibular malformation, where the cochlea has no bony modiolus, resulting in an empty cystic cochlea. This is accompanied by a dilated cystic vestibule with developmental arrest at the fifth week of gestation.

name: cochlear aplasia
cochlear aplasia
HP:0011375.def: Absence of the cochlea, a spiral shaped cavity in the inner ear, owing to a developmental defect.

name: abnormal morphology of the vestibule of the inner ear
abnormal morphology of the vestibule of the inner ear
HP:0011376.def: A morphological abnormality of the vestibule, the central part of the osseous labyrinth that is situated medial to the tympanic cavity, behind the cochlea, and in front of the semicircular canals.
synonym: morphological abnormality of the vestibule of the inner ear
morphological abnormality of the vestibule of the inner ear

name: aplasia of the vestibule
aplasia of the vestibule
HP:0011377.def: Complete absence of the vestibule of the inner ear.

name: hypoplasia of the vestibule of the inner ear
hypoplasia of the vestibule of the inner ear
HP:0011378.def: Underdevelopment of the vestibule of the inner ear.

name: dilated vestibule of the inner ear
dilate vestibule of the inner ear
HP:0011379.def: Dilatation of the vestibule of the inner ear.

name: abnormal semicircular canal morphology
abnormal semicircular canal morphology
HP:0011380.def: An abnormality of the morphology of the semicircular canal.
synonym: morphological abnormality of the semicircular canal
morphological abnormality of the semicircular canal

name: enlarged semicircular canal
enlarge semicircular canal
HP:0011383.def: Increased size of the semicircular canal.

name: abnormality of the internal auditory canal
abnormality of the internal auditory canal
HP:0011384.def: An abnormality of the Internal acoustic meatus, i.e., of the canal in the petrous part of the temporal bone through which the cranial nerve VII and cranial nerve VIII traverse.
synonym: abnormality of the internal acoustic meatus
abnormality of the internal acoustic meatus

name: absent internal auditory canal
absent internal auditory canal
HP:0011385.def: Aplasia of the internal auditory canal.

name: narrow internal auditory canal
narrow internal auditory canal
HP:0011386.def: Reduction in diameter of the internal auditory canal.

name: enlarged vestibular aqueduct
enlarge vestibular aqueduct
HP:0011387.def: Increased size of the vestibular aqueduct.

name: enlarged cochlear aqueduct
enlarge cochlear aqueduct
HP:0011388.def: Increased size of the cochlear duct, i.e., of a duct that communicates between the perilymphatic space and the subarachnoid space, and transmits a vein from the cochlea to join the internal jugular.

name: functional abnormality of the inner ear
functional abnormality of the inner ear
HP:0011389.def: An abnormality of the function of the inner ear.
synonym: functional abnormality of the inner ear
functional abnormality of the inner ear

name: abnormal inner ear morphology
abnormal inner ear morphology
HP:0011390.def: A structural anomaly of the internal part of the ear.
synonym: morphological abnormality of the inner ear
morphological abnormality of the inner ear

name: abnormal inner ear nerve morphology
abnormal inner ear nerve morphology
synonym: morphological abnormality of the nerves of the inner ear
morphological abnormality of the nerve of the inner ear

name: aplasia of the vestibular nerve .
aplasia of the vestibular nerve .
synonym: aplasia of the eighth cranial nerve
aplasia of the eighth cranial nerve

name: hypoplasia of the vestibular nerve
hypoplasia of the vestibular nerve
synonym: hypoplasia of the eighth cranial nerve
hypoplasia of the eighth cranial nerve

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the cochlea
aplasia / hypoplasia of the cochlea
HP:0011395.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the cochlea, a spiral shaped cavity in the inner ear, owing to a developmental defect.

name: abnormality of the cochlear nerve
abnormality of the cochlear nerve
HP:0011396.def: Any anomaly of the cohclear nerve, which is the part of the vestibulocochlear nerve that is responsible for transmitting auditory signals from the inner ear to the cochlear nuclei within the brainstem and ultimately to the primary auditory cortex within the temporal lobe.

name: abnormality of the dorsal column of the spinal cord
abnormality of the dorsal column of the spinal cord
HP:0011397.def: An abnormality of the dorsal columns, i.e., of the dorsal portion of the gray substance of the spinal cord. The dorsal column consists of the fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus cuneatus and itself is part of the dorsal funiculus.

name: tibialis anterior muscle atrophy
tibialis anterior muscle atrophy
HP:0011399.def: Wasting of the tibialis anterior muscle.

name: abnormal cns myelination
abnormal cns myelination
HP:0011400.def: An abnormality of myelination of nerves in the central nervous system.

name: delayed peripheral myelination
delay peripheral myelination
HP:0011401.def: Delayed myelination in the peripheral nervous system.

name: abnormal umbilical cord blood vessel morphology
abnormal umbilical cord blood vessel morphology
lethal short - trunk short stature
lethal short - trunk short stature
HP:0011404.def: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs that is lethal at birth.

name: childhood onset short - limb short stature
childhood onset short - limb short stature
synonym: short - limb dwarfism identifiable during childhood
short - limb dwarfism identifiable during childhood

name: infancy onset short - trunk short stature
infancy onset short - trunk short stature
HP:0011406.def: A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs with onset in infancy.
synonym: short - trunk dwarfism , identifiable in infancy
short - trunk dwarfism , identifiable in infancy

name: moderate intrauterine growth retardation
moderate intrauterine growth retardation
HP:0011408.def: Intrauterine growth retardation that is at least 3 standard deviations (SD) below average, but not as low as 4 SD, corrected for sex and gestational age.

name: abnormal placental membrane morphology
abnormal placental membrane morphology
HP:0011409.def: Structural anomaly of the fetal membranes (also known as the amniochorionic or placental membranes), which comprise a vital intrauterine compartment, where they perform mechanical, immune, and endocrine functions to promote growth of the fetus and protection from environmental adversity. Amniochorionic membranes anatomically consist of a single layer of cuboidal amnion epithelial cells, chorionic trophoblasts, and scattered fibroblasts connected by a layer of type IV collagen-rich extracellular matrix.

name: caesarian section
caesarian section
HP:0011410.def: Delivery of a fetus through surgical incisions made through the abdominal wall (laparotomy) and the uterine wall (hysterotomy).

name: ventouse delivery
ventouse delivery
HP:0011412.def: Delivery of newborn by means of a ventouse, a vacuum device used to assist the delivery of a baby when the second stage of labour has not progressed adequately.

name: shoulder dystocia
shoulder dystocia
HP:0011413.def: Shoulder dystocia occurs when the fetal anterior shoulder impacts against the maternal symphysis following delivery of the vertex.

name: hydropic placenta
hydropic placenta
HP:0011414.def: An abnormality of the placenta in which there are numerous cystic spaces within the placenta as well as placental enlargement.

name: long umbilical cord
long umbilical cord
HP:0011417.def: Increased length of the umbilical cord.

name: abnormal insertion of umbilical cord
abnormal insertion of umbilical cord
HP:0011418.def: Anomalous location of the insertion of umbilical cord in the placenta. Normally, the insertion is at least two centimers distant from the edge of the placenta.

name: placental abruption
placental abruption
HP:0011419.def: Separation of the placenta from the uterus wall before delivery.

name: age of death
age of death
HP:0011420.def: The age group when the cessation of life happens.

name: death in adolescence
death in adolescence
HP:0011421.def: Death during adolescence, the period between childhood and adulthood (roughly between the ages of 10 and 19 years).

name: abnormal blood chloride concentration
abnormal blood chloride concentration
HP:0011422.def: An abnormality of chloride homeostasis or concentration in the body.

name: hyperchloremia
hyperchloremia
HP:0011423.def: An abnormally increased chloride concentration in the blood.

name: increased serum zinc
increase serum zinc
HP:0011424.def: An increased consentration of zinc in the blood.

name: fetal ultrasound soft marker
fetal ultrasound soft marker
HP:0011425.def: An finding upon obstetric ultrasound examination performed at around 16 to 20 weeks of gestation that is abnormal but not clearly identifiable as a fetal anatomic malformation or growth restriction. Such findings are known as soft markers since they are associated with increased risk for fetal aneuploidy or other disorders.

name: fetal choroid plexus cysts
fetal choroid plexus cyst
HP:0011426.def: Fetal choroid plexus cysts (CPCs) are sonographically discrete, small cysts found in the choroid plexus within the lateral cerebral ventricles of the developing fetus at 14 to 24 weeks gestation. Imaging of the choroid plexus is performed in the transverse plane of the fetal head at the same level that the lateral cerebral ventricle is evaluated. The choroid plexus should be inspected bilaterally for the presence of cysts. The size of CPCs is not of clinical relevance (PMID:16100637).

name: enlarged fetal cisterna magna
enlarge fetal cisterna magna
HP:0011427.def: The cisterna magna is measured on a transaxial view of the fetal head angled 15 degrees caudal to the canthomeatal line. The anterior/posterior diameter is taken between the inferior/posterior surface of the vermis of the cerebellum to the inner surface of the cranium. An enlarged cisternal magna is defined by an anterior/posterior diameter of 10 mm or more (PMID:16100637).

name: short fetal femur length
short fetal femur length
HP:0011428.def: A short femur length is defined as either a measurement below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or a measurement that is less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The femur should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).

name: short fetal humerus length
short fetal humerus length
HP:0011429.def: A short humerus length is defined as a length below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or as a measurement less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The humerus should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).
synonym: short fetal long bone in upper arm length
short fetal long bone in upper arm length
short foetal long bone in upper arm length
short foetal long bone in upper arm length

name: hypoplasia of fetal nasal bone
hypoplasia of fetal nasal bone
HP:0011430.def: On prenatal ultrasound, the nasal bone is a thin echogenic line within the bridge of the fetal nose. The fetus is imaged facing the transducer with the fetal face strictly in the midline. The angle of insonation is 90 degrees, with the longitudinal axis of the nasal bone as the reference line. Calibres are placed at each end of the nasal bone. Absence of the nasal bone or measurements below 2.5th percentile are considered significant (PMID:16100637).

name: fetal fifth finger clinodactyly
fetal fifth finger clinodactyly
HP:0011431.def: Fifth finger clinodactyly is defined by a hypoplastic or absent mid-phalanx of the fifth digit. Ultrasound identification of the fetal hand must first be undertaken and then appropriate magnification accomplished. The evaluation requires stretching of the 5 fingers. The diagnosis is established when the middle phalanx of the fifth finger is markedly smaller than normal or absent, which often causes the finger to be curved inward (PMID:16100637).

name: high maternal circulating alpha - fetoprotein concentration
high maternal circulating alpha - fetoprotein concentration
HP:0011432.def: Increase in the levels of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein levels during pregnancy.
synonym: high maternal serum alpha - fetoprotein mom
high maternal serum alpha - fetoprotein mom
increased maternal serum alpha - fetoprotein level
increase maternal serum alpha - fetoprotein level

name: high maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
high maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
HP:0011433.def: An abnormally high concentration of maternal serum human chorionic gonadotropin as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

name: low maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
low maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
HP:0011434.def: An abnormally low concentration of maternal serum human chorionic gonadotropin as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

name: low maternal circulating papp - a concentration
low maternal circulating papp - a concentration
HP:0011435.def: An abnormally low concentration of serum PAPP-A (pregnancy associated plasma protein A), as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

name: abnormal maternal serum screening
