abnormal maternal serum screening
HP:0011436.def: An abnormally elevated or decreased level of a maternal serum marker analytes used in screening for aneuploidy.

name: maternal autoimmune disease
maternal autoimmune disease
HP:0011437.def: A medical history of a fetus or child born to a mother with an autoimmune disease.

name: maternal teratogenic exposure
maternal teratogenic exposure
HP:0011438.def: A medical history of exposure of the mother of a child or fetus to a teratogenic substance during pregnancy.

name: alcohol - induced rhabdomyolysis
alcohol - induced rhabdomyolysis
HP:0011440.def: Rhabdomyolysis induced by intake of alcohol.

name: abnormal medulla oblongata morphology
abnormal medulla oblongata morphology
HP:0011441.def: An abnormality of the medulla oblongata, the lower half of the brainstem.

name: abnormal central motor function
abnormal central motor function
HP:0011442.def: An anomaly of the control or production of movement in the central nervous system.

name: decorticate rigidity
decorticate rigidity
HP:0011444.def: A type of rigidity in which the arms are in flexion and adduction and the legs are extended. This signifies a lesion in the cerebral white matter, internal capsules, or thalamus.

name: athetoid cerebral palsy
athetoid cerebral palsy
HP:0011445.def: A type of cerebral palsy characterized by slow, involuntary muscle movement and mixed muscle tone.

name: hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei
hyposegmentation of neutrophil nucleus
synonym: hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood
hyposegmentation of neutrophil nucleus in peripheral blood

name: ankle clonus
ankle clonus
HP:0011448.def: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Ankle clonus is tested by rapidly flexing the foot upward.

name: knee clonus
knee clonus
HP:0011449.def: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Knee clonus can be tested by rapidly pushing the patella towards the toes.

name: unusual cns infection
unusual cns infection
HP:0011450.def: A type of infection of the central nervous system that can be regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection.

name: primary microcephaly
primary microcephaly
HP:0011451.def: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender at birth.
synonym: decreased head circumference present at birth
decrease head circumference present at birth
head circumference small for gestational age
head circumference small for gestational age
small head circumference present at birth
small head circumference present at birth

name: functional abnormality of the middle ear
functional abnormality of the middle ear
HP:0011452.def: An abnormality of the function of the middle ear.
synonym: functional abnormality of the middle ear
functional abnormality of the middle ear

name: abnormality of the incus
abnormality of the incus
HP:0011453.def: An abnormality of the incus, an ossicle in the middle ear.

name: abnormality of the malleus
abnormality of the malleus
HP:0011454.def: An abnormality of the malleus, an ossicle in the middle ear.

name: loss of eyelashes
loss of eyelash
HP:0011457.def: This term refers to the loss of eyelashes that were previously present.

name: abdominal symptom
abdominal symptom
HP:0011458.def: A subjective manifestation of disease localized to the abdomen.

name: esophageal carcinoma
esophageal carcinoma
HP:0011459.def: The presence of a carcinoma of the esophagus.

name: embryonal onset
embryonal onset
HP:0011460.def: Onset of disease at up to 8 weeks following fertilization (corresponding to 10 weeks of gestation).

name: fetal onset
fetal onset
HP:0011461.def: Onset prior to birth but after 8 weeks of embryonic development (corresponding to a gestational age of 10 weeks).

name: young adult onset
young adult onset
HP:0011462.def: Onset of disease at the age of between 16 and 40 years.

name: childhood onset
childhood onset
HP:0011463.def: Onset of disease at the age of between 1 and 5 years.

name: aganglionosis of the small intestine
aganglionosis of the small intestine
HP:0011464.def: A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the small intestine.

name: duodenal aganglionosis
duodenal aganglionosis
HP:0011465.def: A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the duodenum.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the gallbladder
aplasia / hypoplasia of the gallbladder
HP:0011466.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the gallbladder.

name: absent gallbladder
absent gallbladder
HP:0011467.def: A developmental defect in which the gallbladder fails to form.

name: facial tics
facial tic
HP:0011468.def: Sudden, repetitive, nonrhythmic motor movements (spasms), involving the eyes and muscles of the face.

name: nasal regurgitation
nasal regurgitation
HP:0011469.def: Regurgitation of milk through the nose.

name: nasogastric tube feeding in infancy
nasogastric tube feeding in infancy
HP:0011470.def: Feeding problem necessitating nasogastric tube feeding.

name: gastrostomy tube feeding in infancy
gastrostomy tube feeding in infancy
HP:0011471.def: Feeding problem necessitating gastrostomy tube feeding.

name: abnormal small intestinal villus morphology
abnormal small intestinal villus morphology
synonym: abnormal shape of small intestinal villus
abnormal shape of small intestinal villus
abnormality of small intestinal villus morphology
abnormality of small intestinal villus morphology

name: villous atrophy
villous atrophy
HP:0011473.def: The enteric villi are atrophic or absent.
synonym: small intestine biopsy shows villous atrophy
small intestine biopsy show villous atrophy

name: childhood onset sensorineural hearing impairment
childhood onset sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0011474.def: Sensorineural hearing impairment with childhood onset.

name: persistent stapedial artery
persistent stapedial artery
HP:0011475.def: Persistence of the stapedial artery, which normally regresses during embryonic life.

name: profound sensorineural hearing impairment
profound sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0011476.def: Complete loss of hearing related to a sensorineural defect.

name: upbeat nystagmus
upbeat nystagmus
HP:0011477.def: In primary position, the eyes drift slowly downward and then spontaneously beat upward. Upward gaze accentuates the nystagmus. The associated oscillopsias are often very irritating, but the symptoms are usually transient.

name: true anophthalmia
true anophthalmia
HP:0011478.def: Absence of globe, optic nerve, chiasm and optic tracts. No evidence of ocular tissue on MRI scan or examination.

name: abnormal lacrimal punctum morphology
abnormal lacrimal punctum morphology
HP:0011479.def: An abnormality of the lacrimal punctum, an opening on the eyelid close to the medial canthus that drains tears from the conjunctival sac into the lacrimal duct in the same eyelid.

name: unilateral microphthalmos
unilateral microphthalmos
HP:0011480.def: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one eye.
synonym: abnormally small eyeball on one side
abnormally small eyeball on one side

name: abnormal lacrimal duct morphology
abnormal lacrimal duct morphology
HP:0011481.def: An abnormality of the lacrimal duct, a duct that drain tears from the conjunctiva, via the lacrimal puncta, into the lacrimal sac.

name: abnormal lacrimal gland morphology
abnormal lacrimal gland morphology
HP:0011482.def: Abnormality of the lacrimal gland, i.e., of the almond-shaped gland that secretes the aqueous layer of the tear film for each eye.

name: anterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
anterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
HP:0011483.def: Adhesions between the iris and the cornea.

name: posterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
posterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
HP:0011484.def: Adhesions between the iris and the lens.

name: corneolenticular adhesion
corneolenticular adhesion
HP:0011485.def: Developmental abnormality in which the lens and cornea are not separated.

name: abnormality of corneal thickness
abnormality of corneal thickness
HP:0011486.def: An abnormal anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.

name: increased corneal thickness
increase corneal thickness
HP:0011487.def: A increased anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.

name: abnormal corneal endothelium morphology
abnormal corneal endothelium morphology
HP:0011488.def: Abnormality of the corneal endothelium, that is, the single layer of cells on the inner surface of the cornea.

name: abnormal descemet membrane morphology
abnormal descemet membrane morphology
HP:0011490.def: Abnormality of Descemet's membrane, which is the basement membrane of the corneal endothelium.

name: reduced number of corneal endothelial cells
reduced number of corneal endothelial cell
HP:0011491.def: A reduction in the number of corneal endothelial cells.

name: abnormal corneal stroma morphology
abnormal corneal stroma morphology
HP:0011492.def: An abnormality of the stroma of cornea, also known as the substantia propria of cornea.

name: central opacification of the cornea
central opacification of the cornea
HP:0011493.def: Reduced transparency of the central portion of the corneal stroma.

name: generalized opacification of the cornea
generalize opacification of the cornea
HP:0011494.def: Generalized reduced transparency of the stroma of the cornea.

name: abnormal corneal epithelium morphology
abnormal corneal epithelium morphology
HP:0011495.def: Abnormality of the corneal epithelium, that is of the epithelial tissue that covers the front of the cornea.

name: corneal neovascularization
corneal neovascularization
HP:0011496.def: Ingrowth of new blood vessels into the cornea.
synonym: new blood vessel formation in cornea
new blood vessel formation in cornea

name: iris neovascularization
iris neovascularization
HP:0011497.def: New growth of vessels on the surface of the iris.
synonym: new blood vessel formation in iris
new blood vessel formation in iris

name: anterior lenticonus
anterior lenticonus
HP:0011501.def: A conical projection of the anterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.

name: posterior lenticonus
posterior lenticonus
HP:0011502.def: A conical projection of the posterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.

name: bull 's eye maculopathy
bull 's eye maculopathy
HP:0011504.def: Progressive maculopathy characterized by concentric regions of hyper- and hypo-pigmentation.

name: cystoid macular edema
cystoid macular edema
HP:0011505.def: Cystoid macular edema (CME) is any type of macular edema that involves cyst formation.

name: choroidal neovascularization
choroidal neovascularization
HP:0011506.def: Choroidal neovascularization (CNV) is the creation of new blood vessels in the choroid layer of the eye.

name: macular flecks
macular fleck
HP:0011507.def: Pale often indistinct lesions of the macula.

name: macular hole
macular hole
HP:0011508.def: A macular hole is a small break in the macula, located in the center of the retina.

name: macular hyperpigmentation
macular hyperpigmentation
HP:0011509.def: Increased amount of pigmentation in the macula lutea.

name: drusen
drusen
HP:0011510.def: Drusen (singular, 'druse') are tiny yellow or white accumulations of extracellular material (lipofuscin) that build up in Bruch's membrane of the eye.

name: macular schisis
macular schisis
HP:0011511.def: Splitting of the retina in the macular region.

name: retinal cavernous angioma
retinal cavernous angioma
HP:0011513.def: A benign tumor of the retina that appears as a grouping of blood-filled saccules within the inner retinal layers or on the surface of the optic disc. Retinal cavernous angioma are described as having a 'cluster of grapes' appearance.

name: abnormality of binocular vision
abnormality of binocular vision
HP:0011514.def: An abnormality of binocular vision, that is of the ability to synthesize the visual inputs from both eyes to a single image with perception of depth.

name: abnormal stereopsis
abnormal stereopsis
HP:0011515.def: Inability to make fine depth discriminations from parallax provided by the two eyes' different positions on the head.

name: achromatopsia
achromatopsia
HP:0011516.def: A condition where the retina contains no functional cone cells, so that in addition to the absence of color discrimination, vision in lights of normal intensity is difficult.

name: cone monochromacy
cone monochromacy
HP:0011517.def: The condition of having both rods and cones, but only a single kind of cone. Affected individuals have good pattern vision in daylight, but cannot distinguish between colors.

name: dichromacy
dichromacy
HP:0011518.def: Individuals affected by dichromacy possess only two types of cones, instead of three.

name: anomalous trichromacy
anomalous trichromacy
HP:0011519.def: Individuals with anomalous trichromacy possess three types of cones, but one of the three types of cones has an abnormal spectral sensitivity compared to normal cones.

name: deuteranomaly
deuteranomaly
HP:0011520.def: A type of anomalous trichromacy associated with abnormal M photopigment, such that the absorption spectrum is shifted toward L wavelengths. Affected individuals have difficulties distinguishing between red and green.

name: deuteranopia
deuteranopia
HP:0011521.def: Complete lack of the M photopigment, which is replaced with the L photopigment. Affected individuals tend to confuse red and green.

name: protanopia
protanopia
HP:0011522.def: Blue and green cones only; no functional red cones.

name: iris cyst
iris cyst
HP:0011523.def: An iris cyst is composed of a single cell layer of epithelium and is filled with fluid.

name: iris melanoma
iris melanoma
HP:0011524.def: Malignant tumor of melanocytes affecting the iris.

name: iris nevus
iris nevus
HP:0011525.def: A benign brown pigmented area over the iris representing proliferation of melanocyte cells in the stromal layer of the iris. An iris nevus can be flat or occasionally slightly elevated.

name: abnormality of lens shape
abnormality of lens shape
HP:0011526.def: An abnormal shape of the lens.

name: lentiglobus
lentiglobus
HP:0011527.def: Exaggerated curvature of the lens of the eye, producing an anterior or posterior spherical bulging.

name: solitary congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
solitary congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
HP:0011528.def: Sharply demarcated hyperpigmentation which is congenital found in around 3-5% of the population and of no functional significance.
synonym: single isolated congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
single isolate congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium

name: multiple bilateral congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
multiple bilateral congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
HP:0011529.def: Sharply demarcated hyperpigmentation which is congenital.

name: retinal hole
retinal hole
HP:0011530.def: A small break in the retina.

name: vitritis
vitritis
HP:0011531.def: Inflammation of the vitreous body, characterized by the presence of inflammatory cells and protein exudate in the vitreous cavity.

name: subretinal exudate
subretinal exudate
HP:0011532.def: A type of retinal exudate located in the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.

name: snowflake vitreoretinal degeneration
snowflake vitreoretinal degeneration
HP:0011533.def: The appearance of yellow/white crystalline-like (hence the name) spots in the retina and thickening of the peripheral part of the vitreous.

name: abnormal spatial orientation of the cardiac segments
abnormal spatial orientation of the cardiac segment
HP:0011534.def: Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the cardiac segments to other components of the heart.

name: abnormal atrial arrangement
abnormal atrial arrangement
HP:0011535.def: Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the atria to other components of the heart.

name: right atrial isomerism
right atrial isomerism
HP:0011536.def: Right atrial isomerism is characterized by bilateral triangular, morphologically right atrial, appendages, both joining the atrial chamber along a broad front with internal terminal crest.

name: left atrial isomerism
leave atrial isomerism
HP:0011537.def: In left atrial isomerism there is a bilateral small finger-shaped morphologically left atrial appendage joining the atrial chamber along a narrow front without an internal terminal crest.

name: atrial situs inversus
atrial situs inversus
HP:0011538.def: Mirror image atrial arrangement, with morphologic right atrium on the left hand side and morphologic left atrium on the right hand side.

name: atrial situs ambiguous
atrial situs ambiguous
HP:0011539.def: Common atrium without defining morphologic features.

name: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
congenitally correct transposition of the great artery
HP:0011540.def: The essence of the lesion is the combination of discordant atrioventricular and ventriculo-arterial connections. Thus, the morphologically right atrium is connected to a morphologically left ventricle across the mitral valve, with the left ventricle then connected to the pulmonary trunk. The morphologically left atrium is connected to the morphologically right ventricle across the tricuspid valve, with the morphologically right ventricle connected to the aorta.

name: criss - cross atrioventricular valves
criss - cross atrioventricular valve
HP:0011541.def: Crossing of the inflow streams of the two ventricles, due to an apparent twisting of the heart about its long axis.

name: criss - cross atrioventricular valves with superior - inferior ventricles
criss - cross atrioventricular valve with superior - inferior ventricle
HP:0011542.def: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with a rare cardiac malformation characterized by the two ventricles lying one above the other instead of side by side.

name: superior - inferior ventricles without criss - cross atrioventricular valves
superior - inferior ventricle without criss - cross atrioventricular valve
l - looping of the right ventricle
l - looping of the right ventricle
abnormal connection of the cardiac segments
abnormal connection of the cardiac segment
HP:0011545.def: A deviance in the normal connections between two cardiac segements.
synonym: abnormal connexion of the cardiac segments
abnormal connexion of the cardiac segment
discordant connection of the cardiac segments
discordant connection of the cardiac segment

name: abnormal atrioventricular connection
abnormal atrioventricular connection
HP:0011546.def: An abnormality of the circulatory connection between atria and ventricles.

name: absent left sided atrioventricular connection
absent leave sided atrioventricular connection
HP:0011547.def: A defect where there is no connection between the left atrium and left ventricle.

name: absent right sided atrioventricular connection
absent right side atrioventricular connection
HP:0011548.def: A defect where there is no connection between the right atrium and right ventricle.

name: univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connection
univentricular heart with absent left side atrioventricular connection
synonym: univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connexion
univentricular heart with absent left side atrioventricular connexion

name: biventricular heart with straddling right sided atrioventricular valve and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
biventricular heart with straddle right side atrioventricular valve and absent leave sided atrioventricular connection
right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
right side atrium to leave ventricle and absent leave sided atrioventricular connection
synonym: right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connexion
right side atrium to leave ventricle and absent leave sided atrioventricular connexion

name: ambiguous atrioventricular connection
ambiguous atrioventricular connection
HP:0011552.def: With left or right cardiac isomerism in a biventricular, the atrioventricular connections are perforce ambiguous, in that one of the connections is concordant (e.g., right-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic right ventricle) and one of the connections is discordant (e.g., left-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic left ventricle).

name: discordant atrioventricular connection
discordant atrioventricular connection
HP:0011553.def: Connection of the right atrium to the left ventricle and of the left atrium to the right ventricle in a biventricular heart.

name: double inlet atrioventricular connection
double inlet atrioventricular connection
HP:0011554.def: The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve.

name: double inlet left ventricle
double inlet leave ventricle
HP:0011555.def: The condition in which both atria are joined to the left ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually there is a hypoplastic right ventricle, which may be on the opposite side of the heart as usual.

name: double inlet right ventricle
double inlet right ventricle
HP:0011556.def: The condition in which both atria are joined to the right ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually, the left ventricle is hypoplastic.

name: double inlet to single ventricle of indeterminate morphology
double inlet to single ventricle of indeterminate morphology
HP:0011557.def: The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. The morphology of this ventricle does not allow one to determine if it corresponds to the left or right ventricle.

name: double inlet to single ventricle with common atrioventricular orifice
double inlet to single ventricle with common atrioventricular orifice
double inlet to single ventricle with two atrioventricular valves
double inlet to single ventricle with two atrioventricular valve
mitral atresia
mitral atresia
HP:0011560.def: A congenital defect with failure to open of the mitral valve orifice.

name: overriding atrioventricular valve
override atrioventricular valve
HP:0011561.def: An atrioventricular valve that empties into both ventricles. The valve overrides the interventricular septum above a ventricular septum defect.

name: straddling atrioventricular valve
straddle atrioventricular valve
HP:0011562.def: Anomalous insertion of the chordae tendinae or papillary muscles into the contralateral ventricle in the presence of a ventricular septum defect.

name: abnormal ventriculoarterial connection
abnormal ventriculoarterial connection
HP:0011563.def: An abnormality of the circulatory connection between the ventricles and the pulmonary artery and aorta.

name: mitral valve arcade
mitral valve arcade
HP:0011564.def: Anomalous mitral valve arcade is diagnosed based on the following features (1) An adequately sized mitral valve orifice; (2) short, thick, and poorly differentiated chordae with direct union of the papillary muscles to the anterior leaflet; (3) narrow or nearly nonexistent spaces between the abnormal chordae; and (4) greater differentiation of the chordae attached to the posterior papillary muscle.

name: common atrium
common atrium
HP:0011565.def: Complete absence of the interatrial septum with common atrioventricular valve and two atrioventricular connections.

name: cor triatriatum dexter
cor triatriatum dexter
HP:0011566.def: A congenital anomaly with partitioning of the right atrium to form a triatrial heart caused by persistence of the right valve of the sinus venosus. Typically, the right atrial partition is due to exaggerated fetal eustachian and thebesian valves, which together form an incomplete septum across the lower part of the atrium. This septum may range from a reticulum to a substantial sheet of tissue.

name: sinus venosus atrial septal defect
sinus venosus atrial septal defect
HP:0011567.def: An interatrial communication caused by a deficiency of the common wall between the superior vena cava (SVC) and the right-sided pulmonary veins. SVASD is commonly associated with anomalous pulmonary venous connection (APVC) of some or all of the pulmonary veins, which produces additional left-to-right shunting.

name: double orifice mitral valve
double orifice mitral valve
HP:0011568.def: The left atrio-ventricular connection consists of two anatomically distinct orifices separated by accessory fibrous tissue.

name: cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet
cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet
HP:0011569.def: Cleft in the anterior mitral valve leaflet not associated with an atrioventricular canal defect.

name: parachute mitral valve
parachute mitral valve
HP:0011571.def: Abnormality of the mitral valve apparatus, whereby chordae attach to a single papillary muscle or hypoplastic papillary muscles.

name: supramitral ring
supramitral ring
HP:0011572.def: A congenital stenotic mitral valvular anomaly with a ring of tissue above the mitral valve.

name: hypoplastic tricuspid valve
hypoplastic tricuspid valve
HP:0011573.def: Congenital defect characterized by underdevelopment of the tricuspid valve.

name: imperforate atrioventricular valve
imperforate atrioventricular valve
HP:0011574.def: An atrioventricular valve that has failed to open (atretic).

name: imperforate tricuspid valve
imperforate tricuspid valve
HP:0011575.def: A tricuspid valve that has failed to open.

name: intermediate atrioventricular canal defect
intermediate atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0011576.def: A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and inlet ventricular defect. There is one valve annulus and two valve orifices.

name: partial atrioventricular canal defect
partial atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0011577.def: A specific combination of heart defects including a primum atrial septal defect and cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet. There is not an inlet ventricular septal defect present. There are two valve annuluses and two valve orifices.

name: transitional atrioventricular canal defect
transitional atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0011578.def: A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and an inlet ventricular septal defect. There are two valve annuli and two valve orifices.

name: unbalanced atrioventricular canal defect
unbalanced atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0011579.def: Anatomic features of unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) include varying amounts of ventricular hypoplasia, as well as malalignment of the atrioventricular junction. In complete AVSD, the common AV valve can be situated either equally over the right and left ventricles (balanced) or unequally over the ventricles (unbalanced).

name: short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve
short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve
HP:0011580.def: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve.

name: double outlet left ventricle
double outlet leave ventricle
HP:0011581.def: A congenital defect of heart development characterized by origin of both pulmonary artery and aorta from the morphological left ventricle.

name: abdominal ectopia cordis
abdominal ectopia cordis
HP:0011582.def: Displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and into the abdomen.

name: cervical ectopia cordis
cervical ectopia cordis
HP:0011583.def: A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region and without a defect of the sternum.

name: thoracocervical ectopia cordis
thoracocervical ectopia cordis
HP:0011584.def: A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region with a defect of the superior portion of the sternum.

name: thoracic ectopia cordis
thoracic ectopia cordis
HP:0011585.def: Congenital malformation of the thoracic wall with partial or total displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity. This feature is associated with sternal cleft or absence of the sternum.

name: thoracoabdominal ectopia cordis
thoracoabdominal ectopia cordis
HP:0011586.def: Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and displacement partially into the abdominal cavity.

name: abnormal branching pattern of the aortic arch
abnormal branch pattern of the aortic arch
HP:0011587.def: A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries.

name: cervical aortic arch
cervical aortic arch
HP:0011588.def: The aortic arch extends into the soft tissues of the neck before turning down into to become the descending aorta.

name: common origin of the right brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery
common origin of the right brachiocephalic artery and leave common carotid artery
HP:0011589.def: The left common carotid artery has a common origin with the innominate artery.

name: double aortic arch
double aortic arch
HP:0011590.def: A conenital abnormality of the aortic arch in which the two embryonic aortc arches form a vascular ring that surrounds the trachea or esophagus and then join to form the descending aorta. Double aortic arch can cause symptoms because of compression of the esophagus (dysphagia, cyanosis while eating) or trachea (stridor).

name: left aortic arch with cervical origin of the right subclavian artery
leave aortic arch with cervical origin of the right subclavian artery
left aortic arch with isolated subclavian artery
leave aortic arch with isolated subclavian artery
HP:0011592.def: The subclavian artery arises from ductus arteriosus. While the ductus arteriosus is patent its blood supply comes from the ductus, hence from the pulmonary artery. After it closes, the blood supply is retrogradely from the vertebral artery via the circle of Willis.

name: left aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of kommerell
leave aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of kommerell
HP:0011593.def: A patent ductus arteriosus or ductal ligament completes the ring.

name: right aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of kommerell
right aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of kommerell
HP:0011594.def: Aortic arch crosses the right mainstem bronchus. The left carotid artery is the first branch, right carotid artery the second branch and right subclavian artery as the third branch.

name: left aortic arch with retroesophageal right subclavian artery
leave aortic arch with retroesophageal right subclavian artery
HP:0011595.def: Aortic arch crosses the left mainstem bronchus. The first branch is the right carotid artery, the second branch is the left carotid artery, the third branch is the subclavian artery, the fourth branch is the right subclavian artery arising from the posteromedial aspect of the distal aortic arch and continuing posterior to the esophagus to the right hand side of the body.

name: left aortic arch with right descending aorta and right ductus arteriosus
leave aortic arch with right descend aorta and right ductus arteriosus
HP:0011596.def: The ring may be completed by the ductal ligament.

name: right aortic arch with left descending aorta and left ductus arteriosus
right aortic arch with left descend aorta and leave ductus arteriosus
right aortic arch with retroesophageal left subclavian artery
right aortic arch with retroesophageal leave subclavian artery
synonym: right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery
right aortic arch with aberrant leave subclavian artery
right aortic arch with anomalous left subclavian artery
right aortic arch with anomalous left subclavian artery

name: mesocardia
mesocardia
HP:0011599.def: Mesocardia is an abnormal location of the heart in which the heart is in a midline position and the longitudinal axis of the heart lies in the mid-sagittal plane.

name: abnormal direction of ventricular apex
abnormal direction of ventricular apex
HP:0011600.def: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex. Left sided is normal.

name: rightward direction of ventricular apex
rightward direction of ventricular apex
HP:0011601.def: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex towards the right. Left sided is normal.

name: midline direction of ventricular apex
midline direction of ventricular apex
HP:0011602.def: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex in the midline. Left sided is normal.

name: congenital malformation of the great arteries
congenital malformation of the great artery
HP:0011603.def: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the aorta and pulmonary arteries.

name: aortopulmonary window
aortopulmonary window
HP:0011604.def: A congenital anomaly with an abnormal connection between the aorta and the main pulmonary artery resulting in an aortopulmonary shunt.

name: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with ventricular septal defect
congenitally correct transposition of the great artery with ventricular septal defect
HP:0011605.def: A congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with a ventricular septal defect: a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The ventricular septal defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.

name: obsolete transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum
obsolete transposition of the great artery with intact ventricular septum
obsolete transposition of the great arteries with ventricular septal defect
obsolete transposition of the great artery with ventricular septal defect
type ii truncus arteriosus
type ii truncus arteriosus
HP:0011608.def: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with each pulmonary artery arising separate from each other on the posterior or lateral aspect of the truncus.

name: type iii truncus arteriosus
type iii truncus arteriosus
HP:0011609.def: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby one of the two pulmonary artery branched does not arise from the common pulmonary trunk, but instead from the ductus arteriosus or directly from the aorta.

name: type iv truncus arteriosus
type iv truncus arteriosus
HP:0011610.def: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby the aortic arch is hypoplastic or interrupted, and a large patent ductus arteriosus is present.

name: interrupted aortic arch
interrupt aortic arch
HP:0011611.def: Non-continuity of the arch of aorta with an atretic point or absent segment.

name: interrupted aortic arch type a
interrupt aortic arch type a
HP:0011612.def: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment at the level of the isthmus.

name: interrupted aortic arch type b
interrupt aortic arch type b
HP:0011613.def: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the left carotid and subclavian arteries.

name: interrupted aortic arch type c
interrupt aortic arch type c
HP:0011614.def: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the innominate and left carotid arteries.

name: abnormal pulmonary situs morphology
abnormal pulmonary situs morphology
HP:0011615.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, which is defined by characteristics such as the number of lobes per lung and the relationship of the pulmonary arteries to their bronchi.

name: pulmonary situs inversus
pulmonary situs inversus
HP:0011616.def: Mirror image arrangement of the mainstem bronchi with the right pulmonary artery posterior to the right upper lobe bronchus and the left pulmonary artery anterior to the left upper lobe bronchus.

name: pulmonary situs ambiguus
pulmonary situs ambiguus
HP:0011617.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which the morphology of both left and right lungs is the same.

name: pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic right lungs
pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic right lung
HP:0011618.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a right lung.

name: pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic left lungs
pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic leave lung
HP:0011619.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a left lung.

name: abnormality of abdominal situs
abnormality of abdominal situs
HP:0011620.def: An abnormality of the abdominal situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the abdomen and its organs.

name: gerbode ventricular septal defect
gerbode ventricular septal defect
HP:0011621.def: A type of ventricular septal defect communicating directly between the left ventricle and right atrium. This is anatomically possible because the normal tricuspid valve is more apically displaced than the mitral valve.

name: inlet ventricular septal defect
inlet ventricular septal defect
HP:0011622.def: A ventricular septal defect that involves the inlet of the right ventricular septum immediately inferior to the AV valve apparatus.
synonym: atrioventricular canal type ventricular septal defect
atrioventricular canal type ventricular septal defect

name: muscular ventricular septal defect
muscular ventricular septal defect
HP:0011623.def: The trabecular septum is the largest part of the interventricular septum. It extends from the membranous septum to the apex and superiorly to the infundibular septum. A defect in the trabecular septum is called muscular VSD if the defect is completely rimmed by muscle.

name: apical muscular ventricular septal defect
apical muscular ventricular septal defect
HP:0011624.def: A muscular ventricular septal defect located at the apex of the heart.

name: multiple muscular ventricular septal defects
multiple muscular ventricular septal defect
HP:0011625.def: A type of muscular ventricular septal defect characterized by the presence of multiple small defects in the ventricular septum.

name: scimitar anomaly
scimitar anomaly
HP:0011626.def: Right pulmonary venous return to the inferior vena cava.

name: aorto - ventricular tunnel
aorto - ventricular tunnel
HP:0011627.def: Aorto-ventricular tunnel is a congenital, extracardiac channel which connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the left, or (less commonly) right ventricle.

name: congenital defect of the pericardium
congenital defect of the pericardium
HP:0011628.def: A developmental defect of the pericardium with congenital onset.

name: total absence of the pericardium
total absence of the pericardium
HP:0011629.def: No pericardium around the heart, occurring as a congenital defect, not the result of a surgical pericardectomy.

name: complete diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
complete diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
HP:0011630.def: No pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

name: complete right sided absence of pericardium
complete right side absence of pericardium
HP:0011631.def: No pericardium is present on the righthand side of the heart. It is a congenital absence of pericardium rather than the result of a pericardectomy.

name: partial right sided absence of pericardium
partial right side absence of pericardium
HP:0011632.def: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the righthand side of the heart.

name: complete left sided absence of pericardium
complete leave sided absence of pericardium
HP:0011633.def: A congenital anomaly with complete lack of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.
synonym: absent lining around of left side of heart
absent line around of left side of heart

name: partial left sided absence of pericardium
partial leave sided absence of pericardium
HP:0011634.def: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.

name: partial diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
partial diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
HP:0011635.def: Lack of a part of the pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

name: abnormal coronary artery origin
abnormal coronary artery origin
HP:0011636.def: Isolated abnormalities of the coronary artery origins. This may be in associated with other structural heart malformations but not the patterns of complex structural heart malformations which result in abnormal course of the coronary arteries.

name: anomalous origin of coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
anomalous origin of coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
HP:0011637.def: A coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta.

name: anomalous origin of left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
anomalous origin of left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
HP:0011638.def: Left main coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the left cusp of the aortic valve.
synonym: anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
anomalous leave coronary artery from the pulmonary artery

name: anomalous origin of right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
anomalous origin of right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
HP:0011639.def: Right coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the right cusp of the aortic valve.

name: single coronary artery origin
single coronary artery origin
HP:0011640.def: The presence of a single coronary artery ostium from which both coronary arteries arise.

name: coronary artery fistula
coronary artery fistula
HP:0011641.def: A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and a heart chamber or another blood vessel.

name: abnormal coronary sinus morphology
abnormal coronary sinus morphology
HP:0011642.def: An abnormality of the coronary sinus, which is formed by the union of the great cardiac vein and the left marginal vein and terminates in the right atrium. The coronary sinus functions to o collect deoxygenated blood from the myocardium of the heart and drain it into the right atrium.

name: coronary sinus atrial septal defect
coronary sinus atrial septal defect
HP:0011643.def: An atrial septal defect characterized by a deficiency in the tissue separating the coronary sinus from the left atrium (LA). This results in partial or complete unroofing of the coronary sinus leading to a predominantly left-to-right shunt through the coronary sinus (LA to coronary sinus to right atrium [RA]). The orifice of the ostium is frequently large because of the increased flow. From the RA side, the defect is located at the level of the coronary sinus ostium and may also include some deficiency in atrial tissue around the ostium. From the LA side, the size can be variable depending on the degree of unroofing of the coronary sinus.

name: coronary sinus diverticulum
coronary sinus diverticulum
HP:0011644.def: A venous pouch within the left ventricular wall, with a neck opening into the coronary sinus.

name: dilatation of the sinus of valsalva
dilatation of the sinus of valsalva
HP:0011645.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation of one of the anatomic dilations of the ascending aorta, which occurs just above the aortic valve.

name: juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta
juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta
HP:0011646.def: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized at the insertion of the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the juxtaductal region of aortic arch.

name: postductal coarctation of the aorta
postductal coarctation of the aorta
HP:0011647.def: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized distal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the postductal region of aortic arch.

name: patent ductus arteriosus after birth at term
patent ductus arteriosus after birth at term
HP:0011648.def: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus in postnatal life when birth was at 37 completed weeks of gestation or greater.

name: patent ductus arteriosus after premature birth
patent ductus arteriosus after premature birth
HP:0011649.def: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus when birth was at less than 37 weeks completed gestation.

name: bilateral ductus arteriosus
bilateral ductus arteriosus
HP:0011650.def: The presence of both a left and a right ductus arteriosus.

name: double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with doubly commit ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011651.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with doubly committed vsd and pulmonary stenosis
dorv with doubly commit vsd and pulmonary stenosis

name: double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with doubly commit ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011652.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventritricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: double outlet right ventricle , doubly committed ventricular septal defect
double outlet right ventricle , doubly commit ventricular septal defect

name: double outlet right ventricle with non - committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with non - committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011653.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, and also has a pulmonary stenosis; abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with non - committed vsd and pulmonary stenosis
dorv with non - commit vsd and pulmonary stenosis

name: double outlet right ventricle with non - committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with non - committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011654.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, but there is not accompanying pulmonary stenosis; the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with non - committed vsd without pulmonary stenosis
dorv with non - committed vsd without pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle , noncommitted ventricular septal defect
double outlet right ventricle , noncommitted ventricular septal defect

name: double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011655.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with subaortic vsd and pulmonary stenosis
dorv with subaortic vsd and pulmonary stenosis

name: double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011656.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with subaortic vsd without pulmonary stenosis
dorv with subaortic vsd without pulmonary stenosis

name: double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011657.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with subpulmonary vsd and pulmonary stenosis
dorv with subpulmonary vsd and pulmonary stenosis

name: double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011658.def: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
synonym: dorv with subpulmonary vsd without pulmonary stenosis
dorv with subpulmonary vsd without pulmonary stenosis

name: tetralogy of fallot with absent pulmonary valve
tetralogy of fallot with absent pulmonary valve
HP:0011659.def: Features of tetralogy of Fallot with either rudimentary ridges or the complete absence of pulmonic valve tissue.
synonym: tetralogy of fallot with absent pulmonary valve syndrome
tetralogy of fallot with absent pulmonary valve syndrome

name: anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from ascend aorta
HP:0011660.def: Anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from the ascending aorta with the contralateral pulmonary artery arising from the right ventricle.

name: anomalous origin of left pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
anomalous origin of left pulmonary artery from ascend aorta
HP:0011661.def: The left pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

name: tricuspid atresia
tricuspid atresia
HP:0011662.def: Failure to develop of the tricuspid valve and thus lack of the normal connection between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

name: right ventricular cardiomyopathy
right ventricular cardiomyopathy
HP:0011663.def: Right ventricular dysfunction (global or regional) with functional and morphological right ventricular abnormalities, with or without left ventricular disease.

name: left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
leave ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
HP:0011664.def: Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) is characterized by prominent left ventricular trabeculae and deep inter-trabecular recesses. The myocardial wall is often thickened with a thin, compacted epicardial layer and a thickened endocardial layer. In some patients, LVNC is associated with left ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction, which can be transient in neonates.

name: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
takotsubo cardiomyopathy
HP:0011665.def: Transient left ventricular apical ballooning syndrome or takotsubo cardiomyopathy is characterized by transient regional systolic dysfunction involving the left ventricular apex and/or mid-ventricle in the absence of obstructive coronary disease on coronary angiography. Patients present with an abrupt onset of angina-like chest pain, and have diffuse T-wave inversion, sometimes preceded by ST-segment elevation, and mild cardiac enzyme elevation.

name: absent right superior vena cava
absent right superior vena cava
HP:0011666.def: Absence of the right superior vena cava (RSVC). An absent RSVC is always associated with a persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC). During normal fetal development, the left-sided anterior venous cardinal system regresses, leaving the coronary sinus (CS) and the ligament of Marshall. Failure of the closure of the left anterior cardinal vein results in PLSVC. In general, PLSVC is associated with the right superior vena cava (RSVC) and drains into the RA via a dilated CS. When developmental arrest occurs at an earlier stage, the CS is absent and the PLSVC drains into the left atrium.

name: bilateral superior vena cava with bridging vein
bilateral superior vena cava with bridging vein
bilateral superior vena cava with no bridging vein
bilateral superior vena cava with no bridging vein
left superior vena cava draining directly to the left atrium
leave superior vena cava drain directly to the left atrium
HP:0011669.def: A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the left atrium instead of the right atrium via the coronary sinus, resulting in a right to left sided shunt.

name: left superior vena cava draining to coronary sinus
leave superior vena cava drain to coronary sinus
HP:0011670.def: A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the right atrium via the coronary sinus. This is the case in 80-92% of cases of PLSVC and results in no hemodynamic consequence.

name: interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation
interrupt inferior vena cava with azygous continuation
HP:0011671.def: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation is the result of connection failure between the right subcardinal vein and the right vitelline vein. Consequently, venous blood from the caudal part of the body reaches the heart via the azygous vein and superior vena cava.

name: cardiac myxoma
cardiac myxoma
HP:0011672.def: A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) of the heart. Cardiac myxomas consist of stellate to plump, cytologically bland mesenchymal cells set in a myxoid stroma. Cardiac myxomas are of endocardial origin and general project from the endocardium into a cardiac chamber.

name: cardiac hemangioma
cardiac hemangioma
HP:0011673.def: Abnormal proliferation of blood vessels within the cardiac cavities attached to the endocardium.

name: cardiac teratoma
cardiac teratoma
HP:0011674.def: A teratoma within the heart. Most commonly, these tumors are detected in the pericardial cavity attached to the pulmonary artery and aorta. The tumor size within the heart varies from 2 to 9 cm in diameter, and intrapericardial tumors as large as 15 cm have been reported. Intracardiac tumors arise from the atrial or ventricular wall as nodular masses protruding into the cardiac chambers. Cardiac and pericardial teratomas are easily detected in the fetus and neonate by two-dimensional echocardiography as heterogeneous and encapsulated cystic masses. Histologically, cardiac teratomas contain multiple immature elements including epithelium, neuroglial tissue, thyroid, pancreas, smooth and skeletal muscle, cartilage and bone.

name: arrhythmia
arrhythmia
HP:0011675.def: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

name: tetralogy of fallot with absent subarterial conus
tetralogy of fallot with absent subarterial conus
tetralogy of fallot with atrioventricular canal defect
tetralogy of fallot with atrioventricular canal defect
tetralogy of fallot with pulmonary atresia and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries
tetralogy of fallot with pulmonary atresia and major aortopulmonary collateral artery
HP:0011678.def: A type of tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia in which all pulmonary blood flow is derived from major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (MAPCA).

name: tetralogy of fallot with pulmonary stenosis
tetralogy of fallot with pulmonary stenosis
HP:0011679.def: The commonest form of tetralogy of Fallot characterized by pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy, without pulmonary atresia, absent pulmonary valve, atrioventricular canal defect or absent subarterial conus.

name: subarterial ventricular septal defect
subarterial ventricular septal defect
HP:0011681.def: A ventricular septal defect that lies beneath the semilunar valve(s) in the conal or outlet septum.

name: perimembranous ventricular septal defect
perimembranous ventricular septal defect
HP:0011682.def: A ventricular septal defect that is confluent with and involves the membranous septum and is bordered by an atrioventricular valve, not including the type 3 VSDs.

name: restrictive ventricular septal defect
restrictive ventricular septal defect
HP:0011683.def: Any ventricular septal defect (VSD) that is small enough to restrict flow across it such that a pressure gradient exists between the two sides of the VSD.

name: non - restrictive ventricular septal defect
non - restrictive ventricular septal defect
HP:0011684.def: Any ventricular septal defect (VSD) that does not restrict flow across it sufficiently to generate a pressure gradient between the two sides of the VSD.

name: infra - aortic superior vena cava
infra - aortic superior vena cava
HP:0011685.def: The superior vena cava passes below the aortic arch.

name: abnormal coronary artery course
abnormal coronary artery course
HP:0011686.def: An abnormal path of a coronary artery.

name: av nodal tachycardia
av nodal tachycardia
HP:0011687.def: A type of supraventricular tachycardia that originates in the atrioventricular node.

name: supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediated pathway
supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediate pathway
HP:0011688.def: Supraventricular tachycardia in which an accessory pathway connecting the atria and ventricles, apart from the AV node, participates as a necessary part of a reentrant mechanism.
synonym: supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connexion mediated pathway
supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connexion mediate pathway

name: supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connection
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connection
HP:0011689.def: Supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediated pathway that is called concealed becasue it is not seen on the ECG during sinus rhythm.
synonym: supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connexion
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connexion

name: permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia
permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia
HP:0011690.def: An incessant orthodromic tachycardia with anterograde conduction over the atrioventricular node and by retrograde conduction via an accessory pathway usually located in the posteroseptal region with slow and decremental conduction.

name: supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the left free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the left free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the right free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the right free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the septum
supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the septum
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway
cerebellar hemorrhage
cerebellar hemorrhage
HP:0011695.def: Hemorrhage into the parenchyma of the cerebellum.

name: supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the left free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the left free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the right free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the right free wall
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the septum
supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the septum
automatic atrial tachycardia
automatic atrial tachycardia
HP:0011700.def: Chronic supraventricular tachycardia predominantly seen in childhood.

name: multifocal atrial tachycardia
multifocal atrial tachycardia
HP:0011701.def: Multifocal atrial tachycardia is a rare supraventricular arrhythmia in neonates and young infants that is characterized by multiple P waves with varying P wave morphology and is usually asymptomatic.

name: abnormal electrophysiology of sinoatrial node origin
abnormal electrophysiology of sinoatrial node origin
HP:0011702.def: An abnormality of the sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium. THe SA node acts as the pacemaker of the heart.

name: sinus tachycardia
sinus tachycardia
HP:0011703.def: Heart rate of greater than 100 beats per minute.

name: sick sinus syndrome
sick sinus syndrome
HP:0011704.def: An abnormality involving the generation of the action potential by the sinus node and is characterized by an atrial rate inappropriate for physiological requirements. Manifestations include severe sinus bradycardia, sinus pauses or arrest, sinus node exit block, chronic atrial tachyarrhythmias, alternating periods of atrial bradyarrhythmias and tachyarrhythmias, and inappropriate responses of heart rate during exercise or stress.

name: first degree atrioventricular block
first degree atrioventricular block
HP:0011705.def: Delay of conduction through the atrioventricular node, which is manifested as prolongation of the PR interval in the electrocardiogram (EKG). All atrial impulses reach the ventricles.

name: second degree atrioventricular block
second degree atrioventricular block
HP:0011706.def: An intermittent atrioventricular block with failure of some atrial impulses to conduct to the ventricles, i.e., some but not all atrial impulses are conducted through the atrioventricular node and trigger ventricular contraction.

name: mobitz i atrioventricular block
mobitz i atrioventricular block
HP:0011707.def: Progressive PR interval prolongation with the subsequent occurrence of a single nonconducted P wave that results in a pause. The pause that follows the nonconducted impulse is less than fully compensatory (less than the sum of two normal sinus intervals).

name: mobitz ii atrioventricular block
mobitz ii atrioventricular block
HP:0011708.def: A type of second degree atrioventricular (AV) block characterized by sudden failure to conduct an impulse through the AV node without a preceding change in the PR interval.

name: atrioventricular dissociation
atrioventricular dissociation
HP:0011709.def: Atrioventricular (AV) dissociation is present if the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers. AV dissociation can occur in the absence of a primary AV conduction disturbance.

name: bundle branch block
bundle branch block
HP:0011710.def: Block of conduction of electrical impulses along the Bundle of His or along one of its bundle branches.

name: left anterior fascicular block
leave anterior fascicular block
HP:0011711.def: Conduction block in the anterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

name: right bundle branch block
right bundle branch block
HP:0011712.def: A conduction block of the right branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a prolongation of the QRS complex (greater than 0.12 s) with delayed activation of the right ventricle and terminal delay on the EKG.

name: left bundle branch block
leave bundle branch block
HP:0011713.def: A conduction block of the left branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a generalized disturbance of QRS morphology on EKG.

name: libman - sacks lesions
libman - sack lesion
HP:0011714.def: Libman-Sacks valvular lesions are sterile fibrofibrinous vegetations that favor the left-sided heart valves and usually form on the ventricular surface of the mitral valve.

name: trifascicular block
trifascicular block
HP:0011715.def: Abnormal conduction in all three divisions of the intraventricular conducting tissue.

name: junctional ectopic tachycardia
junctional ectopic tachycardia
HP:0011716.def: Junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET) is a unique type of supraventricular arrhythmia defined by narrow QRS complex and atrioventricular (AV) dissociation or retrograde atrial conduction in a 1:1 pattern.

name: atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
HP:0011717.def: Accessory pathway-related atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) involves an abnormal electrical conduction of the accessory pathway. The accessory pathway connecting impulses between the atrium and the ventricle can be seen at any site in the AV groove.

name: abnormality of the pulmonary veins
abnormality of the pulmonary vein
HP:0011718.def: An abnormality of the pulmonary veins.

name: supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP:0011719.def: Type 1 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.
synonym: supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
total anomalous pulmonary venous connection , supracardiac
total anomalous pulmonary venous connection , supracardiac
type 1 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
type 1 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection

name: cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP:0011720.def: Type 2 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.
synonym: cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
total anomalous pulmonary venous connection , intracardiac
total anomalous pulmonary venous connection , intracardiac
type 2 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
type 2 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection

name: infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP:0011721.def: Type 3 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.
synonym: infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
type 3 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
type 3 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection

name: mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP:0011722.def: Type 4 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.
synonym: mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
total anomalous pulmonary venous connection , mixed
total anomalous pulmonary venous connection , mixed
type 4 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
type 4 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection

name: congenital malformation of the right heart
congenital malformation of the right heart
HP:0011723.def: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the right heart identifiable at birth.

name: uhl 's anomaly
uhl 's anomaly
HP:0011724.def: Uhl anomaly of the right ventricle refers to the almost complete absence of right ventricular myocardium, normal tricuspid valve, and preserved septal and left ventricular myocardium.

name: persistent fetal circulation
persistent fetal circulation
HP:0011726.def: Systemic desaturation of a liveborn baby resulting from persistent pulmonary hypertension with a patent ductus arteriosus and patent foramen ovale, such that the circulation in postnatal life follows the fetal course.

name: elbow clonus
elbow clonus
HP:0011728.def: Clonus at the elbow joint, i.e., an exaggerated phasic stretch reflex characterized by repetitive, rhythmic contractions at the elbow, generated by rapid passive stretch at the elbow joint.

name: abnormality of joint mobility
abnormality of joint mobility
HP:0011729.def: An abnormality in the range and ease of motion of joints across their normal range.

name: abnormal central sensory function
abnormal central sensory function
HP:0011730.def: An abnormality of sensation related to CNS function. Assuming the primary sensory modalities are intact and the patient is alert and cooperative, the presence of an abnormality of sensory function may indicate a lesion of a parietal cortex, the thalamocortical projections to the parietal cortex, or the spinal cord.

name: abnormality of circulating cortisol level
abnormality of circulate cortisol level
HP:0011731.def: An abnormality of the concentration of cortisol in the blood.

name: abnormal adrenal morphology
abnormal adrenal morphology
HP:0011732.def: Any structural anomaly of the adrenal glands.

name: abnormality of adrenal physiology
abnormality of adrenal physiology
HP:0011733.def: A functional abnormality of the adrenal glands.

name: central adrenal insufficiency
central adrenal insufficiency
HP:0011734.def: A form of adrenal insufficiency related to a lack of ACTH, which leads to a decrease in the production of cortisol by the adrenal glands. Aldosterone production is not usually affected.

name: adrenocorticotropin deficient adrenal insufficiency
adrenocorticotropin deficient adrenal insufficiency
HP:0011735.def: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in ACTH production.

name: primary hyperaldosteronism
primary hyperaldosteronism
HP:0011736.def: A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by a defect within the adrenal gland.

name: corticotropin - releasing hormone deficient adrenal insufficiency
corticotropin - release hormone deficient adrenal insufficiency
HP:0011737.def: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in corticotropin-releasing hormone production.

name: corticotropin - releasing hormone receptor defect
corticotropin - release hormone receptor defect
HP:0011738.def: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor.
synonym: corticotropin - releasing hormone receptor ( crhr ) resistance
corticotropin - release hormone receptor ( crhr ) resistance

name: dexamethasone - suppressible primary hyperaldosteronism
dexamethasone - suppressible primary hyperaldosteronism
HP:0011739.def: A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone can be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone.

name: glucocortocoid - insensitive primary hyperaldosteronism
glucocortocoid - insensitive primary hyperaldosteronism
HP:0011740.def: A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone cannot be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone or similar glucocorticoids.

name: secondary hyperaldosteronism
secondary hyperaldosteronism
HP:0011741.def: A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by abnormally increased renin levels.

name: ectopic adrenal gland
ectopic adrenal gland
HP:0011742.def: Abnormal anatomical location of the adrenal gland.

name: adrenal gland agenesis
adrenal gland agenesis
HP:0011743.def: Absent development of the adrenal gland.

name: secondary hypercortisolism
secondary hypercortisolism
HP:0011744.def: Hypercortisolemia associated with a overproduction of ACTH (often from a tumor), leading secondarily to overproduction of cortisol.

name: non - secretory adrenocortical adenoma
non - secretory adrenocortical adenoma
HP:0011745.def: An hormonally inactive adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that does not secrete excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.

name: secretory adrenocortical adenoma
secretory adrenocortical adenoma
HP:0011746.def: An hormonally active adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that secretes excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.

name: abnormality of the anterior pituitary
abnormality of the anterior pituitary
HP:0011747.def: An abnormality of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

name: adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency
adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency
HP:0011748.def: A reduced ability to secrete adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), a hormone that stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete of glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

name: adrenocorticotropic hormone excess
adrenocorticotropic hormone excess
HP:0011749.def: Overproduction of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), which generally leads secondarily to overproduction of cortisol by the adrenal cortex.

name: neoplasm of the anterior pituitary
neoplasm of the anterior pituitary
HP:0011750.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

name: abnormal posterior pituitary morphogenesis
abnormal posterior pituitary morphogenesis
HP:0011751.def: An abnormality of the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.

name: neoplasm of the posterior pituitary
neoplasm of the posterior pituitary
HP:0011752.def: The presence of a neoplasm (tumor) in the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.

name: posterior pituitary dysgenesis
posterior pituitary dysgenesis
HP:0011753.def: Abnormal development of the neurohypophysis during embryonic growth and development.

name: pituicytoma
pituicytoma
HP:0011754.def: A solid, low grade, spindle cell, glial neoplasm of adults that originates in the neurohypophysis or infundibulum. Clinical signs and symptoms include visual disturbance, headache and features of hypopituitarism. Pituicytomas are well-circumscribed, solid masses that can measure up to several centimeters. Histologically, they show a compact architecture consisting of elongate, bipolar spindle cells arranged in interlacing fascicles or assuming a storiform pattern.

name: ectopic posterior pituitary
ectopic posterior pituitary
HP:0011755.def: An abnormal anatomical location of the posterior lobe of the hypophysis, also known as the neurohypophysis. The posterior pituitary is normally present in the dorsal portion of the sella turcica, but when ectopic is usually near the median eminence. This defect is likely to be due to abnormal migration during embryogenesis.

name: posterior pituitary agenesis
posterior pituitary agenesis
HP:0011756.def: Absence of the neurohypophysis owing to a developmental defect.

name: pituitary gonadotropic cell adenoma
pituitary gonadotropic cell adenoma
HP:0011759.def: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces gonadotropins.

name: pituitary growth hormone cell adenoma
pituitary growth hormone cell adenoma
HP:0011760.def: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces growth hormone.

name: pituitary null cell adenoma
pituitary null cell adenoma
HP:0011761.def: A type of pituitary adenoma that is of unknown cellular origin and that lacks immunocytochemical or fine structural markers. Null cell adenomas are not associated with hormone excess.

name: pituitary thyrotropic cell adenoma
pituitary thyrotropic cell adenoma
HP:0011762.def: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH).

name: pituitary carcinoma
pituitary carcinoma
HP:0011763.def: A pituitary tumor with subarachnoid, brain, or systemic metastasis. The diagnosis of a pituitary carcinoma requires evidence of metastatic disease, either outside the central nervous system (CNS) or as separate noncontiguous foci within the CNS.

name: pituitary spindle cell oncocytoma
pituitary spindle cell oncocytoma
HP:0011764.def: A spindled-to-epithelioid, oncocytic, nonendocrine neoplasm of the anterior hypophysis that manifests in adults and follows a benign clinical course. Pituitary spindle cell oncocytomas are firm, fibrous, and adherent to surrounding structures and are highly vascular.

name: abnormal parathyroid morphology
abnormal parathyroid morphology
HP:0011766.def: A structural abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

name: abnormality of the parathyroid physiology
abnormality of the parathyroid physiology
HP:0011767.def: A functional abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

name: parathyroid dysgenesis
parathyroid dysgenesis
HP:0011768.def: Abnormal embryonic development of the parathyroid gland.

name: ectopic parathyroid
ectopic parathyroid
HP:0011769.def: An abnormal anatomical location of the parathyroid gland.

name: tertiary hyperparathyroidism
tertiary hyperparathyroidism
HP:0011770.def: A type of hyperparathyroidism that occurs following kidney transplantation, which is a treatment for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Although kidney transplantation leads to a normalization of serum calcium and parathyroid hormone in most patients. The state of persistent hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism is referred to as tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

name: autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
HP:0011771.def: A type of hypoparathyroidism with circulating antiparathyroid or anti-calcium sensing receptor antibodies indicative of autoimmunity.

name: abnormal thyroid morphology
abnormal thyroid morphology
HP:0011772.def: A structural abnormality of the thyroid gland.

name: uninodular goiter
uninodular goiter
HP:0011773.def: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to a singular nodule in the thyroid gland.

name: thyroid hemiagenesis
thyroid hemiagenesis
HP:0011780.def: Absence of a lobe of the thyroid gland related to a failure of its embryologic development.

name: thyroid c cell hyperplasia
thyroid c cell hyperplasia
HP:0011781.def: An abnormal growth of parafollicular (C-cells) cells.

name: thyrotoxicosis with toxic single thyroid nodule
thyrotoxicosis with toxic single thyroid nodule
central hypothyroidism
central hypothyroidism
HP:0011787.def: A type of hypothyroidism due to an insufficient stimulation of an otherwise normal thyroid gland. Central hypothyroidism is caused by either pituitary (secondary hypothyroidism) or hypothalamic (tertiary hypothyroidism) defects.

name: increased circulating free t3
