HP:0012801.def: Bigonial distance (lower facial width) more than 2 standard deviations below the mean (objective); or an apparently decreased width of the lower jaw (mandible) when viewed from the front (subjective).

name: broad jaw
broad jaw
HP:0012802.def: Bigonial distance (lower facial width) more than 2 SD above the mean (objective); or an apparently increased width of the lower jaw (mandible) when viewed from the front (subjective).

name: anisometropia
anisometropia
HP:0012803.def: Inequality of refractive power of the two eyes.

name: corneal ulceration
corneal ulceration
HP:0012804.def: Disruption of the epithelial layer of the cornea with involvement of the underlying stroma.

name: iris transillumination defect
iris transillumination defect
HP:0012805.def: Transmission of light through the iris as visualized upon slit lamp examination or infrared iris transillumination videography. The light passes through defects in the pigmentation of the iris.

name: proboscis
proboscis
HP:0012806.def: A fleshy, tube-like structure usually located in the midline of the face or just to one side of the midline.

name: high insertion of columella
high insertion of columella
HP:0012807.def: Insertion of the posterior columella superior to the nasal base.

name: abnormal nasal base norphology
abnormal nasal base norphology
HP:0012808.def: An anomaly of the nasal base, which can be conceived of as an imaginary line between the most lateral points of the external inferior attachments of the alae nasi to the face.

name: narrow nasal base
narrow nasal base
HP:0012809.def: Decreased distance between the attachments of the alae nasi to the face.
synonym: decreased width of base of nose
decrease width of base of nose

name: wide nasal base
wide nasal base
HP:0012810.def: Increased distance between the attachments of the alae nasi to the face.
synonym: increased width of base of nose
increase width of base of nose

name: wide nasal ridge
wide nasal ridge
HP:0012811.def: Increased width of the nasal ridge.
synonym: increased width of dorsum of nose
increase width of dorsum of nose

name: fullness of paranasal tissue
fullness of paranasal tissue
HP:0012812.def: Increased bulk of tissue alongside the nose. The fullness can be caused by both bony and soft tissues.
synonym: fullness of tissue around the nose
fullness of tissue around the nose

name: unilateral breast hypoplasia
unilateral breast hypoplasia
HP:0012813.def: Underdevelopment of the breast on one side only.

name: bilateral breast hypoplasia
bilateral breast hypoplasia
HP:0012814.def: Underdevelopment of the breast on both sides.

name: hypoplastic female external genitalia
hypoplastic female external genitalia
HP:0012815.def: Underdevelopment of part or all of the female external reproductive organs (which include the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, Bartholin glands, and clitoris).

name: right ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
right ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
HP:0012816.def: A predominantly right ventricular variant of isolated noncompaction cardiomyopathy.

name: noncompaction cardiomyopathy
noncompaction cardiomyopathy
HP:0012817.def: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized anatomically by deep trabeculations in the ventricular wall, which define recesses communicating with the main ventricular chamber.

name: biventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
biventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
HP:0012818.def: Noncompaction cardiomyopathy that affects both ventricles.

name: bilateral vocal cord paralysis
bilateral vocal cord paralysis
HP:0012820.def: A loss of the ability to move the vocal fold on both sides.

name: unilateral vocal cord paresis
unilateral vocal cord paresis
HP:0012821.def: Decreased strength of the vocal fold on one side.

name: bilateral vocal cord paresis
bilateral vocal cord paresis
HP:0012822.def: Decreased strength of the vocal fold on both sides.

name: clinical modifier
clinical modifier
HP:0012823.def: This subontology is designed to provide terms to characterize and specify the phenotypic abnormalities defined in the Phenotypic abnormality subontology, with respect to severity, laterality, age of onset, and other aspects.

name: severity
severity
HP:0012824.def: The intensity or degree of a manifestation.

name: mild
mild
HP:0012825.def: Having a relatively minor degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of between two and three standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

name: moderate
moderate
HP:0012826.def: Having a medium degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of between three and four standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

name: borderline
borderline
HP:0012827.def: Having a minor degree of severity that is considered to be on the boundary between the normal and the abnormal ranges. For quantitative traits, a deviation of that is less than two standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

name: severe
severe
HP:0012828.def: Having a high degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of between four and five standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

name: profound
profound
HP:0012829.def: Having an extremely high degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of more than five standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

name: position
position
HP:0012830.def: The anatomical localization of the specified phenotypic abnormality.

name: laterality
laterality
HP:0012831.def: The localization with respect to the side of the body of the specified phenotypic abnormality.

name: bilateral
bilateral
HP:0012832.def: Being present on both sides of the body.

name: unilateral
unilateral
HP:0012833.def: Being present on only the left or only the right side of the body.

name: right
right
HP:0012834.def: Being located on the right side of the body.

name: left
left
HP:0012835.def: Being located on the left side of the body.

name: spatial pattern
spatial pattern
HP:0012836.def: The pattern by which a phenotype affects one or more regions of the body.

name: generalized
generalize
HP:0012837.def: Affecting all regions without specificity of distribution.

name: localized
localize
HP:0012838.def: Being confined or restricted to a particular location.

name: distal
distal
HP:0012839.def: Localized away from the central point of the body.

name: proximal
proximal
HP:0012840.def: Localized close to the central point of the body.

name: retinal vascular tortuosity
retinal vascular tortuosity
HP:0012841.def: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the retinal blood vessels.

name: skin appendage neoplasm
skin appendage neoplasm
HP:0012842.def: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the hair follicles, sebaceous glands, or sweat glands.

name: hair follicle neoplasm
hair follicle neoplasm
HP:0012843.def: An uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation originating in a hair follicle, which is an epidermal adnexal structures responsible for hair growth.

name: trichilemmoma
trichilemmoma
HP:0012844.def: A benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

name: single trichilemmoma
single trichilemmoma
HP:0012845.def: Presence of a unitary trichilemmoma, a benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

name: multiple trichilemmomata
multiple trichilemmomata
HP:0012846.def: Presence of multiple trichilemmomata, a benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

name: epilepsia partialis continua
epilepsia partialis continuum
HP:0012847.def: Epilepsia partialis continua (also called Kojevnikov's or Kozhevnikov's epilepsia) is a type of focal motor status epilepticus characterized by repeated stereotyped simple motor manifestations such as jerks, typically of a limb or the face, recurring every few seconds or minutes for extended periods (days or years).

name: small intestinal stenosis
small intestinal stenosis
HP:0012848.def: The narrowing or partial blockage of a portion of the small intestine.

name: small intestinal dysmotility
small intestinal dysmotility
HP:0012850.def: Abnormal small intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.

name: colonic stenosis
colonic stenosis
HP:0012851.def: A narrowing of a segment of colon whereby bowel continuity is maintained.

name: hepatic bridging fibrosis
hepatic bridging fibrosis
HP:0012852.def: Hepatic fibrosis that reaches from a portal area to another portal area.

name: scrotal hypospadias
scrotal hypospadias
HP:0012853.def: Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the scrotum.

name: midshaft hypospadias
midshaft hypospadias
HP:0012854.def: Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the middle of the inferior shaft of the penis.

name: scrotal hyperpigmentation
scrotal hyperpigmentation
HP:0012855.def: Increased pigmentation (skin color) of the scrotum.

name: abnormal scrotal rugation
abnormal scrotal rugation
HP:0012856.def: Anomaly of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.

name: increased scrotal rugation
increase scrotal rugation
HP:0012857.def: Increased number or density of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.

name: decreased scrotal rugation
decrease scrotal rugation
HP:0012858.def: Decreased number or density of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.

name: esophageal leukoplakia
esophageal leukoplakia
HP:0012859.def: A white patch or plaque occurring on the surface of the esophageal mucous membranes that cannot be rubbed off and cannot be characterized clinically as any other disease.

name: testicular fibrosis
testicular fibrosis
HP:0012860.def: Formation of excess connective tissue in the testicle.

name: ovotestis
ovotestis
HP:0012861.def: A gonad that contains both ovarian follicles and testicular tubular elements.

name: abnormal germ cell morphology
abnormal germ cell morphology
HP:0012862.def: Any structural anomaly of a reproductive cell.
synonym: abnormal shape of a reproductive cell
abnormal shape of a reproductive cell

name: abnormal male germ cell morphology
abnormal male germ cell morphology
HP:0012863.def: A structural anomaly of a male reproductive cell.

name: abnormal sperm head morphology
abnormal sperm head morphology
HP:0012865.def: A structural abnormality of the sperm head.

name: abnormal sperm neck morphology
abnormal sperm neck morphology
HP:0012866.def: A structural abnormality of the sperm neck.

name: abnormal sperm mid - piece morphology
abnormal sperm mid - piece morphology
HP:0012867.def: A structural abnormality of the sperm mid-piece.

name: abnormal sperm tail morphology
abnormal sperm tail morphology
HP:0012868.def: A structural abnormality of the sperm tail.

name: acephalic spermatozoa
acephalic spermatozoon
HP:0012869.def: Spermatozoa with very small cranial ends devoid of any nuclear material, that is, lacking a typical sperm head.

name: vanishing testis
vanish testis
HP:0012870.def: A condition which is considered to be due to the subsequent atrophy and disappearance in fetal life of an initially normal testis. In the presence of spermatic cord structures is evidence of the presence of the testis in early intrauterine life. When associated with a blind-ending spermatic cord, this entity is named as his absence of a testis in an otherwise normal 46XY male is usually unilateral and is assumed to be a consequence of intrauterine or perinatal torsion or infarction.

name: varicocele
varicocele
HP:0012871.def: A varicocele is a widening of the veins along the spermatic cord, leading to enlarged, twisted veins in the scrotum, and manifested clinically by a painless testicle lump, scrotal swelling, or bulge in the scrotum.

name: abnormal vas deferens morphology
abnormal va deferens morphology
HP:0012872.def: A structural anomaly of the secretory duct of the testicle that carries spermatozoa from the epididymis to the prostatic urethra where it terminates to form ejaculatory duct.

name: absent vas deferens
absent va deferens
HP:0012873.def: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the vas deferens.
synonym: congenital absence of the vas deferens
congenital absence of the va deferens

name: abnormal male reproductive system physiology
abnormal male reproductive system physiology
HP:0012874.def: An abnormal functionality of the male genital system.

name: abnormal ejaculation
abnormal ejaculation
HP:0012875.def: Abnormality in the process of ejection of semen (usually carrying sperm) from the male reproductive tract.

name: premature ejaculation
premature ejaculation
HP:0012876.def: The emission of semen and seminal fluid during the act of preparation for sexual intercourse, i.e. before there is penetration, or shortly after penetration.

name: retrograde ejaculation
retrograde ejaculation
HP:0012877.def: The emission of semen and seminal fluid into the bladder instead of through the penis during orgasm.

name: retarded ejaculation
retard ejaculation
HP:0012878.def: Difficulty of a male in achieving orgasm.

name: abnormal labia minora morphology
abnormal labium minora morphology
HP:0012880.def: An anomaly of the labia minora, the folds of skin between the outer labia.
synonym: abnormality of the inner vaginal lips
abnormality of the inner vaginal lip

name: abnormal labia majora morphology
abnormal labium majora morphology
HP:0012881.def: An anomaly of the outer labia.

name: fallopian tube cyst
fallopian tube cyst
HP:0012883.def: A fluid filled sac located in the Fallopian tube.

name: fallopian tube torsion
fallopian tube torsion
HP:0012884.def: A twisting of the Fallopian tube. Sudden onset with sharp, colicky pelvic pain associated with nausea, vomiting, bowel, and bladder symptoms is the usual presentation.

name: fallopian tube duplication
fallopian tube duplication
HP:0012885.def: The presence of a supernumerary Fallopian tube.

name: hemorrhagic ovarian cyst
hemorrhagic ovarian cyst
HP:0012886.def: An abdominal mass formed by bleeding into a follicular ovarian cyst or corpus luteum cyst.

name: ovarian serous cystadenoma
ovarian serous cystadenoma
HP:0012887.def: A cystic tumor of the ovary, containing thin, clear, yellow serous fluid and varying amounts of solid tissue.

name: abnormal uterine cervix morphology
abnormal uterine cervix morphology
HP:0012888.def: An anomaly of the neck of the uterus (lower part of the uterus), called the uterine cervix.

name: cervical endometriosis
cervical endometriosis
HP:0012889.def: Abnormal growth of endometrial cells (which are normally limited to the uterus) within the cervix.

name: high posterior hairline
high posterior hairline
HP:0012891.def: Hair on the neck extends less inferiorly than usual.
synonym: high hairline at back of head
high hairline at back of head

name: facial muscle hypertrophy
facial muscle hypertrophy
HP:0012892.def: Hypertrophy of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

name: neck muscle hypertrophy
neck muscle hypertrophy
HP:0012893.def: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the muscles of the neck.

name: paraspinal muscle hypertrophy
paraspinal muscle hypertrophy
HP:0012894.def: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the paraspinal muscles.

name: scapular muscle hypertrophy
scapular muscle hypertrophy
HP:0012895.def: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the scapular muscles.

name: abnormal motor evoked potentials
abnormal motor evoke potential
HP:0012896.def: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs). MEPs are measured following single-pulse or repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and can be used for the assessment of the excitability of the motor cortex and the integrity of conduction along the central and peripheral motor pathways.

name: abnormal upper - limb motor evoked potentials
abnormal upper - limb motor evoke potential
HP:0012897.def: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs) in the arm.
synonym: abnormal motor evoked potentials in the upper limb
abnormal motor evoke potential in the upper limb

name: abnormal lower - limb motor evoked potentials
abnormal low - limb motor evoke potential
HP:0012898.def: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs) in the leg.
synonym: abnormal motor evoked potentials in the lower limb
abnormal motor evoke potential in the low limb

name: handgrip myotonia
handgrip myotonia
HP:0012899.def: Difficulty releasing one's grip associated with prolonged first handgrip relaxation times.

name: myotonia of the face
myotonia of the face
HP:0012900.def: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the face.

name: myotonia of the jaw
myotonia of the jaw
HP:0012901.def: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the jaw.

name: myotonia of the lower limb
myotonia of the low limb
HP:0012902.def: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the leg.

name: myotonia of the upper limb
myotonia of the upper limb
HP:0012903.def: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the arm.

name: cold - sensitive myotonia
cold - sensitive myotonia
HP:0012904.def: An involuntary and painless delay in the relaxation of skeletal muscle following contraction or electrical stimulation that is induced by exposure to cold.

name: euryblepharon
euryblepharon
HP:0012905.def: Euryblepharon is a congenital eyelid anomaly characterized by horizontal enlargement of the palpebral fissure. The eyelid is shortened vertically compared with the horizontal dimension, with associated lateral canthal malpositioning and lateral ectropion abnormally wide lid opening.

name: ciliary body coloboma
ciliary body coloboma
HP:0020006.def: A coloboma of the ciliary body.

name: diffuse
diffuse
HP:0020034.def: A spatial pattern that is spread out, i.e., not localized.

name: lower limb dysmetria
low limb dysmetria
HP:0020035.def: A lack of coordination of leg movement manifested by undershoot or overshoot of the intended position of the leg.

name: upper limb dysmetria
upper limb dysmetria
HP:0020036.def: A lack of coordination of arm movement manifested by undershoot or overshoot of the intended position of the arm.

name: astasia
astasia
HP:0020037.def: A postural abnormality characterized by the inability to stand without external support despite having sufficient muscle strength.

name: vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia
vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia
HP:0020038.def: Elongation, dilatation, and/or tortuosity of the vertebrobasilar segment. The definition of VBD includes: (i) diameter of basilar or vertebral artery over 4.5 mm; or (ii) deviation of any portion more than 10 mm from the shortest expected course; and (iii) length of basilar artery over 29.5 mm or length of intracranial vertebral artery over 23.5 mm.

name: double elevator palsy
double elevator palsy
HP:0020041.def: A type of incomitant strabismus in which both elevator muscles (i.e., the inferior oblique and superior rectus muscles) of the same eye are weak leading to restricted elevation and hypotropia.

name: double depressor palsy
double depressor palsy
HP:0020042.def: An ocular movement abnormality characterised by simultaneous weakness of the inferior rectus muscle and superior oblique muscle of the same eye.

name: vertical incomitant strabismus
vertical incomitant strabismus
HP:0020043.def: A type of incomitant strabismus in which the angle of deviation varies as the patient's gaze shifts upwards and/or downwards.

name: esodeviation
esodeviation
HP:0020045.def: A manifest or latent ocular deviation in which one or both eyes tends to deviate nasally.

name: accommodative esotropia
accommodative esotropia
HP:0020046.def: A form of esotropia (convergent deviation of the eyes) associated with activation of the accommodative reflex.

name: abnormal myeloid cell morphology
abnormal myeloid cell morphology
HP:0020047.def: Any structural anomaly of a cell of the monocyte, granulocyte, mast cell, megakaryocyte, or erythroid lineage.

name: reduced bone - marrow pro - b cell count
reduce bone - marrow pro - b cell count
HP:0020048.def: A reduction in the numbers of pro-B cells (defined by coexpression of CD34 and CD19). Earlier B-cell precursors are defined by expressing surface CD34 and cytoplasmic TdT in the absence of CD19.

name: exodeviation
exodeviation
HP:0020049.def: A manifest or latent ocular deviation in which one or both eyes tends to deviate temporally.

name: anti - granulocyte - macrophage colony stimulating factor antibody positivity
anti - granulocyte - macrophage colony stimulate factor antibody positivity
HP:0020050.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor.

name: abnormal erythrocyte physiology
abnormal erythrocyte physiology
HP:0020054.def: Any functional abnormality of erythrocytes (red-blood cells).

name: abnormal red blood cell count
abnormal red blood cell count
HP:0020058.def: Any deviation from the normal number of red blood cells per volume in the circulation.

name: increased red blood cell count
increase red blood cell count
HP:0020059.def: An abnormal elevation above the normal number of red blood cells per volume in the circulation.

name: decreased red blood cell count
decrease red blood cell count
HP:0020060.def: An abnormal reduction below the normal number of red blood cells per volume in the circulation.

name: abnormal hemoglobin concentration
abnormal hemoglobin concentration
HP:0020061.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of hemoglobin in the blood.

name: decreased hemoglobin concentration
decrease hemoglobin concentration
HP:0020062.def: An abnormal reduction below normal hemoglobin concentration in the circulation.

name: increased hemoglobin concentration
increase hemoglobin concentration
HP:0020063.def: An abnormal elevation above normal hemoglobin concentration in the circulation.

name: abnormal eosinophil count
abnormal eosinophil count
HP:0020064.def: Any deviation from the normal number of eosinophils per volume in the blood circulation.

name: viremia
viremia
HP:0020071.def: The presence of virus in the blood.

name: persistent ebv viremia
persistent ebv viremia
HP:0020072.def: Persistent presence of Epstein-Barr virus in the blood.

name: hypopigmented macule
hypopigmented macule
HP:0020073.def: A white or lighter patch of skin that may appear anywhere on the body and are caused by decreased skin pigmentation.

name: crystalluria
crystalluria
HP:0020074.def: The presence of crystals in the urine.

name: leucine crystalluria
leucine crystalluria
HP:0020075.def: The presence of leucine crystals in the urine.

name: wrist ganglion
wrist ganglion
HP:0020076.def: A benign soft tissue tumor of the wrist usually found in the dorsal aspect of the wrist and communicate with the joint via a pedicle. This pedicle usually originates not only at the scapholunate ligament, but also may arise from a number of other sites over the dorsal aspect of the wrist capsule.

name: carnitinuria
carnitinuria
HP:0020077.def: An elevated level of carnitine in the urine.

name: alaninuria
alaninuria
HP:0020078.def: An increased level of alanine in the urine.

name: beta - alaninuria
beta - alaninuria
HP:0020079.def: An increased level of beta-alanine in the urine.

name: erythrocyte inclusion bodies
erythrocyte inclusion body
HP:0020080.def: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates of substances in red blood cells.

name: pappenheimer bodies
pappenheimer body
HP:0020081.def: A type of erythrocyte inclusion characterized by basophilic stippling of erythrocytes, that is, by numerous very small coarse or fine blue granules within the cytoplasm with the additional stipulation that the stippled particles are due to iron granules (demonstrable by the Prussian blue stain).

name: heinz bodies
heinz body
HP:0020082.def: A type of erythrocyte inclusion composed of denatured hemoglobin.

name: furuncle
furuncle
HP:0020083.def: An infection of a hair follicle that extends subcutaneously, forming an abscess.

name: carbuncle
carbuncle
HP:0020084.def: A pustular lesion of the skin emerging from group of infected hair follicles, characterized by a deep location and dissecting through tissue planes. A carbuncle is larger and deeper than a furuncle.

name: infection following live vaccination
infection follow live vaccination
HP:0020085.def: An infection resulting from live attenuated vaccines (LAV), that is, a vaccine prepared from living viruses or bacteria that have been weakened under laboratory conditions. LAV vaccines will replicate in a vaccinated individual and produce an immune response but usually cause mild or no disease. are derived from disease-causing pathogens.

name: bcgitis
bcgitis
HP:0020086.def: Local or regional infection with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination.

name: bcgosis
bcgosis
HP:0020087.def: Distant, or disseminated infection with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination associated with failure to contain thebacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination leading to spread of BCG to many sites in the body. The tuberculosis vaccine BCG contains live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis.

name: post - vaccination measles
post - vaccination measles
HP:0020088.def: Infection with the measles virus of the live-attenuated vaccine. This is an extremely rare event and may indicate immunocompromise in some cases.

name: post - vaccination rubella
post - vaccination rubella
HP:0020089.def: Infection with the rubella virus of the live-attenuated vaccine.

name: post - vaccination polio
post - vaccination polio
HP:0020090.def: Infection with live attenuated polio vaccine following vaccination. This is an extreemely rare event that may indicate immunocompromise.

name: post - vaccination rotavirus infection
post - vaccination rotavirus infection
HP:0020091.def: Infection with live attenuated rotavirus vaccine following vaccination.

name: recurrent deep organ abscess formation
recurrent deep organ abscess formation
HP:0020093.def: Repeated episodes of the formation of abscesses in organs. An abscess is a circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma or an organ.

name: prolonged need of intravenous antibiotic therapy
prolonged need of intravenous antibiotic therapy
HP:0020095.def: Clinical assessment of a requirement to treat with intravenous antibiotics over an unusually prolonged period of time.

name: recurrent streptococcal infections
recurrent streptococcal infection
HP:0020096.def: Increased susceptibility to streptococcal infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of streptococcal infections.

name: infection due to encapsulated bacteria
infection due to encapsulated bacteria
HP:0020097.def: An infection by an encapsulated bacterial agent. Isolates which cause invasive disease are usually surrounded by a polysaccharide capsule, which is a major virulence factor and the key antigen in protective protein-polysaccharide conjugate vaccines.

name: severe norovirus infection
severe norovirus infection
HP:0020099.def: An unusually severe course of infection with Human norovirus, previously known as Norwalk virus. Norovirus, an RNA virus of the family Caliciviridae, is a human enteric pathogen. Norovirus infection-associated illness may also be more prolonged and severe in immunocompromised individuals and may be associated with remarkably persistent viral excretion in some of these individuals.

name: unusual fungal infection
unusual fungal infection
HP:0020100.def: An unusual fungal infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a fungal agent.

name: invasive fungal infection
invasive fungal infection
HP:0020101.def: Fungal infection characterized by invasion of host tissues.

name: pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
HP:0020102.def: An opportunistic disease caused by invasion of unicellular fungus Pneumocystis jirovecii. Transmission of P. jirovecii cysts takes place through the airborne route, and usually, its presence in lungs is asymptomatic. However, people with impaired immunity, especially those with CD4+ T cell count below 200/microliter, are still at risk of the development of Pneumocystis pneumonia due to P. jirovecii invasion. Symptoms induced by this disease are not specific: progressive dyspnoea, non-productive cough, low-grade fever, arterial partial pressure of oxygen below 65 mmHg, and chest radiographs demonstrating bilateral, interstitial shadowing.

name: invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
HP:0020103.def: Infection of the lungs with aspergillus. In the respiratory mucosa, the spores may germinate into hyphae, which in turn can invade the mucosa leading to invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

name: unusual protozoan infection
unusual protozoan infection
HP:0020104.def: An unusual protozoan infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a protozoal agent.

name: severe toxoplasmosis
severe toxoplasmosis
HP:0020105.def: Toxoplasmosis is a widespread parasitic infection that is frequently asymptomatic in immunocompetent patients. However, this obligate intracellular protozoan parasite can evade the immune system and persist for the life of its host in cyst form, predominantly in the brain, retina, and muscles. Reactivation of latent cysts may occur when the immune system fails to maintain cytokine pressure, which mainly relies on gamma interferon (IFN-gamma). Toxoplasmosis is a life-threatening infection in immunocompromised patients (ICPs).

name: severe giardiasis
severe giardiasis
HP:0020106.def: An unusually severe infection due to Giardia lamblia, also called Giardia duodenalis or Giardia intestinalis, which is a protozoan parasite of the small intestine that causes extensive morbidity worldwide.

name: unusual helminthic infection
unusual helminthic infection
HP:0020107.def: An unusual helminthic infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a worm (helminth).

name: unusual parasitic infection
unusual parasitic infection
HP:0020108.def: An unusual parasitic infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a parasite.

name: bone fracture
bone fracture
HP:0020110.def: A partial or complete breakage of the continuity of a bone.

name: abnormal cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cell proportion
abnormal cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cell proportion
HP:0020111.def: A deviation from the normal proportion of CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cells in circulation, relative to another population of cells.

name: increased proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cells
increase proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cell
HP:0020112.def: An abnormally increased proportion of CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cells in circulation, relative to another population of cells.
synonym: elevated proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cells
elevate proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cell
increased proportion of cd4+cd25+ treg cells
increase proportion of cd4+cd25+ treg cell

name: decreased proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cells
decreased proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cell
HP:0020113.def: An abnormally decreased proportion of CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cells in circulation, relative to another population of cells.
synonym: decreased proportion of cd4+cd25+ treg cells
decreased proportion of cd4+cd25+ treg cell
reduced proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cells
reduce proportion of cd4+cd25+ regulatory t cell

name: persistent human papillomavirus infection
persistent human papillomavirus infection
HP:0020114.def: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are small oncogenic viruses. HPV has been shown to cause a variety of lesions and malignancies, which predominantly affect the anogenital region. Low-risk, non-oncogenic HPV types are associated with anogenital warts and recurrent respiratory papillomatosis while high-risk, oncogenic types are associated with cervical, penile, anal, vaginal, vulvar, and oropharyngeal cancers. Infection with anogenital HPV is usually asymptomatic and resolves spontaneously without consequences in the immunocompetent host. When disease does occur, the most common manifestation is genital warts, which may be small papules, or flat, smooth or pedunculated lesions. This resolution of HPV lesions is not generally seen in the immunosuppressed, resulting in severe, persistent and extensive manifestations of HPV disease.

name: hypoplastic dermoepidermal hemidesmosomes
hypoplastic dermoepidermal hemidesmosomes
HP:0020117.def: Underdeveloped hemidesmosomes at the dermoepidermal junction. Hemidesmosomes are the specialized junctional complexes, that contribute to the attachment of epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane in stratified and other complex epithelia, such as the skin.

name: radial artery aplasia
radial artery aplasia
HP:0020118.def: Congenital absence of the radial artery.

name: abnormal retinal nerve fiber layer morphology
abnormal retinal nerve fiber layer morphology
HP:0020119.def: A structural abnormality of the retinal nerve fiber layer
synonym: abnormal retinal nerve fibre layer morphology
abnormal retinal nerve fibre layer morphology

name: retinal nerve fiber edema
retinal nerve fiber edema
HP:0020120.def: Swelling (edema) of the retinal nerve fibers.

name: conception by assisted reproductive technology
conception by assisted reproductive technology
HP:0020121.def: A history of conception by an assisted reproductive technology such as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and cryopreservation.

name: bite cells
bite cell
HP:0020122.def: Red blood cells that appear to have parts of them bitten away.

name: tympanosclerosis
tympanosclerosis
HP:0020123.def: A stiffening of the tympanic membrane due to calcification, typically presents as white plaque-like lesions, involving discrete regions of the tympanic membrane and/or middle ear.

name: spontaneous conjunctival filtering bleb
spontaneous conjunctival filter bleb
HP:0020125.def: Avascular cystic elevations of the superior conjunctiva not related to ocular surgery or trauma.

name: prostate mass
prostate mass
HP:0020126.def: A lump detected in the prostate. In this context, mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction.

name: periarticular soft - tissue mass
periarticular soft - tissue mass
HP:0020127.def: A lump detected in the region that surrounds a joint. In this context, mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction.

name: aplasia of the olfactory tract
aplasia of the olfactory tract
HP:0020128.def: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the olfactory tract, which causes anosmia, a complete loss of the sense of smell.

name: abnormal urine protein level
abnormal urine protein level
HP:0020129.def: Any deviation of the concentration of one or more proteins in the urine.

name: increased urinary neutrophil gelatinase - associated lipocalin
increase urinary neutrophil gelatinase - associate lipocalin
HP:0020130.def: An increased concentration of neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin in the urine (there is no generally accepted threshold, but some studies choose a threshold of above 150 nanogram per milliliter).

name: abnormal tubular basement membrane morphology
abnormal tubular basement membrane morphology
HP:0020131.def: Abnormal structure of the basement membrane of the renal tubulus.

name: thickening of the tubular basement membrane
thickening of the tubular basement membrane
HP:0020132.def: Increase in thickness of the basement membrane of the tubulus of the kidney.

name: podocyte hypertrophy
podocyte hypertrophy
HP:0020133.def: Increased visceral epithelial cell size, with or without cytoplasmic protein droplets.

name: increased urine neutrophil count
increase urine neutrophil count
HP:0020134.def: Abnormally increased count of neutrophils in urine.

name: myofibromatosis
myofibromatosis
HP:0020135.def: A mesenchymal neoplasm characterized by solitary or multiple nodules involving the skin, striated muscles, bones and, sometimes, viscera. It usually appears as a subcutaneous nodule, but can also appear as an ulcer, pedunculated lesion, or similar to a hemangioma. Histology shows well-circumscribed tapered cell lobes, resembling smooth muscle cells. At its center, perivascular round cells (hemangiopericitoides) are usually observed, giving a biphasic appearance.

name: anticardiolipin igg antibody positivity
anticardiolipin igg antibody positivity
HP:0020136.def: The presence of circulating IgG autoantibodies to cardiolipin.

name: anticardiolipin igm antibody positivity
anticardiolipin igm antibody positivity
HP:0020137.def: The presence of circulating IgM autoantibodies to cardiolipin.

name: history of recent animal bite
history of recent animal bite
HP:0020138.def: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to an animal.

name: history of recent insect bite
history of recent insect bite
HP:0020139.def: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to an insect.

name: history of recent tick bite
history of recent tick bite
HP:0020140.def: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to a tick.

name: blood pressure substantially higher in legs than arms
blood pressure substantially high in legs than arm
HP:0020141.def: An abnormal blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities with the blood pressure measured in the legs being much higher than the blood pressure measure in the arms. In healthy individuals, ankle systolic blood pressures are only slightly higher than the systolic blood pressure measured in the arm.
synonym: blood pressure substantially higher in lower than upper extremities
blood pressure substantially higher in low than upper extremity
blood pressure substantially lower in arms than legs
blood pressure substantially low in arm than leg
blood pressure substantially lower in upper than lower extremities
blood pressure substantially low in upper than low extremity

name: blood pressure substantially higher in arms than legs
blood pressure substantially high in arm than leg
HP:0020142.def: An abnormal blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities with the blood pressure measured in the arms being much higher than the blood pressure measure in the legs. In healthy individuals, ankle systolic blood pressures are only slightly higher than the systolic blood pressure measured in the arm.
synonym: blood pressure substantially higher in upper than lower extremities
blood pressure substantially high in upper than low extremity
increased arm - leg blood pressure gradient
increase arm - leg blood pressure gradient

name: tracheal duplication cyst
tracheal duplication cyst
HP:0020143.def: A cyst in the trachea, whose wall is made up by tissue similar to the bronchial tree, including cartilage and smooth muscle, and is lined by secretory respiratory epithelium composed of cuboid or columnar ciliated epithelium.

name: calcium phosphate crystalluria
calcium phosphate crystalluria
HP:0020144.def: The presence of calcium phosphate crystals in the urine.

name: calcium oxalate crystalluria
calcium oxalate crystalluria
HP:0020145.def: The presence of calcium oxalate crystals in the urine.

name: calcium carbonate crystalluria
calcium carbonate crystalluria
HP:0020146.def: The presence of calcium carbonate crystals in the urine.

name: 2 - methylbutyryl glycinuria
2 - methylbutyryl glycinuria
HP:0020147.def: Increased concentration of 2-methylbutyryl glycine in the urine.

name: increased circulating mead acid level
increase circulate mead acid level
HP:0020148.def: An abnormally elevated concentration od mead acid in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating succinate
elevate circulate succinate
HP:0020149.def: An increase concentration of succinate in the blood circulation.

name: elevated urinary uromodulin level
elevate urinary uromodulin level
HP:0020150.def: The concentration of uromodulin (also known as Tamm Horsfall protein) in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: elevated urinary tamm - horsfall protein concentration
elevate urinary tamm - horsfall protein concentration

name: anti - dsdna antibody positivity
anti - dsdna antibody positivity
HP:0020151.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against double-stranded DNA.

name: distal joint laxity
distal joint laxity
HP:0020152.def: Lack of stability of a distal joint (e.g., finger).

name: positive blood 1,3 beta glucan test
positive blood 1,3 beta glucan test
HP:0020153.def: Beta-1,3-glucan is a major constituent of all of the characterized fungal cell walls, making up between 30-80 percent of the mass of the wall. It is a biomarker of fungal infections such as invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

name: nevus comedonicus
nevus comedonicus
HP:0020154.def: A type of epidermal nevus characterized by closely arranged, dilated follicular openings with keratinous plugs resembling classical comedones.

name: abnormal oocyte morphology
abnormal oocyte morphology
HP:0020155.def: An abnormal structure of the female germ cell (egg cell).

name: abnormal zona pellucida morphology
abnormal zona pellucida morphology
HP:0020156.def: Abnormal structure of the oocyte extracellular matrix region known as teh zona pellucida.

name: thin zona pellucida
thin zona pellucida
HP:0020157.def: Reduced thickness of the zona pellucida.

name: increased circulating adrenic acid concentration
increase circulate adrenic acid concentration
HP:0020158.def: An increased concentration of adrenic acid (also known as cis-7,10,13,16-Docosatetraenoic acid) in the blood circulation.

name: reduced response to gonadotropin - releasing hormone stimulation test
reduce response to gonadotropin - release hormone stimulation test
HP:0020159.def: Failure of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test to induce an appropriate increased in luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels.
synonym: reduce response to gnrh stimulation test
reduce response to gnrh stimulation test

name: branch retinal artery occlusion
branch retinal artery occlusion
HP:0020161.def: Blockage of a branch of the retinal artery. This can cause loss of a section of visual field.

name: cilioretinal artery occlusion
cilioretinal artery occlusion
HP:0020163.def: Blockage of the cilioretinal artery. The central retinal artery supplies the inner retina and the surface of the optic nerve. In some individuals, the cilioretinal artery, a branch of the ciliary circulation, may supply a portion of the retina including the macula. In cilioretinal artery occlusion, vision loss results from cell death in the inner retinal layers (mainly ganglion cells) despite relative sparing of the outer layers.

name: ophthalmic artery occlusion
ophthalmic artery occlusion
HP:0020164.def: A partial or complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery (branch of the internal carotid artery) that may lead to severe ischemia of the affected globe and associated ocular tissues. It can present with a similar picture to central retinal artery occlusion; however, profound choroidal ischaemia also occurs.

name: branch retinal vein occlusion
branch retinal vein occlusion
HP:0020165.def: Blockage of a branch of the retinal vein. It may present with sudden-onset of painless vision loss or visual field defect correlating to the area of perfusion of the obstructed vessels.

name: central retinal vein occlusion
central retinal vein occlusion
HP:0020166.def: Central retinal vein occlusion is an occlusion of the main retinal vein posterior to the lamina cribrosa of the optic nerve and is typically caused by thrombosis.

name: hemiretinal vein occlusion
hemiretinal vein occlusion
HP:0020167.def: A variant of central retinal vein occlusions that involves the superior or inferior half of the retina.

name: abnormal drug response
abnormal drug response
HP:0020169.def: An anomalous response to a medication related to individual variation in metabolic or immune response to drugs varying from potentially from potentially life-threatening adverse drug reactions to alteration of therapeutic efficacy.

name: increased blood drug concentration
increase blood drug concentration
HP:0020170.def: High plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.

name: decreased blood drug concentration
decrease blood drug concentration
HP:0020171.def: Low plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.

name: adverse drug response
adverse drug response
HP:0020172.def: An unpleasant or harmful reaction resulting from treatment with a drug.

name: reduced drug efficacy
reduce drug efficacy
HP:0020173.def: Decreased response to a drug intervention in comparison to the expected response.

name: refractory drug response
refractory drug response
HP:0020174.def: Absent or significantly reduced efficacy of drug intervention characterized by lack of measurable benefit or deterioration of disease course.

name: reduced cholinesterase level
reduced cholinesterase level
HP:0020175.def: A decreased amount of cholinesterase in the blood circulation.

name: cholesterol crystalluria
cholesterol crystalluria
HP:0020176.def: The presence of cholesterol crystals in the urine.

name: abnormal proportion of cd8 - positive , alpha - beta temra t cells
abnormal proportion of cd8 - positive , alpha - beta temra t cell
HP:0020177.def: An abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta effector memory RA TEMRA T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, and CCR7-negative.
synonym: abnormal proportion of effector memory cd8 - positive , alpha - beta t cells , terminally differentiated
abnormal proportion of effector memory cd8 - positive , alpha - beta t cell , terminally differentiate

name: abnormal dendritic cell count
abnormal dendritic cell count
HP:0020178.def: A deviation from the normal count of dendritic cells in the peripheral blood circulation. Dendritic cells are of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).

name: abnormal circulating haptoglobin concentration
abnormal circulate haptoglobin concentration
HP:0020179.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation.

name: elevated haptoglobin level
elevate haptoglobin level
HP:0020180.def: An abnormally high concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation. Haptoglobin is an acute-phase reactant whose levels can become elevated in the presence of infection and inflammation.

name: reduced haptoglobin level
reduce haptoglobin level
HP:0020181.def: An abnormally low concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation. Decreased haptoglobin in conjunction with increased reticulocyte count and anemia may indicate hemolysis. Decreased haptoglobin levels can also occur in the absence of hemolysis, due to cirrhosis of the liver, disseminated ovarian carcinomatosis, pulmonary sarcoidosis, and elevated estrogen state.

name: abnormal circulating a - type atrial natriuretic peptide concentration
abnormal circulate a - type atrial natriuretic peptide concentration
HP:0020182.def: A measurable change in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.
synonym: abnormal a - type atrial natriuretic peptide level
abnormal a - type atrial natriuretic peptide level

name: increased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide concentration
increase circulate a - type natriuretic peptide concentration
HP:0020183.def: A measurable elevation in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.
synonym: increased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide level
increase circulate a - type natriuretic peptide level

name: decreased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide concentration
decrease circulate a - type natriuretic peptide concentration
HP:0020184.def: A measurable reduction in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.
synonym: decreased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide level
decrease circulate a - type natriuretic peptide level

name: superior cerebellar dysplasia
superior cerebellar dysplasia
HP:0020185.def: Abnormal morphological development of the superior part of the cerebellum.

name: multilobulated spleen
multilobulated spleen
HP:0020186.def: The fetal spleen is lobulated, and these lobules normally disappear before the birth. Lobulation of the spleen may persist into adult life and be typically seen along the medial part of the spleen. A persisting lobule results in a variation in shape of the spleen.

name: thick pachygyria
thick pachygyria
HP:0020187.def: Pachygyria with a very thick cerebral cortex measuring 10-20 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.
synonym: pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm
pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm

name: anterior predominant pachygyria with 5 - 10 mm cortical thickness
anterior predominant pachygyria with 5 - 10 mm cortical thickness
HP:0020188.def: Pachygyria with cortical thickness between 5 and 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severety gradient. The severety gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically over 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

name: posterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
posterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
HP:0020189.def: Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severety gradient. The severety gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.
synonym: pachygyria with cortical thickness over 10 mm posterior predominant
pachygyria with cortical thickness over 10 mm posterior predominant

name: perisylvian predominant thick cortex pachygyria
perisylvian predominant thick cortex pachygyria
HP:0020190.def: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and a perisylvian predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Perisylvian predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.
synonym: pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm perisylvian predominant
pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm perisylvian predominant

name: anterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
anterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
HP:0020191.def: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and an anterior predominant severity gradient. The severety gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Anterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe over the frontal and temporal lobes.
synonym: pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm anterior predominant
pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm anterior predominant

name: pachygyria with 5 - 10 mm cortical thickness
pachygyria with 5 - 10 mm cortical thickness
HP:0020192.def: Pachygyria with a mildly thickend cerebral cortex measuring 5-10 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.

name: prolonged reptilase time
prolonged reptilase time
HP:0020193.def: An abnormally increased duration of the reptilase time. Reptilase time is a functional plasma clotting assay, which is based on the enzymatic activity of batroxobin. By specifically cleaving fibrinogen A from fibrinogen, batroxobin leads to the formation of a stable fibrin clot. The time, starting from the addition of batroxobin to the plasma sample, until clot formation is the reptilase time and is given in seconds.

name: iga heavy chain paraproteinemia
iga heavy chain paraproteinemia
HP:0020194.def: An abnormal IgA heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: igg heavy chain paraproteinemia
igg heavy chain paraproteinemia
HP:0020195.def: An abnormal IgG heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: igm heavy chain paraproteinemia
igm heavy chain paraproteinemia
HP:0020196.def: An abnormal IgM heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: increased circulating arachidonic acid concentration
increase circulate arachidonic acid concentration
HP:0020197.def: An increased circulation of arachidonic acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating 18 - hydroxycorticosterone level
abnormal circulate 18 - hydroxycorticosterone level
HP:0020198.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating 18 - hydroxycortisone level
decrease circulate 18 - hydroxycortisone level
HP:0020199.def: A subnormal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating 18 - hydroxycortisone level
increase circulate 18 - hydroxycortisone level
HP:0020200.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal sarcomere morphology
abnormal sarcomere morphology
HP:0020201.def: Any structural anomaly of the sarcomere, which is unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

name: abnormal z disc morphology
abnormal z disc morphology
HP:0020202.def: Any structural anomaly of the Z disc, which is the platelike region of a muscle sarcomere to which the plus ends of actin filaments are attached.

name: z - band streaming
z - band stream
HP:0020203.def: Streaming or smearing of the Z band, which is then no longer confined to a narrow zone which bisects the I band. The Z disc may extend across the I band or the entire sarcomere in a zigzag manner. Focal thickening, smudging, and blurring of the Z band takes place concurrently. Myofibrillar disorganization is a frequent but not invariable accompanying change.

name: tubulointerstitial bacterial infiltration
tubulointerstitial bacterial infiltration
HP:0020204.def: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of bacteria identified on routine and/or special (Brown-Hopps) stains.

name: tubulointerstitial fungal infiltration
tubulointerstitial fungal infiltration
HP:0020205.def: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of yeast or hyphal-microrganisms identified on routine and/or special (PAS, silver) stains.

name: simple ear
simple ear
HP:0020206.def: The pinna has fewer folds and grooves than usual.

name: eating - induced seizure
eat - induced seizure
HP:0020208.def: A seizure precipitated by aspects of anticipating food, eating itself, or the post-prandial period.

name: hot water - induced seizure
hot water - induced seizure
HP:0020209.def: A seizure precipitated by pouring cupfuls of very hot water (40 to 50 degrees Celsius) in rapid succession over the head. Bathing in this manner is the most common trigger.

name: praxis - induced seizure
praxis - induced seizure
HP:0020210.def: A seizure precipitated by complex, cognition-guided tasks often involving visuomotor coordination and decision-making.

name: proprioceptive - induced seizure
proprioceptive - induced seizure
HP:0020211.def: A seizure precipitated by movement or a change in posture.

name: somatosensory - induced seizure
somatosensory - induced seizure
HP:0020213.def: A somatosensory reflex seizure is a seizure precipitated by somatic stimulation of a specific part of the body in the absence of startle or surprise.

name: startle - induced seizure
startle - induced seizure
HP:0020214.def: Startle-induced seizures are triggered by multiple and non-specific stimuli (auditory, somatosensory, and rarely visual) and are characterized by their sudden unexpected nature. Sudden noise rather than pure sound is the most effective acoustic stimulus.

name: thinking - induced seizure
think - induced seizure
HP:0020215.def: Seizures induced by thinking and decision-making. comment:

name: visually - induced seizure
visually - induced seizure
HP:0020216.def: Seizures evoked by visual stimuli. This includes clinical seizures induced by strobe lighting, television and other screens, flickering environmental lighting and self-induction by causing a strobe effect.

name: focal aware motor seizure
focal aware motor seizure
HP:0020217.def: A type of focal motor seizure in which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.

name: focal aware atonic seizure
focal aware atonic seizure
HP:0020218.def: A type of focal atonic seizure during which awareness is fully retained throughout.

name: motor seizure
motor seizure
HP:0020219.def: A motor seizure is a type of seizure that is characterized at onset by involvement of the skeletal musculature. The motor event could consist of an increase (positive) or decrease (negative) in muscle contraction to produce a movement.

name: focal atonic seizure
focal atonic seizure
HP:0020220.def: A focal seizure characterized at onset by sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic activity, typically lasting more than 500 ms but less than 2 seconds. It may involve the head, trunk, jaw or limb musculature.

name: clonic seizure
clonic seizure
HP:0020221.def: A clonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking, that is regularly repetitive.

name: hypohomocysteinemia
hypohomocysteinemia
HP:0020222.def: A decreased concentration of homocystine in the blood.

name: dermal sinus tract
dermal sinus tract
HP:0020223.def: A dermal sinus tract is an abnormality present at birth over the dorsal midline where an abnormal epithelialized connection from the skin tracks inwards towards the spine, most commonly seen in the lumbosacral region.

name: mammary duct ectasia
mammary duct ectasia
HP:0020224.def: A non-proliferative inflammatory disorder of the large duct (milk duct) of the breast; as such, it affects nipple and areola complex. The condition is characterized by focal dilatation of the lactiferous duct system is due to endoluminal changes, as well as the loss of duct wall elastin, leading to abnormally dilated and tortuous lactiferous ducts with associated periductal inflammation and fibrosis. Mammary duct ectasia may present with nipple discharge or palpable mass.

name: breast abscess
breast abscess
HP:0020225.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the breast.

name: nipple tenderness
nipple tenderness
HP:0020226.def: Pain or discomfort produced by touching the nipple.

name: floating gallbladder
float gallbladder
HP:0020227.def: An abnormal configuration in which the gallbladder is pedunculated, hanging free of the liver, and attached only by the cystic mesentery,

name: hallux rigidus
hallux rigidus
HP:0025004.def: Osteoarthritis of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the first toe.

name: thickening of glomerular capillary wall
thickening of glomerular capillary wall
HP:0025005.def: Widening of the wall of capillary blood vessels in the glomerulus. This feature may be produced by deposits and other changes affecting either subepithelial and subendothelial regions or the glomerular basement membrane itself.

name: abnormal glomerular capillary morphology
abnormal glomerular capillary morphology
HP:0025006.def: A structural anomaly of the capillary blood vessels in the renal glomerulus.
synonym: abnormalities of the glomerular capillary wall
abnormality of the glomerular capillary wall

name: ectopic fovea
ectopic fovea
HP:0025007.def: An abnormal anatomic position of the fovea, the small, central pit composed of closely packed cones that is located in the macula of the retina.

name: tracheal tug on inspiration
tracheal tug on inspiration
HP:0025008.def: Downward movement of the trachea during inspiration due to downward traction on the tracheobronchial tree.

name: forward slanting upper incisors
forward slant upper incisor
HP:0025009.def: The upper incisors deviate from the normal angle of being roughly parallel to the surface of the face and instead slant outwards.

name: foveal atrophy
foveal atrophy
HP:0025010.def: Partial or complete loss of foveal tissue that was once present.

name: pyriform aperture stenosis
pyriform aperture stenosis
HP:0025011.def: Narrowing of the anterior nasal aperture (piriform or pyriform aperture), which is a pear-shaped opening in the skull that forms the bony inlet of the nose.

name: status cribrosum
status cribrosum
HP:0025012.def: Diffusely widened perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia, affecting especially the corpus striatum. Status cribrosum is usually symmetrical, with the perivascular spaces showing CSF signal and without diffusion restriction. The word cribriform means sievelike, with multiple perforations.

name: decerebrate rigidity
decerebrate rigidity
HP:0025013.def: A type of rigidity that is manifested by an exaggerated extensor posture of all extremities.

name: subcutaneous spheroids
subcutaneous spheroid
HP:0025014.def: Small, hard cyst-like nodules, freely moveable in the subcutis over the bony prominences of the legs and arms, which have an outer calcified layer with a translucent core on x-ray.

name: abnormal capillary morphology
abnormal capillary morphology
HP:0025016.def: A structural anomaly of the tiny blood vessels that connect arterioles with venules and whose walls act as semipermeable membranes that mediate the diffusion of fluids and gases between the blood circulation and body tissues.

name: capillary fragility
capillary fragility
HP:0025017.def: Reduced resistance to rupture of capillary blood vessels. Capillary fragility may manifest as a bleeding diathesis with spontaneous ecchymoses (bruises).

name: abnormal capillary physiology
abnormal capillary physiology
HP:0025018.def: A functional anomaly of the tiny blood vessels that connect arterioles with venules and whose walls act as semipermeable membranes that mediate the diffusion of fluids and gases between the blood circulation and body tissues.

name: arterial rupture
arterial rupture
HP:0025019.def: Sudden breakage of an artery leading to leakage of blood from the circulation.

name: elevated prostate - specific antigen level
elevate prostate - specific antigen level
HP:0025020.def: An increased concentration of prostate specific antigen (PSA) in the circulation.

name: abnormal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
abnormal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
HP:0025021.def: A deviation from normal range of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.

name: decreased erythrocyte sedimentation rate
decrease erythrocyte sedimentation rate
HP:0025022.def: A reduced erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The ESR is a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.

name: rectal atresia
rectal atresia
HP:0025023.def: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the rectum. That is, there is an abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the rectum.

name: megarectum
megarectum
HP:0025024.def: An abnormal dilation of the rectum. There is a large filled rectum as a result of underlying innervation or muscular abnormalities, which remains after disimpaction of the rectum.

name: rectovestibular fistula
rectovestibular fistula
HP:0025025.def: A congenital malformation characterized by an abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the vulval vestibule, at the lower aspect of the vaginal opening.

name: h - type rectovestibular fistula
h - type rectovestibular fistula
HP:0025026.def: Rectovestibular fistula with a normal anus is known as H-type fistula or double termination of the alimentary tract.

name: osteoma cutis
osteoma cutis
HP:0025027.def: The term osteoma refers to the anomalous presence of ossification (bone formation) in the interior of the dermis or epidermis. The dermal or subcutaneous bone formation presents as stony hard nodules. The osteomata appear as irregular, hardened small nodules that are well circumscribed and generally of the same color as the skin.

name: abnormal enteric nervous system morphology
abnormal enteric nervous system morphology
HP:0025028.def: A structural anomaly of nerves of the enteric nervous system.
synonym: abnormality of enteric nervous system morphology
abnormality of enteric nervous system morphology

name: enteric neuronal degeneration
enteric neuronal degeneration
HP:0025030.def: Deterioration of enteric neurons with impairment of enteric neuronal structure. Typical neuropathological findings include qualitative (e.g., neuronal swelling, intranuclear inclusions, axonal degeneration) and quantitative (e.g., reduction in the number of neurons) abnormalities of the enteric neurons.

name: abnormality of digestive system physiology
abnormality of digestive system physiology
HP:0025032.def: A functional anomaly of the digestive system.

name: abnormal digestive system morphology
abnormal digestive system morphology
HP:0025033.def: A structural anomaly of the digestive system.

name: abnormal morphology of erythroid progenitor cell
abnormal morphology of erythroid progenitor cell
HP:0025034.def: Abnormal form of the progenitor cells committed to the erythroid lineage.

name: abnormal proerythroblast morphology
abnormal proerythroblast morphology
HP:0025035.def: Anomalous form of the proerythroblast, i.e., the immature, nucleated erythrocyte occupying the stage of erythropoeisis that follows formation of erythroid progenitor cells. This cell is CD71-positive, has both a nucleus and a nucleolus, and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

name: hypothalamic gliosis
hypothalamic gliosis
HP:0025037.def: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the hypothalamus.

name: intratesticular abscess
intratesticular abscess
HP:0025038.def: A collection of pus within a testicle. Ultrasonographic features include shaggy, irregular walls, intratesticular location, low-level internal echoes, and occasionally, hypervascular margins.

name: basal ganglia edema
basal ganglion edema
HP:0025039.def: Swelling within the basal ganglia due to the accumulation of fluid.

name: thalamic edema
thalamic edema
HP:0025040.def: Swelling within the thalamus due to the accumulation of fluid.

name: abnormality of mesenteric lymph nodes
abnormality of mesenteric lymph node
HP:0025042.def: A morphological anomaly of lymph nodes in the mesenteric root or throughout the mesentery.

name: enlarged mesenteric lymph node
enlarge mesenteric lymph node
HP:0025043.def: Increase in size of one or more mesenteric lymph nodes.

name: lung abscess
lung abscess
HP:0025044.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in lung parenchyma, which leads to a cavity, and after formation of bronchopulmonary fistula, can manifest as an air-fluid level inside the cavity.

name: abnormal brain lactate level by mrs
abnormal brain lactate level by mr
HP:0025045.def: A deviation from normal of the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: abnormal lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
abnormal lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: reduced brain lactate level by mrs
reduce brain lactate level by mr
HP:0025046.def: A decrease in the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: reduced brain lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
reduce brain lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: abnormal brain choline level by mrs
abnormal brain choline level by mr
HP:0025047.def: A deviation from normal in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: abnormal brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
abnormal brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: reduced brain choline level by mrs
reduce brain choline level by mr
HP:0025048.def: An decrease in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: reduced brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
reduce brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: abnormal brain creatine level by mrs
abnormal brain creatine level by mr
synonym: abnormal brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
abnormal brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: elevated brain creatine level by mrs
elevate brain creatine level by mr
HP:0025050.def: An increase in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: elevated brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
elevate brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: reduced brain creatine level by mrs
reduce brain creatine level by mr
HP:0025051.def: A decrease in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: reduced brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
reduce brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: abnormal brain n - acetyl aspartate level by mrs
abnormal brain n - acetyl aspartate level by mr
HP:0025052.def: A deviation from normal in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: abnormal brain n - acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
abnormal brain n - acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: elevated brain n - acetyl aspartate level by mrs
elevate brain n - acetyl aspartate level by mr
HP:0025053.def: An increase in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: elevated brain n - acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
elevate brain n - acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

name: abnormal olfactory lobe morphology
abnormal olfactory lobe morphology
HP:0025057.def: A structural anomaly of the olfactory lobe, the structure within the brain that receives neural input from the nasal cavity and thereby processes the sense of smell.

name: hypothalamic atrophy
hypothalamic atrophy
HP:0025058.def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of hypothalamus tissue that was once present.

name: splenic abscess
splenic abscess
HP:0025059.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma of the spleen.

name: multifocal splenic abscess
multifocal splenic abscess
HP:0025060.def: Multiple abscess lesions in the spleen.

name: geophagia
geophagia
HP:0025062.def: The practice of eating earth or soil-like substrates such as clay or chalk.

name: scaphoid abdomen
scaphoid abdomen
HP:0025063.def: The anterior abdominal wall is sunken and presents a concave rather than a convex contour.

name: abnormal mean corpuscular volume
abnormal mean corpuscular volume
HP:0025065.def: A deviation from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume (MCV) of red blood cells, usually taken to be 80 to 100 femtoliters.

name: decreased mean corpuscular volume
decrease mean corpuscular volume
HP:0025066.def: A reduction from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume (MCV) of red blood cells (usually defined as an MCV below 80 femtoliters).

name: incomitant strabismus
incomitant strabismus
HP:0025068.def: Strabismus in which the angle of deviation differs depending upon the direction of gaze or according to which eye is fixing, associated with: (i) defective movement of the eye, (ii) asymmetrical accommodative effort.

name: concomitant strabismus
concomitant strabismus
HP:0025069.def: Strabismus in which the angle of deviation of the squiting eye remains the same in relation to the other eye, in all directions of gaze, and whichever eye is fixing.

name: abnormal u wave
abnormal u wave
HP:0025070.def: An anomaly of the U wave of the electrocardiogram (EKG). The U wave is a small (0.5 mm) deflection immediately following the T wave, usually in the same direction as the T wave. It is best seen in leads V2 and V3.

name: u wave inversion
u wave inversion
HP:0025071.def: Direction of the U wave opposite to the T wave (i.e., below baseline) in leads with upright T waves.

name: prominent u wave
prominent u wave
HP:0025072.def: Increased amplitude of the U wave, defined as an amplitude grerater than 1-2mm or 25 percent of the height of the T wave.

name: exercise - induced u wave inversion
exercise - induced u wave inversion
HP:0025073.def: U wave inversion that is induced by exercise stress testing.

name: abnormal qrs complex
abnormal qrs complex
HP:0025074.def: An anomaly of the complex formed by the Q, R, and S waves, which occur in rapid succession on the electrocardiogram.

name: increased qrs voltage
increase qrs voltage
HP:0025075.def: Elevation of the voltage (height) of the QRS complex. There are several criteria in use, but the most common is the Sokolov-Lyon criterion (S wave depth in V1 + tallest R wave height in V5-V6 greater than 35 mm).

name: abnormal qrs voltage
abnormal qrs voltage
HP:0025076.def: Abnormal amplitude of the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (EKG).

name: decreased qrs voltage
decrease qrs voltage
HP:0025077.def: Reduced amplitude (height) of the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (EKG), defined as amplitudes of all the QRS complexes in the limb leads are less than 5 mm or amplitudes of all the QRS complexes in the precordial leads less than 10 mm.

name: electrical alternans
electrical alternans
HP:0025078.def: The QRS complexes of the electrocardiogram alternate in height.

name: pancreatic abscess
pancreatic abscess
HP:0025079.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma of the pancreas.

name: orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
HP:0025080.def: A form of hyperkeratosis characterized by thickening of the cornified layer without retained nuclei.

name: darier 's sign
darier 's sign
HP:0025081.def: A skin change elicited by briskly rubbing the skin lesion in urticaria pigmentosa (UP), whereby the area begins to itch and becomes raised and surrounded by erythema. Unlike other forms of dermatographism, Darier's sign refers to urtication that is limited to the UP involved areas and, as in this case, spares the skin unaffected by UP.

name: abnormal cutaneous elastic fiber morphology
abnormal cutaneous elastic fiber morphology
HP:0025082.def: Any structural anomaly of the elastic fibers of the skin. Elastic fibers are the essential extracellular matrix macromolecules comprising an elastin core surrounded by a mantle of fibrillin-rich microfibrils.

name: elevated dermal desmosine content
elevate dermal desmosine content
HP:0025083.def: An increased amount of desmosine measure in the skin. Desmosine is a cross-linking amino acid formed from lysyl residues in elastin.

name: folliculitis
folliculitis
HP:0025084.def: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, creating a follicular-based pustule.

name: bloody diarrhea
bloody diarrhea
HP:0025085.def: Passage of many stools containing blood.

name: bloody mucoid diarrhea
bloody mucoid diarrhea
HP:0025086.def: Passage of many stools containing blood and mucus.

name: delayed recoil upon stretching of skin
delay recoil upon stretch of skin
HP:0025087.def: Area of skin requiring an increased amount of time to return to its original shape after being stretched.

name: onychomadesis
onychomadesis
HP:0025088.def: Complete shedding (separation) of the nail from the proximal matrix. Onychomadesis is the proximal separation of the nail plate from the nail matrix due to a temporary cessation of nail growth.

name: feculent vomiting
feculent vomit
HP:0025089.def: Vomiting of material that is of fecal origin.

name: abnormal large intestinal mucosa morphology
abnormal large intestinal mucosa morphology
HP:0025090.def: A structural anomaly of the mucous lining of the large intestine.

name: epidermal acanthosis
epidermal acanthosis
HP:0025092.def: Diffuse hypertrophy or thickening of the stratum spinosum of the epidermis (prickle cell layer of the skin).
synonym: thickening of upper layer of skin
thickening of upper layer of skin

name: peripapillary exudate
peripapillary exudate
HP:0025093.def: A retinal exudate in the area surrounding the optic nerve head.

name: disciform macular scar
disciform macular scar
HP:0025094.def: A subretinal scar with a disc-like shape in the region of the macula.

name: sneeze
sneeze
HP:0025095.def: A sudden violent, spasmodic, audible expiration of breath through the nose and mouth.

name: eyelid myoclonus
eyelid myoclonus
HP:0025097.def: Marked, involuntary jerking of the eyelids.

name: dysgenesis of the hypothalamus
dysgenesis of the hypothalamus
HP:0025098.def: Structural abnormality of the hypothalamus related to defective development.

name: dysgenesis of the thalamus
dysgenesis of the thalamus
HP:0025099.def: Structural abnormality of the thalamus related to defective development.

name: abnormal hippocampus morphology
abnormal hippocampus morphology
HP:0025100.def: Any structural anomaly of the hippocampus,

name: dysgenesis of the hippocampus
dysgenesis of the hippocampus
HP:0025101.def: Structural abnormality of the hippocampus related to defective development.

name: dysgenesis of the basal ganglia
dysgenesis of the basal ganglion
HP:0025102.def: Structural abnormality of the basal ganglia related to defective development.

name: umbilicated nodule
umbilicated nodule
HP:0025103.def: A type of skin nodule that has a small depression that resembles a navel (i.e., is umbilicated).

name: capillary malformation
capillary malformation
