HP:0025104.def: A capillary malformation is a flat, sharply defined vascular stain of the skin. It may cover a large surface area or it may be scattered and appear as little islands of color. In a capillary maformation, the predominant vessels are small, slow-flow vessels (i.e., arterioles and postcapillary venules).

name: nevus anemicus
nevus anemicus
HP:0025105.def: A congenital skin lesion characterized by irregular hypopigmented macules that coalesce to form plaques and occur particularly on the chest. It is generally present at birth or develops in the first days of life. It is more common in females. Diagnosis is confirmed by applying gentle friction to the lesion and the surrounding skin and checking that the erythema produced in the healthy skin does not appear in the hypopigmented lesion. This pale macule becomes more conspicuous when the lesion and its surroundings are rubbed. The margin of the naevus is ill-defined and consists of an archipelago of small anaemic spots.

name: nevus roseus
nevus roseus
HP:0025106.def: A variant of port-wine stain characterized by a pale red or even pink tone, in contrast to the darker hue of the port-wine stain. By analogy with the term port-wine stain, this variant rose-wine stain, or nevus roseus. Nevus roseus, however, cannot be definitely diagnosed until adulthood as port-wine stains are sometimes pink in children. While the natural history of port-wine stains includes hypertrophy, darkening, and nodularity, nevus roseus remains unchanged for life.

name: cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita
cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita
HP:0025107.def: A congenital vascular malformation that presents as localized or generalized erythematous-telangiectatic lesions with a reticular pattern; the lesions are almost always present at birth or develop in the first days of life. Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita (CMTC) appears as marble-like pattern (mottling) on the surface of the skin. In contrast to cutis marmorata, the marbling is more severe and always visible.

name: angioma serpentinum
angioma serpentinum
HP:0025108.def: Angioma serpiginosum consists of punctate, tightly packed telangiectatic lesions. Characteristic histopathological features are dilated and tortuous capillaries involving the uppermost part of the dermis.

name: reduced red cell pyruvate kinase level
reduce red cell pyruvate kinase level
HP:0025109.def: Decrease in the level of pyruvate kinase (PK) within erythrocytes. PK catalyzes the reaction: ATP + pyruvate = ADP + phosphoenolpyruvate.

name: placoid macular lesion
placoid macular lesion
HP:0025110.def: Yellow/white, sharply delineated lesion, typically of inflammatory nature, involving the macula.

name: misophonia
misophonia
HP:0025113.def: An adverse response (dislike) to sound no matter what volume the sound is, characterized by a strong negative reaction to soft sounds that can sometimes be further triggered by seeing the source of the offending sound.

name: hypergranulosis
hypergranulosis
HP:0025114.def: Hypergranulosis is an increased thickness of the stratum granulosum.

name: civatte bodies
civatte body
HP:0025115.def: Eosinophilic hyaline ovoid bodies which are often found in the subepidermal papillary regions or sometimes in the epidermis. Civatte bodies (CBs) are seen as rounded, homogenous, eosinophilic masses on routine H and E staining lying in the deeper parts of epidermis/epithelium and more frequently in dermis/connective tissue. They are known as CBs (in epithelium/epidermis), colloid bodies, or hyaline bodies (in connective tissue). They are 10-25 micrometers in diameter and situated mostly within or above the inflammatory cell infiltrate. In lichen planus, the number of necrotic keratinocytes may be so large that they are seen lying in clusters in the uppermost dermis. These bodies show a positive periodic acid Schiff reaction and are diastase resistant

name: fetal distress
fetal distress
HP:0025116.def: An intrauterine state characterized by suboptimal values in the fetal heart rate, oxygenation of fetal blood, or other parameters indicative of compromise of the fetus. Signs of fetal distress include repetitive variable decelerations, fetal tachycardia or bradycardia, late decelerations, or low biophysical profile.

name: rete ridge flattening
rete ridge flattening
HP:0025117.def: Rete pegs (or ridges) are the epithelial extensions that project into the underlying connective tissue in both skin and mucous membranes. Rete ridge flattening refers to the loss of these projections so that the skin epithelium acquires a relatively flat appearance.

name: lip discoloration
lip discoloration
HP:0025118.def: Lightening or darkening of the lips from their usual coloring.

name: violet lip discoloration
violet lip discoloration
HP:0025119.def: An alteration of the color of the lip to take on a violet color. This term does not include cyanosis.

name: sawtooth acanthosis
sawtooth acanthosis
HP:0025122.def: A type of epidermal acanthosis characterized by a jagged (sawtooth) appearance of the rete ridges of the epidermis.

name: white streaks / specks on enamel .
white streak / speck on enamel .
HP:0025123.def: Areas of white discoloration visible on the surface of the teeth (enamel) in the form of streaks or specks.

name: fragile teeth
fragile teeth
HP:0025124.def: A tendency of teeth to fracture as manifested by a history of repeated fracture of the dental enamel without adequate trauma.

name: white lesion of the oral mucosa
white lesion of the oral mucosa
HP:0025125.def: White lesions of the oral mucosa are generally caused by a condition that increases the thickness of the epithelium. This increases the distance to the vascular bed and thereby tends to change the usual reddish color of the oral mucosa to white. Common causes include hyperkeratosis (thickening of the keratin layer), acanthosis (thickening of the spinous cell layer), increased edema in the epithelium (leukoedema), and reduced vascularity of the underlying lamina propria. Additionally, fibrin caps or surface ulcerations and collapsed bullae can appear white.

name: oral hairy leukoplakia
oral hairy leukoplakia
HP:0025126.def: A corrugated white lesion of the oral mucosa that usually occurs on the lateral or ventral surfaces of the tongue and may have a shaggy or frayed appearance.

name: actinic keratosis
actinic keratosis
HP:0025127.def: A scaly, crusty lesion caused by damage from the ultraviolet radiation of the sun, with typical location on sun-exposed areas of the skin. Actinic keratosis lesions are often elevated, rough, and wartlike, and may be red, or occasionally tan, pink, or flesh-toned in color.

name: reduced intraabdominal adipose tissue
reduce intraabdominal adipose tissue
HP:0025128.def: An abnormally reduced amount of adipose tissue in the abdominal cavity.

name: abnormal small intestinal mucosa morphology
abnormal small intestinal mucosa morphology
HP:0025129.def: A structural anomaly of the mucous lining of the small intestine.

name: decreased small intestinal mucosa lactase level
decrease small intestinal mucosa lactase level
HP:0025130.def: Lactase is produced in the small intestine in humans, Lactase is a member of the beta-galactosidase family of enzymes, and hydrolyzes D-lactose to form D-galactose and D-glucose, which can be absorbed by the small intestine. There are many ways of assessing lactase activity. In one test, an endoscopic biopsy from the postbulbar duodenum is incubated with lactose on a test plate, and a color reaction develops within 20 min as a result of hydrolyzed lactose (a positive result) in patients with normolactasia, whereas no reaction (a negative result) develops in patients with severe hypolactasia. Other, less direct, tests include the hydrogen breath test, and blood tests following lactose challenges.

name: finger swelling
finger swell
HP:0025131.def: Enlargement of the soft tissues of one or more fingers.

name: abnormal circulating estrogen level
abnormal circulate estrogen level
HP:0025132.def: A deviation from normal concentration of the hormone estrogen in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal serum estradiol
abnormal serum estradiol
HP:0025133.def: A deviation from normal concentrations of estradiol in the circulation.

name: increased serum estradiol
increase serum estradiol
HP:0025134.def: An elevation above normal limits of the concentration of estradiol in the circulation.

name: abnormal serum estriol
abnormal serum estriol
HP:0025135.def: A deviation from normal concentration of estriol in the circulation.

name: increased serum estriol
increase serum estriol
HP:0025136.def: An elevation above normal limits of estriol concentration in the circulation.

name: decreased serum estriol
decrease serum estriol
HP:0025137.def: A reduction below normal limits of estriol in the circulation.

name: abnormal serum estrone
abnormal serum estrone
HP:0025138.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of circulating estrone.

name: increased serum estrone
increase serum estrone
HP:0025139.def: An elevation above normal limits of the concentration of estrone in the circulation.

name: decreased serum estrone
decrease serum estrone
HP:0025140.def: A reduction below normal limits of the concentration of estrone in the circulation.

name: gingival calcification
gingival calcification
HP:0025141.def: Ectopic deposition of calcium salts found in the gingiva.

name: constitutional symptom
constitutional symptom
HP:0025142.def: A symptom or manifestation indicating a systemic or general effect of a disease and that may affect the general well-being or status of an individual.

name: chills
chill
HP:0025143.def: A sudden sensation of feeling cold.

name: shivering
shiver
HP:0025144.def: Involuntary contraction or twitching of the muscles.

name: rigors
rigor
HP:0025145.def: Severe chills with violent shivering. A rigor is an episode of shaking or exaggerated shivering which can occur with a high fever.

name: foveal degeneration
foveal degeneration
HP:0025146.def: Deterioration of the tissue of the fovea, i.e.,the region of sharpest vision within the macula of the retina.

name: beaten bronze macular sheen
beat bronze macular sheen
HP:0025147.def: A shiny appearance of the macula, which is often called a beaten bronze appearance.

name: dark choroid
dark choroid
HP:0025148.def: A fluorescein angiographic finding of absence of the normal background fluorescence (a dark choroid).

name: atrophic muscularis propria
atrophic muscularis propria
HP:0025149.def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of muscularois propria tissue that was once present. The atrophy may involve a marked vacuolar degeneration of myocytes, loss of muscle fibers and some cases a highly characteristic honeycomb fibrosis.

name: ganglioneuromatosis
ganglioneuromatosis
HP:0025151.def: Hyperplastic submucosal and myenteric plexus containing an increased number of ganglion cells, glial cells and nerve fibers.

name: poor visual behavior for age
poor visual behavior for age
HP:0025152.def: Lack of visual responsiveness or decrease in visual capabilities suggesting a lack of visual responsiveness or decrease in visual capabilities in an infant or young child in which visual behavior fails to meet normal developmental milestones.

name: transient
transient
HP:0025153.def: Short-lived and not permanent. This term applies to a phenotypic abnormality that is temporary and of short duration.

name: portosystemic collateral veins
portosystemic collateral vein
HP:0025154.def: Presence of biliary veins that serve as a collateral channel to the systemic circulation

name: abnormality of hepatobiliary system physiology
abnormality of hepatobiliary system physiology
HP:0025155.def: A functional anomaly of the hepatobiliary system

name: dependency on intravenous nutrition
dependency on intravenous nutrition
HP:0025156.def: Inability to be weaned from intravenous (parenteral) nutrition, as judged by the hydration status (urine output, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, urine sodium concentration), ability to maintain weight, stool output, and serum electrolyte status.

name: increased urinary sedoheptulose
increase urinary sedoheptulose
HP:0025157.def: An increased concentration of sedoheptulose in the urine. Sedoheptulose is a monosaccharide with seven carbon atoms and a ketone functional group.

name: hyperautofluorescent retinal lesion
hyperautofluorescent retinal lesion
HP:0025158.def: Increased amount of autofluorescence in the retina as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

name: hypoautofluorescent retinal lesion
hypoautofluorescent retinal lesion
HP:0025159.def: Decreased amount of autofluorescence in the retina as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

name: abnormal temper tantrums
abnormal temper tantrum
HP:0025160.def: Temper tantrums are brief episodes of extreme, unpleasant, and sometimes aggressive behaviors in response to frustration or anger, which are a normal part of development in toddlers. Temper tantrums that occur more frequently in a given time and/or are more severe in symptomatology and/or longer in duration and/or inappropriate for the given age compared to a temper tantrum that naturally occurs as a part of the developmental process are classified as abnormal temper tantrums.

name: frequent temper tantrums
frequent temper tantrum
HP:0025161.def: Temper tantrums that occur more frequently compared to the temper tantrums that are a part of the normal developmental process.

name: severe temper tantrums
severe temper tantrum
HP:0025162.def: Temper tantrums, which occur with more severe symptomatology compared to a temper tantrum that occurs as a part of normal developmental process.

name: abnormal optic chiasm morphology
abnormal optic chiasm morphology
HP:0025163.def: A structural abnormality of the optic chiasm.The optic chiasm, located below the hypothalamus, is a partial crossing of the optic nerves.

name: increased number of elastic fibers in the dermis
increased number of elastic fiber in the dermis
HP:0025164.def: An elevated number of elastic fibers, that is of bundles of proteins and glycoproteins in the extracellular matrix in the reticular dermis. Elastic fibers can stretch and recoil back to their original length. This feature can be appreciated on histology with hematoxylin and eosin or other staining methods.
synonym: increased number of elastic fibres in the dermis
increased number of elastic fibre in the dermis

name: clumping of elastic fibers in the dermis
clumping of elastic fiber in the dermis
HP:0025165.def: Formation of clumps or aggregates that make up small protuberances from elastic fibers within the dermis (especially the reticular dermis).
synonym: clumping of elastic fibres in the dermis
clumping of elastic fibre in the dermis

name: thickened elastic fibers in the dermis
thicken elastic fiber in the dermis
HP:0025166.def: An increase of the diameter of elastic fibers in the dermis.
synonym: thickened elastic fibres in the dermis
thicken elastic fibre in the dermis

name: fragmented elastic fibers in the dermis
fragment elastic fiber in the dermis
HP:0025167.def: Elastic fibers in the dermis exhibit an increased number of breaks associated with disorganization of the structure of the elastic fibers.
synonym: fragmented elastic fibres in the dermis
fragment elastic fibre in the dermis

name: left ventricular diastolic dysfunction
leave ventricular diastolic dysfunction
HP:0025168.def: Abnormal function of the left ventricule during left ventricular relaxation and filling.

name: left ventricular systolic dysfunction
leave ventricular systolic dysfunction
HP:0025169.def: Abnormality of left ventricular contraction, often defined operationally as an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent.

name: neuronal / glioneuronal neoplasm of the central nervous system
neuronal / glioneuronal neoplasm of the central nervous system
HP:0025170.def: A central nervous system neoplasm with neuronal and, less consistently, glial differentiation.
synonym: neuronal and mixed neuronal - glial tumor
neuronal and mixed neuronal - glial tumor
neuronal and mixed neuronal - glial tumour
neuronal and mixed neuronal - glial tumour
neuronal / glioneuronal neoplasm of the cns
neuronal / glioneuronal neoplasm of the cns

name: rosette - forming glioneuronal tumor
rosette - form glioneuronal tumor
HP:0025171.def: A tumor of the central nervous system that has components of both neurocytic and glial areas, whereby usually the glial component of the tumor predominates. Rossette-forming glioneuronal tumors (RGNT) have biphasic cytoarchitecture with two elements; neurocytic rosettes resembling Homer-Wright rosettes, and astrocytic component resembling a pilocytic astrocytoma. RGNTs are low-grade tumors that lack histopathological signs of malignancy.
synonym: rosette - forming glioneuronal tumor of the fourth ventricle
rosette - form glioneuronal tumor of the fourth ventricle
rosette - forming glioneuronal tumour of the fourth ventricle
rosette - form glioneuronal tumour of the fourth ventricle

name: smooth septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
smooth septal thicken on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025172.def: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with a smooth appearance of the interlobular septa.

name: nodular septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
nodular septal thicken on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025173.def: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with a nodular or beaded appearance of the interlobular septa.

name: irregular septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
irregular septal thicken on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025174.def: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with an irregular appearance of the interlobular septa. THis feature is often associated with distortion of lung architecture.

name: honeycomb lung
honeycomb lung
HP:0025175.def: Honeycombing represents destroyed and fibrotic lung tissue containing numerous cystic airspaces with thick fibrous walls, representing the late stage of various lung diseases, with complete loss of acinar architecture. The cysts range in size from a few millimeters to several centimeters in diameter, have variable wall thickness, and are lined by metaplastic bronchiolar epithelium. On chest radiographs, honeycombing appears as closely approximated ring shadows, typically 3-10 mm in diameter with walls 1-3 mm in thickness, that resemble a honeycomb; the finding implies end-stage lung disease. On CT scans, the appearance is of clustered cystic air spaces, typically of comparable diameters on the order of 3-10 mm but occasionally as large as 2.5 cm. Honeycombing is usually subpleural and is characterized by well-defined walls. It is a CT feature of established pulmonary fibrosis. Because honeycombing is often considered specific for pulmonary fibrosis and is an important criterion in the diagnosis of usual interstitial pneumonia, the term should be used with care, as it may directly impact patient care.

name: intralobular interstitial thickening
intralobular interstitial thickening
HP:0025176.def: A fine reticular pattern on high-resolution computed tomography, with the visible lines separated by a few millimeters. Regions of the lung with intralobular interstitial thickening characteristically show a fine lacelike or netlike appearance.

name: peribronchovascular interstitial thickening
peribronchovascular interstitial thickening
HP:0025177.def: Thickening of the peribronchovascular interstitium, a connective tissue sheath that surrounds the central bronchi and pulmonary arteries. The peribronchovascular interstitium extends from the level of the pulmonary hila into the peripheral lung. This feature may be ascertained on high-resolution computer tomography.

name: subpleural interstitial thickening
subpleural interstitial thickening
HP:0025178.def: Increase in thickness of the subpleural interstitium.

name: ground - glass opacification
ground - glass opacification
HP:0025179.def: On chest radiographs, ground-glass opacity appears as an area of hazy increased lung opacity, usually extensive, within which margins of pulmonary vessels may be indistinct. On CT scans, it appears as hazy increased opacity of lung, with preservation of bronchial and vascular margins. It is caused by partial filling of airspaces, interstitial thickening (due to fluid, cells, and/or fibrosis), partial collapse of alveoli, increased capillary blood volume, or a combination of these, the common factor being the partial displacement of air. Ground-glass opacity is less opaque than consolidation, in which bronchovascular margins are obscured.
synonym: ground - glass opacification on pulmonary hrct
ground - glass opacification on pulmonary hrct

name: centrilobular ground - glass opacification on pulmonary hrct
centrilobular ground - glass opacification on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025180.def: A hazy area of increased attenuation in centrilobular areas of the lung with preserved bronchial and vascular markings seen on a computer tomography scan. Centrilobular refers to a location that is central within secondary pulmonary lobules.

name: abdominal aseptic abscess
abdominal aseptic abscess
HP:0025181.def: An abscess-like lesion located within the abdomen. The lesions are localized in the spleen, liver, abdominal lymph nodes. The lesions represent visceral sterile collections of mature neutrophils that do not respond to antibiotics but regress quickly when treated with corticosteroids, but relapses occur frequently.

name: localized area of pendulous skin
localized area of pendulous skin
HP:0025182.def: A confined region of lax skin that hangs below the level of the surrounding skin. Histopatholigically, there is a loss of elastic fibers in the dermis of the affected region.

name: marcus gunn jaw winking synkinesis
marcus gunn jaw wink synkinesis
HP:0025186.def: Unilateral ptosis with associated upper eyelid contraction and contraction of either the external or the internal pterygoid muscle. It is thought to occur because of congenital miswiring of a branch of the fifth cranial nerve into the branch of the third cranial nerve supplying the levator muscle. In Marcus Gunn jaw winking synkinesis, elevation and even retraction of the affected eyelid is triggered by chewing, suction, lateral mandible movement, smiling, sternocleidomastoid contraction, protruding tongue, Valsalva manoeuvre and even by breathing.

name: retinal vasculitis
retinal vasculitis
HP:0025188.def: Inflammation of retinal blood vessels as manifested by perivascular sheathing or cuffing, vascular leakage and/or occlusion.

name: bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with generalized onset
bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with generalized onset
HP:0025190.def: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset is a type of bilateral tonic-clonic seizure characterised by generalized onset; these seizures rapidly engage networks in both hemispheres at the start of the seizure.
synonym: bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with generalised onset
bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with generalised onset
generalised tonic - clonic seizure without focal onset
generalise tonic - clonic seizure without focal onset
generalised tonic - clonic seizure without partial onset
generalise tonic - clonic seizure without partial onset
generalised tonic - clonic seizures without focal onset
generalise tonic - clonic seizure without focal onset
generalized tonic - clonic seizure without focal onset
generalize tonic - clonic seizure without focal onset
generalized tonic - clonic seizure without partial onset
generalize tonic - clonic seizure without partial onset
generalized tonic - clonic seizures without focal onset
generalize tonic - clonic seizure without focal onset

name: subtentorial periventricular white matter hyperdensity
subtentorial periventricular white matter hyperdensity
HP:0025192.def: Areas of brighter than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter that surrounds the fourth cerebral ventricle (which is located beneath the tentorium of the cerebellum).

name: posterolateral diaphragmatic hernia
posterolateral diaphragmatic hernia
HP:0025193.def: A posterolateral defect in the diaphragm, commonly referred to as a Bochdalek hernia, which is often accompanied by herniation of the stomach, intestines, liver, and/or spleen into the chest cavity.

name: morgagni diaphragmatic hernia
morgagni diaphragmatic hernia
HP:0025194.def: An anterior retrosternal or parasternal hernia that can result in the herniation of liver or intestines into the chest cavity.

name: central diaphragmatic hernia
central diaphragmatic hernia
HP:0025195.def: A congenital diaphragm defect involving the central tendinous (e.g., amuscular) portion of the diaphragm, whereby the entire rim of diaphragmatic musculature is present.

name: increased total iron binding capacity
increase total iron binding capacity
HP:0025196.def: An elevation in the total-iron binding capacity, which measures how much serum iron is bound if an excess of radioactive iron is added. A high TIBC corresponds to a high transferrin concentration. The latent (or free) iron binding capacity is the difference between the TIBC and the measured serum iron, corresponding to the transferrin not bound to iron, i.e., free iron binding capacity.

name: inclusion body fibromatosis
inclusion body fibromatosis
HP:0025197.def: A benign tumor made up of mostly myofibroblasts that appears almost exclusively on the digits of the hands and feet, rarely involving the thumb or big toe. The lesion displays a proliferation of bland intradermal spindle cells arranged in whorls, fascicles, or a storiform pattern in a collagenous background of varying degrees. Also usually present are perpendicular tumor cell fascicles that extend to the epidermis. The small intracytoplasmic inclusions are said to appear similar to red blood cells. The inclusion bodies have been shown to be made up of densely packed vimentin and actin filaments. The tumor often causes a dome-shaped elevation of the overlying structures, forming a protuberant or polypoid nodule. The overlying epidermis can display a host of changes, including acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, rete ridge flattening, entrapment of adnexal structures, and, rarely, ulceration.

name: inflammatory cap polyp
inflammatory cap polyp
HP:0025198.def: A non-malignant sessile or pedunculated polyp in the colon and rectum that displays a cap of inflammatory granulation tissue with fibrinopurulent exudate that covers the polyp.

name: muscle fiber actin filament accumulation
muscle fiber actin filament accumulation
HP:0025200.def: Accumulation in muscle cells of filaments composed of actin.

name: abnormal circulating apolipoprotein concentration
abnormal circulate apolipoprotein concentration
HP:0025201.def: A deviation from the normal concentration in blood of an apolipoprotein, i.e., of a protein that binds lipids to form lipoprotein and is thereby responsible for the transport of lipids in the blood and lymph circulation.

name: elevated circulating apolipoprotein a - iv concentration
elevate circulate apolipoprotein a - iv concentration
HP:0025202.def: An increased concentration in blood of apolipoprotein A-IV, a major component of HDL and chylomicrons that has a role in VLDL secretion and catabolism and is required for efficient activation of lipoprotein lipase by ApoC-II.

name: caput medusae
caput medusa
HP:0025203.def: Distended and engorged umbilical veins which are seen radiating from the umbilicus across the abdomen to join systemic veins.

name: triggered by
trigger by
HP:0025204.def: A trigger is defined as an external factor that leads to the manifestation of a sign or symptom in a person with a susceptibility to developing that manifestation.

name: triggered by breast feeding
trigger by breast feeding
HP:0025205.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by breast feeding in an infant.

name: triggered by cold
trigger by cold
HP:0025206.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to cold surroundings.

name: triggered by dehydration
trigger by dehydration
HP:0025207.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by being dehydrated, i.e., by a deficit in total body water.

name: triggered by carbohydrate ingestion
trigger by carbohydrate ingestion
HP:0025208.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking carbohydrates.

name: triggered by fructose ingestion
trigger by fructose ingestion
HP:0025209.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking fructose.

name: triggered by glucose ingestion
trigger by glucose ingestion
HP:0025210.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking glucose.

name: triggered by ethanol ingestion
trigger by ethanol ingestion
HP:0025211.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by drinking or otherwise ingesting ethanol.

name: triggered by fasting
trigger by fast
HP:0025212.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by abstaining from eating food (fasting).

name: triggered by galactose ingestion
trigger by galactose ingestion
HP:0025213.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking galactose. Galactose usually is ingested as lactose, which is composed of equimolar amounts of glucose and galactose.
synonym: triggered by ingestion of lactose - containing milk
trigger by ingestion of lactose - contain milk

name: triggered by heat
trigger by heat
HP:0025214.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to heat.

name: triggered by febrile illness
trigger by febrile illness
HP:0025215.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by febrile illness.

name: triggered by heavy meal
trigger by heavy meal
HP:0025216.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating large quantities of food, for instance, by a heavy meal.

name: triggered by high - fat diet
trigger by high - fat diet
HP:0025217.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating a diet high in lipids.

name: triggered by hyperventilation
trigger by hyperventilation
HP:0025218.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by excessively rapid and deep breathing.

name: triggered by vaccination
trigger by vaccination
HP:0025219.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a vaccination.

name: triggered by menstruation
trigger by menstruation
HP:0025220.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by menstruation in a female.

name: triggered by pregnancy
trigger by pregnancy
HP:0025221.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by pregnancy in a female.

name: triggered by sleep deprivation
trigger by sleep deprivation
HP:0025222.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a lack of sufficient sleep.

name: triggered by smoking
trigger by smoke
HP:0025223.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by smoking.

name: triggered by sodium ingestion
trigger by sodium ingestion
HP:0025224.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking sodium.

name: triggered by sound
trigger by sound
HP:0025225.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to sound or noise.

name: triggered by stress
trigger by stress
HP:0025226.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a physical, mental, or emotional factor associated with bodily or mental tension.

name: triggered by excitement
trigger by excitement
HP:0025227.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a a state of excitement or by being startled.

name: triggered by sudden movement
trigger by sudden movement
HP:0025228.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a sudden movement.

name: triggered by vestibular stimulation
trigger by vestibular stimulation
HP:0025229.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by vestibular stimulation, including head turning, cold calorics, postural changes, or rotating chair.

name: abnormal synovial bursa morphology
abnormal synovial bursa morphology
HP:0025231.def: A structural anomaly of a synovial bursa.

name: sleep paralysis
sleep paralysis
HP:0025233.def: An inability to move the body at the onset of sleep or upon awakening from sleep, lasting for seconds to a few minutes.

name: parasomnia
parasomnia
HP:0025234.def: An undesirable physical event or experience that occurs during the process of falling asleep, while asleep, or when waking up from sleep.

name: nrem parasomnia
nrem parasomnia
HP:0025235.def: A parasomnia that occurs during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

name: somnambulism
somnambulism
HP:0025236.def: Ambulation or other complex motor behaviors may occur after getting out of bed in a sleep-like state. During sleepwalking episodes, the individual who is somnambulating appears confused or dazed, with their eyes usually open. They may mumble or give inappropriate answers to questions, and occasionally appear agitated.

name: confusional arousal
confusional arousal
HP:0025237.def: A nocturnal episode is characterized by disorientation, grogginess, and, at times, significant agitation upon awakening from slow-wave sleep or following forced awakenings.
synonym: slow speech or confused thinking upon waking
slow speech or confuse think upon wake

name: foot pain
foot pain
HP:0025238.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the foot.

name: subhyaloid hemorrhage
subhyaloid hemorrhage
HP:0025239.def: A localized detachment of the vitreous from the retina due to the accumulation of blood. When localized in the macular area, it results in sudden profound loss of vision. Subhyaloid premacular hemorrhage is typically characterized by a circumscribed, round or dumb-bell shaped, bright red mound of blood beneath the internal limiting membrane (ILM) or between the ILM and hyaloid face, in or near to the central macular area.

name: preretinal hemorrhage
preretinal hemorrhage
HP:0025240.def: An accumulation of blood between the neurosensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) arising from the choroidal or retinal circulation.

name: flame - shaped retinal hemorrhage
flame - shape retinal hemorrhage
HP:0025241.def: A type of retinal hemorrhage that is located within the nerve fiber layer (NFL) of the retina and that exhibits a characteristic flame shape which results from constraints by the structure of the NFL (axons of the ganglion cells).

name: dot - and - blot retinal hemorrhage
dot - and - blot retinal hemorrhage
HP:0025242.def: Accumulation of blood located in the retina's inner nuclear and outer plexiform layers, and having a dot-like or blot-like shape. THe shape results from intraretinal compression, restricting the hemorrhages within a specific location.

name: subretinal hemorrhage
subretinal hemorrhage
HP:0025243.def: Accumulation of blood located beneath the neurosensory retina in the space between the neurosensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.

name: subretinal pigment epithelium hemorrhage
subretinal pigment epithelium hemorrhage
HP:0025244.def: An accumulation of blood located between the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and Bruch's membrane.

name: cutaneous cyst
cutaneous cyst
HP:0025245.def: A hollow mass located in the skin that is surrounded by an epithelium-lined wall and is well demarcated from the adjacent tissue. Cysts are often said to be sac-like and may contain serous liquid or semisolid material.

name: trichilemmal cyst
trichilemmal cyst
HP:0025246.def: Nontender, round and firm, but slightly compressible, intradermal or subcutaneous cyst measuring 0.5-5 cm in diameter. Trichilemmal cysts are acquired rather than congenital, and tend to appear on the scalp rather than the face, and to be intradermal rather than subcutaneous.

name: dermoid cyst
dermoid cyst
HP:0025247.def: A congenital subcutaneous cyst that arises from entrapment of skin along the lines of embryonic fusion. In contrast to epidermal cysts, dermoid cysts tend to contain various adnexal structures such as hair, sebaceous, eccrine or apocrine glands. Dermoid cysts are present at birth, and are indolent, firm, deep, subcutaneous nodules. They are often located on the head and neck, and rarely in the anogenital area. Dermoid cysts are slowly progressive and can grow to a size of 1 to 4 cm.

name: eruptive vellus hair cyst
eruptive vellus hair cyst
HP:0025248.def: A cutaneous cyst that is small (one or two millimeters in diameter) and painless, presenting as a follicular papule that usually is skin colored but may have a reddish or brownish tinge.

name: comedo
comedo
HP:0025249.def: A clogged cutaneous sebaceous follicle, which is a cutaneous gland that secretes sebum (usually into a hair follicle).

name: closed comedo
close comedo
HP:0025250.def: A comedo in which the top of the pore is not stretched open and thus does not expose the clogged portion (which would appear black), hence the name whitehead.

name: open comedo
open comedo
HP:0025251.def: A comedo in which the part of the pore at the surface of the skin is stretched and open, exposing the contents of the comedo, which appear black.

name: geographic tongue
geographic tongue
HP:0025252.def: An anomaly of the tongue characterized by loss (atrophy) of filiform papillae of the tongue, leaving areas of erythema (redness), surrounded by a serpiginous, white, hyperkeratotic border. The name geographic tongue refers to an appearance that is said to be similar to a map.

name: claustrophobia
claustrophobia
HP:0025253.def: An abnormal fear of being in a closed or narrow space with no escape is called claustrophobia.

name: ameliorated by
ameliorate by
HP:0025254.def: An ameliorating factor is defined as an external factor that leads to a sign or symptom that is already present improving or becoming more bearable

name: ameliorated by pregnancy
ameliorate by pregnancy
HP:0025255.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by pregnancy in a female.

name: ameliorated by heat
ameliorate by heat
HP:0025256.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by heat (including fever).

name: ameliorated by carbohydrate ingestion
ameliorate by carbohydrate ingestion
HP:0025257.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by eating or drinking carbohydrates including glucose (sugar).

name: stiff neck
stiff neck
HP:0025258.def: A sensation of tightness in the neck when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity. Neck stiffness often involves soreness and difficulty moving the neck, especially when trying to turn the head to the side.

name: stiff elbow
stiff elbow
HP:0025259.def: A sensation of tightness in the elbow joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: stiff wrist
stiff wrist
HP:0025260.def: A sensation of tightness in the wrist joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: stiff finger
stiff finger
HP:0025261.def: A sensation of tightness in a finger joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: stiff hip
stiff hip
HP:0025262.def: A sensation of tightness in the hip joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: stiff knee
stiff knee
HP:0025263.def: A sensation of tightness in the knee joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: stiff ankle
stiff ankle
HP:0025264.def: A sensation of tightness in the ankle joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: stiff toe
stiff toe
HP:0025265.def: A sensation of tightness in a toe joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

name: snoring
snore
HP:0025267.def: Deep, noisy breathing during sleep, accompanied by hoarse or harsh sounds, is caused by the vibration of respiratory structures, especially the soft palate. This vibration results in sound due to obstructed air movement during breathing while sleeping.

name: stuttering
stutter
HP:0025268.def: Disruptions in the production of speech sounds, with involuntary repetitions of words or parts of words, prolongations of speech sounds, or complete blockage of speech production for several seconds.

name: panic attack
panic attack
HP:0025269.def: A sudden episode of intense fear in a situation where there is no danger or apparent cause.

name: abnormal esophagus physiology
abnormal esophagus physiology
HP:0025270.def: Any physiological abnormality of the esophagus.

name: esophageal spasms
esophageal spasm
HP:0025271.def: Involuntary contractions of the esophagus that are irregular, uncoordinated, and painful.

name: ovarian dermoid cyst
ovarian dermoid cyst
HP:0025274.def: An cystic ovarian teratoma composed of dermal and epidermal elements and containing tissue components including hair, teeth, bone, thyroid, and others.

name: lateral
lateral
HP:0025275.def: Applies to an abnormality that is located farther from the median plane or midline of the body or of the referenced structure.

name: abnormality of skin adnexa physiology
abnormality of skin adnexa physiology
HP:0025276.def: Any functional anomaly of the skin adnexa (skin appendages), which are specialized skin structures located within the dermis and focally within the subcutaneous fatty tissue, comprising three histologically distinct structures: (1) the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle and sebaceous glands); (2) the eccrine sweat glands; and (3) the apocrine glands.

name: gustatory sweating
gustatory sweating
HP:0025277.def: Hyperhidrosis that occurs with gustatory stimulation (e.g., moisture on face from sweating that occurs after eating).

name: cold - induced sweating
cold - induce sweating
HP:0025278.def: Sweating provoked by cold temperature rather than by heat.

name: pain characteristic
pain characteristic
HP:0025280.def: A pain characteristic is defined as a subjective category or type of pain.

name: sharp
sharp
HP:0025281.def: Applied to pain that is described as sharp, i.e., sudden and severe.

name: dull
dull
HP:0025282.def: Applied to pain that is dull, i.e., not severe but that continues over a long period of time.

name: tender
tender
HP:0025283.def: Applied to pain that is tender, i.e., elicited by touching the affected body part.

name: sleep - interrupting
sleep - interrupting
HP:0025284.def: Applied to pain that wakes the affecting individual from sleep.

name: aggravated by
aggravate by
HP:0025285.def: An aggravating factor is defined as an external factor that leads to a sign or symptom that is already present getting worse or becoming more severe.

name: aggravated by activity
aggravate by activity
HP:0025286.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is aggravated by activity, exertion, or exercise.

name: axial
axial
HP:0025287.def: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the central part of the body, in the head and trunk as distinguished from the limbs.

name: cervical lymphadenopathy
cervical lymphadenopathy
HP:0025289.def: Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck.
synonym: swollen lymph nodes in the neck
swollen lymph node in the neck

name: upper - body predominance
upper - body predominance
HP:0025290.def: Applies to an abnormality that affects the arms, trunk, head more than the legs.

name: lower - body predominance
low - body predominance
HP:0025291.def: Applies to an abnormality that affects the legs more than the arms, trunk, head.

name: acral
acral
HP:0025292.def: Applies to an abnormality that affects the distal portions of limbs (hand, foot) and head (ears, nose).

name: distributed along blaschko lines
distribute along blaschko line
HP:0025293.def: Applies to an abnormality whose localization corresponds to the lines of Blaschko, which correspond to the lineage of epithelia cells. Blaschko lines are normally invisible but may become apparent with certain skin diseases and then can be seen to be distributed in lines horizontal to the body.

name: dermatomal
dermatomal
HP:0025294.def: Applies to an abnormality whose localization corresponds to the dermatomes, i.e., the nerve root distribution.

name: herpetiform
herpetiform
HP:0025295.def: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles that of the grouped umbilicated vesicles seen in herpes simplex and herpes zoster infections.

name: morbilliform
morbilliform
HP:0025296.def: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles that of measles, i.e., maculopapular lesions that are red and roughly 2 to 10 mm in diameter and may be partially confluent.

name: prolonged
prolong
HP:0025297.def: Applied to an abnormality whose duration is extended over a longer period of time than is expected or usual (e.g., prolonged fever lasts longer than one usually sees with an infection).

name: malar rash
malar rash
HP:0025300.def: An erythematous (red), flat facial rash that affects the skin in the malar area (over the cheekbones) and extends over the bridge of the nose.

name: nocturnal
nocturnal
HP:0025301.def: Applies to an abnormality that occurs in or is exacerbated during the night.

name: diurnal
diurnal
HP:0025302.def: Applies to a sign, symptom, or other abnormality that occurs in or is exacerbated in the day time.

name: episodic
episodic
HP:0025303.def: Applied to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that occurs multiple times at usually irregular intervals. The occurences are separated by an interval in which the sign, symptom, or manifestation is not present.

name: periodic
periodic
HP:0025304.def: Applies to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that recurs with a fixed time interval, i.e., the symptom-free periods are always of the same length.

name: quotidian
quotidian
HP:0025305.def: Applies to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that is episodic with a fixed time interval of one day (24 hours).

name: acute emergence over minutes
acute emergence over minute
HP:0025306.def: Acute appearance of disease manifestations in a period of minutes.

name: acute emergence over hours
acute emergence over hour
HP:0025307.def: Acute appearance of disease manifestations in a period of hours.

name: acute emergence over days
acute emergence over day
HP:0025308.def: Acute appearance of disease manifestations in a period of days.

name: abnormal pupil shape
abnormal pupil shape
HP:0025309.def: A deviation from the normal circular shape of the pupil

name: oval pupil
oval pupil
HP:0025310.def: An abnormal pupil shape that is elliptical, i.e., egg-like.

name: anterior chamber cyst
anterior chamber cyst
HP:0025311.def: A closed sac, having a distinct membrane and division compared to the nearby tissue located within the anterior chamber. The sac that may contain air, fluids, or semi-solid material.

name: esophoria
esophoria
HP:0025312.def: A form of strabismus with both eyes turned inward to a relatively mild degree, usually defined as less than 10 prism diopters.

name: exophoria
exophoria
HP:0025313.def: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes deviated outward to a milder degree than with exotropia.

name: choroidal nevus
choroidal nevus
HP:0025314.def: A benign, flat or slightly elevated melanocytic lesions of the posterior uveawith clearly defined margins. Choroidal nevi tend they remain stable in size, and to display features such as overlying drusen as well as retinal pigment epithelial atrophy, hyperplasia or fibrous metaplasia.

name: exacerbated by head trauma
exacerbate by head trauma
HP:0025315.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is worsened, aggravated, or exacerbated by head trauma.

name: cubitus varus
cubitus varus
HP:0025317.def: A deformity of the elbow in which there is a deviation of the forearm toward the midline of the body.

name: ovarian carcinoma
ovarian carcinoma
HP:0025318.def: A malignant neoplasm originating from the surface ovarian epithelium.

name: rubeosis iridis
rubeosis iridis
HP:0025319.def: Formation of new blood vessels on the iris. The new vessels do not display the typical radially symmertic growth pattern of normal iris blood vessels, but rather appear disorganized. Rubeosis usually starts from the pupillary border with tiny tufts of dilated capillaries or red spots that can only be appreciated with high magnification.

name: leakage of dye on fundus fluorescein angiography
leakage of dye on fundus fluorescein angiography
HP:0025320.def: Leakage of fluorescein dye observed upon retinal fluorescein angiography. Areas of leakage can be appreciated as showing gradual enlargement with blurring of margins.

name: copper accumulation in liver
copper accumulation in liver
HP:0025321.def: An anomalous build up of copper (Cu) in the liver.

name: venous occlusion
venous occlusion
HP:0025322.def: Blockage of venous return (flow of blood from the periphery back towards the right atrium) in a vein.

name: arterial occlusion
arterial occlusion
HP:0025324.def: Blockage of blood flow through an artery.

name: sparse medial eyebrow
sparse medial eyebrow
HP:0025325.def: Decreased density/number and/or decreased diameter of medial eyebrow hairs.

name: retinal arterial occlusion
retinal arterial occlusion
HP:0025326.def: Blockage of the retinal artery, generally associated with interruption of blood flow and oxygen delivery to the retina.

name: decreased renal parenchymal thickness
decrease renal parenchymal thickness
HP:0025327.def: Reduced dimension of the solid part of the kidney (parenchyma, the renal cortex and medulla) as measured from the collecting system (renal calyces and pelvis) to the border of the kidney. This measurement can be performed by measuring the thickness of the parenchyma in computed tomography scans.

name: antepartum hemorrhage
antepartum hemorrhage
HP:0025328.def: Significant maternal hemorrhage/bleed in the second half of pregnancy and prior to the birth of the baby.

name: anti - glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody positivity
anti - glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody positivity
HP:0025329.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase.

name: downgaze palsy
downgaze palsy
HP:0025330.def: A limitation of the ability to direct one's gaze below the horizontal meridian.

name: upgaze palsy
upgaze palsy
HP:0025331.def: A limitation of the ability to direct one's gaze above the horizontal meridian.

name: abnormality of foot cortical bone
abnormality of foot cortical bone
HP:0025332.def: An anomaly of the outer shell (cortex) of a foot bone.
synonym: abnormality of the cortex of foot bones
abnormality of the cortex of foot bone

name: cortical thinning of foot bones
cortical thinning of foot bone
HP:0025333.def: A reduction in the thickness of the outer shell (cortex) of foot bones.

name: triggered by emotion
trigger by emotion
HP:0025334.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a strong spontaneously arising mental state, reaction or feeling (emotion).

name: delayed ability to stand
delay ability to stand
HP:0025335.def: A failure to achieve the ability to stand up at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children begin to walk alone at 11 to 15 months of age. On average, children can stand while holding on at the age of 9 to 10 months, can pull up to stand and walk with one hand being held at 12 months, and can stand alone and walk well at 18 months.

name: delayed ability to sit
delay ability to sit
HP:0025336.def: A failure to achieve the ability to sit at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children sit with support at 6 months of age and sit steadily without support at 9 months of age.

name: red eye
red eye
HP:0025337.def: A reddish appearance over the white part (sclera) of the eye ranging from a few enlarged blood vessels appearing as wiggly lines over the sclera to a bright red color completely covering to sclera.

name: circumlimbal hyperemia
circumlimbal hyperemia
HP:0025338.def: A ring of redness at the limbus of the eye, the border between the cornea and the sclera.

name: superficial episcleral hyperemia
superficial episcleral hyperemia
HP:0025339.def: Prominence of blood vessels of the superficial episcleral tissues.

name: deep episcleral hyperemia
deep episcleral hyperemia
HP:0025340.def: Prominence of blood vessels of the deep episcleral tissues.

name: corneal keratic precipitates
corneal keratic precipitate
HP:0025341.def: An inflammatory cellular deposit deposited on the corneal endothelium and visible as spots on the cornea.

name: central retinal artery occlusion
central retinal artery occlusion
HP:0025342.def: Blockage of the main artery in the retina. The typical presentation is one of profound monocular visual loss.

name: lupus anticoagulant
lupus anticoagulant
HP:0025343.def: Presence of lupus anticoagulant (LA) autoantibodies. LA represent a heterogeneous group of autoantibodies, IgG, IgM, or a mixture of both classes, that interfere with standard phospholipid-based coagulant tests (this is only an in vitro phenomenon, LA do not cause reduction of coagulation in vivo). The antibodies are directed against plasma proteins which also bind to phospholipid surfaces.

name: interlobular bile duct destruction
interlobular bile duct destruction
HP:0025344.def: Damage to and obliteration of intrahepatic bile ducts (bile ducts that transport bile between the Canals of Hering and the interlobar bile ducts).

name: abnormality of circulating beta - 2 - microglobulin level
abnormality of circulate beta - 2 - microglobulin level
HP:0025345.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood.
synonym: abnormality of circulating beta2 microglobulin level
abnormality of circulate beta2 microglobulin level
abnormality of circulating beta2 - m level
abnormality of circulate beta2 - m level

name: increased circulating beta - 2 - microglobulin level
increase circulate beta - 2 - microglobulin level
HP:0025346.def: Elevated concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood.

name: decreased circulating beta - 2 - microglobulin level
decrease circulate beta - 2 - microglobulin level
HP:0025347.def: Reduced concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood.

name: abnormal corneal limbus morphology
abnormal corneal limbus morphology
HP:0025348.def: An anomaly of the margin of the cornea overlapped by the sclera.

name: limbal edema
limbal edema
HP:0025349.def: Swelling of the margin of the cornea overlapped by the sclera.

name: giant conjunctival papillae
giant conjunctival papilla
HP:0025350.def: Conjunctival papillae with a diameter greater than 1 millimeter. They characteristically have flattened tops which sometimes demonstrate staining with fluorescein.

name: recurrent interdigital mycosis
recurrent interdigital mycosis
HP:0025351.def: A history of repeated fungal infections located between the fingers or toes, usually manifested by scaling, maceration, and itching. The toes are more commonly affected than the fingers.

name: typically de novo
typically de novo
HP:0025352.def: Description of conditions that are exclusively or predominantly observed to display de novo variants. In some cases, this may be due to the limited reproductive fitness of affected individuals.
synonym: autosomal dominant germline de novo mutation
autosomal dominant germline de novo mutation

name: anti - multiple nuclear dots antibody positivity
anti - multiple nuclear dot antibody positivity
HP:0025353.def: A type of antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity revealed by indirect immunofluorescence (IFL). The multiple nuclear dots (MND) pattern is immunomorphologically characterized by the staining of 3-20 dots of variable size distributed all over the cell nucleus, but sparing the nucleoli, and, in contrast to the anticentromere pattern, MND reactivity does not stain the chromosomes in mitotic cells.

name: abnormal cellular phenotype
abnormal cellular phenotype
HP:0025354.def: An anomaly of cellular morphology or physiology.

name: retinal arterial macroaneurysms
retinal arterial macroaneurysms
HP:0025355.def: Acquired focal dilatations of branches of the retinal artery, usually second-order retinal arterioles, that range in size from 100 to 200 micrometers in diameter. Macroaneurysms are generally located at the termporal retina and may be hemorrhagic or exudative.

name: erratic myoclonus
erratic myoclonus
HP:0025357.def: A type of myoclonus in which the myoclonias shift from body region to another in a random and asynchronous fashion. Erratic myoclonus can affect the face or limbs, are brief, single or repetitive, very frequent and nearly continuous.

name: uveal ectropion
uveal ectropion
HP:0025358.def: Presence of iris pigment epithelium on the anterior surface of the iris.

name: polygonal renal calices
polygonal renal calices
HP:0025359.def: An abnormal polygonal shape of the calices of the kidney (which normally have a rounded or cup-shaped appearance).

name: polycalycosis
polycalycosis
HP:0025360.def: Increased number of calices of the kidney.

name: abnormal medullary pyramid morphology
abnormal medullary pyramid morphology
HP:0025361.def: A structural anomaly of the pyramid of the adult kidney, cone-shaped structures with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla.

name: renal medullary pyramid hypoplasia
renal medullary pyramid hypoplasia
HP:0025362.def: Undergrowth of the pyramid of the adult kidney, cone-shaped structures with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla.

name: glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity
glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity
HP:0025363.def: Hypercellularity due to increased number of cells within glomerular capillary lumina, causing narrowing of the lumina.

name: glomerular extracapillary hypercellularity
glomerular extracapillary hypercellularity
HP:0025364.def: Hypercellularity (increased number of cells) in the renal glomerulus but external to the glomerular capillaries, i.e., in the Bowman space or more than one layer of parietal or visceral epithelial cells.

name: trichoepithelioma
trichoepithelioma
HP:0025367.def: A benign hair follicle tumor whose tumor cells form rudimentary hair follicles but not actual hair shafts. A trichoepithelioma is usually less than one centimeter, firm, round, and shihy with yellow, pink, brown, or bluish color. They may occur multiply, usually on the face, and may gradually increase in number with age.

name: abnormal growth plate morphology
abnormal growth plate morphology
HP:0025368.def: A structural anomaly of the growth plates (epiphyseal plates), areas of cartilage located near the ends of long bones that are located between the metaphysis (widened part of the shaft of the bone) and the epiphysis (end of the bone) and in which growth occurs in the developing bone. After conclusion of bone growth, the growth plates ossify (harden into solid bone).

name: thick growth plates
thick growth plate
HP:0025369.def: Increased thickness (dimension along the axis of the bone) of the growth plate.

name: abnormal ossification of the sacrum
abnormal ossification of the sacrum
HP:0025370.def: Abnormal bone tissue formation (ossification) affecting the sacrum.

name: delayed ossification of the sacrum
delay ossification of the sacrum
HP:0025371.def: Formation of the sacrum bone tissue occurs later than age-adjusted norms.

name: loud snoring
loud snoring
HP:0025372.def: Snoring at a particularly loud or abnormally high volume.

name: interictal eeg abnormality
interictal eeg abnormality
HP:0025373.def: Interictal refers to a period of time between epileptic seizures. Electroencephalographic (EEG) patterns are important in the differential diagnosis of epilepsy, and the EEG is almost always abnormal during a seizure. Some persons with seizures may show EEG abnormalities between seizures, while others do not. In some cases, multiple interictal EEGs must be recorded before an abnormality is observed. In most cases the electrographic pattern of seizure onset is completely different from the activity recorded during interictal discharge.

name: duplicated odontoid process
duplicate odontoid process
HP:0025374.def: The presence of two distinct odontoid processes. The odontoid process, also known as the dens of the axis, is a protuberance of the C2 vertebral body around which the first vertebra rotates.

name: orthotopic os odontoideum
orthotopic o odontoideum
HP:0025375.def: Os odontoideum is classified into two anatomic types (orthotopic and dystopic). Os odontoideum is defined as an ossicle that consists of smooth and separate caudal portions of the odontoid process.With dystopic os odontoideum, the ossicle is located near the basion or is fused with the clivus.

name: hyperglutaminuria
hyperglutaminuria
HP:0025376.def: An increased concentration of glutamine in the urine.

name: triggered by exertion
trigger by exertion
HP:0025377.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exertion or physical exercise.

name: anti - thyroid peroxidase antibody positivity
anti - thyroid peroxidase antibody positivity
HP:0025379.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against thyroid peroxidase.

name: increased circulating androstenedione concentration
increase circulate androstenedione concentration
HP:0025380.def: Increased concentration of androstenedione in the blood circulation.

name: anti - pituitary antibody positivity
anti - pituitary antibody positivity
HP:0025381.def: Circulating antipituitary antibodies (APA) are markers of autoimmune hypophysitis, which may cause deficient pituitary function.

name: hypodipsia
hypodipsia
HP:0025382.def: Reduced fluid intake (drinking) in a clinical situation where the plasma molarity or sodium concentration normally would induce greater fluid intake.

name: dorsocervical fat pad
dorsocervical fat pad
HP:0025383.def: An area of fat accumulation at the back of the neck in the form of a hump.

name: diet - resistant subcutaneous adipose tissue
diet - resistant subcutaneous adipose tissue
HP:0025384.def: Areas of subcutanous fat tissue that are resistant to (do not respond as expected to) diet, life-style alteration, or bariatric surgery.

name: diet - resistant subcutaneous adipose tissue below waist
diet - resistant subcutaneous adipose tissue below waist
HP:0025385.def: Areas of subcutanous fat tissue below the waist that are resistant to (do not respond as expected to) diet, life-style alteration, or bariatric surgery.

name: bitemporal hollowing
bitemporal hollowing
HP:0025386.def: Depression of profile in both temporal regions.

name: pill - rolling tremor
pill - rolling tremor
HP:0025387.def: A type of resting tremor characterized by simultaneous rubbing movements of thumb and index fingers against each other.

name: thyroid nodule
thyroid nodule
HP:0025388.def: A nodular lesion that develops in the thyroid gland. The term \"thyroid nodule\

name: pulmonary interstitial high - resolution computed tomography abnormality
pulmonary interstitial high - resolution compute tomography abnormality
HP:0025389.def: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) can distinguish findings that characterize characterise interstitial lung diseases in a way not possible with other modalities.

name: reticular pattern on pulmonary hrct
reticular pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025390.def: On pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography, reticular pattern is characterised by innumerable interlacing shadows suggesting a mesh.

name: crazy paving pattern
crazy paving pattern
HP:0025391.def: The so-called crazy paving pattern appears as thickened interlobular septa and intralobular lines superimposed on a background of ground-glass opacity, resembling irregularly shaped paving stones. The crazy-paving pattern is often sharply demarcated from more normal lung and may have a geographic outline. It was originally reported in patients with alveolar proteinosis and is also encountered in other diffuse lung diseases that affect both the interstitial and airspace compartments, such as lipoid pneumonia.
synonym: crazy paving pattern on pulmonary hrct
crazy pave pattern on pulmonary hrct

name: nodular pattern on pulmonary hrct
nodular pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025392.def: A nodular pattern is characterised on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography by the presence of numerous rounded opacities that range from 2 mm to 1 cm in diameter, with micronodules defined as smaller than 3 mm in diameter.

name: reticulonodular pattern on pulmonary hrct
reticulonodular pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025393.def: Co-occurrence of reticular and micronodular patterns on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

name: cystic pattern on pulmonary hrct
cystic pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025394.def: On pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography, the cystic pattern is composed by well-defined, round and circumscribed air-containing parenchymal spaces with a well-defined wall and interface with normal lung. The wall of the cysts may be uniform or varied in thickness, but usually is thin (less than 2 mm) and occurs without associated emphysema.

name: combined cystic and ground - glass pattern on pulmonary hrct
combine cystic and ground - glass pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025395.def: Co-occurrence of the cystic pattern and the ground-glass pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography,

name: decreased attenuation pattern on pulmonary hrct
decrease attenuation pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025396.def: Areas of low density corresponding to parenchymal destruction and reduced perfusion, and attenuation of the pulmonary vasculature, as visualized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.
synonym: black lung pattern on pulmonary hrct
black lung pattern on pulmonary hrct

name: mosaic attenuation pattern on pulmonary hrct
mosaic attenuation pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025397.def: A patchwork of intermingled areas of increased and decreased attenuation visualized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

name: nodular - perilymphatic pattern on pulmonary hrct
nodular - perilymphatic pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025398.def: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that has a perilymphatic distribution.

name: nodular - centrilobular with tree - in - bud pattern on pulmonary hrct
nodular - centrilobular with tree - in - bud pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025399.def: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that displays a tree-in-bud pattern, representing centrilobular branching structures that resemble a budding tree.

name: nodular - random pattern on pulmonary hrct
nodular - random pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0025400.def: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that has an apparently random pattern.

name: staring gaze
star gaze
HP:0025401.def: An abnormality in which the eyes are held permanently wide open.

name: square - wave jerks
square - wave jerk
HP:0025402.def: Square wave jerks are saccadic eye movements which, when recorded with open eyes are considered to be a pathological sign, caused by fixation instability, and pointing to a central neurological lesion.

name: stooped posture
stooped posture
HP:0025403.def: A habitual positioning of the body with the head and upper back bent forward.

name: abnormal visual fixation
abnormal visual fixation
HP:0025404.def: Any anomaly in the process of ocular fixation, which is the maintaining of the visual gaze on a single location.

name: visual fixation instability
visual fixation instability
HP:0025405.def: A deficit in the ability to fixate eye movements in order to stabilize images on the retina

name: asthenia
asthenia
HP:0025406.def: A state characterized by a feeling of weakness and loss of strength leading to a generalized weakness of the body.

name: rectourethral fistula
rectourethral fistula
HP:0025407.def: An abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the urethra.

name: abnormal spleen morphology
abnormal spleen morphology
HP:0025408.def: Any anomaly of the structure of the spleen.

name: abnormal spleen physiology
abnormal spleen physiology
HP:0025409.def: Any anomaly of the function of the spleen.

name: splenogonadal fusion
splenogonadal fusion
HP:0025410.def: Joining of the spleen and a gonad during embryological development.

name: fossa navicularis urethral stricture
fossa navicularis urethral stricture
HP:0025413.def: A type of urethral stricture affecting the fossa navicularis, which is the spongy part of the male urethra located at the glans penis.

name: pendulous urethral stricture
pendulous urethral stricture
HP:0025414.def: A type of urethral stricture affecting the pendulous urethra, which is straight and fixed to the corpora cavernosa.

name: bulbar urethral stricture
bulbar urethral stricture
HP:0025415.def: A type of urethral stricture affecting the bulbar urethra, which is the part of the urethra that traverses the root of the penis.

name: vaginal stricture
vaginal stricture
HP:0025416.def: A narrowing of the vagina owing to scar formation.

name: patulous urethra
patulous urethra
HP:0025417.def: Urethra more open or expanded than normal.

name: renal cortical necrosis
renal cortical necrosis
HP:0025418.def: Patchy or diffuse ischemic destruction of all the elements of renal cortex resulting from significantly diminished renal arterial perfusion. Coagulative necrosis may be present, involving all tubular segments and glomeruli. Nuclei may be pale and pyknotic, or may no longer be apparent. Thrombi may be present in vessels at the edge of the infarct.

name: pulmonary pneumatocele
pulmonary pneumatocele
HP:0025419.def: A pneumatocele is a thin walled, gas-filled space in the lung. It is most frequently caused by acute pneumonia, trauma, or aspiration of hydrocarbon fluid and is usually transient. The mechanism is believed to be a combination of parenchymal necrosis and check-valve airway obstruction. A pneumatocele appears as an approximately round, thin-walled airspace in the lung.

name: diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
HP:0025420.def: A type of of pulmonary hemorrhage that originates from the pulmonary microcirculation, including the alveolar capillaries, arterioles, and venules. It presents with hemoptysis, anemia, diffuse lung infiltration, and acute respiratory failure. The diagnosis is confirmed by the observation of the accumulation of red blood cells, fibrin, or hemosiderin-laden macrophage in the alveolar space on pathologic biopsy. Hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, appears at least 48-72 hours after bleeding and is helpful in distinguishing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage from surgical trauma. Mild interstitial thickening, organizing pneumonia, or diffuse alveolar damage can also be seen.

name: pneumomediastinum
pneumomediastinum
HP:0025421.def: The presence of free air in the mediastinum.

name: pleural cyst
pleural cyst
HP:0025422.def: A closed sac-like structure originating from the pleura that contains a liquid, gaseous, or semisolid substance.

name: abnormal larynx morphology
abnormal larynx morphology
HP:0025423.def: Any anomaly of the structure of the larynx.

name: abnormal larynx physiology
abnormal larynx physiology
HP:0025424.def: Any anomaly of the function of the larynx.

name: laryngospasm
laryngospasm
HP:0025425.def: A spasm (involuntary contraction) of the vocal cords that can make it difficult to speak or breathe.

name: abnormal bronchus morphology
abnormal bronchus morphology
HP:0025426.def: Any structural anomaly of the bronchi, i.e., of the airways leading from the trachea to the lungs.

name: abnormal bronchus physiology
abnormal bronchus physiology
HP:0025427.def: Any anomaly of the function of the bronchi.

name: bronchospasm
bronchospasm
HP:0025428.def: A spasm (sudden, involuntary constriction) of the bronchioles.

name: abnormal cry
abnormal cry
HP:0025429.def: Any anomaly of the vocalizing of an infant's crying, i.e.,the typically loud voice production that is accompanied by tears and agitation.

name: high - pitched cry
high - pitch cry
HP:0025430.def: A type of crying in an abnormally high-pitched voice.

name: staccato cry
staccato cry
HP:0025431.def: A type of cry that is abnormal because it is consists of unusually shortened and detached vocalizations.

name: acanthoma
acanthoma
HP:0025432.def: A benign epithelial skin tumor manifesting as a slightly elevated circular plaque or nodule with a red, pink or brown color and a diameter up to 22 mm.

name: decreased lecithin cholesterol acyl transferase level
decrease lecithin cholesterol acyl transferase level
HP:0025433.def: Reduced level of the enzyme lecithin cholesterol acyl transferase.

name: reduced hemolytic complement activity
reduce hemolytic complement activity
HP:0025434.def: A diminished activity of the classical complement pathway as measured by the assay for 50% haemolytic complement (CH50) activity of serum.

name: increased circulating lactate dehydrogenase concentration
increase circulate lactate dehydrogenase concentration
HP:0025435.def: An elevated level of the enzyme lactate dehydrogenase in the blood circulation.

name: elevated serum 11 - deoxycortisol
elevate serum 11 - deoxycortisol
HP:0025436.def: Increased concentration of 11-deoxycortisol in the circulation. 11-deoxycorticosterone, which is also known as simply deoxycorticosterone and 21-hydroxyprogesterone, is a steroid hormore that is produces in the adrenals and is a precursor to aldosterone.

name: macrozoospermia
macrozoospermia
HP:0025437.def: Increased size of the head of sperm.

name: pharyngitis
pharyngitis
HP:0025439.def: Inflammation (due to infection or irritation) of the pharynx.

name: warm reactive autoantibody positivity
warm reactive autoantibody positivity
HP:0025440.def: Warm reactive autoantibodies are RBC-directed immune responses that are maximally reactive at 37 degrees C.

name: achilles tendon calcification
achilles tendon calcification
HP:0025441.def: Ectopic deposition of calcium salts in the Achilles tendon.

name: abnormal cardiac atrial physiology
abnormal cardiac atrial physiology
HP:0025443.def: An abnormality of the function of the cardiac atria.

name: reduced amygdala volume
reduce amygdala volume
HP:0025444.def: A decrease in the volume (size) of the amygdyla.

name: abnormal papillary muscle morphology
abnormal papillary muscle morphology
HP:0025445.def: Any structural anomaly of the papillary muscles of the left ventricle.
synonym: morphological abnormality of the papillary muscles
morphological abnormality of the papillary muscle

name: anomalous insertion of papillary muscle directly into anterior mitral leaflet
anomalous insertion of papillary muscle directly into anterior mitral leaflet
HP:0025446.def: A congenital malformation in which one or both of the papillary muscles (posteromedial or anterolateral) insert directly (that is, without interpositioned chordae tendineae) into the anterior mitral leaflet.

name: displacement of the papillary muscles
displacement of the papillary muscle
HP:0025447.def: Abnormal location of the insertion of a papillary muscle into the left ventricular wall.

name: anterior displacement of the papillary muscles
anterior displacement of the papillary muscle
HP:0025448.def: Abnormally anterior location of the papillary muscles of the left ventricle.

name: apically displaced anterolateral papillary muscle
apically displaced anterolateral papillary muscle
HP:0025449.def: Abnormal location of the insertion of the anterolateral papillary muscle near to the apex of the left ventricle. This feature may be appreciated by noting that this muscle is usually not seen in the apical level of the parasternal short-axis echocardiographic view,

name: testicular adrenal rest tumor
testicular adrenal rest tumor
HP:0025451.def: Testicular adrenal rest tumor (TART) is a abenign tumor of the testis. TART generally occurs multiply and bilaterally within the rete testis. Histologically, TART resemble adrenocortical tissue, which led to the name. The tumous are not encapsulated and consist of sheets or confluent cords of large polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm.

name: pyoderma gangrenosum
pyoderma gangrenosum
HP:0025452.def: A deep skin ulcer with a well defined border, which is usually violet or blue. The ulcer edge is often undermined (worn and damaged) and the surrounding skin is erythematous and indurated. The ulcer often starts as a small papule or collection of papules, which break down to form small ulcers with a so called cat's paw appearance. These coalesce and the central area then undergoes necrosis to form a single ulcer.

name: delayed adrenarche
delay adrenarche
HP:0025453.def: Occurence of adrenarche at a later than normal age. Adrenarche normally occurs between six and eight years of age with increased adrenal androgen secretion; its exact biologic role is not well understood. It is accompanied by changes in pilosebaceous units, a transient growth spurt and the appearance of axillary and pubic hair in some children, but no sexual development.

name: abnormal csf metabolite concentration
abnormal csf metabolite concentration
HP:0025454.def: Any deviation from the normal range of concentration of a metabolite in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: decreased csf 5 - hydroxyindolacetic acid concentration
decrease csf 5 - hydroxyindolacetic acid concentration
HP:0025455.def: 5-HIAA (5-hydroxyindolacetic acid) concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.

name: abnormal csf protein concentration
abnormal csf protein concentration
HP:0025456.def: Any deviation from the normal range of a protein concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: decreased csf protein concentration
decrease csf protein concentration
HP:0025457.def: CSF total protein level is below the lower limit of normal.

name: decreased csf albumin concentration
decrease csf albumin concentration
HP:0025458.def: CSF albumin level is below the lower limit of normal.

name: increased csf / serum albumin ratio
increase csf / serum albumin ratio
HP:0025459.def: An increase above normal limits of the ratio of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) albumin concentration to serum albumin concentration.

name: high myoinositol in brain by mrs
high myoinositol in brain by mr
HP:0025460.def: An elevated level of myoinositol in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
synonym: high myo - inositol in brain by mrs
high myo - inositol in brain by mr

name: abnormality of redox activity
abnormality of redox activity
HP:0025463.def: An abnormality of the processes that maintain the redox environment of a cell or compartment within a cell, that is, the balance between reduction and oxidation chemical reactions.

name: increased reactive oxygen species production
increase reactive oxygen specie production
HP:0025464.def: An accumulation of free radical groups in the body inadequately neutralized by antioxidants, which creates a potentially unstable and damaging cellular environment linked to tissue damage.

name: abnormal circulating beta globulin level
abnormal circulate beta globulin level
