HP:0025465.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of beta globulin. The beta globulins are a group of globular (globe-shaped) proteins in blood.

name: beta 2 - microglobulinuria
beta 2 - microglobulinuria
HP:0025466.def: Increased level of beta 2-microglobulins in the urine.

name: anagen effluvium
anagen effluvium
HP:0025469.def: An abnormal loss of anagen (growth phase) hairs.

name: telogen effluvium
telogen effluvium
HP:0025470.def: A type of hair loss characterized by an abnormal increase in dormant, telogen stage hair follicles.

name: congenital panfollicular nevus
congenital panfollicular nevus
HP:0025471.def: A hamartomatous proliferation containing malformed hair follicles in various stages of development. Panfolliculomas are well-circumscribed lesions demonstrating all stages of follicular differentiation.

name: recurrent plantar mycosis
recurrent plantar mycosis
HP:0025472.def: A history of repeated fungal infections located on the sole of the foot, usually manifested by scaling, maceration, and itching.

name: hyperpigmented papule
hyperpigmented papule
HP:0025473.def: A papule (circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point) that exhibits increased pigmentation (is darker) compared to the surrounding skin.

name: erythematous plaque
erythematous plaque
HP:0025474.def: A plaque (a solid, raised, plateau-like (flat-topped) lesion greater than 1 cm in diameter) with a red or reddish color often associated with inflammation or irritation.

name: erythematous macule
erythematous macule
HP:0025475.def: A macule (flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin) with a red or reddish color often associated with inflammation or irritation.

name: testicular lipomatosis
testicular lipomatosis
HP:0025476.def: Multiple foci of adipocytes within the testicular interstitium, usually presenting as multiple bilateral ill-defined hyperechoic intratesticular lesions of different sizes but generally with maximum diameter of 4 mm.

name: periarticular calcification
periarticular calcification
HP:0025477.def: Calcified deposits in soft tissue structures outside a joint.

name: atrial standstill
atrial standstill
HP:0025478.def: Atrial standstill or silent atrium is a rare condition presenting with the absence of electrical and mechanical activity in the atria. It presents with the absence of P waves, bradycardia, and wide QRS complex in the electrocardiogram.

name: self - neglect
self - neglect
HP:0025479.def: Neglecting one's own needs and well-being.

name: lipomyelomeningocele
lipomyelomeningocele
HP:0025480.def: A type of spinal dysraphism presenting as a subcutaneous fatty mass, that is, a spinal defect associated with lipomatous tissue, and covered by skin. The most usual location for lipomyelomeningocele is at the gluteal cleft.

name: cervical hemivertebrae
cervical hemivertebrae
HP:0025481.def: Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the cervical spine.

name: positive perchlorate discharge test
positive perchlorate discharge test
HP:0025482.def: An abnormal result of the perchlorate discharge test. In this test, first radioactive iodine is administered, sufficient time is allowed to pass so that the radioactive iodine is captured by the thyroid,and then, perchlorate is administered orally. The perchlorate displaces non-organified iodide from the thyroid. The perchlorate discharge test is considered positive (abnormal) if there is an abnormally rapid loss of radioactive iodine from the thyroid.

name: abnormal circulating thyroglobulin level
abnormal circulate thyroglobulin level
HP:0025483.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of thyroglobulin, a protein produced in the thyroid gland that acts as a precursor to thyrroid hormones.

name: increased circulating thyroglobulin level
increase circulate thyroglobulin level
HP:0025484.def: An abnormal elevation of the concentration of thyroglobulin, a protein produced in the thyroid gland that acts as a precursor to thyrroid hormones.

name: vaginal adenosis
vaginal adenosis
HP:0025485.def: Vaginal adenosis is defined by the presence of metaplastic cervical or endometrial epithelium within the vaginal wall, thought to be derived from persistent Müllerian (synonymous with paramesonephric) epithelium islets in postembryonic life.

name: fused labia majora
fuse labium majora
HP:0025486.def: The outer labia are sealed together.

name: abnormal bladder morphology
abnormal bladder morphology
HP:0025487.def: Any structural anomaly of the bladder.

name: detrusor sphincter dyssynergia
detrusor sphincter dyssynergia
HP:0025488.def: A urodynamic anomaly characterized by bladder outlet obstruction from detrusor muscle contraction with concomitant involuntary urethral sphincter activation.

name: bladder duplication
bladder duplication
HP:0025489.def: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of two bladders.

name: myocardial bridging
myocardial bridging
HP:0025490.def: A congenital variant of a coronary artery in which a portion of an epicardial coronary artery (most frequently the middle segment of the left anterior descending artery) takes an intramuscular course.

name: venous stenosis
venous stenosis
HP:0025491.def: Narrowing of a vein due to intimal hyperplasia and fibrosis.

name: microcoria
microcoria
HP:0025492.def: A small pupil (typically diameter less than 2 mm) that dilates poorly or not at all in response to topically administered mydriatic drugs.

name: palmoplantar erythema
palmoplantar erythema
HP:0025493.def: Redness of the skin of the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

name: coated aorta
coat aorta
HP:0025494.def: Regular circumferential periaortic fibrosis involving the whole aorta and leading to a coated aorta appearance on computed tomography scans

name: descending aorta hypoplasia
descend aorta hypoplasia
HP:0025495.def: Significant luminal narrowing of a long segment of the descending aorta.

name: abnormal coronary artery physiology
abnormal coronary artery physiology
HP:0025496.def: Any anomaly of the function of a coronary artery.

name: coronary artery spasm
coronary artery spasm
HP:0025497.def: A brief and sudden narrowing of a coronary artery.

name: aceruloplasminemia
aceruloplasminemia
HP:0025498.def: Absence of ceruloplasmin in the blood.

name: class i obesity
class i obesity
HP:0025499.def: Obesity with a body mass index of 30 to 34.9 kg per square meter.

name: class ii obesity
class ii obesity
HP:0025500.def: Obesity with a body mass index of 35 to 39.9 kg per square meter.

name: class iii obesity
class iii obesity
HP:0025501.def: Obesity with a body mass index of 40 kg per square meter or higher.

name: overweight
overweight
HP:0025502.def: Increased body weight with a body mass index of 25-29.9 kg per square meter.

name: anomalous coronary artery arising from the opposite sinus
anomalous coronary artery arise from the opposite sinus
HP:0025503.def: Origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left sinus of Valsalva or of the left main (LM) or left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva.

name: anomalous origin of the circumflex artery from the right sinus of valsalva
anomalous origin of the circumflex artery from the right sinus of valsalva
HP:0025505.def: The circumflex coronary artery originates from the right aortic sinus of Valsalva.

name: coronary artery sandwich anomaly
coronary artery sandwich anomaly
HP:0025506.def: Origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left sinus of Valsalva or of the left main (LM) or left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva, with the additional feature that the artery passes between the two great arteries. This carries a risk of the artery being compressed by these two vessels,
synonym: anomalous coronary artery with aortic origin and course between the great arteries
anomalous coronary artery with aortic origin and course between the great artery

name: gottron 's papules
gottron 's papule
HP:0025508.def: Violaceous papules overlying the dorsal and lateral aspects of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints.

name: piezogenic pedal papules
piezogenic pedal papule
HP:0025509.def: Flesh-colored or yellowish papules, 2 mm or larger, that are responses to internal mechanical pressure and weakness in the connective tissue in the dermis, appear commonly over the medial aspect of the heel, but in some cases on the wrists. They are thought to represent herniations of adipose tissue through the plantar fascia retinaculum.

name: nevus spilus
nevus spilus
HP:0025510.def: A tan, regularly bordered patch with darker macules within the lesion.

name: nevus sebaceus
nevus sebaceus
HP:0025511.def: A solitary yellow-orange slightly raised plaque typically on scalp or face. The plaque typically thickens and becomes more verrucous or pebbly during childhood.

name: skin - colored papule
skin - color papule
HP:0025512.def: A papule with the same color as the surrounding skin.

name: morning glory anomaly
morning glory anomaly
HP:0025514.def: An abnormality of the optic nerve in which the optic nerve is large and funneled and displays a conical excavation of the optic disc. The optic disc appears dysplastic.

name: delayed thelarche
delay thelarche
HP:0025515.def: Later than normal development of the breasts.

name: coronary - pulmonary artery fistula
coronary - pulmonary artery fistula
HP:0025516.def: A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and the pulmonary artery.

name: visual gaze preference
visual gaze preference
HP:0025518.def: An abnormality of gaze that can be observed following an acute supranuclear cerebral lesion (e.g., stroke) that is characterized by an acute inability to direct gaze contralateral to the side of the lesion and is accompanied by a tendency for tonic deviation of the eyes toward the side of the lesion.

name: multiple biliary hamartomas
multiple biliary hamartoma
HP:0025519.def: Multiple biliary hamartomas are a rare clinicopathologic entity, consisting of small (less than 1.5cm), usually multiple and nodular cystic lesions in the liver.

name: calcinosis cutis
calcinosis cutis
HP:0025520.def: Deposition of calcium in the skin.

name: increased body fat percentage
increase body fat percentage
HP:0025521.def: The percentage of fat as a part of total body weight above the norm, usually defined as 32% for females and 25% for males.

name: elongated chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
elongate chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
HP:0025522.def: Abnormal increased in length of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve.

name: abnormal morphology of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
abnormal morphology of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
HP:0025523.def: A structural anomaly of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve, whose main function is to transmit the contraction and relaxation of the papillary muscles during the cardiac cycle, thus ensuring the closing of the leaflets of the mitral valve.

name: palmoplantar scaling skin
palmoplantar scale skin
HP:0025524.def: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.

name: scaling skin on fingertip
scale skin on fingertip
HP:0025525.def: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes localized to one or more fingertips.

name: psoriasiform lesion
psoriasiform lesion
HP:0025526.def: A skin lesions that resembles the lesions observed in psoriasis, viz., an erythematous plaque covered by fine silvery scales. Psoriasiform lesions can be observed in psoriasis as well as in other conditions including allergic contact dermatitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, Atopic dermatitis, pityriasis rubra, and lichen simplex chronicus.

name: serpiginous cutaneous lesion
serpiginous cutaneous lesion
HP:0025527.def: A skin lesion with a snake- or serpent-like distribution.

name: annular cutaneous lesion
annular cutaneous lesion
HP:0025528.def: A lesion of the skin with a ring-like distribution.

name: hyperpigmented nodule
hyperpigmented nodule
HP:0025529.def: A nodule of the skin that exhibits an increased amount of pigmentation.

name: xanthomas of the palmar creases
xanthoma of the palmar crease
HP:0025530.def: The presence of multiple xanthomas (xanthomata) in the skin distributed in the creases of the palm of the hand. Xanthomas are yellowish, firm, lipid-laden nodules in the skin.

name: harlequin phenomenon
harlequin phenomenon
HP:0025531.def: The Harlequin phenomenon consists of a sudden change in skin colour, resulting in two different body colours, one on each half of the body.

name: positive pathergy test
positive pathergy test
HP:0025532.def: With the pathergy test, a small, sterile needle is inserted into the skin of the forearm. The site of injectionis circuled and observed after one and two days. If a small red bump or pustule at the site of needle insertion occurs, the pathergy test is considered to have a positive (abnormal) result.

name: ocular melanocytosis
ocular melanocytosis
HP:0025534.def: A congenital lesion of the sclera characterized by unilateral patchy but extensive slate-gray or bluish discoloration of the sclera . The conjunctiva are spared.

name: shawl sign
shawl sign
HP:0025535.def: Erythematous, poikilodermatous macules distributed in a shawl pattern over the shoulders, arms and upper back.

name: v - sign
v - sign
HP:0025536.def: Erythematous, poikilodermatous macules distributed in a V-shaped distribution over the anterior neck and chest.

name: plantar edema
plantar edema
HP:0025537.def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on sole of the foot.

name: palmar edema
palmar edema
HP:0025538.def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the palm of the hand.

name: abnormal t cell subset distribution
abnormal t cell subset distribution
HP:0025540.def: Any abnormality in the proportion T cells subsets relative to the total number of T cells.

name: obsolete decreased activity of complement receptor
obsolete decrease activity of complement receptor
abnormal mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
abnormal mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
HP:0025546.def: A deviation from the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell). A reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) may indicate a hypochromic anemia, but the MCH may be normal if both the total hemoglobin and the red blood cell count are reduced.

name: decreased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
decrease mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
HP:0025547.def: A reduction from the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell). A reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) may indicate a hypochromic anemia, but the MCH may be normal if both the total hemoglobin and the red blood cell count are reduced.

name: increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
increase mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
HP:0025548.def: An elevation over the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell).

name: eccentric visual fixation
eccentric visual fixation
HP:0025549.def: A uniocular condition in which there is fixation of an object by a point other than the fovea. This point adopts the principal visual direction. The degree of the eccentric fixation is defined by its distance from the fovea in degrees.

name: elevated circulating ribitol concentration
elevate circulate ribitol concentration
HP:0025550.def: An increase above the normal concentration of ribitol in the blood.
synonym: increased level of ribitol in serum
increase level of ribitol in serum

name: optic nerve misrouting
optic nerve misrouting
HP:0025551.def: Abnormal decussation of the visual pathways, typically identified using visual evoked potentials (VEP) (asymmetrical distribution of the VEP over the posterior scalp).

name: periorbital purpura
periorbital purpura
HP:0025552.def: Multiple red/purple spots on the skin that surrounds the eyes that do not blanch (whiten) upon pressure. Purpura is caused by subcutaneous bleeding.

name: periorbital ecchymosis with tarsal plate sparing
periorbital ecchymosis with tarsal plate sparing
HP:0025553.def: Subcutaneous bleeding with a diameter greater than 1 cm (ecchymosis). The bleeding does not extend into the tarsal plate (the comparatively thick, elongated plates of dense connective tissue within the eyelid) due to an anatomic structure called the orbital septum, which limits extravasation of blood beyond the tarsal plate.

name: yellow nodule
yellow nodule
HP:0025554.def: A type of skin nodule (a lesions that is greater than either 10mm in both width and depth, and most frequently centered in the dermis or subcutaneous fat) with a yellowish coloration (that reflects a high lipid content of the lesion).

name: periungual teleangiectasia
periungual teleangiectasia
HP:0025555.def: Telangiectasia (small dilated blood vessels) located near to the fingernails or toenails.

name: lamellar cataract with riders
lamellar cataract with rider
HP:0025558.def: Lamellar cataracts with associated linear lens opacities radially extending towards the periphery of the lens.

name: coronary cataract
coronary cataract
HP:0025559.def: A type of cataract characterised by club-shaped and dot opacities distributed radially in the deep cortex. These lens opacities surround the nucleus in an appearance that is though to resemble a crown.

name: anterior chamber cells
anterior chamber cell
HP:0025560.def: Tiny deposits corresponding to cells floating in the anterior chamber of the eye. This appearance is typically associated with intraocular inflammation leading to breakdown of the blood-aqueous barrier and resulting in an increase in the number of cells and in the aqueous humor. Grading (SUN Working Group) is performed by estimating the number of cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: anterior chamber cells grade 1+
anterior chamber cell grade 1+
HP:0025561.def: Anterior chamber cells with 6-15 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: anterior chamber cells grade 0.5+
anterior chamber cell grade 0.5+
HP:0025562.def: Anterior chamber cells with 1-5 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: anterior chamber cells grade 0
anterior chamber cell grade 0
HP:0025563.def: Anterior chamber cells with less than one cell in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: anterior chamber cells grade 2+
anterior chamber cell grade 2+
HP:0025564.def: Anterior chamber cells with 16-25 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: anterior chamber cells grade 3+
anterior chamber cell grade 3+
HP:0025565.def: Anterior chamber cells with 26-50 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: anterior chamber cells grade 4+
anterior chamber cell grade 4+
HP:0025566.def: Anterior chamber cells with more than 50 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

name: central serous chorioretinopathy
central serous chorioretinopathy
HP:0025567.def: An anomaly of the retina with serous detachment of the neurosensory retina secondary to one or more focal lesions of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and associated with blurred vision, usually in one eye only and perceived typically by the patient as a dark spot in the centre of the visual field with associated micropsia and metamorphopsia. Normal vision often recurs spontaneously within a few months.

name: abnormal morphology of the choroidal vasculature
abnormal morphology of the choroidal vasculature
polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy
polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy
HP:0025569.def: The presence of aneurysmal polypoidal lesions in the choroidal vasculature. The aneurysmal dilatations, also known as polyps, may be found at subfoveal, juxtafoveal, extrafoveal, peripapillary or even peripheral regions. These polypoidal dilatations may be visible as reddish-orange subretinal nodules during ophthalmoscopic examination. The polypoidal lesions are best detected on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) and might be associated with a branching vascular network (BVN) of neovascularization.

name: choroidal vascular hyperpermeability
choroidal vascular hyperpermeability
HP:0025570.def: Increased tendency of choiroidal blood vessels to allow fluids to leak characterized by multifocal choroidal hyperfluorescence on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA).

name: christmas tree cataract
christmas tree cataract
HP:0025571.def: A type of cataract that shows a spectacular display of multiple colours that glitters with the change of incident light like an illuminated Christmas tree.

name: punctal stenosis
punctal stenosis
HP:0025572.def: Punctal stenosis is a condition in which the external opening of the lacrimal canaliculus is narrowed or occluded.

name: mild myopia
mild myopia
HP:0025573.def: A mild form of myopia with up to -3.00 diopters.

name: macular hemorrhage
macular hemorrhage
HP:0025574.def: Bleeding occurring within the macula lutea of the retina.

name: abnormal superior vena cava morphology
abnormal superior vena cava morphology
HP:0025575.def: Any structural anomaly of the principal vein draining blood from the upper portion of the body and delivering it to the right ventricle of the heart.

name: abnormal inferior vena cava morphology
abnormal inferior vena cava morphology
HP:0025576.def: Any structural anomaly of the principal vein draining blood from the lower portion of the body.

name: aortic valve prolapse
aortic valve prolapse
HP:0025578.def: Aortic valve prolapse can be diagnosed when either or both of the right or non-coronary aortic valve cusps (seen in the cross sectional echocardiographic long axis view) show backward bowing towards the left ventricle beyond a line joining the points of attachment of the aortic valve leaflets to the annulus.

name: abnormal left atrium morphology
abnormal leave atrium morphology
HP:0025579.def: Any structural abnormality of the left atrium.

name: abnormal right atrium morphology
abnormal right atrium morphology
HP:0025580.def: Any structural abnormality of the right atrium.

name: submacular hemorrhage
submacular hemorrhage
HP:0025582.def: Bleeding between the neurosensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) arising from the choroidal or retinal circulation.

name: tapetal - like fundal reflex
tapetal - like fundal reflex
HP:0025583.def: Golden, scintillating, particulate reflection noted on fundus examination (typically in the macula and sparing the fovea). The term tapetal is used to describe this 'metallic' sheen appearance as it is thought to be similar to the 'tapetal' reflex seen in the eyes of certain animals.

name: hypotropia
hypotropia
HP:0025584.def: A form of manifest strabismus (heterotropia) in which one eye is deviated downwards when both eyes are open.

name: hyperphoria
hyperphoria
HP:0025585.def: Tendency for the visual axis of one eye to be higher than that of the other.

name: hypertropia
hypertropia
HP:0025586.def: A type of strabismus characterized by permanent upward deviation of the visual axis of one eye.

name: hyperdeviation
hyperdeviation
HP:0025587.def: A type of strabismus in which the visual axis of one eye is higher than that of the other.

name: hypodeviation
hypodeviation
HP:0025588.def: A type of strabismus in which the visual axis of one eye is lower than that of the other.

name: cyclodeviation
cyclodeviation
HP:0025589.def: Cyclodeviation is defined as the rotation of an eyeball along the anteroposterior axis and cyclotropia as a misalignment of cyclodeviation between the two eyes.

name: abnormal extraocular muscle physiology
abnormal extraocular muscle physiology
HP:0025590.def: A functional anomaly of the muscles of the eye.

name: abnormal superior oblique muscle physiology
abnormal superior oblique muscle physiology
HP:0025591.def: A functional anomaly of the superior oblique muscle, a fusiform muscle that originates in the upper, medial side of the orbit. The superior oblique muscle abducts, depresses and internally rotates the eye, and is the only extraocular muscle innervated by the fourth cranial nerve.

name: superior oblique muscle weakness
superior oblique muscle weakness
HP:0025592.def: Decreased strength of the superior oblique muscle.

name: superior oblique muscle restriction
superior oblique muscle restriction
HP:0025593.def: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the superior oblique muscle.

name: superior oblique muscle overaction
superior oblique muscle overaction
HP:0025594.def: An ocular motility abnormality characterized by an overacting superior oblique muscle resulting to vertical incomitance of the eyes in lateral gaze. On examination, this is commonly seen as a downshoot of the adducting eye occuring when gaze is directed into the field of action of the inferior oblique muscle, producing a greater downward excursion of the adducted eye than of the abducted eye.

name: superior oblique muscle underaction
superior oblique muscle underaction
HP:0025595.def: Reduced ocular movement of the superior oblique muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

name: abnormal inferior oblique muscle physiology
abnormal inferior oblique muscle physiology
HP:0025596.def: A functional anomaly of the inferior oblique muscle, an extraocular muscle that has its origin on the maxillary bone just posterior to the inferior medial orbital rim and lateral to the nasolacrimal canal and that is innervated by the inferior branch of the oculomotor nerve.

name: inferior oblique muscle restriction
inferior oblique muscle restriction
HP:0025597.def: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the inferior oblique muscle.

name: inferior oblique muscle weakness
inferior oblique muscle weakness
HP:0025598.def: Decreased strength of the inferior oblique muscle.

name: inferior oblique muscle overaction
inferior oblique muscle overaction
HP:0025599.def: A common ocular motility disorder characterized by vertical incomitance of the eyes in lateral gaze. In primary inferior oblique muscle overaction, an upshoot of the adducting eye occurs when gaze is directed into the field of action of the inferior oblique muscle, producing a greater upward excursion of the adducted eye than of the abducted eye.

name: abnormal inferior rectus muscle physiology
abnormal inferior rectus muscle physiology
HP:0025600.def: A functional anomaly of the inferior rectus muscle, which is innervated by the inferior division of oculomotor nerve and functions in the depression, adduction, and lateral rotation (extortion) of the eye.

name: inferior rectus muscle weakness
inferior rectus muscle weakness
HP:0025601.def: Decreased strength of the inferior rectus muscle.

name: inferior rectus muscle restriction
inferior rectus muscle restriction
HP:0025602.def: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the inferior rectus muscle.

name: abnormal superior rectus muscle physiology
abnormal superior rectus muscle physiology
HP:0025603.def: A functional anomaly of the superior rectus muscle, an extraocular muscle that is innervated by the superior division of the oculomotor nerve, and whose primary function is the elevation of the globe.

name: orbital schwannoma
orbital schwannoma
HP:0025604.def: A schwannoma (benign, usually encapsulated slow growing tumor composed of Schwann cells) located in the orbit.

name: lid lag on downgaze
lid lag on downgaze
HP:0025605.def: Delayed descent of the upper eyelid on downgaze. Also described by some authors as von Graefe sign.

name: abnormal medial rectus muscle physiology
abnormal medial rectus muscle physiology
HP:0025606.def: A functional anomaly of the medial rectus muscle, an extraocular muscle that is innervated by the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve and whose sole action is the adduction of the eyeball.

name: upper eyelid entropion
upper eyelid entropion
HP:0025607.def: An inward turning (inversion) of the margin of the upper eyelid.

name: cicatricial ectropion
cicatricial ectropion
HP:0025608.def: An outward turning (eversion) or rotation of the eyelid margin (i.e., ectropion) caused by shortening or contraction of the anterior or middle lamellae related to scarring.

name: anterior blepharitis
anterior blepharitis
HP:0025609.def: A type of blepharitis that affects the eyelid skin, base of the eyelashes, and the eyelash follicles.

name: posterior blepharitis
posterior blepharitis
HP:0025610.def: A type of blepharitis that affects the meibomian glands and meibomian gland orifices. This abnormality can be associated with a spectrum of appearances ranging from meibomian seborrhoea (foaming meibomian gland secretions) and meibomianitis (inflamed meibomian glands), to chalazia.

name: epicanthus superciliaris
epicanthus superciliaris
HP:0025611.def: A type of epicanthus in which more extensive epicanthal folds with their origins in the eyebrow cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus (middle corner of the eye).

name: corneal astigmatism
corneal astigmatism
HP:0025612.def: A type of refractive error related abnormal curvatures on the anterior or posterior surface of the cornea.

name: focal emotional seizure
focal emotional seizure
HP:0025613.def: Seizures presenting with an emotion or the appearance of having an emotion as an early prominent feature, such as fear, spontaneous joy or euphoria, laughing (gelastic), or crying, (dacrystic). These emotional seizures may occur with or without objective clinical signs of a seizure evident to the observer.

name: sterile abscess
sterile abscess
HP:0025616.def: An abscess not caused by infection with pyogenic bacteria. Operationally, a sterile abscess is inferred if investigations of an abscess fail to reveal evidence of pathogenic organisms.

name: abnormal plasma cell count
abnormal plasma cell count
HP:0025617.def: An abnormal number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

name: reduced plasma cell count
reduce plasma cell count
HP:0025618.def: An abnormally low number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

name: elevated plasma cell count
elevate plasma cell count
HP:0025619.def: An abnormally high number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

name: abnormal proportion of cd4+ central memory cells
abnormal proportion of cd4+ central memory cell
HP:0025620.def: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD4+ T cells. These are memory cells that are located in the secondary lymphoid organs. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L+/CD45RA- phenotype.
synonym: abnormal proportion of central memory cd4+ , alpha - beta t cells
abnormal proportion of central memory cd4+ , alpha - beta t cell

name: obsolete increased proportion of cd4+ central memory cells
obsolete increase proportion of cd4+ central memory cell
obsolete decreased proportion of cd4+ central memory cells
obsolete decrease proportion of cd4+ central memory cell
abnormal proportion of cd4+ effector memory cells
abnormal proportion of cd4+ effector memory cell
HP:0025623.def: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells have the phenotype CD3-positive, CD4-positive, CD62L-negative, CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
synonym: abnormal proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory cells
abnormal proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory cell
abnormal proportion of effector memory cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells
abnormal proportion of effector memory cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cell

name: reduced proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells
reduce proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cell
HP:0025624.def: An abnormally decreased proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells have the phenotype CD3-positive, CD4-positive, CD62L-negative, CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
synonym: decreased proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells
decreased proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cell
decreased proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory t cells
decreased proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory t cell
decreased proportion of effector memory cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells
decreased proportion of effector memory cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cell

name: elevated proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells
elevate proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cell
HP:0025625.def: An abnormally increased proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L-/CD45RA phenotype.
synonym: increased proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells
increase proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cell
increased proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory t cells
increase proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory t cell
increased proportion of effector cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells
increase proportion of effector cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cell

name: increased circulating oleate level
increase circulate oleate level
HP:0025626.def: An abnormally high concentration of oleic acid (oleate) in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating octadecanoate level
increase circulate octadecanoate level
HP:0025627.def: An abnormally high concentration of octadecanoate in the blood circulation. Octadecanoate is a fatty acid anion 18:0 that is the conjugate base of octadecanoic acid (stearic acid).

name: increased circulating myristoleate level
increase circulate myristoleate level
HP:0025628.def: An abnormally high concentration of myristoleate in the blood circulation.

name: anti - myelin - associated glycoprotein antibody positivity
anti - myelin - associate glycoprotein antibody positivity
HP:0025629.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG).

name: argininosuccinic aciduria
argininosuccinic aciduria
HP:0025630.def: Increased amount of argininosuccinate in the urine.

name: alpha - aminobutyric aciduria
alpha - aminobutyric aciduria
HP:0025631.def: Increased amount of alpha-aminobutyric acid in the urine.

name: reduced reactive oxygen species production in neutrophils
reduce reactive oxygen specie production in neutrophil
HP:0025632.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of reactive oxygen produced by neutrophils in the respiratory burst.

name: abnormal ureter morphology
abnormal ureter morphology
HP:0025633.def: A structural abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

name: abnormal ureter physiology
abnormal ureter physiology
HP:0025634.def: A functional abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

name: ureteral polyp
ureteral polyp
HP:0025635.def: A growth protruding from the mucous membrane of the ureter. Ureteral polyps can be attached to the ureter by a broad base or a thin stalk.

name: endometritis
endometritis
HP:0025636.def: Inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus (endometrium).
synonym: inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus
inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus

name: vasospasm
vasospasm
HP:0025637.def: Narrowing of an artery due to constriction of the blood vessels.

name: elevated urinary n - butyrylglycine
elevate urinary n - butyrylglycine
HP:0025638.def: An increased level of N-butyrylglycine in the urine.

name: increased urinary zinc level
increase urinary zinc level
HP:0025639.def: An abnormally elevated amount of zinc in the urine, typically as assessed by a 24 hour urine collection.

name: abnormal urinary mineral level
abnormal urinary mineral level
HP:0025640.def: An abnormal concentration or amount of a mineral in the urine. Medically relevant minerals include calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, chloride, magnesium, iron, zinc, iodine, chromium, copper, fluoride, molybdenum, manganese, and selenium.

name: elevated circulating glycolate concentration
elevate circulate glycolate concentration
HP:0025641.def: The concentration of glycolate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: tarlov cyst
tarlov cyst
HP:0025643.def: A cerebrospinal fluid-filled nerve root cyst most often localized in the sacral spine.

name: fixation - off epileptiform discharges
fixation - off epileptiform discharge
HP:0025644.def: Fixation off sensitivity (FOS) is characterized by posterior or generalized epileptiform discharges that consistently occur with conditions that eliminate central vision, such as closed eyes, complete darkness, modified Ganzfeld stimulation (using a large white surface without visual cues), and Frenzel lenses. The FOS electroencephalogram (EEG) pattern usually consists of spikes/polyspikes and waves localized in occipital regions (bilateral or unilateral) or generalized discharges. It is usually inhibited by fixation of gaze, observing patterns, or intermittent photic stimulation (e.g., flashing light or patterns used as stimuli during the recording of the EEG).

name: bilateral polymicrogyria
bilateral polymicrogyria
HP:0025646.def: Polymicrogyria that affects all or some of both cerebral hemispheres.

name: steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome
steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome
HP:0025647.def: A type of nephrotic syndrome in which complete remission (albumin urine dipstick negative/trace or proteinuria <4mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio <200mg/g (<20 mg/mmol) for 3 consecutive days) is achieved within initial 4 weeks of corticosteroid therapy.

name: steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome with infrequent relapses
steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome with infrequent relapse
HP:0025648.def: A type of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in which relapses occur at a frequency of one relapse (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria over 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) within 6 months of initial response, or one to three relapses in any 12-month period.

name: steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome with frequent relapses
steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome with frequent relapse
HP:0025649.def: A type of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in which relapses occur at a frequency of two or more relapses (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria over 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) within 6 months of initial response or four or more relapses in any 12-month period.

name: steroid - dependent nephrotic syndrome
steroid - dependent nephrotic syndrome
HP:0025650.def: A type of nephrotic syndrome in which two consecutive relapses (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria greater than 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) occur during corticosteroid therapy, or within 14 days of ceasing therapy.

name: abnormal placental adhesion into the uterine wall
abnormal placental adhesion into the uterine wall
HP:0025652.def: Abnormal placental adhesion is characterized by an anomalous adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall. Based on the degree of adhesion, placental invasion can be classified into accreta, increta, or percreta.

name: placenta percreta
placenta percreta
HP:0025653.def: Placenta percreta is a rare form of morbidly adherent placenta with penetration through the myometrium reaching serosa and even adjacent pelvic organs.
synonym: abnormal placental pentration beyond the uterine wall
abnormal placental pentration beyond the uterine wall

name: placenta accreta
placenta accreta
HP:0025654.def: Abnormally firm adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall.

name: placenta increta
placenta increta
HP:0025655.def: Abnormal placental pentration into but not beyond the uterine wall.

name: prenatal double bubble sign
prenatal double bubble sign
HP:0025656.def: Sonographic detection of a double bubble sign in the upper abdomen is strongly indicative of duodenal obstruction. One bubble represents fetal stomach, and the other is attributed to a dilated proximal part of the duodenum; continuity between both bubbles is required for the sign.

name: obsolete abnormal umbilical artery doppler pattern in pregnancy
obsolete abnormal umbilical artery doppler pattern in pregnancy
decreased circulating creatine kinase concentration
decrease circulate creatine kinase concentration
HP:0025659.def: A reduction in the level of the enzyme creatine kinase (also known as creatine phosphokinase (CK; EC 2.7.3.2) in the blood.

name: chiari type ii malformation
chiari type ii malformation
HP:0025660.def: A type of Chiari malformation that consists of brainstem herniation and a towering cerebellum in addition to the herniated cerebellar tonsils and vermis due to an open distal spinal dysraphism/myelomeningocele.

name: chiari type iii malformation
chiari type iii malformation
HP:0025661.def: A type of Chiari malformation that involves herniation of the hindbrain (cerebellum with or without the brainstem) into a low occipital or high cervical meningoencephalocele.

name: abnormal fetal skeletal morphology
abnormal fetal skeletal morphology
HP:0025662.def: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal skeleton. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other terms from the skeletal hierarchy can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: reduced fetal femur / foot length ratio
reduce fetal femur / foot length ratio
HP:0025663.def: This ratio relates the length of the fetal femur to that of the fetal foot. The ratio is approximately 1 throughout the age range of 14 to 40 weeks of gestation. A substantial reduction in the raio can help differentiate fetuses that have dysplastic limb reduction from those whose limbs are short because of constitutional factors or IUGR. It can reduce the problem of an unknown gestational age and help to distinguish between fetal skeletal dysplasia and intrauterine growth retardation caused by other factors.

name: moderate to late preterm birth
moderate to late preterm birth
HP:0025664.def: Birth at 32 to 36 completed weeks of gestation.

name: extremely preterm birth
extremely preterm birth
HP:0025665.def: Birth before 28 completed weeks of gestation (up to and including 27 weeks and 6 days of gestation).

name: very preterm birth
very preterm birth
HP:0025666.def: Birth before 32 completed weeks of gestation (28 up to but not including 32 weeks).

name: fetal neck anomaly
fetal neck anomaly
HP:0025667.def: A structural anomaly in the fetal neck region. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: abnormal neck morphology
abnormal neck morphology
HP:0025668.def: Any structural anomaly of the neck region.

name: abnormal neck physiology
abnormal neck physiology
HP:0025669.def: Any functional anomaly of the neck region.

name: syntelencephaly
syntelencephaly
HP:0025670.def: Syntelencephaly is a rare malformation that consists of an abnormal midline connection of the cerebral hemispheres in the posterior frontal and parietal regions, with interhemispheric separation of the basal forebrain, anterior frontal lobes, and occipital regions.

name: fetal pericardial effusion
fetal pericardial effusion
HP:0025671.def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid in which the heart is partially or completely surrounded by fluid that is seen in all views and the thickness of the fluid as observed by prenatal ultrasound is above age-dependent norms.

name: fetal skin edema
fetal skin edema
HP:0025672.def: A separation of skin in one or more regions of the body or even along the entire length of body wall (to a degree greater than gestational-age related norms) related to pathologically increased fluid accumulation in the subcutaneous tissue.

name: loculated ascites
loculated ascites
HP:0025673.def: A type of ascites (peritoneal fluid collection) that is divided into loculi (compartments) by septa (fibrous walls). Ascites fluid can become loculated when confined by adhesions, malignancy or infection.

name: meconium pseudocyst
meconium pseudocyst
HP:0025674.def: A meconium-containing cyst in the peritoneal space . Meconium pseudocysts form in the presence of meconium peritonitis, which is defined as a sterile peritonitis caused by escape of meconium from the intestinal tract into the general peritoneal cavity during the fetal or perinatal period. When the extruded meconium becomes walled off, it can form a rim-calcified mass representing the meconium pseudocyst.

name: premature closure of the ductus arteriosus
premature closure of the ductus arteriosus
HP:0025675.def: A prenatal partial or complete closure of the ductus arteriosus (i.e., prior to delivery).
synonym: idiopathic constriction of the fetal ductus arteriosus
idiopathic constriction of the fetal ductus arteriosus
idiopathic constriction of the foetal ductus arteriosus
idiopathic constriction of the foetal ductus arteriosus

name: fetal pleural effusion
fetal pleural effusion
HP:0025676.def: Fetal pleural effusion is the accumulation of excess fluid in the layers of tissue (pleura) lining the lungs and wall of the chest. It may be primary, also termed hydrothorax, occurring as an isolated finding or it may be secondary, most commonly resulting from non-immune hydrops.

name: fetal chylothorax
fetal chylothorax
HP:0025677.def: The presence of chyle (a type of lipid-rich lymph) in the pleural space (the space surrounding the lung) as observed in a fetus.

name: fetal hydrothorax
fetal hydrothorax
HP:0025678.def: Accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the pleural space. This finding is usually observed by prenatal sonography. Once neonatal feeding is established and the lymphatic fluid contains chyle, transformation to chylothorax may be observed.

name: diskitis
diskitis
HP:0025679.def: Inflammation of an intervertebral disc or disk space.

name: compound muscle action potential amplitude facilitation
compound muscle action potential amplitude facilitation
HP:0025680.def: Compound muscle action potential amplitude (CMAP) facilitation denotes an increase in tendon reflexes, strength, or CMAP amplitude after 10 seconds of maximal voluntary contraction.

name: distal clavicular thinning
distal clavicular thinning
HP:0025681.def: Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles that is limited to the distal region.

name: crouch gait
crouch gait
HP:0025682.def: A gait disturbance that is characterized by excessive ankle dorsiflexion, knee and hip flexion during the stance phase.

name: abnormal amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
abnormal amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
HP:0025683.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Amyloid beta is a peptide of 36-43 amino acids that is processed from the Amyloid precursor protein. ABeta42, which is 42 amino acids in length, is the longer form.

name: decreased amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
decrease amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
HP:0025684.def: A reduction from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: increased amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
increase amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
HP:0025685.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: abnormal amyloid beta 40 peptide csf concentration
abnormal amyloid beta 40 peptide csf concentration
HP:0025686.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Amyloid beta is a peptide of 36-43 amino acids that is processed from the Amyloid precursor protein. ABeta40, which is 40 amino acids in length, is the shorter form.

name: increased amyloid beta 40 peptide csf concentration
increase amyloid beta 40 peptide csf concentration
HP:0025687.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of amyloid beta 40 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: abnormal amyloid beta peptide csf concentration
abnormal amyloid beta peptide csf concentration
HP:0025688.def: Any anomaly in the concentration of a cleaved APP amyloid beta protein fragment in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: extra - abdominal umbilical vein varix
extra - abdominal umbilical vein varix
HP:0025689.def: Focal dilatation of the extra-abdominal portion of the umbilical vein. An extra-abdominal umbilical varix is difficult to diagnose prenatally as it can appear like a cyst on ultrasound prior to birth.

name: fetal intra - abdominal umbilical vein varix
fetal intra - abdominal umbilical vein varix
HP:0025690.def: Fetal intra-abdominal umbilical vein varix (FIUVV) is defined by the focal dilatation of the fetal umbilical vein between its entry in the abdomen and its ending in the portal system. The dilatation can be defined using one of the following criteria: a portion of intra-abdominal umbilical vein that is at least 50% wider than the non-dilated portion; a dilatation of 9 mm or more, or a dilatation greater than 2 SD above the mean value for gestational age.

name: impaired fasting glucose
impaired fasting glucose
HP:0025691.def: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG) is indicated by a fasting plasma glucose above normal but below the diabetic range. Levels between 110 mg/dl (6.1 mmol/l) to 125 mg/dl (6.9 mmol/l) are diagnostic of IFG.

name: atelencephaly
atelencephaly
HP:0025692.def: A defect of development of the brain characterized by absence of the telencephalon (embryonic structure from which the mature cerebrum develops).

name: pituitary macroadenoma
pituitary macroadenoma
HP:0025693.def: A pituitary gland adenoma that is larger than 10mm.

name: pituitary microadenoma
pituitary microadenoma
HP:0025694.def: A pituitary adenoma that is less than 10 mm in diameter.

name: mucus plug
mucus plug
HP:0025695.def: Mucus that is abnormally thick in consistency (ie, inspissated) and plugs the airway is known as a mucus plug. Mucus plugs consist of mucins and cells and can partially or completely obstruct one or more airways and cause serious consequences, including atelectasis and recurrent infection.

name: airway casts
airway cast
HP:0025696.def: A replicate of airways from accumulated and condensed mucous and cellular material. These semisolid occlusions take the shape of the airway within they are formed, leading to obstruction of the tracheobronchial tree with consecutive respiratory insufficiency. Based on their principal composition, one can differentiate fibrin casts and mucin casts. Plastic bronchitis is the name of the condition characterized by the formation of airway casts.

name: fibrin casts
fibrin cast
HP:0025697.def: A type of airway casts that consist of plasma components and inflammatory cells.

name: mucin casts
mucin cast
HP:0025698.def: A type of airway casts that consist of impacted mucus.

name: perisylvian fdg hypermetabolism
perisylvian fdg hypermetabolism
HP:0025699.def: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography and computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) evaluates the glucose metabolism of the brain. FDG uptake is interpreted to represent glycolysis. This term therefore represents an abnormally increased FDG uptake (increased glucose metabolism) in the region of the brain that surrounds the Sylvian fissure.

name: anhydramnios
anhydramnios
HP:0025700.def: A complete or near-complete lack of amniotic fluid surrounding a fetus. This finding can be observed sonographically in the third trimesters if the deepest pocket of amniotic fluid is less than or equal to 2 cm.

name: distended jugular lymphatic sacs
distend jugular lymphatic sac
HP:0025701.def: The jugular lymphatic sacs (JLS) are a physiological and temporary part of fetal lymphatic development. They are formed from small buds of lymphatic endothelial cells arising from the internal jugular veins. By 14 weeks gestation they have developed into lymphatic nodes which drain into the systemic circulation. Visibility of JLS on ultrasound past 14 weeks of gestation implies distension and this may be associated with raised nuchal translucency.

name: type 1 schizencephaly
type 1 schizencephaly
HP:0025702.def: A type of Schizencephaly in which there is a trans-mantle column of abnormal grey matter but no evidence of a CSF-containing cleft on MR imaging.

name: type 2 schizencephaly
type 2 schizencephaly
HP:0025703.def: A type of Schizencephaly in which CSF-containing cleft is present with abutting lining lips of abnormal grey matter that are opposed to each other.

name: type 3 schizencephaly
type 3 schizencephaly
HP:0025704.def: A type of Schizencephaly in which CSF-containing cleft present with non-abutting lining lips of abnormal grey matter.

name: abnormal fetal nasal bone visualization
abnormal fetal nasal bone visualization
HP:0025705.def: Abnormal appearance or non-visualization (apparent absence) of the nasal bone of a fetus in first trimester sonographic screening. Assessment of the fetal nasal bone is generally performed at 11-14 weeks gestational age.

name: absent fetal nasal bone
absent fetal nasal bone
HP:0025706.def: The nasal bone is considered absent when it is not visualized on a midsagittal view of the profile. In the second trimester, a true midsagittal view of the fetal profile is obtained and magnified to fill the majority of the image space. The nasal bone appears as an echogenic linear structure below the skin edge. The optimal angle of insonation is 45 degrees to the longitudinal axis of the fetal nasal bone. If the angle of insonation is 0 or 180 degrees, the nasal bone may appear artificially absent. The presence or absence of the nasal bone may be determined at the time of the 11- to 14-week ultrasound examination and used as part of the risk assessment for aneuploidy.

name: hypoplastic nasal bone
hypoplastic nasal bone
HP:0025707.def: Length of the nasal bone below a predetermined cut-off as seen on antenatal ultrasound using standard imaging techniques.

name: early young adult onset
early young adult onset
HP:0025708.def: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 16 to under 19 years.

name: intermediate young adult onset
intermediate young adult onset
HP:0025709.def: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 19 to under 25 years.

name: late young adult onset
late young adult onset
HP:0025710.def: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 25 to under 40 years.

name: convergence - retraction nystagmus
convergence - retraction nystagmus
HP:0025711.def: Convergence-retraction nystagmus is an irregular, jerky nystagmus in which both eyeballs rhythmically converge and retract into the orbit, particularly on attempting an upward gaze.

name: spontaneous chorioamniotic separation
spontaneous chorioamniotic separation
HP:0025712.def: Persistence separation of the chorionic and amnionic membranes after the 16th week of gestation (not as a result of a procedure such as amniocentesis).

name: neurite dystrophy
neurite dystrophy
HP:0025713.def: Dystrophic neurites are abnormal neuronal processes characterized microscopically by aberrant sprouting, dystrophic expansion, and accumulation of various cellular organelles and cytoskeletal/signaling proteins.

name: cerebral cortical microinfarct
cerebral cortical microinfarct
HP:0025714.def: An infarct located on the outer layer of the cerebrum that can only be observed microscopically. Cerebral microinfarcts are typically defined as sharply delimited microscopic regions of cellular death or tissue necrosis, sometimes with cavitation (that is, a central fluid-filled cavity). The term microscopic denotes that these lesions are not visible by gross inspection of the brain but seen by light microscopy. The term infarct is most commonly used for ischemia-related tissue loss, and indeed the pathologic appearance of microinfarcts is consistent with that of known ischemic infarctions.

name: abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform during pregnancy
abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform during pregnancy
HP:0025715.def: Abnormal waveforms the Doppler sonographic examination of bloodflow in the umbilical artery. vUmbilical arterial Doppler assessment is used in surveillance of fetal health in the third trimester.

name: fetal anemia
fetal anemia
HP:0025716.def: Low hemoglobin/hematocrit in a fetus as evidenced by percutaneous umbilical cord sampling and Doppler ultrasonographic assessment of the peak velocity of systolic blood flow in the middle cerebral artery.

name: skeletal muscle autophagosome accumulation
skeletal muscle autophagosome accumulation
HP:0025717.def: Abnormal accumulation of autophagosomes in skeletal muscle tissue.

name: skeletal muscle hyperechogenicity
skeletal muscle hyperechogenicity
HP:0025718.def: An increased echo intensity of muscle tissue on sonography, defined as an increased amount of returning echoes per square area of muscle tissue. On cross-section, normal muscle appears as a relatively anechoic structure with hyperechoic speckles within the tissue representing perimysial septa, giving it a starry night appearance. The boundaries of each muscle are delineated by the presence of hyperechoic fascia. In muscle disorders, one of the hallmark findings is replacement of healthy muscle with fat and fibrosis, manifested by an increase in echogenicity from higher sound transitions in the muscle. This increase in echogenicity is most distinct in conditions that lead to chronic pathology, such as long-standing muscle inflammation, dystrophy, or denervation.

name: maternal vascular malperfusion
maternal vascular malperfusion
HP:0025719.def: Gross findings of maternal vascular malperfusion include placental hypoplasia, placental infarction, and retroplacental hemorrhage. If information is available, it is preferable to annotate using the HPO terms that corresponding to the specific abnormalities.

name: limited horizontal extraocular movement
limited horizontal extraocular movement
HP:0025720.def: Limited mobility of the eye to move from side to side (horizontally) within its socket.

name: limited vertical extraocular movement
limited vertical extraocular movement
HP:0025721.def: Limited mobility of the eye to move up and down (vertically) within its socket.

name: cerebral infarct
cerebral infarct
HP:0025722.def: A necrotic lesion in the cerebrum resulting from a sudden insufficiency of arterial or venous blood supply due to emboli, thrombi or mechanical factors.

name: abnormal fetal skin morphology
abnormal fetal skin morphology
HP:0025723.def: Any structural anomaly of the skin of the fetus or newborn. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: caseous vernix - like desquamation
caseous vernix - like desquamation
HP:0025724.def: Vernix caseosa is a physiological, viscous biofilm that is produced by desquamated fetal skin and sebaceous glands covering the fetus at the third trimester in-utero. The substance's gross morphology in post-partum is described by the etymology, as vernix means varnish, and caseosa means cheesy-like matter. This finding refers to an abnormally thick and greasy vernix caseosa-like scale present at birth.
synonym: greasy , thick vernix caseosa - like scale
greasy , thick vernix caseosa - like scale

name: type 1 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
type 1 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP:0025725.def: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by multiple large cysts or a single dominant cyst.

name: type 2 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
type 2 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP:0025726.def: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by multiple evenly spaced cysts (sponge-like appearance).

name: type 3 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
type 3 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP:0025727.def: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by a bulky firm mass with an adenomatoid appearance.

name: periventricular pseudocyst
periventricular pseudocyst
HP:0025728.def: Pseudocysts that lack an epithelial lining, PVPCs are frequently observed in the caudothalamic groove or in the infero-lateral aspect of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles, but may also be located elsewhere along the periventricular germinal matrix, as in the temporal or occipital horns.

name: fetal vascular malperfusion
fetal vascular malperfusion
HP:0025729.def: The term fetal vascular malperfusion (FVM) is used to describe placental pathology that is throught to result from an obstruction in fetal blood flow that could result from a number of conditions (eg, umbilical cord lesions, hypercoagulability, complications of fetal cardiac dysfunction, such as hypoxia, etc.).

name: foramen ovale aneurysm
foramen ovale aneurysm
HP:0025730.def: Foramen ovale aneurysm (FOA) or atrial septal aneurysm is abnormal redundancy of the atrial septum primum, with bulging of the septum by at least half the width of the atrial chamber, or by at least 10 mm beyond the level of the atrial septum. The abnormal protrusion of the interatrial septum results in decreased left atrial volume. On color Doppler there is reduced left ventricular inflow.

name: emg : repetitive nerve stimulation abnormality
emg : repetitive nerve stimulation abnormality
HP:0030000.def: Abnormality observed upon electromyography when nerve studied is electrically stimulated six to ten times at 2 or 3 Hertz.

name: lagophthalmos
lagophthalmos
HP:0030001.def: A condition in which the eyelids do not close to cover the eye completely.

name: nocturnal lagophthalmos
nocturnal lagophthalmos
HP:0030002.def: The inability to close the eyelids during sleep.
synonym: inability to close the eyelids at night
inability to close the eyelid at night

name: paralytic lagophthalmos
paralytic lagophthalmos
HP:0030003.def: A type of lagophthalmos that occurs in association with facial nerve palsy.

name: cicatricial lagophthalmos
cicatricial lagophthalmos
HP:0030004.def: A type of lagophthalmos that occurs following trauma or surgery.
synonym: eyelids stay open due to scarring
eyelid stay open due to scar
inability to close the eyelids due to scarring
inability to close the eyelid due to scar

name: capillary leak
capillary leak
HP:0030005.def: An acute phenomenon characterized by hypotension and anasarca due to the loss of plasma volume into peripheral tissues, with evidence of decreased plasma volume (hemoconcentration) and protein loss from the intravascular space (hypoalbuminemia) during acute episodes.

name: single fiber emg abnormality
single fiber emg abnormality
HP:0030006.def: Abnormality in single fiber EMG recording, a technique that allows identification of action potentials (APs) from individual muscle fibers.

name: emg : positive sharp waves
emg : positive sharp wave
HP:0030007.def: These are spontaneous firing action potentials stimulated by needle movement of an injured muscle fiber. There is propagation to, but not past, the needle tip. This inhibits the display of the negative deflection of the waveform.

name: cervical insufficiency
cervical insufficiency
HP:0030009.def: A cervix that shows a painless dilation and shortening during the second trimester of pregnancy with resultant recurrent pregnancy loss or delivery is considered incompetent

name: hydrometrocolpos
hydrometrocolpos
HP:0030010.def: Hydrometrocolpos is an accumulation of uterine and vaginal secretions as well as menstrual blood in the uterus and vagina.

name: imperforate hymen
imperforate hymen
HP:0030011.def: A congenital disorder where the hymen (a membrane that surrounds or partially covers the external vaginal opening) does not have an opening and completely obstructs the vagina.

name: female sexual dysfunction
female sexual dysfunction
HP:0030014.def: A problem occurring during any phase of the female sexual response cycle that prevents the individual from experiencing satisfaction from the sexual activity

name: female anorgasmia
female anorgasmia
HP:0030015.def: The persistent of recurrent difficulty, delay in, or absence of attaining orgasm following sufficient sexual stimulation and arousal.

name: dyspareunia
dyspareunia
HP:0030016.def: Recurrent or persistent genital pain associated with sexual intercourse.

name: vaginismus
vaginismus
HP:0030017.def: Recurrent or persistent involuntary spasms of the musculature of the outer third of the vagina that interferes with vaginal penetration, and which causes personal distress.

name: question mark ear
question mark ear
HP:0030022.def: Cleft between the helix and the lobe.

name: quelprud nodule
quelprud nodule
HP:0030023.def: Small cartilaginous prominence on the posterior concha.

name: pretragal ectopia
pretragal ectopia
HP:0030024.def: Variably shaped, cartilage-containing tissue anterior to the external auditory meatus.
synonym: extra cartilage in front of the ear
extra cartilage in front of the ear

name: auricular pit
auricular pit
HP:0030025.def: Small indentation in the lower part of the ascending helix, concha, or in the crus helix.

name: squared superior portion of helix
square superior portion of helix
HP:0030026.def: Flattening instead of curving or rounded superior helix, allowing the superior helix to run more horizontally than usual.

name: abnormal nasal cartilage morphology
abnormal nasal cartilage morphology
HP:0030027.def: A morphological anomaly of the nasal cartilage.

name: absent nasal cartilage
absent nasal cartilage
HP:0030028.def: Lack of a palpable nasal cartilage.
synonym: failure of development of cartilage of nose
failure of development of cartilage of nose
failure of development of nasal cartilage
failure of development of nasal cartilage

name: splayed fingers
splayed finger
HP:0030029.def: Divergence of digits along the A/P axis (in the plane of the palm).

name: absent ray
absent ray
HP:0030030.def: The absence of all phalanges of a digit and the associated metacarpal /metatarsal.

name: small toe
small toe
HP:0030031.def: Significant reduction in both length and girth of the toe compared to the contralateral toe, or alternatively, compared to a typical toe size for an age-matched individual.

name: partial absence of foot
partial absence of foot
HP:0030032.def: An incomplete absence of the foot, with no bony elements distal to the tarsals, but with preservation of some or all of the tarsals.

name: small finger
small finger
HP:0030033.def: Significant reduction in both length and girth of the finger compared to the contralateral finger, or alternatively, compared to a typical finger size for an age-matched individual.

name: glomerular basement membrane lamellation
glomerular basement membrane lamellation
HP:0030034.def: Presence of abnormal additional layers of the basement membrane of the glomerulus.
synonym: lamellated / basket - woven thickened glomerular basement membranes
lamellated / basket - woven thicken glomerular basement membrane
lamellation of the glomerular basement membrane
lamellation of the glomerular basement membrane

name: struvite nephrolithiasis
struvite nephrolithiasis
HP:0030035.def: Presence of struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate) containing calculi (kidney stones).

name: isothenuria
isothenuria
HP:0030036.def: Inability of the kidneys to produce either concentrated or dilute urine.

name: enchondroma
enchondroma
HP:0030038.def: A solitary, benign, intramedullary cartilage tumor that is often found in the short tubular bones of the hands and feet, distal femur, and proximal humerus.

name: fused thoracic vertebrae
fuse thoracic vertebra
HP:0030039.def: A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more thoracic vertebral bodies with one another.

name: fused lumbar vertebrae
fuse lumbar vertebra
HP:0030040.def: A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more lumbar vertebral bodies with one another.

name: schmorl 's node
schmorl 's node
HP:0030041.def: A Schmorl's node is the herniation of nucleus pulposus through the cartilaginous and bony end plate into the body of the adjacent vertebra.

name: incomplete ossification of pubis
incomplete ossification of pubis
HP:0030042.def: Failure to complete ossification (maturation and calcification) of the pubic bone.
synonym: incomplete maturation of the pubic bone
incomplete maturation of the pubic bone

name: hip subluxation
hip subluxation
HP:0030043.def: A partial dislocation of the hip joint, whereby the head of the femur is partially displaced from the socket.

name: flexion contracture of digit
flexion contracture of digit
HP:0030044.def: A bent (flexed) finger or toe joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.

name: hypoglycosylation of alpha - dystroglycan
hypoglycosylation of alpha - dystroglycan
HP:0030046.def: A reduction in the degree of glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan in muscle tissue.

name: abnormal lateral ventricle morphology
abnormal lateral ventricle morphology
HP:0030047.def: A morphological anomaly of the lateral ventricle.

name: colpocephaly
colpocephaly
HP:0030048.def: Colpocephaly is an anatomic finding in the brain manifested by occipital horns that are disproportionately enlarged in comparison with other parts of the lateral ventricles.

name: brain abscess
brain abscess
HP:0030049.def: A collection of pus, immune cells, and other material in the brain.

name: narcolepsy
narcolepsy
HP:0030050.def: An abnormal phenomenon characterized by a classic tetrad of excessive daytime sleepiness with irresistible sleep attacks, cataplexy (sudden bilateral loss of muscle tone), hypnagogic hallucinations, and sleep paralysis.

name: tip - toe gait
tip - toe gait
HP:0030051.def: An abnormal gait pattern characterized by the failure of the heel to contact the floor at the onset of stance during gait.

name: inguinal freckling
inguinal freckling
HP:0030052.def: The presence in the inguinal region (groin) of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

name: perifollicular fibrosis
perifollicular fibrosis
HP:0030054.def: Presence of excess fibrous connective tissue surrounding hair follicules.

name: hyperconvex toenail
hyperconvex toenail
HP:0030055.def: When viewed on end (with the tip of the toe pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the toenail forms a tighter curve of convexity.

name: uncombable hair
uncombable hair
HP:0030056.def: Hair that is disorderly, stands out from the scalp, and cannot be combed flat.

name: autoimmune antibody positivity
autoimmune antibody positivity
HP:0030057.def: The presence of an antibody in the blood circulation that is directed against the organism's own cells or tissues.

name: sickled erythrocytes
sickled erythrocyte
HP:0030058.def: An irreversible distortion of the morphology of an erythrocyte such that the cells are elongated and curved, resembling the blade of a sickle (the hand-held agricultural tool traditionally used to harvest grains).

name: mitochondrial depletion
mitochondrial depletion
HP:0030059.def: An abnormal reduction in mitochondrial DNA content of cells.

name: nervous tissue neoplasm
nervous tissue neoplasm
HP:0030060.def: A neoplasm derived from nervous tissue (not necessarily a neoplasm located in the nervous system).

name: neuroectodermal neoplasm
neuroectodermal neoplasm
HP:0030061.def: A neoplasm arising in the neuroectoderm, the portion of the ectoderm of the early embryo that gives rise to the central and peripheral nervous systems, including some glial cells.

name: craniopharyngioma
craniopharyngioma
HP:0030062.def: A benign pituitary-region neoplasm that originates from Rathke's pouch. Craniopharyngiomas are benign slow growing tumors that are located within the sellar and para sellar region of the central nervous system.

name: neuroepithelial neoplasm
neuroepithelial neoplasm
HP:0030063.def: A neoplasm composed of neural epithelium, not necessarily a neoplasm located in the neural epithelium or neuroepithelium.

name: neurocytoma
neurocytoma
HP:0030064.def: A benign brain tumor composed of neural elements which most often arise from the septum pellucidum and the walls of the lateral ventricles.

name: primitive neuroectodermal tumor
primitive neuroectodermal tumor
HP:0030065.def: A tumor that originates in cells from the primitive neural crest. This group of tumors is characteirzed by the presence of primitive cells with elements of neuronal and/or glial differentiation.

name: ependymoblastoma
ependymoblastoma
HP:0030066.def: A highly malignant embryonal tumor of infancy and young childhood characterized by neuroectodermal elements organized in distinctive multilayered rosettes. Ependymoblastomas are large lesions that occur in the supratentorial compartment, typically displaying a physical connection to the ventricular system.

name: peripheral primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm
peripheral primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm
HP:0030067.def: A primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm that occurs extracranially in soft tissue and bone.

name: olfactory esthesioneuroblastoma
olfactory esthesioneuroblastoma
HP:0030068.def: A malignant olfactory neuroblastoma arising from the olfactory epithelium of the superior nasal cavity and cribriform plate.

name: primary central nervous system lymphoma
primary central nervous system lymphoma
HP:0030069.def: A form of extranodal, high-grade non-Hodgkin B-cell neoplasm, usually large cell or immunoblastic type that originates in the brain, leptomeninges, spinal cord, or eyes and typically remains confined to the CNS.

name: central primitive neuroectodermal tumor
central primitive neuroectodermal tumor
HP:0030070.def: A primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm that occurs in the central nervous system.

name: medulloepithelioma
medulloepithelioma
HP:0030071.def: A primitive neuroectodermal tumor that originates from the cells of the embryonic medullary canal.

name: paranasal sinus neoplasm
paranasal sinus neoplasm
HP:0030072.def: A tumor that originates in the paranasal sinus.

name: chemodectoma
chemodectoma
HP:0030074.def: A usually benign neoplasm originating in the chemoreceptor tissue of the carotid body, glomus jugulare, glomus tympanicum, aortic bodies, or the female genital tract.

name: ductal carcinoma in situ
ductal carcinoma in situ
HP:0030075.def: Presence of abnormal cells inside a milk duct, that is, non-invasive breast cancer. Ductal carcinoma in situ is considered to be a precursor lesion to invasive breast cancer.

name: bronchial neoplasm
bronchial neoplasm
HP:0030077.def: A tumor originating in a bronchus.

name: cervix cancer
cervix cancer
HP:0030079.def: A tumor of the uterine cervix.

name: burkitt lymphoma
burkitt lymphoma
HP:0030080.def: A form of undifferentiated malignant lymphoma commonly manifested as a large osteolytic lesion in the jaw or as an abdominal mass.

name: punctate periventricular t2 hyperintense foci
punctate periventricular t2 hyperintense focus
HP:0030081.def: Multiple pointlike areas of high T2 signal observed upon magnetic resonance imaging of the periventricular cerebral white matter.

name: abnormal drinking behavior
abnormal drinking behavior
HP:0030082.def: Abnormal consumption of fluids with excessive or insufficient consumption of fluid or any other abnormal pattern of fluid consumption.

name: salt craving
salt crave
HP:0030083.def: Hypersalivation, also known as salt craving, refers to an excessive desire to consume salt (sodium chloride) or salty foods.

name: clinodactyly
clinodactyly
HP:0030084.def: An angulation of a digit at an interphalangeal joint in the plane of the palm (finger) or sole (toe).

name: abnormal csf lactate concentration
abnormal csf lactate concentration
HP:0030085.def: Abnormal concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: reduced csf lactate
reduce csf lactate
HP:0030086.def: Decreased concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: abnormal circulating testosterone concentration
abnormal circulate testosterone concentration
HP:0030087.def: An anomalous concentration of testosterone in the blood.

name: increased serum testosterone level
increase serum testosterone level
HP:0030088.def: An elevated circulating testosterone level in the blood.

name: abnormal muscle fiber protein expression
abnormal muscle fiber protein expression
HP:0030089.def: An anomalous amount of protein present in or on the surface of muscle fibers. This feature may be appreciate upon immunohistochemical investigation of muscle biopsy tissue.

name: abnormal muscle fiber merosin expression
abnormal muscle fiber merosin expression
HP:0030090.def: An anomalous amount of merosin in muscle fibers. Merosin is a basement membrane-associated protein found in placenta, striated muscle, and peripheral nerve.

name: absent muscle fiber merosin
absent muscle fiber merosin
HP:0030091.def: Lack of merosin protein in the muscle biopsy.
synonym: absent merosin staining in muscle biopsy
absent merosin stain in muscle biopsy

name: reduced muscle fiber merosin
reduce muscle fiber merosin
HP:0030092.def: A reduced amount of merosin in muscle fibers. This feature is usually assessed by immunohistochemical examination of muscle biopsy tissue.

name: abnormal muscle fiber laminin beta 1
abnormal muscle fiber laminin beta 1
HP:0030093.def: A deviation from normal of the amount of laminin beta 1 in muscle fiber tissue. Laminin 2 is a major component of the basal lamina of skeletal muscle cells. It is a heterotrimer composed of 3 chains: merosin (laminin alpha 2 chain), beta 1, and gamma 1.

name: reduced muscle fiber laminin beta 1
reduce muscle fiber laminin beta 1
HP:0030094.def: A reduced amount of laminin beta 1 in muscle fiber tissue. Laminin 2 is a major component of the basal lamina of skeletal muscle cells. It is a heterotrimer composed of 3 chains: merosin (laminin alpha 2 chain), beta 1, and gamma 1.

name: reduced muscle collagen vi
