reduce muscle collagen vi
HP:0030095.def: A decreased amount of collagen VI in muscle tissue. Collagen VI is a primarily associated with the extracellular matrix of skeletal muscle.

name: abnormal muscle fiber dystrophin expression
abnormal muscle fiber dystrophin expression
HP:0030096.def: A deviation from normal in the amount of dystrophin in muscle fiber tissue. Dystrophin is located at the muscle sarcolemma in a membrane-spanning protein complex that connects the cytoskeleton to the basal lamina.

name: absent muscle dystrophin expression
absent muscle dystrophin expression
HP:0030097.def: Lack of dystrophin in muscle tissue. Immunohistochemistry reveals absent dystrophin protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle dystrophin expression
reduce muscle dystrophin expression
HP:0030098.def: A decreased amount of dystrophin in muscle fiber tissue.

name: reduced muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
reduce muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
HP:0030099.def: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced alpha dystroglycan protein in the muscle biopsy. Alpha-dystroglycan is a heavily glycosylated peripheral-membrane component of the dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex (DAPC), which, in addition to laminin alpha2, binds perlecan and agrin in the extracellular matrix, whereas beta-dystroglycan, derived from the same gene, is a transmembrane protein that links to dystrophin intracellularly.

name: abnormal muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
abnormal muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
HP:0030100.def: Deviation from normal in the amount of alpha sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

name: absent muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
absent muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
HP:0030101.def: Lack of alpha sarcoglycan in muscle. Immunohistochemistry reveals absent alpha sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
reduce muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
HP:0030102.def: A decreased amount of alpha sarcoglycan in muscle. Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced alpha sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: abnormal muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
abnormal muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
HP:0030103.def: Deviation from normal in the amount of beta sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

name: abnormal muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
abnormal muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
HP:0030104.def: Deviation from normal in the amount of gamma sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

name: abnormal muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
abnormal muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
HP:0030105.def: Deviation from normal in the amount of delta sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

name: absent muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
absent muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
HP:0030106.def: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of beta sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
reduce muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
HP:0030107.def: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced beta sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
reduce muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
HP:0030108.def: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced gamma sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: absent muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
absent muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
HP:0030109.def: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of gamma sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: absent muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
absent muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
HP:0030110.def: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of delta sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
reduce muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
HP:0030111.def: Abnormally reduced amount of delta sarcoglycan in muscle.

name: abnormal muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
abnormal muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
HP:0030112.def: A deviation from normal of muscle alpha-dystroglcan expression. Alpha-dystroglycan is a heavily glycosylated peripheral-membrane component of the dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex (DAPC), which, in addition to laminin alpha2, binds perlecan and agrin in the extracellular matrix, whereas beta-dystroglycan, derived from the same gene, is a transmembrane protein that links to dystrophin intracellularly.

name: abnormal muscle fiber dysferlin
abnormal muscle fiber dysferlin
HP:0030113.def: A deviation from normal in the expression of dysferlin in muscle tissue. Dysferlin is an ubiquitous 230-kDa transmembrane protein involved in calcium-mediated sarcolemma resealing.

name: absent muscle fiber dysferlin
absent muscle fiber dysferlin
HP:0030114.def: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of dysferlin protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle fiber dysferlin
reduce muscle fiber dysferlin
HP:0030115.def: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced dysferlin protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: abnormal muscle fiber emerin
abnormal muscle fiber emerin
HP:0030116.def: A deviation from normal of the amount of the inner nuclear membrane protein emerin in muscle tissue.

name: absent muscle fiber emerin
absent muscle fiber emerin
HP:0030117.def: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of emerin protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: reduced muscle fiber emerin
reduce muscle fiber emerin
HP:0030118.def: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced emerin protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: abnormal muscle fiber calpain - 3
abnormal muscle fiber calpain - 3
HP:0030119.def: A deviation from normal in the amount of calpain-3 in muscle tissue. Calpains are intracellular nonlysosomal cysteine proteases modulated by calcium ions. A typical calpain is a heterodimer composed of two distinct subunits, one large (over 80 kDa) and the other small (30 kDa). While only one gene encoding the small subunit has been demonstrated, there are many genes for the large one. CAPN3 is similar to ubiquitous Calpain 1 and 2 (m-calpain and micro-calpain), but contains specific insertion sequences (NS, IS1 and IS2). Calpains cleave target proteins to modify their properties, rather than breaking down the substrates.

name: absent muscle fiber calpain - 3
absent muscle fiber calpain - 3
HP:0030120.def: Western blot shows complete lack of calpain-3 protein in the muscle biopsy tissue.

name: reduced muscle fiber calpain - 3
reduce muscle fiber calpain - 3
HP:0030121.def: Western blot reveals reduced calpain-3 protein in the muscle biopsy tissue.

name: reduced muscle fiber perlecan
reduce muscle fiber perlecan
HP:0030122.def: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced perlecan protein in the muscle biopsy. Perlecan is a basement membrane-specific heparan sulfate proteoglycan core protein (HSPG) also known as heparan sulfate proteoglycan 2 (HSPG2).

name: abnormal muscle fiber lamin a / c
abnormal muscle fiber lamin a / c
HP:0030123.def: A deviation from the normal amount of lamin A/C in muscle tissue. The LMNA gene gives rise to at least three splicing isoforms including the two main isoforms, lamin A and lamin C. These are constitutive components of the fibrous nuclear lamina and have different roles, ranging from mechanical nuclear membrane maintenance to gene regulation.
synonym: abnormal muscle fibre lamin a / c
abnormal muscle fibre lamin a / c

name: reduced muscle fiber lamin a / c
reduce muscle fiber lamin a / c
HP:0030124.def: A decreased amount of lamin A/C in muscle tissue. This feature can be shown by immunohistochemistry or Western blotting of muscle tissue.
synonym: reduced muscle fibre lamin a / c
reduce muscle fibre lamin a / c

name: sacralization of the fifth lumbar vertebra
sacralization of the fifth lumbar vertebra
HP:0030125.def: A congenital anomaly, in which the transverse process of the last lumbar vertebra (L5) fuses to the sacrum on one side or both, or to ilium, or both.

name: abnormal endometrium morphology
abnormal endometrium morphology
HP:0030126.def: An anomaly of the inner mucous membrane of the uterus.

name: endometriosis
endometriosis
HP:0030127.def: The growth of endometrial tissue outside the uterus.

name: impaired ristocetin cofactor assay activity
impaired ristocetin cofactor assay activity
HP:0030129.def: Abnormal response to ristocetin as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ristocetin to platelet-poor plasma.

name: impaired von willebrand factor collagen binding activity
impaired von willebrand factor collagen binding activity
HP:0030130.def: Reduced ability of von Willebrand factor (vWF) to bind collagen. Abnormal response to collagen as manifested by reduced or lacking ability of plasma von WIllebrand Factor to bind collagen. An ELISA-based assay is typically used; the test is sensitive to loss of von Willebrand Factor high molecular weight multimers.

name: abnormal von willebrand factor multimer distribution
abnormal von willebrand factor multimer distribution
HP:0030131.def: Deviation from the normal von Willebrand factor multimer pattern.

name: absence of large von willebrand factor multimers
absence of large von willebrand factor multimers
HP:0030132.def: Absence of large von Willebrand Factor multimers on gel electrophoresis.

name: abnormal presence of ultra - large von willebrand factor multimers
abnormal presence of ultra - large von willebrand factor multimers
HP:0030133.def: Detection of abnormal ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers.

name: total absence von willebrand factor multimers
total absence von willebrand factor multimers
HP:0030134.def: Complete absence of all von Willebrand factor multimers.

name: absence of intermediate von willebrand factor multimers
absence of intermediate von willebrand factor multimers
HP:0030135.def: Lack of intermediate von Willebrand Factor multimers on gel electrophoresis.

name: enhanced ristocetin cofactor assay activity
enhance ristocetin cofactor assay activity
HP:0030136.def: Abnormal response to ristocetin as manifested by increased aggregation of platelets upon addition of low-dose ristocetin to platelet-rich plasma.

name: prolonged bleeding following circumcision
prolonged bleeding follow circumcision
HP:0030137.def: Bleeding that persists for a longer than usual time following circumcision.

name: excessive bleeding from superficial cuts
excessive bleeding from superficial cut
HP:0030138.def: An abnormally increased degree of bleeding following a superfical injury to the surface of the skin.

name: excessive bleeding after a venipuncture
excessive bleeding after a venipuncture
HP:0030139.def: An abnormal high amount of bleeding following the procedure of taking a blood sample.

name: oral cavity bleeding
oral cavity bleeding
HP:0030140.def: Recurrent or excessive bleeding from the mouth.

name: abnormality of the posterior hairline
abnormality of the posterior hairline
HP:0030141.def: An anomaly in the placement or shape of the hairline (trichion) on the back of the head (neck), that is, the border between skin on the back of the head that has head hair.
synonym: abnormality of hairline at back of head
abnormality of hairline at back of head

name: abnormal bowel sounds
abnormal bowel sound
HP:0030142.def: An anomaly of the amount or nature of abdominal sounds. Abdominal sounds (bowel sounds) are made by the movement of the intestines as they promote passage of abdominal contents by peristalsis.

name: hyperactive bowel sounds
hyperactive bowel sound
HP:0030143.def: Abnormally increased gurgling/rumbling sounds made by the movement of fluid and gas in the intestines.

name: hypoactive bowel sounds
hypoactive bowel sound
HP:0030144.def: An decreased amount of bowel sounds.

name: lack of bowel sounds
lack of bowel sound
HP:0030145.def: Complete lack of abdominal sounds as assayed by examination of the abdomen with a stethoscope.

name: abnormal liver parenchyma morphology
abnormal liver parenchyma morphology
HP:0030146.def: A structural anomaly of the liver located predominantly in the hepatocytes as opposed to stromal cells.

name: truncal titubation
truncal titubation
HP:0030147.def: Tremor of the trunk in an anterior-posterior plane at 3-4 Hz.

name: heart murmur
heart murmur
HP:0030148.def: An extra or unusual sound heard during a heartbeat caused vibrations resulting from the flow of blood through the heart.

name: cardiogenic shock
cardiogenic shock
HP:0030149.def: Severely decreased cardiac output with evidence of inadequate end-organ perfusion (i.e., tissue hypoxia) in the presence of adequate intravascular volume.

name: plasmacytosis
plasmacytosis
HP:0030150.def: An abnormally increased number of plasma cells in tissues, exudates, or blood

name: cholangitis
cholangitis
HP:0030151.def: Inflammation of the biliary ductal system, affecting the intrahepatic or extrahepatic portions, or both.

name: cholangiocarcinoma
cholangiocarcinoma
HP:0030153.def: Cholangiocarcinoma is a primary cancer originating in the biliary epithelium i.e., the cholangiocytes, of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic biliary ducts. It is extremely invasive, develops rapidly, often metastasizes, and has a very poor prognosis. They are slow growing tumors which spread longitudinally along the bile ducts with neural, perineural and subepithelial extension.

name: gallbladder perforation
gallbladder perforation
HP:0030154.def: Rupture of the wall of the gallbladder.

name: scrotal pain
scrotal pain
HP:0030155.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the scrotum.

name: bence jones proteinuria
bence jones proteinuria
HP:0030156.def: The presence of free monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains in the urine.

name: flank pain
flank pain
HP:0030157.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the flank.

name: cervical ectropion
cervical ectropion
HP:0030158.def: Cervical ectropion occurs when eversion of the endocervix exposes columnar epithelium to the vaginal milieu

name: cervical polyp
cervical polyp
HP:0030159.def: Abnormal growth of tissue projecting from a mucous membrane of the endocervix.

name: vaginal pruritus
vaginal pruritus
HP:0030161.def: A sensation of itching in the vagina.

name: jaw claudication
jaw claudication
HP:0030164.def: Pain in the jaw or ear induced by chewing or otherwise moving the jaw.

name: temporal artery tortuosity
temporal artery tortuosity
HP:0030165.def: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the temporal artery.

name: night sweats
night sweat
HP:0030166.def: Occurrence of excessive sweating during sleep.

name: antimitochondrial antibody positivity
antimitochondrial antibody positivity
HP:0030167.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against mitochondria.

name: dilated superficial abdominal veins
dilate superficial abdominal vein
HP:0030168.def: Increase in diameter of the veins located underneath the skin of the abdomen.
synonym: dilatation of the superficial abdominal veins
dilatation of the superficial abdominal vein

name: gastric varix
gastric varix
HP:0030169.def: Extreme dilation of the submucusoal veins in the stomach.

name: cystic artery pseudoaneurysm
cystic artery pseudoaneurysm
HP:0030170.def: Presence of a pseudoaneurysm in the artery that supplies the gallbladder and cystic duct with blood. A pseudoaneurysm, also known as a false aneurysm, forms when blood leaks through a breach of the arterial wall but is contained by the adventitia or surrounding perivascular soft tissue.

name: perirenal hematoma
perirenal hematoma
HP:0030171.def: A collection of clotted blood surrounding the kidney.

name: peripheral amyelination
peripheral amyelination
HP:0030172.def: Congenital absence of the myelin sheath on a nerve.

name: increased peripheral myelin thickness
increase peripheral myelin thickness
HP:0030174.def: Elevated thickness of the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves, in a regular and concentric fashion.

name: myelin tomacula
myelin tomacula
HP:0030175.def: The presence of multiple sausage-shaped swellings of the myelin sheath (The Latin tomaculum means sausage).

name: asymmetric peripheral demyelination
asymmetric peripheral demyelination
HP:0030176.def: Loss of myelin from peripheral nerves in a pattern that differs between right and left.

name: abnormality of peripheral nervous system electrophysiology
abnormality of peripheral nervous system electrophysiology
HP:0030177.def: An abnormality of the function of the electrical signals with which peripheral nerve cells communicate with each other or with muscles.

name: abnormality of central nervous system electrophysiology
abnormality of central nervous system electrophysiology
abnormal peripheral action potential amplitude
abnormal peripheral action potential amplitude
HP:0030179.def: An anomaly in the magnitude of the action potential along a peripheral nerve, that is, of the rapid rise and fall of the electrical membrane potential of the nerve.

name: oppenheim reflex
oppenheim reflex
HP:0030180.def: Dorsiflexion of the big toe, sometimes accompanied by fanning of the other toes, elicited by stroking along the medial side of the tibia (the normal response would be no movement of the big toe).

name: gordon reflex
gordon reflex
HP:0030181.def: Dorsal extension of the big toe, sometimes accompanied by fanning of the other toes, elicited by compressing the calf muscles (a normal response is no movement of the big toe).

name: tetraplegia / tetraparesis
tetraplegia / tetraparesis
HP:0030182.def: Loss of strength in all four limbs. Tetraplegia refers to a complete loss of strength, whereas Tetraparesis refers to an incomplete loss of strength.

name: impaired visually enhanced vestibulo - ocular reflex
impair visually enhance vestibulo - ocular reflex
HP:0030183.def: The vestibulo-ocular reflex is responsible for the stabilization of the retinal image during movement. The visual vestibular ocular reflex (VVOR) or visual enhanced VOR, maintains ocular stability during head motion by generating compensatory eye movement opposite to head movement, and is a major component of visual vestibular interaction. This feature is an impairment of this reflex, manifested as the combined impairment of the three compensatory eye movement reflexes, namely the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), smooth pursuit (SP) and optokinetic reflex (OKR).
synonym: visually enhanced vestibulo - ocular reflex impairment
visually enhance vestibulo - ocular reflex impairment

name: isometric tremor
isometric tremor
HP:0030185.def: An isometric tremor occurs with muscle contraction against a rigid stationary object (e.g., when making a fist).

name: kinetic tremor
kinetic tremor
HP:0030186.def: Tremor that occurs during any voluntary movement. It may include visually or non-visually guided movements. Tremor during target directed movement is called intention tremor.

name: titubation
titubation
HP:0030187.def: Nodding movement of the head or body.

name: tremor by anatomical site
tremor by anatomical site
HP:0030188.def: Tremor classified by the affected body part.

name: oral motor hypotonia
oral motor hypotonia
HP:0030190.def: Reduced muscle tone of oral musculature. In infants, this feature may be associated with difficulties in breast feeding, and may affect the latch, jaw motions, tongue placement, lip seal, suck/swallow/breathe pattern and overall feeding behavior.

name: abnormal peripheral nervous system synaptic transmission
abnormal peripheral nervous system synaptic transmission
HP:0030191.def: An anomaly in the communication from a neuron to a target across a synapse in the peripheral nervous system.

name: fatigable weakness of bulbar muscles
fatigable weakness of bulbar muscle
HP:0030192.def: A type of weakness of the bulbar muscles (muscles of the mouth and throat responsible for speech and swallowing) that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of chewing muscles
fatigable weakness of chew muscle
HP:0030193.def: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in chewing that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of speech muscles
fatigable weakness of speech muscle
HP:0030194.def: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in speech that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of swallowing muscles
fatigable weakness of swallow muscle
HP:0030195.def: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in swallowing that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of respiratory muscles
fatigable weakness of respiratory muscle
HP:0030196.def: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in breathing (respiration) that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles
fatigable weakness of skeletal muscle
HP:0030197.def: A type of weakness of skeletal muscle that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of distal limb muscles
fatigable weakness of distal limb muscle
HP:0030198.def: A type of weakness of a skeletal muscle of distal part of a limb that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatigable weakness of neck muscles
fatigable weakness of neck muscle
HP:0030199.def: A type of weakness of a skeletal muscle in the neck that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: fatiguable weakness of proximal limb muscles
fatiguable weakness of proximal limb muscle
HP:0030200.def: A type of weakness of a skeletal muscle of proximal part of a limb that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

name: response to drugs acting on neuromuscular transmission
response to drug act on neuromuscular transmission
HP:0030201.def: Specific drugs interfere selectively with the different cellular mechanisms involved in neuromuscular transmission (synthesis, storage, release, action and inactivation of transmitter). The response of a patient to a specific drug can therefore be useful information for the differential diagnosis.

name: favorable response of weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors
favorable response of weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitor
HP:0030202.def: Improvement of muscle strength in response to administration of an acetylcholine esterase inhibitor.
synonym: favourable response of weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors
favourable response of weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitor

name: unfavorable response of muscle weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors
unfavorable response of muscle weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitor
HP:0030203.def: Lack of improvement of muscle strength in response to administration of an acetylcholine esterase inhibitor.
synonym: unfavourable response of muscle weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors
unfavourable response of muscle weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitor

name: increased jitter at single fiber emg
increase jitter at single fiber emg
HP:0030205.def: The variation in the time interval between the two action potentials of the same motor unit is called jitter. This term therefore applies to increased variability in the interval between successive action potentials of the same motor unit, which is measured by electromyography (EMG).
synonym: increased jitter at single fibre electromyography
increase jitter at single fibre electromyography
increased jitter at single fibre emg
increase jitter at single fibre emg

name: emg : incremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation
emg : incremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation
HP:0030206.def: A compound muscle action potential (CMAP) is a type of electromyography (EMG). CMAP refers to a group of almost simultaneous action potentials from several muscle fibers in the same area evoked by stimulation of the supplying motor nerve and are recorded as one multipeaked summated action potential. This abnormality refers to an abnormal increase in the amplitude during the course of the investigation.

name: paradoxical respiration
paradoxical respiration
HP:0030207.def: Breathing movements in which the chest wall moves in on inspiration and out on expiration, in reverse of the normal movements. It may be seen in children with respiratory distress of any cause, which leads to indrawing of the intercostal spaces during inspiration. Patients with chronic airways obstruction also show indrawing of the lower ribs during inspiration, due to the distorted action of a depressed and flattened diaphragm. Crush injuries of the chest, with fractured ribs and sternum, can lead to a severe degree of paradoxical breathing.

name: anti - acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
anti - acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
HP:0030208.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ganglioside-monosialic acid (GM1), which is a type of glycosphingolipid with one sialic acid. GM1 is located on the outer layer of the plasma membrane, and plays a vital role in neurogenesis, nerve development, differentiation and repair after injury.

name: calcium channel antibody positivity
calcium channel antibody positivity
HP:0030209.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against voltage-gated calcium channels.

name: anti - muscle - specific tyrosine kinase antibody
anti - muscle - specific tyrosine kinase antibody
HP:0030210.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against muscle specific kinase (anti-MuSK Ab).
synonym: anti - muscle - specific tyrosine kinase antibody
anti - muscle - specific tyrosine kinase antibody

name: slow pupillary light response
slow pupillary light response
HP:0030211.def: Reduced velocity and acceleration in the pupillary light response.

name: collectionism
collectionism
HP:0030212.def: Excessive or pathological tendency to save and collect possessions.

name: emotional blunting
emotional blunting
HP:0030213.def: Inability to feel positive or negative emotions, feelings of detachment, or reduced emotional responsiveness.

name: hypersexuality
hypersexuality
HP:0030214.def: Pathological persistent sexual disinhibiting behavior, directed towards oneself or others.

name: inappropriate crying
inappropriate cry
HP:0030215.def: Uncontrolled episodes of crying occur without any apparent motivating stimuli.

name: inertia
inertia
HP:0030216.def: Reduction of goal-directed behaviors linked to the impairment in frontal executive functions (planning of an action for example).

name: limb apraxia
limb apraxia
HP:0030217.def: Difficulty in performing the correct execution of limbs movements in absence of motor impairment.

name: punding
punding
HP:0030218.def: Punding is a stereotypical motor behavior characterized by an intense fascination with repetitive, excessive and non-goal oriented handling, and examining of objects.

name: semantic dementia
semantic dementia
HP:0030219.def: A progressive loss of the ability to remember the meaning of words, faces and objects.

name: socially inappropriate behavior
socially inappropriate behavior
HP:0030220.def: Behavior that is not in line with social norms.

name: sweet craving
sweet crave
HP:0030221.def: Excessive desire to eat sweet foods.

name: visual agnosia
visual agnosia
HP:0030222.def: The condition is known as visual agnosia, which refers to the inability to recognize objects that are visually presented, even though the individual may have normal visual field, acuity, color vision, brightness discrimination, language, and memory.

name: perseverative thought
perseverative thought
HP:0030223.def: Manifestations of perseverative thoughts are behaviors that do not meet the demands of the situation, are not the product of deliberation, and may unfold despite counter intention.

name: abnormal muscle fiber desmin
abnormal muscle fiber desmin
HP:0030224.def: A deviation from normal in the expression of desmin in muscle tissue. Desmin is an 53-kDa protein.

name: accumulation of muscle fiber desmin
accumulation of muscle fiber desmin
HP:0030225.def: Immunohistochemistry shows accumulation of desmin protein in the muscle biopsy.
synonym: muscle fiber desmin - reactive inclusion bodies
muscle fiber desmin - reactive inclusion body
muscle fibre desmin - reactive inclusion bodies
muscle fibre desmin - reactive inclusion body

name: abnormal muscle fiber myotilin
abnormal muscle fiber myotilin
HP:0030226.def: A deviation from normal in the expression of myotilin in muscle tissue. Myotilin is a 57kDa cytoskeletal protein.

name: accumulation of muscle fiber myotilin
accumulation of muscle fiber myotilin
HP:0030227.def: Immunohistochemistry shows accumulation of myotilin protein in the muscle biopsy.

name: abnormal muscle fiber valosin - containing protein
abnormal muscle fiber valosin - containing protein
HP:0030228.def: A deviation from normal in the expression of valosin-containing protein in muscle tissue. Valosin-containing protein is an ubiquitously expressed multifunctional 100-kD protein that is a member of the AAA+ (ATPase associated with various activities) protein family.
synonym: abnormal muscle fibre valosin - containing protein
abnormal muscle fibre valosin - containing protein

name: accumulation of muscle fiber valosin - containing protein
accumulation of muscle fiber valosin - containing protein
HP:0030229.def: Immunohistochemistry shows accumulation of valosin-containing protein in the muscle biopsy.
synonym: accumulation of muscle fibre valosin - containing protein
accumulation of muscle fibre valosin - containing protein

name: central core regions in muscle fibers
central core region in muscle fiber
HP:0030230.def: The presence of disorganized areas called cores in the center of muscle fibers. There is a typical appearance of the biopsy on light microscopy, where the muscle cells have cores that are devoid of mitochondria and specific enzymes. Cores are typically well demarcated and centrally located, but may occasionally be multiple and of eccentric.
synonym: central core regions in muscle fibres
central core region in muscle fibre

name: glycogen accumulation in muscle fiber lysosomes
glycogen accumulation in muscle fiber lysosome
HP:0030231.def: An increased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue found specifically in lysosomes.
synonym: glycogen accumulation in muscle fibre lysosomes
glycogen accumulation in muscle fibre lysosome

name: increased sarcoplasmic glycogen
increase sarcoplasmic glycogen
HP:0030232.def: Elevated glycogen content in the sarcoplasm (cytoplasm) of muscle fibers.

name: bethlem sign
bethlem sign
HP:0030233.def: Limitation of wrist and finger extension on asking patient to form a prayer sign. This is a result of progressive wrist and finger flexion contractures.

name: highly elevated creatine kinase
highly elevate creatine kinase
HP:0030234.def: An increased CPK level between 4X and 50X above the upper normal level.

name: extremely elevated creatine kinase
extremely elevated creatine kinase
HP:0030235.def: An increased creatine kinase level more than 50X above the upper normal level.
synonym: extremely elevated phospho - ck serum level
extremely elevate phospho - ck serum level

name: abnormality of muscle size
abnormality of muscle size
HP:0030236.def: Abnormalities of the overall muscle bulk based on clinical observation.

name: hand muscle weakness
hand muscle weakness
HP:0030237.def: Reduced strength of the musculature of the hand.

name: hypoplasia of the upper arm musculature
hypoplasia of the upper arm musculature
HP:0030239.def: Underdevelopment of the musculature of the upper arm, which may include the deltoid, the triceps, the biceps, and the brachioradialis.

name: portal vein thrombosis
portal vein thrombosis
HP:0030242.def: Thrombosis of the portal vein and/or its tributaries, which include the splenic vein and the superior and inferior mesenteric veins.

name: hepatic vein thrombosis
hepatic vein thrombosis
HP:0030243.def: An obstruction in the veins of the liver caused by a blood clot (thrombosis).

name: maternal fever in pregnancy
maternal fever in pregnancy
HP:0030244.def: The occurence of an elevated body temperature of the mother during pregnancy.

name: intrapartum fever
intrapartum fever
HP:0030245.def: The occurence of maternal fever during labor.

name: maternal first trimester fever
maternal first trimester fever
HP:0030246.def: The occurence of fever in a mother during the first trimester of pregnancy.

name: splanchnic vein thrombosis
splanchnic vein thrombosis
HP:0030247.def: The term splanchnic vein thrombosis encompasses Budd-Chiari syndrome (hepatic vein thrombosis), extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO), and mesenteric vein thrombosis; the word splanchnic is used to refer to the visceral organs (of the abdominal cavity).

name: mesenteric venous thrombosis
mesenteric venous thrombosis
HP:0030248.def: A clot that obstructs blood flow in a mesenteric vein (the superior and the inferior mesenteric vein drain blood from the small and large intestine).

name: enanthema
enanthema
HP:0030249.def: A sudden eruption (rash) of the surface of a mucous membrane of the mouth or pharynx.

name: pulmonary granulomatosis
pulmonary granulomatosis
HP:0030250.def: The presence of multiple granulomata (small nodular inflammatory lesions containing grouped mononuclear phagocytes) in the lung.

name: absence of memory b cells
absence of memory b cell
HP:0030251.def: Complete lack of memory B cells, that is, of mature B cell type that is long-lived, readily activated upon re-encounter of its antigenic determinant, and has been selected for expression of higher affinity immunoglobulin.

name: absent circulating b cells
absent circulate b cell
HP:0030252.def: Complete lack of mature B cells, that is, of B cells that have left the bone marrow.

name: defective t cell proliferation
defective t cell proliferation
HP:0030253.def: A reduced ability of a T cell population to expand by cell division following T cell activation.

name: nail bed hemorrhage
nail bed hemorrhage
HP:0030254.def: Small areas of bleeding (hemorrhage) under the fingernail or toenail.

name: large intestinal polyposis
large intestinal polyposis
HP:0030255.def: The presence of multiple polyps in the large intestine.

name: small intestinal polyposis
small intestinal polyposis
HP:0030256.def: The presence of multiple polyps in the small intestine.

name: freckled genitalia
freckle genitalia
HP:0030257.def: One or more brown punctate macules on the skin of the genitalia.

name: hyperpigmented genitalia
hyperpigmented genitalia
HP:0030258.def: Localized or generalized increased genital pigmentation.

name: hypopigmented genitalia
hypopigmented genitalia
HP:0030259.def: Localized or generalized decreased genital pigmentation.

name: microphallus
microphallus
HP:0030260.def: Length of penis more than 2 SD below the mean for age accompanied by hypospadias.

name: narrow penis
narrow penis
HP:0030262.def: Penile width more than 2 standard deviations (SD) below the mean for age. Alternatively circumference of the flaccid penis more than 2 SD below the mean for age. Alternatively, apparently decreased penile width for age.

name: torsion of the penis
torsion of the penis
HP:0030263.def: Rotated position of the glans, with or without the penile shaft, of 30 degrees or more.

name: webbed penis
web penis
HP:0030264.def: Ventral skinfold extending from penis to scrotum.

name: wide penis
wide penis
HP:0030265.def: Distance between left and right side of the flaccid penis at the attachment to the skin above the pubic symphysis more than 2 standard deviations above the mean for age.

name: obsolete abnormality of the sacroiliac notch
obsolete abnormality of the sacroiliac notch
calcification of the interosseus membrane of the forearm
calcification of the interosseus membrane of the forearm
HP:0030267.def: Deposition of calcium salts in the fibrous sheet that connects the radius and the ulna.

name: hyperplastic callus formation
hyperplastic callus formation
HP:0030268.def: Increased growth of callus, the bony and cartilaginous material that forms a connecting bridge across a bone fracture during fracture healing.

name: increased circulating insulin - like growth factor 1 concentration
increase circulate insulin - like growth factor 1 concentration
HP:0030269.def: An elevated level of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) in the blood circulation.
synonym: increased serum insulin - like growth factor 1
increase serum insulin - like growth factor 1

name: elevated red cell adenosine deaminase activity
elevate red cell adenosine deaminase activity
HP:0030270.def: Increase in the level of adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzyme involved in purine metabolism, within erythrocytes. ADA is involved in the catabolism of adenosine.

name: reduced erythrocyte 2,3 - diphosphoglycerate concentration
reduce erythrocyte 2,3 - diphosphoglycerate concentration
HP:0030271.def: This term refers to an inappropriate low 2,3-DPG concentration in erythrocytes. 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG) controls the movement of oxygen from red blood cells to tissues. Anemia is usually accompanied by an increased level of 2,3-DPG in order to promote tissue oxygenation.

name: abnormal erythrocyte enzyme level
abnormal erythrocyte enzyme level
HP:0030272.def: An altered level of any enzyme to act as catalysts within erythrocytes. This term includes changes due to altered activity of an enzyme.

name: reduced red cell adenosine deaminase level
reduce red cell adenosine deaminase level
HP:0030273.def: Decrease in the level of adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzyme involved in purine metabolism, within erythrocytes. ADA is involved in the catabolism of adenosine.

name: accessory scrotum
accessory scrotum
HP:0030274.def: Additional scrotum, or part of a scrotum in an abnormal location.

name: ectopic scrotum
ectopic scrotum
HP:0030275.def: Scrotum in a position other than the usual position inferior to the base of the penis.

name: abnormal vertebral pedicle morphology
abnormal vertebral pedicle morphology
HP:0030277.def: Abnormal morphology of a vertebral pedical.

name: hypoplastic l5 vertebral pedicle
hypoplastic l5 vertebral pedicle
HP:0030279.def: Underdeveloped pedicle of the fifth lumbar vertebra.

name: rib gap
rib gap
HP:0030280.def: Radiolucent focal defect of a rib shaft.

name: cervical c3 / c4 vertebral fusion
cervical c3 / c4 vertebral fusion
HP:0030281.def: Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C3 and C4, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development.

name: posterior rib gap
posterior rib gap
HP:0030282.def: Radiolucent focal defect of the posterior portion of a rib shaft. The 'gaps' may lead to flail chest.

name: partial absence of the septum pellucidum
partial absence of the septum pellucidum
HP:0030283.def: Only part of the septum pellucidum (a thin, triangular, vertical membrane separating the lateral ventricles of the brain) is present. This feature can be appreciated on magnetic resonance tomography or computed tomography of the brain.

name: triangular tongue
triangular tongue
HP:0030284.def: A form of macrogloassia (increased size of the tongue) characterized by a broad based root of the tongue but a small tongue tip, giving the appearance of a triangle.

name: splayed superior cerebellar peduncle
splay superior cerebellar peduncle
HP:0030285.def: Abnormal splayed configuration (spreading out) of the superior cerebellar peduncle.

name: atrophic superior cerebellar peduncle
atrophic superior cerebellar peduncle
HP:0030286.def: Atrophy of the superior cerebellar peduncle.

name: flattened femoral epiphysis
flatten femoral epiphysis
HP:0030289.def: An abnormal flattening of an epiphysis of femur.
synonym: flattended end part of thigh bone
flattended end part of thigh bone

name: unossified sacrum
unossified sacrum
HP:0030290.def: Lack of ossification of the sacrum.

name: lower - limb metaphyseal irregularity
low - limb metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0030291.def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of one or more metaphyses of a bone of the leg.

name: tibial metaphyseal irregularity
tibial metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0030292.def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of a metaphysis of a tibia.

name: fibular metaphyseal irregularity
fibular metaphyseal irregularity
HP:0030293.def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of a metaphysis of a fibula.
synonym: irregularity of wide portion of calf bone
irregularity of wide portion of calf bone

name: distal femoral metaphyseal abnormality
distal femoral metaphyseal abnormality
HP:0030299.def: An anomaly of the metaphysis of the distal femur (close to the knee).
synonym: abnormality of wide portion of outermost thighbone
abnormality of wide portion of outermost thighbone

name: 10 pairs of ribs
10 pair of rib
HP:0030300.def: Presence of only 10 (instead of the usual 12) pairs of ribs.

name: abnormality of the anterior commissure
abnormality of the anterior commissure
HP:0030301.def: An anomaly of the anterior commissure, a bundle of nerve fibers that connect the two cerebral hemispheres across the midline. The anterior commissure plays a role in pain sensation and contains decussating fibers from the olfactory tracts.

name: abnormal number of vertebrae
abnormal number of vertebra
HP:0030304.def: A deviation from the normal number of vertebrae in the spinal column.

name: 11 thoracic vertebrae
11 thoracic vertebra
HP:0030306.def: The presence of 11 instead of the normal 12 thoracic vertebrae.

name: flared lower limb metaphysis
flare low limb metaphysis
HP:0030307.def: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones of the leg.
synonym: flared metaphysis of lower limb bone
flared metaphysis of low limb bone

name: flared distal tibial metaphysis
flare distal tibial metaphysis
HP:0030308.def: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the distal tibia.

name: flared distal fibular metaphysis
flare distal fibular metaphysis
HP:0030309.def: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the distal fibula.
synonym: flared outermost wide portion of of calf bone
flare outermost wide portion of of calf bone

name: upper extremity joint dislocation
upper extremity joint dislocation
HP:0030310.def: Displacement or malalignment of one or more joints in the upper extremity (arm).

name: lower extremity joint dislocation
low extremity joint dislocation
HP:0030311.def: Displacement or malalignment of one or more joints in the lower extremity (leg).

name: obliteration of the calvarial diploe
obliteration of the calvarial diploe
HP:0030312.def: Absence of the spongy bone structure (or tissue) of the internal part of the skull cap (i.e., of the calvarial diploe).

name: abnormal periosteum morphology
abnormal periosteum morphology
HP:0030313.def: An anomalous structure of the periosteum, i.e., of the membrane that covers the outer surface of bones.

name: angular cheilitis
angular cheilitis
HP:0030318.def: A type of inflammation of the lips involving one or both of the corners of the mouth.
synonym: inflammation of corners of the mouth
inflammation of corner of the mouth
red and sore corners of the mouth
red and sore corner of the mouth

name: weakness of facial musculature
weakness of facial musculature
HP:0030319.def: Reduced strength of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

name: increased intervertebral space
increase intervertebral space
HP:0030320.def: An increase in the vertical distance between adjacent vertebral bodies, observed as an increase in the intervertebral disc space.

name: abnormal vertebral artery morphology
abnormal vertebral artery morphology
HP:0030321.def: An anomaly of the vertebral artery, the major artery of the neck that originates from the subclavian artery and merges to form the single midline basilar artery in a complex called the vertebrobasilar system.

name: unilateral vertebral artery hypoplasia
unilateral vertebral artery hypoplasia
HP:0030323.def: Underdevelopment of the vertebral artery on one side.

name: bilateral vertebral artery hypoplasia
bilateral vertebral artery hypoplasia
HP:0030324.def: Underdevelopment of the vertebral artery on both sides.

name: cervicomedullary schisis
cervicomedullary schisis
HP:0030325.def: Fissure within the spinal cord of the neck.

name: abnormal macrophage count
abnormal macrophage count
HP:0030326.def: An anomaly in the number of macrophages.

name: abnormal osteoclast count
abnormal osteoclast count
HP:0030327.def: An anomaly in the number of osteoclasts in bone tissue, bone-resorbing cells that develop from macrophages. This finding can be observed by histological examination of bone tissue.

name: decreased osteoclast count
decrease osteoclast count
HP:0030328.def: Decreased number of osteoclasts in bone tissue.

name: retinal thinning
retinal thinning
HP:0030329.def: Reduced anteroposterior thickness of the retina. This phenotype can be appreciated by retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT).

name: multinucleated giant chondrocytes in epiphyseal cartilage
multinucleated giant chondrocytes in epiphyseal cartilage
HP:0030330.def: The presence of cartilage cells (chondrocytes) that are substantially increased in size and contain more than one nucleus and are located within the resting zone of the epiphyseal cartilage.

name: impaired stimulus - induced skin wrinkling
impaired stimulus - induced skin wrinkling
HP:0030331.def: A reduced ability of the skin of the fingertips to wrinkle when exposed to stimuli such as soaking in water or application of EMLA cream (the fingertip remains smooth).

name: abnormal alpha - beta t cell morphology
abnormal alpha - beta t cell morphology
HP:0030333.def: A structuraly anomaly of T cells that express an alpha-beta T cell receptor.

name: abnormal cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive , alpha - beta regulatory t cell morphology
abnormal cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive , alpha - beta regulatory t cell morphology
HP:0030334.def: A structural anomaly of a CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta T cell. These cells are regulatory T cells.

name: abnormal cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive , alpha - beta regulatory t cell count
abnormal cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive , alpha - beta regulatory t cell count
HP:0030335.def: A deviation from the normal count of CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cells.

name: absence of cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive regulatory t cells
absence of cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive regulatory t cell
HP:0030336.def: Lack of CD4+CD25+ T regulatory cells.
synonym: absence of cd4+cd25+ t regulatory cells
absence of cd4+cd25+ t regulatory cell

name: elevated cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive regulatory t cell count
elevate cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive regulatory t cell count
HP:0030337.def: An increased number of CD4-positive, CD25-positive regulatory T cells.

name: abnormal circulating gonadotropin concentration
abnormal circulate gonadotropin concentration
HP:0030338.def: An anomaly of the circulating level of a gonadotropin, that is, of a protein hormone secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary of vertebrates. The primary gonadotropins are luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

name: decreased circulating gonadotropin concentration
decrease circulate gonadotropin concentration
HP:0030339.def: A reduction of the circulating level of a gonadotropin, that is, of a protein hormone secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary of vertebrates. The primary gonadotropins are luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

name: decreased circulating follicle stimulating hormone concentration
decrease circulate follicle stimulate hormone concentration
HP:0030341.def: A reduction of the circulating level of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
synonym: decreased circulating follicle stimulating hormone level
decrease circulate follicle stimulate hormone level

name: decreased circulating luteinizing hormone level
decrease circulate luteinizing hormone level
HP:0030344.def: A reduction in the circulating level of luteinizing hormone (LH).

name: abnormal circulating luteinizing hormone concentration
abnormal circulate luteinizing hormone concentration
HP:0030345.def: An anomaly of the circulating level of luteinizing hormone (LH).

name: abnormal circulating follicle - stimulating hormone concentration
abnormal circulate follicle - stimulate hormone concentration
HP:0030346.def: An anomaly of the circulating level of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
synonym: abnormal circulating follicle - stimulating hormone level
abnormal circulate follicle - stimulate hormone level

name: abnormal circulating androgen level
abnormal circulate androgen level
HP:0030347.def: An anomaly in the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.

name: increased circulating androgen concentration
increase circulate androgen concentration
HP:0030348.def: An elevation of the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.

name: decreased circulating androgen concentration
decrease circulate androgen concentration
HP:0030349.def: A reduction in the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.

name: erythematous papule
erythematous papule
HP:0030350.def: A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid that is reddish (erythematous) in color.

name: urticarial plaque
urticarial plaque
HP:0030351.def: A well-circumscribed, intensely pruritic, raised wheal (edema of the superficial skin) typically 1 to 2 cm in diameter.

name: abnormal serum insulin - like growth factor 1 level
abnormal serum insulin - like growth factor 1 level
HP:0030352.def: An anomalous level of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) in the blood circulation.

name: decreased serum insulin - like growth factor 1
decrease serum insulin - like growth factor 1
HP:0030353.def: A reduced level of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interferon concentration
abnormal circulate interferon concentration
HP:0030354.def: Abnormal levels of interferon in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating interferon - gamma concentration
abnormal circulate interferon - gamma concentration
HP:0030355.def: Abnormal levels of interferon gamma measured in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interferon - gamma concentration
increase circulate interferon - gamma concentration
HP:0030356.def: An elevation in the concentration of interferon gamma measured in the blood circulation.

name: small cell lung carcinoma
small cell lung carcinoma
HP:0030357.def: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a type of highly malignant lung cancer that is composed of small ovoid cells. In the past, SCLC was called oat cell carcinoma because the microscopic appearance of the cells was felt to resemble oats. SLCLC usually originates near the bronchi and in many cases may grow and metastasize quickly.

name: squamous cell lung carcinoma
squamous cell lung carcinoma
HP:0030359.def: A type of non-small cell lung carcinoma that is derived from stratified squamous epithelial cells.

name: large cell lung carcinoma
large cell lung carcinoma
HP:0030360.def: A type of non-small cell lung carcinoma that is derived from undifferentiated malignant neoplasms originating from transformed epithelial cells in the lung, and which is differentiate from small-cell lung carcinoma by the larger size of the anaplastic cells, a higher cytoplasmic-to-nuclear size ratio, and a lack of salt-and-pepper appearance of the chromatin.

name: abnormal circulating eicosanoid concentration
abnormal circulate eicosanoid concentration
HP:0030361.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of an icosanoid (also known as eicosanoids). These are signaling molecules derived from oxidation of 20-carbon fatty acids. Most are produced from arachidonic acid, a 20-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acid (5,8,11,14-eicosatetraenoic acid).

name: reduced muscle carnitine level
reduce muscle carnitine level
HP:0030362.def: A reduction in the level of carnitine in muscle tissue.

name: primary caesarian section
primary caesarian section
HP:0030363.def: Delivery by Caesarian section representing the first time the mother has delivered by Caesarian section.

name: secondary caesarian section
secondary caesarian section
HP:0030364.def: Delivery by Caesarian section representing where the mother has already had a previous Cesarean delivery, and this is a repeat Cesarean birth.

name: vaginal birth after caesarian
vaginal birth after caesarian
HP:0030365.def: Vaginal birth after Caesarian (VBAC) refers to the situation where the mother has had a previous Cesarean delivery but has now delivered vaginally.

name: delivery by odon device
delivery by odon device
HP:0030366.def: The Odon device is an instrument for assisted vaginal deliveries that is applied on the head of the baby and used to apply traction to assist the birth process.

name: finger hyperphalangy
finger hyperphalangy
HP:0030367.def: Hyperphalangy is a digit morphology in which increased numbers of phalanges are arranged linearly within a digit. That is, there is an accessory phalanx that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges.

name: hyperphalangy of the 2nd finger
hyperphalangy of the 2nd finger
HP:0030368.def: An accessory phalanx of the index (second) finger that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges. Hyperphalangy of the index finger results from an accessory ossification center at the metacarpophalangeal joint, resulting in radial deviation of the index finger. Note that this term refers only to this type of hyperphalangy.

name: induced vaginal delivery
induced vaginal delivery
HP:0030369.def: Vaginal delivery following induction of labor, a procedure used to stimulate uterine contractions during pregnancy before labor begins on its own.

name: abnormal proportion of naive b cells
abnormal proportion of naive b cell
HP:0030370.def: A deviation in the normal proportion of naive B cells (CD19+/CD27-/IgD+/IgM+) relative to the total number of B cells. Naive B cells represent one of the subtypes of B cells in the peripheral blood, and are B cells that have not been exposed to antigen.

name: increased proportion of naive b cells
increase proportion of naive b cell
HP:0030371.def: An elevation above the normal proportion of naive B cells (CD19+/CD27-/IgD+/IgM+) relative to total number of B cells. Naive B cells represent one of the subtypes of B cells in the peripheral blood, and are B cells that have not been exposed to antigen.

name: decreased proportion of naive b cells
decreased proportion of naive b cell
HP:0030372.def: A reduction below normal proportion of naive B cells (CD19+/CD27-/IgD+/IgM+) relative to total number of B cells. Naive B cells represent one of the subtypes of B cells in the peripheral blood, and are B cells that have not been exposed to antigen.

name: abnormal proportion of memory b cells
abnormal proportion of memory b cell
HP:0030373.def: A deviation of the normal proportion of memory B cells in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Memory B cells develop from naive B cells. Upon antigen rechallenge, memory B cells rapidly expand and differentiate into plasma cells under the cognate control of memory Th cells (Phase IV).

name: decreased proportion of memory b cells
decreased proportion of memory b cell
HP:0030374.def: A reduction in the normal proportion of memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. Memory B cells develop from naive B cells. Upon antigen rechallenge, memory B cells rapidly expand and differentiate into plasma cells under the cognate control of memory Th cells (Phase IV).

name: increased proportion of memory b cells
increase proportion of memory b cell
HP:0030375.def: An elevation in the proportion of memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. Memory B cells develop from naive B cells. Upon antigen rechallenge, memory B cells rapidly expand and differentiate into plasma cells under the cognate control of memory Th cells (Phase IV).

name: abnormal proportion of immature b cells
abnormal proportion of immature b cell
HP:0030376.def: A deviation from normal proportion of immature B cells (CD19+/ CD21low) in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Immature B cells (IgM+) are still in final stages of development within the bone marrow. Naive B cells are those which have left the bone marrow, before they bind to the antigen for which they're specific (IgM+/IgD+).
synonym: abnormal proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cells
abnormal proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cell

name: increased proportion of immature b cells
increase proportion of immature b cell
HP:0030377.def: An elevation in the proportion above normal of immature B cells (CD19+/ CD21low) in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Immature B cells (IgM+) are still in final stages of development within the bone marrow. Naive B cells are those which have left the bone marrow, before they bind to the antigen for which they're specific (IgM+/IgD+).
synonym: increased proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cells
increase proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cell

name: decreased proportion of immature b cells
decreased proportion of immature b cell
HP:0030378.def: A reduction in normal proportion of immature B cells (CD19+/ CD21low)in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Immature B cells (IgM+) are still in final stages of development within the bone marrow. Naive B cells are those which have left the bone marrow, before they bind to the antigen for which they're specific (IgM+/IgD+).
synonym: decreased proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cells
decreased proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cell

name: abnormal proportion of transitional b cells
abnormal proportion of transitional b cell
HP:0030379.def: A deviation in the normal proportion of transitional B cells (CD19+/CD38high/IgMhigh) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. B cells originate from precursors in the bone marrow, and the first cells which migrate to the peripheral blood have been classified as transitional B cells.

name: decreased proportion of transitional b cells
decreased proportion of transitional b cell
HP:0030380.def: A reduction in the normal proportion of transitional B cells (CD19+/CD38high/IgMhigh) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. B cells originate from precursors in the bone marrow, and the first cells which migrate to the peripheral blood have been classified as transitional B cells.

name: increased proportion of transitional b cells
increase proportion of transitional b cell
HP:0030381.def: An elevation in the normal proportion of transitional B cells (CD19+/CD38high/IgMhigh) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. B cells originate from precursors in the bone marrow, and the first cells which migrate to the peripheral blood have been classified as transitional B cells.

name: abnormal proportion of marginal zone b cells
abnormal proportion of marginal zone b cell
HP:0030383.def: A deviation of the normal proportion of marginal zone B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.

name: decreased proportion of marginal zone b cells
decreased proportion of marginal zone b cell
HP:0030384.def: A reduction in the normal proportion of marginal zone B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.

name: increased proportion of marginal zone b cells
increase proportion of marginal zone b cell
HP:0030385.def: An elevation in the normal proportion of marginal zone B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.

name: abnormal proportion of class - switched memory b cells
abnormal proportion of class - switched memory b cell
HP:0030386.def: A deviation of the normal proportion of class-switched memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM-/IgD-) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. Marginal zone B cells undergo limited somatic hypermutation and produce high-affinity IgM and some IgG, whereas class-switched memory B cells synthetize IgG, IgM, and IgA.

name: increased proportion of class - switched memory b cells
increase proportion of class - switched memory b cell
HP:0030387.def: An increase in the normal proportion of class-switched memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) relative to the total number of B cells. Marginal zone B cells undergo limited somatic hypermutation and produce high-affinity IgM and some IgG, whereas class-switched memory B cells synthetize IgG, IgM, and IgA.

name: decreased proportion of class - switched memory b cells
decreased proportion of class - switched memory b cell
HP:0030388.def: A reduction in the normal proportion of class-switched memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) relative to the total number of B cells. Marginal zone B cells undergo limited somatic hypermutation and produce high-affinity IgM and some IgG, whereas class-switched memory B cells synthetize IgG, IgM, and IgA.

name: abnormal circulating thromboxane concentration
abnormal circulate thromboxane concentration
HP:0030389.def: Any deivation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of a thromboxane. Thromboxanes are derived from prostaglandin precursors in platelets, and stimulate aggregation of platelets and constriction of blood vessels.

name: reduced circulating leukotriene c4 concentration
reduce circulate leukotriene c4 concentration
HP:0030390.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of leukotriene C4 in the blood circulation.

name: spoken word recognition deficit
speak word recognition deficit
HP:0030391.def: Reduced ability of lexical discrimination, which refers to the process of distinguishing a stimulus word from other phonologically similar words. Lexical discrimination can be defined as the process of correctly identifying words in the mental lexicon to match the phonological input of a stimulus.

name: choroid plexus carcinoma
choroid plexus carcinoma
HP:0030392.def: Intraventricular papillary neoplasm derived from choroid plexus epithelium. Plexus tumors are most common in the lateral and fourth ventricles; while 80% of lateral ventricle tumors present in children, fourth ventricle tumors are evenly distributed in all age groups. Clinically, choroid plexus tumors tend to cause hydrocephalus and increased intracranial pressure. Histologically, choroid plexus papillomas correspond to WHO grade I, choroid plexus carcinomas to WHO grade III.

name: endolymphatic sac tumor
endolymphatic sac tumor
HP:0030393.def: A low-grade papillary epithelial neoplasm (adenocarcinoma) with a slow growth pattern. The endolymphatic duct emerges from the posterior wall of the saccule (of the inner ear) and ends in a blind pouch, the endolymphatic sac. Endolymphatic sac tumors (ELSTs) are known under different names in the literature (Heffner tumor, aggressive papillary middle ear tumor, and low-grade adenocarcinoma of endolymphatic sac origin).
synonym: low - grade adenocarcinoma of endolymphatic sac origin
low - grade adenocarcinoma of endolymphatic sac origin

name: fallopian tube carcinoma
fallopian tube carcinoma
HP:0030394.def: Carcinoma that originates in the Fallopian tube. It may be located in the wall or within the lumen as a growth attached to the wall by a stalk.

name: abnormal platelet granule secretion
abnormal platelet granule secretion
HP:0030396.def: Platelets are replete with secretory granules, which are critical to normal platelet function. Among the three types of platelet secretory granules - alpha-granules, dense granules, and lysosomes - the alpha-granule is the most abundant. Granule contents must be released from their intracellular repository in order to achieve their physiologic function, and this term refers to a functional defect in granule secretion.

name: abnormal platelet dense granule secretion
abnormal platelet dense granule secretion
HP:0030397.def: Abnormal release of dense granules from platelets.

name: abnormal platelet atp dense granule secretion
abnormal platelet atp dense granule secretion
HP:0030398.def: Abnormal secretion of the platelet dense-granule content adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

name: abnormal platelet alpha granule secretion
abnormal platelet alpha granule secretion
HP:0030399.def: Abnormal release of alpha granule contents from platelets.

name: abnormal platelet lysosome secretion
abnormal platelet lysosome secretion
HP:0030400.def: Abnormal release of lysosome contents from platelets.

name: abnormal platelet dense granule atp / adp ratio
abnormal platelet dense granule atp / adp ratio
HP:0030401.def: Deviation from normal of the ratio of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to adenosine diphosphate (ADP) within platelets.

name: abnormal platelet aggregation
abnormal platelet aggregation
HP:0030402.def: An abnormality in the rate and degree to which platelets aggregate after the addition of an agonist that stimulates platelet clumping. Platelet aggregation is measured using aggregometer to measure the optical density of platelet-rich plasma, whereby platelet aggregation causes the plasma to become more transparent.

name: spontaneous platelet aggregation
spontaneous platelet aggregation
HP:0030403.def: Clumping together of platelets in the blood in a platelet aggregation test without addition of agents normally used to induce aggregation.

name: glucagonoma
glucagonoma
HP:0030404.def: An endocrine tumor of the pancreas that secretes excessive amounts of glucagon.

name: pancreatic endocrine tumor
pancreatic endocrine tumor
HP:0030405.def: A neuroendocrine tumor originating in a hormone-producing cell (islet cell) of the pancreas.

name: primary peritoneal carcinoma
primary peritoneal carcinoma
HP:0030406.def: A type of cancer that originates in the peritoneum. It is to be distinguished from metastatic cancer of the peritoneum. Peritoneal cancer can occur anywhere in the abdominal space, and affects the surface of organs contained inside the peritoneum.

name: pineocytoma
pineocytoma
HP:0030407.def: A type of pineal parenchymal cell neoplasm that is a mature well-differentiated tumor (WHO grade I).

name: pineoblastoma
pineoblastoma
HP:0030408.def: Pineoblastoma is a rare primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) arising in the pineal gland. Pineoblastomas are classified as a WHO grade IV tumor and comprise one-fourth to one-half of pineal parenchymal tumors. Pineoblastoma is a highly cellular tumor originating in the pineal gland and containing small, poorly differentiated cells.

name: renal transitional cell carcinoma
renal transitional cell carcinoma
HP:0030409.def: A malignant tumor that arises from the transitional (urothelial) epithelial cells lining the urinary tract from the renal calyces to the ureteral orifice.

name: sebaceous gland carcinoma
sebaceous gland carcinoma
HP:0030410.def: A carcinoma that arises in a sebaseous gland (an exocrine gland of the skin that secretes sebum, a waxy substance)

name: jejunal adenocarcinoma
jejunal adenocarcinoma
HP:0030411.def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the jejunum.

name: ileal adenocarcinoma
ileal adenocarcinoma
HP:0030412.def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the ileum.

name: squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue
squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue
HP:0030413.def: A carcinoma derived from a squamous epithelial cell of the tongue.

name: verrucous cell carcinoma of the tongue
verrucous cell carcinoma of the tongue
HP:0030414.def: A low-grade variant of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue with a warty (verrucous) appearance.

name: sarcomatoid carcinoma of the tongue
sarcomatoid carcinoma of the tongue
HP:0030415.def: Sarcomatoid (spindle cell) carcinomas of the tongue is a variant of squamous carcinoma of tongue that is monoclonal, having evolved from a conventional squamous carcinoma with dedifferentiation associated with sarcomatoid transformation.
synonym: spindle cell carcinoma of the tongue
spindle cell carcinoma of the tongue

name: vulvar neoplasm
vulvar neoplasm
HP:0030416.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the female external genital tract (vulva).

name: squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva
squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva
HP:0030417.def: A cancer that originates in the squamous cells that line the surface of the vulva.

name: vulvar melanoma
vulvar melanoma
HP:0030418.def: A type of vulvar cancer that originates from melanocytes of the vulva.

name: bartholin gland carcinoma
bartholin gland carcinoma
HP:0030419.def: A cancer arising in a cell of the Bartholin gland, a racemose gland located slightly posterior to the opening of the vagina.

name: vulvar adenocarcinoma
vulvar adenocarcinoma
HP:0030420.def: An adenocarcinoma arising in the vulva.

name: epididymal neoplasm
epididymal neoplasm
HP:0030421.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the epididymis, an duct that transports spermatozoa from the testis to the vas deferens.

name: obsolete papillary cystadenoma of the epididymis
obsolete papillary cystadenoma of the epididymis
splenic cyst
splenic cyst
HP:0030423.def: A closed sac located in the spleen.

name: epididymal cyst
epididymal cyst
HP:0030424.def: A smooth, extratesticular, spherical cyst in the head of the epididymis.

name: calcified ovarian cyst
calcified ovarian cyst
HP:0030425.def: A cyst of the ovary that exhibits deposition of calcium salts.

name: ossifying fibroma
ossify fibroma
HP:0030426.def: A benign central bone tumor composed of fibrous connective tissue within which bone is formed.

name: ossifying fibroma of the jaw
ossify fibroma of the jaw
HP:0030427.def: A benign central bone tumor of the jaw composed of fibrous connective tissue within which bone is formed.

name: cutaneous myxoma
cutaneous myxoma
HP:0030428.def: A myxoma originating in the skin.

name: juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
HP:0030429.def: A benign but highly vascular nasopharyngeal neoplasm. The tumor originates from the sphenopalatine foramen and involves both the pterygopalatine fossa and the posterior nasal cavity.

name: neuroma
neuroma
HP:0030430.def: A tumor made up of nerve cells and nerve fibers.

name: osteochondroma
osteochondroma
HP:0030431.def: A cartilage capped bony outgrowth of a long bone. Osteochondroma arises on the external surface of bone containing a marrow cavity that is continuous with that of the underlying bone.

name: chondroblastoma
chondroblastoma
HP:0030432.def: A usually benign tumor composed of cells which arise from chondroblasts or their precursors and which tend to differentiate into cartilage cells.

name: osteoid osteoma
osteoid osteoma
HP:0030433.def: A bening tumor of bone composed of a central zone named nidus which is an atypical bone completely enclosed within a well vascularized stroma and a peripheral sclerotic reaction zone.

name: pilomatrixoma
pilomatrixoma
HP:0030434.def: Pilomatricoma is an asymptomatic slowly growing benign cutaneous tumor, differentiating towards the hair matrix of the hair follicle. It is covered by normal or hyperemic skin, and usually varies in size from 0.5 to 3 cm.

name: fibrofolliculoma
fibrofolliculoma
HP:0030436.def: Fibrofolliculoma is a clinically asymptomatic, 2-4 mm, skin-colored, dome-shaped smooth papule. It usually arises in the form of multiple lesions in adults in different areas such as the scalp, forehead, face, and neck. According to histology, the lesion is a fibrotic hamartoma characterized by infundibular epithelial proliferation and perifollicular fibrous proliferation.

name: anal canal squamous cell carcinoma
anal canal squamous cell carcinoma
HP:0030438.def: A squamous cell carcinoma that originates in the anal canal.

name: anal canal adenocarcinoma
anal canal adenocarcinoma
HP:0030439.def: An adenoma carcinoma that originates in the anal canal.

name: anal margin neoplasm
anal margin neoplasm
HP:0030440.def: A tumor of the anal margin.

name: anal margin paget 's disease
anal margin paget 's disease
HP:0030441.def: An intraepithelial adenocarcinoma originating in the anal margin and characterized by presence of typical Paget's cells, appearing as large rounded vacuolated cells.

name: anal margin squamous cell carcinoma
anal margin squamous cell carcinoma
HP:0030442.def: A squamous cell carcinoma that originates in the skin of the anal margin.

name: anal margin basal cell carcinoma
anal margin basal cell carcinoma
HP:0030443.def: A basal cell carcinoma that originates in the anal margin.

name: anal margin melanoma
anal margin melanoma
HP:0030444.def: A melanoma that originates in the anal margin.

name: pulmonary carcinoid tumor
pulmonary carcinoid tumor
HP:0030445.def: A malignant neuroendocrine tumor of the lung. According to histopathologic criteria (WHO 2004), carcinoids are divided into four groups i.e. typical and atypical carcinoids, large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and small cell lung carcinoma.

name: merkel cell skin cancer
merkel cell skin cancer
HP:0030447.def: A malignant cutaneous tumor of the elderly that is characterized by an aggressive course with regional nodal involvement, distant metastases and a high rate of recurrence. Most patients present with rapidly growing, painless, firm, non-tender, dome-shaped red, occasionally ulcerated skin nodules, which have a red or bluish color, measuring up to several centimeters, on predominantly sun-exposed areas of the body. The overlying skin is smooth and shiny, sometimes exhibiting ulcerative, acneiform or telangiectatic features.
synonym: merkel cell cancer of the skin
merkel cell cancer of the skin
primary small cell carcinoma of the skin
primary small cell carcinoma of the skin
primary undifferentiated carcinoma of the skin
primary undifferentiated carcinoma of the skin

name: soft tissue sarcoma
soft tissue sarcoma
HP:0030448.def: A type of sarcoma (A connective tissue neoplasm formed by proliferation of mesodermal cells) that develops from soft tissues like fat, muscle, nerves, fibrous tissues, blood vessels, or deep skin tissues.

name: therapeutic abortion
therapeutic abortion
HP:0030449.def: Delivery by means of therapeutic termination of pregnancy. Therapeutic abortion may be done to end a pregnancy if the mother's life is in danger or if the baby has abnormalities involving the major organ systems and is not expected to survive after birth or by choice.

name: neoplasm of the autonomic nervous system
neoplasm of the autonomic nervous system
HP:0030450.def: A tumor that arises from an element of the autonomic nervous system.

name: mesenteric cyst
mesenteric cyst
HP:0030451.def: A closed fluid filled sac originating from the mesentary.

name: chylolymphatic mesenteric cyst
chylolymphatic mesenteric cyst
HP:0030452.def: A type of mesenteric cyst that is lined with a thin endothelium or mesothelium and filled with chylous and lymphatic fluid.

name: abnormal electrooculogram
abnormal electrooculogram
HP:0030454.def: The clinical electro-oculogram (EOG) is an electrophysiological test of function of the outer retina and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) in which changes in electrical potential across the RPE are recorded during successive periods of dark and light adaptation.

name: abnormality of pattern visual evoked potentials
abnormality of pattern visual evoke potential
abnormality of pattern onset / offset visual evoked potentials
abnormality of pattern onset / offset visual evoked potential
synonym: abnormality of pattern onset / offset vep
abnormality of pattern onset / offset vep

name: abnormal amplitude of pattern onset / offset visual evoked potentials
abnormal amplitude of pattern onset / offset visual evoked potential
synonym: abnormal amplitude of pattern onset / offset vep
abnormal amplitude of pattern onset / offset vep

name: abnormal timing of pattern onset / offset visual evoked potentials
abnormal timing of pattern onset / offset visual evoked potential
abnormal timing of pattern reversal visual evoked potentials
abnormal timing of pattern reversal visual evoke potential
abnormal timing of flash visual evoked potentials
abnormal timing of flash visual evoke potential
abnormal amplitude of flash visual evoked potentials
abnormal amplitude of flash visual evoke potential
asymmetrical distribution of flash visual evoked potentials
asymmetrical distribution of flash visual evoke potential
synonym: crossed asymmetry of flash visual evoked potentials
crossed asymmetry of flash visual evoke potential

name: asymmetrical distribution of pattern reversal visual evoked potentials
asymmetrical distribution of pattern reversal visual evoke potential
synonym: crossed asymmetry of pattern reversal visual evoked potentials
crossed asymmetry of pattern reversal visual evoke potential

name: undetectable light - adapted electroretinogram
undetectable light - adapt electroretinogram
