HP:0030465.def: No detectable response to the light-adapted 3.0 ERG (single-flash cone response). This type of ERG measures responses of the cone system; a-waves arise from cone photoreceptors and cone off-bipolar cells; the b-wave comes from On- and Off-cone bipolar cells.
synonym: absent photopic ( cone ) responses on erg
absent photopic ( cone ) responses on erg

name: abnormal pattern electroretinogram
abnormal pattern electroretinogram
HP:0030467.def: An anomalous response to a pattern electroretinogram (PERG), a particular kind of ERG obtained in response to contrast modulation of patterned visual stimuli at constant mean luminance-typically contrast-reversing gratings or checkerboards-whose characteristics are fundamentally different from those of the traditional ERG in response to diffuse flashes of light.

name: abnormal dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram
abnormal dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram
abnormal dark - adapted dim flash electroretinogram
abnormal dark - adapt dim flash electroretinogram
abnormal light - adapted single flash electroretinogram
abnormal light - adapt single flash electroretinogram
abnormal timing of dark - adapted dim flash electroretinogram
abnormal timing of dark - adapted dim flash electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of dark - adapted dim flash electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of dark - adapted dim flash electroretinogram
abnormal timing of dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram
abnormal timing of dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of light - adapted flicker electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of light - adapt flicker electroretinogram
abnormal timing of light - adapted flicker electroretinogram
abnormal timing of light - adapt flicker electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of light - adapted single flash electroretinogram
abnormal amplitude of light - adapt single flash electroretinogram
abnormal timing of light - adapted single flash electroretinogram
abnormal timing of light - adapt single flash electroretinogram
reduced amplitude of dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram a - wave
reduce amplitude of dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram a - wave
HP:0030483.def: An abnormal reduction in the amplitude of the a-wave.

name: supernormal dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram b - wave
supernormal dark - adapted bright flash electroretinogram b - wave
abnormal p50 / n95 ratio of pattern electroretinogram
abnormal p50 / n95 ratio of pattern electroretinogram
abnormal central response of multifocal electroretinogram
abnormal central response of multifocal electroretinogram
abnormal paracentral response of multifocal electroretinogram
abnormal paracentral response of multifocal electroretinogram
choriocapillaris atrophy
choriocapillaris atrophy
HP:0030491.def: Atrophy of the capillary lamina of choroid.

name: abnormality of foveal pigmentation
abnormality of foveal pigmentation
HP:0030493.def: An anomaly of the pigmentation in the fovea centralis.

name: macular microaneurysm / hemorrhage
macular microaneurysm / hemorrhage
HP:0030494.def: Small, red dots in the superficial retinal layers (it is difficult to distinguish between small hemorrhages and microaneurysms).

name: abnormality morphology of the macular vasculature
abnormality morphology of the macular vasculature
HP:0030495.def: Any structural anomaly of the blood vessels of the macula.

name: macular exudate
macular exudate
HP:0030496.def: Yellow-white intraretinal deposits in the macula typically associated with damaged outer blood-retina barrier and exudation of serous fluid and lipids from the retinal microvasculature.

name: macular cotton wool spot
macular cotton wool spot
HP:0030497.def: Fluffy white patch on the macula, representing localized areas of dense white swelling of the retinal nerve fibre layer. They often have a zigzag internal structure, a feathered edge but an otherwise well-delineated form and an approximately 1 mm dimension; they project slightly into the vitreous and sometimes deflect retinal vessels.

name: macular thickening
macular thickening
HP:0030498.def: Abnormal increase in retinal thickness in the macular area observed on fundoscopy or fundus imaging.

name: macular drusen
macular drusen
HP:0030499.def: Drusen (singular, 'druse') are tiny yellow or white accumulations of extracellular material (lipofuscin) that build up in Bruch's membrane of the eye. This class refers to the presence of Drusen in the macula.

name: yellow / white lesions of the macula
yellow / white lesion of the macula
retinoschisis
retinoschisis
HP:0030502.def: Splitting of the neuroretinal layers of the retina.

name: grouped congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
group congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
synonym: bear track congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
bear track congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium

name: nummular pigmentation of the fundus
nummular pigmentation of the fundus
HP:0030505.def: Clumped pigmentary changes of nummular appearance (i.e., thought to resemble the shape of a coin or multiple coins stuck together) at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium.

name: yellow / white lesions of the retina
yellow / white lesion of the retina
combined hamartoma of the retinal pigment epithelium and retina
combine hamartoma of the retinal pigment epithelium and retina
difficulty adjusting to changes in luminance
difficulty adjust to change in luminance
difficulty adjusting from light to dark
difficulty adjust from light to dark
difficulty adjusting from dark to light
difficulty adjust from dark to light
moderately reduced visual acuity
moderately reduce visual acuity
HP:0030515.def: Moderate reduction of the ability to see defined as visual acuity less than 6/18 (20/60 in US notation; 0.5 in decimal notation) but at least 6/60 (20/200 in US notation; 0.1 in decimal notation).

name: mild constriction of peripheral visual field
mild constriction of peripheral visual field
HP:0030522.def: A diminution of the peripheral visual field whereby at least 50 degrees of central field are preserved in all meridians.

name: obsolete peripheral visual field constriction with 40 - 50 degrees central field preserved
obsolete peripheral visual field constriction with 40 - 50 degree central field preserve
obsolete peripheral visual field constriction with 30 - 39 degrees central field preserved
obsolete peripheral visual field constriction with 30 - 39 degree central field preserve
moderate constriction of peripheral visual field
moderate constriction of peripheral visual field
HP:0030525.def: Peripheral visual field constriction with 20-49 degrees binocular visual field preserved.

name: severe constriction of peripheral visual field
severe constriction of peripheral visual field
HP:0030526.def: Peripheral visual field constriction with 10-19 degrees central field preserved.

name: very severe constriction of peripheral visual field
very severe constriction of peripheral visual field
HP:0030527.def: Peripheral visual field constriction with <10 degrees central field preserved.
synonym: very severe peripheral visual field loss
very severe peripheral visual field loss

name: ring scotoma
ring scotoma
HP:0030529.def: An annular field defect centered on fixation.

name: abnormal best corrected visual acuity test
abnormal best correct visual acuity test
visual acuity light perception with projection
visual acuity light perception with projection
visual acuity light perception without projection
visual acuity light perception without projection
abnormal hardy - rand - rittler plate test
abnormal hardy - rand - rittler plate test
abnormal visual field test
abnormal visual field test
HP:0030588.def: Abnormal result of a test designed to test an individual's central and peripheral vision by determining the ability of the individual to perceive objects at differing locations of the visual field.

name: abnormal esterman grid perimetry test
abnormal esterman grid perimetry test
HP:0030599.def: The Esterman grid test assays scores visual acuity. The grid consists of 100 units whose unequal size and distribution reflect the unequal functional value of different parts of the field-in effect a weighted or relative-value scale. Because each unit equals 1 percent, a simple count of units yields the functional score in percent.

name: abnormal fundus autofluorescence imaging
abnormal fundus autofluorescence imaging
HP:0030602.def: Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) is a non-invasive retinal imaging modality used in clinical practice to provide a density map of lipofuscin, the predominant ocular fluorophore, in the retinal pigment epithelium. Autofluorescent patterns result from the complex interaction of fluorophores such a lipofuscin, which release an autofluorescent signal, and elements such as melanin and rhodopsin, which absorb the excitation beam and attenuate autofluorescence. Other structures such as retinal vessels and the crystalline lens may also influence autofluorescence through blocking and interference.

name: abnormal fundus fluorescein angiography
abnormal fundus fluorescein angiography
HP:0030604.def: An abnormality observed by retinal fluorescein angiography, which involves the intravenous injection of fluorescein dye followed by fluorescent imaging of the fundus immediately after injection and for up to ten minutes thereafter. It can be used to study various retinal abnormalities including especially anomalies of the choroidal and retinal circulation.

name: photoreceptor layer loss on macular oct
photoreceptor layer loss on macular oct
HP:0030609.def: Loss of the outer nuclear layer (photoreceptor layer) as assessed by ocular coherence tomography.

name: photoreceptor outer segment loss on macular oct
photoreceptor outer segment loss on macular oct
retinal pigment epithelial loss on macular oct
retinal pigment epithelial loss on macular oct
abnormal retinal morphology on macular oct
abnormal retinal morphology on macular oct
abnormal foveal morphology on macular oct
abnormal foveal morphology on macular oct
foveal photoreceptor layer loss on macular oct
foveal photoreceptor layer loss on macular oct
foveal photoreceptor outer segment loss on macular oct
foveal photoreceptor outer segment loss on macular oct
foveal retinal pigment epithelial loss on macular oct
foveal retinal pigment epithelial loss on macular oct
inner retinal layer loss on macular oct
inner retinal layer loss on macular oct
foveal inner retinal layer loss on macular oct
foveal inner retinal layer loss on macular oct
abnormal foveal pit on macular oct
abnormal foveal pit on macular oct
intraretinal hyporeflective spaces on macular oct
intraretinal hyporeflective space on macular oct
subretinal hyporeflective spaces on macular oct
subretinal hyporeflective space on macular oct
foveal intraretinal hyporeflective spaces on macular oct
foveal intraretinal hyporeflective space on macular oct
foveal hyporeflective spaces on macular oct
foveal hyporeflective space on macular oct
foveal subretinal hyporeflective spaces on macular oct
foveal subretinal hyporeflective space on macular oct
hyperautofluorescent macular lesion
hyperautofluorescent macular lesion
HP:0030631.def: Increased amount of autofluorescence in the macula as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

name: hypoautofluorescent macular lesion
hypoautofluorescent macular lesion
HP:0030632.def: Decreased amount of autofluorescence in the macula as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

name: perifoveal ring of hyperautofluorescence surrounded by normal autofluorescence
perifoveal ring of hyperautofluorescence surround by normal autofluorescence
perifoveal ring of hyperautofluorescence surrounded by abnormal autofluorescence
perifoveal ring of hyperautofluorescence surround by abnormal autofluorescence
retinal dystrophy with early macular involvement
retinal dystrophy with early macular involvement
occult macular dystrophy
occult macular dystrophy
HP:0030636.def: Occult macular dystrophy is a, typically hereditary, abnormality of the macula associated with progressive foveal cone dysfunction and no apparent fundoscopic, full-field electroretinogram (ERG), or fluorescein angiogram abnormalities.

name: congenital stationary cone dysfunction
congenital stationary cone dysfunction
HP:0030637.def: Retinal phenotype characterised by cone photoreceptor dysfunction and preserved rod system. The abnormality is typically stationary or very slowly progressive and findings may include reduced central vision, colour vision abnormalities, nystagmus and photophobia.

name: congenital stationary night blindness with normal fundus
congenital stationary night blindness with normal fundus
congenital stationary night blindness with abnormal fundus
congenital stationary night blindness with abnormal fundus
central
central
HP:0030645.def: Applies to an abnormality that is located close to the median plane or midline of the body or of the referenced structure.

name: vitreous haze
vitreous haze
HP:0030652.def: Vitreous haze is the obscuration of fundus details by vitreous cells and protein exudation.

name: umbilical cord cyst
umbilical cord cyst
HP:0030654.def: Any cystic lesion associated with the umbilical cord.

name: umbilical cord knot
umbilical cord knot
HP:0030655.def: An entwining of a segment of umbilical cord, usually without obstructing fetal circulation and commonly result from fetal slippage through a loop of the cord.

name: umbilical vein varix
umbilical vein varix
HP:0030656.def: Focal dilation of the umbilical vein.

name: umbilical cord hematoma
umbilical cord hematoma
HP:0030657.def: Bleeding from the vessels of the cord with extravasation of blood into the Wharton jelly surrounding the umbilical cord vessels.

name: marginal umbilical cord insertion
marginal umbilical cord insertion
HP:0030658.def: Insertion of the umbilical cord within 2 cm from the placental edge.

name: velamentous cord insertion
velamentous cord insertion
HP:0030659.def: Insertion of the umbilical cord into the chorio-amniotic membranes of the placenta.

name: furcate cord insertion
furcate cord insertion
HP:0030660.def: Branching of the umbilical cord before its insertion into the placenta.

name: vitreous snowballs
vitreous snowball
HP:0030661.def: Yellow-white inflammatory aggregates in the vitreous that are found in the midvitreous and inferior periphery.

name: vitreous inflammatory cells
vitreous inflammatory cell
HP:0030662.def: The presence of inflammatory cells such as lymphocytes and macrophages in the vitreous.

name: optically empty vitreous
optically empty vitreous
HP:0030663.def: Vestigial vitreous gel occupying the immediate retrolental space and minimal to no discernable gel in the central vitreous cavity, giving the appearance of an empty vitreous cavity.

name: beevor 's sign
beevor 's sign
HP:0030664.def: Weakness of the inferior portion of the rectus abdominal muscle, which is ascertained clinically as follows. When a patient sits up or raises the head from a recumbent position, the umbilicus is displaced toward the head. This is the result of paralysis of the inferior portion of the rectus abdominal muscle, so that the upper fibres predominate pulling upwards the umbilicus.

name: rubral tremor
rubral tremor
HP:0030665.def: Rubral tremor is characterized by a slow coarse tremor at rest that is exacerbated by postural adjustments and by guided voluntary movements.

name: retinal neovascularization
retinal neovascularization
HP:0030666.def: In wound repair, neovascularization (NV) involves the sprouting of new vessels from pre-existent vessels to repair or replace damaged vessels. In the retina, NV is a response to ischemia. The NV adheres to the inner surface of the retina and outer surface of the vitreous. NV are deficient in tight junctions and hence leak plasma into surrounding tissue including the vitreous. Plasma causes the vitreous gel to degenerate, contract, and eventually collapse which pulls on the retina. Since retinal NV is adherent to both retina and vitreous, as the vitreous contracts the NV may be sheared resulting in vitreous hemorrhage or the NV may remain intact and pull the retina with the vitreous resulting in retinal elevation referred to as traction retinal detachment.

name: peripheral retinal neovascularization
peripheral retinal neovascularization
HP:0030667.def: A type of retinal neovascularization that affects the periphery of the retina.

name: periorbital dermoid cyst
periorbital dermoid cyst
HP:0030668.def: A cyst that is localized in the region of the orbit and exhibits an epithelial lining with a keratin-filled lumen. Hair follicles are one of the adnexal structures that are commonly found in walls of dermoid cysts.

name: abnormal ocular adnexa morphology
abnormal ocular adnexa morphology
HP:0030669.def: A structural anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

name: hamartoma of the orbital region
hamartoma of the orbital region
HP:0030670.def: A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) which can originate from any tissue of the orbital region.

name: abnormal common tendinous ring morphology
abnormal common tendinous ring morphology
HP:0030671.def: Any anomaly of the ring of fibrous tissue that surrounds the optic nerve at its entrance at the apex of the orbit. The common tendinous ring, also known as the annulus of Zinn or annular tendon, is the origin for five of the seven extraocular muscles.
synonym: abnormality of the common tendinous ring
abnormality of the common tendinous ring

name: asteroid hyalosis
asteroid hyalosis
HP:0030672.def: The presence of small, white vitreous opacities consisting of calcium phosphate and complex, layered lipid deposits.

name: erosive vitreoretinopathy
erosive vitreoretinopathy
HP:0030673.def: A form of vitreoretinopathy characterized by thinning (erosion) of the retinal pigment epithelium that permits increased visualization of the choroidal vessels.

name: contracture of proximal interphalangeal joints of 2nd - 5th fingers
contracture of proximal interphalangeal joint of 2nd - 5th finger
HP:0030675.def: Chronic loss of joint motion of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th fingers due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

name: satyr ear
satyr ear
HP:0030676.def: Sharp pointed superior portion of the ear, with variable overfolding of the helix.

name: mozart ear
mozart ear
HP:0030677.def: A congenital auricular deformity, which is mainly characterized by a bulging appearance of the anterosuperior portion of the auricle, a convexly protruded cavum conchae, and a slit-like narrowing of the orifice of the external auditory meatus.

name: ash - leaf spot
ash - leaf spot
HP:0030679.def: A hypopigmented spot in the shape of a leaf from the mountain ash tree.

name: abnormal cardiovascular system morphology
abnormal cardiovascular system morphology
HP:0030680.def: Any structural anomaly of the heart and great vessels.

name: abnormal morphology of myocardial trabeculae
abnormal morphology of myocardial trabecula
HP:0030681.def: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the right and left ventricles of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

name: left ventricular noncompaction
leave ventricular noncompaction
HP:0030682.def: Left ventricular noncompaction (LVNC) is defined by 3 markers: prominent left ventricular (LV) trabeculae, deep intertrabecular recesses, and the thin compacted layer.

name: vaginitis
vaginitis
HP:0030683.def: Inflammation of the vagina that can result from a spectrum of conditions that cause vaginal and sometimes vulvar symptoms, such as itching, burning, irritation, odor, and vaginal discharge.

name: abnormal adiponectin level
abnormal adiponectin level
HP:0030684.def: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of adiponectin, a 30-kDa complement C1-related protein that is the most abundant secreted protein expressed in adipose tissue, and that plays a crucial role in the regulation of insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism.

name: decreased adiponectin level
decrease adiponectin level
HP:0030685.def: A reduced circulating concentration of adiponectin, a 30-kDa complement C1-related protein that is the most abundant secreted protein expressed in adipose tissue.

name: increased adiponectin level
increase adiponectin level
HP:0030686.def: An elevated circulating concentration of adiponectin, a 30-kDa complement C1-related protein that is the most abundant secreted protein expressed in adipose tissue.

name: abnormal glucagon level
abnormal glucagon level
HP:0030687.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of glucagon in the blood circulation.

name: increased glucagon level
increase glucagon level
HP:0030688.def: An elevated concentration of glucagon in the blood circulation.

name: decreased glucagon level
decrease glucagon level
HP:0030689.def: A reduced concentration of glucagon in the blood circulation.

name: gingival cleft
gingival cleft
HP:0030690.def: A fissure in the gingiva (gums), i.e., the mucosal tissue that lies over the mandible and maxilla.

name: divergence nystagmus
divergence nystagmus
HP:0030691.def: A condition in which both eyes beat outward simultaneously.

name: brain neoplasm
brain neoplasm
HP:0030692.def: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from or metastasizes to the brain.

name: supratentorial neoplasm
supratentorial neoplasm
HP:0030693.def: A benign or malignant neoplasm that occurs within the intracranial cavity above the tentorium cerebelli.

name: ranula
ranula
HP:0030706.def: A ranula is a mucocele that occurs in the floor of the mouth and usually involve the major salivary glands. Specifically, the ranula originates in the body of the sublingual gland, in the ducts of the sublingual gland, in the Wharton's duct of the submandibular gland or infrequently from the minor salivary glands at this location.

name: unilateral lung agenesis
unilateral lung agenesis
HP:0030707.def: Lack of development of one lung.

name: myeloschisis
myeloschisis
HP:0030708.def: The severe form of a neural tube defect where the open neural tube appears as a flattened, plate-like mass of nervous tissue with no overlying membrane.

name: myelocystocele
myelocystocele
HP:0030709.def: Myelocystocele is characterized by a large, ependyma-lined, cystic dilation of the caudal end of the central canal of the spinal cord; it projects dorsally through a lamina defect, with overlying varying amounts of lipomatous subcutaneous tissue. Myelocystoceles are associated with a tethered cord and meningocele, which communicates with the spinal subarachnoid space, but not with the central canal cyst.

name: lipomeningocele
lipomeningocele
HP:0030710.def: A form of closed neural tube defect in which the spinal tissue lies within the spinal cord having a junction between the spinal cord and the lipoma. Intact skin covers the defect. Neurologic findings first appear during the second year of life.

name: hydrocolpos
hydrocolpos
HP:0030711.def: Distention of the vagina caused by accumulation of fluid due to congenital vaginal obstruction.

name: uterine synechiae
uterine synechiae
HP:0030712.def: Adhesions or scar tissue that form inside the cavity of the uterus.

name: vein of galen aneurysmal malformation
vein of galen aneurysmal malformation
HP:0030713.def: Vein of Galen aneurysmal malformation is a choroidal type of arteriovenous malformation that develops between 6 and 11 weeks of gestation. It results from 1 or more arteriovenous fistulas shunting blood toward the prosencephalic vein of Markowski, the embryonic precursor of the vein of Galen. This abnormal shunt leads to progressive dilation of the vein and prevents its involution and subsequent development into the vein of Galen.

name: subchorionic thrombohematoma
subchorionic thrombohematoma
HP:0030714.def: A large maternal clot that separates the chorionic plate from the villous chorion.

name: bronchial atresia
bronchial atresia
HP:0030715.def: A developmental anomaly characterised by focal obliteration of the proximal segment of a bronchus. The bronchial pattern is entirely normal distal to the site of stenosis.

name: acrania
acrania
HP:0030716.def: Partial or complete absence of the flat bones of the cranial vault. The condition is frequently, though not always, associated with anencephaly.

name: meconium peritonitis
meconium peritonitis
HP:0030717.def: Peritonitis caused by intrauterine intestinal rupture and spillage of fetal meconium into the fetal peritoneal cavity. Intra-peritoneal meconium usually calcifies, sometimes within 24 hours. Ultrasound findings may include intraabdominal calcifications.

name: right atrial enlargement
right atrial enlargement
HP:0030718.def: Increase in size of the right atrium.

name: unguarded tricuspid valve
unguarded tricuspid valve
HP:0030719.def: A form of agenesis of the tricuspid valve in which (although the normal orifice between the right atrium and right ventricle exists) there is no tricuspid valvular tissue.

name: subchorionic septal cyst
subchorionic septal cyst
HP:0030720.def: Cyst on the surface of the placenta consisting of amnion and chorion.

name: ectopic liver
ectopic liver
HP:0030722.def: Ectopic liver is a rare developmental anomaly in which liver tissue is situated outside the liver. Thus, ectopic liver refers to autonomous islands of normal liver parenchyma located outside the liver. The term ectopic liver is also used, to include liver appendices attached to the native liver by a thin stalk although being fully separated from the latter.

name: congenital megalourethra
congenital megalourethra
HP:0030723.def: Dilation and elongation of the penile urethra associated with absence or hypoplasia of the corpora spongiosa and cavernosa.

name: central nervous system cyst
central nervous system cyst
HP:0030724.def: A fluid-filled sac (cyst) located within the central nervous system.
synonym: cyst of the central nervous system
cyst of the central nervous system

name: neurenteric cyst
neurenteric cyst
HP:0030725.def: The neurenteric cyst is a rare lesion composed of heterotopic endodermal tissue. During the third week of human embryogenesis, the neurenteric canal unites the yolk sac and the amniotic cavity as it traverses the primitive notochordal plate. Persistence of the normally transient neurenteric canal prevents appropriate separation of endoderm and notochord. This results in a variable degree of communication between neural and enteric epithelium.

name: spinal neurenteric cyst
spinal neurenteric cyst
HP:0030726.def: A neurenteric cyst located in the spine.

name: intracranial neurenteric cyst
intracranial neurenteric cyst
HP:0030727.def: A neurenteric cyst located within the skull.

name: meromelia
meromelia
HP:0030728.def: Partial absence of a free limb (excluding girdle). It can refer to the proximal, middle or distal segment of the upper or lower limb. The deficiency may be transverse or longitudinal. Thus, meromelia is a lack of a part, but not all, of one or more limbs with the presence of a hand or foot.

name: frontoethmoidal meningocele
frontoethmoidal meningocele
HP:0030729.def: A herniation of meninges through a congenital bone defect in the skull at the junction of the frontal and ethmoidal bones.

name: parietal meningocele
parietal meningocele
HP:0030730.def: A herniation of meninges through a congenital bone defect in the skull in the parietal region.

name: carcinoma
carcinoma
HP:0030731.def: A malignant tumor arising from epithelial cells. Carcinomas that arise from glandular epithelium are called adenocarcinomas, those that arise from squamous epithelium are called squamous cell carcinomas, and those that arise from transitional epithelium are called transitional cell carcinomas (NCI Thesaurus).

name: dysplastic tricuspid valve
dysplastic tricuspid valve
HP:0030732.def: A congenital malformation of the tricuspid valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

name: vesicoallantoic abdominal wall defect
vesicoallantoic abdominal wall defect
HP:0030733.def: An abdominal wall defected related to a developmental anomaly of the allantois, which is an embryonic structure that develops as a diverticulum off the yolk sac at about 16 days post fertilization. During further development, the allantois becomes incorporated into the body of the embryo, connecting the ventral aspect of the urogenital sinus (which will develop into the upper pole of the urinary bladder) to the external portion of the umbilicus. Upon further development, the lumen of the allantois becomes obliterated and forms a thick fibrous cord called the urachus, which connects the apex of the bladder to the umbilicus. In adults, the urachus is known as the median umbilical ligament. Failure of the allantoic cavity to obliterate can result of one of four conditions: 1) congenital patent urachus (a completely open connection between bladder and umbilicus); 2) vesicourachal diverticulum (a diverticulum off the bladder but not communicating with the umbilicus); umbilical cyst and sinus (not communicating with the bladder); and 4) alternating urachal sinus. An abdominal wall defect can be associated with a urachal cyst.

name: ureterovesical junction obstruction
ureterovesical junction obstruction
HP:0030735.def: Blockage at the level of the bladder and the ureter caused by stenosis of the ureteral valves or failure of a narrow juxtavesical ureteral segment to dilate due to segmented fibrosis or localized absence of muscle.

name: sacrococcygeal teratoma
sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP:0030736.def: A teratoma arising in the sacro-coccygeal region.

name: altman type i sacrococcygeal teratoma
altman type i sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP:0030737.def: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma that is predominantly external and projects from the sacrococcygeal region and presents with distortion of the buttocks.

name: altman type ii sacrococcygeal teratoma
altman type ii sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP:0030738.def: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma that is predominantly external but has a large intrapelvic component.

name: altman type iii sacrococcygeal teratoma
altman type iii sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP:0030739.def: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma that is predominantly intrapelvic with a small external, buttock mass.

name: anomalous muscle bundle of the right ventricle
anomalous muscle bundle of the right ventricle
HP:0030740.def: An accessory (not normally present) muscle bundle in the right ventricle which obstructs the right ventricular outflow tract.

name: mediastinal teratoma
mediastinal teratoma
HP:0030741.def: A teratoma located within the mediastinum (the cavity between the pleural sacs that contains the heart and all of the thoracic viscera except the lungs).

name: glial remnants posterior to lens
glial remnant posterior to lens
HP:0030742.def: This anomaly, also known as Mittendorf dot, is a benign, nonprogressive recognizable lesion that does not cause visual impairment. However, it can resemble a pathological congenital or acquired cataract lesion which may enlarge and cause visual impairment. The dot appears as a black speck that ranges in size from the dot made by a sharp pencil point to the size of a poppy seed. It is usually well defined, although occasionally there may be irregular, fine lines radiating outward from the dot.

name: glial remnants anterior to the optic disc
glial remnant anterior to the optic disc
HP:0030743.def: Persistance of a posterior remnant of the hyaloid artery located at the optic disc.

name: hyaloid vascular remnant and retrolental mass
hyaloid vascular remnant and retrolental mass
HP:0030744.def: A type of persistance of the hyaloid vascular system associated with a retrolental mass that may lead to fetal cataract.

name: dilatation of the ductus arteriosus
dilatation of the ductus arteriosus
HP:0030745.def: Ductus arteriosus aneurysm (DAA) is a saccular dilatation of the ductus arteriosus. DAA can be either congenital or acquired (e.g. as a complication of surgical closure of a patent ductus arteriosus). Although the majority of patients with congenital DAA are asymptomatic and have a benign course, severe complications, such as rupture or thromboembolism, can occur. DAA is likely to emerge in the third trimester from the aortic junction of the DA, extending towards its pulmonary end.

name: intraventricular hemorrhage
intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030746.def: Bleeding into the ventricles of the brain.

name: preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030747.def: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a premature infant.

name: grade i preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
grade i preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030748.def: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that is restricted to subependymal region/germline matrix which is seen in the caudothalamic groove.

name: grade ii preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
grade ii preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030749.def: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that has extension into normal-sized ventricles and typically fills less than 50% of the volume of the ventricle.

name: grade iii preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
grade iii preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030750.def: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that has extension into dilated ventricles.

name: grade iv preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
grade iv preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0030751.def: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that shows parenchymal extension.

name: dacryocystocele
dacryocystocele
HP:0030752.def: A nasolacrimal duct obstruction presenting as a grey-blue cystic swelling just below the medial canthus. Believed to be a result of concomitant upper obstruction of the Rosenmuller valve and lower obstruction of the Hasner valve.

name: intrauterine fetal demise of one twin after midgestation
intrauterine fetal demise of one twin after midgestation
HP:0030753.def: Loss of one twin occurring after midgestation (17 weeks gestation).
synonym: intrauterine foetal demise of one twin after midgestation
intrauterine foetal demise of one twin after midgestation

name: allantoic cyst
allantoic cyst
HP:0030754.def: A swelling formed at the base of umbilicus associated with a patent urachus which results from an allantoic remnant. The urachus is a fibrous remnant of the allantois which communicates from the apex of the urinary bladder to the umbilicus. Failed obliteration of the urachus can lead to various abnormalities: urachal cyst, urachal diverticulum, sinus or patent urachus - the most common type. Allantoic cysts in infants with patent urachus can be formed due to the drainage of urine into the umbilical cord, or in uncommon situations, after leakage of hypo-osmotic urine into the Wharton's jelly.

name: craniofacial teratoma
craniofacial teratoma
HP:0030755.def: A teratoma located in the craniofacial region.

name: erythrodontia
erythrodontia
HP:0030756.def: Reddish, brown opalescent discoloration of teeth in normal light.

name: tooth abscess
tooth abscess
HP:0030757.def: A pocket of pus located within a region of a tooth.

name: periapical tooth abscess
periapical tooth abscess
HP:0030758.def: A tooth abscess that occurs at the tip of the root (apex) of a tooth.

name: adipocyte hypertrophy
adipocyte hypertrophy
HP:0030759.def: An increase in mean adipocyte cell size. This feature can be measured by determining the average cell diameter of adipocytes microscopically using abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue obtained by biopsy.

name: renal fibrosis
renal fibrosis
HP:0030760.def: Renal fibrosis is the consequence of an excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix that occurs in virtually every type of chronic kidney disease.

name: mesangiolysis
mesangiolysis
HP:0030762.def: Partial or complete dissolution of the mesangial matrix, identified by reduced staining on a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) or silver stain.

name: amniotic sheet
amniotic sheet
HP:0030763.def: A sheet like projection that can result from uterine synechiae that has been encompassed by the expanding chorion and amnion.

name: ochronosis
ochronosis
HP:0030764.def: Brown or blue-gray discoloration of the skin that can present on the axillary and inguinal areas, face, palms or soles. In addition, blue-black discoloration can be apparent on skin overlying cartilage in which the pigment is deposited, such as the ears. This is a characteristic manifestation of alkaptonuria, which is an autosomal recessively inherited deficiency of homogentisic acid oxidase that results in accumulation of homogentisic acid in collagenous structures. The sclerae are also typically involved.

name: sleep terror
sleep terror
HP:0030765.def: Episodes of intense fear, screaming, and flailing occur even though the affected individuals are still asleep.

name: ear pain
ear pain
HP:0030766.def: Pain in the ear can be a consequence of otologic disease (primary or otogenic otalgia), or can arise from pathologic processes and structures other than the ear (secondary or referred otalgia).

name: epignathus
epignathus
HP:0030767.def: Epignathus is a teratoma originating from the upper jaw, usually connected with the sphenoid bone or hard palate.

name: exencephaly
exencephaly
HP:0030769.def: A malformation of the neural tube with a large amount of protruding brain tissue and absence of calvarium.

name: craniorachischisis
craniorachischisis
HP:0030770.def: A neural tube defect in which both the brain and spinal cord remain open to varying degrees.

name: mallet finger
mallet finger
HP:0030771.def: Mallet finger refers to a condition in which the end joint of a finger bends but will not straighten by itself. In this situation, the joint can be pushed straight but will not hold that position on its own.

name: proximal femoral focal deficiency
proximal femoral focal deficiency
HP:0030772.def: Proximal femoral focal deficiency is a deformity manifested by hypoplasia of a variable portion of the femur with shortening of the entire limb.

name: internuclear ophthalmoplegia
internuclear ophthalmoplegia
HP:0030773.def: An abnormality of conjugate lateral gaze in which the affected eye shows impairment of adduction. The pathognomonic clinical sign of internuclear ophthalmoplegia is an impaired adduction while testing horizontal saccades on the side of the lesion in the ipsilateral medial longitudinal fascicule.

name: mitochondrial swelling
mitochondrial swelling
HP:0030774.def: The mitochondrial matrix refers to the substance occupying the space enclosed by the inner membrane of a mitochondrion, which contains enzymes, DNA, granules, and inclusions of protein crystals, glycogen, and lipid. Mitochondrial swelling refers to an increase in size of the mitochondrial matrix. This phenomenon is thought to be related to a permeabilized inner membrane that originates a large swelling in the mitochondrial matrix. Mitochondrial swelling may distend the outer membrane until it ruptures.

name: modic type vertebral endplate changes
modic type vertebral endplate change
HP:0030775.def: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate according to a widely used classification published by Dr. Michael Modic.

name: modic type i vertebral endplate changes
modic type i vertebral endplate change
HP:0030776.def: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate with a low signal on T1-weighted sequences and high signal on T2-weighted sequences. Modic type I changes are thought to represent bone marrow edema and inflammation.

name: modic type ii vertebral endplate changes
modic type ii vertebral endplate change
HP:0030777.def: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate with a high signal on T1-weighted sequences and high- or isointense signal on T2 sequences. Modic type II signals are thought to indicate fatty replacement in the bone marrow.

name: modic type iii vertebral endplate changes
modic type iii vertebral endplate change
HP:0030778.def: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate with a low signal on T1 and T2-weighted sequences. Modic type III signals are thought to correspond to subchondral sclerosis seen on plain radiographs.

name: ethmocephaly
ethmocephaly
HP:0030779.def: Ethmocephaly is the rarest form of holoprosencephaly, which occurs due to an incomplete cleavage of the forebrain. Clinically, the disease presents with a proboscis, hypotelorism, microphthalmos and malformed ears.

name: abnormality of the protein c anticoagulant pathway
abnormality of the protein c anticoagulant pathway
HP:0030780.def: An anomaly of the protein C anticoagulant pathway, which serves as a major system for controlling thrombosis, limiting inflammatory responses, and potentially decreasing endothelial cell apoptosis in response to inflammatory cytokines and ischemia. A natural anticoagulant system denoted the protein C pathway exerts its anticoagulant effect by regulating the activity of FVIIIa and FVa. The vitamin K-dependent protein C is the key component of the pathway. Activated protein C (APC) cleaves and inhibits coagulation cofactors FVIIIa and FVa, which result in downregulation of the activity of the coagulation system. The endothelial protein C receptor stimulates the T-TM-mediated activation of protein C on the endothelial cell surface. The two cofactors, protein S and the intact form of FV, enhance the anticoagulant activity of APC.

name: increased circulating free fatty acid level
increase circulate free fatty acid level
HP:0030781.def: A higher than normal levels of the fatty acids which can occur in plasma as a result of lipolysis in adipose tissue or when plasma triacyglycerols are taken into tissues.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin concentration
HP:0030782.def: An abnormal amount of any of the interleukins, a class of cytokines, in the circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 6 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 6 concentration
HP:0030783.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-6 in the blood circulation.

name: anomic aphasia
anomic aphasia
HP:0030784.def: An inability to name people and objects that are correctly perceived. The individual is able to describe the object in question, but cannot provide the name.

name: mediastinal cystic lymphangioma
mediastinal cystic lymphangioma
HP:0030785.def: A lymphangioma (congenital malformation consisting of focal proliferations of well-differentiated lymphatic tissue in multi cystic or sponge like structures) located within the mediastinum, i.e., the central compartment of the thoracic cavity that is surrounded by loose connective tissue. Mediastinal lymphangioma is a slow growing mass with benign features, and accounts for 1% of all mediastinal tumors.

name: cerumen abnormality
cerumen abnormality
HP:0030787.def: Any anomaly of the cerumen (ear wax), the yellowish waxy substance secreted in the ear canal.

name: impacted cerumen
impact cerumen
HP:0030788.def: Blockage of the external auditory canal by a buildup of earwax.

name: abnormal cerumen color
abnormal cerumen color
HP:0030790.def: An anomolous earwax color. Earwax (cerumen) is usually light to dark brown or orange in color.

name: abnormal jaw morphology
abnormal jaw morphology
HP:0030791.def: A structural anomaly of the jaw, the bony structure of the mouth that consists of the mandible and the maxilla.

name: jaw neoplasm
jaw neoplasm
HP:0030792.def: A tumor originating in the jaw (mandible or maxilla).

name: jaw swelling
jaw swell
HP:0030793.def: Abnormal enlargement in the upper jaw (maxilla) or in the lower jaw (mandible).

name: abnormal circulating c - peptide concentration
abnormal circulate c - peptide concentration
HP:0030794.def: An anomolous circulating concentration of the connecting (C) peptide, which links the insulin A and B chains in proinsulin, providing thereby a means to promote their efficient folding and assembly in the endoplasmic reticulum during insulin biosynthesis. After cleavage of proinsulin, C-peptide is stored with insulin in the soluble phase of the secretory granules and is subsequently released in equimolar amounts with insulin, providing a useful independent indicator of insulin secretion.

name: reduced c - peptide level
reduce c - peptide level
HP:0030795.def: A decreased concentration of C-peptide in the circulation. Since C-peptide is secreted in equimolar amounts to insulin, this feature correlates with reduced insulin secretion.

name: increased c - peptide level
increase c - peptide level
HP:0030796.def: An elevated concentration of C-peptide in the circulation. Since C-peptide is secreted in equimolar amounts to insulin, this feature correlates with increased insulin secretion.

name: reduced volume of central subdivision of bed nucleus of stria terminalis
reduced volume of central subdivision of bed nucleus of stria terminalis
HP:0030797.def: A diminished volume of the central part of the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis.

name: abnormality of the bed nucleus of stria terminalis
abnormality of the bed nucleus of stria terminalis
HP:0030798.def: The stria terminalis is a slender, compact fiber bundle that connects the amygdala (amygdaloid body) with the hypothalamus and other basal forebrain regions. The bed nucleus of the stria terminalis is a limbic forebrain structure that receives heavy projections from, among other areas, the basolateral amygdala, and projects in turn to hypothalamic and brainstem target areas that mediate many of the autonomic and behavioral responses to aversive or threatening stimuli. This term refers to an anomaly of the bed nucleus.

name: scaphocephaly
scaphocephaly
HP:0030799.def: Scaphocephaly is a subtype of dolichocephaly where the anterior and posterior aspects of the cranial vault are pointed (boat-shaped). Scaphocephaly is caused by a precocious fusion of sagittal suture without other associated synostosis.

name: abnormal visual accommodation
abnormal visual accommodation
HP:0030800.def: An anomaly in the process of visual accommodation, which is the process of adjustment of the eye to enable sharp vision of objects at different distances. Accommodation is mediated by contraction of the ciliary muscles, which alter the convexity of the lens and, consequently, its refractive power.

name: reduced visual accommodation
reduce visual accommodation
HP:0030801.def: A decreased ability of the eye to adjust and thereby enable sharp vision of objects at different distances.

name: lower eyelid retraction
low eyelid retraction
HP:0030802.def: Inferior malposition of the lower eyelid margin without eyelid eversion.

name: trachyonychia
trachyonychia
HP:0030804.def: Excessive longitudinal ridging that gives the surface of the nail plate a rough appearance. It results from multiple foci of defective keratinization of the proximal nail matrix.

name: absent lunula
absent lunula
HP:0030805.def: Lack of the lunula at the base of a nail. The lunula is the crescent-shaped whitish area of the bed of a fingernail or toenail.

name: fast - growing nails
fast - grow nail
HP:0030806.def: Nails whose growth is quicker than normal.

name: abnormal nail growth
abnormal nail growth
HP:0030807.def: Nail whose growth pattern or speed deviates from normal.

name: ragged cuticle
rag cuticle
HP:0030808.def: The cuticle (properly known as the eponychium, or the medial nail fold or the proximal nail fold), is the thickened layer of skin surrounding fingernails and toenails. Its function is to protect the area between the nail and epidermis from exposure to bacteria. This term refers to the presence of and irregular edge or outline of the cuticle.

name: abnormal tongue morphology
abnormal tongue morphology
HP:0030809.def: Any structural anomaly of the tongue.

name: abnormal tongue physiology
abnormal tongue physiology
HP:0030810.def: Any functional anomaly of the tongue.

name: tongue pain
tongue pain
HP:0030811.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the tongue.

name: enlarged tonsils
enlarge tonsil
HP:0030812.def: Increase in size of the tonsils, small collections of lymphoid tissue facing into the aerodigestive tract on either side of the back part of the throat.

name: orange discolored tonsils
orange discolor tonsil
HP:0030814.def: A phenomenon of orange colored oral tonsils. This feature is characteristic of Tangier disease and illustrated will by Figure 1 of PMID:19470903.

name: lipoma of the tongue
lipoma of the tongue
HP:0030815.def: A lipoma localized to the tongue. May present as a nontender, soft, spherical mass of the tongue.

name: gingival recession
gingival recession
HP:0030816.def: The loss of gum tissue. The result is that gum tissue is recessed and its position on the tooth is lowered, exposing the roots of the teeth.

name: beaked nails
beak nail
HP:0030817.def: Severe nail curvature, causing the tip of the nail to point downwards with respect to the axis of the finger. Beaked nails are caused by resorption of the distal digit.

name: central nail canal
central nail canal
HP:0030818.def: The presence of a depressed line (\"canal\") in the center of the nail.

name: ski jump nail
ski jump nail
HP:0030819.def: Nails that slope upward at the free edge.

name: hooded eyelid
hood eyelid
HP:0030820.def: Eyelid partly covered by skin when eyes are open.

name: hooded lower eyelid
hood low eyelid
HP:0030821.def: Lower eyelid partly covered by skin when eyes are open.

name: hooded upper eyelid
hood upper eyelid
HP:0030822.def: Upper eyelid partly covered by skin when eyes are open.

name: scleral thickening
scleral thickening
HP:0030823.def: Increased dimension of the sclera in the anterior-posterior axis.

name: mizuo phenomenon
mizuo phenomenon
HP:0030824.def: Change in the color of the fundus from red in the dark-adapted state to golden immediately or shortly after the onset of the light. The color of the fundus reflex in the light adapted state has also been described as golden-yellow, gray-white, and yellow-white. This reflex can appear either homogeneous or in streaks in the fundus. The retinal vessels appear to be protruding in contrast to the radiant background. Dark adaptation leads to disappearance of the unusual fundus coloration [Digital Journal of Ophthalmology 2008; Volume 14, Number 14].

name: absent foveal reflex
absent foveal reflex
HP:0030825.def: Lack of the foveal reflex, which normally occurs as a result of the reflection of light from the ophthalmoscope in the foveal pit upon examination. The foveal reflex is a bright pinpoint of light that is observed to move sideways or up and down in response to movement of the opthalmoscope.

name: eyelid fasciculation
eyelid fasciculation
HP:0030826.def: Tiny, repetitive muscle contractions in the eyelids, causing the appearance of twitching.

name: wheezing
wheeze
HP:0030828.def: A high-pitched whistling sound associated with labored breathing.

name: abnormal breath sound
abnormal breath sound
HP:0030829.def: An anomalous (adventitious) sound produced by the breathing process.

name: crackles
crackle
HP:0030830.def: Crackles are discontinuous, explosive, and nonmusical adventitious lung sounds normally heard in inspiration and sometimes during expiration. Crackles are usually classified as fine and coarse crackles based on their duration, loudness, pitch, timing in the respiratory cycle, and relationship to coughing and changing body position.

name: rhonchi
rhonchus
HP:0030831.def: Abnormal breath sounds characterized by low-pitched, snoring or rattle-like sounds.

name: vitreous strands
vitreous strand
HP:0030832.def: Fiber- or rope-like opacities located within the vitreous humor.

name: neck pain
neck pain
HP:0030833.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the neck.

name: shoulder pain
shoulder pain
HP:0030834.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the shoulder.

name: elbow pain
elbow pain
HP:0030835.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the elbow.

name: wrist pain
wrist pain
HP:0030836.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the wrist.

name: finger pain
finger pain
HP:0030837.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the finger.

name: hip pain
hip pain
HP:0030838.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the hip.

name: knee pain
knee pain
HP:0030839.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the knee.

name: ankle pain
ankle pain
HP:0030840.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the ankle.

name: toe pain
toe pain
HP:0030841.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the toe.

name: choking episodes
choke episode
HP:0030842.def: Incidents in which a piece of food or other objects get stuck in the upper airway and provoke coughing, gagging, inability to talk, and difficulty breathing.

name: cardiac amyloidosis
cardiac amyloidosis
HP:0030843.def: Extracellular deposition in cardiac tissue of a proteinaceous material that, when stained with Congo red, demonstrates apple-green birefringence under polarized light and that has a distinct color when stained with sulfated Alcian blue. Viewed with electron microscopy, the amyloid deposits are seen to be composed of a beta-sheet fibrillar material. These nonbranching fibrils have a diameter of 7.5 to 10 nm and are the result of protein misfolding.

name: undetectable pattern electroretinogram
undetectable pattern electroretinogram
HP:0030844.def: Absent response to a pattern electroretinogram (PERG).

name: heliotrope rash of eyelid
heliotrope rash of eyelid
HP:0030845.def: Heliotrope rash is a violaceous discoloration of the eyelids associated with periorbital edema.

name: abnormal jugular venous pressure
abnormal jugular venous pressure
HP:0030847.def: An anomaly of the jugular venous pressure. The internal jugular veins, being continuous with the superior vena cava, provide a visible measure of the degree to which the systemic venous reservoir is filled. The vertical height above the right atrium to which they are distended and above which they are in a collapsed state provides an imperfect reflection of the right atrial pressure.

name: hepatojugular reflux
hepatojugular reflux
HP:0030849.def: The examiner applies firm but persistent pressure over the liver for 10 seconds while observing the mean jugular venous pressure. Normally there is either no rise or only a transient (i.e., 2 to 3 sec) rise in mean jugular venous pressure. A sustained increase in the mean venous pressure until abdominal compression is released is abnormal and indicates impaired right heart function. This abnormal response is called hepatojugular reflux.

name: abnormal pulse pressure
abnormal pulse pressure
HP:0030850.def: An anomaly of the pulse pressure, which is defined as the systolic pressured minus the diastolic pressure.

name: low pulse pressure
low pulse pressure
HP:0030851.def: Reduced amplitude of the pulse pressure (systolic blood pressure minus diastolic blood pressure).

name: high pulse pressure
high pulse pressure
HP:0030852.def: Increased amplitude of the pulse pressure (systolic blood pressure minus diastolic blood pressure).

name: heterotaxy
heterotaxy
HP:0030853.def: An abnormality in which the internal thoraco-abdominal organs demonstrate abnormal arrangement across the left-right axis of the body.

name: scleral staphyloma
scleral staphyloma
HP:0030854.def: A staphyloma is a localized defect in the eye wall with protrusion of uveal tissue due to alterations in scleral thickness and structure.

name: anterior staphyloma
anterior staphyloma
HP:0030855.def: A localized defect in the anterior eye wall with protrusion of uveal tissue due to alterations in scleral thickness and structure.

name: posterior staphyloma
posterior staphyloma
HP:0030856.def: A localized defect in the posterior eye wall with protrusion of uveal tissue due to alterations in scleral thickness and structure.

name: eye movement - induced pain
eye movement - induced pain
HP:0030857.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the eye that is worse in certain directions of gaze and during prolonged gaze holding.

name: addictive behavior
addictive behavior
HP:0030858.def: When an activity, substance, object, or behavior becomes a major focus of a person's life, excluding other activities, or has begun to harm the individual or others physically, mentally, or socially, it can be considered addictive behavior. A person can become addicted or compulsively engaged with anything.

name: anti - topoisomerase i antibody positivity
anti - topoisomerase i antibody positivity
HP:0030859.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against topoisomerase I.

name: abnormal csf amyloid concentration
abnormal csf amyloid concentration
HP:0030860.def: Abnormal concentration of amyloid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: decreased csf amyloid concentration
decrease csf amyloid concentration
HP:0030861.def: Reduced concentration of amyloid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: elevated csf amyloid concentration
elevate csf amyloid concentration
HP:0030862.def: Increased concentration of amyloid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: nasal flaring
nasal flare
HP:0030863.def: Widening of the nostrils upon inhalation as a manifestation of respiratory distress.

name: intercostal retractions
intercostal retraction
HP:0030864.def: A pulling inward of the soft tissues between the ribs upon inhalation. This is a sign of increased use of the chest muscles for breathing and is a manifestation of respiratory distress.

name: large elbow
large elbow
HP:0030865.def: Abnormal increased size of the elbow joint.

name: large knee
large knee
HP:0030866.def: Abnormally increased size of the knee joint.

name: vertical orbital dystopia
vertical orbital dystopia
HP:0030867.def: The orbits do not lie on the same horizontal plane, that is, one eye is lower than the other.

name: monorchism
monorchism
HP:0030868.def: Having only one testis in the scrotum.

name: anorchism
anorchism
HP:0030869.def: An abnormality of XY sexual development characterized by the absence of both testes at birth.

name: abnormality of spinal facet joint
abnormality of spinal facet joint
HP:0030870.def: An anomaly of the small joints located between and behind adjacent vertebrae.

name: facet joint arthrosis
facet joint arthrosis
HP:0030871.def: Osteoarthritis of facet joints in the spine. Degeneration of cartilage in the facet joints results in bone rubbing on bone and reactive new bone formation visible on X-ray.

name: abnormal cardiac ventricular function
abnormal cardiac ventricular function
HP:0030872.def: An abnormality of the cardiac ventricular function.

name: anti - centromere antibody positivity
anti - centromere antibody positivity
HP:0030873.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the centromeres or centromere components.

name: oxygen desaturation on exertion
oxygen desaturation on exertion
HP:0030874.def: Oxygen saturation less than 95% on exertion or arterial partial pressure of oxygen falling by more than 1kPa.

name: abnormality of pulmonary circulation
abnormality of pulmonary circulation
HP:0030875.def: A functional anomaly of that portion of the cardiosvascular system that carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs and returns oxygenated blood back to the heart.

name: reduced fev1 / fvc ratio
reduce fev1 / fvc ratio
HP:0030877.def: Abnormally low FEV1/FVC (FEV1 - forced expiratory volume in 1 second; FVC forced vital capacity).
synonym: obstructive deficit on pulmonary function test
obstructive deficit on pulmonary function test
obstructive deficit on pulmonary function testing
obstructive deficit on pulmonary function test

name: abnormality on pulmonary function testing
abnormality on pulmonary function test
HP:0030878.def: Any anomaly measure by pulmonary function testing, which includes spirometry, measures of diffusing capacity, and plethysmography.

name: interlobular septal thickening
interlobular septal thickening
HP:0030879.def: Presence of thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a CT scan.
synonym: interlobular septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
interlobular septal thicken on pulmonary hrct

name: shoulder impingement
shoulder impingement
HP:0030881.def: Trapping and compression of the rotator cuff tendons during shoulder movements.

name: coronary artery aneurysm
coronary artery aneurysm
HP:0030882.def: Enlargement of the diameter (cross-section) of a coronary artery as defined by a focal dilation of a segment at least 1.5 times larger than the reference vessel.

name: femoroacetabular impingement
femoroacetabular impingement
HP:0030883.def: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) results from one or more bony abnormalities that lead to abnormal contact between the acetabulum and the femoral head or neck. The femoral abnormality is proposed to cause compression and shear stresses in the region between the labrum and cartilage, anterosuperiorly. These stresses cause a separation between the labrum and cartilage as the labrum is pushed outwards and the cartilage is pushed centrally. This eventually leads to articular degeneration and eventually global hip osteoarthritis.

name: gastrojejunal tube feeding in infancy
gastrojejunal tube feeding in infancy
HP:0030884.def: Feeding problem necessitating gastrojejunal tube feeding.
synonym: gastro - jejunal tube feeding in infancy
gastro - jejunal tube feeding in infancy

name: recurrent parasitic infections
recurrent parasitic infection
HP:0030885.def: Increased susceptibility to parasitic infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of parasitic infection.

name: abnormal lymphocyte apoptosis
abnormal lymphocyte apoptosis
HP:0030886.def: A anomaly in the rate of programmed cell death (apoptosis) in lymphocytes.

name: increased lymphocyte apoptosis
increase lymphocyte apoptosis
HP:0030887.def: A elevation in the rate of apoptosis in lymphocytes.

name: c3 nephritic factor positivity
c3 nephritic factor positivity
HP:0030888.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against C3 convertase (C3bBb).

name: congenital shortened small intestine
congenital shorten small intestine
HP:0030889.def: Substantially shortened length of the small intestine as a result of a developmental defect.

name: hyperintensity of cerebral white matter on mri
hyperintensity of cerebral white matter on mri
HP:0030890.def: A brighter than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter.

name: periventricular white matter hyperintensities
periventricular white matter hyperintensities
HP:0030891.def: Areas of brighter than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter that surrounds the cerebral ventricles.

name: deep cerebral white matter hyperintensities
deep cerebral white matter hyperintensities
HP:0030892.def: Areas of brighter than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from locations distant from the ventricular system.

name: abnormal response to short acting pulmonary vasodilator
abnormal response to short act pulmonary vasodilator
HP:0030893.def: Pulmonary vasodilator testing is performed during right-heart catheterization and involves a short-acting vasoactive agent such as adenosine, epoprostenol, or inhaled nitric oxide. The current definition of a normal (positive) response is a drop in mean pulmonary artery pressure of at least 10 mm Hg (or 20 percent) to below 40 mm Hg.

name: insufficient response to short acting pulmonary vasodilator
insufficient response to short act pulmonary vasodilator
HP:0030894.def: No fall in mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) falls by at least 10 mmHg to an absolute value less than 40 mmHg without a degradation in cardiac output (CO) in response to a short-acting vasoactive agent such as adenosine, epoprostenol, or inhaled nitric oxide.

name: abnormal gastrointestinal motility
abnormal gastrointestinal motility
HP:0030895.def: An anomaly of the muscular contractions that propel food though the gastrointestinal tract.

name: abnormal gastrointestinal transit time
abnormal gastrointestinal transit time
HP:0030896.def: A deviation from the normal amount of time required for food to pass through the intestines.

name: decreased intestinal transit time
decrease intestinal transit time
HP:0030897.def: A reduction in the length of time required for food to pass through the intestines.

name: pruritis on abdomen
pruritis on abdomen
HP:0030898.def: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the skin of the abdomen.

name: pruritis on hand
pruritis on hand
HP:0030899.def: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the skin of the hand.

name: pruritus on foot
pruritus on foot
HP:0030900.def: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the skin of the foot.

name: pruritis on breast
pruritis on breast
HP:0030901.def: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the skin of the breast.

name: palmomental reflex
palmomental reflex
HP:0030902.def: A type of primitive reflex characterized by an involuntary contraction of the mentalis muscle of the chin caused by stimulation of the thenar eminence of the palm.

name: grasp reflex
grasp reflex
HP:0030903.def: A type of primitive reflex that can be elicated when the hand of the examiner is gently inserted into the palm of the patient's hand. The palmar surface is stroked or simply touched. The flexor surfaces of the fingers may be stimulated also by the examiner's fingers. The stimulus should be in a distal direction. With a positive response, the patient grasps the examiner's hand with variable strength and continues to grasp as the examiner's hand is moved. Ability to release the grip voluntarily depends on the activity of the reflex; some patients can do so readily, while others can even be lifted off the bed, since the grasp has such power [NCBI Books:NBK395].

name: glabellar reflex
glabellar reflex
HP:0030904.def: A type of primitive reflex that is elicited by repetitive tapping on the forehead. Normal subjects usually blink in response to the first several taps, but if blinking persists, the response is abnormal and considered to be a sign of frontal release. Persistent blinking is also known as Myerson's sign.

name: snout reflex
snout reflex
HP:0030905.def: A type of primitive reflex that is elicited by tapping the upper lip lightly. The contraction of the muscles causes the mouth to resemble a snout.

name: suck reflex
suck reflex
HP:0030906.def: A type of primitive reflex that is elicited by lightly touching or tapping on the lips with an object such as a tongue blade, reflex hammer, or the examiner's finger. At times the reflex is obtained merely by approaching the lips with an object. A positive suck reflex consists of sucking movements by the lips when they are stroked or touched.

name: thunderclap headache
thunderclap headache
HP:0030907.def: Severe head pain with sudden onset, reaching its maximum intensity in less than one minute and lasting from one hour to ten days.

name: liver kidney microsome type 1 antibody positivity
liver kidney microsome type 1 antibody positivity
HP:0030908.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against P450 2D6, a cytochrome P450 mono-oxygenase. Anti-LKM-1 antibodies are considered to be a diagnostic marker of autoimmune hepatitis type 2 (AIH2).
synonym: anti - liver kidney microsomal type 1 antibody positivity
anti - liver kidney microsomal type 1 antibody positivity
anti - type i liver - kidney microsomal antibody positivity
anti - type i liver - kidney microsomal antibody positivity

name: anti - liver cytosolic antigen type 1 antibody positivity
anti - liver cytosolic antigen type 1 antibody positivity
HP:0030909.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a 60-kd peptide contained in the liver cytosolic fraction.

name: bifid clitoris
bifid clitoris
HP:0030911.def: Two clitorides located side by side.

name: exaggerated rugosity of the labia majora
exaggerated rugosity of the labium majora
HP:0030913.def: Marked rugae formation of the skin of the labia majora.

name: abnormal peristalsis
abnormal peristalsis
HP:0030914.def: An anomaly of the wave-like muscle contractions of the digestive tract.

name: cerebellar edema
cerebellar edema
HP:0030915.def: Swelling from fluid accumulation (serous fluid infiltration into the interstitial space) in the cerebellum.

name: oral erythroplakia
oral erythroplakia
HP:0030934.def: A velvety red but not ulcerated lesion of the oral mucosa. The texture may be roughened or normal, and the lesion is neither raised nor depressed.

name: abnormal intestinal smooth muscle morphology
abnormal intestinal smooth muscle morphology
HP:0030935.def: A structural anomaly of the nonstriated, involuntary muscle tissue of the intestine.
synonym: abnormality of intestinal smooth muscle morphology
abnormality of intestinal smooth muscle morphology

name: abnormal layering of muscularis propria
abnormal layering of muscularis propria
HP:0030936.def: Abnormal layering of the intestinal muscularis propria into three layers; (1) inner circular; (2) additional oblique; and (3) outer longitudinal layer.

name: fibrotic muscularis propria
fibrotic muscularis propria
HP:0030937.def: The presence of excessive fibrous connective tissue in the muscularis propria of the intestine. Fibrosis is a reparative or reactive process.

name: enteric intraneuronal nuclear inclusion bodies
enteric intraneuronal nuclear inclusion body
HP:0030938.def: Aggregates of stainable substances (proteins) in the nuclei of enteric neurons.

name: palpebral thickening
palpebral thickening
HP:0030939.def: An increased thickness of the eyelid not related to acute inflammation.

name: conjunctival papillae
conjunctival papilla
HP:0030946.def: Raised tissue masses located on the palpebral conjunctiva with a central vessel. Papillae are created by a focal infiltration of inflammatory cells.

name: conjunctival follicles
conjunctival follicle
HP:0030947.def: Small, dome-shaped nodules without a prominent central vessel located on the conjunctiva. The lymphoid follicles are located in the subendothelial region of the conjunctiva. They consist of a germinal center that contains immature, proliferating lymphocytes, as well as a corona that contains mature lymphocytes and plasma cells.

name: elevated gamma - glutamyltransferase level
elevate gamma - glutamyltransferase level
HP:0030948.def: Increased level of the enzyme gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT). GGT is mainly present in kidney, liver, and pancreatic cells, but small amounts are present in other tissues.

name: glomerular deposits
glomerular deposit
HP:0030949.def: An abnormal accumulation of protein in the glomerulus.

name: pulmonary venous hypertension
pulmonary venous hypertension
HP:0030950.def: An abnormal increase in pressure in the pulmonary veins, usually as a result of left atrial hypertension.

name: skeletal muscle fibrosis
skeletal muscle fibrosis
HP:0030951.def: Excessive formation of fibrous bands of scar tissue in between muscle fibers.

name: birdshot retinochoroidopathy
birdshot retinochoroidopathy
HP:0030952.def: Multiple cream-yellow colored hypopigmented lesions typically located at the level of the choroid or retinal pigment epithelium; ovoid, cream-colored with indistinct borders. They are between 50 and 1,500 micrometers in size with a characteristic nasal, radial distribution in the postequatorial fundus.

name: conjunctival hyperemia
conjunctival hyperemia
HP:0030953.def: Dilatation of the blood vessels of the conjunctiva leading to a red appearance of the sclera.

name: addictive alcohol use
addictive alcohol use
HP:0030955.def: An addictive behavior is defined as drinking excessive amounts of alcohol over a prolonged period of time, having difficulty in reducing the amount of alcohol consumed, strongly desiring alcohol, and experiencing withdrawal symptoms when not drinking alcohol.

name: abnormality of cardiovascular system electrophysiology
abnormality of cardiovascular system electrophysiology
HP:0030956.def: An anomaly of the electrical conduction physiology of the heart.

name: ventricular septal aneurysm
ventricular septal aneurysm
HP:0030957.def: A bowing (bulging to one side) of the interventricular septum of more than 15 mm on either side in adults and 5 mm in children during normal cardiac motion.

name: membranous ventricular septal aneurysm
membranous ventricular septal aneurysm
HP:0030958.def: Bowing (bulging out) of the membranous part of the interventricular septum of more than 10-15 mm into the cavity of an adjacent ventricle (usually into the right ventricle).
synonym: aneurysm of the membranous ventricular septum
aneurysm of the membranous ventricular septum

name: muscular ventricular septal aneurysm
muscular ventricular septal aneurysm
HP:0030959.def: Bowing (bulging out) of the muscular part of the interventricular septum of more than 10-15 mm into the cavity of an adjacent ventricle (usually into the right ventricle).
synonym: aneurysm of the muscular ventricular septum
aneurysm of the muscular ventricular septum

name: microspherophakia
microspherophakia
HP:0030961.def: Lens of the eye is smaller than normal and spherically shaped.

name: abnormal morphology of the great vessels
abnormal morphology of the great vessel
HP:0030962.def: A structural anomaly affecting a blood vessel involved in the circulation of the heart, i.e., the superior or inferior vena cava, the pulmonary arteries, the pulmonary veins, and the aorta.

name: aortic stiffness
aortic stiffness
HP:0030965.def: The elastic properties of the aorta allow the aorta to store half of the cardiac ejected blood volume per beat, whereby aortic recoil during diastole pushes the remaining stored volume forward into the peripheral circulation, a phenomenon known as the Windkessel function. Aortic stiffness occurs as the elastic fibers within the arterial wall become disrupted due to mechanical stress (with age or due to other factors). Aortic stiffness refers to a reduction in the elasticity of the aorta, which is associated with an elevated pulse pressure, increased wave reflection, and often hypertension.

name: abnormal pulmonary artery morphology
abnormal pulmonary artery morphology
HP:0030966.def: An abnormality of the structure of the pulmonary artery.

name: abnormal pulmonary artery physiology
abnormal pulmonary artery physiology
HP:0030967.def: An abnormality of the function of the pulmonary artery.

name: abnormal pulmonary vein morphology
abnormal pulmonary vein morphology
HP:0030968.def: An abnormality of the structure of the pulmonary veins.

name: abnormal pulmonary vein physiology
abnormal pulmonary vein physiology
HP:0030969.def: An abnormality of the function of the pulmonary veins.

name: abnormal vena cava physiology
abnormal vena cava physiology
HP:0030970.def: An abnormality of the function of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

name: abnormal systemic blood pressure
abnormal systemic blood pressure
HP:0030972.def: A chronic deviation from normal pressure in the systemic arterial system.

name: postexertional symptom exacerbation
postexertional symptom exacerbation
HP:0030973.def: Post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE), also referred to as post-exertional malaise (PEM), is defined as the worsening of symptoms that can follow minimal cognitive, physical, emotional, or social activity, or activity that could previously be tolerated. Symptoms typically worsen 12 to 72 hours after activity and can last for days or even weeks, sometimes leading to a relapse.

name: cryptozoospermia
cryptozoospermia
HP:0030974.def: A type of oligozoospermia in which spermatozoa can be detected in an ejaculate only after centrifugation and inspection of the pellet.

name: pontine tegmental cap
pontine tegmental cap
HP:0030975.def: An abnormal curved or vaulted (capped) structure covering the middle third of the dorsal pontine tegmentum and projecting into the fourth ventricle.

name: abnormal factor viii activity
abnormal factor viii activity
HP:0030976.def: A deviation from the normal activity of coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.

name: increased factor viii activity
increase factor viii activity
HP:0030977.def: Increased activity of the coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.

name: decreased csf / serum albumin ratio
decrease csf / serum albumin ratio
HP:0030978.def: A reduction below normal limits of the ratio of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) albumin concentration to serum albumin concentration.

name: dilatation of large choroidal vessels
dilatation of large choroidal vessel
HP:0030979.def: Enlargement of the large blood vessels in the choroid.

name: reduced brain glutamine level by mrs
reduce brain glutamine level by mr
HP:0030980.def: An decrease in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: abnormal csf / serum albumin ratio
abnormal csf / serum albumin ratio
HP:0030981.def: A deviation from the normal range of the ratio of the albumin concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to the concentration in serum (which may be defined as 3.2-9.0). This is an index of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, adjusted for the serum albumin concentration, and an increased ratio is taken as a sign of a loss of integrity of the BBB with leakage of albumin into the CSF.

name: ovarian thecoma
ovarian thecoma
HP:0030983.def: A sex cord-stromal tumor of the ovary. Thecomas range from small tumors to large solid or solid-cystic masses of up to 15 cm.
