They are unilateral in over 90 percent of cases and are rarely malignant. Thecomas are stromal tumors made up of cells that resemble theca cells, lutein cells and fibroblasts. They are traditionally classified within the sex cord-stromal tumor category of ovarian tumor types.

name: abnormal serum bile acid concentration
abnormal serum bile acid concentration
HP:0030984.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of serum bile acid concentration.

name: decreased serum bile acid concentration
decrease serum bile acid concentration
HP:0030985.def: A reduction in the concentration of bile acid in the blood.

name: biliary epithelial hyperplasia
biliary epithelial hyperplasia
HP:0030986.def: Hyperplasia of lining epithelia of the septal and large bile ducts manifesting as micropapillary projections or as a stratification of the epithelium with or without dilatation of the duct lumen.

name: suppurative cholangitis
suppurative cholangitis
HP:0030987.def: Cholangitis characterized by the presence of numerous polymorphonuclear cells around and within the wall as well as within the lumen of the ducts. This may involve ducts of any size and is occasionally associated with abscess formation (cholangitic abscess).

name: granulomatous cholangitis
granulomatous cholangitis
HP:0030988.def: Cholangitis characterized by the accumulation of granulomas. Granulomas are aggregates of modified macrophages (epithelioid cells) and other inflammatory cells that accumulate after chronic exposure to antigens. The underlying trigger may be exposure to noxious agents that cannot be biochemically degraded or to immune dysfunction. The ultimate result is a release of a variety cytokines that stimulate mononuclear cells that fuse to form multinucleated giant cells with a surrounding rim of lymphocytes and fibroblasts.

name: lymphoid cholangitis
lymphoid cholangitis
HP:0030989.def: Cholangitis characterized by a close association between duct branches, usually interlobular bile ducts, and lymphocytic aggregates, which may show a follicular arrangement.

name: pleomorphic cholangitis
pleomorphic cholangitis
HP:0030990.def: Cholangitis associated with mixed inflammatory infiltrates and the presence of fibrosis or sclerosis of the biliary tree.

name: sclerosing cholangitis
sclerosing cholangitis
HP:0030991.def: Cholangitis associated with evident ductal fibrosis that develops as a consequence of long-standing bile duct inflammatory, obstruction, or ischemic injury; it can be obliterative or nonobliterative.

name: abnormal pancreatic duct morphology
abnormal pancreatic duct morphology
HP:0030992.def: Any structural anomaly of the pancreatic duct, which is the tubular structure that collects exocrine pancreatic secretions and transports them to the duodenum.

name: duplication of pancreatic duct
duplication of pancreatic duct
HP:0030993.def: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of two separate pancreatic ducts.

name: pancreas divisum
pancreas divisum
HP:0030994.def: A congenital anomaly of the pancreas that results from failed fusion of the dorsal and ventral ducts during embyological development. Three variants have been described: type 1 or classical divisum in which there is total failure of fusion; type 2 in which dorsal drainage is dominant in the absence of the duct of Wirsung; and type 3 or incomplete divisum where a small communicating branch is present.

name: peritoneal effusion
peritoneal effusion
HP:0030995.def: An increase in the amount of fluid present in the peritoneal cavity (between the layers of the peritoneum that lines the abdomen).

name: megaduodenum
megaduodenum
HP:0030996.def: Dilation and elongation of the duodenum with hypertrophy of all layers of the duodenum.

name: atretic vas deferens
atretic va deferens
HP:0030997.def: Abnormal closure or blockage of the vas deferens.

name: cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhoea
cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhoea
HP:0030998.def: Drainage of cerebrospinal fluid through the nose. This can occur when there is a fistula between the dura and the skull base and discharge of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the nose.

name: abnormal vestibular saccule morphology
abnormal vestibular saccule morphology
HP:0030999.def: Any structural anomaly of the saccule of the vestibule. The saccule is the otolith organ that senses motions in the sagittal plane (i.e., up-down movement).

name: vestibular saccular degeneration
vestibular saccular degeneration
HP:0031000.def: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the saccule of the vestibule.

name: minifascicle formation
minifascicle formation
HP:0031001.def: A nerve fascicle or fasciculus is a small bundle of axons, enclosed by the perineurium. A minifascule refers to a group of thinly myelinated and unmyelinated axons surrounded by a delicate perineurium, and with a smaller diameter than a normal nerve fascicle.

name: hemiareflexia
hemiareflexia
HP:0031004.def: Areflexia that is limited to one side of the body.

name: acroparesthesia
acroparesthesia
HP:0031006.def: A type of paresthesia (tingling, pins-and-needles, burning or numbness or stiffness) that occurs in the hands and feet and particularly in the fingers and toes.

name: orofacial action - specific dystonia induced by speech
orofacial action - specific dystonia induce by speech
lingual dystonia
lingual dystonia
HP:0031008.def: Involuntary protrusions, movements, spams and contortions of the tongue.

name: ainhum
ainhum
HP:0031009.def: Development of a fibrotic constriction ring involving the base of one or more toes, conditioning eversion and absorption of distal structures, possibly progressing to spontaneous amputation.

name: hyperphalangy of the 3rd finger
hyperphalangy of the 3rd finger
HP:0031010.def: An accessory phalanx of the third (middle) finger that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges. Hyperphalangy results from an accessory ossification center at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

name: fatty streak
fatty streak
HP:0031011.def: Yellow-colored streaks, patches, or spots on the intimal surface of arteries. Fatty streaks stain red with Sudan III or Sudan IV.

name: thin - cap fibroatheroma
thin - cap fibroatheroma
HP:0031012.def: Thin-cap fibroatheroma is characterized by a relatively large necrotic core with an overlying thin fibrous cap measuring less than 65 micrometers and typically containing numerous macrophages, and is considered to be the precursor lesion of plaque rupture which is the most common cause of coronary thrombosis.

name: ankylosis
ankylosis
HP:0031013.def: A reduction of joint mobility resulting from changes involving the articular surfaces.

name: arteria lusoria
arteria lusoria
HP:0031014.def: Usually, three large arteries arise from the arch of the aorta: the brachiocephalic trunk (divided into the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery), the left common carotid artery, and the left subclavian artery. However, when aberrant right subclavian artery variant is present, the brachiocephalic trunk is absent and four large arteries arise from the arch of the aorta: the right common carotid artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery, and the final one with the most distal left sided origin, the right subclavian artery, also called the arteria lusoria.

name: intrahepatic portal vein sclerosis
intrahepatic portal vein sclerosis
HP:0031015.def: Sclerosis of the intrahepatic portal veins of the liver and generally accompanied by non-cirrhotic portal hypertension, features of which may include splenomegaly and varices.

name: alternating radiolucent and radiodense metaphyseal lines
alternate radiolucent and radiodense metaphyseal line
HP:0031016.def: Areas of radio-opaque sclerotic bands alternating with those of normal lucency give rise to stripes akin to a zebra.

name: swiss cheese atrial septal defect
swiss cheese atrial septal defect
HP:0031017.def: Multiple defects in the atrial septum.

name: eccrine syringofibroadenoma
eccrine syringofibroadenoma
HP:0031018.def: Eccrine syringofibroadenoma (ESFA) is a benign adnexal tumor arising most often on the extremities of elderly individuals characterized by anastomosing cords of cuboidal epithelial cells surrounded by a fibrovascular stroma containing plasma cells and ductal structures. ESFA stains positively with epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA).

name: pyknotic bone marrow neutrophils
pyknotic bone marrow neutrophil
HP:0031019.def: Nuclear lobes of neutrophils in the bone marrow are thickened and condensed, and individual lobes are connected by unusually long chromatin filaments.

name: bone marrow hypercellularity
bone marrow hypercellularity
HP:0031020.def: A larger than normal amount or percentage of hematopoietic cells relative to marrow fat.

name: squamous papilloma
squamous papilloma
HP:0031021.def: A benign epithelial neoplasm characterized by a papillary growth pattern and a proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells without morphologic evidence of malignancy [NCI thesaurus].

name: oropharyngeal squamous papilloma
oropharyngeal squamous papilloma
HP:0031022.def: A benign exophytic neoplasm that arises from the oropharynx. It is characterized by the presence of a connective tissue core covered by stratified squamous epithelium [NCI thesaurus].

name: multiple mucosal neuromas
multiple mucosal neuroma
HP:0031023.def: Multiple painful, dome-shaped, translucent pink to skin-colored papules on oral mucosa. Histologically, the lesions may demonstrate dermal proliferation of well-demarcated nerve bundles associated with abundant mucin and surrounded by a distinct perineural sheath.

name: cylindroma
cylindroma
HP:0031024.def: A benign skin adnexal tumor of eccrine differentiation.

name: gastric leiomyosarcoma
gastric leiomyosarcoma
HP:0031025.def: A malignant neoplasm of the stomach that grows submucosally in the gastric wall. Necrosis and hemorrhage may be visible radiologically. Histologically, spindle cells with abnormal mitotic activity may be visible.

name: snail - like ilia
snail - like ilium
HP:0031026.def: The ilia is round and hypoplastic with a very flat acetabular roof and a very unusual medial projection of bone that is said to resemble the head of a snail. Figure 4 of PMID:3799723 illustrates this feature.

name: internal notch of the femoral head
internal notch of the femoral head
HP:0031027.def: A small V-shaped indentation on the internal aspect of the femoral head. This feature is well illustrated in Figure 5 of PMID:11694546.

name: lactescent serum
lactescent serum
HP:0031028.def: Serum sample with a grossly white (milk-like, i.e., lactescent) appearance. This feature is indicative of an extremely elevated serum triglyceride level.

name: elevated carcinoembryonic antigen level
elevate carcinoembryonic antigen level
HP:0031029.def: An increased blood concentration of the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA). CEA is a member of the immunoglobulin supergene family. The human CEA gene family is clustered on chromosome 19q and comprises 29 genes. CEA is highly expressed in embryonic tissue and in some cancers, and is a widely used tumor marker.

name: elevated carcinoma antigen 125 level
elevate carcinoma antigen 125 level
HP:0031030.def: An increased blood concentration of carcinoma antigen 125 (CA-125). CA-125, also known as mucin 16, can exhibit increased blood levels in certain types of cancer.

name: abnormal retinol - binding protein level
abnormal retinol - binding protein level
HP:0031031.def: A deviation from normal blood concentration of retinol-binding protein (RBP). The most commonly used indicator of vitamin A status is the serum retinol concentration (retinol is one of the several compounds known as vitamin A). The serum RBP concentration is used as a surrogate measure for serum retinol.

name: decreased retinol - binding protein level
decrease retinol - bind protein level
HP:0031032.def: A reduced blood concentration of retinol-binding protein. This finding predicts vitamin A deficiency with high sensitivity and specificity.

name: impaired urinary acidification
impaired urinary acidification
HP:0031033.def: The kidney contributes towards acid-base homeostasis by excreting H+ ions and retaining bicarbonate. This process is known as acidification of the urine. The pH of urine ranges normally from 4.5 to 8. The inability to reduce the pH of the urine in a situation where it would be otherwise expected is known as an acidification defect.

name: abnormal insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit level
abnormal insulin like growth factor bind protein acid labile subunit level
HP:0031034.def: A deviation from the normal blood concentration of the insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit (IGFALS; Entrez Gene ID 3483). The acid-labile subunit (IGFALS) acts in the insulin-like growth (IGF) system by binding circulating IGF1 in a ternary complex with binding protein (IGFBP)-3 to prevent IGF1 from crossing the endothelial barrier.

name: chronic infection
chronic infection
HP:0031035.def: Presence of a protracted or persistent infection by a pathogen potentially related to an underlying abnormality of the immune system that is not able to clear the infection.

name: reduced growth - hormone binding protein level
reduce growth - hormone bind protein level
HP:0031036.def: A decreased blood concentration of growth hormone binding protein.

name: reduced insulin - like factor 3 level
reduce insulin - like factor 3 level
HP:0031037.def: Blood concentration of insulin-like factor 3 (ILF3) is below normal limits.

name: spermatogenesis maturation arrest
spermatogenesis maturation arrest
HP:0031038.def: Maturation arrest (MA) is defined as germ cells that fail to complete maturation. Uniform MA is characterized by spermatogenic arrest at the same stage of spermatogenesis throughout the seminiferous tubules. MA is subcategorized into early MA, in which only spermatogonia or spermatocytes are found, and late MA, in which spermatids are detected without spermatozoa.

name: spermatocyte maturation arrest
spermatocyte maturation arrest
HP:0031039.def: A type of spermatogenesis maturation arrest in which the block of developmental occurs in the spermatocyte stage. Testicular histology shows seminiferous tubules with Sertoli cells, spermatogonial cells and spermatocytes but no further differentiated cells like round spermatids.

name: round spermatid arrest
round spermatid arrest
HP:0031040.def: A failure of spermatogenesis to progress beyond the round spermatid stage. The round spermatid is the first haploid cells produced during spermatogenesis and normally further develop into mature spermatozoa. This abnormality can be visualized with testicular biopsy and is characterized seminiferous tubules with increased numbers of round spermatids with few or no mature spermatozoa.
synonym: maturation arrest of spermatogenesis at spermatid stage
maturation arrest of spermatogenesis at spermatid stage

name: obstruction of the superior vena cava
obstruction of the superior vena cava
HP:0031041.def: Blockage of blood flow through the superior vena cava (SVC). Because the venous drainage from the upper extremities, upper thorax and head is obstructed, SVC obstruction presents with symptoms related to engorgement of these areas. Both the degree of SVC compromise and the extent of collateral veins determine the varied clinical presentation, which can be as mild as slight facial and upper extremity edema or as dire as intracranial swelling, seizures, hemodynamic instability and tracheal obstruction.

name: strawberry tongue
strawberry tongue
HP:0031042.def: Inflammed tongue with hyperplastic (enlarged) fungiform papillae that is said to resemble a strawberry or raspberry.

name: type a4 brachydactyly
type a4 brachydactyly
HP:0031043.def: A type of brachydactyly characterized by brachymesophalangy affecting mainly the 2nd and 5th digits.

name: type a5 brachydactyly
type a5 brachydactyly
HP:0031044.def: A type of brachydactyly characterized by absent middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5.

name: acral blistering
acral blistering
HP:0031045.def: Bullae (defined as fluid-filled blisters more than 5 mm in diameter with thin walls) of the skin with an acral distribution (affecting peripheral regions such as hands and feet).

name: absent soft palate
absent soft palate
HP:0031046.def: A developmental defect characterized by lack of a soft palate.

name: paraproteinemia
paraproteinemia
HP:0031047.def: An abnormal immunoglobulin or part of an Ig (light chain) in the circulation. Paraproteins are typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: light - chain paraproteinemia
light - chain paraproteinemia
HP:0031048.def: An abnormal immunoglobulin light chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: heavy - chain paraproteinemia
heavy - chain paraproteinemia
HP:0031049.def: An abnormal immunoglobulin heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: whole - immunoglobulin paraproteinemia
whole - immunoglobulin paraproteinemia
HP:0031050.def: An abnormal immunoglobulin (heavy and light chain) in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

name: tarsal sclerosis
tarsal sclerosis
HP:0031051.def: An elevation in bone density in one or more tarsal bones of the foot. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

name: elevated vascular endothelial growth factor level
elevate vascular endothelial growth factor level
HP:0031052.def: Increased blood concentration of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).

name: coarctation in the transverse aortic arch
coarctation in the transverse aortic arch
HP:0031053.def: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized to the region of the transverse aortic arch.

name: long segment coarctation of the aorta
long segment coarctation of the aorta
HP:0031054.def: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a long segment of the arch of the aorta.

name: abnormal branching pattern of left aortic arch
abnormal branch pattern of left aortic arch
HP:0031055.def: A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries, whereby the aortic arch descends on the left as normal (as opposed to right aortic arch).

name: fusiform cerebral aneurysm
fusiform cerebral aneurysm
HP:0031056.def: A localized circumferential (i.e., bulges on all sides) dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.

name: skin fissure
skin fissure
HP:0031057.def: A clearly-defined and roughly linear cleavage in the skin that usually extends to the dermis.

name: impairment of activities of daily living
impairment of activity of daily living
HP:0031058.def: Difficulty in performing one or more activities normally performed every day, such as eating, bathing, dressing, grooming, work, homemaking, and leisure.

name: impaired ability to bathe oneself
impaired ability to bathe oneself
HP:0031059.def: This term applies to an individual who requires help to bathe more than one part of the body, get in or out of the tub or shower, or who requires total bathing.

name: impaired ability to dress oneself
impaired ability to dress oneself
HP:0031060.def: This applies to an individual who needs help with dressing or needs to be completely dressed.

name: impaired toileting ability
impaired toileting ability
HP:0031061.def: This term applies to an individual who requires help transferring to the toilet, cleaning self or who uses bedpan or commode.

name: impaired transferring ability
impaired transferring ability
HP:0031062.def: Applies to an individual who needs help in moving from bed to chair or requires a complete transfer.

name: impaired feeding ability
impaired feeding ability
HP:0031063.def: Applies to an individual who needs partial or total help with feeding or requires parenteral feeding.

name: impaired continence
impaired continence
HP:0031064.def: Partial or total incontinence of bowel or bladder.

name: empty ovarian follicle
empty ovarian follicle
HP:0031067.def: A failure to collect oocytes after an apparently normal controlled ovarian hyperstimulation cycle for in vitro fertilization.

name: abnormal femoral torsion
abnormal femoral torsion
HP:0031069.def: Femoral torsion, also known as femoral rotation or femoral version, refers to the twist between the proximal and distal parts of the femur on the transverse plane. Femoral anteversion averages between 30-40 degress at birth, and between 8-14 degrees in adults. This term applies if the amount of femoral torsion deviates from this range.

name: abnormal endocrine morphology
abnormal endocrine morphology
HP:0031071.def: Any anomaly of the structure of an organ ofthe endocrine system.

name: abnormal endocrine physiology
abnormal endocrine physiology
HP:0031072.def: Any anomaly of the function of the endocrine system.

name: abnormal response to endocrine stimulation test
abnormal response to endocrine stimulation test
HP:0031073.def: An anomalous response to a test that is designed to probe the function of the endocrine system.

name: abnormal response to acth stimulation test
abnormal response to acth stimulation test
HP:0031074.def: An anomolous response to stimulation by adminstration of the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH). ACTH stimulation normally stimulates the adrenal glands to release cortisol and adrenaline.
synonym: abnormal response to adrenocorticotropic - hormone stimulation test
abnormal response to adrenocorticotropic - hormone stimulation test
abnormal response to corticotropin stimulation test
abnormal response to corticotropin stimulation test

name: abnormal response to insulin tolerance test
abnormal response to insulin tolerance test
HP:0031075.def: An anomalous response to the insulin tolerance test (ITT), in which insulin is administered intravenously and blood glucose and potentially other compounds are measured at intervals. Insulin administration is intended to induce extreme hypoglycemia (bloodgluoce below 40 mg/dl), which in turn induces release of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and growth hormone (GH). ACTH induces the adrenal gland to release cortisol, which together with GH opposes the action of insulin on the blood glucose level.

name: impaired cortisol response to insulin stimulation test
impaired cortisol response to insulin stimulation test
HP:0031076.def: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the insulin tolerance test (ITT).

name: abnormal response to corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test
abnormal response to corticotropin release hormone stimulation test
HP:0031077.def: An anomalous response to the corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH) stimulation test. Normally,CRH is released by the hypothalamus to induce adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) release by the anterior pituitary. In the stimulation test, CRH is administered intravenously and ACTH and cortisol are measured at intervals.
synonym: abnormal response to crh stimulation test
abnormal response to crh stimulation test

name: impaired cortisol response to corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test
impaired cortisol response to corticotropin release hormone stimulation test
HP:0031078.def: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test.

name: impaired growth - hormone response to insulin stimulation test
impaired growth - hormone response to insulin stimulation test
HP:0031079.def: Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the insulin tolerance test (ITT).

name: abnormal response to glucagon stimulation test
abnormal response to glucagon stimulation test
HP:0031080.def: An anomalous response to the glucagon stimulation test, which like the insulin tolerance test (ITT) stimulates the release of both adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and growth hormone (GH).

name: impaired cortisol response to glucagon stimulation test
impaired cortisol response to glucagon stimulation test
HP:0031081.def: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the glucagon stimulation test.

name: impaired growth - hormone response to glucagon stimulation test
impaired growth - hormone response to glucagon stimulation test
HP:0031082.def: Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the glucagon stimulation test.

name: abnormal response to human chorionic gonadotrophin stimulation test
abnormal response to human chorionic gonadotrophin stimulation test
HP:0031083.def: An anomalous response to intravenous stimulation by human chorionic gonadotrophin. Stimulation with hCG stimulates testicular Leydig cells to secrete androgens via the Leydig hormone receptors.
synonym: abnormal response to hcg stimulation test
abnormal response to hcg stimulation test

name: excessive insulin response to glucagon test
excessive insulin response to glucagon test
HP:0031084.def: An abnormally high increase in insulin levels following a glucagon stimulation test.

name: decreased prealbumin level
decrease prealbumin level
HP:0031085.def: A reduced concentration of prealbumin in the blood. Prealbumin, also known as transthyretin, has a half-life in plasma of about 2 days, much shorter than that of albumin. Prealbumin is therefore more sensitive to changes in protein-energy status than albumin, and its concentration closely reflects recent dietary intake rather than overall nutritional status.

name: ectopic ovary
ectopic ovary
HP:0031086.def: Undescended or ectopic ovaries are characterized by the attachment of the upper pole of the ovary to an area above the level of the common iliac vessels.

name: absent pubertal growth spurt
absent pubertal growth spurt
HP:0031087.def: The abrupt and transient increase in the annual growth rate normally observed in adolescent individuals does not occur.

name: palatal edema
palatal edema
HP:0031089.def: Swelling related to fluid accumulation within the palate.

name: finger dactylitis
finger dactylitis
HP:0031090.def: Fingers appear swollen and plump owing to inflammation of the complete finger.

name: toe dactylitis
toe dactylitis
HP:0031091.def: Toes appear swollen and plump owing to inflammation of the complete toe.

name: spindle - shaped finger
spindle - shape finger
HP:0031092.def: Swelling of the hand at the knuckles, that gives the fingers a spindle shape (i.e., a round stick with tapered end and a broader base).

name: abnormal breast morphology
abnormal breast morphology
HP:0031093.def: Any anomaly of the structure of the breast.

name: abnormal breast physiology
abnormal breast physiology
HP:0031094.def: Any anomaly of the function of the breast.

name: abnormal humerus morphology
abnormal humerus morphology
HP:0031095.def: Any anomaly of the structure of the humerus.

name: delayed vertebral ossification
delay vertebral ossification
HP:0031096.def: A decrease in the amount of mineralized bone in one or more vertebrae compared with that expected for a given developmental age.

name: abnormal thyroid - stimulating hormone level
abnormal thyroid - stimulate hormone level
HP:0031097.def: Any deviation from the normal amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.

name: decreased thyroid - stimulating hormone level
decrease thyroid - stimulate hormone level
HP:0031098.def: Reduced amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.

name: abnormal circulating inhibin level
abnormal circulate inhibin level
HP:0031099.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of inhibins, which are heterodimeric protein hormones secreted by granulosa cells of the ovary in females and Sertoli cells of the testis in males. Inhibins suppress the secretion of pituitary follicle-stimulating hormone.

name: decreased inhibin b level
decrease inhibin b level
HP:0031100.def: A reduced concentration of inhibin B in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating antimullerian hormone concentration
abnormal circulate antimullerian hormone concentration
HP:0031101.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the antimullerian hormone, a peptide produced by the granulosa cells of follicles. Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), also known as Mullerian inhibiting substance, is produced by the granulosa cells of small antral follicles of the ovary. AMH has an inhibiting role in the ovary, contributing to follicular arrest. AMH levels in women are low until the age of 8, rise rapidly until puberty and decline steadily from the age of 25 until menopause, when AMH production ceases.

name: increased circulating antimullerian hormone concentration
increase circulate antimullerian hormone concentration
HP:0031102.def: An elevation above the normal range of the antimullerian hormone in the circulation.

name: decreased cirrculating antimullerian hormone circulation
decrease cirrculating antimullerian hormone circulation
HP:0031103.def: A reduction below the normal range of the antimullerian hormone in the circulation.

name: insulin receptor antibody positivity
insulin receptor antibody positivity
HP:0031104.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the insulin receptor.

name: abnormal uterus morphology
abnormal uterus morphology
HP:0031105.def: Any anomaly of the structure of the uterus

name: t - shaped uterus
t - shape uterus
HP:0031106.def: An abnormality of the uterus characterized by a normal uterine outline but with an abnormal T-shaped uterine cavity with narrowing cavity due to thickened lateral walls with a correlation 2/3 uterine corpus and 1/3 cervix. The abnormlaity is said to resemble the letter T in hysterosalpingographic imaging.

name: decreased fibular diameter
decrease fibular diameter
HP:0031107.def: Reduced width of the cross sectional diameter of the fibula.

name: triceps weakness
triceps weakness
HP:0031108.def: A lack of strength in the triceps muscle, which normally is responsible for extending (straightening) the elbow and mediating certain shoulder movements.

name: agalactia
agalactia
HP:0031109.def: Failure of secretion of milk following childbirth associated with an inability to breastfeed an infant.

name: twin - to - twin transfusion
twin - to - twin transfusion
HP:0031110.def: As a result of sharing a single placenta, the blood supplies of monochorionic twin fetuses can become connected, so that they share blood circulation: although each fetus uses its own portion of the placenta, the connecting blood vessels within the placenta allow blood to pass from one twin to the other.Depending on the number, type and direction of the interconnecting blood vessels (anastomoses), blood can be transferred disproportionately from one twin (the donor) to the other (the recipient). This state of transfusion causes the donor twin to have decreased blood volume, retarding the donor's development and growth. The blood volume of the recipient twin is increased, which can strain the fetus's heart and eventually lead to heart failure.

name: cutaneous hamartoma
cutaneous hamartoma
HP:0031111.def: A hamartoma (tissue malformation consisting of an abnormal mixture of constitutive components) originating in the skin.

name: purely bicuspid aortic valve
purely bicuspid aortic valve
HP:0031117.def: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by two equal-sized cusps, with no raphe and only two commissures. There is a lateral arrangement of the free edge of the cusps. Note that this differs from some other forms of BAV in which there are three commissures and two of the three cusps are joined by a raphe forming two functional leaflets. This type of BAV often is associated with aortic stenosis.

name: single raphe bicuspid aortic valve
single raphe bicuspid aortic valve
HP:0031118.def: A type of bicuspid aortic valvue (BAV) characterized by the presence of a single raphe that extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps, resulting in two leaflets of unequal size.

name: bicuspid aortic valve with right - left cusp fusion
bicuspid aortic valve with right - leave cusp fusion
HP:0031119.def: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the right and left cusps (RL fusion pattern). This results in two leaflefts with an anterior-posterior leaflet orientation (also called the typical pattern). There is thus one completely developed noncoronary cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped left and right coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

name: bicuspid aortic valve with right - noncoronary cusp fusion
bicuspid aortic valve with right - noncoronary cusp fusion
HP:0031120.def: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the right and noncoronary cusps (RN fusion pattern). This results in two leaflets with right-left leaflet orientation (also called the atypical pattern). There is thus one completely developed left cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped right and noncoronary coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

name: bicuspid aortic valve with left - noncoronary cusp fusion
bicuspid aortic valve with left - noncoronary cusp fusion
HP:0031121.def: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the left and noncoronary cusps (LN fusion pattern). There is thus one completely developed right cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped left and noncoronary coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

name: two - raphe bicuspid aortic valve
two - raphe bicuspid aortic valve
HP:0031122.def: A type of bicuspid aortic valvue (BAV) characterized by the presence of two raphes that each extend from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps. This type of BAV has developmental anlagen of three cusps, commissures, and sinuses, but two commissures are more or less malformed and obliterated, giving rise to a raphe, a fibrous ridge, which extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps. This type of BAV is typically associated with a high degree of aortic stenosis.

name: recurrent gastroenteritis
recurrent gastroenteritis
HP:0031123.def: Increased susceptibility to gastroenteritis, an infectious inflammationof the stomach and small intestines manifested by signs and symptoms such as diarheas and abdominal pain, as manifested by recurrent episodes of gastroenteritis.

name: decreased platelet thromboxane a2 receptor
decrease platelet thromboxane a2 receptor
HP:0031124.def: Decreased cell membrane concentration of thromboxane A2 receptor that is stimulated by thromboxane A2 (TBXA2).

name: decreased platelet alpha - 2a - adrenergic receptor
decrease platelet alpha - 2a - adrenergic receptor
HP:0031125.def: Decreased cell membrane concentration of alpha-2A adrenergic receptor that is stimulated by epinephrine.

name: impaired clot retraction
impaired clot retraction
HP:0031126.def: Platelets contain contractile proteins (actin and myosin) that induce clot retraction. As the platelets contract, they pull on the surrounding fibrin strands, squeezing serum form the mass, compacting the clot and drawing the ruptured edges of the blood vessel more closely together. Clot retraction is directly proportional to the platelet count and inversely proportional to the fibrinogen concentration.

name: impaired convulxin - induced platelet aggregation
impaired convulxin - induced platelet aggregation
HP:0031127.def: Abnormal response to convulxin as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of convulxin.

name: impaired collagen - related peptide - induced platelet aggregation
impaired collagen - relate peptide - induced platelet aggregation
HP:0031128.def: Abnormal response to collagen-related peptide (CRP) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of CRP.

name: impaired phorbol myristate acetate - induced platelet aggregation
impaired phorbol myristate acetate - induced platelet aggregation
HP:0031129.def: Abnormal response to phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of PMA.

name: impaired calcium ionophore - induced platelet aggregation
impaired calcium ionophore - induced platelet aggregation
HP:0031130.def: Abnormal response to calcium Ionophore (such as A23187) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of the ionophore.
synonym: impaired ca ionophore - induced platelet aggregation
impaired ca ionophore - induced platelet aggregation
impaired ca2+ ionophore - induced platelet aggregation
impaired ca2+ ionophore - induced platelet aggregation

name: abnormal platelet phosphatidylserine exposure
abnormal platelet phosphatidylserine exposure
HP:0031131.def: An abnormality of phosphatidylserine (PS) on activated platelets. PS is normally located on the cytoplasmic face of the resting platelet membrane but appears on the plasma-oriented surface of discrete membrane vesicles that derive from activated platelets. Thrombin, the central molecule of coagulation, is produced from prothrombin by a complex (prothrombinase) between factor Xa and its protein cofactor (factor V(a)) that forms on platelet-derived membranes. This complex enhances the rate of activation of prothrombin to thrombin by roughly 150,000 fold relative to factor X(a) in solution. The negatively charged surface of PS-containing platelet-derived membranes is at least partly responsible for this rate enhancement.

name: impaired annexin v binding to platelet phosphatidylserine
impaired annexin v bind to platelet phosphatidylserine
HP:0031132.def: Reduced binding of annexin V to platelet membrane, which is mediated by exposed phosphatidylserine. This can be measured by flow cytometry.

name: increased annexin v binding to platelet phosphatidylserine
increase annexin v bind to platelet phosphatidylserine
HP:0031133.def: Elevated binding of annexin V to platelet membrane, which is mediated by exposed phosphatidylserine. This can be measured by flow cytometry.

name: cor triatrium sinister
cor triatrium sinister
HP:0031134.def: A developmental anomaly of the heart characterized by the presence of three atria because the left atrium is divided by an abnormal septum.

name: triggered by physical trauma
trigger by physical trauma
HP:0031135.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a trauma (injury to tissue).

name: decreased acrosin in sperm head
decrease acrosin in sperm head
HP:0031136.def: A reduced amount of the enzyme acrosin in the sperm head acrosome. The acrosome is an organelle in the anterior half of the head of spermatozoa, and acrosin is a protease that contributes to the digestation of the zona pellucida in the fertilization process.

name: storage in hepatocytes
storage in hepatocytes
HP:0031137.def: Hepatocytes (liver parenchymal cells) exhibit a bloated appearance because of expansion of the cytoplasm by accumulated material.

name: abnormal b - type natriuretic peptide concentration
abnormal b - type natriuretic peptide concentration
HP:0031138.def: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP).
synonym: abnormal b - type natriuretic peptide level
abnormal b - type natriuretic peptide level

name: frog - leg posture
frog - leg posture
HP:0031139.def: A type of rest posture in an infant that indicated a generalized reduction in muscle tone. The hips are flexed and the legs are abducted to an extent that causes the lateral thigh to rest upon the supporting surface. This posture is said to resemble the legs of a frog.

name: abnormal liver sonography
abnormal liver sonography
HP:0031140.def: An abnormal appearance of the liver or any of its components on sonography (ultrasound).

name: increased hepatic echogenicity
increase hepatic echogenicity
HP:0031141.def: Increased echogenicity of liver tissue on sonography, manifested as an increased amount of white on the screen of the sonography device.

name: abnormal hepatic echogenicity
abnormal hepatic echogenicity
HP:0031142.def: Any deviation from the normal degree of echogenicity of the liver on sonography. Echogenicity refers to the ability of a tissue to reflect or transmit ultrasound waves in the context of surrounding tissues. Whenever there is an interface of structures with different echogenicities, a visible difference in contrast will be apparent on the screen. Based on echogenicity, a structure can be characterized as hyperechoic (white on the screen), hypoechoic (gray on the screen) and anechoic (black on the screen).

name: decreased hepatic echogenicity
decrease hepatic echogenicity
HP:0031143.def: Reduced echogenicity of liver tissue on sonography, manifested as an increased amount of black on the screen of the sonography device.

name: coarsened hepatic echotexture
coarsen hepatic echotexture
HP:0031144.def: The appearance of the liver in sonographic images is normally uniform. This term applies when there is an irregular or non-uniform appearance of the liver parenchyma in liver sonography.

name: starry sky appearance on hepatic sonography
starry sky appearance on hepatic sonography
HP:0031145.def: An abnormal echotexture visible in liver ultrasound manifesting as a diffuse hyperechoic liver echotexture with multiple, small hypoechoic lesions. The appearance is said to resemble a starry sky (multiple white spots on a dark background).

name: impaired oral bolus formation
impaired oral bolus formation
HP:0031146.def: An abnormality of swallowing characterized by reduced tongue coordination to form bolus after chewing. Food material spreads over the oral cavity instead of being concentrated into a bolus that is easily swallowed.

name: vitreomacular adhesion
vitreomacular adhesion
HP:0031150.def: Perifoveal vitreous separation with remaining vitreomacular attachment and unperturbed foveal morphologic features. It is an OCT finding that is almost always the result of normal vitreous aging, which may lead to pathologic conditions.

name: vitreomacular traction
vitreomacular traction
HP:0031151.def: Vitreomacular traction is characterized by anomalous posterior vitreous detachment accompanied by anatomic distortion of the fovea, which may include pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid. Vitreomacular traction can be subclassified by the diameter of vitreous attachment to the macular surface as measured by OCT, with attachment of 1500 micrometers or less defined as focal and attachment of more than 1500 micrometers as broad.

name: full - thickness macular hole
full - thickness macular hole
HP:0031152.def: Full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) is defined as a foveal lesion with interruption of all retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium. Full-thickness macular hole is primary if caused by vitreous traction or secondary if directly the result of pathologic characteristics other than vitreomacular traction. Full-thickness macular hole is subclassified by size of the hole as determined by OCT and the presence or absence of vitreomacular traction.

name: membranous vitreous appearance
membranous vitreous appearance
HP:0031153.def: Vitreous humor of the eye displaying consisting of a vestigial gel in the retrolental space bounded by a convoluted membrane.

name: beaded vitreous appearance
bead vitreous appearance
HP:0031154.def: Vitreous humor of the eye displaying beaded bundles of irregular diameters.

name: increased arden ratio of electrooculogram
increase arden ratio of electrooculogram
HP:0031155.def: An abnormal increase in the Arden ratio, which is the ratio between the light peak and the dark trough of the smoothed (physiologic) EOG record.

name: decreased platelet glycoprotein ib
decrease platelet glycoprotein ib
HP:0031156.def: Decreased platelet cell membrane concentration of glycoprotein Ib.

name: carotid cavernous fistula
carotid cavernous fistula
HP:0031157.def: An abnormal connection between a carotid artery and the cavernous sinus.

name: widened atrophic scar
widen atrophic scar
HP:0031158.def: An atrophic scar (fibrous connective tissue resulting from incomplete healing of a wound) that has stretched (gotten wider), a manifestation of tissue fragility.

name: thinning of descemet membrane
thinning of descemet membrane
HP:0031159.def: A reduction in the thickness of Descemet's membrane.

name: myelokathexis
myelokathexis
HP:0031160.def: Impaired egress of mature neutrophils from bone marrow causing neutropenia.

name: reduced brain glutamate level by mrs
reduce brain glutamate level by mr
HP:0031161.def: An decrease in the level of glutamate (Glu) in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: impaired oropharyngeal swallow response
impaired oropharyngeal swallow response
HP:0031162.def: Delay or absence of the swallow response, reflexes triggered by the contact the food bolus makes with the anterior faucial pillars.

name: low femoral bone density
low femoral bone density
HP:0031163.def: Reduced bone mineral density of the femur.

name: growth arrest lines
growth arrest line
HP:0031164.def: Growth arrest lines are alternating transverse rings of sclerosis at the metaphysis of a long bone.

name: multifocal seizures
multifocal seizure
HP:0031165.def: Seizures that start from several different areas of the brain (i.e., with multiple ictal onset locations).

name: eyelid myokymia
eyelid myokymia
HP:0031166.def: Involuntary, fine, continuous, undulating contractions of the eyelid.

name: triggered by ingestion of potassium - rich food
trigger by ingestion of potassium - rich food
HP:0031167.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking foods rich in potassium.
synonym: triggered by ingestion of k - rich food
trigger by ingestion of k - rich food

name: postterm pregnancy
postterm pregnancy
HP:0031169.def: A pregnancy that extends to 42 weeks of gestation or beyond.

name: female fetal virilization
female fetal virilization
HP:0031170.def: Fetal masculinization of female external genitalia.

name: femoral spur
femoral spur
HP:0031171.def: A bony projection (spur, osteophyte) originating from the femur, often in the medial femoral neck.

name: sectoral retinitis pigmentosa
sectoral retinitis pigmentosa
HP:0031172.def: A variant of retinitis pigmentosa in which there is a regional distribution of the retinal degeneration.

name: tibial spur
tibial spur
HP:0031173.def: A bony projection (spur, osteophyte) originating from the tibia.

name: double - layered patella
double - layer patella
HP:0031174.def: An anomaly of the patella characterized by two layers visible on lateral knee X-ray such that one layer is in front of the other in the sagittal orientation (See Figure 2A and 3B of PMID:12966518). This finding persists into adulthood.

name: absent cervical vertebra
absent cervical vertebra
HP:0031175.def: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies of the cervical spine.

name: absent thoracic vertebra
absent thoracic vertebra
HP:0031176.def: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies of the thoracic spine.

name: finger flexor weakness
finger flexor weakness
HP:0031177.def: Reduced ability to flex (bend) the fingers. This can manifest as incomplete closure of the hand due to weakness in finger flexion.

name: fixed head retroflexion
fix head retroflexion
HP:0031178.def: Head is bent in the posterior direction in a permanent fashion.

name: nuchal rigidity
nuchal rigidity
HP:0031179.def: Resistance of the extensor muscles of the neck to being bent forwards (i.e., impaired neck flexion) as a result of muscle spasm of the extensor muscles of the neck. Nuchal rigidity is not a fixed rigidity. Nuchal rigidity has been used as a bedside test for meningism, although its sensitivity for this purpose has been debated.

name: erythema migrans
erythema migrans
HP:0031180.def: An expanding erythematous (red) skin lesion, usually round or oval, by definition at least 5 cm in size (in largest diameter).

name: necrolytic migratory erythema
necrolytic migratory erythema
HP:0031181.def: Acral or periorificial lesions that evolve in recurrent crops, with an annular and migratory distribution.

name: increased circulating nt - probnp concentration
increase circulate nt - probnp concentration
HP:0031185.def: An elevated level of circulating N-terminal part of the prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP).

name: abnormal circulating deoxycorticosterone level
abnormal circulate deoxycorticosterone level
HP:0031186.def: An abnormality of the concentration of deoxycorticosterone in the blood. Deoxycorticosterone comprises 11-deoxycorticosterone and 21-deoxycorticosterone.

name: abnormal circulating pregnenolone concentration
abnormal circulate pregnenolone concentration
HP:0031187.def: An abnormality of the concentration of pregnenolone in the blood.

name: genital edema
genital edema
HP:0031188.def: A buildup of fluid that causes swelling in the soft tissues of the genital area.

name: wrist drop
wrist drop
HP:0031189.def: A condition in which the affected individual cannot extend the wrist, which hangs flaccidly.

name: superficial dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
superficial dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
HP:0031190.def: Numerous lymphocytes surrounding blood vessels in the superfical part of the dermis.

name: deep dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
deep dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
HP:0031191.def: Numerous lymphocytes surrounding blood vessels in the deep part of the dermis.

name: abnormal morphology of left ventricular trabeculae
abnormal morphology of left ventricular trabecula
HP:0031192.def: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the left ventricle of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

name: abnormal morphology of right ventricular trabeculae
abnormal morphology of right ventricular trabecula
HP:0031193.def: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the right ventricle of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

name: increased density of left ventricular trabeculae
increase density of left ventricular trabecula
HP:0031194.def: An increased density (number and tightness) of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the left ventricles of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

name: apical hypertrabeculation of the left ventricle
apical hypertrabeculation of the left ventricle
HP:0031195.def: An increased number and density of the trabeculae in the apex (tip) of the left ventricle.

name: thin myocardium compact layer
thin myocardium compact layer
HP:0031196.def: Reduced thickness of the outer, dense layer of the myocardium.

name: cellular urinary casts
cellular urinary cast
HP:0031197.def: A type of urinary cast composed of cells incorporated in a protein matrix. The cells can be those found in the urinary sediment (erythrocytes, leuklocytes, renal tubular epithelial cells).

name: renal tubular epithelial cell casts
renal tubular epithelial cell cast
HP:0031198.def: A type of cellular urinary cast composed of renal tubular epithelial cells.

name: acellular urinary casts
acellular urinary cast
HP:0031199.def: A type of urinary cast composed of a proteinaceous matrix without a substantial number of cells.

name: hyaline casts
hyaline cast
HP:0031200.def: A type of acellular urinary cast that are composed only of Tamm-Horsfall glycoprotein, a fact which explains their low refractive index. Hyaline casts may display a spectrum of morphologies, which includes fluffy, compact, convoluted or wrinkled casts. Hyaline casts have a smooth texture and usually have parallel sides with clear margins and blunted ends.

name: granular casts
granular cast
HP:0031201.def: A type of acelluar casts that have a surface composed of granules, which can vary in size. The granules can be rather heterogeneous, ranging from fine (finely granular cast) up to coarse (coarsely granular cast), dark, clear, and pigmented.

name: waxy casts
waxy cast
HP:0031202.def: A type of acellular urinary casts that display a melted wax (waxy) appearance, which gives them a high refractive index. They are frequently dark, with blunt extremities, indented and cracked edges and a large size, which is often several times that of other types of casts.

name: fatty casts
fatty cast
HP:0031203.def: A type of acellular urinary casts that contain lipid droplets, oval fat bodies or cholesterol crystals, and are often associated with the free forms of these elements. Their identification may require the use of polarised light microscopy, under which fatty particles embedded into the cast matrix appear as Maltese crosses.

name: bacterial cell casts
bacterial cell cast
HP:0031204.def: A type of urinary cast that contain bacteria. Bacterial casts can be difficult to identify and can be distinguished from other types of casts using phase contrast microscopy. Bacterial casts are diagnostic of acute pyelonephritis or intrinsic renal infection.

name: reduced lysosomal acid lipase activity
reduce lysosomal acid lipase activity
HP:0031205.def: Reduction in the activity of lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) in the blood. Lysosomal lipase activity is measured. LAL hydrolyzes cholesteryl esters derived from cell internalization of plasma lipoproteins.

name: striatal t2 hyperintensity
striatal t2 hyperintensity
HP:0031206.def: Abnormally bright T2 signal from the striatum on brain magnetic resonance imaging.

name: hepatic hemangioma
hepatic hemangioma
HP:0031207.def: A congenital vascular malformation in the liver composed of masses of blood vessels that are atypical or irregular in arrangement and size.

name: increased pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
increase pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
HP:0031208.def: An increased concentration of circulating alpha polypeptide of glycoprotein hormones (NCBI Gene 1081). This alpha subunit is common to luteinizing hormone (LH) , follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) , thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) and human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), which are glycoprotein hormones composed of an identical alpha subunit together with a beta subunit that confers biological specificity. The alpha subunit is used as a marker for tumors that produce these hormones.
synonym: increased pituitary glycoprotein alpha subunit level
increase pituitary glycoprotein alpha subunit level
increased pituitary glycoprotein polypeptide alpha subunit level
increase pituitary glycoprotein polypeptide alpha subunit level

name: decreased circulating lipoprotein lipase concentration
decrease circulate lipoprotein lipase concentration
HP:0031209.def: Reduction in the level of lipoprotein lipase in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating hyaluronic acid concentration
abnormal circulate hyaluronic acid concentration
HP:0031210.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of hyaluronic acid in the blood.

name: elevated cholesterol ester level
elevate cholesterol ester level
HP:0031211.def: An elevated concentration of circulating cholesterol esters, which are fatty acid esters of cholesterol and make up about two-thirds of total plasma cholesterol.

name: elevated circulating 17 - hydroxyprogesterone concentration
elevate circulate 17 - hydroxyprogesterone concentration
HP:0031213.def: An increased level of 17-hydroxyprogesterone in the blood. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is an intermediate steroid in the adrenal biosynthetic pathway from cholesterol to cortisol and is the substrate for steroid 21-hydroxylase.

name: decreased circulating dehydroepiandrosterone - sulfate concentration
decrease circulate dehydroepiandrosterone - sulfate concentration
HP:0031215.def: A reduced concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate in the blood.

name: increased circulating progesterone
increase circulate progesterone
HP:0031216.def: An elevated concentration of progesterone in the blood.

name: hot flashes
hot flash
HP:0031217.def: Sudden feelings of warmth that are generally most pronounced over the face, neck and chest.

name: inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
HP:0031218.def: A state of increased circulating antidiuretic hormone despite hyponatremia and hypo-osmolality with normal or increased plasma volume.
synonym: syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion

name: reduced radioactive iodine uptake
reduce radioactive iodine uptake
HP:0031219.def: A decreased amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.

name: increased radioactive iodine uptake
increase radioactive iodine uptake
HP:0031220.def: An elevated amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.

name: abnormal radioactive iodine uptake test result
abnormal radioactive iodine uptake test result
HP:0031221.def: Any deviation from normal in the amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.

name: increased circulating thyroxine - binding globulin level
increase circulate thyroxine - binding globulin level
HP:0031222.def: An elevated concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) in the blood.
synonym: thyroxine - binding globulin high in blood
thyroxine - binding globulin high in blood

name: focal pancreatic islet hyperplasia
focal pancreatic islet hyperplasia
HP:0031223.def: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans that affects only certain regions of the pancreas and not others.

name: diffuse pancreatic islet hyperplasia
diffuse pancreatic islet hyperplasia
HP:0031224.def: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans with a generalized distribution.

name: intrapulmonary shunt
intrapulmonary shunt
HP:0031225.def: Blood flow through a region of the lung in which little or no ventilation takes place, resulting in reduced oxygenation of the blood leaving the lungs.

name: perinephric fluid collection
perinephric fluid collection
HP:0031226.def: An accumulation of fluid in one or more of the perinephric spaces, which consist of the subcapsular, perirenal, anterior and posterior pararenal spaces. This abnormality can be demonstrated by cross-sectional imaging, particularly computed tomography.

name: nasopharyngeal teratoma
nasopharyngeal teratoma
HP:0031227.def: A teratoma arising in the nasopharyngeal region.

name: abnormal incisura morphology
abnormal incisura morphology
HP:0031228.def: An abnormal shape of the incisura, defined as the narrowed downward continuation of the conchal space bounded anteriorly by the borders of the tragus, posteriorly by the antitragus, and along its lower lateral margins and inferior boundary by the connection between the first two. The upper boundary is a somewhat arbitrary line crossing from the apices of the antitragus and the tragus.

name: increased incisura length
increase incisura length
HP:0031229.def: The length of the incisura from the upper to lower border is greater than that observed in the average population.

name: decreased incisura length
decrease incisura length
HP:0031230.def: The length of the incisura from the upper to lower border is less than that observed in the average population.

name: narrow incisura width
narrow incisura width
HP:0031231.def: Width of the incisura from the anterior to posterior border less than that observed in the average population.

name: increased incisura width
increase incisura width
HP:0031232.def: Breadth of the incisura from the anterior to posterior border greater than that observed in the average population.

name: horizontal inferior border of scapula
horizontal inferior border of scapula
HP:0031233.def: A morphological abnormality of the scapula in which there is a flat (horizontal) inferior edge of the scapula. The entire scapula is said to resemble a square, leading to the designation sqaring of the scapula (in Figure 1 of PMID:24706940 the scapulae have a roughly rectangular shape).

name: neutrophilic infiltration of the skin
neutrophilic infiltration of the skin
HP:0031234.def: A predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate of the dermis and or epidermis (i.e., a large number of neutrophils inferred to have migrated into the skin).

name: predominantly epidermal neutrophilic infiltrate
predominantly epidermal neutrophilic infiltrate
HP:0031235.def: Collection of neutrophils in the epidermis.

name: predominantly dermal neutrophilic infiltrate
predominantly dermal neutrophilic infiltrate
HP:0031236.def: Collection of neutrophils in the dermis.

name: internally nucleated skeletal muscle fibers
internally nucleated skeletal muscle fiber
HP:0031237.def: An abnormally increased proportion of nuclei of sarcomeres with an internal localization. Individual muscle fibers are syncytia, formed by embryonic fusion of many myoblasts or later, myosatellite cells. Each muscle fiber contains many nuclei, peripherally positioned immediately adjacent to the sarcolemmal membrane. In healthy muscle only 3-5% of fibers contain nuclei that are located internally, within the cell, but many disease processes lead to internal nuclei.

name: necklace skeletal muscle fibers
necklace skeletal muscle fiber
HP:0031238.def: A histological alteration of muscle fibers that resembles a necklace (necklace fibers). A substantial proportion of fibers (4-20% in PMID:19084976) show internalized nuclei aligned in a basophilic ring (necklace) at 3 micrometers beneath the sarcolemma. Ultrastructurally, such necklaces consist of myofibrils of smaller diameter, in oblique orientation, surrounded by mitochondria, sarcoplasmic reticulum and glycogen granules.

name: extrafoveal choroidal neovascularization
extrafoveal choroidal neovascularization
HP:0031239.def: A type of choroidal neovascularization in which the nearest edge of the area of neovascularization is located 200 to 1500 micrometers from the center of the fovea.

name: juxtafoveal choroidal neovascularization
juxtafoveal choroidal neovascularization
HP:0031240.def: A type of choroidal neovascularization in which the nearest edge of the area of neovascularization is located 1 to 199 micrometers from the center of the fovea.

name: subfoveal choroidal neovascularization
subfoveal choroidal neovascularization
HP:0031241.def: A type of choroidal neovascularization in which the area of neovascularization overlaps with the center of the fovea.

name: decreased circulating chylomicron concentration
decrease circulate chylomicron concentration
HP:0031242.def: Reduced plasma concentrations of chylomicrons, the large lipid droplet (up to 100 mm in diameter) of reprocessed lipid synthesized in epithelial cells of the small intestine and containing triacylglycerols, cholesterol esters, and several apolipoproteins.

name: decreased vldl cholesterol concentration
decrease vldl cholesterol concentration
HP:0031243.def: A reduction in the amount of very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
synonym: decreased circulating very - low - density lipoprotein levels
decreased circulate very - low - density lipoprotein level

name: swollen lip
swell lip
HP:0031244.def: Enlargement of the lip typically due to fluid buildup or inflammation.

name: productive cough
productive cough
HP:0031245.def: A cough that produces phlegm or mucus.

name: nonproductive cough
nonproductive cough
HP:0031246.def: A cough that does not produce phlegm or mucus.

name: whooping cough
whooping cough
HP:0031247.def: A type of cough characterized by a burst of numerous and rapid coughs followed by a long inhaling effort that is accompanied by a high-pitched whooping sound produced by the inhalation of air.

name: palmar pruritus
palmar pruritus
HP:0031248.def: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the palm(s) of the hand.

name: parageusia
parageusia
HP:0031249.def: A distortion of the sense of taste, often characterized by the sensation of a metallic taste.

name: lip fissure
lip fissure
HP:0031250.def: A severe crack in a lip. A lip fissure may be painful, may bleed and often is a recurring manifestation.

name: abnormal subclavian artery morphology
abnormal subclavian artery morphology
HP:0031251.def: Any anomaly of a subclavian artery.

name: dilated left subclavian artery
dilate leave subclavian artery
HP:0031252.def: Abnormally increased caliber of the left subclavian artery.

name: anomalous origin of left subclavian artery
anomalous origin of left subclavian artery
HP:0031253.def: Origin of the left subclavian artery from an anomalous anatomical location.

name: thalamic arteriovenous malformation
thalamic arteriovenous malformation
HP:0031254.def: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the thalamus.

name: hypothalamic arteriovenous malformation
hypothalamic arteriovenous malformation
HP:0031255.def: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the hypothalamus.

name: optic nerve arteriovenous malformation
optic nerve arteriovenous malformation
HP:0031256.def: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the optic nerve.

name: arteriovenous malformation of the maxilla
arteriovenous malformation of the maxilla
HP:0031257.def: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the maxilla.

name: delirium
delirium
HP:0031258.def: A state of sudden and severe confusion.

name: oophoritis
oophoritis
HP:0031259.def: An inflammation of the ovary or ovaries.

name: triangular tibia
triangular tibia
HP:0031260.def: A short, dysplastic tibia with a triangular shape. Instead of the normal shaft configuration of the tibia, the tibia forms a triangle with the longest side corresponding to the proximal-distal dimension, and the apex of the triangle directed laterally.

name: bladder polyp
bladder polyp
HP:0031261.def: An abnormal growth that projects from the mucous membrane of the urinary bladder.

name: abnormal renal corpuscle morphology
abnormal renal corpuscle morphology
HP:0031263.def: Any anomolous structure of the renal corpuscle, which is the initial component of the nephron that filters blood. The renal corpuscle consists of a knot of capillaries (glomerulus) that is surrounded by a double-walled capsule (Bowman capsule) that opens into a renal tubule.

name: abnormal bowman capsule morphology
abnormal bowman capsule morphology
HP:0031264.def: A structural anomaly of the double-walled capsule (Bowman capsule) that opens into a renal tubule.

name: abnormal glomerular visceral epithelial cell morphology
abnormal glomerular visceral epithelial cell morphology
HP:0031265.def: Any structural anomaly of the podocyte, which is a highly specialized cell of the Bowman capsule and which forms multiple interdigitating foot processes. Podocytes are interconnected by slit diaphragms and cover the exterior basement membrane surface of the glomerular capillary.

name: podocyte foot process effacement
podocyte foot process effacement
HP:0031266.def: An anomaly of podocyte morphology characterized by the loss of the interdigitating foot process pattern (generally called foot process effacement; FPE). The term FPE designates the loss of the usual interdigitating pattern of foot processes of neighboring podocytes, leading to relatively broad expanses of podocyte processes covering the glomerular basement membrane (GBM). It is widely viewed as a pathological derangement that is associated with leakage of macromolecules such as albumin through the glomerular filtration barrier.

name: abnormal cd69 upregulation upon tcr activation
abnormal cd69 upregulation upon tcr activation
HP:0031267.def: Any abnormality in the upregulation of CD69 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR). Upregulation of CD69 is one of the earliest and most sensitive measures of antigen recognition in the periphery, and transient expression of CD69 is associated with positive selection in the thymus.

name: decreased cd69 upregulation upon tcr activation
decrease cd69 upregulation upon tcr activation
HP:0031268.def: Reduced or impaired upregulation of CD69 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR).

name: abnormal cd25 upregulation upon tcr activation
abnormal cd25 upregulation upon tcr activation
HP:0031269.def: Any abnormality in the upregulation of CD25 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR). CD25 is the alpha chain of the IL2 receptor. Ligation of the T cell antigen receptor leads to the induction of CD25 expression.

name: decreased cd25 upregulation upon tcr activation
decrease cd25 upregulation upon tcr activation
HP:0031270.def: Decreased or impaired upregulation of CD25 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR).
synonym: poor cd25 upregulation upon tcr activation
poor cd25 upregulation upon tcr activation
reduced il2ra upregulation upon tcr activation
reduce il2ra upregulation upon tcr activation

name: absent ankle pulse
absent ankle pulse
HP:0031271.def: The pulsation of the posterior tibial artery behind the internal malleolus, or of the dorsalis pedis artery, cannot be detected on physical examination.

name: pulmonary arterial atherosclerosis
pulmonary arterial atherosclerosis
HP:0031272.def: Accumulation of lipids and inflammatory cells along the inner walls of the pulmonary artery.

name: shock
shock
HP:0031273.def: The state in which profound and widespread reduction of effective tissue perfusion leads first to reversible, and then if prolonged, to irreversible cellular injury.

name: hypovolemic shock
hypovolemic shock
HP:0031274.def: A state of shock characterized by decreased circulating blood volume in relation to total vascular capacity. This type of shock is characterized by a reduction of diastolic filling pressures.

name: distributive shock
distributive shock
HP:0031275.def: A hyperdynamic process resulting from excessive vasodilatation. Impaired blood flow causes inadequate tissue perfusion, which can lead to end-organ damage

name: obstructive shock
obstructive shock
HP:0031276.def: A type of shock characterized by inadequate cardiac preload due to obstructed venous return (e.g. pericardial tamponade, tension pneumothorax, abdominal compartment) or obstruction of arterial blood flow (e.g. pulmonary embolism).

name: abnormal thoracic duct morphology
abnormal thoracic duct morphology
HP:0031278.def: Any structural anomaly of the thoracic duct.

name: abnormal response to gonadotropin - releasing hormone stimulation test
abnormal response to gonadotropin - release hormone stimulation test
HP:0031279.def: An abnormal response to the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test. This test typically involves intravenous administration of GnRH followed by repeated blood sampling at various time points to measure the levels of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
synonym: abnormal response to gnrh stimulation test
abnormal response to gnrh stimulation test

name: increased lh response to gonadotropin - releasing hormone stimulation test
increase lh response to gonadotropin - release hormone stimulation test
HP:0031280.def: An abnormally high amount of luteinizing hormone (LH) is released upon gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test.

name: malalignment of the great toenail
malalignment of the great toenail
HP:0031282.def: A lateral deviation of the nail plate of the great toe along the longitudinal axis due to the lateral rotation of the nail matrix. The nail plate grows out in ridges.

name: tufted hairs
tufted hair
HP:0031283.def: The presence of tufts of 8-15 hairs that appear to emerge from a single follicular orifice.

name: flushing
flush
HP:0031284.def: Recurrent episodes of redness of the skin together with a sensation of warmth or burning of the affected areas of skin.

name: abnormal perifollicular morphology
abnormal perifollicular morphology
HP:0031285.def: Any structural anomaly in the areas surrounding the hair follicles.

name: seborrheic keratosis
seborrheic keratosis
HP:0031287.def: A raised growth on the skin of older individuals. The lesion usually is initially light tan and may darken to dark brown or nearly black. The consistent feature of seborrheic keratoses is their waxy, pasted-on or stuck-on look.

name: cobblestone - like hyperkeratosis
cobblestone - like hyperkeratosis
HP:0031288.def: The presence of verrucous, cobblestone-like papules and nodules in a region of skin that is said to have an appearance like that of cobblestones.

name: tuberous xanthoma
tuberous xanthoma
HP:0031290.def: A type of xanthoma characterized by a nodular form. Tuberous xanthomas are firm subcutaneous nodules,whereby the overlying skin can have red or red-yellow color changes.

name: ichthyosis follicularis
ichthyosis follicularis
HP:0031291.def: Ichthyosis follicularis is characterized by widespread non inflammatory thorn-like follicular projections. Dyskeratotic papules are most pronounced over the extensor extremities and scalp and are symmetrically distributed.

name: cutaneous abscess
cutaneous abscess
HP:0031292.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the skin.

name: digital pitting scar
digital pitting scar
HP:0031293.def: Pinhole-sized concave depressions with hyperkeratosis in the skin of a finger or toe.

name: left atrial enlargement
leave atrial enlargement
HP:0031295.def: Increase in size of the left atrium.

name: atrial septal hypertrophy
atrial septal hypertrophy
HP:0031296.def: An abnormal increase in the thickness of the atrial septum.

name: unroofed coronary sinus
unroofed coronary sinus
HP:0031297.def: Unroofed coronary sinus (CS) is a rare congenital cardiac anomaly in which there is partial (either focal or fenestrated) or complete absence of the roof of the CS, which results in a communication between the CS and the LA. Unroofed CS is the rarest type of atrial septal defect. It is often associated with persistent left superior vena cava (LSVC) and other forms of complex congenital heart disease, usually heterotaxia syndromes. The morphological types have been classified into 4 groups: Type I, completely unroofed with persistent LSVC; type II, completely unroofed without persistent LSVC; type III, partially unroofed mid portion; and type IV, partially unroofed terminal portion.

name: coronary sinus enlargement
coronary sinus enlargement
HP:0031298.def: Abnormal increase in size of the coronary sinus.

name: elevated left atrial pressure
elevate leave atrial pressure
HP:0031299.def: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the left atrium.

name: abnormal circulating properdin level
abnormal circulate properdin level
HP:0031300.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of properdin in the blood.

name: peripheral arterial calcification
peripheral arterial calcification
HP:0031301.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall.

name: lower extremity peripheral arterial calcification
low extremity peripheral arterial calcification
HP:0031302.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the leg.

name: femoral arterial calcification
femoral arterial calcification
HP:0031303.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the femoral artery.

name: iliac arterial calcification
iliac arterial calcification
HP:0031304.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the iliac artery.

name: tibial arterial calcification
tibial arterial calcification
HP:0031305.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the tibial artery.

name: intracranial arterial calcification
intracranial arterial calcification
HP:0031306.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in an artery that is located within the skull (intracranial).

name: internal carotid artery calcification
internal carotid artery calcification
HP:0031307.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the internal carotid artery.

name: vertebral artery calcification
vertebral artery calcification
HP:0031308.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the vertebral artery.

name: cerebral artery calcification
cerebral artery calcification
HP:0031309.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a cerebral artery.

name: basilar artery calcification
basilar artery calcification
HP:0031310.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the basilar artery.

name: middle cerebral artery calcification
middle cerebral artery calcification
HP:0031311.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the middle cerebral artery.

name: abdominal aortic calcification
abdominal aortic calcification
HP:0031313.def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in abdominal aorta.
