There is a lateral displacement of the inner canthus with a mild thinning, aplasia, or irregularity of the medial end of the eyebrow. There are no eyelid clefts. The soft tissue contour of the forehead is normal, with only a short downward prolongation of the paramedian frontal hairline to mark the superior extent of the soft tissue cleft. Flattening of the frontal process of the maxilla, an increase in the transverse dimension of the ethmoid sinus, and a laterally convex bowing of the medial orbital wall produce orbital hypertelorism. Superiorly there is a minor flattening of the frontal bone medially, and the nasofrontal angle is somewhat obtuse. The extensive pneumatization of the sinuses on the cleft side extends backward through the frontal and ethmoid sinuses and into the sphenoid sinus. The anatomy of the sphenoid, including the pterygoid processes, is otherwise normal. The anterior and middle cranial fossae floors are both broadened on the cleft side with minor widening of the cribriform plate.

name: tessier number 13 facial cleft
tessier number 13 facial cleft
HP:0031585.def: There is a paramedian frontal encephalocele and a soft tissue cleft that passes medial to an intact eyebrow. The frontal bone shows a paramedian bony cleft with an associated encephalocele. The olfactory groove, cribriform plate, and ethmoid sinus are all increased in transverse diameter, resulting in hypertelorism. The cleft extends medially to the undisturbed eyebrow to end in a short paramedian frontal widow's peak. The bony cleft begins in the region of the nasal bone and extends superiorly through the full height of the frontal bone. Posteriorly, the cleft extends through the cribriform plate and ethmoid sinus as far as the lesser wing and body of the sphenoid. The pterygoid processes are anatomically normal, but they are displaced laterally from the midline on the cleft side. There is orbital hypertelorism below and asymmetry of the floor of the anterior cranial fossa above.

name: tessier number 14 facial cleft
tessier number 14 facial cleft
HP:0031586.def: This midline cranial cleft usually occurs with a midline facial cleft that completes a median craniofacial dysraphia. A broad nasal root and bifid nose are associated with orbital hypertelorism and a median frontal encephalocele. The frontal bone abnormality varies from a minor flattening to a large midline defect. There is an increased distance between the olfactory grooves. The crista galli is widened, duplicated, or in some cases absent. Marked inferior prolapse of the enlarged ethmoid bone occurs with orbital hypertelorism. The severe orbital hypertelorism is associated with a broad flattening of the glabella and extreme lateral displacement of the inner canthi. The periorbita, including the eyelids and eyebrows, are otherwise normal. A long midline projection of the frontal hairline marks the superior extent of the soft tissue features of this midline cranial cleft. The median frontal defect delineates the region through which the frontal encephalocele herniates. The lateral segments of the frontal bone sweep upward from the region of the intact glabella and are flattened laterally. No pneumatization of the frontal sinus is evident. The crista galli and the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid are bifid. Just as the ethmoid, including the cribriform plate, is widened and caudally displaced, the sphenoid sinus is broadened and extensively, but symmetrically pneumatized. The lateral rotation of the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid results in a relative shortening of the anteroposterior dimension of the middle cranial fossa. The floor of the anterior cranial fossa is upslanting from its medial aspect to its lateral aspect, with a harlequin appearance on the coronal scan.

name: tessier number 30 facial cleft
tessier number 30 facial cleft
HP:0031587.def: A lower midline facial cleft, also known as the median mandibular cleft. It is a rare anomaly, which may be limited to a defect in the soft tissue of the lower lip. However, in the more severe form, it may extend into the bony mandibular symphysis.

name: unhappy demeanor
unhappy demeanor
HP:0031588.def: A noticeably unhappy disposition is characterized by negative assumptions, self-defeating talk, fear of failure, and negative rumination about past events.

name: suicidal ideation
suicidal ideation
HP:0031589.def: Frequent thoughts about or preoccupation with killing oneself.

name: asthenopia
asthenopia
HP:0031590.def: Eye strain, i.e., a feeling of fatigue or discomfort of the eyes related to 'overuse' of the eyes in activities such as reading or working at the computer and often accompanied by lacrimation or headache.

name: enlarged eustachian valve
enlarge eustachian valve
HP:0031591.def: An abnormally large Eustachian valve (postnatally). The Eustachian valve is also known as the valve of the inferior vena cava, and is an embryologic remnant of the valve of the inferior vena cava.

name: situs inversus with levocardia
situs inversus with levocardia
HP:0031592.def: Situs inversus of thoracic and abdominal viscera with the heart remaining normally situated on the left; usually associated with congenital cardiac abnormalities such as transposition of the great vessels and/or spleen defects including asplenia or polysplenia.

name: abnormal pr interval
abnormal pr interval
HP:0031593.def: An anomaly of the PR interval, which is the portion of the ECG from the onset of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex. A normal PR interval in adults is 0.12-0.2 seconds.

name: pr segment depression
pr segment depression
HP:0031594.def: A reduction in voltage of the PR segment below baseline.

name: abnormal p wave
abnormal p wave
HP:0031595.def: Any anomaly of the P wave of the EKG, which results from atrial depolarization. The P wave occurs when the sinoatrial node creates an action potential that depolarizes the atria.

name: abnormal pr segment
abnormal pr segment
HP:0031596.def: An anomaly of the PR segment, which begins at the endpoint of the P wave and ends at the onset of the QRS complex. The PR segment is normally flat and isoelectric.

name: pr segment elevation
pr segment elevation
HP:0031597.def: An increase in voltage of the PR segment above baseline.

name: notched p wave
notch p wave
HP:0031598.def: V-shaped cut (notch) in the middle of the P wave.

name: p mitrale
p mitrale
HP:0031599.def: A broad (120 ms or longer in duration) and bifid P-wave in EKG lead II.

name: p wave inversion
p wave inversion
HP:0031600.def: P wave below instead of above the baseline. P-wave inversion in the inferior leads may indicate a non-sinus origin of the P waves.

name: p pulmonale
p pulmonale
HP:0031601.def: The presence of tall, peaked P waves in EKG lead II.

name: abnormal mucociliary clearance
abnormal mucociliary clearance
HP:0031602.def: An anomaly in the system of mucociliary transport, which functions to transport the mucous layer lining the respiratory epithelium by ciliary beating.

name: impaired nasal mucociliary clearance
impaired nasal mucociliary clearance
HP:0031603.def: An abnormally increased amount of time required to clear mucus (and substances contained in the mucus) from the nasal mucosa. The nasal mucociliary clearance (NMC) system functions to transport the mucous layer lining the nasal epithelium towards the naso pharynx by ciliary beating in a metachronous fashion at a frequency of 7-16 Hz. NMC depends upon two principal components: physicochemical qualities and quantities of mucus and the properties of cilia that propel it. NMC is considered to be representative of pulmonary clearance. normal NMC time is determined to be up to 20 minutes. Duration of 30 minutes is considered as the cutoff point that discriminates normal subjects from subjects with impaired NMC. NMC can be measured by determination of the transport time of markers that are placed on the nasal mucosa including saccharine, radioactive markers, and dyes.

name: agenesis of the carotid canal
agenesis of the carotid canal
HP:0031604.def: A developmental defect characterized by the lack of formation of the carotid canal, which normally is a circular aperture in the temporal bone of the skull through which the internal carotid artery and the carotid plexus of nerves traverse.

name: abnormality of fundus pigmentation
abnormality of fundus pigmentation
HP:0031605.def: Any anomaly of the pigmentation of the fundus, the posterior part of the eye including the retina and optic nerve.

name: retinal cotton wool spot
retinal cotton wool spot
HP:0031606.def: Fluffy white patch on the retina, representing localized areas of dense white swelling of the retinal nerve fibre layer. They often have a zigzag internal structure, a feathered edge but an otherwise well-delineated form and an approximately 1 mm dimension; they project slightly into the vitreous and sometimes deflect retinal vessels.

name: pelvic organ prolapse
pelvic organ prolapse
HP:0031607.def: Weakness in the supporting structures of the pelvic floor allowing the pelvic viscera to descend or one or more of the pelvic organs drop from their normal position.

name: geographic atrophy
geographic atrophy
HP:0031609.def: Sharply demarcated area of partial or complete depigmentation of the fundus reflecting atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium with associated retinal photoreceptor loss. The margins of the de-pigmented area are usually scalloped and the large choroidal vessels are visible through the atrophic retinal pigment epithelium.

name: sub - inner limiting membrane hemorrhage
sub - inner limit membrane hemorrhage
HP:0031611.def: A type of intraretinal hemorrhage that is located in the superficial retina between the inner limiting membrane and the retinal nerve fiber layer.

name: inferior chorioretinal coloboma
inferior chorioretinal coloboma
HP:0031613.def: Absence of a region of the retina, retinal pigment epithelium, and choroid at the lower part of the fundus.

name: inferior retinal coloboma
inferior retinal coloboma
HP:0031614.def: A notch or cleft of the lower part of the retina.

name: hypopyon
hypopyon
HP:0031615.def: Presence of pus (appears as a white fluid) producing a fluid level in the inferior part of the anterior chamber.

name: anterior chamber flare
anterior chamber flare
HP:0031616.def: An abnormal appearance of the beam of light traveling through the anterior chamber of the eye in a slit lamp examination. The flare is produced by an increased concentration of proteins in the aqueous humor in the anterior chamber.

name: anterior chamber flare grade 2+
anterior chamber flare grade 2+
HP:0031619.def: Moderate anterior chamber flare (iris and lens details clear).

name: anterior chamber flare grade 3+
anterior chamber flare grade 3+
HP:0031620.def: Marked anterior chamber flare (iris and lens details hazy).

name: brown anomaly
brown anomaly
HP:0031622.def: An ocular motility defect where the affected eye(s) does not elevate in adduction but has full depression in adduction. It can be congenital or acquired from injury to or defect of the superior oblique tendon or trochlea and has a positive forced duction test result.

name: brow ptosis
brow ptosis
HP:0031623.def: Drooping of the upper eyebrow below the superior orbital rim.

name: moderate myopia
moderate myopia
HP:0031624.def: A moderate form of myopia with refractive error of between -3.00 and -6.00 diopters.

name: pseudoaneurysm
pseudoaneurysm
HP:0031625.def: A contained rupture of an artery with a disruption in all 3 layers of the arterial wall.

name: coronary ostial atresia
coronary ostial atresia
HP:0031626.def: Absence of the normal opening of a coronary ostium. There are normally two coronary ostia, which are site of origin of the main left or right main coronary artery and are located in the ascending aorta just above the aortic valve.

name: globus pallidus calcification
globus pallidus calcification
HP:0031627.def: Pathological deposition of calcium salts in the globus pallidus.

name: aborted sudden cardiac death
abort sudden cardiac death
HP:0031628.def: Cardiac arrest that would have led to rapid and unexpected death had an intervention not taken place to prevent it.

name: impaired tandem gait
impaired tandem gait
HP:0031629.def: Reduced ability to walk in a straight line while placing the feet heel to toe.

name: abnormal subpleural morphology
abnormal subpleural morphology
HP:0031630.def: Any structural anomaly located between the pleura and the chest wall.

name: subpleural honeycombing
subpleural honeycombing
HP:0031631.def: So-called honeycombs (variably sized cysts in a background of densely scarred tissue) located in the subpleural space.

name: anomalous origin of the right subclavian artery from the descending aorta
anomalous origin of the right subclavian artery from the descending aorta
HP:0031632.def: Abnormal origin of the right subclavian artery from the descending aorta. The right subclavian artery normally arises from the brachiocephalic trunk, which divides into the right common carotid artery and right subclavian artery.

name: isolation of the left subclavian artery
isolation of the left subclavian artery
HP:0031633.def: The loss of continuity between the left subclavian artery and the aorta, with persistent connection to the homolateral pulmonary artery through the patent (PDA) or nonpatent ductus arteriosus.

name: anomalous origin of the left common carotid artery from the main pulmonary artery
anomalous origin of the left common carotid artery from the main pulmonary artery
HP:0031634.def: The left common carotid artery normally originates from the aortic arch. This term refers to an origin of this artery from the main pulmonary artery.

name: anomalous origin of the left common carotid artery from the brachiocephalic artery
anomalous origin of the left common carotid artery from the brachiocephalic artery
HP:0031635.def: The left common carotid artery normally originates from the aortic arch. This term refers to an origin of this artery from the brachiocephalic artery.
synonym: anomalous origin of the left common carotid artery from the brachiocephalic trunk
anomalous origin of the left common carotid artery from the brachiocephalic trunk

name: anomalous origin of the right common carotid artery from the aorta
anomalous origin of the right common carotid artery from the aorta
HP:0031636.def: The right common carotid artery normally originates from the brachiocephalic artery. This term refers to an origin of this artery directly from the aorta.

name: right coronary artery ostial atresia
right coronary artery ostial atresia
HP:0031637.def: Absence of the normal opening of the coronary ostium from which the right main coronary artery originates.

name: anomalous origin of the left anterior descending artery from the pulmonary artery
anomalous origin of the left anterior descend artery from the pulmonary artery
HP:0031638.def: The left anterior descending artery (LAD) branches off from the pulmonary artery.

name: absent left main coronary artery
absent leave main coronary artery
HP:0031639.def: The left main coronary artery (LMCA) is absent and the left anterior descending (LAD) and left circumflex (LCX) arteries arise from separate but adjacent ostia in the left sinus of Valsava.

name: abnormal radial artery morphology
abnormal radial artery morphology
HP:0031640.def: Any structural anomaly of the radial artery.

name: fusiform ascending tubular aorta aneurysm
fusiform ascend tubular aorta aneurysm
HP:0031643.def: A concentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the ascending tubular aorta that involves the full circumference of the vessel wall.

name: fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm
fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm
HP:0031644.def: A concentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta that involves the full circumference of the vessel wall

name: saccular abdominal aortic aneurysm
saccular abdominal aortic aneurysm
HP:0031645.def: An eccentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta that involves only a portion of the circumference of the vessel wall.

name: fusiform aortic arch aneurysm
fusiform aortic arch aneurysm
HP:0031646.def: A concentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch that involves the full circumference of the vessel wall.

name: saccular aortic arch aneurysm
saccular aortic arch aneurysm
HP:0031647.def: An eccentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch that involves only a portion of the circumference of the vessel wall.

name: penetrating aortic ulcer
penetrate aortic ulcer
HP:0031648.def: A focal defect in the elastic lamina of the aortic wall that leads to localized medial disruption and potential rupture.

name: aortic rupture
aortic rupture
HP:0031649.def: Tearing of the aortic wall generally associated with profuse internal bleeding.

name: abnormal atrioventricular valve physiology
abnormal atrioventricular valve physiology
HP:0031650.def: Any functional defect of the mitral or tricuspid valve.

name: abnormal tricuspid valve physiology
abnormal tricuspid valve physiology
HP:0031651.def: Any functional defect of the tricuspid valve.

name: abnormal heart valve physiology
abnormal heart valve physiology
HP:0031653.def: Any functional abnormality of a cardiac valve.

name: abnormal pulmonary valve physiology
abnormal pulmonary valve physiology
HP:0031654.def: Any functional anomaly of the pumonary valve.

name: quadricuspid aortic valve
quadricuspid aortic valve
HP:0031655.def: The presence of an aortic valve with four instead of the normal three cusps (flaps).

name: systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
HP:0031656.def: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve (SAM) is a paradoxical motion of the anterior, and occasionally posterior, mitral valve leaflet towards the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) during systole.

name: abnormal heart sound
abnormal heart sound
HP:0031657.def: Any abnormal noise generated by the beating heart.

name: third heart sound
third heart sound
HP:0031658.def: The third heart sound (S3) is related to rapid filling in diastole. S3 can be a normal finding in children and adolescents but suggests heart failure in older patients.

name: fourth heart sound
fourth heart sound
HP:0031659.def: The fourth heart sound (S4) is a low-pitched sound that occurs just before the first heart sound (S1) when the atria contract to force blood into the left ventricle, that is, coincident with late diastolic filling of the ventricle due to atrial contraction.

name: loud first heart sound
loud first heart sound
HP:0031660.def: Abnormally increased volume of the first heart sound.

name: abnormal second heart sound
abnormal second heart sound
HP:0031661.def: Any anomaly of the second heart sound (S2), which is produced by aortic (A2) and pulmonic (P2) valve closure. The A2-P2 interval normally increases with inspiration and narrows with expiration.

name: fixed splitting of the second heart sound
fix splitting of the second heart sound
HP:0031662.def: Lack of variation in the splitting between the two components of the second heart sound with respiration. Normally, the aortic valve closure (A2) is followed by the pulmonic valve closure (P2) but the A2-P2 interval increases with inspiration and decreases with expiration.

name: paradoxical splitting of the second heart sound
paradoxical splitting of the second heart sound
HP:0031663.def: Normally, the aortic valve closure (A2) is followed by the pulmonic valve closure (P2) but the A2-P2 interval increases with inspiration and decreases with expiration. With paradoxical splitting, there is a delay in the closure of the aortic valve, so that A2 can follow P2; the individual components can be appreciated at the end of expiration and the interval narrows with inspiration (which is the oposite of the normal pattern).
synonym: reversed splitting of the second heart sound
reverse splitting of the second heart sound

name: systolic heart murmur
systolic heart murmur
HP:0031664.def: A heart murmur limited to systole, i.e., between the first and second heart sounds S1 and S2.

name: midsystolic murmur
midsystolic murmur
HP:0031665.def: A systolic murmur that begins after S1 and ends before S2, typically with a crescendo-decrescendo pattern.

name: late systolic murmur
late systolic murmur
HP:0031666.def: A murmur that occurs in the latter phase of systole.

name: holosystolic murmur
holosystolic murmur
HP:0031667.def: A heart murmur that occurs during the entire systolic phase from S1 to S2.

name: diastolic heart murmur
diastolic heart murmur
HP:0031668.def: A heart murmur that occurs during diastole, i.e., in the time between S2 and the subsequent S1.

name: middiastolic murmur
middiastolic murmur
HP:0031669.def: A murmur that occurs in the middle of the diastolic phase.

name: continuous heart murmur
continuous heart murmur
HP:0031670.def: A murmur that occurs in both systole and diastole.

name: typical atrial flutter
typical atrial flutter
HP:0031671.def: Typical atrial flutter is an organised atrial tachycardia. It can also be defined as a macroreentrant tachycardia confined to the right atrium. This arrhythmia has a 200-260 ms cycle length, although it may fluctuate depending on patient's previous treatment or ablation, congenital heart disease, etc. Ventricular rate response will be limited by the atrioventricular node conductions, usually presenting a 2:1 or 3:1 response, during atrial flutter. Typical (counter clockwise) flutter is associated with the common flutter pattern: a regular continuous undulation with dominant negative deflections in inferior leads II, III and aVF, often described also as a saw tooth pattern, and flat atrial deflections in leads I and aVL. Atrial deflections in V1 can be positive, biphasic or negative.

name: reverse typical atrial flutter
reverse typical atrial flutter
HP:0031672.def: A type of atrial flutter associated with rounded or bimodal positive deflections in inferior leads II, III and aVF, and a very characteristic bimodal negative wave in the shape of a W is seen in lead V1.

name: orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
HP:0031673.def: A type of atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) where the atrioventricular node is used for anterograde conduction and the accessory pathway for retrograde conduction.

name: antidromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
antidromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
HP:0031674.def: A type of atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) where the accessory pathway is used for anterograde conduction and the atrioventricular node for retrograde conduction.

name: fascicular left ventricular tachycardia
fascicular leave ventricular tachycardia
HP:0031675.def: A ventricular tachycardia (VT) characterized by right bundle branch block (RBBB) and left axis deviation (LAD) on electrocardiogram (ECG).

name: monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
HP:0031676.def: A type of ventricular tachycardia that is characterized by uniform QRS complexes within each lead (i.e., each QRS is identical or nearly so).

name: polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
HP:0031677.def: A type of ventricular tachycardia that is characterized by variable QRS complexes within each lead (i.e., QRS complexes may be different from beat to beat).

name: atherosclerotic lesion
atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0031678.def: A lesion associated with atherosclerosis, a multifactorial and multipart progressive disease manifested by the focal development within the arterial wall of lesions, that ranges from teh development of a fatty streak, plaque progression, and plaque disruption. Atherosclerotic lesions demonstrate consistent morphological characteristics, which indicate that each type may stabilize temporarily or permanently and that progression to the next type may require an additional stimulus.

name: type i atherosclerotic lesion
type i atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0031679.def: Type I lesions represent the very initial changes and are recognized as an increase in the number of intimal macrophages and the appearance of macrophages filled with lipid droplets (foam cells).

name: type ii atherosclerotic lesion
type ii atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0031680.def: Type II atherosclerotic lesions include the fatty streak lesion, the first grossly visible lesion, and are characterized by layers of macrophage foam cells and lipid droplets within intimal smooth muscle cells and minimal coarse-grained particles and heterogeneous droplets of extracellular lipid.

name: type iii atherosclerotic lesion
type iii atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0031681.def: Type III (intermediate) atherosclerotic lesions are the morphological and chemical bridge between type II and advanced lesions. Type III lesions appear in some adaptive intimal thickenings (progression-prone locations) in young adults and are characterized by pools of extracellular lipid in addition to all the components of type II lesions.

name: type v atherosclerotic lesion
type v atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0031682.def: Type V lesions are defined as lesions in which prominent new fibrous connective tissue has formed. When the new tissue is part of a lesion with a lipid core (type IV), this type of morphology may be referred to as fibroatheroma or type Va lesion. A type V lesion in which the lipid core and other parts of the lesion are calcified may be referred to as type Vb. A type V lesion in which a lipid core is absent and lipid in general is minimal may be referred to as type Vc. With these lesions, arteries are variously narrowed, generally more than with type IV. Importantly, as with type IV lesions, type V lesions may develop fissures, hematoma, and/or thrombus (type VI lesion), and for this reason too they are clinically relevant.

name: type vi atherosclerotic lesion
type vi atherosclerotic lesion
HP:0031683.def: Type VI atherosclerotic lesions generally have the underlying morphology of type IV or V lesions, surface disruptions, hematoma, and thrombosis may be (although less often) superimposed on any other type of lesion and even on intima without an apparent lesion. Complicating features may arise because of individual differences in risk factors and tissue reactions. These may include differences in composition of the blood, the relative quantities and distributions in the components of the underlying lesion or intima, as well as modifications of shear and tensile forces to which the lesion or intima is exposed. Clinical imaging of lesions may be expected to contribute greatly to the understanding of type VI lesions and the associated clinical syndromes.

name: renal artery atherosclerosis
renal artery atherosclerosis
HP:0031684.def: An atherosclerotic lesion located in the renal artery.

name: abnormal stool composition
abnormal stool composition
HP:0031685.def: Abnormal level of metabolite or other abnormal analyte result in a stool test.

name: increased stool alpha1 - antitrypsin concentration
increase stool alpha1 - antitrypsin concentration
HP:0031686.def: An abnormally elevated amount of alpha1-antitrypsin in the feces.

name: abnormally loud pulmonic component of the second heart sound
abnormally loud pulmonic component of the second heart sound
synonym: accentuation of the pulmonic component of the second heart sound
accentuation of the pulmonic component of the second heart sound

name: erythroid dysplasia
erythroid dysplasia
HP:0031688.def: Dysplasia in the erythroid lineage, which presents with a variety of morphological changes in the bone marrow, including nuclear budding or irregular nuclear contour in erythroblasts.

name: megakaryocyte dysplasia
megakaryocyte dysplasia
HP:0031689.def: The presence of micro-megakaryocytes, hypo-lobed, or non-lobed nuclei in megakaryocytes of all sizes and multiple, widely-separated nuclei.

name: opportunistic infection
opportunistic infection
HP:0031690.def: An infection that is caused by a pathogen that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such pathogens take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

name: severe cytomegalovirus infection
severe cytomegalovirus infection
HP:0031692.def: An unusually severe infection by cytomegalovirus.

name: severe epstein barr virus infection
severe epstein barr virus infection
HP:0031693.def: An unusually severe Epstein Barr virus (EBV) infection.

name: severe parainfluenza infection
severe parainfluenza infection
HP:0031695.def: An unusually severe infection by a parainfluenza virus.

name: disseminated viral infection
disseminate viral infection
HP:0031696.def: A viral infection that fails to be contained by the immune sytem and spreads throughout the body.

name: disseminated infection with live vaccine virus
disseminate infection with live vaccine virus
HP:0031697.def: A dissemination viral infection caused by a live attenuated vaccine virus.

name: obsolete disseminated bacillus calmette - guerin infection
obsolete disseminate bacillus calmette - guerin infection
HP:0031698.def: Failure to contain thebacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination leading to spread of BCG to many sites in the body. The tuberculosis vaccine BCG contains live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis.

name: disseminated cryptosporidium infection
disseminated cryptosporidium infection
HP:0031699.def: Failure to contain infection by a protozoan of the genus Cryptosporidium, leading to spread to many parts of the body.

name: invasive parasitic infection
invasive parasitic infection
HP:0031700.def: A parasitic infection whereby the parasite invades (migrates through) tissues of the infected host.

name: anterior chamber inflammatory cells
anterior chamber inflammatory cell
HP:0031701.def: The presence of inflammatory cells in the aqueous humor of the anterior chamber of the eye.

name: anterior chamber red blood cells
anterior chamber red blood cell
HP:0031702.def: The presence of erythrocyte in the aqueous humor of the anterior chamber of the eye.

name: abnormal ear morphology
abnormal ear morphology
HP:0031703.def: Any structural anomaly of the ear.

name: abnormal ear physiology
abnormal ear physiology
HP:0031704.def: Any functional anomaly of the ear.

name: compensatory head posture
compensatory head posture
HP:0031705.def: A compensatory head posture occurs when the head is deviated out of the normal primary straight head position in order to compensate for an ocular problem.

name: compensatory chin depression
compensatory chin depression
HP:0031706.def: A tendency to hold the chin depressed (lowered) to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

name: compensatory face turn to the right
compensatory face turn to the right
HP:0031707.def: A tendency to turn the face to the right to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

name: compensatory face turn to the left
compensatory face turn to the left
HP:0031708.def: A tendency to turn the face to the left to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

name: compensatory head tilt to the right shoulder
compensatory head tilt to the right shoulder
HP:0031709.def: A tendency to tilt the head towards the right shoulder to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

name: compensatory head tilt to the left shoulder
compensatory head tilt to the left shoulder
HP:0031710.def: A tendency to tilt the head towards the left shoulder to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

name: asymmetric abdominal aortic aneurysm
asymmetric abdominal aortic aneurysm
HP:0031711.def: An abdominal aortic aneurysm that is not symmetric around its axis (not axisymmetric).

name: constant exotropia
constant exotropia
HP:0031713.def: A form of divergent strabismus (exotropia) in which the eye turns outward at all distances and at all times.

name: distance exotropia
distance exotropia
HP:0031714.def: A type of divergent strabismus (exotropia) in which an eye tends to turn outwards (i.e., the eye squints) mainly when looking at distant objects. The eyes tend to remain straight when they look at near objects. Distance exotropia may be constant or intermittent.

name: near exotropia
near exotropia
HP:0031715.def: An intermittent exotropia where there is binocular single vision on distance fixation and exotropia at near (intermittent or constant).

name: cyclic exotropia
cyclic exotropia
HP:0031716.def: A type of exotropia (divergent strabismus) in which binocular single vision alternates with large angle exotropia in rhythmic cycle.

name: alternating exotropia
alternate exotropia
HP:0031717.def: A type of exotropia in which either eye may be used for fixation.

name: consecutive exotropia
consecutive exotropia
HP:0031718.def: Exotropia in an individual who has previously had esotropia or esophoria.

name: true distance exotropia
true distance exotropia
HP:0031719.def: Exotropia (intermittent or constant) on distance fixation with binocular single vision on near fixation under all testing conditions. The accommodative convergence/accommodation (AC:A) ratio is within normal limits.

name: simulated distance exotropia
simulated distance exotropia
HP:0031720.def: Exotropia (intermittent or constant) worse for distance fixation in which the near angle of deviation increases (or near exophoria becomes exotropia) with: (1) prolonged disruption of fusion and/or (2) elimination of accommodation.

name: sensory exotropia
sensory exotropia
HP:0031721.def: A type of divergent strabismus (exotropia) that develops in a poorly seeing eye.

name: near esotropia
near esotropia
HP:0031722.def: An intermittent esotropia where there is binocular single vision on distance fixation and esotropia at near even when the accommodation is relieved.

name: secondary esotropia
secondary esotropia
HP:0031723.def: Convergent squint which follows loss or impairment of vision.

name: microtropia
microtropia
HP:0031724.def: A small angle heterotropia (usually of 10 diopters or less) in which a form of binocular single vision occurs.

name: hypophoria
hypophoria
HP:0031725.def: A form of latent strabismus (heterophoria) in which, on dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards.

name: incyclotropia
incyclotropia
HP:0031726.def: A type of cyclotropia (torsion of one or both eye around the visual axis of the eyes) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated inward (medially) to each other.

name: excyclotropia
excyclotropia
HP:0031727.def: A type of cyclotropia (torsion of one or both eye around the visual axis of the eyes) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated outward (laterally) to each other.

name: mild hypermetropia
mild hypermetropia
HP:0031728.def: A form of hypermetropia with not more than +2.00 diopters.

name: moderate hypermetropia
moderate hypermetropia
HP:0031729.def: A form of hypermetropia with more than +2.00 diopters but not more than +5.00 diopters.

name: axial myopia
axial myopia
HP:0031730.def: A form of myopia related to an axial length above the norm and too long for the refractive power of the whole optical system of the eye.

name: increased tear production
increase tear production
HP:0031731.def: Increased lacrimation owing to overproduction of tears.

name: increased basal tear production
increase basal tear production
HP:0031732.def: A form of watery eye associated with overproduction of tears due to an increased parasympathetic drive to the secretory component of the lacrimal system (lacrimal gland); this could be due to pro-secretory drug use (e.g. pilocarpine) or autonomic disturbance.

name: reflex tearing
reflex tear
HP:0031733.def: A form of watery eye associated with overproduction of tears due to reflex tearing in response to a local irritant (e.g. trichiasis or foreign body), chronic ocular surface disease (e.g. blepharitis) or systemic disease (e.g. thyroid eye disease).

name: lacrimal pump failure
lacrimal pump failure
HP:0031734.def: A form of watery eye associated with abnormal lid tone and/or lid position. The former is due to lid laxity (common involutional change in the elderly) or a weak orbicularis muscle (e.g. due to VII cranial nerve palsy). The latter is typically associated with ectropion causing punctal eversion.

name: involutional entropion
involutional entropion
HP:0031736.def: An abnormal inversion of the eyelid towards the globe resulting from inferior retractor muscle dysfunction with tissue laxity and, possibly, overriding of the preseptal orbicularis muscle over the pretarsal orbicularis muscle.

name: cicatricial entropion
cicatricial entropion
HP:0031737.def: Abnormal inversion (turning inward) of the eyelid towards the globe associated with scarring that vertically shortens the posterior lamella of the eyelid.

name: mechanical entropion
mechanical entropion
HP:0031738.def: A type of entropion (abnormal inversion of the eyelid towards the globe) that is related to a mass effect of a lesion (e.g., a tumor) that pulls the eyelid margin away from the globe.

name: abnormal oblique muscle physiology
abnormal oblique muscle physiology
HP:0031739.def: A functional anomaly of the inferior or superior oblique muscle.

name: abnormal horizontal rectus muscle physiology
abnormal horizontal rectus muscle physiology
HP:0031740.def: A functional anomaly of the medial rectus muscle or lateral rectus muscle.

name: inferior oblique muscle underaction
inferior oblique muscle underaction
HP:0031741.def: Reduced ocular movement by the inferior oblique muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

name: inferior rectus muscle underaction
inferior rectus muscle underaction
HP:0031742.def: Reduced movement by the inferior rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

name: inferior rectus muscle overaction
inferior rectus muscle overaction
HP:0031743.def: Excessive action of the inferior rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

name: superior rectus muscle weakness
superior rectus muscle weakness
HP:0031744.def: Decreased strength of the superior rectus muscle.

name: superior rectus muscle overaction
superior rectus muscle overaction
HP:0031745.def: Excessive action of the superior rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

name: superior rectus muscle restriction
superior rectus muscle restriction
HP:0031746.def: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the superior rectus muscle.

name: superior rectus muscle underaction
superior rectus muscle underaction
HP:0031747.def: Reduced movement of the superior rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

name: abnormal vertical rectus muscle physiology
abnormal vertical rectus muscle physiology
HP:0031748.def: A functional anomaly of the superior or inferior rectus muscle.

name: abnormal lateral rectus muscle physiology
abnormal lateral rectus muscle physiology
HP:0031749.def: A functional anomaly of the lateral rectus muscle.

name: lateral rectus muscle weakness
lateral rectus muscle weakness
HP:0031750.def: Decreased strength (ability to move) of the lateral rectus muscle.

name: lateral rectus muscle underaction
lateral rectus muscle underaction
HP:0031751.def: Reduced movement of the lateral rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

name: lateral rectus muscle overaction
lateral rectus muscle overaction
HP:0031752.def: Excessive action of the lateral rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

name: medial rectus muscle weakness
medial rectus muscle weakness
HP:0031753.def: Decreased strength of the medial rectus muscle.

name: medial rectus muscle overaction
medial rectus muscle overaction
HP:0031754.def: Excessive action of the medial rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

name: abnormal rectus muscle physiology
abnormal rectus muscle physiology
HP:0031755.def: A functional anomaly of a vertical or horizontal rectus muscle.

name: medial rectus muscle underaction
medial rectus muscle underaction
HP:0031756.def: Reduced movement of the medial rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

name: medial rectus muscle restriction
medial rectus muscle restriction
HP:0031757.def: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the medial rectus muscle.

name: lateral rectus muscle restriction
lateral rectus muscle restriction
HP:0031758.def: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the lateral rectus muscle.

name: basic constant esotropia
basic constant esotropia
HP:0031759.def: A form of convergent strabismus (esotropia) in which the deviation is present under all conditions (ie at all distances and at all times).

name: non - accomodative esotropia
non - accomodative esotropia
HP:0031760.def: A form of esotropia in which the angle of deviation is not affected by accommodative effort.

name: infantile constant esotropia
infantile constant esotropia
HP:0031761.def: Constant esotropia occurring before 6 months of age. It is typically associated with a large angle of deviation, alternating fixation (therefore low risk of amblyopia) and poor potential for binocular single vision. Other features that might be present in individuals with infantile (constant) esotropia include latent nystagmus or manifest latent nystagmus, dissociated vertical divergence, cyclotropia, abnormal head posture, limited abduction.

name: distance esotropia
distance esotropia
HP:0031762.def: An intermittent esotropia where binocular single vision is present on near fixation and an esotropia on distance fixation. Often associated with myopia and aging.

name: cyclic esotropia
cyclic esotropia
HP:0031763.def: Convergent strabismus in which normal binocular single vision is alternating with large angle esotropia in rhythmic cycle.

name: fully accomodative esotropia
fully accomodative esotropia
HP:0031764.def: Esotropia in which normal binocular single vision is present for all distances when the hypermetropic refractive error is corrected. Esotropia is present for near and distance on accommodation without correction.

name: partially accomodative esotropia
partially accomodative esotropia
HP:0031765.def: A form of constant esotropia in which the angle of deviation is partially affected by accommodative effort. Typically there is esotropia at near and distance with hypermetropic correction and the angle of deviation increases without glasses.
synonym: constant esotropia with an accommodative component
constant esotropia with an accommodative component
constant esotropia with an accommodative element
constant esotropia with an accommodative element

name: convergence excess esotropia
convergence excess esotropia
HP:0031766.def: An intermittent esotropia with binocular single vision present at distance fixation but esotropia on accommodation for near fixation. Usually associated with hypermetropia but patients can be emmetropic and rarely myopic. Associated with a high accommodative convergence/accommodation (AC/A) ratio.

name: consecutive esotropia
consecutive esotropia
HP:0031767.def: Esotropia in a patient who has previously had exotropia or exophoria; may be constant or intermittent and usually follows surgical overcorrection.

name: parafoveal fixation
parafoveal fixation
HP:0031768.def: Fixation of an object in the area adjacent to the fovea.

name: peripheral fixation
peripheral fixation
HP:0031769.def: Fixation of an object in a peripheral area of the retina.

name: epicanthus palpebralis
epicanthus palpebralis
HP:0031770.def: A type of epicanthus in which a medial vertical fold is present between upper and lower lids.

name: epicanthus tarsalis
epicanthus tarsalis
HP:0031771.def: A type of epicanthus in which a primarily upper lid fold is present.

name: abnormal posterior circulating artery morphology
abnormal posterior circulate artery morphology
HP:0031772.def: Any structural anomaly of the posterior circulating artery (PCOM).

name: posterior communicating artery aneurysm
posterior communicate artery aneurysm
HP:0031773.def: A widening (ballooning) localized in the wall of the posterior communicating artery.

name: posterior communicating artery infundibulum
posterior communicate artery infundibulum
HP:0031774.def: A funnel-shaped symmetrical enlargement of the origin of the posterior communicating artery at its junction with the internal carotid artery.

name: neurogenic strabismus
neurogenic strabismus
HP:0031775.def: An ocular deviation caused by a palsy to one or more of the extraocular muscles or nerves supplying them.

name: cyclotropia
cyclotropia
HP:0031776.def: A form of manifest strabismus (heterotropia) in which the one eye is wheel rotated so that the upper end of its vertical axis is nasal (incyclotropia) or temporal (excyclotropia).

name: cyclophoria
cyclophoria
HP:0031777.def: A form of latent strabismus (heterophoria) in which the occluded eye wheel-rotates on dissociation.

name: incyclophoria
incyclophoria
HP:0031778.def: A type of cyclophoria (latent strabismus in which the occluded eye wheel-rotates on dissociation.) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated inward (medially) to each other.

name: excyclophoria
excyclophoria
HP:0031779.def: A type of cyclophoria (latent strabismus in which the occluded eye wheel-rotates on dissociation.) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated outward (laterally) to each other.

name: eosinophilic ascites
eosinophilic ascites
HP:0031780.def: A type of ascites in which there are large numbers of eosinophils in the ascitis fluid.

name: microtropia with identity
microtropia with identity
HP:0031781.def: A type of microtropia with no manifest movement on cover test, the eccentric fixation point coinciding with the angle of ARC.

name: microtropia without identity
microtropia without identity
HP:0031782.def: A type of microtropia in which the manifest movement is demonstrated on the cover-uncover test.

name: absent coronary sinus
absent coronary sinus
HP:0031783.def: A developmental defect in which the coronary sinus fails to form.

name: abnormal ascending aorta morphology
abnormal ascend aorta morphology
HP:0031784.def: Any structural anomaly of the portion of the aorta that arises from the base of the left ventricle and extends upward to the aortic arch and from which the coronary arteries arise.

name: abnormal eyelid movement
abnormal eyelid movement
HP:0031785.def: An abnormality in voluntary or involuntary eyelid movements or their control.

name: cogan lid twitch
cogan lid twitch
HP:0031786.def: Transient eyelid retraction during refixation from down to straight ahead.

name: oblique astigmatism
oblique astigmatism
HP:0031787.def: Astigmatism in which the refractive power of the vertical meridian is the greatest.

name: with the rule astigmatism
with the rule astigmatism
HP:0031788.def: Refractive error in which the vertical meridian is relatively hypermetropic and the horizontal meridian is relatively myopic (or ocular astigmatism in which the refractive power of the horizontal meridian is the greatest).

name: against the rule astigmatism
against the rule astigmatism
HP:0031789.def: Astigmatism with more plus power on the horizontal meridian.

name: mixed astigmatism
mixed astigmatism
HP:0031790.def: A type of astigmatism in which an unequal curvature of the cornea and some cases additionally of the lens causes one meridian of the eye to be hyperopic (farsighted) and a second meridian that is perpendicular to the first to be myopic (nearsighted).

name: lenticular astigmatism
lenticular astigmatism
HP:0031791.def: A type of astigmatism related to an irregular shape of the lens.

name: irregular astigmatism
irregular astigmatism
HP:0031792.def: A type of astigmatism in which the principle meridians are not 90 degrees apart and which is associated with loss of vision.

name: increased serum leptin
increase serum leptin
HP:0031793.def: An increased concentration of leptin in the blood.

name: decreased circulating glycerol level
decrease circulate glycerol level
HP:0031794.def: A decrease below the normal concentration of glycerol in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating glycerol level
abnormal circulate glycerol level
HP:0031795.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glycerol in the blood.

name: recurrent
recurrent
HP:0031796.def: Applies to a sign, symptom or manifestation that occurs multiple times separated by intervals in which the sign, symptom, or manifestation is not present.

name: clinical course
clinical course
HP:0031797.def: The course a disease typically takes from its onset, progression in time, and eventual resolution or death of the affected individual.

name: elevated circulating apolipoprotein b concentration
elevate circulate apolipoprotein b concentration
HP:0031798.def: Increased circulating level of apolipoprotein B, which is the main apolipoprotein of chylomicrons and low density lipoproteins. It occurs in plasma as two main isoforms, apoB-48 and apoB-100.

name: decreased circulating apolipoprotein a - i concentration
decrease circulate apolipoprotein a - i concentration
HP:0031799.def: Concentration of apolipoprotein A-I below the lower limit of normal. Apolipoprotein A-I is the major protein component of high density lipoprotein (HDL) in plasma. Defects in this gene are associated with HDL deficiencies, including Tangier disease.

name: elevated circulating apolipoprotein a - ii concentration
elevate circulate apolipoprotein a - ii concentration
HP:0031800.def: An increased concentration in blood of apolipoprotein A-II, a major component of HDL particles, associated with triglyceride and glucose metabolism.

name: vocal cord dysfunction
vocal cord dysfunction
HP:0031801.def: Any functional anomaly of the vocal cord.

name: fundus hemorrhage
fundus hemorrhage
HP:0031803.def: Bleeding within the fundus of the eye.

name: intraretinal hemorrhage
intraretinal hemorrhage
HP:0031805.def: A subtype of fundus hemorrhage occurring within the neurosensory retina. Intraretinal haemorrhages may be 'dot' or' blot' shaped or flame shaped depending upon their depth within the retina.

name: abnormal basophil count
abnormal basophil count
HP:0031806.def: Any deviation from the normal number of basophils per volume in the blood circulation.

name: increased basophil count
increase basophil count
HP:0031807.def: An abnormally increased count of basophils per volume in the blood circulation.

name: decreased basophil count
decrease basophil count
HP:0031808.def: An abnormally reduced count of basophils per volume in the blood circulation.

name: archibald 's sign
archibald 's sign
HP:0031809.def: Shortening of the fourth and fifth metacarpals when the fist is clenched.

name: anti - ganglioside antibody positivity
anti - ganglioside antibody positivity
HP:0031810.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react to gangliosides.

name: bilirubinuria
bilirubinuria
HP:0031811.def: Presence of conjugated bilirubin in the urine.

name: nitrituria
nitrituria
HP:0031812.def: Presence of nitrites in the urine.

name: colonic eosinophilia
colonic eosinophilia
HP:0031813.def: An excess of eosinophilic cells in colonic tissue, i.e., eosinophilic infiltration in the colon.

name: palilalia
palilalia
HP:0031814.def: Repetition of one's own words or phrases is a common occurrence.

name: abnormal oral physiology
abnormal oral physiology
HP:0031815.def: A functional anomaly of the mouth (which is also known as the oral cavity).

name: abnormal oral morphology
abnormal oral morphology
HP:0031816.def: Any structural anomaly of the mouth, which is also known as the oral cavity.

name: decreased circulating parathyroid hormone level
decrease circulate parathyroid hormone level
HP:0031817.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of parathyroid hormone.

name: abnormal waist to hip ratio
abnormal waist to hip ratio
HP:0031818.def: A deviation from normal of the waist to hip ratio, defined as the waist measurement divided by hip measurement.

name: increased waist to hip ratio
increase waist to hip ratio
HP:0031819.def: Increased waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) is a measurement above the average for the dimensionless ratio of the circumference of the waist to that of the hips. WHR is calculated as waist measurement divided by hip measurement.

name: decreased waist to hip ratio
decrease waist to hip ratio
HP:0031820.def: Decreased waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) is a measurement below the average for the dimensionless ratio of the circumference of the waist to that of the hips. WHR is calculated as waist measurement divided by hip measurement.

name: abnormal hypoxanthine - guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
abnormal hypoxanthine - guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
HP:0031821.def: Altered level of the enzyme that catalyzes conversion of hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate and guanine to guanosine monophosphate via transfer of the 5-phosphoribosyl group from 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate.

name: elevated hypoxanthine - guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
elevate hypoxanthine - guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
HP:0031822.def: Abnormally increased level of the enzyme that catalyzes conversion of hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate and guanine to guanosine monophosphate via transfer of the 5-phosphoribosyl group from 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate.

name: reduced hypoxanthine - guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
reduce hypoxanthine - guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
HP:0031823.def: Abnormally decreased level of the enzyme that catalyzes conversion of hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate and guanine to guanosine monophosphate via transfer of the 5-phosphoribosyl group from 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate.

name: freezing of gait
freezing of gait
HP:0031825.def: Freezing of gait is defined as a brief, episodic absence or marked reduction of forward progression of the feet despite the intention to walk.

name: abnormal reflex
abnormal reflex
HP:0031826.def: Any anomaly of a reflex, i.e., of an automatic response mediated by the nervous system (a reflex does not need the intervention of conscious thought to occur).

name: absent abdominal reflex
absent abdominal reflex
HP:0031827.def: Lack of contraction of abdominal muscles in the quadrant of the abdomen that is stimulated by scraping the skin tangential to or toward the umbilicus.

name: abnormal superficial reflex
abnormal superficial reflex
HP:0031828.def: An anomaly of a reflex that is elicited as a motor response to scraping of the skin. They are generally graded as present or absent. They differ from tendon reflexes in that the sensory signal must ascend the spinal cord to reach the brain and then descend the spinal cord to reach the motor neurons.

name: absent cremaster reflex
absent cremaster reflex
HP:0031829.def: Lack of response to scratching of the skin of the medial thigh, which in males normally elicits a brisk, short elevation of the ipsilateral testis, a phenomenon that is referred to as the cremaster reflex.

name: pinguecula
pinguecula
HP:0031830.def: A pinguecula is a yellowish to brown protruding lesion in the conjunctiva that is easily seen on the nasal and temporal sides of the cornea.

name: decreased serum zinc
decrease serum zinc
HP:0031831.def: A reduced concentration of zinc in the blood.

name: hypermetric downward saccades
hypermetric downward saccade
HP:0031832.def: Overshoot of downward saccadic eye movements.

name: hypometric upward saccades
hypometric upward saccade
HP:0031833.def: Saccadic undershoot of upward saccadic eye movements, i.e., an upward saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

name: aortopulmonary collateral arteries
aortopulmonary collateral artery
HP:0031834.def: Small ectopic arteries or arterial branches that connect the aorta, aortic branches and/or subclavian artery regions directly to the lung parenchyma, usually seen in conjunction with pulmonary atresia, ventricular septal defect (VSD) and/or closed ductus arteriosus.

name: abnormal superoxide dismutase level
abnormal superoxide dismutase level
HP:0031835.def: An abnormal level of catalysis of the reaction: 2 superoxide + 2 H+ = O2 + hydrogen peroxide.

name: increased superoxide dismutase level
increase superoxide dismutase level
HP:0031836.def: Increased level of catalysis of the reaction: 2 superoxide + 2 H+ = O2 + hydrogen peroxide.

name: decreased superoxide dismutase level
decrease superoxide dismutase level
HP:0031837.def: Decreased level of catalysis of the reaction: 2 superoxide + 2 H+ = O2 + hydrogen peroxide.

name: presence of xenobiotic
presence of xenobiotic
HP:0031838.def: Presence of a chemical substance found within an individual that is not naturally produced or expected to be present in human tissues or bodily fluids.

name: urine xenobiotic
urine xenobiotic
HP:0031840.def: The presence of a xenobiotic in urine.

name: positive urine methadone test
positive urine methadone test
HP:0031841.def: Detection of methadone or its metabolite 2-ethylidene-1,5-dimethyl-3,3- diphenylpyrrolidine (EDDP) in urine.

name: lymphangiectasis
lymphangiectasis
HP:0031842.def: Dilation of the lymphatic vessels, the basic process that may result in the formation of a lymphangioma.

name: euphoria
euphoria
HP:0031844.def: Euphoria is a feeling of intense joy, happiness, excitement, or elation that surpasses what would typically be anticipated in a given situation.

name: abnormal libido
abnormal libido
HP:0031845.def: Any deviation from the normal sexual drive or desire for sexual activity.

name: femur fracture
femur fracture
HP:0031846.def: A break or crush injury of the thigh bone (femur).

name: difficulty walking backward
difficulty walk backward
HP:0031847.def: Reduced ability to walk (ambulate) in a backwards direction.

name: cock - walk gait
cock - walk gait
HP:0031848.def: An abnormality of gait that can be observed in individuals with dystonic posture in which the individual walks with an extended trunk and flexed arms, while strutting on the toes without the heels touching the floor.

name: sleep - wake inversion
sleep - wake inversion
HP:0031849.def: A reversal of sleeping habits, with a tendency to sleep during the day and be awake at night.

name: abnormal hematocrit
abnormal hematocrit
HP:0031850.def: Any deviation from the normal ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

name: reduced hematocrit
reduce hematocrit
HP:0031851.def: A reduction below the normal ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

name: isomerism
isomerism
HP:0031853.def: Isomerism in the context of the congenitally malformed heart is defined as a situation where some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are, in morphologic terms, symmetrical mirror images of each other.

name: left isomerism
leave isomerism
HP:0031854.def: A type of heterotaxy where some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are symmetrical mirror images of each other, and have the morphology of the normal left-sided structures.

name: right isomerism
right isomerism
HP:0031855.def: A type of heterotaxy where some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are symmetrical mirror images of each other, and have the morphology of the normal right-sided structures.

name: hobby horse gait
hobby horse gait
HP:0031856.def: An abnormal gait characterized by toe walking, stiff legs, and skipping. The gait pattern has some resemblance to cock-walk gait, but affected individuals are able to improve their dystonic gait by walking backward.

name: ineffective esophageal peristalsis
ineffective esophageal peristalsis
HP:0031857.def: Reduced or inadequate esophageal peristalsis, with resultant slow passage of contents through the esophagus.

name: esophageal furrows
esophageal furrow
HP:0031858.def: Longitudinal grooves in the surface of the esophagus arranged in a longitudinal fashion (from top to bottom of the esophagus).

name: abnormal heart rate variability
abnormal heart rate variability
HP:0031860.def: Any abnormality in the variability of the time interval between successive heartbeats.

name: decreased heart rate variability
decreased heart rate variability
HP:0031861.def: Reduced variation of beat-to-beat intervals of the heart that occurs in conjunction with the respiratory cycle.

name: increased heart rate variability
increase heart rate variability
HP:0031862.def: Increased variation of beat-to-beat intervals of the heart that occurs in conjunction with the respiratory cycle.

name: bloodstream infectious agent
bloodstream infectious agent
HP:0031863.def: The presence of an infectious agent in the blood circulation.

name: bacteremia
bacteremia
HP:0031864.def: Presence of viable bacteria in the blood.

name: abnormal liver physiology
abnormal liver physiology
HP:0031865.def: Any functional anomaly of the liver.

name: clasp - knife sign
clasp - knife sign
HP:0031866.def: Clasp-knife phenomonen refers to increased muscle tone while bending or stretching a limb, whereby there is a sudden relaxation (decrease in resistance) as the muscle continues to be streched. This phenomenon has been likened to opening a clasp knife.

name: neck hypertonia
neck hypertonia
HP:0031867.def: Increased passive stiffness or tightness of the neck musculature.

name: optic ataxia
optic ataxia
HP:0031868.def: Difficulty reaching visually guided goals in peripheral vision, with the deficit, leaves voluntary eye movements largely unaffected.

name: recurrent joint dislocation
recurrent joint dislocation
HP:0031869.def: Dislocation of a given joint repeated times.

name: phosphohydroxylysinuria
phosphohydroxylysinuria
HP:0031870.def: An elevated concentration of phosphohydroxylysine in the urine.

name: abnormal langerhans cell morphology
abnormal langerhans cell morphology
HP:0031871.def: Any functional anomaly of Langerhans cells, which are dendritic cells in the epidermis and some other locations. Langerhans cells play roles in immune surveillance and homeostasis.

name: absent birbeck granules in langerhans cells
absent birbeck granule in langerhans cell
HP:0031872.def: Birbeck granules (BG) are cytoplasmic organelles that are only found in Langerhans cells (LC). The function of BG is still not completely understood, although most studies point toward an active role in receptor-mediated endocytosis and participation in the antigen-processing/presenting function of LC. This feature refers to the absence of BG in LC, a feature that can be documented by means of electron microscopy.

name: early chronotype
early chronotype
HP:0031873.def: A tendency towards rising very early in the morning and going to bed early in the evening.

name: late chronotype
late chronotype
HP:0031874.def: A tendency towards waking up very late in the morning and staying up late at night.

name: abnormal circulating hepcidin concentration
abnormal circulate hepcidin concentration
HP:0031875.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating hepcidin concentration
decrease circulate hepcidin concentration
HP:0031876.def: Concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating hepcidin concentration
elevate circulate hepcidin concentration
HP:0031877.def: Concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: acromicria
acromicria
HP:0031878.def: Small hands and feet in proportion to the rest of the body.

name: abnormal eyelid physiology
abnormal eyelid physiology
HP:0031879.def: Any functional abnormality of the eyelid.

name: eyelid laxity
eyelid laxity
HP:0031880.def: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation; it can be demonstrated by the eyelid distraction test and/or the eyelid snap test.

name: decreased tear drainage
decrease tear drainage
HP:0031881.def: A form of watery eye associated with obstruction of the nasolacrimal system. This may arise at the level of the punctum, the canaliculi, the sac or the nasolacrimal duct.

name: agyria
agyria
HP:0031882.def: A congenital abnormality of the cerebral hemisphere characterized by lack of gyrations (convolutions) of the cerebral cortex. Agyria is defined as cortical regions lacking gyration with sulci great than 3 cm apart and cerebral cortex thicker than 5 mm.

name: increased proinsulin : insulin ratio
increase proinsulin : insulin ratio
HP:0031883.def: An elevated concentration of proinsulin (the prohormone precursor to insulin) to mature insulin in the circulation.

name: abnormal csf glucose concentration
abnormal csf glucose concentration
HP:0031884.def: A deviation from normal concentration of glucose content in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: hyperglycorrhachia
hyperglycorrhachia
HP:0031885.def: Abnormally high glucose concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: abnormal ldl cholesterol concentration
abnormal ldl cholesterol concentration
HP:0031886.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal chylomicron concentration
abnormal chylomicron concentration
HP:0031887.def: Any deviation from the normal circulating concentration of chylomicrons.

name: abnormal hdl cholesterol concentration
abnormal hdl cholesterol concentration
HP:0031888.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL) in the blood.

name: abnormal vldl cholesterol concentration
abnormal vldl cholesterol concentration
HP:0031889.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.

name: increased urine urobilinogen
increase urine urobilinogen
HP:0031890.def: An elevated concentration of urobilinogen in the urine.

name: decreased eosinophil count
decrease eosinophil count
HP:0031891.def: Abnormal reduction in the count of eosinophils in the blood per volume.

name: rouleaux formation
rouleau formation
HP:0031898.def: Increased amount of stacking of erythrocytes into long chains. Rouleaux (singular: rouleau) is derived from a French word that can refer to a stack of coins put into a cylindircal paper roll. Rouleaux formation is observed with increased serum proteins, particularly fibrinogen and globulins, and represents the cause of increased erythrocte sedimentation rate because rouleaux sediment more readily than isolated red blood cells.

name: abnormal coagulation factor v activity
abnormal coagulation factor v activity
HP:0031899.def: Any deviation from the activity of coagulation factor V.

name: elevated total serum tryptase
elevate total serum tryptase
HP:0031901.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of total tryptase (alpha and beta tryptase) in the blood circulation.

name: obsolete decreased serum mast cell beta - tryptase concentration
obsolete decrease serum mast cell beta - tryptase concentration
abnormal circulating selenium concentration
abnormal circulate selenium concentration
HP:0031903.def: Any deviation from the normal circulating concentration of selenium.

name: abnormal total hemolytic complement activity
abnormal total hemolytic complement activity
HP:0031904.def: Any deviation from the normal total hemolytic complement activity in the circulation.

name: increased total hemolytic complement activity
increase total hemolytic complement activity
HP:0031905.def: An abnormally elevated total hemolytic complement activity in the circulation.

name: decreased total hemolytic complement activity
decrease total hemolytic complement activity
HP:0031906.def: An abnormally reduced total hemolytic complement activity in the circulation.

name: anti - mitochondrial m2 antibody positivity
anti - mitochondrial m2 antibody positivity
HP:0031907.def: The presence of M2 anti-mitochondrial antibody (immunoglobulins) in the serum.

name: micrographia
micrographia
HP:0031908.def: Abnormally small-sized handwriting is formally defined as an impairment of fine motor skills, which mainly manifests as a progressive or stable reduction in amplitude during a writing task.

name: unicornuate uterus
unicornuate uterus
HP:0031909.def: A uterus that has a single horn, with a banana-like shape that may or may not have a secondary rudimentary uterine horn.

name: abnormal cranial nerve physiology
abnormal cranial nerve physiology
HP:0031910.def: A functional abnormality affecting one or more of the cranial nerves, which emerge directly from the brain stem.

name: trigeminal anesthesia
trigeminal anesthesia
HP:0031912.def: Decreased or absent sensation in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, which provides tactile, proprioceptive, and nociceptive sensation in the area of the face and mouth.

name: rhombencephalosynapsis
rhombencephalosynapsis
HP:0031913.def: Rhombencephalosynapsis is a rare brain malformation defined by midline fusion of the cerebellar hemispheres with partial or complete loss of the intervening vermis.

name: fluctuating
fluctuate
HP:0031914.def: Varying irregularly over time in severity, amount, or amplitude.

name: stable
stable
HP:0031915.def: This modifier can be applied to a phenotypic feature that does not vary in severity or amount over time.

name: digital ulcer
digital ulcer
HP:0031917.def: An open sore on the surface of the skin of a finger or toe.

name: ovarian sex cord - stromal tumor
ovarian sex cord - stromal tumor
HP:0031918.def: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is composed of granulosa cells, Sertoli cells, Leydig cells, theca cells, and fibroblasts.

name: juvenile type ovarian granulosa cell tumor
juvenile type ovarian granulosa cell tumor
HP:0031919.def: Juvenile granulosa cell ovarian tumor (JGCOT) is a rare sex cord stromal tumor, occuring most frequently in premenarchal girls or young women. In contrast to adult granulosa cell tumor, JGCOT has a high mitotic index and more aggressive tumor growth. Microscopically it is seen as diffuse and regularly distributed neoplastic cells with a wide cytoplasm and pleomorphic hyperchromatic nucleus. Follicle formation, in various sizes and shapes, is important in JGCOT. Call-Exner bodies are infrequently seen in JGCOT in contrast to the adult type.
synonym: juvenile type ovarian granulosa cell tumour
juvenile type ovarian granulosa cell tumour

name: malignant ovarian granulosa cell tumor
malignant ovarian granulosa cell tumor
HP:0031920.def: An aggressive granulosa cell tumor that arises from the ovary.

name: renal artery duplication
renal artery duplication
HP:0031922.def: The renal arteries carry blood from the aorta to the kidney; normally one renal artery is present on each side of the body. Renal artery duplication refers to the presence of two rather than one renal artery on a given side of the body.

name: hematocolpos
hematocolpos
HP:0031923.def: Accumulation of blood in the vagina usually due to vaginal obstruction.

name: rope sign
rope sign
HP:0031924.def: The presence of linear erythematous palpable cords, often on the lateral trunk.

name: rosette
rosette
HP:0031925.def: A halo or spoke-wheel arrangement of cells surrounding a central core or hub. The central hub may consist of an empty-appearing lumen or a space filled with cytoplasmic processes. The cytoplasm of each of the cells in the rosette is often wedge-shaped with the apex directed toward the central core; the nuclei of the cells participating in the rosette are peripherally positioned and form a ring or halo around the hub.

name: homer wright rosette
homer wright rosette
HP:0031926.def: A type of rosette in which the central lumen or hub is filled with fiber-like processes.

name: flexner - wintersteiner rosette
flexner - wintersteiner rosette
HP:0031927.def: The tumor cells that form the Flexner-Wintersteiner rosette circumscribe a central lumen that contains small cytoplasmic extensions of the encircling cells; however, unlike the center of the Homer Wright rosette, the central lumen does not contain the fiber-rich neuropil.

name: true ependymal rosette
true ependymal rosette
HP:0031928.def: A type of rosette in which a halo of cells surrounds an empty lumen.

name: perivascular pseudorosette
perivascular pseudorosette
HP:0031929.def: A type of rosette in which a spoke-wheel arrangement of cells with tapered cellular processes radiates around a wall of a centrally placed vessel.

name: neurocytic rosette
neurocytic rosette
HP:0031930.def: A type of rosette that is similar to the Homer Wright rosette, but the central fiber-rich neuropil island is larger and more irregular.

name: ocular flutter
ocular flutter
HP:0031931.def: Ocular flutter is an abnormal eye movement consisting of repetitive, irregular, involuntary bursts of horizontal saccades without an intersaccadic interval. It is generally superimposed on normal oculomotor behaviour and its occurrence may be favoured by various events, such as blinks, the triggering of normal saccades or optokinetic stimulation.

name: aorto - left ventricular tunnel
aorto - leave ventricular tunnel
HP:0031932.def: Aorto-left ventricular tunnel (ALVT) is a congenital extracardiac channel connecting the ascending aorta above the sino-tubular junction to either left or right ventricular cavity.

name: aorto - right ventricular tunnel
aorto - right ventricular tunnel
HP:0031933.def: The presence of an extracardiac channel that connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the right ventricle.

name: abnormal descending aorta morphology
abnormal descend aorta morphology
HP:0031934.def: A structural abnormality of the part of the aorta that begins at the aortic arch and then descends through the chest and abdomen.

name: ascending aorta hypoplasia
ascend aorta hypoplasia
HP:0031935.def: Significant luminal narrowing of a long segment of or the entire ascending aorta.

name: delayed ability to walk
delay ability to walk
HP:0031936.def: A failure to achieve the ability to walk at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children learn to walk in a series of stages, and learn to walk short distances independently between 12 and 15 months.

name: abnormal conus terminalis morphology
abnormal conus terminalis morphology
HP:0031938.def: Any structural anomaly of the conus terminalis, which is the distal bulbous part of the spinal cord at the location where the spinal cord tapers and ends (usually between the L1 and L2 lumbar vertebrae).

name: abnormal portal venous system morphology
abnormal portal venous system morphology
HP:0031941.def: Any structural anomaly of the portal venous sytem, which comprises all of the veins draining the abdominal part of the digestive tract, including the lower esophagus but excluding the lower anal canal. The portal vein conveys blood from viscera and ramifies like an artery at the liver, ending at the sinusoids. Tributaries of the portal vein, which make up the portal venous system, are the splenic, superior mesenteric, left gastric, right gastric, paraumbilical, and cystic veins.

name: congenital absence of portal vein
congenital absence of portal vein
HP:0031942.def: Anomaly where the intestinal and the splenic venous drainage bypass the liver and drain into systemic veins through other possible venous shunts.

name: akathisia
akathisia
HP:0031943.def: A state of motor restlessness, usually in the lower extremities, that is often but not always accompanied by a subjective sense of inner restlessness, an urge to move, and anxiety or dysphoria.

name: pleural thickening
pleural thickening
HP:0031944.def: An increase in the thickness of the pleura, generally related to scarring of the pleural tissue.

name: elevated circulating n , n - dimethylglycine concentration
elevate circulate n , n - dimethylglycine concentration
HP:0031945.def: An increased concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine in the circulation.

name: elevated urinary n , n - dimethylglycine level
elevate urinary n , n - dimethylglycine level
HP:0031946.def: An increased concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine in the urine.

name: tongue tremor
tongue tremor
HP:0031947.def: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the tongue.

name: snowball lesion of corpus callosum
snowball lesion of corpus callosum
HP:0031948.def: Centrally located corpus callosum hyperintensities said to resemble snowballs upon magnetic resonance imaging (with T2 or Sagittal fluid attenuated inversion recovery [FLAIR] sequences). The central location in the callosum makes them pathognomonic for Susac syndrome.

name: recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections
recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infection
HP:0031949.def: An increased susceptibility to bacterial upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections (running ears - otitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis).

name: usual interstitial pneumonia
usual interstitial pneumonia
HP:0031950.def: Temporal and spatial heterogeneity in lungs based on presence of fibrosis and honeycombing.

name: nocturnal seizures
nocturnal seizure
HP:0031951.def: Seizures that occur while the affected individual is sleeping.

name: neurogenic claudication
neurogenic claudication
HP:0031952.def: Lumbar spinal stenoses may induce symptoms following an individually typical latency on standing or when walking due to swelling of the cauda equina, which leads to compression. This is referred to as neurogenic claudication. The symptoms of lumbar spinal stenosis can be explained by an increase in lumbar lordosis and spinal canal stenosis in an upright position compared to the sitting position or if spondylolisthesis is present by a shift of the vertebrae while standing and walking. Following an individually characteristic distance, walking becomes associated with deep muscular pain and with neurological deficits, such as sensory deficits and paresis in the lower limbs, which resolve within minutes when the affected person sits or lies down. Activities performed in a flexed posture, such as cycling often cause less problems than walking. For the same reason, walking uphill may be tolerated better than walking downhill. Clinical neurological examination at rest may be entirely normal but there is usually pain on hyperextension of the lumbar spine.

name: cautious gait
cautious gait
HP:0031953.def: Cautious gait refers to an excessive degree of age-related changes in walking and fear of falling. The walking difficulties seem out of proportion when considering the patient's actual sensory or motor deficits. The gait appears slow, with a wider base than normal, reduced arm swing bilaterally and a slightly stooped posture. This type of gait change often occurs after the first time a patient has fallen.

name: dystonic gait
dystonic gait
HP:0031954.def: Dystonic gait disorders frequently appear bizarre, particularly because activity increases dystonic tonus and posture. The abnormal posture of the foot in dystonic gait typically involves inversion, plantar flexion and tonic extension of the big toe.
