In many patients complex types of walking, such as walking backwards and running are paradoxically less impaired than walking forward and may seem completely unaffected. Sensory tricks, for instance, if the affected individual rests a hand on his or her neck, may improve or even normalize dystonic gait in some patients.

name: antalgic gait
antalgic gait
HP:0031955.def: To avoid pain weight is put on the affected leg for as short a time as possible, resulting in a limp. The patients appear to be walking as if there were a thorn in the sole of the foot. To reduce the load on the affected leg the patients lift and lower their foot in a fixed ankle position.

name: elevated circulating aspartate aminotransferase concentration
elevate circulate aspartate aminotransferase concentration
HP:0031956.def: An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of aspartate aminotransferase (AST).

name: spastic hemiparetic gait
spastic hemiparetic gait
HP:0031957.def: Spastic hemiparesis is characterized by a dominance of the tonus in the upper limb flexor muscles: the arm is held in an adducted posture and is bent and rotated inwards, the forearm is pronated and the hand and the fingers are flexed. The leg is slightly bent at the hip, the knee cannot be extended fully at the end of the stance phase and the foot is inverted and in a plantar flexed position. Gait is slow, with a wide base and asymmetrical with a shortened weight-bearing phase on the paretic side. During the swing phase, the paretic leg performs a lateral movement (circumduction) which is characteristic of this gait disorder, also termed Wernicke-Mann gait. Spastic gait problems typically worsen on attempts to walk faster.

name: spastic paraparetic gait
spastic paraparetic gait
HP:0031958.def: A type of spastic gait in which the legs are usually slightly bent at the hip and in an adducted position. The knees are extended or slightly bent and the feet are in a plantar flexion position. This posture requires circumduction of the legs during walking. The gait may appear stiff (spastic gait disorder) or stiff as well as insecure (spastic ataxic gait disorder). In spastic paraparetic gait, each leg appears to be dragged forward. If the muscle tone in the adductors is marked, the resulting gait disorder is referred to as scissor gait.

name: leg dystonia
leg dystonia
HP:0031959.def: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the legs.

name: arm dystonia
arm dystonia
HP:0031960.def: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the arms.

name: abnormal serum anion gap
abnormal serum anion gap
HP:0031961.def: Any deviation from the normal value of the serum anion gap, which is calculated from the electrolytes measured in the chemical laboratory, is defined as the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration.

name: elevated serum anion gap
elevate serum anion gap
HP:0031962.def: An abnormally high value of the serum anion gap (the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration).

name: decreased serum anion gap
decrease serum anion gap
HP:0031963.def: An abnormally low value of the serum anion gap (the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration).

name: elevated circulating alanine aminotransferase concentration
elevate circulate alanine aminotransferase concentration
HP:0031964.def: An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of alanine aminotransferase (ALT).

name: increased rbc distribution width
increase rbc distribution width
HP:0031965.def: Red blood cell distribution width (RDW) is a simple parameter of the standard full blood count and a measure of heterogeneity in the size of circulating erythrocytes. It is provided by automated hematology analyzers and it reflects the range of the red cell size. It is calculated by dividing the standard deviation of erythrocyte volume by the mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and multiplied by 100 to convert to a percentage.
synonym: increased red blood cell distribution width
increase red blood cell distribution width

name: cloudy urine
cloudy urine
HP:0031967.def: The appearance of the urine having visible material in suspension, i.e., appearing cloudy.

name: reduced blood urea nitrogen
reduce blood urea nitrogen
HP:0031969.def: An abnormally low concentration of urea nitrogen in the blood.

name: abnormal blood urea nitrogen concentration
abnormal blood urea nitrogen concentration
HP:0031970.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of urea nitrogen in the blood.

name: subaortic ventricular septal bulge
subaortic ventricular septal bulge
HP:0031971.def: A localized hypertrophy of the subaortic segment of the ventricular septum has been frequently described in elderly persons, and variously termed subaortic ventricular septal bulge (VSB), sigmoid-shaped septum, localized or discrete upper septal hypertrophy.

name: presyncope
presyncope
HP:0031972.def: Presyncope is a state of lightheadedness, muscular weakness, blurred vision, and feeling faint. Presyncope is most often cardiovascular in cause.

name: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio
increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio
HP:0031973.def: An abnormal increase in the ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc.

name: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.6
increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.6
HP:0031974.def: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.6 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

name: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.7
increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.7
HP:0031975.def: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.7 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

name: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.8
increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.8
HP:0031976.def: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.8 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

name: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.9
increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.9
HP:0031977.def: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.9 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

name: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 1.0
increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 1.0
HP:0031978.def: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 1.0 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

name: abnormal urine carbohydrate level
abnormal urine carbohydrate level
HP:0031979.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carbohydrate in the urine.

name: abnormal urine carboxylic acid level
abnormal urine carboxylic acid level
HP:0031980.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carboxylic acid in the urine.

name: elevated urine glycolate
elevate urine glycolate
HP:0031981.def: An increased concentration of glycolate in the urine.

name: abnormal putamen morphology
abnormal putamen morphology
HP:0031982.def: Any structural anomaly of the putamen, a brain nucleus which together with the caudate nucleus and fundus striati makes up the striatum.

name: abnormal pulmonary thoracic imaging finding
abnormal pulmonary thoracic image find
HP:0031983.def: This term groups terms representing abnormal findings derived from chest X-ray investigation of the lung. In general, lung abnormalities can manifest as opacities (areas of increased density) or as regions with decreased density.

name: esophageal food impaction
esophageal food impaction
HP:0031984.def: A piece of food that has gotten stuck in the esophagus and prevents further swallowing.

name: esophageal exudate
esophageal exudate
HP:0031985.def: An exudate is a mass of fluid and cells that has seeped out of blood vessels or an organ, usually related to inflammation. In the esophagus, exudates usually present as whitish plagues on the surface of the esophageal mucosa.

name: polyminimyoclonus
polyminimyoclonus
HP:0031986.def: Irregular, small-amplitude myoclonic movements of the hands and/or fingers on keeping outstretched posture (jerky postural tremor). Polyminimyoclonus is stimulus-sensitive and accentuated during voluntary movements. A cortical origin can be demonstrated by back-averaging techniques, and somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs) are sometimes giant.

name: diminished ability to concentrate
diminish ability to concentrate
HP:0031987.def: Being unable to focus one's attention or mental effort on a particular object or activity.

name: perioral spasm
perioral spasm
HP:0031989.def: A sudden involuntary contraction of the musculature surrounding the mouth.

name: chvostek sign
chvostek sign
HP:0031990.def: A contraction of ipsilateral facial muscles subsequent to percussion over the facial nerve.

name: increased urinary excretion of galactosyl hydroxylysine
increase urinary excretion of galactosyl hydroxylysine
HP:0031991.def: An increased concentration of beta-1-galactosyl-O-hydroxylysine (Gal-Hyl) in the urine. This is a biochemical marker of bone resorption.

name: apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
HP:0031992.def: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (AHCM) is diastolic dysfunction due to abnormal stiffness of the left ventricle during diastole, with resultant impaired ventricular filling. In AHCM thickened apical segments produce a crowded, spade-shaped, small apical cavity.

name: hoffmann sign
hoffmann sign
HP:0031993.def: A Hoffmann test is performed by flicking the fingernail of the long finger, from dorsal to volar, on each hand while the hand was supported by the examiner's hand. The test was done with the neck in the neutral position and then with the neck maximally forward flexed. Any flexion of the ipsilateral thumb and/or index finger was interpreted as a positive test.

name: bronchial breath sound
bronchial breath sound
HP:0031994.def: Bronchial breath sounds contain much higher frequency components than normal breath sounds due to alteration of the low pass filtering function of the alveoli, as occurs in consolidation. It is loud, hollow, and high pitch. Expiratory phase is longer than inspiratory phase with the inspiratory-expiratory ratio (I:E) changing from normal 3:1 to 1:2. There is distinct pause between inspiration and expiration due to absent alveolar phase. It is associated with whispering pectoriloquy.

name: squawks
squawk
HP:0031995.def: Squawks are short inspiratory wheezes of less than 200 ms duration and are also known as squeaks. Acoustic analysis shows the fundamental frequency varying between 200 and 300 Hz. Squawks usually occur in late inspiration and are often preceded by late inspiratory crackles.

name: inspiratory crackles
inspiratory crackle
HP:0031996.def: Crackles that are heard during the inspiratory phase.

name: early inspiratory crackles
early inspiratory crackle
HP:0031997.def: Crackles that appear at the beginning of inspiration and end before mid-inspiration.

name: late inspiratory crackles
late inspiratory crackle
HP:0031998.def: Crackles that appear any time after the beginning of inspiration and last till the end of inspiration.

name: pleural rub
pleural rub
HP:0032000.def: An abnormal breath sound that is nonmusical, short and explosive. It is grating, rubbing, creaky, or leathery in character and present in both phases of respiration. Typically the expiratory component mirrors the inspiratory component. It occurs due to inflamed pleural surface rubbing each other during breathing. Clinically, it is important to differentiate it from crackles

name: pink urine
pink urine
HP:0032001.def: An abnormal pink color of urine.

name: orange urine
orange urine
HP:0032002.def: An abnormal orange color of urine.

name: green urine
green urine
HP:0032003.def: An abnormal green color of urine.

name: pruritus vulvae
pruritus vulva
HP:0032004.def: A sensation of itching in the vulvar region.

name: hemidystonia
hemidystonia
HP:0032005.def: Hemidystonia refers to dystonia which involves the ipsilateral face, arm, and leg.

name: lip tremor
lip tremor
HP:0032006.def: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the lip.

name: maceration
maceration
HP:0032007.def: A softening and breaking down of skin resulting from prolonged exposure to moisture. Macerated skin becomes soft and wrinkly and takes on a whitish hue.

name: pulmonary fat embolism
pulmonary fat embolism
HP:0032008.def: The release of fat globules into the venous circulation, thereby blocking blood circulation to the lung.

name: infantile constant exotropia
infantile constant exotropia
HP:0032009.def: Constant exotropia occurring before 6 months of age.; often associated with a large angle of deviation and ocular/CNS abnormalities.

name: basic constant exotropia
basic constant exotropia
HP:0032010.def: Constant exotropia for near and distance, presenting after 6 months of age.

name: heterophoria
heterophoria
HP:0032011.def: Heterophorias are latent deviations that are controlled by fusion. In certain circumstances (specific visual tasks, fatigue, illness, etc.), fusion can no longer be maintained and decompensation occurs.

name: heterotropia
heterotropia
HP:0032012.def: Manifest deviation of the visual axes not controlled by fusion.

name: hypermetric horizontal saccades
hypermetric horizontal saccade
HP:0032013.def: Overshoot of horizontal (sideways) saccadic eye movements.

name: dysmetric vertical saccades
dysmetric vertical saccade
HP:0032014.def: Inaccurate saccades (rapid movement of the eye between fixation points) in the vertical direction.

name: dysmetric horizontal saccades
dysmetric horizontal saccade
HP:0032015.def: Inaccurate saccades (rapid movement of the eye between fixation points) in the horizontal direction.

name: abnormal sputum
abnormal sputum
HP:0032016.def: Abnormal appearance of material expectorated (coughed up) from the respiratory system and that is composed of mucus but may contain other substances such as pus, blood, microorganisms, and fibrin.

name: sputum eosinophilia
sputum eosinophilia
HP:0032017.def: An increased proportion of eosinophils in sputum in the differentiated cell count.

name: multiple mononeuropathy
multiple mononeuropathy
HP:0032018.def: A type of peripheral neuropathy that happens when there is damage to two or more different nerve areas characterized by peripheral neuropathy of both the motor and sensory nerves of at least two different nerve trunks. Different nerves are affected either simultaneously or sequentially.

name: eosinophilic bladder infiltration
eosinophilic bladder infiltration
HP:0032020.def: Transmural inflammation of the bladder predominantly with eosinophils, associated with fibrosis with or without muscle necrosis.

name: eosinophilic liver infiltration
eosinophilic liver infiltration
HP:0032021.def: Cellular infiltration of the liver parenchyma with a preponderance of eosinophils.

name: eosinophilic dermal infiltration
eosinophilic dermal infiltration
HP:0032022.def: Presence of abnormally increased amounts of intraepidermal inflammatory cells with a predominance of eosinophils.

name: eosinophilic gallbladder infiltration
eosinophilic gallbladder infiltration
HP:0032023.def: Cellular infiltrate confirmed by a cellular infiltrate comprised of mainly eosinophils in the gallbladder wall on histological examination.

name: ileal ulcer
ileal ulcer
HP:0032024.def: An erosion of the mucous membrane in a portion of the ileum.

name: reduced serum alpha - 1 - antitrypsin
reduce serum alpha - 1 - antitrypsin
HP:0032025.def: A reduced concentration of circulating alpha-1 antitrypsin, which is a 52-kDa glycoprotein mainly synthesised and secreted by hepatocytes into the bloodstream. Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a serine-proteinase inhibitor that it is crucial in maintaining protease-antiprotease homeostasis in the lungs.

name: anetoderma
anetoderma
HP:0032026.def: Circumscribed area of flaccid skin due to the loss of elastic tissue in the dermis.

name: retinal dots
retinal dot
HP:0032027.def: Yellow, white or greyish lesions in the retina that are well-defined/distinct, individual and mostly uniform in size.

name: macular dots
macular dot
HP:0032028.def: Yellow, white or greyish lesions in the macula that are well-defined/distinct, individual and mostly uniform in size.

name: floppy eyelid
floppy eyelid
HP:0032029.def: Excessive eyelid tissue laxity, typically affecting both upper eyelids and associated with spontanteous tarsal eversion during sleep. It is more common in the obese, it may be associated with obstructive sleep apnea and it may result in corneal exposure or chronic papillary conjunctivitis.

name: lateral canthal tendon laxity
lateral canthal tendon laxity
HP:0032030.def: Laxity of the tendon stabilising the lateral aspect of the tarsal plate to the zygomatic bone. This can result in rounded appearence of the lateral canthus. Also, when the eyelid is pulled medially, more than 2 mm movement of the canthal angle may be observed.

name: medial canthal tendon laxity
medial canthal tendon laxity
HP:0032031.def: Laxity of the tendon stabilising the medial aspect of the tarsal plate to the anterior and posterior lacrimal crests. This may lead to more than 2mm movement of the punctum when the eyelid is pulled laterally.

name: horizontal eyelid laxity
horizontal eyelid laxity
HP:0032032.def: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation, predominantly in the horizontal plane. It can be demonstrated by the horizontal eyelid distraction test (e.g. by pulling the eyelid medially and laterally). Medial and/or lateral canthal tendon laxity are often present.

name: vertical eyelid laxity
vertical eyelid laxity
HP:0032033.def: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation, predominantly in the vertical plane. It can be demonstrated by vertical lid pull. Loosening of vertical stabilising structures (e.g. lower lid retractors) or tarsal atrophy are often present.

name: upper eyelid laxity
upper eyelid laxity
HP:0032034.def: Abnormally lax upper eyelid associated with tissue relaxation.

name: lower eyelid laxity
low eyelid laxity
HP:0032035.def: Abnormally lax lower eyelid associated with tissue relaxation.

name: reduced contrast sensitivity
reduce contrast sensitivity
HP:0032036.def: An abnormality in perception of contrast. Spatial contrast is a physical dimension referring to the light-dark transition of a border or an edge in an image that delineates the existence of a pattern or an object. Contrast sensitivity refers to a measure of how much contrast a person requires to see a target. Contrast-sensitivity measurements differ from acuity measurements; acuity is a measure of the spatial-resolving ability of the visual system under conditions of very high contrast, whereas contrast sensitivity is a measure of the threshold contrast for seeing a target.

name: mildly reduced visual acuity
mildly reduce visual acuity
HP:0032037.def: Mild reduction of the ability to see defined as visual acuity less than 6/12 (20/40 in US notation; 0.5 in decimal notation) but at least 6/18 (20/63 in US notation; 0.32 in decimal notation).

name: abnormality of the ocular adnexa
abnormality of the ocular adnexa
HP:0032039.def: An anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

name: abnormal ocular adnexa physiology
abnormal ocular adnexa physiology
HP:0032040.def: A functional anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

name: vocal cord polyp
vocal cord polyp
HP:0032041.def: A small growth on a vocal cord that may appear as pedunculated or sessile and have varying size, shape, and color.

name: decreased vigilance
decrease vigilance
HP:0032044.def: A decrease in the ability to maintain sustained attention is characterized by reduced alertness.

name: hypoplastic carotid canal
hypoplastic carotid canal
HP:0032045.def: Underdevelopment of the carotid canal, which normally is a circular aperture in the temporal bone of the skull through which the internal carotid artery and the carotid plexus of nerves traverse.

name: focal cortical dysplasia
focal cortical dysplasia
HP:0032046.def: A type of malformation of cortical development that primarily affects areas of neocortex. It can be identified on conventional magnetic resonance imaging as focal cortical thickening, abnormal gyration, and blurring between gray and white matter, often associated with clusters of heterotopic neurons.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type i
focal cortical dysplasia type i
HP:0032047.def: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by abnormal cortical layering.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type ia
focal cortical dysplasia type ia
HP:0032048.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal radial cortical lamination.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type ib
focal cortical dysplasia type ib
HP:0032049.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal tangential cortical lamination.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type ic
focal cortical dysplasia type ic
HP:0032050.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal radial and tangential cortical lamination.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type ii
focal cortical dysplasia type ii
HP:0032051.def: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by disrupted cortical lamination and specific cytological abnormalities.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iia
focal cortical dysplasia type iia
HP:0032052.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type II that is characterized by dysmorphic neurons, which present with a significantly enlarged cell body and nucleus, malorientation, abnormally distributed intracellular Nissl substance and cytoplasmic accumulation of neurofilament proteins.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iib
focal cortical dysplasia type iib
HP:0032053.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type II that is characterized by dysmorphic neurons (significantly enlarged with accumulation of neurofilament proteins) and balloon cells.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iii
focal cortical dysplasia type iii
HP:0032054.def: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by cortical lamination abnormalities associated with a principal lesion, usually adjacent to or affecting the same cortical area/lobe.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iiia
focal cortical dysplasia type iiia
HP:0032055.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by alterations in architectural organisation (cortical dyslamination) or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons outside Layer 5) in patients with hippocampal sclerosis (also known as Ammon's horn sclerosis).

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iiib
focal cortical dysplasia type iiib
HP:0032056.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by altered architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia without six-layered structure) and/or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons) of the neocortex, which occur adjacent to glial or glioneuronal tumor.

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iiic
focal cortical dysplasia type iiic
HP:0032057.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by alterations in architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia) or cytoarchitectural composition of the neocortex (hypertrophic neurons), which occur adjacent to vascular malformations (cavernomas, arteriovenous malformations, leptomeningeal vascular malformations, telangiectasias, meningioangiomatosis).

name: focal cortical dysplasia type iiid
focal cortical dysplasia type iiid
HP:0032058.def: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by altered architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia without six-layered structure) or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons) of the neocortex, which occur adjacent to other lesions acquired during early life (not included into FCD Type IIIa-c). These lesions comprise a large spectrum including traumatic brain injury, glial scarring after prenatal or perinatal ischemic injury or bleeding, and inflammatory or infectious diseases, i.e. Rasmussen encephalitis, limbic encephalitis, bacterial or viral infections.

name: mild malformation of cortical development
mild malformation of cortical development
HP:0032059.def: A malformation of cortical development characterized by mild abnormalities of the cortex: excessive heterotopic neurons in Layer 1 or microscopic neuronal clusters or excess of single neurons of normal morphology in deep white matter.

name: epithelioid hemangioma
epithelioid hemangioma
HP:0032060.def: A benign neoplasm that includes blood vessel proliferation and a dense eosinophilic inflammatory infiltrate, manifesting as flesh/plum-colored pruritic nodules and papules, most commonly affecting the ear and the periauricular area.

name: hypereosinophilia
hypereosinophilia
HP:0032061.def: A severely increased count of eosinophils in the blood defined as a blood eosinophil count of at least 1.5 billion cells per liter.

name: mallory - weiss tear
mallory - wei tear
HP:0032062.def: Vomiting-induced mucosal laceration at the esophago-gastric junction.

name: ankle joint effusion
ankle joint effusion
HP:0032063.def: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in or around the ankle joint.

name: gastrointestinal eosinophilia
gastrointestinal eosinophilia
HP:0032064.def: Eosinophilic infiltration of one or more gastrointestinal organs. Gastrointestinal eosinophilia is a broad term for abnormal eosinophil accumulation in the GI tract, involving many different disease identities. These diseases include primary eosinophil associated gastrointestinal diseases, gastrointestinal eosinophilia in HES and all gastrointestinal eosinophilic states associated with known causes. Each of these diseases has its unique features but there is no absolute boundary between them.

name: abnormal serum bicarbonate concentration
abnormal serum bicarbonate concentration
HP:0032065.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

name: decreased serum bicarbonate concentration
decrease serum bicarbonate concentration
HP:0032066.def: An abnormal reduction of the concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

name: elevated serum bicarbonate concentration
elevate serum bicarbonate concentration
HP:0032067.def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

name: increased urinary mucus
increase urinary mucus
HP:0032068.def: An increased amount of urinary mucus. A small amount of mucus is produced by mucous membrane epithelial cells of the urinary tract. An increased amount of mucus can be detected upon urinalysis or other assays and may indicate conditions such as urinary tract infection, urinary tract reconstruction involving the use of bowel segments, or contamination of the urine sample prior to urinalysis.

name: anti - thyroglobulin antibody positivity
anti - thyroglobulin antibody positivity
HP:0032069.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react to thyroglobulin.

name: leptomeningeal enhancement
leptomeningeal enhancement
HP:0032070.def: Contrast material enhancement of the pia mater or enhancement that extends into the subarachnoid spaces of the sulci and cisterns is leptomeningeal enhancement. Leptomeningeal enhancement is usually associated with meningitis, which may be bacterial, viral, or fungal. The primary mechanism of this enhancement is breakdown of the blood-brain barrier without angiogenesis.

name: eosinophilic pneumonia
eosinophilic pneumonia
HP:0032071.def: The presence of eosinophils in lung tissue, generally as detected by tissue biopsy, with or without blood eosinophilia.

name: popliteal synovial cyst
popliteal synovial cyst
HP:0032072.def: A fluid-filled mass that is a distention of a preexisting bursa in the popliteal fossa, most commonly the gastrocnemio-semimembranosus bursa. This bursa is unique in that it communicates with the knee joint, unlike other periarticular bursae, via an opening in the joint capsule posterior to the medial femoral condyle.

name: aplasia of the fallopian tube
aplasia of the fallopian tube
HP:0032073.def: Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the fallopian tube.

name: splenopancreatic fusion
splenopancreatic fusion
HP:0032075.def: Fusion of the pancreatic tail and spleen.

name: male urethral meatus stenosis
male urethral meatus stenosis
HP:0032077.def: An abnormal narrowing of the urethral opening (meatus) of the penis.

name: angel - shaped phalanx
angel - shape phalanx
HP:0032078.def: A phalangeal malformation that is termed angel-shaped phalanx (ASP), because of its resemblance to the angels used for decoration of Christmas trees. The various components of an angel-shaped phalanx are: diaphyseal cuff (wings), surrounding a meta-diaphyseal core (body), which may appear empty or structured with a cone-shaped epiphysis (skirt) and pseudoepiphysis (head).

name: medial degeneration
medial degeneration
HP:0032079.def: Medial degeneration of the aorta is to be used as an overarching term for any aortic surgical specimens that demonstrate one or more of the specific histopathologies mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation, elastic fiber fragmentation and/or loss, elastic fiber thinning, elastic fiber disorganization, smooth muscle cell nuclei loss, laminar medial collapse, smooth muscle cell disorganization, medial fibrosis. Grading of medial degeneration is based on the average overall severity of specific histopathologies as described, considering the worst area(s) sampled from multiple slides and aorta sections.

name: intralamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
intralamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
HP:0032081.def: A type of mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation in which the increase in mucoid extracellular matrix does not significantly alter the arrangement of the lamellar units.

name: translamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
translamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
HP:0032082.def: A type of mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation in which the increase in mucoid extracellular matrix alters the arrangement of the lamellar units to varying degrees.

name: aortic elastic fiber fragmentation
aortic elastic fiber fragmentation
HP:0032083.def: Loss and/or fragmentation of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta creating increasingly extended translamellar spaces, with absence of elastic fibers, and increased gaps in elastic fiber lamellae as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

name: aortic elastic fiber thinning
aortic elastic fiber thinning
HP:0032084.def: A thinning out of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta that creates widening of intralamellar spaces, as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

name: aortic elastic fiber disorganization
aortic elastic fiber disorganization
HP:0032085.def: Nonparallel arrangement/disarray of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

name: aortic smooth muscle cell nuclei loss
aortic smooth muscle cell nuclei loss
HP:0032086.def: A region of the aortic media in which smooth muscle cell nuclei, involving multiple lamellae, are not clearly identifiable on an hematoxylin and eosin stain.

name: aortic laminar medial collapse
aortic laminar medial collapse
HP:0032087.def: Architecturally, a compaction of aortic medial elastic fibers that creates thinning of the lamellar unit secondary to a band-like smooth muscle cell loss identified using a stain for elastic fibers.

name: aortic smooth muscle cell disorganization
aortic smooth muscle cell disorganization
HP:0032088.def: Nonparallel arrangement/disarray of smooth muscle cells of the aortic media creating focal/multifocal disarray or sometimes nodular aggregates of smooth muscle cells.

name: aortic medial fibrosis
aortic medial fibrosis
HP:0032089.def: An increase in collagen fibers creating areas of substitutive fibrosis or a widening of intralamellar spaces in the media of the aorta. This can be seen in conjunction with a loss to varying degrees of parallel arrangement of the elastic lamellae (or lamellar units).

name: intralamellar aortic medial fibrosis
intralamellar aortic medial fibrosis
HP:0032090.def: A type of aortic medial fibrosis in which the increase in collagen does not significantly alter the arrangement of the lamellar units.

name: translamellar aortic medial fibrosis
translamellar aortic medial fibrosis
HP:0032091.def: A type of aortic medial fibrosis in which the increase in collagen is more scar-like, altering the arrangement of the lamellar units.

name: left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
leave ventricular outflow tract obstruction
HP:0032092.def: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction can occur at the valvular, subvalvular, or supravalvular level. In general, there is an obstruction to forward flow which increases afterload, and if untreated, can result in hypertrophy, dilatation, and eventual failure of the left ventricle.

name: increased circulating surfactant protein level
increase circulate surfactant protein level
HP:0032094.def: An increased concentration of a surfactant protein in the blood circulation. Pulmonary surfactant is a highly surface-active mixture of proteins and lipids that is synthesized and secreted onto the alveoli by type II epithelial cells. The protein part of surfactant constitutes of four types of surfactant proteins (SP), SP-A, SP-B, SP-C and SP-D. SP-A and SP-D are hydrophilic proteins that regulate surfactant metabolism and have immunologic functions. These two proteins are detectable in the bloodstream and an elevated level may reflect idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

name: abnormal manganese concentration
abnormal manganese concentration
HP:0032096.def: A deviation from the normal range of manganese in the blood circulation.

name: hypermanganesemia
hypermanganesemia
HP:0032097.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of manganese in the blood.

name: hypomanganesemia
hypomanganesemia
HP:0032098.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of manganese in the blood.

name: perioral radial furrowing
perioral radial furrowing
HP:0032099.def: The presence of radial grooves in the skin surrounding the mouth (see Figure 4 of PMID:27833976).

name: abnormal doll 's eye reflex
abnormal doll 's eye reflex
HP:0032100.def: The doll's eye reflex (also known as oculocephalic reflex) is a test of brain function that is performed in comatose patients by elevating the head roughly 30 degrees and rapidly rotating the head from side to side with the eyes kept open. A normal response is for the eyes to move in the opposite direction. If the eyes do not move in the opposite direction this may indicate severe brain damage.

name: unusual infection
unusual infection
HP:0032101.def: A type of infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection. There are five general subtypes. (i) Opportunistic infection, meaning infection by a pathogen that is not normally able to cause infection in a healthy host (e.g., pneumonia by Pneumocystis jirovecii or CMV); (ii) Unusual location (focus) of an infection (e.g., an aspergillus brain abscess); (iii) a protracted course or lack of adequate response to treatment (e.g., chronic rhinosinusitis); (iv) Unusual severity or intensity of an infection; and (v) unusual recurrence of infections.

name: wilson sign
wilson sign
HP:0032102.def: Wilson sign is defined as the elicitation of pain by internally rotating the patient's tibia during knee extension between 90 degrees and 30 degrees of flexion and then relieving that pain by externally rotating the tibia.

name: saccadic oscillation
saccadic oscillation
HP:0032104.def: An involuntary abnormality of fixation in which there is an abnormal saccade away from fixation followed by an immediate corrective saccade.

name: macrosaccadic oscillations
macrosaccadic oscillation
HP:0032105.def: A type of saccadic oscillations with brief periods of fixation between saccades (intersaccadic interval approximately 200 msec). Macrosaccadic oscillations (up to 40 degrees) straddle the intended fixation position and show a crescendo-decrescendo pattern.

name: conjunctival icterus
conjunctival icterus
HP:0032106.def: Conjunctival icterus is a condition where there is yellowing of the whites of the eyes. This is most commonly seen in patients who have liver disease.
synonym: yellowing of the whites of the eyes
yellowing of the white of the eye

name: limbal stem cell deficiency
limbal stem cell deficiency
HP:0032107.def: A condition characterized by a loss or deficiency of the stem cells in the limbus that are vital for re-population of the corneal epithelium and to the barrier function of the limbus.

name: mildly reduced contrast sensitivity
mildly reduce contrast sensitivity
HP:0032108.def: A mild reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 0.20-0.59 log unit contrast sensitivity loss.

name: moderately reduced contrast sensitivity
moderately reduce contrast sensitivity
HP:0032109.def: A moderate reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 0.60-0.99 log unit contrast sensitivity loss.

name: severely reduced contrast sensitivity
severely reduce contrast sensitivity
HP:0032110.def: A severe reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 1.00 log unit or more contrast sensitivity loss.

name: abnormal vistech contrast sensitivity test
abnormal vistech contrast sensitivity test
HP:0032111.def: An abnormality in perception of contrast as measured by the Vistech wall chart sine wave grating test.

name: abnormal pelli robson contrast sensitivity chart test
abnormal pelli robson contrast sensitivity chart test
HP:0032112.def: An abnormality in perception of contrast as measured by the Pelli-Robson contrast sensitivity chart, which is a large wall-mounted chart, with letters of a fixed size (comprising spatial frequencies appropriate for estimating peak contrast sensitivity) that decrease in contrast.

name: semidominant inheritance
semidominant inheritance
HP:0032113.def: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on chromosomes in which a trait can manifest in a monoallelic (e.g. heterozygotes) and biallelic (e.g. homozygotes, compound heterozygotes) state, with similar or differing phenotype severity present dependent on the number of alleles affected.

name: saccadic intrusion
saccadic intrusion
HP:0032114.def: An involuntary abnormality of fixation in which there is an abnormal saccade away from fixation followed by a delayed corrective saccade.

name: macrosquare - wave jerks
macrosquare - wave jerk
HP:0032116.def: Horizontal 10-40 degree excursions from fixation and back again.

name: retinitis
retinitis
HP:0032118.def: Inflammation of the retina of the eye.

name: abnormal peripheral nervous system physiology
abnormal peripheral nervous system physiology
HP:0032120.def: Any functional abnormality of the part of the nervous system that consists of the nerves and ganglia outside of the brain and spinal cord.

name: froment sign
froment sign
HP:0032121.def: An abnormal result of a physical examination of the the hand that tests for palsy of the ulnar nerve. This nerve innervates the adductor pollicis and interossei muscles and thereby enables adduction of the thumb and extension of the interphalangeal joint. An abnormal result consists in reduced functionality and muscular weakness in the pinch grip between the thumb and index finger of the affected hand as the patient attempts to pinch a piece of paper that the examiner tries to pull away. The flexor pollicis longus muscle tries to compensate for the weakness by flexing the tip of the thumb at the interphalangeal joint.

name: very low visual acuity
very low visual acuity
HP:0032122.def: A reduction in visual acuity with best corrected visual acuity between 1.40 (20/500) and 1.89 logMAR (up to roughly 20/1590).

name: ultra - low vision
ultra - low vision
HP:0032123.def: Best corrected visual acuity worse than 1.90 logMAR (roughly 20/1590).

name: abnormal proportion of unswitched memory b cells
abnormal proportion of unswitched memory b cell
HP:0032124.def: A deviation of the normal proportion of unswitched memory B cells in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.
synonym: abnormal proportion of non - class - switched memory b cells
abnormal proportion of non - class - switched memory b cell

name: increased proportion of unswitched memory b cells
increase proportion of unswitched memory b cell
HP:0032125.def: An increase above the normal proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells relative to the total number of B cells.
synonym: elevated proportion of unswitched memory b cells
elevate proportion of unswitched memory b cell
increased proportion of non - class - switched memory b cells
increase proportion of non - class - switched memory b cell

name: decreased proportion of unswitched memory b cells
decreased proportion of unswitched memory b cell
HP:0032126.def: A reduction below the normal proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells relative to the total number of B cells.
synonym: decreased proportion of non - class - switched memory b cells
decreased proportion of non - class - switched memory b cell
reduced proportion of unswitched memory b cells
reduce proportion of unswitched memory b cell

name: abnormal plasmablast proportion
abnormal plasmablast proportion
HP:0032127.def: A deviation from the normal proportion of plasmablasts in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Plasmablasts are antibody-secreting cells that originate after infection or vaccination.

name: increased proportion of plasmablasts
increase proportion of plasmablast
HP:0032128.def: An elevation above the normal proportion of plasmablasts in circulation relative to total number of B cells.

name: decreased proportion of plasmablasts
decreased proportion of plasmablast
HP:0032129.def: A reduction below the normal proportion of plasmablasts in circulation relative to total number of B cells.

name: mycobacterium abscessus abscessus infection
mycobacterium abscessus abscessus infection
HP:0032130.def: Mycobacterium abscessus complex comprises a group of rapidly growing, multidrug-resistant, nontuberculous mycobacteria that are responsible for a wide spectrum of skin and soft tissue diseases, central nervous system infections, bacteremia, and ocular and other infections.

name: cervical dysplasia
cervical dysplasia
HP:0032131.def: Cervical dysplasia is the precursor to cervical cancer. It is caused by the persistent infection of the human papillomavirus (HPV) into the cervical tissue. Affected cells develop morphologic features with immature basaloid- type squamous cells and mitotic figures in the upper half of the cervical epithelium.

name: decreased circulating total igg
decrease circulate total igg
HP:0032132.def: A reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.

name: transient decreased circulating total igg
transient decrease circulate total igg
HP:0032133.def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.

name: chronic decreased circulating total igg
chronic decrease circulate total igg
HP:0032134.def: A lasting reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.
synonym: chronic decreased total igg in blood
chronic decrease total igg in blood

name: decreased circulating igg subclass level
decrease circulate igg subclass level
HP:0032135.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of a subclass of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.
synonym: decreased igg subclass level in blood
decrease igg subclass level in blood

name: decreased circulating igg1 level
decrease circulate igg1 level
HP:0032136.def: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG1 subclass in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating igg3 level
decrease circulate igg3 level
HP:0032137.def: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG3 subclass in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating igg4 level
decrease circulate igg4 level
HP:0032138.def: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG4 subclass in the blood circulation.

name: reduced isohemagglutinin level
reduce isohemagglutinin level
HP:0032139.def: Level of isohemagglutinin reduced below expected concentration. An isohemagglutinin refers to the naturally occurring antibodies in the ABO blood group system (i.e., anti-A in a group B person, anti-B in a group A person, and anti-A, anti-B, and anti-A,B in a group O person).
synonym: decreased natural antibody to blood group agents
decreased natural antibody to blood group agent

name: decreased specific antibody response to vaccination
decrease specific antibody response to vaccination
HP:0032140.def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against toxoids and polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

name: precordial pain
precordial pain
HP:0032141.def: A type of chest pain that arises in the or under the left breast and often described as throbbing, stabbing, or burning, and lasting hours or longer. The pain may arise with or after effort, and may spread to the left arm or left side of the neck.

name: fetor hepaticus
fetor hepaticus
HP:0032142.def: Fetor hepaticus is the characteristic breath of patients with severe parenchymal liver disease, which has been said to resemble the odor of a mixture of rotten eggs and garlic.

name: burning mouth
burn mouth
HP:0032143.def: An intense sensation of burning, scalding, or tingling feeling of the tongue or other regions of the oral mucosa.

name: coffee ground vomitus
coffee ground vomitus
HP:0032144.def: Vomit that has the appearance of coffee grounds, which occurs due to the presence of coagulated blood in the vomit.

name: sural nerve atrophy
sural nerve atrophy
HP:0032145.def: Wasting of the sural nerve, a sensory nerve in the calf region of the leg.

name: hbc hemoglobin
hbc hemoglobin
HP:0032146.def: Presence of an abnormal type of hemoglobin characterized by the subsitution of a glutamic acid residue at position 7 following the initial methionine residue by a lysine (6GAG>6AAG). The presence of HbC can be determined by hemoglobin electrophoresis.

name: erythromelalgia
erythromelalgia
HP:0032147.def: Recurrent episodes of redness, burning pain, and warmth of the extremities following exposure to heat or exercise with symptoms predominantly involving the feet.

name: episodic pain
episodic pain
HP:0032148.def: Intermittent pain, i.e., pain that occurs occasionally and at irregular intervals.

name: breakthrough pain
breakthrough pain
HP:0032149.def: A episode of severe pain that breaks through (i.e., temporarily exacerbates) a period of persistent pain.

name: paroxysmal rectal pain
paroxysmal rectal pain
HP:0032150.def: Excruciating burning pain in the rectal area that may be triggered by defecation.

name: episodic eosinophilia
episodic eosinophilia
HP:0032151.def: Recurrent episodes of marked eosinophilia that resolve spontaneously.

name: keratosis pilaris
keratosis pilaris
HP:0032152.def: An anomaly of the hair follicles of the skin that typically presents as small, rough, brown folliculocentric papules distributed over characteristic areas of the skin, particularly the outer-upper arms and thighs.

name: joint subluxation
joint subluxation
HP:0032153.def: A partial dislocation of a joint.

name: aphthous ulcer
aphthous ulcer
HP:0032154.def: Oral aphthous ulcers typically present as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a hyperemic border.

name: abdominal cramps
abdominal cramp
HP:0032155.def: A type of abdominal pain characterized by a feeling of contractions and typically fluctuating in intensity.

name: skin detachment
skin detachment
HP:0032156.def: Loss of sections of skin either spontaneously or after gentle handling.

name: recurrent genital herpes
recurrent genital herpes
HP:0032157.def: Recurrent episodes of genital herpes, typically characterized by stages of erythema, papules, short-lived vesicles, painful ulcers, and crusts on the skin of the genitals and surrounding area, and that typically resolve over a period of 2 to 3 weeks.

name: unusual infection by anatomical site
unusual infection by anatomical site
HP:0032158.def: An unusual infection classified by the affected body part.

name: fungal meningitis
fungal meningitis
HP:0032159.def: An infection of the meninges caused by a fungus. Generally, only individuals with deficiencies of the immune system contract fungal meningitis.

name: cryptococcal meningitis
cryptococcal meningitis
HP:0032160.def: A type of fungal meningitis caused by an encapsulated yeast that belongs to the genus Cryptococcus. Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are responsible for the majority of cases of human cryptococcosis.

name: coccidioidal meningitis
coccidioidal meningitis
HP:0032161.def: A type of fungal meningitis caused by dissemination of coccidioides to basilar meninges.

name: unusual skin infection
unusual skin infection
HP:0032162.def: A type of infection of the skin that can be regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection.

name: molluscum contagiosum
molluscum contagiosum
HP:0032163.def: Molluscum contagiosum is a cutaneous viral infection that is commonly observed in both healthy and immunocompromised children. The infection is caused by a member of the Poxviridae family, the molluscum contagiosum virus. Molluscum contagiosum presents as single or multiple small white or flesh-colored papules that typically have a central umbilication. The central umbilication may be difficult to observe in young children and, instead, may bear an appearance similar to an acneiform eruption. The lesions vary in size (from 1 mm to 1 cm in diameter) and are painless, although a subset of patients report pruritus in the area of infection. On average, 11-20 papules appear on the body during the course of infection and generally remains a self-limiting disease. However, in immunosuppressed patients, molluscum contagiosum can be a severe infection with hundreds of lesions developing on the body. Extensive eruption is indicative of an advanced immunodeficiency state.

name: increased blood folate concentration
increase blood folate concentration
HP:0032164.def: An elevated circulating concentration of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9.

name: placental mesenchymal dysplasia
placental mesenchymal dysplasia
HP:0032165.def: Placental mesenchymal dysplasia is a rare anomaly characterized by placentomegaly, dilatation of chorionic vessels and hydropic stem villi with cistern-like formation. It is often clinically mistaken for a partial hydatidiform mole but there is no trophoblastic proliferation. P57 immunohistochemical expression is discordant, showing a normal positive expression in the cytotrophoblastic cells, and loss of expression in the stromal cells.

name: clostridium difficile enteritis
clostridium difficile enteritis
HP:0032167.def: An infection of the small intestine (enteritis) by clostridium difficile.

name: clostridium difficile colitis
clostridium difficile colitis
HP:0032168.def: An infection of the colon (colitis) by clostridium difficile.

name: severe infection
severe infection
HP:0032169.def: A type of infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection because of unusual severity or intensity of the infection.

name: severe varicella zoster infection
severe varicella zoster infection
HP:0032170.def: An unusually severe form of varicella zoster virus (VZV) infection. In the majority of the cases, especially in children, varicella is a very mild infection characterised by skin lesions, low grade fever and malaise. Severe infection is characterized by manifestions including VZV pneumonia, hepatitis, meningitis, and disseminated varicella.

name: bladder pain
bladder pain
HP:0032171.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the urinary bladder. Bladder pain may be more pronounced with a full bladder and relieved upon urination, but this is not always the case.

name: air crescent sign
air crescent sign
HP:0032172.def: A crescent of air surrounding a soft-tissue mass in a pulmonary cavity and can be seen in both plain X-ray and CT scan.

name: continuous diaphragm sign
continuous diaphragm sign
HP:0032173.def: This sign is seen in pneumomediastinum in which air accumulates between the lower border of the heart and the superior part of the diaphragm, which results in complete visualization of the diaphragm in chest X-ray, hence named continuous diaphragm sign.

name: tree - in - bud pattern
tree - in - bud pattern
HP:0032174.def: The tree-in-bud pattern represents centrilobular branching structures that resemble a budding tree. The pattern reflects a spectrum of endo- and peribronchiolar disorders, including mucoid impaction, inflammation, and/or fibrosis (See Figure 70 of PMID:18195376).

name: signet ring sign
signet ring sign
HP:0032175.def: This finding is composed of a ring-shaped opacity representing a dilated bronchus in cross section and a smaller adjacent opacity representing its pulmonary artery, with the combination resembling a signet (or pearl) ring. It is the basic sign of bronchiectasis in pulmonary computed tomography imaging.

name: apical pulmonary opacity
apical pulmonary opacity
HP:0032176.def: An apical cap is a caplike lesion at the lung apex, usually caused by intrapulmonary and pleural fibrosis pulling down extrapleural fat or possibly by chronic ischemia resulting in hyaline plaque formation on the visceral pleura. The prevalence increases with age. It can also be seen in hematoma resulting from aortic rupture or in other fluid collection associated with infection or tumor, either outside the parietal pleura or loculated within the pleural space.

name: parenchymal consolidation
parenchymal consolidation
HP:0032177.def: Consolidation refers to an exudate or other product of disease that replaces alveolar air, rendering the lung solid (as in infective pneumonia).

name: flaky paint dermatosis
flaky paint dermatosis
HP:0032178.def: A dermatosis characterized by generalized shiny, enamel-like, hyperpigmented scales in an irregular pattern. The scales may peel or desquamate, rather like old, sun-baked blistered paint, often with areas of underlying hypopigmentation. This has led to the terms peeling paint or flaky paint dermatosis (See the Figure in PMID:24285001).

name: abnormal circulating globulin concentration
abnormal circulate globulin concentration
HP:0032179.def: An abnormal concentration of globulins in the blood. Albumin makes up more than half of the total protein present in serum. The remaining blood proteins except albumin and fibrinogen (which is not in serum) are referred to as globulins. The globulin fraction includes hundreds of serum proteins including carrier proteins, enzymes, complement, and immunoglobulins. Most of these are synthesized in the liver, although the immunoglobulins are synthesized by plasma cells. Globulins are divided into four groups by electrophoresis. The four fractions are alpha1, alpha2, beta and gamma, depending on their migratory pattern between the anode and the cathode.

name: abnormal circulating metabolite concentration
abnormal circulate metabolite concentration
HP:0032180.def: An abnormal level of an analyte measured in the blood.

name: anomalous hepatic venous drainage into the left atrium
anomalous hepatic venous drainage into the left atrium
HP:0032181.def: An abnormality of the hepatic veins, which normally drain de-oxygenated blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava, whereby the hepatic veins drain into the left atrium.

name: abnormal proportion of memory t cells
abnormal proportion of memory t cell
HP:0032182.def: An abnormal proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. Memory T cells have previously encountered and responded to their cognate antigen and upon a repeated encounter with the antigen can mount a faster and stronger response.

name: decreased proportion of memory t cells
decreased proportion of memory t cell
HP:0032183.def: An abnormally reduced proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood.

name: increased proportion of memory t cells
increase proportion of memory t cell
HP:0032184.def: An abnormally elevated proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood.

name: disseminated molluscum contagiosum
disseminate molluscum contagiosum
HP:0032185.def: The presense of molluscum contagiosum lesions across multiple areas of the body.

name: anal neoplasm
anal neoplasm
HP:0032186.def: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the anal canal or anal margin.

name: anal intraepithelial neoplasia
anal intraepithelial neoplasia
HP:0032187.def: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) is a premalignant lesion of the anal mucosa that is a precursor to anal cancer.

name: cellular hypersensitivity to mitomycin c
cellular hypersensitivity to mitomycin c
HP:0032188.def: An increased cellular sensitivity to the DNA cross-linking agent, mitomycin C (MMC). In the presence of increased sensitivity, MMC causes increased cell death, chromosome breakage, and accumulation in the G2 phase of the cell cycle.

name: cellular hypersensitivity to diepoxybutane
cellular hypersensitivity to diepoxybutane
HP:0032189.def: An increased cellular sensitivity to the DNA cross-linking agent, diepoxybutane (DEB). In the presence of increased sensitivity, DEB causes cell death, chromosome breakage, and accumulation in the G2 phase of the cell cycle.

name: abnormal meniscus morphology
abnormal meniscus morphology
HP:0032190.def: Abnormal structure of the meniscus of the knee, two crescent shape fibrocartilaginous pads that disperse the weight of the body and reduce friction of the knee joint during movement.

name: torn meniscus
torn meniscus
HP:0032191.def: A tear in the cartilaginous pad (meniscus) of the knee.

name: hydatidiform mole
hydatidiform mole
HP:0032192.def: Hydatidiform mole (HM) is an aberrant human pregnancy with absence of, or abnormal embryonic development, hydropic degeneration of chorionic villi, and excessive proliferation of the trophoblast.

name: decreased low - density lipoprotein particle size
decrease low - density lipoprotein particle size
HP:0032193.def: An abnormal decrease in the average size of low-density lipoprotein particle size in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal s wave
abnormal s wave
HP:0032195.def: Any anomaly of the S wave, which is the third component of the QRS wave complex. The S wave signifies the final depolarization of the ventricles at the base of the heart.

name: prominent s wave in lead i
prominent s wave in lead i
HP:0032196.def: Increased amplitude (0.1 mV or more) and/or duration (40 ms or more) of the S wave as measured in lead I of the electrocardiogram.

name: deep s wave in lead v5
deep s wave in lead v5
HP:0032197.def: Abnormal depth of the S wave in lead V5 of the electrocardiogram.

name: decreased prothrombin time
decrease prothrombin time
HP:0032198.def: Abnormally short time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

name: abnormal prothrombin time
abnormal prothrombin time
HP:0032199.def: Any deviation from the normal amount of time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

name: perivascular fibrosis
perivascular fibrosis
HP:0032200.def: The presence of thick collagen bundles around blood vessels, often in an onion-skin type whorling pattern.

name: rotator cuff tear
rotator cuff tear
HP:0032201.def: The term rotator cuff describes the tendons connecting the infraspinatus, supraspinatus, teres minor, and subscapularis muscles to the humeral head.Traumatic tears of the rotator cuff tend to occur at the tendon-bone junction of the supraspinatus and greater tuberosity of the humerus whereas degenerative tears tend to be seen posteriorly at the junction of the supraspinatus and infraspinatu A rotator cuff tear is when one or more of these tendons tears or detaches from the humerus.

name: vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
HP:0032202.def: Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is widely accepted as the precursor lesion of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC). VSCC arises via either a human papilloma virus (HPV)-associated pathway, or more commonly, via a mechanism independent of HPV, often being linked to chronic inflammatory conditions such as lichen sclerosus (LS). Accordingly, two distinct subtypes of VIN are recognised: the HPV-associated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion/usual VIN (HSIL/uVIN) and the non-HPV-associated differentiated VIN (dVIN). HSIL is clinically identified by its multifocal, warty appearance and on histology by conspicuous cytological and architectural atypia. Differentiated VIN, on the other hand, often produces ill-defined lesions, and on histology, notoriously mimics non-neoplastic epithelial disorders (NNED), particularly LS. As a result, dVIN is rarely identified in advance of a diagnosis of invasive malignancy, despite being the precursor lesion of the majority of VSCC.

name: lymphoid nodular hyperplasia
lymphoid nodular hyperplasia
HP:0032203.def: Lymphoid nodular hyperplasia (LNH) of the terminal ileum and colon has been considered a mucosal response to nonspecific stimuli, most often infections, and consequently has been regarded as a pathophysiologic phenomenon during infancy and childhood. LNH can be ascertained by colonoscopy, whereby a lymphoid nodule is defined as an extruding follicle with a diameter of not more than 2 mm, and LNH is defined as a cluster of not more than 10 of such extruding lymphoid nodules (see Figure 1 of PMID:17368236).

name: chronic active epstein - barr virus infection
chronic active epstein - barr virus infection
HP:0032204.def: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is an uncommon outcome of EBV infection and may present as a waxing and waning or fulminant syndrome. Unlike acute infectious mononucleosis, wherein EBV establishes lifelong infection and survives by maintaining a delicate balance with the host as a latent infection, in chronic active EBV infection the host-virus balance is disturbed.

name: increased circulating galectin - 3 level
increase circulate galectin - 3 level
HP:0032205.def: An increased circulation of galectin-3 in the blood circulation.

name: obsolete abnormal cerebrospinal fluid metabolite concentration
obsolete abnormal cerebrospinal fluid metabolite concentration
increased urinary type 1 collagen n - terminal telopeptide level
increase urinary type 1 collagen n - terminal telopeptide level
HP:0032208.def: An increased concentration of type 1 collagen N-terminal telopeptide (NTx) level in the urine. Generally the test is performed over a period of time, for instance, 10 cc of morning urine can be collected following 12 hours overnight fasting or for 24 hours.
synonym: increased collagen crosslinked n - telopeptide [ moles / volume ] in 24 hour urine
increase collagen crosslinked n - telopeptide [ mole / volume ] in 24 hour urine

name: abnormal circulating free t3 concentration
abnormal circulate free t3 concentration
HP:0032209.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of free triiodothyronine (T3) in the blood circulation. A proportion of T3 is bound to plasma proteins in the blood, including mainly thyroxine binding globulin, transthyretin, and albumin. T3 that is not bound to a protein is referred to as free T3.

name: decreased circulating free t3
decrease circulate free t3
HP:0032210.def: A reduced concentration of free 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine in the blood circulation.

name: increased urinary epithelial cell count
increase urinary epithelial cell count
HP:0032211.def: An increased number of epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

name: increased urinary squamous epithelial cell count
increase urinary squamous epithelial cell count
HP:0032212.def: An increased number of squamous epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

name: increased urinary renal tubular epithelial cell count
increase urinary renal tubular epithelial cell count
HP:0032213.def: An increased number of renal tubular epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

name: increased urinary transitional epithelial cell count
increase urinary transitional epithelial cell count
HP:0032214.def: An increased number of transitional epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

name: disseminated cutaneous warts
disseminate cutaneous wart
HP:0032215.def: Multiple skin warts located in multiple parts of the body, e.g., neck, trunks, and extremities.

name: lymphocytic infiltration of the colorectal mucosa
lymphocytic infiltration of the colorectal mucosa
HP:0032216.def: Abnormally increased intraepithelial lymphocyte count. This finding may be appreciated as large numbers of surface intraepithelial lymphocytes as seen (for instance) with hematoxylin and eosin staining of a colonic biopsy sample taken during colonoscopy.

name: indurated nodule
indurate nodule
HP:0032217.def: A skin nodule that is unusually hard (indurated).

name: decreased proportion of cd4 - positive t cells
decreased proportion of cd4 - positive t cell
HP:0032218.def: A reduction in the proportion of CD4-positive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
synonym: decreased proportion of cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells
decreased proportion of cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cell
reduced proportion of cd4 - positive cells
reduce proportion of cd4 - positive cell

name: increased proportion of cd4 - positive t cells
increase proportion of cd4 - positive t cell
HP:0032219.def: An elevation in the proportion of CD4-positive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
synonym: elevated proportion of cd4 - positive t cells
elevate proportion of cd4 - positive t cell
increased proportion of cd4+ t cells
increase proportion of cd4+ t cell
increased proportion of cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells
increase proportion of cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cell

name: interface hepatitis
interface hepatitis
HP:0032220.def: Inflammation of the liver characterized by a mononuclear cell infiltrate whereby portal inflammatory cells extend through the limiting plate between the portal tract and liver parenchyma.

name: periportal emperipolesis
periportal emperipolesis
HP:0032221.def: The engulfing of lymphocytes by hepatocytes, which typically occurs in the interface hepatitis area.

name: serrated intestinal polyps
serrate intestinal polyp
HP:0032222.def: The presence of multiple serrated polyps in the intestine. Unlike conventional adenomas, which are uniformly dysplastic, the vast majority of serrated lesions contain no dysplasia. The serrated class includes the hyperplastic polyps, which are not considered precancerous; sessile serrated polyps (also called sessile serrated adenomas); and traditional serrated adenomas. Sessile serrated polyps are larger on average and more often located in the proximal colon. Sessile serrated polyps have a more irregular surface, a pattern to the surface that has been called cloudlike, and indistinct edges compared with hyperplastic polyps. Sessile serrated polyps also have large open pits on the surface (type O pits) when viewed with magnification.

name: blood group
blood group
HP:0032223.def: Any of the various types of human blood whose antigen characteristics determine compatibility in transfusion. While the ABO and Rhesus sytems are the most well known, there are in total about 300 different blood type antigens distributed across 34 different blood type systems.

name: abo blood group
abo blood group
HP:0032224.def: The ABO system consists of A and B antigens and antibodies against these antigens.

name: perifollicular fibroma
perifollicular fibroma
HP:0032225.def: Perifollicular fibroma is a rare cutaneous hamartoma that shows differentiation in the connective tissue sheath of hair follicles. It can occur as a solitary papule or as multiple lesions. Histologically, the lesion consists of a concentric arrangement of cellular fibrous tissue around a normal hair follicle.

name: abnormal sebaceous gland morphology
abnormal sebaceous gland morphology
HP:0032226.def: Any structural anomaly of the sebaceous glands.

name: sebaceous hyperplasia
sebaceous hyperplasia
HP:0032227.def: A common, benign skin condition involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands characterized by single or multiple lesions that manifest as yellow, soft, small papules with umbilication. The lesions are located commonly on the central face (specifically, the nose, cheeks and forehead) but may also occur elswehere, including the chest, mouth, scrotum, foreskin, penile shaft, vulva, and areola.

name: trichodiscoma
trichodiscoma
HP:0032228.def: A small benign fibrovascular tumor of the dermal part of the hair disk. Trichodiscoma is rather simple in appearance and consists of a dome-shaped fibrous tumor with a prominent vascular component that fills the papillary dermis under an atrophic epidermis. As in a normal hair disk, a hair follicle may be present at one edge of the papular lesion.

name: perinuclear antineutrophil antibody positivity
perinuclear antineutrophil antibody positivity
HP:0032229.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against proteins predominantly expressed in perinuclear region of neutrophils.

name: cytoplasmic antineutrophil antibody positivity
cytoplasmic antineutrophil antibody positivity
HP:0032230.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against proteins predominantly expressed in cytoplasmic granules of neutrophils.

name: hypochromia
hypochromia
HP:0032231.def: A qualitative impression that red blood cells have less color than normal when examined under a microscope, usually related to a reduced amount of hemoglobin in the red blood cells.

name: increased circulating creatine kinase mb isoform
increase circulate creatine kinase mb isoform
HP:0032232.def: An increased concentration of the MB isoform of creatine kinase in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating creatine kinase bb isoform
increase circulate creatine kinase bb isoform
HP:0032233.def: An increased concentration of the BB isoform of creatine kinase in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating creatine kinase mm isoform
increase circulate creatine kinase mm isoform
HP:0032234.def: An increased concentration of the MM isoform of creatine kinase in the blood circulation.

name: anti - la / ss - b antibody positivity
anti - la / ss - b antibody positivity
HP:0032235.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against La/SSB autoantigens.

name: increased circulating immature neutrophil count
increase circulating immature neutrophil count
HP:0032236.def: An abnormally increased number of immature neutrophils in the peripheral blood circulation.

name: increased circulating myelocyte count
increase circulate myelocyte count
HP:0032237.def: An abnormally increased number of myelocytes in the peripheral blood circulation. Myelocytes are immature neutrophils with a size of 12-18 micrometers, a round or oval nucleus with no nucleoli, bluish-pink staining cytoplasm with primary and seconday granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 2:1.

name: increased circulating metamyelocyte count
increase circulate metamyelocyte count
HP:0032238.def: An abnormally increased number of metamyelocytes in the peripheral blood circulation. Metamyelocytes are immature neutrophils with a size of 10-18 micrometers, an indented or kidney-shaped nucleus, pinkish-blue staining cytoplasm with seconday granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 1.5:1.

name: increased circulating band cell count
increase circulate band cell count
HP:0032239.def: An abnormally increased number of band cells in the peripheral blood circulation. Band cells are immature neutrophils with a size of 10-18 micrometers, a horseshoe-shaped nucleus with no nucleoli, light-pink staining cytoplasm with many small seconday granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 1:2.

name: elevated circulating e selectin level
elevate circulate e selectin level
HP:0032240.def: An increased concentration of E selectin in the blood circulation.

name: cervical neoplasm
cervical neoplasm
HP:0032241.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the uterine cervix.

name: cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
HP:0032242.def: A precancerous condition characterized by dysplasia of the cervical epithelium. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) 1, 2 and 3 based on its relationship with the prognosis. CIN 1 is mild dysplasia, which is mostly observed because it disappears as part of its natural course. CIN 3 includes severe dysplasia and carcinoma in situ, and management involves treatment because it is highly likely to develop into invasive cancer.

name: abnormal tissue metabolite concentration
abnormal tissue metabolite concentration
HP:0032243.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a metabolite in a tissue.

name: decreased serum thromboxane b2
decrease serum thromboxane b2
HP:0032244.def: A reduction in the concentration of thromboxane B2 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal metabolism
abnormal metabolism
HP:0032245.def: An abnormality in the function of the chemical reactions related to processes including conversion of food to enter, synthesis of proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates, or the elimination of waste products.

name: persistent cmv viremia
persistent cmv viremia
HP:0032247.def: Lasting (uncontrolled) presence of cytomegalovirus in the blood circulation.

name: persistent viremia
persistent viremia
HP:0032248.def: Persistence of virus in the blood circulation longer than would be normal in an immunocompentent host.

name: coccidioidomycosis
coccidioidomycosis
HP:0032249.def: Infection by a Coccidioides species fungus. These are dimorphic, soil-dwelling, fungi known to cause a broad spectrum of disease, ranging from a mild febrile illness to severe pulmonary manifestations or disseminated disease. The genus Coccidioides is comprised of two genetically distinct species: Coccidioides immitis and C. posadasii.

name: acinetobacter infection
acinetobacter infection
HP:0032250.def: An infection by Acinetobacter baumannii, a Gram-negative bacillus that is aerobic, pleomorphic and non-motile. An opportunistic pathogen, A. baumannii has a high incidence among immunocompromised individuals, particularly those who have experienced a prolonged (over 90 d) hospital stay.

name: granuloma
granuloma
HP:0032252.def: A compact, organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes, which may be but is not necessarily accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis.

name: eosinophilic granuloma
eosinophilic granuloma
HP:0032253.def: A type of granuloma characterized morphologically by the predominance of Langerhans cells with characteristic grooved, folded, indented nuclei in the appropriate milieu that includes variable numbers of eosinophils and histiocytes including multinucleated forms, often appearing similar to osteoclasts or touton like giant cells, neutrophils and small lymphocytes. The concentration of the eosinophilic infiltrate varies from scattered mature cells to sheet-like masses of cells. Occasionally, areas of bone necrosis may interrupt the cellular infiltrate. The foamy cells may also be amassed in clumps, which are of no clinical significance because these clumps represent phagocytosis of lipid debris.

name: increased circulating copper concentration
increase circulate copper concentration
HP:0032254.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of copper in the blood circulation. This term refers to the total copper concentration.

name: opportunistic fungal infection
opportunistic fungal infection
HP:0032255.def: An infection that is caused by a fungus that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such fungi take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

name: histoplasmosis
histoplasmosis
HP:0032256.def: Histoplasmosis is caused by the fungus Histoplasma capsulatum and is consider to be an opportunistic infection in immunosuppressed persons.

name: disseminated histoplasmosis
disseminate histoplasmosis
HP:0032257.def: Histoplasmosis infection involving multiple sites of the body. Disseminated histoplasmosis can involve various organs, including reticuloendothelial organs, gastrointestinal tract, adrenal glands, central nervous system, endovascular structures, kidney, and skin. It typically presents with systemic symptoms like fever, generalized fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and the symptoms related to the specific organ involved. Severe disseminated disease can manifest as septic shock, multi organ failure, and ARDS.

name: pulmonary histoplasmosis
pulmonary histoplasmosis
HP:0032258.def: Infection of the lungs with Histoplasma capsulatum. Symptoms may include fever, headache, weakness, chest pain and dry cough. When imaging is done, chest radiographs may show patchy pneumonia involving one or more lobes with adenopathy of the mediastinum or hilum.

name: chronic tinea infection
chronic tinea infection
HP:0032259.def: The term tinea means fungal infection, whereas dermatophyte refers to the fungal organisms that cause tinea. This term refers to a tinea infection that is chronic or recalcitrant to treatment and may be reflective of an immune defect.

name: opportunistic bacterial infection
opportunistic bacterial infection
HP:0032260.def: An infection that is caused by a bacterium that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such bacteria take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

name: nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary infection
nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary infection
