HP:0032261.def: An infection of the lung caused by environmental mycobacteria. Such infections can occur in individuals with predisposing lung disease or immune disease.

name: pulmonary tuberculosis
pulmonary tuberculosis
HP:0032262.def: A lung infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis a slightly curved non-motile, aerobic, non-capsulated and non-spore forming strains of mycobacteria.

name: increased blood pressure
increase blood pressure
HP:0032263.def: Abnormal increase in blood pressure. An individual measurement of increased blood pressure does not necessarily imply hypertension. In practical terms, multiple measurements are recommended to diagnose the presence of hypertension.

name: anti - nmda receptor antibody positivity
anti - nmda receptor antibody positivity
HP:0032264.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate)-type glutamate receptor.
synonym: presence of anti - n - methyl - d - aspartate receptor antibody in blood
presence of anti - n - methyl - d - aspartate receptor antibody in blood
presence of anti - nmdar antibody in blood
presence of anti - nmdar antibody in blood

name: csf autoimmune antibody positivity
csf autoimmune antibody positivity
HP:0032265.def: The presence of an antibody in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that is directed against the organism's own cells or tissues.

name: csf anti - nmda receptor antibody positivity
csf anti - nmda receptor antibody positivity
HP:0032266.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against the NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate)-type glutamate receptor.
synonym: presence of anti - n - methyl - d - aspartate receptor antibody in csf
presence of anti - n - methyl - d - aspartate receptor antibody in csf
presence of anti - nmdar antibody in cerebrospinal fluid
presence of anti - nmdar antibody in cerebrospinal fluid
presence of nmdar antibody in csf
presence of nmdar antibody in csf

name: empty delta sign
empty delta sign
HP:0032267.def: This sign is created by a nonenhancing thrombus in the dural sinus surrounded by triangular enhancing dura as seen on cross-section. The sign, seen on contrast-enhanced CT scan images, suggests dural sinovenous thrombosis. It is best seen on wider window settings. It is a reliable sign of sinus thrombosis but is seen only in 25-30% of these cases.

name: dural tail sign
dural tail sign
HP:0032268.def: This sign represents thickening and enhancement of the dura mater in continuity with a mass, which on MR images, gives the appearance of a tail arising from the mass. The dural tail is thought to represent reactive change; however, it may also be due to tumor invasion. Three criteria need to be met for a positive dural tail sign: the tail should be seen on two successive images through the tumor, it should taper away from the tumor, and it must enhance more than the tumor.

name: lemon sign
lemon sign
HP:0032269.def: The lemon sign refers to the shape of the fetal skull at ultrasonography (US) when the frontal bones lose their normal convex contour and appear flattened or inwardly scalloped. This gives the skull a shape that is said to resemble a lemon.. The sign is seen on transverse sonograms of the fetal cranium obtained at the level of the ventricles.

name: optic nerve tram - track sign
optic nerve tram - track sign
HP:0032270.def: A tram-track sign is composed of two enhancing areas of tumor separated from each other by the negative defect of the optic nerve. It is seen on contrast-enhanced CT scan and MRI images, in optic nerve sheath meningioma. The sign helps distinguish between optic nerve sheath meningioma and optic glioma. Optic glioma arises from glial cells within the optic nerve and there is no clear separation between the nerve and the tumor; hence the tram-track sign is not seen in optic gliomas. Calcification may be seen in optic nerve sheath meningiomas in 20-50% of cases and hence the tram-track sign may be seen on nonenhanced CT scan images as a linear calcification around the nerve, but this is less common.

name: extrapulmonary tuberculosis
extrapulmonary tuberculosis
HP:0032271.def: A type of tubercular infection located outside of the lung, which is the most common location of tuberculosis. There are two types of clinical manifestation of tuberculosis (TB) are pulmonary TB (PTB) and extrapulmonary TB (EPTB). The former is most common. EPTB refers to TB involving organs other than the lungs (e.g., pleura, lymph nodes, abdomen, genitourinary tract, skin, joints and bones, or meninges). A patient with both pulmonary and EPTB is classified as a case of PTB.

name: elevated urinary n - acetylaspartic acid level
elevate urinary n - acetylaspartic acid level
HP:0032272.def: Elevated N-acetylaspartic acid (NAA) in urine. This feature can be measured using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.

name: increased circulating n - acetylaspartic acid concentration
increase circulate n - acetylaspartic acid concentration
HP:0032273.def: Concentration of N-acetylaspartic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: increased circulating n - acetyl aspartate level
increase circulate n - acetyl aspartate level
increased circulating n - acetyl aspartic acid level
increase circulate n - acetyl aspartic acid level
increased circulating n - acetyl - l - aspartic acid level
increase circulate n - acetyl - l - aspartic acid level

name: increased csf n - acetylaspartic acid concentration
increase csf n - acetylaspartic acid concentration
HP:0032274.def: An abnormally increased concentration of N-acetylaspartic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
synonym: increased n - acetyl aspartate levels in csf
increase n - acetyl aspartate level in csf
increased n - acetyl aspartic acid levels in csf
increase n - acetyl aspartic acid level in csf
increased n - acetyl - l - aspartic acid levels in csf
increase n - acetyl - l - aspartic acid level in csf
increased n - acetylaspartate levels in csf
increase n - acetylaspartate level in csf

name: recurrent shingles
recurrent shingle
HP:0032275.def: Repeated episodes of a localized, painful cutaneous eruption related to reactivation of varicella zoster virus (VZV) and characterized by a characteristic rash in one or two adjacent dermatomes.

name: prominent subcalcaneal fat pad
prominent subcalcaneal fat pad
HP:0032276.def: Abnormally increased prominence of the fat pad underneath the heal. This feature can be appreciated in figure 1 of PMID:26769062.

name: 2 - hydroxyglutarate aciduria
2 - hydroxyglutarate aciduria
HP:0032278.def: The concentration of 2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: abnormal base excess
abnormal base excess
HP:0032281.def: Deviation from the normal quantity of base excess, defined as the amount of strong acid (in millimoles per liter) that needs to be added in vitro to 1 liter of fully oxygenated whole blood to return a blood sample to standard conditions (pH of 7.40, Pco2 of 40 mm Hg, and temperature of 37 degrees C).

name: contact dermatitis
contact dermatitis
HP:0032282.def: An inflammatory process in skin caused by an exogenous agent that directly or indirectly injure the skin. If the offending agent is identified and removed, the eruption will resolve. An unusual or patterned eruption may be a clue to the presence of a contact dermatitis. Patch testing may be helpful in the differential diagnosis.

name: disseminated nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
disseminate nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
HP:0032283.def: An infection with nontuberculous mycobacteria that affects multiple body sites. Such infections can occur in individuals with immune disease.

name: ultra - low vision with retained motion projection
ultra - low vision with retained motion projection
HP:0032284.def: Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to identify a moving object (typically hand motion at distance of 30 cm).

name: ultra - low vision with retained light projection
ultra - low vision with retained light projection
HP:0032285.def: Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to perceive the difference between light and dark. Also when light is projected in each of the four quadrants of the visual field, the individual is able to correctly identify the origin of the light stimulus.

name: ultra - low vision with retained light perception
ultra - low vision with retained light perception
HP:0032286.def: Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to perceive the difference between light and dark.

name: ultra - low vision with no light perception
ultra - low vision with no light perception
HP:0032287.def: Ultra-low vision with complete lack of light and form perception.

name: polyclonal elevation of circulating igg
polyclonal elevation of circulate igg
HP:0032288.def: An increase in polyclonal immunoglobulins resulting from many different plasma cells. On serum electrophoresis, a polyclonal gammopathy is characterized by a broad diffuse band with one or more heavy chains and kappa and lambda light chains.

name: oligoclonal elevation of circulating igg
oligoclonal elevation of circulate igg
HP:0032289.def: An increase in circulating immunoglobulins characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

name: monoclonal elevation of igg
monoclonal elevation of igg
HP:0032290.def: An increase in circulating immunoglobulins characterized by a single band in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

name: monoclonal elevation of intact igg
monoclonal elevation of intact igg
HP:0032291.def: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has a normal structure with a light and heavy chain.

name: monoclonal elevation of igg light chain
monoclonal elevation of igg light chain
HP:0032292.def: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a light chain but not a heavy chain.

name: monoclonal elevation of igg heavy chain
monoclonal elevation of igg heavy chain
HP:0032293.def: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a heavy chain but not a light chain.

name: monoclonal elevation of igg kappa chain
monoclonal elevation of igg kappa chain
HP:0032294.def: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a kappa light chain but not a heavy chain.

name: monoclonal elevation of igg lambda chain
monoclonal elevation of igg lambda chain
HP:0032295.def: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a lambda light chain but not a heavy chain.

name: increased circulating igg subclass
increase circulate igg subclass
HP:0032296.def: An elevation of circulating IgG level predominantly related to an elevation of one of the four IgG subclasses.

name: increased circulating igg3 level
increase circulate igg3 level
HP:0032297.def: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG3 subtype in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating igg1 level
increase circulate igg1 level
HP:0032298.def: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG1 subtype in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating igg2 level
increase circulate igg2 level
HP:0032299.def: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG2 subtype in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating igg4 level
increase circulate igg4 level
HP:0032300.def: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG4 subtype in the blood circulation.

name: genital warts
genital wart
HP:0032301.def: Warts affecting the skin in the genital area (peniile shaft, scrotum, vagina, or labia majora). Warts can be small, beginning as a pinhead-size swelling that may become larger and take on a pdenuculated appearance. Warts can spread and coalesce into large masses in the genital or anal area. Their color is variable but tends to be skin colored or darker, and they may occasionally bleed. Warts may cause itching, redness, or discomfort. An outbreak of genital warts may also cause psychological distress.

name: kappa bence jones proteinuria
kappa bence jones proteinuria
HP:0032302.def: The presence of free monoclonal kappa immunoglobulin light chains in the urine.

name: lambda bence jones proteinuria
lambda bence jones proteinuria
HP:0032303.def: The presence of free monoclonal lambda immunoglobulin light chains in the urine.

name: abnormal circulating mannose - binding protein concentration
abnormal circulate mannose - binding protein concentration
HP:0032304.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of mannose-binding protein in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating mannose - binding protein concentration
decrease circulate mannose - binding protein concentration
HP:0032305.def: Concentration of mannose-binding protein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: increased circulating mannose - binding protein concentration
increase circulate mannose - binding protein concentration
HP:0032306.def: Concentration of mannose-binding protein in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: increased circulating procalcitonin concentration
increase circulate procalcitonin concentration
HP:0032308.def: An elevated concentration of procalcitonin in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal granulocyte count
abnormal granulocyte count
HP:0032309.def: Any deviation from the normal cell count per volume of granulocytes in the blood circulation.

name: granulocytosis
granulocytosis
HP:0032310.def: An increased count of granulocytes in the peripheral blood circulation.

name: increased circulating globulin level
increase circulate globulin level
HP:0032311.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of globulins in the blood.

name: decreased circulating globulin level
decrease circulate globulin level
HP:0032312.def: An abnormally reduced concentration of globulins in the blood.

name: frontotemporal hypertrichosis
frontotemporal hypertrichosis
HP:0032313.def: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the region of the forehead and temple.

name: abnormal areolar morphology
abnormal areolar morphology
HP:0032314.def: An abnormal appearance or structure of the ring of pigmented skin that surrounds the nipple.

name: areolar fullness
areolar fullness
HP:0032315.def: The areola (ring of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple) is filled out so as to produce a rounded shape.

name: family history
family history
HP:0032316.def: Information about close relatives of an individual who is the proband of a study or who is being investigated with the goal of identifying a medical diagnosis. Usually, the family history includes information from three generations of relatives, including children, brothers and sisters, parents, aunts and uncles, nieces and nephews, grandparents, and cousins.

name: family history of cancer
family history of cancer
HP:0032317.def: A close blood relative had cancer.

name: family history of heart disease
family history of heart disease
HP:0032318.def: A close blood relative had heart disease.

name: health status
health status
HP:0032319.def: Health status of a family member with respect to the disease being investigated in a proband.

name: affected
affected
HP:0032320.def: This term applies to a family member who is diagnosed with the same condition as the individual who is the primary focus of investigation (the proband).

name: unaffected
unaffected
HP:0032321.def: This term applies to a family member in whom the diagnosis that is the primary focus of investigation is excluded.

name: healthy
healthy
HP:0032322.def: No history of any serious disease, including the disease being investigated in the proband.

name: periodic fever
periodic fever
HP:0032323.def: Episodic fever that recurs at regular intervals.

name: non - periodic recurrent fever
non - periodic recurrent fever
HP:0032324.def: Episodic fever that recurs at irregular intervals.

name: lacunar stroke
lacunar stroke
HP:0032325.def: A stroke related to a small infarct (2-20 mm in diameter) in the deep cerebral white matter, basal ganglia, or pons, that is presumed to result from the occlusion of a single small perforating artery supplying the subcortical areas of the brain.

name: methicillin - resistant staphylococcus aureus infection
methicillin - resistant staphylococcus aureus infection
HP:0032326.def: Infection with staphylococcus aureus resistant to the antibiotic methicillin (MRSA). MRSA can infect any individual but is more common among hospitalized patients, and can also occur as an opportunistic infection.

name: interhemispheric cyst
interhemispheric cyst
HP:0032327.def: Cystic collection (sac-like, fluid containing pocket of membranous tissue) located in the interhemispheric fissure, with or without communication with the ventricular system.

name: temporomandibular joint adhesion
temporomandibular joint adhesion
HP:0032328.def: Formation of one or more fibrous bands within the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) with resulting limitation of movement of the TMJ. Adhesions may be seen in degenerative processes that involve the TMJ.

name: increased urinary 11 - deoxycortisol level
increase urinary 11 - deoxycortisol level
HP:0032329.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of 11-deoxycortisol in the urine.

name: increased urinary 11 - deoxycorticosterone level
increase urinary 11 - deoxycorticosterone level
HP:0032330.def: An abnormally elevated concentration or amount of 11-deoxycorticosterone in the urine.

name: increased urinary 11 - deoxytetrahydrocorticosterone level
increase urinary 11 - deoxytetrahydrocorticosterone level
HP:0032331.def: An abnormally elevated concentration or amount of 11-deoxytetrahydrocorticosterone the urine.

name: oligoclonal elevation of circulating igm
oligoclonal elevation of circulate igm
HP:0032332.def: An increase in circulating IgM characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase.

name: polyclonal elevation of circulating iga
polyclonal elevation of circulate iga
HP:0032333.def: A heterogeneous increase in IgA mmunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.

name: oligoclonal elevation of circulating iga
oligoclonal elevation of circulate iga
HP:0032334.def: An increase in circulating IgA characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

name: monoclonal elevation of circulating iga
monoclonal elevation of circulate iga
HP:0032335.def: An increase in circulating IgA characterized by one predominant band in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

name: monoclonal elevation of circulating ige
monoclonal elevation of circulate ige
HP:0032337.def: An increase in circulating IgE characterized by one predominant band in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

name: oligoclonal elevation of circulating ige
oligoclonal elevation of circulate ige
HP:0032338.def: An increase in circulating IgE characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

name: polyclonal elevation of circulating ige
polyclonal elevation of circulate ige
HP:0032339.def: A heterogeneous increase in IgE mmunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.

name: reduced forced vital capacity
reduce forced vital capacity
HP:0032341.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal inspiration.

name: reduced forced expiratory volume in one second
reduce forced expiratory volume in one second
HP:0032342.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second.

name: elevated cancer ag 19 - 9 level
elevate cancer ag 19 - 9 level
HP:0032345.def: An abnormal increased in the amount of the carbohydrate antigen 19-9, a recognizable sialo-ganglioside in the blood circulation.

name: cutaneous lichen amyloidosis
cutaneous lichen amyloidosis
HP:0032346.def: Lichen amyloidosis presents with multiple localized or rarely generalized, hyperpigmented grouped papules with a predilection for the shins, calves, ankles, and dorsa of the feet and thighs.

name: cutaneous macular amyloidosis
cutaneous macular amyloidosis
HP:0032347.def: A type of cutaneous amyloidosis that is characterized by hyperpigmented patches with indefinite margins composed of grayish brown macules, often with a reticulated or rippled appearance.

name: cutaneous nodular amyloidosis
cutaneous nodular amyloidosis
HP:0032348.def: A type of cutaneous amyloidosis that is characterized clinically by waxy, purpuric plaques and nodules and histologically by amyloid deposits in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue.

name: serinuria
serinuria
HP:0032349.def: A increased concentration of serine in the urine.

name: sulfocysteinuria
sulfocysteinuria
HP:0032350.def: A increased concentration of sulfocysteine in the urine.

name: phenylalaninuria
phenylalaninuria
HP:0032351.def: Increased level of phenylalanine in urine.
synonym: increased level of phenylalanine in urine
increase level of phenylalanine in urine

name: methioninuria
methioninuria
HP:0032352.def: Level of methionine in urine above the upper limit of normal.

name: leucinuria
leucinuria
HP:0032353.def: Increased level of leucine in urine.

name: decreased peak expiratory flow
decrease peak expiratory flow
HP:0032355.def: A reduction in the maximum expiratory flow per minute, which can be used to measure how fast a subject can exhale as well as to judge the strength of the expiratory muscles and the condition of the large airways.

name: decreased pre - bronchodilator forced vital capacity
decrease pre - bronchodilator force vital capacity
HP:0032356.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal insipiration, with the test being performed before the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
synonym: decreased pre bronchodilator forced vital capacity
decrease pre bronchodilator force vital capacity

name: decreased post - bronchodilator forced vital capacity
decrease post - bronchodilator force vital capacity
HP:0032357.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal insipiration, with the test being performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
synonym: decreased post bronchodilator forced vital capacity
decrease post bronchodilator force vital capacity

name: decreased post - bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
decrease post - bronchodilator force expiratory volume in one second
HP:0032358.def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second, with the test being performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
synonym: decreased post bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
decrease post bronchodilator force expiratory volume in one second
decreased postbronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
decrease postbronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second

name: decreased forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
decrease forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
HP:0032359.def: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled.

name: decreased pre - bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
decrease pre - bronchodilator force expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
HP:0032360.def: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled. Here, the test is performed before the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
synonym: decreased pre bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
decrease pre bronchodilator force expiratory flow 25 - 75 %

name: decreased post - bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
decrease post - bronchodilator force expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
HP:0032361.def: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled. Here, the test is performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
synonym: decreased post bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
decrease post bronchodilator force expiratory flow 25 - 75 %

name: increased circulating corticosterone level
increase circulate corticosterone level
HP:0032362.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

name: decreased circulating corticosterone level
decrease circulate corticosterone level
HP:0032363.def: An abnormally reduced concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

name: obsolete abnormal csf amino acid level
obsolete abnormal csf amino acid level
exacerbated by aspirin exposure
exacerbate by aspirin exposure
HP:0032365.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by ingestion of aspirin.

name: positive direct antiglobulin test
positive direct antiglobulin test
HP:0032366.def: A positive result of the direct antiglobulin test (DAT), a method of demonstrating the presence of antibody or complement bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes by the use of anti-human globulin to form a visible agglutination reaction.

name: abnormal growth hormone level
abnormal growth hormone level
HP:0032367.def: Any deviation from the normal level of growth hormone (GH) in the blood circulation. GH or somatotropin is a peptide hormone that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration. Its secretion from the pituitary is regulated by the neurosecretory nuclei of the hypothalamus, which can release Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH or somatocrinin) and Growth hormone-inhibiting hormone (GHIH or somatostatin) into the hypophyseal portal venous blood surrounding the pituitary. GH is secreted in a pulsatile manner, which is one of the reasons why an isolated measurement of its blood concentration is not meaningful.

name: acidemia
acidemia
HP:0032368.def: An abnormally low blood pH (usually defined as less than 7.35).

name: alkalemia
alkalemia
HP:0032369.def: An abnormally high blood pH (usually defined as 7.41 or above).

name: blood group a
blood group a
HP:0032370.def: ABO phenotype A, corresponding to the genotype AO or AA.

name: isoleucinuria
isoleucinuria
HP:0032371.def: An increased concentration of isoleucine in the urine.

name: increased peripheral blast count
increase peripheral blast count
HP:0032372.def: An increased count in the peripheral blood of cells that are precursors to mature circulating blood cells such as neutrophiles, monocytes, lymphocutes, and erythrocytes. Blasts are not usually found in significant numbers in the peripheral blood circulation, but can be observed in hematopoietic neoplasms such as leukemia, severe infections, and as a result of certain medications.

name: duffy blood group
duffy blood group
HP:0032373.def: The Duffy blood group system is based on the presence of a glycoprotein termed Fy that is on the surface of erythrocytes and some other cells. There are two Duffy antigens named Fya and Fyb, and thus there are four Duffy phenotypes: a+b+, a+b-, a-b+,a-b-.

name: duffy fya positivity
duffy fya positivity
HP:0032374.def: Presence of the Duffy Fya antigen.

name: duffy fyb positivity
duffy fyb positivity
HP:0032375.def: Presence of the Duffy Fyb antigen.

name: anti - beta 2 glycoprotein i antibody positivity
anti - beta 2 glycoprotein i antibody positivity
HP:0032376.def: Presence of antibodies against beta 2 glycoprotein I in the circulation. Beta-2 glycoprotein I (beta2GPI) is the principal target of autoantibodies in the antiphospholipid syndrome (APS).

name: increased urinary orosomucoid
increase urinary orosomucoid
HP:0032377.def: An increased concentration in the urine of alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP), also known as orosomucoid (ORM). AGP is a 41-43-kDa glycoprotein with a pI of 2.8-3.8. AGP is an acute-phase protein that has many activities including, but not limited to, acting as an acute-phase reactant and disease marker, modulating immunity, binding and carrying drugs, maintaining the barrier function of capillary, and mediating the sphingolipid metabolism.

name: immediate - type hypersensitivity drug reaction
immediate - type hypersensitivity drug reaction
HP:0032378.def: Hypersensitivity that is observed within 1 hr of exposures. A variety of adverse reactions can occur within minutes to hours of exposure to a drug. Some can be related to the pharmacological action of the drug (WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology type A for augmented) and usually have a low mortality. Others are not readily predictable based on the structure and pharmacological action of the drug and have a relatively high mortality risk (Type B for bizarre). The most serious form of immediate onset drug hypersensitivity reaction, anaphylaxis. Other reactions including itching, dizziness/light-headedness, nausea, chest discomfort but without any objective skin features, physical signs or physiological compromise. Skin only reactions include generalized erythema, urticaria or angioedema without any sentinel features (see below) of other organ involvement.

name: polymorphous light eruption
polymorphous light eruption
HP:0032379.def: The cardinal symptom is severely pruritic skin lesions. Macular, papular, papulovesicular, urticarial, multiforme- and plaque-like variants are differentiated morphologically, hence the name polymorphous. Usually one morphology dominates in a single individual (monomorphous). The skin lesions develop a few hours to several days after sun exposure. Initially, patchy erythema develops, accompanied by pruritus. Distinct lesions then develop. The upper chest, upper arms, backs of the hands, thighs, and the sides of the face are the primary localizations. The skin lesions resolve spontaneously within several days of ceasing sun exposure and do not leave behind any traces.

name: hydroa vacciniforme
hydroa vacciniforme
HP:0032381.def: In response to the spring sun distinct inflamed reddened skin develops on the ears, nose, cheeks, fingers, backs of the hands, and the lower arms, on which blisters with serous or hemorrhagic content develop. These dry out with the formation of a blackish scab. After shedding of the scab, depressed, varioliform, often hypopigmented scars remain. In addition, hyper- and hypopigmentation are present together, resulting in a polymorphous skin presentation.
synonym: acute vesiculation and crusting and scarring following sun exposure
acute vesiculation and crusting and scar follow sun exposure

name: uniparental disomy
uniparental disomy
HP:0032382.def: Inheritance of both homologues of a chromosome pair from the same parent.

name: uniparental heterodisomy
uniparental heterodisomy
HP:0032383.def: A type of uniparental disomy in which the two different chromosomes (or chromosome segments) of the same parent are transmitted.

name: uniparental isodisomy
uniparental isodisomy
HP:0032384.def: A type of uniparental disomy in which the two identical chromosomes (or chromosome segments) of the same parent are transmitted.

name: abnormal circulating transferrin concentration
abnormal circulate transferrin concentration
HP:0032385.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating transferrin concentration
elevate circulate transferrin concentration
HP:0032386.def: An abnormally increased concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating transferrin concentration
reduce circulate transferrin concentration
HP:0032387.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

name: periventricular nodular heterotopia
periventricular nodular heterotopia
HP:0032388.def: Nodules of heterotopia along the ventricular walls. There can be a single nodule or a large number of nodules, they can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, they can be small or large, single or multiple.

name: periventricular laminar heterotopia
periventricular laminar heterotopia
HP:0032389.def: A large mass of heterotopia in a laminar configuration along the ventricular walls. Usually bilateral.

name: periventricular ribbonlike heterotopia
periventricular ribbonlike heterotopia
HP:0032390.def: Heterotopia that forms a continuous wavy line along the ventricular wall.

name: subcortical heterotopia
subcortical heterotopia
HP:0032391.def: A form of heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is located deep within the white matter.

name: nodular subcortical heterotopia in peritrigonal regions
nodular subcortical heterotopia in peritrigonal region
HP:0032392.def: Solid nodular heterotopia situated in the region of the peritrigonal optic pathway posterior to the deep gray nuclei.

name: diffuse ribbon - like subcortical heterotopia
diffuse ribbon - like subcortical heterotopia
HP:0032393.def: Subcortical heterotopia consisting of a bilateral and symmetric single continuous, undulating ribbon-like layer of gray matter located in the frontal, parietal and occipital lobes. It has no visible connection to the overlying cortex.

name: mesial parasagittal subcortical heterotopia
mesial parasagittal subcortical heterotopia
HP:0032394.def: Subcortical heterotopia extending along the mesial aspect of the lateral ventricles, with direct connection to mesial polymicrogyria-like cortex at the anterior and posterior limits of the heterotopia.

name: curvilinear subcortical heterotopia
curvilinear subcortical heterotopia
HP:0032395.def: Large subcortical heterotopia of variable morphology wiht streaks and swirls. These always connect to the overlying cortex in at least one, but usually in multiple, locations. Spaces with the signal intensity of CSF are usually seen within the heterotopia.

name: transmantle columnar heterotopia
transmantle columnar heterotopia
HP:0032396.def: Linear heterotopia spanning from the cerebral mantle from the pia to the ependyma.

name: citrullinuria
citrullinuria
HP:0032397.def: An increased concentration of citrulline in the urine.

name: dysgyria
dysgyria
HP:0032398.def: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation.

name: dysgyria with normal cortical thickness
dysgyria with normal cortical thickness
HP:0032399.def: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation but with a normal thickness of the cortex.

name: dysgyria with thickened cortex
dysgyria with thickened cortex
HP:0032400.def: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation and a thickened cortex intermediate between pachygyria and polymicrogyria.

name: aspartic aciduria
aspartic aciduria
HP:0032401.def: A increased concentration of aspartic acid in the urine.

name: asparaginuria
asparaginuria
HP:0032403.def: An increased concentration of asparagine in the urine.
synonym: increased level of asparagine in urine
increase level of asparagine in urine

name: testicular mass
testicular mass
HP:0032404.def: An abnormal bulge or lump in a testis. A testicular mass has a long differential diagnosis including testicular torsion, epididymitis, acute orchitis, strangulated hernia and testicular cancer.

name: increased urinary phosphoserine level
increase urinary phosphoserine level
HP:0032405.def: An increased level of phosphoserine in the urine.
synonym: increased level of phosphoserine in urine
increase level of phosphoserine in urine

name: unilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria
unilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria
HP:0032406.def: A type of perisylvian polymicrogyria that largely affects one side of the brain.

name: bilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria
bilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria
HP:0032407.def: A type of perisylvian polymicrogyria that affects both sides of the brain.

name: breast mass
breast mass
HP:0032408.def: A breast lump is any discrete mass in a breast noticed by the patient, significant other, or physician.

name: subcortical band heterotopia
subcortical band heterotopia
HP:0032409.def: A form of subcortical heterotopia with mislocalized gray matter within the white matter.It is defined as longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter. It is part of the lissencephaly spectrum.

name: bilateral generalized polymicrogyria
bilateral generalize polymicrogyria
HP:0032410.def: Symmetric generalized polymicrogyria with no obvious gradient or region of maximal severity; may have abnormal high signal in white matter.

name: posterior predominant subcortical band heterotopia
posterior predominant subcortical band heterotopia
HP:0032411.def: Longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter visible along the occipital cortex.

name: anterior predominant subcortical band heterotopia
anterior predominant subcortical band heterotopia
HP:0032412.def: Longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter visible in the frontal and temporal lobes.

name: diffuse subcortical band heterotopia
diffuse subcortical band heterotopia
HP:0032413.def: Longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter visible along the whole brain.

name: hydroxylysinuria
hydroxylysinuria
HP:0032414.def: The presence of an elevated amount of 5-hydroxylysine in the urine. This compound is a hydroxylated derivative of the amino acid lysine that is present in certain collagens.

name: parasagittal parieto - occipital polymicrogyria
parasagittal parieto - occipital polymicrogyria
HP:0032415.def: Polymicrogyria in parasagittal and mesial aspects of parieto-occipital cortex.

name: retinal microaneurysm
retinal microaneurysm
HP:0032416.def: A localized dilation of microvasculature formed due to disruption of the internal elastic lamina of a retinal capillary blood vessel. The lesions present as small circular, red dots having distinct margins and are no larger than a blood vessel width at the disk margin. This expansion disturbs the normal flow pattern, changing shear force and pressure along the vessel. Shear force plays a key role in promoting the differentiation and proliferation of endothelial cells.

name: periglomerular fibrosis
periglomerular fibrosis
HP:0032417.def: Circumferential fibrosis in the interstitium surrounding Bowman's capsule

name: abnormal hdl subfraction concentration
abnormal hdl subfraction concentration
HP:0032418.def: An abnormal concentration of an HDL subfraction, which can be determined by methods such as electrophoresis followed by densitometric determination of the areas under the peaks. Large HDL subfractions are defined as HDL1 (greater than 12 nm), HDL2b (9.7-12 nm), and HDL2a (8.8-9.69 nm). Small HDL subfractions are defined as HDL3a (8.2-8.79 nm), HDL3b (7.8-8.19 nm), and HDL3c (7.20-7.79 nm).

name: abnormal hdl2a concentration
abnormal hdl2a concentration
HP:0032419.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL2a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.80-9.69 nm.

name: increased hdl2a concentration
increase hdl2a concentration
HP:0032420.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL2a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.80-9.69 nm.

name: decreased hdl2a concentration
decrease hdl2a concentration
HP:0032421.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL2a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.80-9.69 nm.

name: abnormal hdl2b concentration
abnormal hdl2b concentration
HP:0032422.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL2b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 9.7-12 nm.

name: decreased hdl2b concentration
decrease hdl2b concentration
HP:0032423.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL2b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 9.7-12 nm.

name: increased hdl2b concentration
increase hdl2b concentration
HP:0032424.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL2b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 9.7-12 nm.

name: abnormal hdl3a concentration
abnormal hdl3a concentration
HP:0032425.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL3a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.2-8.79 nm.

name: abnormal hdl3b concentration
abnormal hdl3b concentration
HP:0032426.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL3b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.8-8.19 nm.

name: abnormal hdl3c concentration
abnormal hdl3c concentration
HP:0032427.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL3c subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3c particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.20-7.79 nm.

name: increased hdl3a concentration
increase hdl3a concentration
HP:0032428.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL3a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.2-8.79 nm.

name: decreased hdl3a concentration
decrease hdl3a concentration
HP:0032429.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL3a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.2-8.79 nm.

name: increased hdl3b concentration
increase hdl3b concentration
HP:0032430.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL3b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.8-8.19 nm.

name: decreased hdl3b concentration
decrease hdl3b concentration
HP:0032431.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL3b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.8-8.19 nm.

name: increased hdl3c concentration
increase hdl3c concentration
HP:0032432.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL3c subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3c particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.20-7.79 nm.

name: decreased hdl3c concentration
decrease hdl3c concentration
HP:0032433.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL3c subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3c particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.20-7.79 nm.

name: delayed umbilical cord separation
delay umbilical cord separation
HP:0032434.def: Separation of the umbilical cord occurs at an abnormally late timepoint.

name: neonatal omphalitis
neonatal omphalitis
HP:0032435.def: An infection of the umbilicus and/or surrounding tissues occurring in the neonatal period.

name: abnormal circulating c - reactive protein concentration
abnormal circulate c - reactive protein concentration
HP:0032436.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of C-reactive protein in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating c - reactive protein concecntration
reduce circulate c - reactive protein concecntration
HP:0032437.def: An abnormal decrease of the C-reactive protein level in serum.

name: platelet anisocytosis
platelet anisocytosis
HP:0032438.def: Abnormally increased variability in the size of platelets.

name: airborn particle hypersensitivity
airborn particle hypersensitivity
HP:0032439.def: An abnormally increased sensitivity to airborn particles. This can be diagnosed on the basis of the medical history, taking into account seasonality or a relationship to the concentration of airborn particles in the environment of the affected individual. Aerosol challenge is a gold standard of establishment of the symptom. There exist particle hypersensitivity (diesel exhaust, metals, inorganic material) vs. allergen (including pollen dander, etc) hypersensitivity. The responses are usually different and testing for allergen hypersensitivity is done in concert with serum IgE and or skin testing to the suspected allergen.

name: blood group b
blood group b
HP:0032440.def: ABO phenotype B, corresponding to the genotype BO or BB.

name: blood group ab
blood group ab
HP:0032441.def: ABO phenotype AB, corresponding to the genotype AB.

name: blood group o
blood group o
HP:0032442.def: ABO phenotype O, corresponding to the genotype OO.

name: past medical history
past medical history
HP:0032443.def: In a medical encounter, the physician generally will interview the patient about his or her current problem, and may perform additional testing. The past medical history (PMH) in contrast records information about the patient's medical, personal and family history that might be relevant to the presenting illness or to provide optimal clinical management. The PMH generally includes (if relevant) other major illnesses, hospitalizations, surgeries, injuries, allergies, gynecologic and obstetric history, family history, personal history including occupational history, alcohol and drug use, etc.

name: status post organ transplantation
status post organ transplantation
HP:0032444.def: The affected individual has received an organ transplant previous to the current medical encounter.

name: pulmonary cyst
pulmonary cyst
HP:0032445.def: A round circumscribed space within a lung that is surrounded by an epithelial or fibrous wall of variable thickness. A cyst usually has a thin and regular wall (less than 2 mm) and contains air, although some may contain fluid.

name: pulmonary bulla
pulmonary bulla
HP:0032446.def: Pulmonary bullae are rounded focal regions of emphysema with a thin wall which measure more than 1 cm in diameter. They are often subpleural in location and are typically larger in the apices. In some cases, bullae can be very large and result in compression of adjacent lung tissue. A giant bulla is arbitrarily defined as one that occupies at least one third of the volume of a hemithorax. When large, bullae can simulate pneumothorax. The most common cause is paraseptal emphysema but bullae may also be seen in association with centrilobular emphysema.

name: pulmonary bleb
pulmonary bleb
HP:0032447.def: A bleb is a small gas-containing space within the visceral pleura or in the subpleural lung, not larger than 1 cm in diameter. CT findings show a bleb as a thin-walled cystic air space contiguous with the pleura.

name: achlorhydria
achlorhydria
HP:0032448.def: A condition in which production of hydrochloric acid in the stomach is absent.

name: abnormal dermoepidermal hemidesmosome morphology
abnormal dermoepidermal hemidesmosome morphology
HP:0032449.def: An abnormal structure or appearance of hemidesmosomes, multiprotein complexes that facilitate the stable adhesion of basal epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane.

name: positive blood arsenic test
positive blood arsenic test
HP:0032450.def: Detection of arsenic in the blood circulation.

name: oral melanotic macule
oral melanotic macule
HP:0032451.def: Flat, distinct, discolored area of oral mucosal membrane less than 1 cm wide not associated with a change in the thickness or texture of the affected mucosal membrane. The lesions are small, solitary, well-circumscribed and often uniformly pigmented.

name: oral melanoacanthoma
oral melanoacanthoma
HP:0032452.def: Oral melanoacanthoma usually presents as an asymptomatic, ill-defined, rapidly enlarging, macular pigmentation. Although most lesions are heavily pigmented, the coloration may or may not be uniform. Any mucosal site may be affected, but buccal mucosal involvement is most common. Although typically solitary, rare patients may present with multifocal lesions.

name: abnormal lip pigmentation
abnormal lip pigmentation
HP:0032453.def: Abnormal coloring of the lip, whereby the lip discolored, blotchy, or darker or lighter than normal.

name: labial melanotic macule
labial melanotic macule
HP:0032454.def: Flat, distinct, discolored area on the lip less than 1 cm wide not associated with a change in the thickness or texture.

name: reduced granulocyte cd18 level
reduce granulocyte cd18 level
HP:0032455.def: Reduced level of CD18 on the granulocyte surface. This feature can be assessed by flow cytometry.

name: unlayered lissencephaly
unlayered lissencephaly
HP:0032456.def: A type of lissencephaly whereby upon neuropathological examination the cortical plate is severely disorganized with a festooned-like pattern and with neither lamination nor clear demarcation between white and grey matter.

name: 2 - 3 - layered lissencephaly
2 - 3 - layer lissencephaly
HP:0032457.def: Pachygyria-agyria spectrum whereby at neuropathological examination the cortical plate consists of a two-three layered organization made up of a molecular layer, a relatively thin wavy layer with a higher cellular density and a third layer with lower cellularity.

name: narrowing of medullary canal
narrowing of medullary canal
HP:0032458.def: A reduction in diameter and volume of the central cavity of bone where red or yellow bone marrow is located.

name: abnormal phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
abnormal phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
HP:0032459.def: Any deviation from the normal level of the enzyme phosphoribosyl pyrophosphatesynthetase, which catalyzes the synthesis of PP-ribose-P from ATP and ribose-5-phosphate.

name: decreased phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
decrease phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
HP:0032460.def: Abnormally reduced level of the enzyme phosphoribosyl pyrophosphatesynthetase, which catalyzes the synthesis of PP-ribose-P from ATP and ribose-5-phosphate.

name: increased circulating palmitate level
increase circulate palmitate level
HP:0032462.def: An elevation beyond the normal concentration of palmitate (palmitic acid) in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating fibronectin level
reduce circulate fibronectin level
HP:0032463.def: A reduction below the normal concentration of fibronectin the the blood circulation.

name: bladder trabeculation
bladder trabeculation
HP:0032465.def: Muscular projections that protrude into the lumen of the bladder, criss-crossing the walls of the bladder on its inner surface.

name: aplasia of the olfactory bulb
aplasia of the olfactory bulb
HP:0032466.def: Lack of formation (congenital absence) of the olfactory bulb.

name: past obstetric history
past obstetric history
HP:0032467.def: Information about past pregnancies including gravidity (number of times a woman has been pregnant, regardless of the outcome), parity (total number of births), gestational age of births, and medical conditions related to past pregnancies.

name: history of stillbirth
history of stillbirth
HP:0032468.def: One or more previous pregnancies resulted in stillbirth, defined as death of a fetus in the later stages of pregnancy (definitions in the literature vary, with cut-offs ranging from 20 to 28 weeks gestation).

name: anti - asialoglycoprotein receptor antibody positivity
anti - asialoglycoprotein receptor antibody positivity
HP:0032469.def: Presence of autoantibodies against the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) in the blood circulation.

name: monilethrix
monilethrix
HP:0032470.def: The hair shaft has a beaded appearance due to the presence of elliptical nodes that have the diameter of normal hair and are medullated, regularly separated by internodes that are narrow, devoid of medulla and are the site of fracture.

name: focal polymicrogyria
focal polymicrogyria
HP:0032471.def: Polymicrogyria affecting one or multiple small areas of the cerebral cortex.

name: abnormal urine urobilinogen level
abnormal urine urobilinogen level
HP:0032472.def: An abnormal concentration of urobilinogen in the urine.

name: decreased urine urobilinogen
decrease urine urobilinogen
HP:0032473.def: An abnormally reduced concentration of urobilinogen in the urine.

name: abnormal circulating vitamin b6 level
abnormal circulate vitamin b6 level
HP:0032476.def: An abnormal concentration of vitamin B6 in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating vitamin b6 level
elevate circulate vitamin b6 level
HP:0032477.def: An abnormally increased concentration of vitamin B6 in the blood circulation.

name: lateral spinal meningocele
lateral spinal meningocele
HP:0032478.def: Protrusion of the arachnoid and dura through spinal foramina.

name: preimplantation lethality
preimplantation lethality
HP:0032479.def: It is estimated that about 40-70 percent of human embryos produced in vitro fertilization (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) are viable embryos, whereas others arrest at different early stages of development. The phenotype of preimplantation lethality is inferred if IVF and ICSI cycles fail because all of an individual's embryos are arrested at early stages of development.

name: beta - aminoisobutyric aciduria
beta - aminoisobutyric aciduria
HP:0032480.def: An increased amount of beta-aminoisobutyric acid in the urine. Beta-aminoisobutyric acid is a non-protein amino acid originating from the catabolism of thymine and valine.

name: abnormal pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
abnormal pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
HP:0032481.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of circulating alpha polypeptide of glycoprotein hormones (NCBI Gene 1081).

name: decreased pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
decrease pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
HP:0032482.def: An reduced concentration of circulating alpha polypeptide of glycoprotein hormones (NCBI Gene 1081).
synonym: decreased pituitary glycoprotein alpha subunit level
decrease pituitary glycoprotein alpha subunit level
decreased pituitary glycoprotein polypeptide alpha subunit level
decrease pituitary glycoprotein polypeptide alpha subunit level

name: elevated fecal sodium
elevated fecal sodium
HP:0032484.def: An elevated concentration of sodium in feces.

name: abnormal fecal osmolality
abnormal fecal osmolality
HP:0032485.def: Abnormal concentration of feces as assessed by the total number of solute particles per kilogram.

name: elevated fecal osmolality
elevated fecal osmolality
HP:0032486.def: Abnormally high concentration of feces as assessed by the total number of solute particles per kilogram.

name: reduced fecal osmolality
reduce fecal osmolality
HP:0032487.def: Abnormally low concentration of feces as assessed by the total number of solute particles per kilogram.

name: abnormal fecal ph
abnormal fecal ph
HP:0032488.def: Any deviation from the normal pH of feces. The pH reflects the acidity or alkalinity of a solution on a logarithmic scale on which 7 is neutral, whereby lower values are more acid and higher values more alkaline.

name: elevated fecal ph
elevated fecal ph
HP:0032489.def: Abnormally high fecal pH, i.e., abnormal alkalinity of feces.

name: decreased fecal ph
decreased fecal ph
HP:0032490.def: Abnormally low fecal pH, i.e., abnormal acidity of feces.

name: increased circulating argininosuccinic acid
increase circulate argininosuccinic acid
HP:0032491.def: An increased level of the non-proteinogenic amino acid argininosuccinic acid in the blood circulation.

name: anti - myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody positivity
anti - myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody positivity
HP:0032492.def: Presence of antibodies in the serum that react against myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein.

name: increased circulating trypsinogen
increase circulating trypsinogen
HP:0032493.def: An abnormally high concentration of trypsinogen in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal terminal : vellus ratio
abnormal terminal : vellus ratio
HP:0032495.def: A deviation from the normal proportion of terminal to vellus hairs.

name: elevated terminal : vellus ratio
elevate terminal : vellus ratio
HP:0032496.def: An increased proportion of terminal hairs compared to vellus hairs.

name: reduced terminal : vellus ratio
reduce terminal : vellus ratio
HP:0032497.def: A terminal:vellus ratio under 4:1 is characteristic of androgenetic alopecia.

name: giant neutrophil granules
giant neutrophil granule
HP:0032499.def: The presence of abnormally large granules in neutrophils. This finding can be appreciated on a peripheral blood smear. The finding is characteristic of Chediak Higashi syndrome. The giant granules are derived from azurophil granules, whereas peroxidase-negative granules are not involved in their formation.

name: exacerbated by tobacco use
exacerbate by tobacco use
HP:0032500.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by smoking tobacco products.
synonym: smoking or tobacco use exacerbates symptoms
smoking or tobacco use exacerbate symptom

name: exacerbated by contraceptive medication exposure
exacerbate by contraceptive medication exposure
HP:0032501.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by taking contraceptive medication.

name: exacerbated by barbiturate exposure
exacerbate by barbiturate exposure
HP:0032502.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by taking barbituates.

name: ameliorated by ethanol ingestion
ameliorate by ethanol ingestion
HP:0032503.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by drinking alcohol (ethanol).

name: lhermitte 's sign
lhermitte 's sign
HP:0032504.def: An electric shock-like sensation that occurs on flexion of the neck. This sensation radiates down the spine, often into the legs, arms, and sometimes to the trunk.

name: hydrophobia
hydrophobia
HP:0032505.def: Pharyngeal spasms that are provoked by an attempt to drink.

name: alien limb phenomenon
alien limb phenomenon
HP:0032506.def: Alien limb phenomenon refers to involuntary motor activity of a limb in conjunction with the feeling of estrangement from that limb.

name: labiomental fasciculations
labiomental fasciculation
HP:0032507.def: Fasciculations affecting the tongue muscle and the musculature of the chin.

name: polyembolokoilamania
polyembolokoilamania
HP:0032508.def: Habitual insertion of foreign bodies into bodily orifices.

name: onychotillomania
onychotillomania
HP:0032509.def: Onychotillomania is characterized by the compulsive or irresistible urge in patients to pick at, pull off, or harmfully bite or chew their nails.

name: tendon pain
tendon pain
HP:0032510.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to a tendon.

name: superiorly positioned umbilicus
superiorly position umbilicus
HP:0032511.def: The position of the umbilicus (belly button) is abnormally high (superior).

name: four - vessel umbilical cord
four - vessel umbilical cord
HP:0032513.def: Four-vessel umbilical cord containing two arteries and two veins.

name: duplicated lacrimal punctum
duplicate lacrimal punctum
HP:0032514.def: A congenital developmental anomaly characterized by the presence of two (instead of the normal one) lacrimal punctum on one or both sides of the face.

name: deep dermatophytosis
deep dermatophytosis
HP:0032515.def: A type of invasive dermatophyte infection of the deep dermis characterized by extensive dermal infiltration by fungal elements.

name: invasive dermatophyte infection
invasive dermatophyte infection
HP:0032516.def: Infection that extends deeply into the dermis by dermatophytes, fungi that typically cause different types of superficial infection (tinea) or skin, hair, or nails.

name: majocchi 's granuloma
majocchi 's granuloma
HP:0032517.def: Majocchi's granuloma (MG) is an inflammatory and granulomatous, dermatophytic infection characterized by a granulomatous inflammation around the hair follicle. Histopathologically, MG demonstrates a nodular perifollicular granulomatous infiltrate of lymphoid cells, macrophages, epithelioid cells, multinucleated giant cells, and neutrophils. Unlike superficial dermatophytoses, fungal hyphae and spores can be detected not only on the surface of the epidermis but also within or around the hair follicles.

name: disseminated dermatophytosis
disseminate dermatophytosis
HP:0032518.def: A type of invasive dermatophyte infection characterized by vascular involvement and dissemination to other organs.

name: increased burr cell count
increase burr cell count
HP:0032519.def: Burr cells, also known as echinocytes, have a speculated border over the entire cell surface. Burr cells are commonly found in both end-stage renal disease and liver disease. Small numbers of Burr cells are commonly found in healthy individuals.

name: masseter muscular weakness
masseter muscular weakness
HP:0032520.def: Reduced strength of the masseter muscle, whose primary function is to elevate the mandible and thereby raise the mandible towards the maxilla, closing the jaw.

name: self hugging
self hugging
HP:0032521.def: Involuntary, tic-like movements consisted of crossing both arms across the chest and tensing the body or clasping the hands and squeezing the arms to the sides. The movements last a few seconds and may occur in series or flurries, generally accompanied by facial grimacing and occasional grunting.

name: ameliorated by immunosuppresion
ameliorate by immunosuppresion
HP:0032522.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with immunosuppresive medication.

name: tendon thickening
tendon thicken
HP:0032523.def: An abnormal increase in the thickness (diameter) of a tendon.

name: long thumb
long thumb
HP:0032524.def: Length of the thumb is greater than normal.

name: exacerbated by acetylcholinesterase inhibitor exposure
exacerbate by acetylcholinesterase inhibitor exposure
HP:0032525.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor such as tensilon (edrophonium) or pyridostigmine (Mestinon).

name: ameliorated by acetylcholinesterase inhibitor
ameliorate by acetylcholinesterase inhibitor
HP:0032526.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor such as mestinon or tensilon.

name: inferiorly positioned umbilicus
inferiorly position umbilicus
HP:0032527.def: The position of the umbilicus (belly button) is abnormally low (inferior).

name: elevated urinary 4 - hydroxybutyric acid
elevate urinary 4 - hydroxybutyric acid
HP:0032528.def: An increased amount of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the urine.

name: obsolete elevated circulating gamma - aminobutyric acid concentration
obsolete elevate circulate gamma - aminobutyric acid concentration
decreased succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase level
decrease succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase level
HP:0032530.def: Reduced level of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH).

name: elevated csf gamma - aminobutyric acid concentration
elevate csf gamma - aminobutyric acid concentration
synonym: gamma - aminobutyric acid ( gaba ) high in csf
gamma - aminobutyric acid ( gaba ) high in csf

name: elevated csf 4 - hydroxybutyric acid concentration
elevate csf 4 - hydroxybutyric acid concentration
HP:0032532.def: Abnormally increased level of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: elevated circulating acetone concentration
elevate circulate acetone concentration
HP:0032533.def: An increased level of acetone in the blood circulation. Acetone is one of the predominant ketone bodies.

name: exacerbated by methylxanthine ingestion
exacerbate by methylxanthine ingestion
HP:0032534.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by ingestion of food containing a methylxanthine compound (for instance, coffee, caffeine, chocolate).

name: cervical ( neck )
cervical ( neck )
HP:0032535.def: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the neck.

name: increased number of lymph nodes
increased number of lymph node
HP:0032536.def: An abnormally elevated number of lymph nodes in an anatomical region.

name: delayed fracture healing
delay fracture heal
HP:0032537.def: A delay in healing of a fracture past the expected duration.

name: pretibial dimple
pretibial dimple
HP:0032538.def: A groove or crease on the shins (pretibial, i.e., over the shin bone). Pretibial creases may be obvious at birth and may range from 3 cm to over 15 cm in length and lenghten as the limb grows. They appear as an elongated dimple because of the attachment of skin to underlying tissue (e.g., to the tibia). The dimple or crease grows in proportion to the growth of the leg.

name: joint extensor surface localization
joint extensor surface localization
HP:0032539.def: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in extensor surface of the joint. The extensor surface refers to the skin on the opposite side of a joint.

name: joint flexor surface localization
joint flexor surface localization
HP:0032540.def: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in flexor surface of the joint. The flexor surface refers to the skin that touches when a joint is bent (flexed).

name: knuckle pad
knuckle pad
HP:0032541.def: Knuckle pads are benign fibrofatty subcutaneous pads located over the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints that can be mistaken for arthritis. Rarely they affect the dorsal aspect of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints. Clinically they are painless and often affect both hands in an asymmetrical pattern.
synonym: knuckle pads on dorsal aspect of finger joints
knuckle pad on dorsal aspect of finger joint

name: exacerbated by pregnancy
exacerbate by pregnancy
HP:0032542.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by being pregnant.

name: lithoptysis
lithoptysis
HP:0032543.def: Expectoration (coughing up) of a broncholith. Broncholithiasis is defined as the presence of calculi in the tracheobronchial tree. It is a rare disease but can be characterized by clinical and radiological findings of a calcified lymph node eroding bronchial wall and opening into the bronchial lumen.

name: predominant small joint localization
predominant small joint localization
HP:0032544.def: Applies to an abnormality that mainly affects the small joints, including fingers, toes, interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal, metatarsophalangeal, wrists, ankles, vertebrae, and neck.

name: abdominal rigidity
abdominal rigidity
HP:0032545.def: Involuntary tightening of the abdominal musculature that occurs in response to touching the abdomen to avoid pain. Rigidity can occur in the presence of abdominal inflammation and usually involves only the inflamed area.

name: abdominal guarding
abdominal guarding
HP:0032546.def: A voluntary contraction of the abdominal wall musculature to avoid pain.

name: low intraocular pressure
low intraocular pressure
HP:0032547.def: An abnormal decrease of the pressure within the eye.

name: persistent asymmetrical tonic neck reflex
persistent asymmetrical tonic neck reflex
HP:0032549.def: Persistence beyond the normal age (roughly the first half of the first year of life) of the asymmetric tonic neck reflex (ATNR), which is an easily elicited primitive reflex in the immediate newborn period. The ATNR refers to the phenomenon whereby when the face of an infant is turned to one side, the ipsilateral arm and leg extend and the contralateral arm and leg flex. This posture has been compared to a typical posture of fencers.
synonym: tonic neck reflex asymmetrical and persistent
tonic neck reflex asymmetrical and persistent

name: howell - jolly bodies
howell - jolly body
HP:0032550.def: Howell-Jolly bodies are small, intra-erythrocytic remnants of erythrocyte nuclei. These inclusions are solitary in each erythrocyte and strongly basophilic. These are often confused with overlying platelets, but can be distinguished by the presence of a halo around overlying platelets.

name: hemorrhoids
hemorrhoid
HP:0032551.def: Enlarged, bulging blood vessels in and around the anus often associated with rectal bleeding, itching, and pain.

name: abnormal pulse
abnormal pulse
HP:0032552.def: An anomaly of the rhythmic throbbing of an artery that reflects the widening of the artery as blood flows through it and is caused by successive contractions of the heart.

name: weak pulse
weak pulse
HP:0032553.def: A diminution in the amplitude (strength) of the pulse such that the examiner has difficulty feeling the pulse.

name: absent pulse
absent pulse
HP:0032554.def: The pulsation of an artery where the pulse is taken (e.g. the radial artery at the wrist) cannot be detected on physical examination.

name: circumoral cyanosis
circumoral cyanosis
HP:0032556.def: Persistent blue color of the skin that surrounds the mouth.

name: history of bone marrow transplant
history of bone marrow transplant
HP:0032557.def: A past medical history of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation involving myeloablative chemoradiotherapy followed by stem cell rescue with autologous or human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-matched stem cells derived from a donor.
synonym: status post haematopoietic stem cell transplantation
status post haematopoietic stem cell transplantation
status post hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
status post hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

name: short sperm flagella
short sperm flagellum
HP:0032559.def: Sperm cells with abnormally short flagella.

name: coiled sperm flagella
coil sperm flagellum
HP:0032560.def: Sperm cells whose flagella are twisted (coiled).

name: microcephalic sperm head
microcephalic sperm head
HP:0032561.def: Decreased size of the head of sperm.

name: tapered sperm head
tapered sperm head
HP:0032562.def: Sperm with cigar-shaped heads that gradually dimish in diameter (taper).

name: dacryocytosis
dacryocytosis
HP:0032563.def: Presence of teardrop-shaped red blood cells.

name: lipiduria
lipiduria
HP:0032567.def: An increased lipid content in the urine.

name: urinary mulberry cells
urinary mulberry cell
HP:0032568.def: Distal tubular epithelial cells in which globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) has accumulated. they are the characteristic feature of Fabry disease. Urinary mulberry bodies are a component of mulberry cells that can be distinguished easily from fat particles by their inner lamellar appearance.

name: temporal bossing
temporal bossing
HP:0032569.def: Prominence (bulging) in the temple region, which is the part of the skull where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones join on the side of the head.

name: pontine ischemic lacunes
pontine ischemic lacunes
HP:0032570.def: Lacunes are infarcts less than 15 mm in diameter in the cortical white matter or in the corona radiata, internal capsule, centrum semiovale, thalamus, basal ganglia, or pons.

name: increased oocyte death
increase oocyte death
HP:0032571.def: An increase in death of oocytes, the female germ cell (egg cell), which can be observed clinically in the setting of in vitro fertilization.

name: abnormal urinary nucleobase concentration
abnormal urinary nucleobase concentration
HP:0032572.def: A deviation from the normal level of a nucleobase in the urine. Nucleobases are nitrogen-containing biological compounds that form nucleosides: adenine (A), cytosine (C), guanine (G), thymine (T), and uracil (U).

name: elevated urinary cytidine
elevate urinary cytidine
HP:0032573.def: Increased levels of urinary cytidine, a pyrimidine nucleoside in which cytosine is attached to ribofuranose via a beta-N1 glycosidic bond.

name: elevated urinary uridine level
elevate urinary uridine level
HP:0032574.def: Increased levels of urinary uridine, a ribonucleoside composed of a molecule of uracil attached to a ribofuranose moiety via a beta-N1 glycosidic bond.

name: decreased circulating 12 - hete
decrease circulate 12 - hete
HP:0032575.def: A reduction in the concentration of 12-HETE in the blood circulation, a metabolite of arachidonic acid.

name: intracellular accumulation of dol - pp - glcnac2man5
intracellular accumulation of dol - pp - glcnac2man5
HP:0032576.def: Intracellular accumulation of the lipid-linked oligosaccharide intermediate Man5GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol.

name: clonal t cell receptor rearrangement
clonal t cell receptor rearrangement
HP:0032577.def: Presence of a predominant T cell clone. In PCR-based assays, this finding is inferred on the basis of one or two prominent bands within a valid size range. In NGS-based assays, this finding is inferred on the basis of a high number of reads that map to a single T cell receptor clone.

name: third ventricle colloid cyst
third ventricle colloid cyst
HP:0032578.def: An epithelial lined cyst filled with gelatinous material. The gelatinous material commonly contains mucin, old blood, cholesterol, and ions. Most colloid cysts identified are currently asymptomatic and identified incidentally on imaging. When a colloid cyst does cause issues, it most commonly causes obstructive hydrocephalus.

name: vascular hamartoma
vascular hamartoma
HP:0032579.def: A benign focal growth composed of vascular tissue.

name: abnormal bulbus cordis morphology
abnormal bulbus cordis morphology
HP:0032580.def: Abnormal structure of the bulbus cordis, which is the single outflow tract of the heart during early embryogenesis.

name: abnormal renal insterstitial morphology
abnormal renal insterstitial morphology
HP:0032581.def: Any structural anomaly of the interstitium of the kidney. The renal interstitium is defined as the intertubular, extraglomerular, extravascular space of the kidney. It is bounded on all sides by tubular and vascular basement membranes and is filled with cells, extracellular matrix, and interstitial fluid.

name: renal interstitial foam cells
renal interstitial foam cell
HP:0032582.def: Accumulation of foam cells (FC) in the interstitium of the kidney. Renal FCs display phenotypic characteristics of macrophages and belong to the monocyte/macrophage lineage. Histologically, renal FCs are characterized by round cells with small nuclei and an abundant PAS-positive cytoplasm with lipid-containing vacuoles.

name: renal interstitial neutrophil infiltration
renal interstitial neutrophil infiltration
HP:0032584.def: Increased numbers of neutrophils in the interstitial tissues of the kidney.

name: renal interstitial eosinophil infiltration
renal interstitial eosinophil infiltration
HP:0032585.def: Increased numbers of eosinophils in the interstitial tissues of the kidney.

name: renal interstitial plasma cell infiltration
renal interstitial plasma cell infiltration
HP:0032586.def: Increased numbers of plasma cells in the interstitial tissues of the kidney.

name: renal interstitial calcium oxalate
renal interstitial calcium oxalate
HP:0032587.def: The presence of birefringent calcium- and oxalate deposits in interstitial cells of the kidney.

name: hand apraxia
hand apraxia
HP:0032588.def: Inability to perform purposeful (learned) movements with the hand upon command, even though the command is understood and there is a willingness to perform the movement. Hand apraxia includes the inability to grasp, pick up, and hold large and small objects.

name: renal lymphocytic tubulitis
renal lymphocytic tubulitis
HP:0032589.def: Infiltration of the renal tubular epithelium by lymphocytes.

name: renal neutrophilic tubulitis
renal neutrophilic tubulitis
HP:0032590.def: Infiltration of the renal tubular epithelium by neutrophils.

name: renal interstitial hemosiderin
renal interstitial hemosiderin
HP:0032591.def: Deposition of hemosiderin (a golden-brown, granular pigment derived from ferritin) in interstitial cells of the kidney.

name: aplasia of the right hemidiaphragm
aplasia of the right hemidiaphragm
HP:0032592.def: Congenital absence of the right-sided diaphragm.

name: myoglobin casts
myoglobin cast
HP:0032593.def: A type of acelluar casts with positive myoglobin staining A that have a surface composed of granules, which can vary in size. The granules can be rather heterogeneous, ranging from fine (finely granular cast) up to coarse (coarsely granular cast), dark, clear, and pigmented.

name: renal tubular basement membrane denudation
renal tubular basement membrane denudation
HP:0032594.def: Naked basement membranes without tubular epithelium.

name: renal tubular epithelial cell detachment
renal tubular epithelial cell detachment
HP:0032595.def: Tubular cross section with a space between the basolateral aspect of tubular epithelium and its basement membrane; classified as global when at least 2/3 circumference of the tubular cross section are involved and segmental when less than 2/3 are involved.

name: renal tubular epithelial cell cytoplasmic vacuolization
renal tubular epithelial cell cytoplasmic vacuolization
HP:0032596.def: Tubular cross section with intracytoplasmic vacuoles in at least one tubular epithelial cell. This feature is classified as isometric when vacuoles are round and similar in size and coarse when vacuoles were not round in shape or varied in size.

name: renal tubular epithelial cell sloughing
renal tubular epithelial cell slough
HP:0032597.def: At least one free floating cell in the tubular lumen without attachment to adjacent cells or basement membrane in a tubular cross section without detachment. These cells must not aggregate into a tubular shape and completely fill the lumen, if so, it should be classified as a cast.

name: blebbing of apical cytoplasm of renal tubular epithelial cells
blebbing of apical cytoplasm of renal tubular epithelial cell
HP:0032598.def: Tubular cross section with round/irregular cytoplasmic protrusion, shaped like the Greek capital letter Omega (or it may be more vertically elongated Omega), pinched off from apical membrane without apparent closure of the lumen, involving over 50 percent of the tubular cells in cross section. The feature can be further classified into proximal or distal tubule.

name: abnormal renal tubular epithelial morphology
abnormal renal tubular epithelial morphology
HP:0032599.def: Any structural anomaly of the renal tubular epithelial cells (RTEC), a layer of cells in the outer layer of the renal tubule. These cells play a role in the absorption of substances such as glucose and amino from the primary urine.

name: renal tubular epithelial cell hyaline droplets
renal tubular epithelial cell hyaline droplet
HP:0032600.def: Tubular epithelium with round strongly PAS-positive cytoplasmic droplet material in at least one tubular epithelial cell.

name: multinucleation of renal tubular epithelial cells
multinucleation of renal tubular epithelial cell
HP:0032601.def: Tubular epithelial cells with greater than 3 nuclei in a single epithelial cell, often overlapping with each other in a single plane of view.

name: prominent nucleoli of renal tubular epithelial cells
