The appearance of feature less decreased attenuation may be indistinguishable from severe constrictive obliterative bronchiolitis.

name: expiratory air trapping
expiratory air trap
HP:0032968.def: Abnormal retention of gas within a lung or part of a lung, as a result of airway obstuction of abnormalities in lung compliance. In the classic presentation, the lung will appear normal at inspiration, but on exhalation, the diseased portions of the lung which have lost connective tissue recoil will remain lucent while the healthy portions of the lung will become more dense due to atelectasis. This helps distinguish it from mosaic attenuation due to patchy fibrosis, as occurs with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia, and in early usual interstitial pneumonitis (the hallmark imaging diagnosis of interstitial lung disease) in which there is no change with inspiration and expiration.

name: traction bronchiectasis
traction bronchiectasis
HP:0032969.def: Distortion of the bronchial airways due to mechanical traction on the bronchi resulting from fibrosis of the surrounding lung parenchyma. CT findings represent irregular bronchial dilatation caused by surrounding retractile pulmonary fibrosis. Dilated airways are usually identifiable as such but may be seen as cysts.

name: computed tomographic halo sign
compute tomographic halo sign
HP:0032971.def: CT finding of ground-glass opacity surrounding a nodule or mass. It was first described as a sign of hemorrhage around foci of invasive aspergillosis. The halo sign is nonspecific and may also be caused by hemorrhage associated with other types of nodules or by local pulmonary infiltration by neoplasm.

name: nodular - centrilobular without tree - in - bud pattern on pulmonary hrct
nodular - centrilobular without tree - in - bud pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP:0032972.def: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography which are anatomically located centrally within secondary pulmonary lobules. Centrilobular nodules may be dense (i.e., solid) and of homogeneous opacity or ground-glass opacity, and may range from a few millimeters to about 1 cm in size. Because of the similar size of secondary lobules, centrilobular nodules often appear to be evenly spaced. Centrilobular nodules are usually separated from the pleural surfaces, fissures, and interlobular septa by a distance of at least several millimeters. They may appear patchy or diffuse in different diseases.

name: abnormal bronchoalveolar lavage fluid morphology
abnormal bronchoalveolar lavage fluid morphology
HP:0032973.def: Abnormal type or counts of nucleated immune cells and acellular components in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid. BAL us performed with a fiberoptic bronchoscope in the wedged position within a selected bronchopulmonary segment. BAL is commonly used to inform the differential diagnosis of interstitial lung disease or to monitor therapeutic interventions.

name: abnormal cellular composition of bronchoalveolar fluid
abnormal cellular composition of bronchoalveolar fluid
HP:0032974.def: Deviation from the commonly in healthy people observe cellular distribution. Normal ranghes are macrophages over 80%, lymphocytes less than 15%, neutrophils less than 3%, eosinophils less than 0.5%, mast cells less than 0.5%.
synonym: abnormal cell differential of broncho - alveolar fluid
abnormal cell differential of broncho - alveolar fluid

name: abnormal bronchoalveolar fluid protein level
abnormal bronchoalveolar fluid protein level
HP:0032975.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of protein in the bronchoalveolar fluid.
synonym: abnormal biochemical composition of broncho - alveolar fluid
abnormal biochemical composition of broncho - alveolar fluid
abnormal level of proteins in the broncho - alveolar fluid
abnormal level of protein in the broncho - alveolar fluid

name: elevated bronchoalveolar lavage fluid lymphocyte proportion
elevate bronchoalveolar lavage fluid lymphocyte proportion
HP:0032976.def: Usually, Lymphoycytes make up less than 15% of all cells found in the bronchoalveloar lavage fluid. This elevated cell proportion can be induced by virus or drugs, or is associated with specific diseases.

name: elevated bronchoalveolar lavage fluid neutrophil proportion
elevate bronchoalveolar lavage fluid neutrophil proportion
HP:0032977.def: Usually, Neutrophils make up less than 3% of all cells found in the broncho-alveloar lavage fluid. In children, standard value of neutrophils is higher depending on their age (children under the age of 5 show a maximum value of 10%). This elevated cell proportion is a sign for acute and chronic infections (HP:0012387, HP:0006538) and can be associated to specific diseases.
synonym: elevated level of neutrophils in broncho - alveolar lavage fluid
elevate level of neutrophil in broncho - alveolar lavage fluid

name: lipid - laden macrophages in bronchoalveolar fluid
lipid - laden macrophage in bronchoalveolar fluid
HP:0032978.def: Accumulation of lipids in alveolar macrophages with droplet-shaped fat inclusions.

name: hemosiderin - laden macrophages in bronchoalveolar fluid
hemosiderin - laden macrophage in bronchoalveolar fluid
HP:0032979.def: Hemosiderin-laden macrophages (HLM) in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid were originally known as adiagnostic biomarker of alveolar hemorrhage, but have also been observed in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) with histopathological pattern of usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP).
synonym: accumulation of hemosiderin laden alveolar macrophages
accumulation of hemosiderin laden alveolar macrophage

name: absent bronchoalveolar surfactant - protein c
absent bronchoalveolar surfactant - protein c
HP:0032980.def: Significantly decreased level or failed detection of surfactant protein C in broncho-alveolar lavage fluid. Comment: Pulmonary surfactant is a highly surface-active mixture of proteins and lipids that is synthesized and secreted onto the alveoli by type II epithelial cells. The protein part of surfactant constitutes of four types of surfactant proteins (SP), SP-A, SP-B, SP-C and SP-D. SP-A and SP-D are hydrophilic proteins that regulate surfactant metabolism and have immunologic functions, whereas SP-B and SP-C are hydrophobic molecules, which play a direct role in the organization of the surfactant structure in the interphase and in the stabilization of the lipid layers during the respiratory cycle. Lack of SP-C may result of surfactant metabolism dysfunction and is also observed in patients with other diffuse parenchymal lung diseaes, pathogenetically related to the alveolar surfactant region.

name: absent bronchoalveolar dimeric surfactant - protein b
absent bronchoalveolar dimeric surfactant - protein b
HP:0032981.def: Significantly decreased level or failed detection of surfactant protein B in broncho-alveolar lavage fluid.

name: atoll sign
atoll sign
HP:0032983.def: CT finding of central ground-glass opacity surrounded by denser consolidation of crescentic shape (forming more than three-fourths of a circle) or complete ring of at least 2 mm in thicknes. A rare sign, it was initially reported to be specific for cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, but was subsequently described in patients with paracoccidioidomycosis.

name: abnormal alveolar macrophage morphology
abnormal alveolar macrophage morphology
HP:0032984.def: Alveolar macrophages usually make up the majority of cells in the bronchoalveolar space (over 80%). The may contain intracellular material depending on underlying diseases or due to exposition to inhaled particles.

name: dust particle inclusion in alveolar macrophages
dust particle inclusion in alveolar macrophage
HP:0032985.def: Accumulation of inhaled, nondigestable particles in macrophages.

name: smoker - inclusions in alveolar macrophages
smoker - inclusion in alveolar macrophage
HP:0032986.def: In otherwise healthy smokers, characteristic so called smoker-inclusion can be found within the macrophages in the bronchoalveolar fluid. These blue/ black/ round/ oval cytoplasmic inclusions consist of pigmented lipid deposits.

name: elevated bronchoalveolar lavage fluid eosinophil proportion
elevate bronchoalveolar lavage fluid eosinophil proportion
HP:0032987.def: Usually, eosinophils make up less than 0.5% of all cells found in the broncho-alveloar lavage fluid. But in eosinophilic lung disease, the eosinophil cell proportion typically represents more than 25%. Comment: An elevated level of eosinophil cells are also a result of infections, or an allergic reaction or can be drug-induced.

name: persistent head lag
persistent head lag
HP:0032988.def: The Premie-Neuro and the Dubowitz Neurological Examination score head lag in the same manner. Scoring for both is as follows: 0 = head drops and stays back, 1 = tries to lift head but drops it back, 2 = able to lift head slightly, 3 = lifts head in line with body, and 4 = head in front of body. This term applies if head lag persists beyond an expected age at a level of 0 or 1. Persistent head lag beyond age 4 mo has been linked to poor outcomes.

name: delayed ability to roll over
delay ability to roll over
HP:0032989.def: Delayed ahcievement of the ability to roll front to back and back to front.

name: localized pulmonary hemorrhage
localize pulmonary hemorrhage
HP:0032990.def: Circumscribed pulmonary hemorrhage originating from a single bleeding site in the lungs. This can be due to infections, tumorigenesis, foreign bodies, or vascular abnormalities. Patient often feel the site of bleeding, contrast CT scan or angiography may localize the bleeder.

name: abnormal pulmonary fissure morphology
abnormal pulmonary fissure morphology
HP:0032991.def: An abnormal form or number of the pulmonary fissures.

name: abnormal pulmonary fissure architecture
abnormal pulmonary fissure architecture
HP:0032992.def: An abnormal form or location of a pulmonary fissure.

name: abnormal pulmonary fissure count
abnormal pulmonary fissure count
HP:0032993.def: A deviation from the normal number of pulmonary fissures.

name: supernumerary pulmonary fissure
supernumerary pulmonary fissure
HP:0032994.def: Presence of a lung fissure that does not exist normally. Supernumerary fissures include the superior accessory fissure, the medial basal fissure, the left horizontal fissure, and the azygos fissure form supernumerary lobes.

name: decreased pulmonary fissure count
decrease pulmonary fissure count
HP:0032995.def: Lack of one or more of the normal pulmonary fissures.

name: abnormal cystatin c level
abnormal cystatin c level
HP:0032996.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of cystatin C in serum or plasma.

name: decreased cystatin c level
decrease cystatin c level
HP:0032997.def: A decreased concentration of cystatin C in the blood circulation.

name: increased cystatin c level
increase cystatin c level
HP:0032998.def: A elevated concentration of cystatin C in the blood circulation.

name: increased fecal porphyrin
increased fecal porphyrin
HP:0032999.def: Abnormally high concentration of fecal porphyrins in feces.

name: subglottic laryngitis
subglottic laryngitis
HP:0033000.def: Narrowing of the larynx, commonly occuring during viral respiratory tract infections, in particular in children, leads to symptoms such as hoarseness, a barking cough, stridor, and sometimes dyspnea and respiratory failure.

name: laryngeal papilloma
laryngeal papilloma
HP:0033001.def: A wart-like lesion (papilloma, i.e., benign epithelial tumors that are caused by infection with the human papilloma virus) located on the larynx.

name: bronchial papilloma
bronchial papilloma
HP:0033002.def: A wart-like lesion (papilloma, i.e., benign epithelial tumors that are caused by infection with the human papilloma virus) located on a bronchus.

name: tracheal papilloma
tracheal papilloma
HP:0033003.def: A wart-like lesion (papilloma, i.e., benign epithelial tumors that are caused by infection with the human papilloma virus) located on the trachea.

name: palmar warts
palmar wart
HP:0033004.def: Multiple verrucous lesions on the skin of the palm. These lesions are raised, have a thickened and rough surface, and may display prominent black dots (thrombosed capillaries). Palmar warts are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV).

name: plantar warts
plantar wart
HP:0033005.def: Multiple verrucous lesions on the skin of the sole of the foot. These lesions are raised, have a thickened and rough surface, and may display prominent black dots (thrombosed capillaries). Palmar warts are caused by caused by human papillomavirus (HPV).

name: diffuse alveolar damage
diffuse alveolar damage
HP:0033006.def: Diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) describes a comon histologic injury pattern of the lung. The early stages are characterized by epithelial cell necrosis and sloughing, fibrous exsudate, edema, and hyaline membranes made of surfactant and proteins, filling the alveoli. This results in impaired gas exchange. In later stages, type II cells and myofibroblasts proliferate within the interstitium and airspaces. The corresponding clinical entity is acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). DAD may result from pulmonary drug toxicity, occurs in immunosuppressed, severe viral infections, acute interstial pneumonitis and crack cocaine inhalation.

name: architectural distortion of the lung
architectural distortion of the lung
HP:0033007.def: Architectural distortion is characterized by abnormal displacement of bronchi, vessels, fissures, or septa caused by diffuse or localized lung disease, particularly interstitial fibrosis. This is visible in lung biopsy and CT scans in a distorted appearance and is usually associated with pulmonary fibrosis and accompanied by volume loss.

name: increased z - disc width
increase z - disc width
HP:0033008.def: Abnormally increased width of the Z-disk of the sarcomere, resulting from splitting or opening of the Z-disc (c.f., Figure 2 of PMID:28732005).

name: increased fecal coproporphyrin 1
increased fecal coproporphyrin 1
HP:0033009.def: Abnormally high concentration of coproporphyrin 1 in feces.

name: increased fecal coproporphyrin 3
increased fecal coproporphyrin 3
HP:0033010.def: Abnormally high concentration of coproporphyrin 3 in feces

name: platystencephaly
platystencephaly
HP:0033011.def: Extreme width of the skull in the occipital region, with anterior narrowing and prognathism.

name: abnormal salivary metabolite concentration
abnormal salivary metabolite concentration
HP:0033012.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a metabolite in saliva.

name: abnormal salivary cortisol level
abnormal salivary cortisol level
HP:0033013.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of cortisol in saliva.

name: decreased salivary cortisol level
decrease salivary cortisol level
HP:0033014.def: Abnormally reduced concentration of cortisol in saliva.

name: increased salivary cortisol level
increase salivary cortisol level
HP:0033015.def: Abnormally elevated concentration of cortisol in saliva.

name: chronic decreased circulating igd
chronic decrease circulate igd
HP:0033016.def: A lasting reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin D (IgD) in the blood.

name: transient decreased circulating igd
transient decrease circulate igd
HP:0033017.def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin D (IgD) in the blood circulation.

name: chronic absent circulating igd
chronic absent circulate igd
HP:0033018.def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin D (IgD) in the blood, whereby at most trace quantities of IgD can be measured.
synonym: chronic ( near ) absent igm in blood
chronic ( near ) absent igm in blood

name: male reproductive system neoplasm
male reproductive system neoplasm
HP:0033019.def: A neoplasm that affects the male reproductive system.

name: female reproductive system neoplasm
female reproductive system neoplasm
HP:0033020.def: A neoplasm that affects the female reproductive system.

name: transient decreased circulating ige
transient decrease circulate ige
HP:0033021.def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin E (IgE) in the blood.

name: chronic decreased circulating ige
chronic decrease circulate ige
HP:0033022.def: A lasting reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin E (IgE) in the blood.

name: chronic absent circulating ige
chronic absent circulate ige
HP:0033023.def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin E (IgE) in the blood circulation, whereby at most trace quantities of IgE can be measured.
synonym: chronic ( near ) absent ige in blood
chronic ( near ) absent ige in blood

name: transient decreased circulating iga
transient decrease circulate iga
HP:0033024.def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin A (IgA) in the blood circulation.

name: chronic absent circulating total igg
chronic absent circulate total igg
HP:0033025.def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood, whereby at most trace quantities of IgG can be measured.
synonym: chronic ( near ) absent total igg in blood
chronic ( near ) absent total igg in blood

name: white oral mucosal macule
white oral mucosal macule
HP:0033026.def: A small circumscribed whitish change in the color of the oral mucosa that is neither elevated nor depressed.

name: retinal peau d'orange
retinal peau d'orange
HP:0033027.def: A pebbly orange appearance of the fundus that is said to resemble the skin of an orange.

name: anti - u1 ribonucleoprotein antibody positivity
anti - u1 ribonucleoprotein antibody positivity
HP:0033028.def: The presence autoantibodies in the serum that react to proteins (70 Kd, A, C) that are associated with U1 RNA and form U1snRNP.

name: anti - glomerular basement membrane - antibody positivity
anti - glomerular basement membrane - antibody positivity
HP:0033030.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react to the glomerular basement membrane.

name: hyperpyrexia
hyperpyrexia
HP:0033031.def: An extreme elevation of core body temperature above normal defined as a rectal temperature of 41.1 degrees Celsius (106 degrees Fahrenheit).

name: triggered by an abusive adult
trigger by an abusive adult
HP:0033032.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is induced by an abusive adult (usually a parent).

name: anti - mda5 antibody positivity
anti - mda5 antibody positivity
HP:0033033.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react to Anti-MDA5 (Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated proteine 5).
synonym: increased level of anti - melanoma differentiation - associated protein 5 antibodies
increase level of anti - melanoma differentiation - associate protein 5 antibody

name: anti - citrullinated protein antibody positivity
anti - citrullinated protein antibody positivity
HP:0033034.def: The presence autoantibodies in the serum that react do different citrullinated antigens, including filaggrin, fibrinogen, vimentin and collagen.

name: abnormal schwann cell morphology
abnormal schwann cell morphology
HP:0033035.def: Abnormality of schwann cells, glial cells that ensheath axons of neurons in the peripheral nervous system and are necessary for their maintenance and function.

name: decreased nasal nitric oxide
decrease nasal nitric oxide
HP:0033036.def: Reduced level of nasal nitric oxide (nNO). Current American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society (ATS/ERS) guidelines for nNO measurements recommend air aspiration via a nasal probe while the subject exhales through the mouth against resistance in order to maintain velum closure.

name: anti - rna - polymerase - iii - autoantibody positivity
anti - rna - polymerase - iii - autoantibody positivity
HP:0033038.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react to RNA-polymerase III.

name: increased circulating precipitin level
increase circulate precipitin level
HP:0033039.def: The presence of high titers of antigen-precipitating IgG in the serum.
synonym: increased level of antigen - precipitating igg antibodies
increase level of antigen - precipitating igg antibody

name: anti - sm antibody positivity
anti - sm antibody positivity
HP:0033040.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react to seven proteins that consist of a core of small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (snRNP) particles.

name: cytokine storm
cytokine storm
HP:0033041.def: Excessive or uncontrolled release of proinflammatory cytokines.

name: abnormal chorion morphology
abnormal chorion morphology
HP:0033042.def: Any structural anomaly of the fetal part of the placenta, which is known as the chorion.

name: edematous chorionic villi
edematous chorionic villus
HP:0033043.def: Swelling of the chorionic villi owing to fluid accumulation.

name: motor regression
motor regression
HP:0033044.def: Loss of previously achieved motor skills, as manifested by loss of developmental motor milestones.

name: bipedal edema
bipedal edema
HP:0033045.def: A palpable swelling in both feet and ankles caused by an increase in interstitial fluid volume (excess fluid).

name: michaelis - gutmann bodies
michaelis - gutmann body
HP:0033046.def: Basophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions in macrophages. The inclusions have a small, round laminated appearance. Electron microscopy of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies exhibits partially digested bacteria.

name: body ache
body ache
HP:0033047.def: Body ache is a complaint that is often used to denote vague symptoms of mild fatigue, lethargy, or dull aches. We will define it here to mean a dull and poorly localizable pain that is described by the affected individual to affect multiple joints or body parts or even the entire body.

name: substantia nigra hypointensity on susceptibility - weighted imaging
substantia nigra hypointensity on susceptibility - weight imaging
HP:0033048.def: Hypointence (dark) appearance of the substantia nigra inmagnetic resonance imaging using susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI).
synonym: low signal intensity in the substantia nigra on susceptibility - weighted imaging ( swi )
low signal intensity in the substantia nigra on susceptibility - weighted imaging ( swi )

name: globus pallidus hypointensity on susceptibility - weighted imaging
globus pallidus hypointensity on susceptibility - weight imaging
HP:0033049.def: Hypointence (dark) appearance of the globus pallidus inmagnetic resonance imaging using susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI).

name: pharyngalgia
pharyngalgia
HP:0033050.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the throat.

name: impaired executive functioning
impaired executive functioning
HP:0033051.def: A disturbance of executive functioning, which is broadly defined as the set of abilities that allow for the planning, executing, monitoring, and self-correcting of goal-directed behavior while inhibiting task-irrelevant behavior. At least some degree of executive skill is needed to complete most cognitive tasks, and deficits in executive abilities are central to many clinical conditions, including fronto-temporal dementia.

name: non - epileptic seizure
non - epileptic seizure
HP:0033052.def: Psychogenic non-epileptic seizures (PNES) are not abnormal perceptions or abnormal beliefs/judgments, nor are they epileptic attacks. They are behaviors that simulate epileptic attacks, not fully consciously.

name: pseudoseizure
pseudoseizure
HP:0033053.def: Sudden, involuntary seizure-like attacks that, unlike epileptic seizures, are not related to electrographic ictal discharges.

name: myoclonic tremor
myoclonic tremor
HP:0033054.def: A tremor-like cortical myoclonus. The tremulous movements are in fact small, high-frequency myoclonic jerks, induced by posture or action. They can be mild, but can also be more incapacitating. When present in the lower limbs, these may lead to gait disorders and even drop attacks. These tremor-like movements during action can be mistaken for essential tremor or epileptic seizures.

name: impaired ability to plan
impaired ability to plan
HP:0033055.def: Impaired ability to anticipate future events, implement instructions or goals, and develop appropriate steps ahead of time in order to carry out a task or activity.

name: impaired ability to organize
impaired ability to organize
HP:0033056.def: Impaired ability to bring order to information, actions, or materials to achieve a goal or to follow an established organized routine.

name: decreased circulating terminal complement component concentration
decrease circulate terminal complement component concentration
HP:0033057.def: Concentration below the lower limit of normal of one or more components of the the terminal membrane attack complex (MAC) portion of complement, which represents the lytic, pore-forming part of the system. The MAC comprises seven components: C5b, C6, C7, C8 (a heterotrimer composed of C8alpha, C8beta and C8gamma) and multiple copies of C9.

name: decreased circulating complement c7 concentration
decrease circulate complement c7 concentration
HP:0033058.def: Concentration of the complement component C7 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: decreased circulating complement c6 concentration
decrease circulate complement c6 concentration
HP:0033059.def: Concentration of the complement component C6 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: decreased circulating complement c5 concentration
decrease circulate complement c5 concentration
HP:0033060.def: Concentration of the complement component C5 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: increased factor ix activity
increase factor ix activity
HP:0033061.def: Elevated activity of coagulation factor IX. Factor IX, which itself is activated by factor Xa or factor VIIa to form factor IXa, activates factor X into factor Xa.

name: abnormal factor ix activity
abnormal factor ix activity
HP:0033062.def: Abnormal activity of coagulation factor IX. Factor IX, which itself is activated by factor Xa or factor VIIa to form factor IXa, activates factor X into factor Xa.

name: shortened sleep phase
shorten sleep phase
HP:0033063.def: A tendency to sleep fewer hours than usual while feeling well-rested.

name: renal interstitial globotriaosylceramide inclusions
renal interstitial globotriaosylceramide inclusion
HP:0033064.def: Accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) in kidney tissues, which can be quantified as the number of globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) inclusions/kidney interstitial capillary (KIC).

name: mild albuminuria
mild albuminuria
HP:0033065.def: The presence of mildly increased concentrations of albumin in the urine, defined as an albumin-creatinine ratio (ACR) less than 30 mg/gm (less than 3.4 mg/mmol).

name: severe albuminuria
severe albuminuria
HP:0033066.def: The presence of severely increased concentrations of albumin in the urine, defined as an albumin-creatinine ratio greater than 300 mg/gm (greater than 34 mg/mmol).

name: medication crystalluria
medication crystalluria
HP:0033068.def: A variety of drugs may occasionally cause transient crystalluria, in isolation or in conjunction with other urinary abnormalities. Overdose, dehydration, or hypoalbuminaemia, which increases the unbound drug which is ultrafiltrated by the glomerulus, are the factors usally favoring the precipitation of crystals within the tubular lumina. In some cases, medication-induced crystalluria has a distinct phenotypic appearance. For instance, Sulphadiazine crystals appear as strongly birefringent 'shocks of wheat' or 'shells' with an amber colour. Acyclovir crystals are birefringent and needle-shaped, and when present in abundance give to urine a silky and opalescent macroscopic appearance.

name: renal interstitial igg4+ plasma cell infiltration
renal interstitial igg4+ plasma cell infiltration
HP:0033069.def: An increased number of IgG4+ plasma cells in the interstitial space of the kidney.

name: impaired self monitoring
impaired self monitoring
HP:0033070.def: Impaired ability to track awareness of the effect that one's behavior has on others and how it compares with standards or expectations for behavior.

name: impaired task monitoring
impaired task monitoring
HP:0033071.def: Impaired ability to keep track of one's problem-solving success or failure, and to identify and correct mistakes during performance of a goal.

name: abnormal macroscopic urine appearance
abnormal macroscopic urine appearance
HP:0033072.def: Anomalous physical appearance (color, cloudiness, clarity) or odor of urine.

name: urate tophus
urate tophus
HP:0033073.def: Intradermal urate crystal deposits appeared as small, superficial, pustule-like, whitish lesions. The lesions may be the focus of inflammatory episodes with increasing pain, swelling, and erythema of the intradermal tophi.

name: steroid - responsive anemia
steroid - responsive anemia
HP:0033074.def: Amelioration of anemia upon treatment with a steroid medication.

name: inappropriately normal thyroid - stimulating hormone level
inappropriately normal thyroid - stimulate hormone level
HP:0033075.def: A normal or elevated serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level in the face of an elevation in circulating FT4 and/or FT3.

name: abnormal circulating free t4 concentration
abnormal circulate free t4 concentration
HP:0033076.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of free thyroxine (T4) in the blood circulation. Circulating T4 is almost entirely bound to specific transport proteins such as thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) but it is the unbound (free) fraction that is able to enter tissues and exert effects.

name: increased circulating free t4 concentration
increase circulate free t4 concentration
HP:0033077.def: An elevated concentration of free thyroxine (fT4) in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating free t4 concentration
decrease circulate free t4 concentration
HP:0033078.def: A reduced concentration of free thyroxine (fT4) in the blood circulation.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the thyroid gland
aplasia / hypoplasia of the thyroid gland
HP:0033079.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the thyroid gland.

name: abnormal tsh response to thyrotrophin - releasing hormone stimulation test
abnormal tsh response to thyrotrophin - release hormone stimulation test
HP:0033080.def: Thyrotrophin-releasing hormone (TRH) is a hypothalamic tripeptide synthesised by, stored within and released from the hypothalamus. It stimulates the synthesis and release of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) from the anterior pituitary gland. Following administration of exogenous TRH, a transient increase in serum TSH is expected. This term refers to an abnormal reponse in the TRH stimulation test.
synonym: abnormal tsh response to trh stimulation test
abnormal tsh response to trh stimulation test

name: absent tsh response to thyrotrophin - releasing hormone stimulation test
absent tsh response to thyrotrophin - release hormone stimulation test
HP:0033081.def: Failure to increase serum TSH levels in response to a TRH stimulation test.

name: reduced tsh response to thyrotrophin - releasing hormone stimulation test
reduce tsh response to thyrotrophin - release hormone stimulation test
HP:0033082.def: A lower than normal TSH response to thyrotrophin-releasing hormone stimulation test.

name: increased circulating farnesol concentration
increase circulate farnesol concentration
HP:0033083.def: An elevated level of farnesol in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal antral follicle count
abnormal antral follicle count
HP:0033084.def: Any deviation from a count of antral follicles that is normal for age. Antral follicles appear as small fluid-filled sacs that contain an immature egg. Antral follicle count can be measured (usually on day 2-5 of the menstrual cycle) by transvaginal ultrasound. The number of antral follicles may reflect ovarian reserve.

name: reduced antral follicle count
reduce antral follicle count
HP:0033085.def: A count of antral follicles that is lower than normal for age.

name: increased antral follicle count
increase antral follicle count
HP:0033086.def: A count of antral follicles that is higher than normal for age.

name: quotidian fever
quotidian fever
HP:0033087.def: Fever that occurs at daily intervals.

name: valinuria
valinuria
HP:0033088.def: Urine valine level above the normal range.

name: branched - chain aminoaciduria
branch - chain aminoaciduria
HP:0033089.def: An increased level of a branched chain family amino acid in the urine.

name: increased aromatic amino acid level in urine
increase aromatic amino acid level in urine
HP:0033090.def: An elevated level of an aromatic amino acid in the urine.

name: tyrosinuria
tyrosinuria
HP:0033091.def: An abnormally increased level of tyrosine in the urine.

name: increased urine succinate level
increase urine succinate level
HP:0033092.def: The concentration of succinate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: increased glutamine family amino acid level in urine
increase glutamine family amino acid level in urine
HP:0033093.def: An elevated level of an glutamine family amino acid in the urine.

name: increased urine glutamate level
increase urine glutamate level
HP:0033094.def: An increased concentration of glutamate in the urine.

name: increased sulfur amino acid level in urine
increase sulfur amino acid level in urine
HP:0033095.def: An elevated level of a sulfur-containing amino acid in the urine.
synonym: increased sulfur - containing amino acid level in urine
increase sulfur - contain amino acid level in urine
increased sulphur amino acid level in urine
increase sulphur amino acid level in urine

name: increased aspartate family amino acid level in urine
increase aspartate family amino acid level in urine
HP:0033096.def: An elevated level of an aspartate family amino acid in the urine.

name: increased urine proteinogenic amino acid derivative level
increase urine proteinogenic amino acid derivative level
HP:0033097.def: An elevated urine level of a compound that is derived from an amino acid.

name: increased urinary non - proteinogenic amino acid level
increase urinary non - proteinogenic amino acid level
HP:0033098.def: An increased level in the urine of an alpha-amino acid which is not a member of the group of 23 proteinogenic amino acids.
synonym: elevated urinary non - proteinogenic amino acid level
elevate urinary non - proteinogenic amino acid level

name: increased serine family amino acid in urine
increase serine family amino acid in urine
HP:0033099.def: An increased level of a serine family amino acid in the urine.

name: increased proteinogenic amino acid level in urine
increase proteinogenic amino acid level in urine
HP:0033100.def: An elevated level of a proteinogenic amino acid in the urine. These are the 23 alpha-amino acids that are precursors to proteins, and are incorporated into proteins during translation. The group includes the 20 amino acids encoded by the nuclear genes of eukaryotes together with selenocysteine, pyrrolysine, and N-formylmethionine.

name: elevated urine aconitic acid level
elevate urine aconitic acid level
HP:0033101.def: An abnormally increased level of aconitic acid in the urine.

name: monkey wrench femoral neck
monkey wrench femoral neck
HP:0033102.def: The femoral neck region shows medial metaphyseal beaking and a significant enlargement of the lesser trochanter (with some enlargement also of the greater trochanter), producing a monkey wrench (Swedish key) configuration of the proximal femur. A monkey wrench refers to a type of adjustable wrench with one fixed and one adjustable jaw at right angles to a straight handle.
synonym: monkey wrench appearance of femoral neck
monkey wrench appearance of femoral neck
monkey wrench configuration of the proximal femur
monkey wrench configuration of the proximal femur
swedish key appearance of femoral neck
swedish key appearance of femoral neck
swedish key configuration of the proximal femur
swedish key configuration of the proximal femur

name: elevated circulating chi3l1 level
elevate circulate chi3l1 level
HP:0033103.def: Increased concentration of chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1) in the blood circulation.

name: inappropriate absence of fever
inappropriate absence of fever
HP:0033104.def: Failure to develop fever in the presence of an infection that normally would be expected to elicit a febrile response.

name: interhypothalamic adhesion
interhypothalamic adhesion
HP:0033105.def: An abnormal parenchymal band connecting the medial margins of the left and right hypothalami across the third ventricle.

name: elevated circulating d - dimer concentration
elevate circulate d - dimer concentration
HP:0033106.def: An increased concentration of D-dimers, a marker of fibrin degradation, in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating proteinogenic amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate proteinogenic amino acid concentration
HP:0033107.def: An elevated level of a proteinogenic amino acid in the blood circulation. These are the 23 alpha-amino acids that are precursors to proteins, and are incorporated into proteins during translation. The group includes the 20 amino acids encoded by the nuclear genes of eukaryotes together with selenocysteine, pyrrolysine, and N-formylmethionine.

name: abnormal circulating proteinogenic amino acid derivative concentration
abnormal circulate proteinogenic amino acid derivative concentration
HP:0033108.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of a compound that is derived from an amino acid.

name: abnormal circulating non - proteinogenic amino acid concentration
abnormal circulate non - proteinogenic amino acid concentration
HP:0033109.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of an alpha-amino acid which is not a member of the group of 23 proteinogenic amino acids.

name: elevated circulating alpha - aminobutyric acid concentration
elevate circulate alpha - aminobutyric acid concentration
HP:0033110.def: An abnormally increased level of alpa-aminobutyric acid in the blood circulation. Alpha-aminobutyric acid alpha-amino acid that is butyric acid bearing a single amino substituent located at position 2.

name: 3 - hydroxyisovaleric aciduria
3 - hydroxyisovaleric aciduria
HP:0033111.def: Concentration of 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid in the urine above the normal range.

name: elevated circulating apolipoprotein c - iii concentration
elevate circulate apolipoprotein c - iii concentration
HP:0033112.def: An increased concentration in blood of apolipoprotein C-III, a protein component of triglyceride (TG)-rich lipoproteins (TRLs) including very low density lipoproteins (VLDL), high density lipoproteins (HDL) and chylomicrons.

name: gallop rhythm
gallop rhythm
HP:0033113.def: In the normal heart cycle, two heart sounds can be heard by auscultation per cycle: S1 and S2. A gallop rhythm refers to the presence of three or four heart sounds per cardiac cycle, which is said to resemble the gallop of a horse.

name: quadruple gallop rhythm
quadruple gallop rhythm
HP:0033114.def: A type of gallop rhytm in which both the third and the fourth sounds are present.

name: elevated circulating tenascin - c level
elevate circulate tenascin - c level
HP:0033115.def: Abnormally increased concentration of tenascin-C in the blood circulation.

name: duodenal gastric metaplasia
duodenal gastric metaplasia
HP:0033116.def: Foci of gastric-type mucus-secreting cells interspersed between duodenal enterocytes. These foci of gastric epithelial cells contain Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive neutral mucin and lack a brush border.

name: duodenitis
duodenitis
HP:0033117.def: Inflammation of the lining of the upper small intestine (duodenum).

name: abnormal right ventricular function
abnormal right ventricular function
HP:0033118.def: Anomalous physiology (function) of the right ventricle.

name: elevated right ventricular systolic pressure
elevate right ventricular systolic pressure
HP:0033119.def: Elevation of right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) above normal limits. In adults, RVSP is normally 20-30 mmHg.

name: nummular eczema
nummular eczema
HP:0033120.def: A type of eczema characterized by pruritic coin-shaped patches on the skin. Nummular eczema most commonly occurs on the extremities, particularly the legs, but may occur anywhere on the trunk, hands, or feet

name: barking cough
barking cough
HP:0033121.def: A cough with a characteristic sound that has been compared to a seal's bark.

name: absent p wave
absent p wave
HP:0033122.def: The P wave that normally precedes each QRS complex by a fixed PR interval of 120 to 200 milliseconds is not present.
synonym: absence of p wave on electrocardiography
absence of p wave on electrocardiography

name: elevated circulating osteopontin level
elevate circulate osteopontin level
HP:0033123.def: Abnormally increased level of osteopontin in the blood circulation

name: increased serum sorbitol concentration
increase serum sorbitol concentration
HP:0033124.def: An increased level of sorbitol in the blood circulation.

name: follicular lymphoma
follicular lymphoma
HP:0033125.def: An indolent B cell lymphoproliferative disorder of transformed follicular center B cells. Follicular lymphoma is characterized by diffuse lymphadenopathy, bone marrow involvement, splenomegaly and less commonly other extranodal sites of involvement.

name: cutaneous necrosis
cutaneous necrosis
HP:0033126.def: Skin and subcutaneous tissue necrosis (tissue death). Clinically, cutaneous necrosis may present as a painful and extremely tender black eschar (dead tissue found in a full-thickness wound) surrounded by dusky grey-red coloured skin.

name: abnormality of the musculoskeletal system
abnormality of the musculoskeletal system
HP:0033127.def: An anomaly of the musculoskeletal system, which consists of the bones of the skeleton, muscles, cartilage, tendons, ligaments, joints, and other connective tissue. The musculoskeletal system supports the weight of the body, maintains body position and produces movements of the body or of parts of the body.

name: delayed ability to crawl
delay ability to crawl
HP:0033128.def: A failure to achieve the ability to crawl at an appropriate developmental stage. Normal infant motor development is marked by a series of postural milestones including learning to crawl on hands and knees between the ages of 6 and 10 months.

name: abnormal shoulder physiology
abnormal shoulder physiology
HP:0033129.def: Anopmalous function of the shoulder. The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint that is made up of humerus, scapula and clavicle, which are connected by the sternoclavicular joint (SC), the acromioclavicular joint (AC), the glenohumeral joint (GH), and the scapulothoracic joint (ST). The GH, AC and SC joints link the upper extremity to the axial skeleton at the thorax and enable movement at the shoulder joint: flexion, extension, and rotation of the arm.

name: abnormal renal echogenicity
abnormal renal echogenicity
HP:0033130.def: Anomalous echogenicity of the kidney on ultrasound examination.

name: renal medullary hyperechogenicity
renal medullary hyperechogenicity
HP:0033131.def: Increased echogenecity of the medullary region of the kidney.

name: renal cortical hyperechogenicity
renal cortical hyperechogenicity
HP:0033132.def: Increased echogenecity of the kidney cortex.

name: abdominal adhesions
abdominal adhesion
HP:0033134.def: Fibrous bands (i.e., bands of scar-like tissue) that span two or more intra-abdominal organs and/or the inner abdominal wall (i.e. peritoneal membrane).

name: hepatic infarction
hepatic infarction
HP:0033135.def: Hepatic infarction is defined as areas of coagulative necrosis from hepatocyte cell death caused by local ischemia. Liver infarctions appear as hypoechoic nonvascular regions on conventional and Doppler sonography.

name: lymph node abscess
lymph node abscess
HP:0033136.def: An inflammed lymph node that is filled with pus.

name: abnormal pulmonary alveolar system morphology
abnormal pulmonary alveolar system morphology
HP:0033137.def: A structural abnormality of the pulmonary acinus, alveolar parenchyma, or alveoli.

name: right atrial thrombus
right atrial thrombus
HP:0033138.def: A thrombus (i.e., a blood clot formed in situ within the vascular system) located in the right atrium of the heart.

name: elevated circulating uracil concentration
elevate circulate uracil concentration
HP:0033139.def: Concentration of uracil in the blood circulation is above the normal range.

name: blake 's pouch cyst
blake 's pouch cyst
HP:0033140.def: The presence of an upwardly displaced normal cerebellar vermis, normal appearance of the fastigium, tentorium and size of the cisterna magna.

name: severe sars - cov - 2 infection
severe sars - cov - 2 infection
HP:0033141.def: Unusually severe clinical course of SARS-CoV-2 infection, manifested clinically by features such as dyspnea and hypoxia with diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities of the lungs on computed tomographic scan with progressive respiratory insufficiency necessitating oxygen supplementation or mechanical ventilation.

name: long nasal bridge
long nasal bridge
HP:0033142.def: Increased superior-inferior length of the nasal bridge, which is the saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose.

name: jejunitis
jejunitis
HP:0033143.def: Inflammation of the lining of the middle section of the small intestine.

name: abnormal circulating ceruloplasmin concentration
abnormal circulate ceruloplasmin concentration
HP:0033144.def: Any deviation of the concentration of ceruloplasmin in the blood from the normal range.

name: increased circulating ceruloplasmin concentration
increase circulate ceruloplasmin concentration
HP:0033145.def: Elevated concentration of ceruloplasmin in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating methylsuccinic acid concentration
elevate circulate methylsuccinic acid concentration
HP:0033146.def: Increased concentration of methylsuccinic acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating short - chain fatty - acid concentration
abnormal circulate short - chain fatty - acid concentration
HP:0033147.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a short-chain fatty acid in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating isovaleric acid concentration
increase circulate isovaleric acid concentration
HP:0033148.def: Increased concentration of isovaleric acid, a C5, branched-chain saturated fatty acid, in the blood concentration.

name: intrahepatic bile duct dilatation
intrahepatic bile duct dilatation
HP:0033149.def: Increased diameter (caliber) of intrahepatic bile ducts (bile ducts that transport bile between the Canals of Hering and the interlobar bile ducts).

name: anorectal abscess
anorectal abscess
HP:0033150.def: An abscess located at the junction of the anal canal and the rectum.

name: abnormal pharynx morphology
abnormal pharynx morphology
HP:0033151.def: A structural anomaly of the pharynx.

name: abnormal pharynx physiology
abnormal pharynx physiology
HP:0033152.def: A functional anomaly of the pharynx.

name: elevated circulating dodecenoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate dodecenoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033153.def: An abnormally increased circulation of dodecenoylcarnitine, C12:1, in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating deoxypyridinoline concentration
elevate circulate deoxypyridinoline concentration
HP:0033154.def: An increased concentration of lysyl-pyridinoline (deoxypyridinoline) cross-links in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating l - alloisoleucine concentration
elevate circulate l - alloisoleucine concentration
HP:0033155.def: Abnormally increased concentration of L-alloisoleucine in the blood circulation.

name: elevated urine l - alloisoleucine level
elevate urine l - alloisoleucine level
HP:0033156.def: Abnormally increased level of L-alloisoleucine in the urine.

name: elevated circulating 3 - methylhistidine concentration
elevate circulate 3 - methylhistidine concentration
HP:0033157.def: Abnormal increase of the concentration of 3-methylhistidine in the blood circulation.

name: reduced respiratory ciliary beating frequency
reduce respiratory ciliary beating frequency
HP:0033158.def: An abnormal reduction in the number of beats per unit time of the respiratory cilia.

name: reduced urinary inosine level
reduce urinary inosine level
HP:0033159.def: Decreased level of inosine in urine. Inosine is a purine nucleoside in which hypoxanthine is attached to ribofuranose via a beta-N(9)-glycosidic bond.

name: decreased urinary guanosine level
decrease urinary guanosine level
HP:0033160.def: Decreased level of guanosine in urine. Guanosine is a purine nucleoside in which guanine is attached to ribofuranose via a beta-N(9)-glycosidic bond.

name: abnormal urinary purine level
abnormal urinary purine level
HP:0033161.def: Any deviation from the normal amount of a purine compound in the urine. Purines are aromatic heterocyclic compounds containing a purine moiety, which is formed a pyrimidine-ring ring fused to an imidazole ring. Two of the four deoxyribonucleotides (deoxyadenosine and deoxyguanosine) and two of the four ribonucleotides (adenosine, or AMP, and guanosine, or GMP) are purines.

name: abnormal urinary pyrimidine level
abnormal urinary pyrimidine level
HP:0033162.def: Any deviation from the normal amount of a pyrimidine compound in the urine. Pyrimidines and pyrimidine derivatives are compounds containing a pyrimidne ring, which is a six-member aromatic heterocycle which consists of two nitrogen atoms (at positions 1 and 3) and four carbon atoms. The nucleotides cytosine, thymine and uracil are pyrimidines.

name: small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
HP:0033163.def: An increased number and/or abnormal type of bacteria in the small bowel. Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth has been defined as the presence of greater than one hundred thousand bacteria (i.e. colony-forming units, CFU) per mL of proximal jejunal aspiration. The normal value is ten thousand or few CFU/ml.

name: focal active colitis
focal active colitis
HP:0033164.def: Focal active colitis (FAC) is characterized by focal crypt damage caused by neutrophils. FAC is characterized by an inflammatory infiltrate consisting of intraepithelial neutrophils and/or neutrophils invading the lumen of the criptae, with no other microscopic alteration of the colonic mucosa and, in particular, without the presence of signs of chronic inflammation.

name: necrotizing enterocolitis
necrotizing enterocolitis
HP:0033165.def: Inflammation of the intestine leading to bacterial invasion causing cellular damage and death which causes necrosis of the colon and intestine.

name: recurrent viral upper respiratory tract infections
recurrent viral upper respiratory tract infection
HP:0033166.def: An increased susceptibility to viral upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent viral upper respiratory tract infections (otitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis).

name: neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis
neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis
HP:0033167.def: A neutrophilic interstitial, perivascular and/or perieccrine infiltrate with leukocytoclasia. Notably, leukocytoclastic vasculitis is not present.

name: reduced mevalonate kinase activity
reduce mevalonate kinase activity
HP:0033168.def: Abnormally reduced activity of mevalonate kinase, which is a key enzyme in the mevalonate biosynthetic pathway that leads to the synthesis of both cholesterol and nonsterol isoprenoids.

name: reduced total lung capacity
reduce total lung capacity
HP:0033169.def: Abnormally reduced volume of air in the lungs upon the maximum effort of inspiration.

name: abnormal skinfold thickness measurement
abnormal skinfold thickness measurement
HP:0033170.def: Any deviation from the normal range of a skinfold thickness, which quantifies the amount of subcutaneous fat when the skin is pinched by specialized calipers.

name: abnormal triceps skinfold thickness
abnormal triceps skinfold thickness
HP:0033171.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the thickness of the tricpes skinfold, which quantifies the amount of subcutaneous fat when the skin is pinched by specialized calipers.

name: increased triceps skinfold thickness
increase triceps skinfold thickness
HP:0033172.def: Increased thickness of the triceps skinfold, which is measured halfway down the back of the upper arm is increased.

name: milky appearance of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
milky appearance of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
HP:0033173.def: Return of lavage fluid with a milky apperance due to the accumulation of a mixture of pulmonary surfactant, which is a lipoprotein complex, in the alveolar space.

name: bloody bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
bloody bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
HP:0033174.def: Return of lavage fluid characteristically has a bloody apperance in pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage. This is due to admixture of blood, which typically increases with each consecutive lavage portion. Microscopically erythrocytes can be seen. After 24 to 48 h macrophages contain phagocytosed erythrocytes, indicating previous bleeding.

name: elevated circulating 5 - oxoproline concentration
elevate circulate 5 - oxoproline concentration
HP:0033175.def: Concentration of L-pyroglutamic acid in the blood is above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: elevated circulating l - pyroglutamic acid concentration
elevate circulate l - pyroglutamic acid concentration

name: submandibular lymph node enlargement
submandibular lymph node enlargement
HP:0033176.def: Increased size of the lymph nodes that are located beneath the mandible (lower jaw).

name: elevated circulating suberic acid concentration
elevate circulate suberic acid concentration
HP:0033177.def: An increased concentration of suberic acid in the blood circulation. Suberic acid is an alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid that is the 1,6-dicarboxy derivative of hexane.

name: increased circulating interleukin 8 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 8 concentration
HP:0033178.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-8 in the circulation.

name: elevated circulating aconitic acid concentration
elevate circulate aconitic acid concentration
HP:0033179.def: Concentration of aconitic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: torsion of appendix of testis
torsion of appendix of testis
HP:0033180.def: The appendix testis or hydatid of Morgagni, is a vestigial remnant of the Müllerian duct located on the superior pole of the testicle between the testis and epididymis. Although this appendage has no vital function, it is present in 50% of males. Torsion of twisting of this vestigial remnant can be incredibly painful, but usually requires no medical intervention.
synonym: twisted vestigial remnant of the muellerian duct
twist vestigial remnant of the muellerian duct

name: spinal epidural abscess
spinal epidural abscess
HP:0033181.def: Spinal epidural abscess (SEA) is caused by a suppurative infection in the epidural space. The mass effect of the abscess can compress and reduce blood flow to the spinal cord, conus medullaris, or cauda equina.
synonym: a severe pyogenic infection of the epidural space
a severe pyogenic infection of the epidural space

name: increased circulating cathepsin d level
increase circulate cathepsin d level
HP:0033182.def: An increase in concentration of cathepsin D in the blood circulation.

name: bilobed right lung
bilobed right lung
HP:0033183.def: A developmental defect of pulmonary lobation characterized by the presence of only two lobes of the right lung.

name: triggered by ebv infection
trigger by ebv infection
HP:0033185.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by infection by the Epstein-Barr virus.
synonym: triggered by epstein barr virus infection
trigger by epstein barr virus infection

name: misalignment of the pulmonary veins
misalignment of the pulmonary vein
HP:0033186.def: The term is commonly used to describe a putative abnormal location of pulmonary vein branches adjacent to pulmonary arteries within the same adventitial sheath. However, evidence has been provided that the vessels in question are not pulmonary veins, however represent dilated bronchial veins.

name: hyperimidodipeptiduria
hyperimidodipeptiduria
HP:0033187.def: Elevated levels of proline-containing dipeptides in urine.

name: cystic acne
cystic acne
HP:0033188.def: A severe type of acne characterized by the formation of cysts enclosing a mixture of keratin and sebum.

name: radiculomegaly
radiculomegaly
HP:0033189.def: Tooth root length more than 2 SD above mean, or subjectively apparently increased tooth root length.

name: hypertrichotic hyperpigmented patch
hypertrichotic hyperpigmented patch
HP:0033190.def: A large nonpalpable spot of the skin over 1 cm in dimension with increased pigmentation and increased hair growth.

name: increased circulating selenium concentration
increase circulate selenium concentration
HP:0033191.def: An increased concentration of selenium in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating selenium concentration
decrease circulate selenium concentration
HP:0033192.def: An abnormally reduced concentration of selenium in the blood circulation.

name: ballooning hepatocyte degeneration
ballooning hepatocyte degeneration
HP:0033193.def: Swelling of the hepatocyte, rounding of its contour, and alteration of the cytoplasm, which takes on a reticulated, rarified, or flocculant quality. The cytoplasm of the ballooned hepatocytes often contains clumps of eosinophilic ropey material known as Mallory-Denk bodies (MDBs) or Mallory hyaline, which is composed of hyperphosphorylated misfolded intermediate filaments, ubiquitin, and ubiquitin-binding protein P62.

name: perioral erythema
perioral erythema
HP:0033194.def: Erythema (Redness of the skin caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin) localized to the region surrounding the mouth.

name: perianal erythema
perianal erythema
HP:0033195.def: Erythema (Redness of the skin caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin) localized to the region surrounding the anus.

name: portal inflammation
portal inflammation
HP:0033196.def: Infiltration of portal fields by inflammatory cells.

name: hepatic lobular inflammation
hepatic lobular inflammation
HP:0033197.def: Infiltration of inflammatory cells in lobules of the liver. A focus of lobular inflammation can be defined as two or more inflammatory cells (neutrophils, lymphocytes and other mononuclear cells, eosinophils and microgranulomas) within the lobule present within the sinusoids or surrounding injured hepatocytes (ballooned or apoptotic hepatocytes).

name: triggered by viral infection
trigger by viral infection
HP:0033198.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by infection by a virus.

name: increased circulating interleukin 10 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 10 concentration
HP:0033199.def: An elevation of the concentration of interleukin 10 in the blood circulation.

name: triceps hyporeflexia
triceps hyporeflexia
HP:0033200.def: Reduced intensity of the triceps tendon reflex.

name: biceps hyporeflexia
biceps hyporeflexia
HP:0033201.def: Reduced intensity of the biceps tendon reflex.

name: brachioradialis hyporeflexia
brachioradialis hyporeflexia
HP:0033202.def: Reduced intensity of the brachioradialis tendon reflex.

name: brachioradialis hyperreflexia
brachioradialis hyperreflexia
HP:0033203.def: Increased intensity of the brachioradialis reflex.

name: triceps hyperreflexia
triceps hyperreflexia
HP:0033204.def: Increased intensity of the triceps reflex.

name: biceps hyperreflexia
biceps hyperreflexia
HP:0033205.def: Increased intensity of the biceps reflex.

name: hyperactive achilles reflex
hyperactive achilles reflex
HP:0033206.def: Increased intensity of the Achilles reflex.

name: increased proportion autoreactive unresponsive cd21 - / low b cells
increase proportion autoreactive unresponsive cd21 - / low b cell
HP:0033207.def: Increased proportion relative to B-lymphocytes of a subset of B lymphocytes characterized by dim/low levels of CD21, i.e., CD21-/low, in flow cytometry, and additionally enriched in autoreactive clones as determined for instance by clonse showing rheumatoid factor (anti-IgG) reactivity and antibodies recognizing cytoplasmic and to a lesser extent nuclear structures.

name: alveolar capillary dysplasia
alveolar capillary dysplasia
HP:0033208.def: A developmental defect of the alveolar airspace during cananicular lung development characterized by a decreased number of pulmonary capillaries located away from the alveolar epithelium, thickened alveolar septae, media hypertrophy of small pulmonary arteries and muscularization of distal arterioles, and in some cases lymphangiectasis.

name: acinar dysplasia
acinar dysplasia
HP:0033209.def: Arrest of lung development in the pseudoglandular stage (weeks 8 to 16 of human gestation) resulting in small sized lungs, predominantly composed of bronchial and bronchiolar structures embedded in abundant loose mesenchyme that is poorly vascularized. Acinar structures are essentially absent, with no significant formation of saccules and no alveoli.

name: congenital alveolar dysplasia
congenital alveolar dysplasia
HP:0033210.def: Arrest of lung development in the cananicular stage (weeks 18 to 26 of human gestation) resulting in simplified acinar spaces, frequently with abundant intervening mesenchyme and no alveoli. In later arrest growth stages early saccular formations may be seen. May resemble the lobular maldevelopment often seen in alveolar capillary dysplasia/misaligment of the pulmonary veins without vein misalignment or marked hypertensive changes of the pulmonary arteries.

name: decreased total iron binding capacity
decrease total iron binding capacity
HP:0033211.def: A reduction in the total-iron binding capacity, which measures how much serum iron is bound if an excess of radioactive iron is added. The latent (or free) iron binding capacity is the difference between the TIBC and the measured serum iron, corresponding to the transferrin not bound to iron, i.e., free iron binding capacity.

name: abnormal total iron binding capacity
abnormal total iron binding capacity
HP:0033212.def: Any deviation from the normal total-iron binding capacity, which measures how much serum iron is bound if an excess of radioactive iron is added.

name: elevated urine suberic acid level
elevate urine suberic acid level
HP:0033213.def: The concentration of suberic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: recurrent viral pneumonia
recurrent viral pneumonia
HP:0033214.def: Increased susceptibility to viral pneumonia, as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral pneumonias.

name: obliterative abnormality of the renal glomerulus
obliterative abnormality of the renal glomerulus
glomerular hyalinosis
glomerular hyalinosis
HP:0033216.def: Accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, glassy, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material in the glomerulus. Distribution can include vascular pole, perihilar, tip or neither tip, perihilar or vascular.

name: perihilar glomerular hyalinosis
perihilar glomerular hyalinosis
HP:0033217.def: Accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, glassy, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material in the glomerulus at the vascular pole/perihilum.

name: glomerular hyalinosis at the tubular pole
glomerular hyalinosis at the tubular pole
HP:0033218.def: Accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, glassy, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material in the glomerulus at the tip/tubular pole.

name: glomerular hyalinosis away from the vascular and tubular poles
glomerular hyalinosis away from the vascular and tubular pole
HP:0033219.def: Accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, glassy, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material in the glomerulus at neither tip nor perihilar/vascular poles. Both the vascular and the tubular pole are present in the glomerular cross section.

name: 2 - ethylhydracylic aciduria
2 - ethylhydracylic aciduria
HP:0033220.def: An increased concentration of 2-ethylhydracylic acid in the urine.

name: increased cd4 : cd8 ratio
increase cd4 : cd8 ratio
HP:0033221.def: An abnormal elevation of the relative proportion of CD4+ to CD8+ T cells.

name: decreased cd4 : cd8 ratio
decrease cd4 : cd8 ratio
HP:0033222.def: An abnormal reduction of the relative proportion of CD4+ to CD8+ T cells.

name: abnormal glomerular parietal epithelial cell morphology
abnormal glomerular parietal epithelial cell morphology
HP:0033223.def: Any structural abnormality of the parietal epithelial cells that line the inside of Bowman's capsule and form an inconspicuous sheet of flat epithelial cells in continuity with the proximal tubular epithelial cells at the urinary pole and with the podocytes at the vascular pole.

name: glomerular parietal epithelial cell hyperplasia
glomerular parietal epithelial cell hyperplasia
HP:0033224.def: Increased number of parietal epithelial cells lining Bowman's capsule. Hyperplasia leads to the cells being present in 2 or more layers, often with crowding and multilayering.
synonym: hyperplasia of the glomerular parietal epithelial cell
hyperplasia of the glomerular parietal epithelial cell

name: glomerular parietal epithelial cell hypertrophy
glomerular parietal epithelial cell hypertrophy
HP:0033225.def: An abnormality of the glomerular parietal epithelial cells characterized by (1) Increased parietal epithelial cell size, with or without cytoplasmic protein droplets; or (2) enlarged nuclei with prominent nucleoli. Both features can be present
synonym: hypertrophy of the glomerular parietal epithelial cell
hypertrophy of the glomerular parietal epithelial cell

name: bowman capsular hyaline drops
bowman capsular hyaline drop
HP:0033226.def: An insudative accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material protruding from Bowman's capsule into the urinary space. Although not always evident by light microscopy, this material is located between Bowman's capsule and the parietal epithelial cells, in some cases associated with newly formed matrix material.
synonym: capsular hyaline drops within bowman 's capsule
capsular hyaline drop within bowman 's capsule

name: glomerular synechial adhesion
glomerular synechial adhesion
HP:0033227.def: An area of basement membrane continuity between the glomerular tuft and Bowman's capsule, without intervening crescent and not adjacent to an area of segmental sclerosis.

name: triceps areflexia
triceps areflexia
HP:0033228.def: Inability to elicit triceps tendon reflex.

name: brachioradialis areflexia
brachioradialis areflexia
HP:0033229.def: Inability to elicit brachioradialis tendon reflex.

name: biceps areflexia
biceps areflexia
HP:0033230.def: Inability to elicit biceps tendon reflex.

name: abnormal glomerular mesangial cellularity
abnormal glomerular mesangial cellularity
HP:0033231.def: Abnormal number of its constituent cells of the mesangium of the glomerulus of the kidney.

name: abnormal glomerular mesangial matrix morphology
abnormal glomerular mesangial matrix morphology
HP:0033232.def: Any structural anomaly of the glomerular matrix. Mesangial cells generate and embed in their own extracellular matrix. The mesangial matrix is different in composition from the glomerular basement membrane. Its constituents are type IV collagen (but only the alpha1 and alpha2 chains); type V collagen; laminin A, B1, and B2; and considerable amounts of fibronectin, heparan sulfate and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans, entactin, and nidogen. Furthermore, small amounts of the proteoglycans decorin and biglycan are found in the mesangial matrix.

name: paramesangial deposits
paramesangial deposit
HP:0033233.def: Mesangial immune deposit located adjacent to the paramesangial glomerular basement membrane.

name: mesangial hyaline deposition
mesangial hyaline deposition
HP:0033234.def: Extracellular mesangial accumulation of moderately electron-dense, generally homogenous, amorphous-appearing extracellular material.

name: cognitive fatigue
cognitive fatigue
HP:0033236.def: A failure to sustain attention that requires self-motivation to optimize performance.

name: visceral epithelial cell detachment
visceral epithelial cell detachment
HP:0033237.def: Detachment of visceral epithelial cells (podocytes) from underlying glomerular basement membrane with intervening new loose basement membrane material (pale on Hematoxylin and eosin, periodic acid-Shiff, trichrome, or silver stain) forming a so-called 'halo'.

name: podocyte microvillous transformation
podocyte microvillous transformation
HP:0033238.def: Cytoplasmic projections into the urinary space from the luminal side of the podocyte.

name: visceral epithelial cell capping
visceral epithelial cell cap
HP:0033239.def: Layer of hypertrophied visceral epithelial cells overlying a sclerosed segment of the tuft of the glomerulus.

name: elevated rv / tlc ratio
elevate rv / tlc ratio
HP:0033240.def: An increase in the ratio of residual volume (RV) to total lung capacity (TLC) on pulmonary function testing. RV is the amount of air remaining aftermaximal expiration and TLC is the total amount of air in theungs at full inspiration. These volumes cannot be determined by spirometry, but can be measured by inert gas dilution, nitrogen washout, and (3) body plethysmography. An elevated RV/TLC can be interpreted as a sign of air trapping and hyperinflation.

name: polyalveolar lobe
polyalveolar lobe
HP:0033241.def: An elevation of the total count of alveoli as determined by microscopic point-counting of randomly taken lung sections, not secondary to abnormalities in number, size and structure of the airways. In polyaveolar lobe, the number of alveoli is generally increased three to fivefold.

name: horseshoe lung
horseshoe lung
HP:0033242.def: A horseshoe lung is an uncommon congenital abnormality caused by the partial fusion of the bases of both lungs behind the pericardial sac.

name: pulmonary necrosis
pulmonary necrosis
HP:0033243.def: Cellular death affecting one or more parts of the lung. Necrosis is caused by diverse external and internal factors which result in the unregulated digestion of cell components.

name: glycogen accumulation in pulmonary interstitial cells
glycogen accumulation in pulmonary interstitial cell
HP:0033244.def: Accumulation of immature interstitial cells containing abundant cytoplasmic glycogen defined by periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) positive cells.

name: abnormal alveolar type ii pneumocyte morphology
abnormal alveolar type ii pneumocyte morphology
HP:0033245.def: Any structural abnormality of alveolar type 2 (ATII) cells.
synonym: abnormal alveolar epithelial type ii cell morphology
abnormal alveolar epithelial type ii cell morphology
abnormal pulmonary type ii cell morphology
abnormal pulmonary type ii cell morphology

name: type ii pneumocyte hypertrophy
type ii pneumocyte hypertrophy
HP:0033246.def: Increase in size of type II pneumocytes, characterized by qualitative morphologic alterations, including cuboidal shapes, increased nucleocytoplasmic ratio, enlarged nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and various alterations in their nuclear chromatin.

name: pulmonary amyloidosis
pulmonary amyloidosis
HP:0033247.def: Extracellular deposition in lung tissue of a proteinaceous material that, when stained with Congo red, demonstrates apple-green birefringence under polarized light and that has a distinct color when stained with sulfated Alcian blue. Viewed with electron microscopy, the amyloid deposits are seen to be composed of a beta-sheet fibrillar material. These nonbranching fibrils have a diameter of 7.5 to 10 nm and are the result of protein misfolding.

name: multiple pulmonary interstitial hyalinized nodules
multiple pulmonary interstitial hyalinized nodule
HP:0033248.def: Fibrosing nodules, consisting of either unilateral or bilateral central whorled deposits of lamellar collagen hyalin.

name: focal substantia nigra t2 hyperintensity
focal substantia nigra t2 hyperintensity
HP:0033249.def: Hyperintense lesion in the substantia nigra on magnetic resonance T2 imaging.
synonym: focal substantia nigra t2 hyperintense lesion
focal substantia nigra t2 hyperintense lesion

name: nailfold capillary tortuosity
nailfold capillary tortuosity
HP:0033250.def: An increased number of turns of the blood vessels of the nailfold with a charactereistic winded or twisted appearance of the blood vessels.

name: elevated residual volume
elevate residual volume
HP:0033251.def: Increase in the amount of air remaining in a person's lungs after full exhalation.

name: palmar hyperlinearity
palmar hyperlinearity
HP:0033252.def: Exaggerated skin markings (dermatoglyphics) on the palms of the hand.

name: reduced circulating interferon gamma concentration
reduce circulate interferon gamma concentration
HP:0033253.def: A reduction in the concentration of interferon gamma measured in the blood circulation.

name: anorectal stricture
anorectal stricture
HP:0033254.def: Narrowing of the anorectum associated with inflammation or scar tissue.

name: congenital lobar overinflation
congenital lobar overinflation
HP:0033255.def: A congenital malformation characterized by an overdistended segment of lung, affecting an party of a lobe or the entire one. It results in progressive overinflation of one or more lobes.

name: delayed ability to walk with support
delay ability to walk with support
HP:0033257.def: A failure to achieve the ability to walk with support (cruise) at an appropriate developmental stage.

name: sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
HP:0033258.def: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) is a sudden, unexpected, witnessed or unwitnessed, non-traumatic and non-drowning death, occurring in benign circumstances, in an individual with epilepsy, with or without evidence for a seizure and excluding documented status epilepticus, in which postmortem examination has not revealed a cause of death.

name: non - motor seizure
non - motor seizure
HP:0033259.def: A seizure with clinical manifestation but without motor signs (other than possible behavior arrest) as its initial clinical manifestation. The electrographic onset may be generalized, focal, or unknown.

name: livedo racemosa
livedo racemosa
HP:0033260.def: Livedo racemosa describes a reddish-blue mottling of the skin in an irregular, reticular pattern. It differs from the more common livedo reticularis by its shape. Livedo racemosa consists of broken circular segments resulting in a seemingly larger pattern, as opposed to the fine, regular, complete network of livedo reticularis. Livedo racemosa results from permanent impairment of peripheral blood flow and, unlike livedo reticularis, it persists on warming.

name: renal artery aneurysm
renal artery aneurysm
HP:0033261.def: Increase in diameter of a segment of the renal artery that can be defined as a focal, isolated dilatation of all three layers of the arterial wall over 1.5 times the diameter of the disease-free proximal adjacent arterial segment.

name: transphyseal fracture of the distal humerus
transphyseal fracture of the distal humerus
HP:0033262.def: A fracture through the distal humeral physis that separates the entire distal humeral epiphysis from the metaphysis.

name: absent platelet dense granules
absent platelet dense granule
HP:0033263.def: Lack of platelet dense granules, a type of platelet organelles.

name: enlarged platelet dense granules
enlarge platelet dense granule
HP:0033264.def: Increased size of platelet dense granules.

name: podocyte myelin figures
podocyte myelin figure
HP:0033265.def: Lamellated intracytoplasmic lipid inclusions within podocytes.

name: glomerular pseudocrescent
glomerular pseudocrescent
HP:0033266.def: Visceral epithelial cell hyperplasia with resulting cellular crowding of the the urinary space. In contrast with true crescents, these proliferations lack inflammatory cells and fibrin. The cells are typically plump (not spindle-shaped) and often vacuolated, and Bowman's capsule is usually intact.

name: abnormal glomerular capillary lumen morphology
abnormal glomerular capillary lumen morphology
HP:0033267.def: Abnormal structural characteristics of the interior space of the capillary of the renal glomerulus.

name: deflation of the glomerular tuft
deflation of the glomerular tuft
HP:0033268.def: Wrinkling and folding of the capillaries without epithelial cell (podocyte) hyperplasia (formerly called ischemic type of collapse) involving o 80% of the glomerular tuft. The wrinkling is generally made by small regular folds of the glomerular basement membrane.

name: glomerular capillary collapse
glomerular capillary collapse
HP:0033269.def: Collapse is generally accompanied by other descriptors such as hypertrophy and hyperplasia of overlying glomerular epithelial cells, halo, protein droplets in podocytes and glomerular parietal epithelial cells (PECs).

name: glomerular capillary congestion
glomerular capillary congestion
HP:0033270.def: Global distention of glomerular capillaries with intraluminal intact red blood cells.

name: glomerular capillary microaneurysm
glomerular capillary microaneurysm
HP:0033271.def: Glomerular capillary dilatation due to loosening/detachment of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) from its anchoring points, usually in the context of mesangiolysis or nodular glomerulosclerosis.

name: abnormal glomerular endothelial cell morphology
abnormal glomerular endothelial cell morphology
HP:0033272.def: An abnormal structure of the glomerular endothelial cells, which are highly specialized cells with fenestrae and a charged luminal glycocalyx layer that contribute to the filtration barrier.

name: loss of glomerular endothelial cell fenestration
loss of glomerular endothelial cell fenestration
HP:0033273.def: Loss of round to oval discontinuities normally present in the glomerular capillary endothelial cell cytoplasm.

name: glomerular endotheliosis
glomerular endotheliosis
HP:0033274.def: Enlargement of glomerular endothelial cells by cytoplasmic swelling with resulting partial or complete occlusion of the lumen.

name: glomerular endothelial tubuloreticular inclusion
glomerular endothelial tubuloreticular inclusion
HP:0033275.def: Inter-anastomosing tubular structures located within cisternae of endoplasmic reticulum, most often within endothelial cells and associated with exposure to interferon.

name: glomerular fibrinoid necrosis
glomerular fibrinoid necrosis
HP:0033277.def: Fibrin associated with glomerular basement membrane disruption and/or lysis of the mesangial matrix; this lesion does not require the presence of karyorrhexis.

name: reduced cd95 - induced lymphocyte apoptosis
reduce cd95 - induced lymphocyte apoptosis
HP:0033278.def: Reduced amount of programmed cell death in peripheral blood lymphocytes following exposure to CD95 (APO-1/Fas), which is a member of the death receptor family, a subfamily of the TNF-R superfamily. Crosslinking of CD95 with its natural ligand CD95L (CD178) or with agonistic antibodies such as anti-APO-1 induces apoptosis in sensitive cells.

name: enterocutaneous fistula
enterocutaneous fistula
HP:0033279.def: An abnormal connection (fistula) between the intra-abdominal intestinal tract and the skin.

name: paratracheal lymphadenopathy
