paratracheal lymphadenopathy
HP:0033280.def: Enlargement of lymph nodes surrounding the trachea.

name: circulating nucleated red blood cells
circulate nucleate red blood cell
HP:0033281.def: The presence of nucleated red blood cells in the peripheral blood circulation.

name: abnormal glomerular basement membrane morphology
abnormal glomerular basement membrane morphology
HP:0033282.def: Any abnormal sttructure of the glomerular basement membrane.

name: segmentally thickened glomerular basement membrane
segmentally thicken glomerular basement membrane
HP:0033283.def: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting a segmental and increase in thickness (subjective estimate) with no evidence of electron dense deposits by EM. Thickening is measured from endothelial to visceral epithelial plasma membrane and mainly attributable to an increase in thickness of the lamina densa, generally to an overall thickness more than 2 standard deviations greater than that of the normal mean GBM thickness for health age- and sex matched individuals.

name: diffusely thickened glomerular basement membrane
diffusely thicken glomerular basement membrane
HP:0033284.def: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting an diffuse and relativly uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate) with no evidence of electron dense deposits by EM. Thickening is measured from endothelial to visceral epithelial plasma membrane and mainly attributable to an increase in thickness of the lamina densa, generally to an overall thickness more than 2 standard deviations greater than that of the normal mean GBM thickness for health age- and sex matched individuals.

name: thickened glomerular basement membranes with no electron dense deposits
thicken glomerular basement membrane with no electron dense deposit
HP:0033285.def: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting an increase in thickness (subjective estimate) with no evidence of electron dense deposits by electron microscopy.

name: thickened glomerular basement membranes with electron dense deposits
thicken glomerular basement membrane with electron dense deposit
glomerular basement membrane lucencies
glomerular basement membrane lucencies
HP:0033287.def: Lucent zones within the glomerular basement membranes. May reflect remote/resolved deposits.

name: glomerular basement membrane wrinkling
glomerular basement membrane wrinkle
HP:0033289.def: Irregular folding of the glomerular basement membrane with an intact lamina densa.

name: glomerular subendothelial widening
glomerular subendothelial widening
HP:0033290.def: Expansion of the space between the glomerular endothelium and lamina densa by electron-lucent material.

name: glomerular karyhorrhectic debris
glomerular karyhorrhectic debris
HP:0033291.def: Apoptotic, pyknotic, and fragmented nuclei within the glomerulus.

name: glomerular fibrin thrombus
glomerular fibrin thrombus
HP:0033292.def: An aggregate of coagulated blood containing fibrin, with or without entrapped cellular elements, within a glomerular capillary lumen.

name: glomerular hyaline pseudothrombus
glomerular hyaline pseudothrombus
HP:0033293.def: Intracapillary amorphous, eosinophilic material consisting of immune deposits.

name: glomerular lipoprotein thrombus
glomerular lipoprotein thrombus
HP:0033294.def: Intracapillary silver-positive material that is finely vacuolated and laminated, and stains with oil red O on frozen sections.

name: mesangial immune complex deposition
mesangial immune complex deposition
HP:0033295.def: Extracellular meangial accumulation of finely granular material corresponding to immunoglobulin and/or complement by immunofluorescence/immunohistochemistry; most typically electron-dense although this may decrease with resorption of the deposit.

name: binucleated visceral epithelial cells
binucleated visceral epithelial cell
HP:0033296.def: Visceral epithelial cells with 2 nuclei. Can be observed on light or ultrastructral microscopy.

name: multinucleated visceral epithelial cells
multinucleated visceral epithelial cell
HP:0033297.def: Visceral epithelial cells with more than two nuclei. Can be observed on light or ultrastructral microscopy.

name: abnormal circulating complement factor h related protein 1 concentration
abnormal circulate complement factor h related protein 1 concentration
HP:0033298.def: A deviation from the normal concentration in blood of factor H-related protein 1 (FHR-1)

name: reduced circulating complement factor h related protein 1 concentration
reduce circulate complement factor h related protein 1 concentration
HP:0033299.def: Decreased level of circulating complement factor H related protein 1 concentration in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating complement factor h related protein 1 concentration
increase circulate complement factor h related protein 1 concentration
HP:0033300.def: Elevated level of circulating complement factor H related protein 1 concentration in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating 1 - methylhistidine concentration
elevate circulate 1 - methylhistidine concentration
HP:0033301.def: An abnormally increased level of 1-methylhistidine in the blood circulation. 1-methylhistidine is a derivative of L-histidine.

name: elevated circulating 4 - hydroxyphenylacetic acid concentration
elevate circulate 4 - hydroxyphenylacetic acid concentration
HP:0033302.def: The concentration of 4-Hydroxyphenylacetic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated urinary monocarboxylic acid level
elevate urinary monocarboxylic acid level
HP:0033303.def: Abnormally increased amount of a monocarboxylic acid in the urine. Monocarboxylic acids are molecules with one COOH functional group.

name: obsolete elevated urine 4 - hydroxyphenylacetic acid level
obsolete elevate urine 4 - hydroxyphenylacetic acid level
abnormal circulating fetuin a concentration
abnormal circulate fetuin a concentration
HP:0033305.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of fetuin A in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating fetuin a concentration
decrease circulate fetuin a concentration
HP:0033306.def: A reduction below normal of fetuin A in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating fetuin a concentration
increase circulate fetuin a concentration
HP:0033307.def: An elevation above normal of fetuin A in the blood circulation.

name: ileoileal intussusception
ileoileal intussusception
HP:0033309.def: A type of intussusception of the small intestine in which one part of the ileum invaginates (telescopes) into another part of the ileum.

name: osmotic diarrhea
osmotic diarrhea
HP:0033310.def: Osmotic diarrhea results from the presence of osmotically active, poorly absorbed solutes in the bowel lumen that inhibit normal water and electrolyte absorption.

name: abdominal aortic dissection
abdominal aortic dissection
HP:0033311.def: A tear in the intimal layer of the abdominal aorta causing a separation between the intima and the medial layers.

name: abnormal bowman space morphology
abnormal bowman space morphology
HP:0033312.def: Structural anomaly located in Bowman's space, which represents the beginning of the urinary space and is contiguous with the proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron.

name: urinary space collagenization
urinary space collagenization
HP:0033313.def: Acellular collagenous matrix within Bowman's space, not associated with extracapillary hypercellularity or necrosis, associated with sclerosis or deflation of the tuft.

name: visceral epithelial cell hyperplasia
visceral epithelial cell hyperplasia
HP:0033314.def: Increased number of visceral epithelial cells (2 or more layers), often with crowding and multilayering, but without continuity with the parietal epithelium.

name: visceral epithelial hyaline droplets
visceral epithelial hyaline droplet
HP:0033315.def: Round to ovoid, Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, fuchsinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions within visceral epithelial cells.

name: glomerular crescent formation
glomerular crescent formation
HP:0033316.def: Glomerular crescent refers hyperplastic lesions involving 10% or more of the circumference of Bowman's capsule. Crescents can be composed of a variable mixture of epithelial/leukocyte hypercellularity, fibrous matrix, and fibrin.

name: cellular crescent
cellular crescent
HP:0033317.def: A type of glomerular crescent characterized by extracapillary hypercellularity of greater than two cell layers and involving more than 10% of the capsular circumference, composed of greater than 75% cells with or without fibrin, and less than 25% fibrous matrix.

name: fibrocellular crescent
fibrocellular crescent
HP:0033318.def: A type of glomerular crescent characterized by extracapillary hypercellularity of more than 2 cell layers and involving over 10% of the capsular circumference, composed of 25% to 75% cells with or without fibrin, and the remainder fibrous matrix.

name: fibrous crescent
fibrous crescent
HP:0033319.def: A type of glomerular crescent characterized by extracapillary fibrosis composed of greater than 75% matrix and of less than 25% cells with or without fibrin, usually associated with disruption of Bowman's capsule and involving over 10% of the capsular circumference.

name: mesangial cell loss
mesangial cell loss
HP:0033320.def: Loss of mesangial cells segmentally or globally.

name: glomerular obsolescence
glomerular obsolescence
HP:0033321.def: Globally sclerotic glomeruli are that are small and without hyalinosis and may appear with collapse of the tuft with collagenization of the urinary space. Bowman's capsule is completely or partially absent and there is no periglomerular fibrosis and glomerular size is decreased by more than 50% compared to all other glomeruli in the same biopsy. Obsolescent glomeruli may appear to be receding into the interstitium.

name: glomerular capillary wall duplication without cellular interposition
glomerular capillary wall duplication without cellular interposition
HP:0033322.def: Double contouring of the original glomerular basement membrane (GBM)/additional layer(s) of overlying basement membrane matrix, with or without endocapillary hypercellularity and no evidence of interposed migrated cells (mesangial, endothelial, monocytes) between the layers of original GBM and de novo GBM.

name: glomerular capillary wall duplication with cellular interposition
glomerular capillary wall duplication with cellular interposition
HP:0033323.def: Double contouring of the original glomerular basement membrane (GBM)/additional layer(s) of overlying basement membrane matrix with interposed migrated cells (mesangial, endothelial, monocytes) between the layers of original GBM and de novo GBM.

name: elevated circulating homovanillic acid concentration
elevate circulate homovanillic acid concentration
HP:0033324.def: The concentration of homovanillic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating sebacic acid concentration
elevate circulate sebacic acid concentration
HP:0033325.def: Increased concentration of sebacic acid in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating hydroxyphenlyllactic acid concentration
elevate circulate hydroxyphenlyllactic acid concentration
HP:0033326.def: An increased concentration of 4-hydroxyphenlyllactic acid in the blood circulation.

name: nail psoriasis
nail psoriasis
HP:0033327.def: Psoriatic nail abnormality characterized by the presence of neutrophils in the nail bed epithelium, hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, presence of exudates on the corneal epithelium, focal hypogranulosis and psoriasiform hyperplasia of the nail bed.

name: type ii pneumocyte hyperplasia
type ii pneumocyte hyperplasia
HP:0033328.def: Increase in the number of type II pneumocytes.

name: abnormal postural reflex
abnormal postural reflex
HP:0033329.def: Anomaly of the physiological response to maintain the body's posture when movement and position is altered.

name: impaired neck - righting reflex
impaired neck - righting reflex
HP:0033330.def: Abnormal neck-righting response, which is said to be a physiological response when a child is placed flat on his or her back and the head is turned 90 degrees to the right or the left. With a normal neck-righting response, there follows a reflected torsion of the vertebral column in the same direction as the induced rotation of the neck. That is, the whole body follows the direction in which the head was turned. The response is present from birth to the age of five years.

name: acute phase response
acute phase response
HP:0033331.def: Presence of one or more manifestations of the acute phase response. Acute phase proteins (APP) are blood proteins primarily synthesized by hepatocytes as part of the acute phase response (APR). The APR is part of the early-defense or innate immune system, which is triggered by different stimuli including trauma, infection, stress, neoplasia, and inflammation. The APR results in a complex systemic reaction with the goal of reestablishing homeostasis and promoting healing.

name: elevated circulating amyloid a
elevate circulate amyloid a
HP:0033332.def: An increased concentration of serum amyloid A in the blood circulation.

name: jaw contracture
jaw contracture
HP:0033333.def: Limitation of motion of the jaw due to structural changes in a muscle such as the massseter responsible for jaw movement.

name: abnormal embryonic development
abnormal embryonic development
HP:0033334.def: An anomaly in the development of the embryo, that is, of the early developmental stage of development that follows the fertilization of an egg by sperm.

name: abnormal preimplantation embryonic development
abnormal preimplantation embryonic development
HP:0033335.def: An anomaly in the development of the embryo in a stage prior to implantation.

name: zygotic cleavage failure
zygotic cleavage failure
HP:0033336.def: Failure of a fertilized oocyte to undergo the first round of cell division.

name: abnormal gametogenesis
abnormal gametogenesis
HP:0033337.def: An anomaly in the process by a a haploid cell is formed from a diploid cells through meiosis. In males, diploid spermatogonia produce two haploid cells (secondary spermatocytes) in meiosis I and four haploid spermatids in meiosis II. In females, primordial germ cells under meiosis II before birth to form primary oocytes. Once puberty cell begins, these cells form secondary oocytes through meiosis II.

name: increased circulating inosine concentration
increase circulate inosine concentration
HP:0033339.def: An increased concentration of inosine in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating guanosine concentration
increase circulate guanosine concentration
HP:0033340.def: Increased concentration of guanosine in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating sitosterol concentration
elevate circulate sitosterol concentration
HP:0033341.def: An increased concentration of beta-sitosterol in the blood circulation.

name: anti - aquaporin 4 antibody positivity
anti - aquaporin 4 antibody positivity
HP:0033342.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against aquaporin-4.

name: mucoid diarrhea
mucoid diarrhea
HP:0033343.def: Passage of an increased number of stools containing mucus, a thick fluid substance secreted by mucous membranes.

name: pleural cobblestoning
pleural cobblestoning
HP:0033344.def: A pleural cobblestone appearance characterized by irregular bumps surrounded by depressed lines in open lung biopsy. Caused by underlying scarring causing retraction of the interlobular septa where they insert on the pleura.

name: neuralgia
neuralgia
HP:0033345.def: Pain (An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience) along the course of a nerve.

name: psychic epileptic aura
psychic epileptic aura
HP:0033346.def: Aura with affective, mnemonic or composite perceptual phenomena including illusory or composite hallucinatory events.

name: cognitive epileptic aura
cognitive epileptic aura
HP:0033347.def: A purely subjective manifestation of an epileptic seizure pertaining to altered cognition.

name: epileptic aura
epileptic aura
HP:0033348.def: An epileptic aura is a purely subjective clinical manifestation of an epileptic seizure. If an epileptic aura is not followed by loss of awareness or propagation to a bilateral tonic-clonic seizure then it is a type of focal aware non-motor seizure.

name: seizure cluster
seizure cluster
HP:0033349.def: A fourfold or greater increase of usual seizure frequency within a 3-day period, where the patient demonstrates full recovery between seizure events within the cluster. The seizure cluster should be recognisable by the primary clinician, carer or patient.

name: elevated forced expiratory volume in one second
elevate forced expiratory volume in one second
HP:0033350.def: An increase in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second, compared to some standard or previous measure of same subject.

name: candida esophagitis
candida esophagitis
HP:0033351.def: Candida infections of the esophagus are considered opportunistic infections and are seen most commonly in immunosuppressed patients, the most common symptoms being dysphagia, odynophagia, and retrosternal pain.

name: pulmonary hypertensive crisis
pulmonary hypertensive crisis
HP:0033352.def: Pulmonary hypertensive crisis involves sudden and potentially lethal increases in PAP and PVR that cause acute rise in right atrial and right ventricular end-diastolic pressure accompanied by low cardiac output.

name: abnormal blood vessel morphology
abnormal blood vessel morphology
HP:0033353.def: Any structural anomaly of a blood vessel (artery, arteriole, capillary, venule, or vein).

name: abnormal urine metabolite level
abnormal urine metabolite level
HP:0033354.def: Any deviation from the normal amount of a metabolite in urine.

name: increased urine deoxypyridinoline level
increase urine deoxypyridinoline level
HP:0033355.def: An increased level of deoxypyridinoline in the urine. Deoxypyridinoline is a crosslink product of collagen molecules found in bone and excreted in urine during bone degradation, has been described as a marker of bone turnover.

name: elevated circulating o - phosphoserine concentration
elevate circulate o - phosphoserine concentration
HP:0033356.def: An abnormally increased level of o-phosphoserine in the blood circulation. o-phosphoserine is a derivative of serine.

name: limited head rotation
limited head rotation
HP:0033357.def: Reduced range of motion turning the head side to side.

name: abnormal urine osmolality
abnormal urine osmolality
HP:0033358.def: A deviation from the normal range of concentration of particles in urine.

name: hyperosthenuria
hyperosthenuria
HP:0033359.def: An abnormally high urinary specific gravity, i.e., increased concentration of solutes in the urine.

name: impaired ability to shift attention
impaired ability to shift attention
HP:0033360.def: A behavioral abnormality whereby a person is unable to move freely from one situation, activity or aspect of aa problem to another as circumstances demand. Key aspects of shifting include the ability to make transitions, problem solve flexibly, switch or alternate attention, and change focus from one mind-set or topic to another. Mild deficits in the ability to shift compromise the efficiency of problem solving, whereas more severe difficulties are reflected in perseverative behaviors. Sometimes this is described as being rigid or inflexible.

name: nasal ulcer
nasal ulcer
HP:0033361.def: An open sore of the nasal mucosa.

name: recurrent coughing spasms
recurrent cough spasm
HP:0033362.def: Repeated occurrence of episodes of coughing, with each episode consisting of at least five minutes of continuous coughing.

name: hyaline membranes
hyaline membrane
HP:0033363.def: Hyaline membranes are homogeneous eosinophilic material composed of cellular debris, plasma proteins, and surfactant plastered against alveolar ducts and alveolar walls. The hyaline membranes are deposited along the walls of the alveoli, where gas exchange typically occurs, thereby making gas exchange difficult.

name: lipoid pneumonia
lipoid pneumonia
HP:0033364.def: A specific form of lung inflammation that results from accumulation of lipids in the alveoli. Lipoid pneumonia can be either exogenous or endogenous in cause based on the source of the lipid.

name: endogenous lipoid pneumonia
endogenous lipoid pneumonia
HP:0033365.def: A type of lipoid pneumonia in which the source of the lipids is the body itself. When an airway is obstructed, it is often the case that distal to the obstruction, lipid-laden macrophages and giant cells fill the lumen of the disconnected airspace.

name: exogenous lipoid pneumonia
exogenous lipoid pneumonia
HP:0033366.def: A type of lipoid pneumonia in which the source of the lipids is external to the body.

name: orthodeoxia
orthodeoxia
HP:0033367.def: Low level of blood oxygen induced by changing from a recumbent to an upright position.

name: platypnea
platypnea
HP:0033368.def: A type of dyspnea that occurs when the affected person changes from a recumbent to an upright position.

name: cavitating leukodystrophy
cavitating leukodystrophy
HP:0033369.def: A type of leukodystrophy characterized by multiple small cavitations typically in the periventricular and deep cerebral white matter. The cavitations are visible as a central cavity with cerebrospinal fluid-like signal intensity.

name: bronchial telangiectasia
bronchial telangiectasia
HP:0033370.def: Telangiectasias (small dilated blood vessels located near the surface of the skin or mucous membranes) located in the trachoebronchial system.

name: bronchocentric granulomatosis
bronchocentric granulomatosis
HP:0033371.def: Granulomatous inflammation that surrounds the bronchi and bronchioles, replacing bronchial walls and mucosa. In bronchocentric granulomatosis, the lumen of the airway contains necrotic debris, and palisaded histiocytes surround the lumen.

name: abnormal kco
abnormal kco
HP:0033372.def: Any deviation from the normal range of KCO. The KCO is a measurement of the rate constant for alveolar uptake of CO during breath-holding in the single breath measurement of DLCO at full inflation. The DLCO is derived as the product of the KCO and the single breath alveolar volume (VA) divided by PB-PH2O.

name: increased kco
increase kco
HP:0033373.def: Increased diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (CO) rate constant (efficiency index).

name: decreased kco
decrease kco
HP:0033374.def: Decreased diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (CO) rate constant (efficiency index).

name: anthracosis
anthracosis
HP:0033375.def: Anthracosis is the deposition of black carbon pigment. It is commonly seen in perihilar lymph nodes as well as within lung parenchyma. There can be prominent storiforming (i.e., spiral patterning) of histiocytes, to such an extent as to mimic a neoplastic lesion histologically. Anthracosis is a common finding in smokers and polluted city dwellers.

name: alveolar septal thickening
alveolar septal thickening
HP:0033376.def: Increased width of the alveolar septum, which is the structure that separates neighboring alveoli. This finding can be appreciated on histology.

name: increased airway neuroendocrine cells
increase airway neuroendocrine cell
HP:0033377.def: Presence of increased numbers of bombesin-immuno-positive neuroendocrine cells (NECs) within distal airways. There are no formal criteria for an increase (which is also dependend on the sensitivity of the staining method), findings of neuroendocrine cells in at least 70% of bronchioles by lung biopsy and at least 10% NECs in an individual airway are consistent with the diagnosis of Neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia of infancy in the appropriate clinical setting. Increases are also seen in other clicnial settings. Neuroendocrine neoplasms of the lung encompass NE tumors (NETs), which split into typical and atypical carcinoids, and NE carcinomas (NECs).

name: increased airway neuroepithelial bodies
increase airway neuroepithelial body
HP:0033378.def: Presence of increased numbers of bombesin-immuno-positive neuroendocrine cell cluster (neuroepithelial bodies) in the alveolar ducts.

name: bilateral superior vena cava
bilateral superior vena cava
HP:0033379.def: The presence of a left and a right superior vena cava.

name: nasal chondritis
nasal chondritis
HP:0033380.def: Inflammation of the cartilage of the nose.

name: elevated circulating stearoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate stearoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033381.def: Abnormally increased concentration of O-stearoylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating palmitoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate palmitoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033382.def: Abnormally increased concentration of palmitoylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

name: decreased compound muscle action potential amplitude
decrease compound muscle action potential amplitude
HP:0033383.def: Reduced level of the compound muscle action potential (CMAP), which is recorded following electrical stimulation of a nerve from surface electrodes overlying a muscle supplied by that nerve.

name: elevated urinary collagen degradation products
elevate urinary collagen degradation product
HP:0033384.def: Increased level in the urine of a metabolite that results from collagen degradation, e.g., a fragment of a collagen produced by a collagenase or serine protease.

name: elevated urine pyridinoline level
elevate urine pyridinoline level
HP:0033385.def: An increased amount of pyridinoline in the urine.

name: abnormal circulating collagen degradation product concentration
abnormal circulate collagen degradation product concentration
HP:0033386.def: Abnormal concentration in the blood circulation of a metabolite that results from collagen degradation, e.g., a fragment of a collagen produced by a collagenase or serine protease.

name: elevated circulating pyridinoline concentration
elevate circulate pyridinoline concentration
HP:0033387.def: An increased concentration of hydroxylysyl-pyridinoline (pyridinoline) in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal bronchial artery morphology
abnormal bronchial artery morphology
HP:0033388.def: Any structural abnormality of a bronchial artery.

name: bronchopulmonary anastomosis
bronchopulmonary anastomosis
HP:0033389.def: Abnormal arterial anastomosis (connection) between bronchial and pulmonary arteries.

name: bronchial artery dilatation
bronchial artery dilatation
HP:0033390.def: Increased caliber of a bronchial artery, which can be defined as a bronchial artery diameter that exceeds 2 mm.

name: bronchial artery hypertrophy
bronchial artery hypertrophy
HP:0033391.def: Increase in the volume of bronchial artery wall due to the enlargement of its component cells.

name: perivascular pre - capillary pulmonary artery inflammation
perivascular pre - capillary pulmonary artery inflammation
HP:0033392.def: Inflammatory cell infiltration surrounding precapillary pulmonary arteries (arterioles; 20-70 micrometer).
synonym: perivascular inflammation of arterioles in the pulmonary circulation
perivascular inflammation of arteriole in the pulmonary circulation
perivascular inflammation of pre - capillary pulmonary arteries
perivascular inflammation of pre - capillary pulmonary artery

name: irregularly shaped sperm tail
irregularly shaped sperm tail
HP:0033393.def: Irregular or changing caliber (diameter) along the tail of the sperm.

name: anti - carbonic anhydrase ii antibody positivity
anti - carbonic anhydrase ii antibody positivity
HP:0033394.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against carbonic anhydrase II.

name: antilactoferrin antibody positivity
antilactoferrin antibody positivity
HP:0033395.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against lactoferrin.

name: glomerular extracapillary fibrin
glomerular extracapillary fibrin
HP:0033396.def: Presence of ropey, eosinophilic material (brght red on Trichrome staining) consistent with extracapillary fibrin outside of capillary lumina.

name: bowman - space proteinaceous debris
bowman - space proteinaceous debris
HP:0033397.def: The presence of eosinophilic Periodic Acid Schiff (PAS)-positive cell free, protein-derived material occupying Bowman's space.

name: pleural plaque
pleural plaque
HP:0033398.def: Deposits of hyalinized collagen fibres in the parietal pleura (preferentially pleura adjacent to ribs, particularly the sixth through ninth ribs).

name: persistent fever
persistent fever
HP:0033399.def: Fever that persists longer than expected for an acute infectious disease. No precise threshold exists, and the clinical interpretation of fever is context-dependent, but as a rule of thumb, this term refers to fever that persists longer than 2-3 weeks.

name: acute abdomen
acute abdomen
HP:0033400.def: A sudden onset of abdominal pain with associated nausea or vomiting. The acute abdomen may be caused by an infection, inflammation, vascular occlusion, or obstruction.

name: tissue ischemia
tissue ischemia
HP:0033401.def: Ischemia is defined as a restriction of arterial blood supply to a tissue associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolis requirements of the tissue. Depending on the involved tissues, clinical manifestations may include pain, pallor, lack of pulse, coldness, paresthesia, and paralysis. Additional associated manifestations include hemodynamic parameters (reduced blood pressure distal to the site of restricted arterial supply) and angiographic evidence of arterial occclusion.

name: digital ischemia
digital ischemia
HP:0033402.def: Restriction of arterial blood supply to a digit (finger or toe) associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the digit. Clinical manifestations may include pain, pallor, lack of pulse, coldness, paresthesia, and paralysis.

name: testicular ischemia
testicular ischemia
HP:0033403.def: Restriction of arterial blood supply to a testis associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the tissue. Clinical manifestations may include pain and swelling of the affected testis.

name: intestinal ischemia
intestinal ischemia
HP:0033404.def: Restriction of arterial blood supply to the intestine associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the tissue. Acute intestinal ischemia can involve the small or large intestine, and usually presents with sudden severe non-specific abdominal pain.

name: abnormal circulating organic amino compound concentration
abnormal circulate organic amino compound concentration
HP:0033405.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of an organic amino compound, defined as a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

name: elevated circulating o - phosphoethanolamine concentration
elevate circulate o - phosphoethanolamine concentration
HP:0033406.def: An increased concentration of o-phosphoethanolamine in the blood circulation.

name: elevated urine acetoacetic acid level
elevate urine acetoacetic acid level
HP:0033407.def: Elevated amount of acetoacetic acid in the urine.

name: elevated circulating acetoacetic acid concentration
elevate circulate acetoacetic acid concentration
HP:0033408.def: An increased level of acetoacetic acid in the blood circulation. Acetoacetic acid is one of the predominant ketone bodies.

name: elevated urinary 2 - hydroxybutyric acid
elevate urinary 2 - hydroxybutyric acid
HP:0033409.def: An increased amount of 2-hydroxybutyric acid in the urine.

name: elevated circulating cartilage oligomeric matrix protein concentration
elevate circulating cartilage oligomeric matrix protein concentration
HP:0033410.def: An increased blood concentration of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP).

name: lower extremity akinesia
low extremity akinesia
HP:0033411.def: Inability to initiate changes in activity or movement and to perform ordinary volitional movements rapidly and easily in the lower extremities.

name: upper extremity akinesia
upper extremity akinesia
HP:0033412.def: Inability to initiate changes in activity or movement and to perform ordinary volitional movements rapidly and easily in the upper extremities.

name: upper extremity hypokinesia
upper extremity hypokinesia
HP:0033413.def: Abnormally diminished movement of the upper extremities. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.

name: lower extremity hypokinesia
low extremity hypokinesia
HP:0033414.def: Abnormally diminished movement of the lower extremities. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.

name: cardiac tamponade
cardiac tamponade
HP:0033415.def: The accumulation of pericardial fluid with subsequent compression of all cardiac chambers which prevents cardiac filling.

name: hip adductor weakness
hip adductor weakness
HP:0033416.def: Reduced ability to bring the leg toward the midline of the body.

name: elevated circulating hydroxybutyric acid concentration
elevate circulate hydroxybutyric acid concentration
HP:0033417.def: An increased concentration in the blood circulation of a hydroxybutyric acid, that is, of a compound comprising a butyric acid core carrying at least one hydroxy substituent.

name: elevated circulating 2 - hydroxybutyric acid concentration
elevate circulate 2 - hydroxybutyric acid concentration
HP:0033418.def: Elevation of the 2-hydroxybutyric acid concentration in the blood above the normal range.

name: elevated circulating 3 - hydroxybutyric acid concentration
elevate circulate 3 - hydroxybutyric acid concentration
HP:0033419.def: Elevation of the 3-hydroxybutyric acid concentration in the blood above the normal range.

name: pulmonary arterial plexiform lesion
pulmonary arterial plexiform lesion
HP:0033420.def: Focal proliferation of pulmonary artery endothelial cells, leading to the formation of complex capillary-like channels.

name: pulmonary artery intimal thickening
pulmonary artery intimal thicken
HP:0033421.def: Increased thickness of the intimal layer of the pulmonary artery. Throughout the pulmonary arterial tree, the thin intima consists of a non-fenestrated monolayer of endothelial cells lining the vessel lumen, as well as a sub-endothelial interstitium that extends to the internal elastic lamina. Intimal thickness in human lung ranges from 1-16% of total wall thickness. Pulmonary artery intimal thickening can be defined as a relative intima thickness to the thickness of the vessel wall of over 10%.

name: pulmonary artery adventitial fibrosis
pulmonary artery adventitial fibrosis
HP:0033422.def: Increased amount of collagen, proteoglycans, and other extracellular matrix proteins resulting in scarring and thickening in the adventia of the pulmonary arterial tree.

name: pulmonary arterial hypertension with positive acute response to no challenge
pulmonary arterial hypertension with positive acute response to no challenge
HP:0033423.def: A form of pulmonary arterial hypertension in which there is a reduction of mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) at leasy 10 mmHg to reach an absolute value of mPAP not more than 40 mmHg with an increased or unchanged cardiac output (CO) in response to inhaled nitric oxide at 10-20 ppm.

name: pulmonary arterial hypertension with lack of acute response to no challenge
pulmonary arterial hypertension with lack of acute response to no challenge
HP:0033424.def: A form of pulmonary arterial hypertension with lack of adequate hemodynamic response to NO challenge (adequate response is defined as a reduction of mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) of at least 10 mmHg to reach an absolute value of mPAP 40 mmHg or less with an increased or unchanged cardiac output (CO) in response to inhaled nitric oxide at 10-20 ppm).

name: periungual erythema
periungual erythema
HP:0033425.def: Erythema (redness of the skin caused by hyperemia in superficial capillaries) in the region surrounding a fingernail or toe nail.

name: pulmonary air embolism
pulmonary air embolism
HP:0033426.def: Venous air embolism is a consequence of air being introduced into the venous circulation, and subsequently to the right heart, and pulmonary circulation. When small amounts of air reach pulmonary circulation they can be removed by gas diffusion across the arteriolar wall into the alveoli, amounts of gas exceeding 50 ml can cause pulmonary outflow tract obstruction with or without concomitant arterial embolisation.

name: pulmonary capillary angioectasia
pulmonary capillary angioectasia
HP:0033427.def: Focal accumulation of dilated pulmonary capillaries.

name: systemic autoinflammation
systemic autoinflammation
HP:0033428.def: Dysregulation of the innate immune system characterized by systemic pathobiology, i.e., with symptoms that can affect the entire body.

name: neuroinflammation
neuroinflammation
HP:0033429.def: Activation of the brain's innate immune system in response to an inflammatory challenge and is characterized by a host of cellular and molecular changes within the brain.

name: non - infectious meningitis
non - infectious meningitis
HP:0033430.def: Inflammation of the layers of tissue that cover the brain and spinal cord (meninges) and of the fluid-filled space between the meninges (subarachnoid space) when it is caused by disorders that are not infections or by drugs or vaccines.

name: cytomegalovirus colitis
cytomegalovirus colitis
HP:0033431.def: A form of cytomegalovirus infection characterized by infection and inflammation of the colon.

name: ileocecal ulcer
ileocecal ulcer
HP:0033433.def: An erosion of the mucous membrane in the region connecting the ileum and cecum.

name: nasal septum perforation
nasal septum perforation
HP:0033434.def: A full-thickness defect of the nasal septum.

name: abnormal circulating keto acid concentration
abnormal circulate keto acid concentration
HP:0033435.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of a keto acid in the blood circulation. Keto acids or ketoacids are organic compounds that contain a carboxylic acid group and a ketone group.

name: elevated circulating 3 - methyl - 2 - oxovaleric acid concentration
elevate circulate 3 - methyl - 2 - oxovaleric acid concentration
HP:0033436.def: The concentration of 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acidin the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating 4 - methyl - 2 - oxopentanoic acid concentration
elevate circulate 4 - methyl - 2 - oxopentanoic acid concentration
HP:0033437.def: The concentration of 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: increased circulating alpha - ketoisocaproic acid concentration
increase circulate alpha - ketoisocaproic acid concentration

name: elevated circulating myoglobin concentration
elevate circulate myoglobin concentration
HP:0033438.def: An increased blood concentration of myoglobin.

name: elevated circulating decenoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate decenoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033439.def: Concentration of decenoylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating octenoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate octenoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033440.def: Concentration of octenoylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating hexanoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate hexanoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033441.def: Concentration of hexanoylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating glutarylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate glutarylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033442.def: Concentration of glutarylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: elevated circulating c5 - dc acylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate c5 - dc acylcarnitine concentration

name: elevated circulating propionylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate propionylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033443.def: Increased concentration of propionylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating dodecanoylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate dodecanoylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033444.def: Concentration of dodecanoylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: reduced circulating acylcarnitine concentration
reduce circulate acylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033445.def: An abnormally reduced concentration in the blood circulation of acylcarnitine, which is produced by reversible esterification of the 3-hydroxyl group of carnitine.

name: elevated circulating butyrylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate butyrylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033446.def: Concentration of O-butyrylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating isovalerylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate isovalerylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033447.def: Concentration of O-isovalerylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: increased mid - arm muscle circumference
increase mid - arm muscle circumference
HP:0033448.def: Elevation of the midupper arm circumference midway between the acromion and olecranon processes of the ulna with the use of a steel or fiberglass tape. This measure is a proxy for the muscle mass of the upper arm and can be used as a part of the assessment of nutritional status in children.

name: decreased mid - arm muscle circumference
decrease mid - arm muscle circumference
HP:0033449.def: Reduction of the midupper arm circumference midway between the acromion and olecranon processes of the ulna with the use of a steel or fiberglass tape. This measure is a proxy for the muscle mass of the upper arm and can be used as a part of the assessment of nutritional status in children.

name: abnormal circulating prealbumin concentration
abnormal circulate prealbumin concentration
HP:0033450.def: Any deviation from normal concentration of albumin in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating prealbumin concentration
increase circulate prealbumin concentration
HP:0033451.def: An elevation above the normal concentration of prealbumin in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating prealbumin concentration
decrease circulate prealbumin concentration
HP:0033452.def: A reduction from the normal concentration of prealbumin in the blood circulation.

name: limited neck extension
limited neck extension
HP:0033453.def: Reduced abilty to move the head back towards the ceiling so that one is looking upwards.

name: tube feeding
tube feeding
HP:0033454.def: Feeding problem necessitating food and nutrient delivery via a tube.

name: obsolete elevated urinary dicarboxylic acid level
obsolete elevate urinary dicarboxylic acid level
elevated urine keto acid level
elevate urine keto acid level
HP:0033456.def: Increased amount of a keta acid in the urine.

name: elevated urine 3 - methyl - 2 - oxovaleric acid level
elevate urine 3 - methyl - 2 - oxovaleric acid level
HP:0033457.def: Increased amount of 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid in the urine.

name: elevated urine 4 - methyl - 2 - oxopentanoic acid level
elevate urine 4 - methyl - 2 - oxopentanoic acid level
HP:0033458.def: Increased amount of 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid in the urine.
synonym: increased urine alpha - ketoisocaproic acid level
increase urine alpha - ketoisocaproic acid level

name: decreased circulating apolipoprotein concentration
decrease circulate apolipoprotein concentration
HP:0033459.def: Reduced concentration in the blood circulation of a lipid-transport protein (apoliprotein).

name: increased circulating apolipoprotein circulation
increase circulate apolipoprotein circulation
HP:0033460.def: Elevated concentration in the blood circulation of a lipid-transport protein (apoliprotein).

name: elevated circulating 3 - hydroxylinoleylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate 3 - hydroxylinoleylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033461.def: Increased concentration of 3-hydroxylinoleylcarnitine in the blood circulation.
synonym: elevated plasma 3 - oh - linoleylcarnitine , c18:1 - oh
elevate plasma 3 - oh - linoleylcarnitine , c18:1 - oh

name: elevated circulating oleylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate oleylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033462.def: Increased concentration of oleylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating 3 - hydroxypalmitoleylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate 3 - hydroxypalmitoleylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033464.def: Concentration of 3-hydroxypalmitoleylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: elevated plasma 3 - oh - palmitoleylcarnitine , c16:1 - oh
elevate plasma 3 - oh - palmitoleylcarnitine , c16:1 - oh

name: weak grip
weak grip
HP:0033466.def: Reduced grip strength. Gripping is the motion by which the hand tightly grasps an object or other hand.

name: low 10 - minute apgar score
low 10 - minute apgar score
HP:0033467.def: A normal APGAR score can be coded as 'not Low 10-minute APGAR score'.

name: limited shoulder abduction
limited shoulder abduction
HP:0033475.def: Decreased ability to move the arm away from the midline of the body.

name: extractable nuclear antigen positivity
extractable nuclear antigen positivity
HP:0033476.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against extractable nuclear components that are referred to as extractable because they can be extracted from cell nuclei with saline solution.

name: abnormal circulating lipoprotein lipase concentration
abnormal circulate lipoprotein lipase concentration
HP:0033477.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of lipoprotein lipase in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating lipoprotein lipase concentration
increase circulate lipoprotein lipase concentration
HP:0033478.def: Increased concentration of lipoprotein lipase in the blood circulation.

name: hypobilirubinemia
hypobilirubinemia
HP:0033480.def: Concentration of bilirubin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: limited lateral neck flexion
limited lateral neck flexion
HP:0033481.def: Reduced range of motion resulting in decreased ability to move the ear toward the top of the shoulder.

name: limited shoulder flexion
limited shoulder flexion
HP:0033482.def: A reduced ability to flex the shoulder. Shoulder flexion is the motion that moves the arms from a resting position by the side of the body to a position above the head.

name: podocyte infolding
podocyte infolding
HP:0033483.def: Folding of cytoplasmic processes of podocytes into the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) with thickening of the lamina densa and microspheres and/or microtubular structures within the GBM.

name: elevated circulating linoleylcarnitine concentration
elevate circulate linoleylcarnitine concentration
HP:0033484.def: Increased concentration of linoleylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

name: glomerular basement membrane disruption
glomerular basement membrane disruption
HP:0033485.def: A point of rupture in the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) where the discontinuous portions of GBM are still identifiable with a basement membrane stain such as Periodic acid Schiff (PAS) or silver.
synonym: disruption of the glomerular basement membrane
disruption of the glomerular basement membrane

name: abnormal glomerular basement membrane texture
abnormal glomerular basement membrane texture
HP:0033486.def: Anomalous appearance or structure of the surface of the glomerular basement membrane.

name: glomerular basement membranes powdery deposit
glomerular basement membrane powdery deposit
HP:0033487.def: Punctate electron-dense material typically in a band-like distribution along the lamina rara interna and within tubular basement membranes within the subendothelial aspect of the glomerular basement membrane.
synonym: glomerular basement membranes with powdery deposit
glomerular basement membrane with powdery deposit

name: glomerular endocapillary leukocyte hypercellularity
glomerular endocapillary leukocyte hypercellularity
HP:0033488.def: Increased number of leukocytes internal to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), but not limited to within glomerular capillaries.
synonym: glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity consisting of leukocytes
glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity consist of leukocyte

name: glomerular endocapillary neutrophil hypercellularity
glomerular endocapillary neutrophil hypercellularity
HP:0033489.def: Increased number of neutrophils internal to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), but not limited to within glomerular capillaries.

name: glomerular endocapillary foam - cell hypercellularity
glomerular endocapillary foam - cell hypercellularity
HP:0033490.def: Presence of lipid-filled cells, often a macrophage, with a vacuolated appearance in the glomerulus often occupying the endocapillary space.

name: global mesangial sclerosis
global mesangial sclerosis
HP:0033491.def: A generalized global (over 80%) increase of mesangial matrix that is present throughout the mesangial stalk (with or without associated mesangial hypercellularity).

name: podocyte cytoskeletal condensation
podocyte cytoskeletal condensation
HP:0033492.def: Reorganization of podocyte cytoskeletal proteins at the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) aspect of the cell, with associated cytoplasmic electron density at the GBM aspect of the podocyte.

name: mesangial matrix expansion
mesangial matrix expansion
HP:0033493.def: Increased mesangial extracellular material with interspace width of over 2 mesangial cell nuclei, in one or more peripheral mesangial areas.

name: glomerular basement membrane amyloid spicule
glomerular basement membrane amyloid spicule
HP:0033494.def: Amyloid spicules are projections of typically silver-positive material from the outer aspect of the glomerular capillary wall, perpendicular to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), most often caused by amyloidosis with the latter confirmed by additional stains.

name: segmental glomerulosclerosis
segmental glomerulosclerosis
HP:0033495.def: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration and can include hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells, podocyte depletion, halo and adhesion of the tuft to the Bowman capsule.

name: perihilar segmental glomerulosclerosis
perihilar segmental glomerulosclerosis
HP:0033496.def: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration is present at the vascular pole, involving less than 50% of the tuft. It can be accompanied by other descriptors such as hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells, podocyte depletion, halo and adhesion of the tuft to the Bowman's capsule.

name: tip variant segmental glomerulosclerosis
tip variant segmental glomerulosclerosis
HP:0033497.def: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft characterized by an adhesion at the tip of the glomerular tuft abutting the proximal tubular taek-off can be accompanied by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration at the glomerular tip. Features including hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells can also be observed.

name: segmental glomerulosclerosis away from the vascular and tubular poles
segmental glomerulosclerosis away from the vascular and tubular pole
HP:0033498.def: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft characterized by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration at neirhter the tubular or vascular poles. Features including hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells can also be observed.

name: glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposits
glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposit
HP:0033499.def: Electron-dense deposits in the lamina densa with a ribbon or a sausage structure.

name: subendothelial glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposits
subendothelial glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposit
HP:0033500.def: Electron dense deposits in the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) subendothelial space associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an increase in thickness. This feature can be associated with GBM remodeling along the endothelial aspect.

name: subepithelial glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposits
subepithelial glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposit
HP:0033501.def: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting a diffuse and relativly uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate) with exogenous material deposited between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the GBM and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM.

name: abnormal esterified to free carnitine ratio
abnormal esterify to free carnitine ratio
HP:0033502.def: Any deviation from the normal ratio of acylcarnitine (i.e., esterified carnitine) to free carnitine.

name: elevated csf fumarate concentration
elevate csf fumarate concentration
HP:0033503.def: An increased concentration of fumarate, an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, in the cebrebrospinal fluid.

name: elevated circulating fumarate concentration
elevate circulate fumarate concentration
HP:0033504.def: An increased concentration of fumarate, an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, in the blood circulation.

name: livedo reticularis
livedo reticularis
HP:0033505.def: Livedo reticularis is characterized by the presence of a bluish purple, mottled or netlike pattern in unbroken circles on the skin. Exposure to cold environments usually intensifies the vascular pattern. Presumably, the condition results from slow or stagnant blood flow, vessel-wall pathology, and decreased oxygen tension.

name: increased esterified to free carnitine ratio
increase esterify to free carnitine ratio
HP:0033506.def: An elevated ratio of acylcarnitine (i.e., esterified carnitine) to free carnitine.

name: decreased esterified to free carnitine ratio
decrease esterify to free carnitine ratio
HP:0033507.def: A reduced ratio of acylcarnitine (i.e., esterified carnitine) to free carnitine.

name: ebv meningitis
ebv meningitis
HP:0033508.def: Inflammation of the meninges related to infection by Epstein-Barr virus.

name: ebv encephalitis
ebv encephalitis
HP:0033509.def: Inflamation of the brain related to infection by Epstein-Barr virus.

name: cutaneous horn
cutaneous horn
HP:0033510.def: A cutaneous horn is a keratinized non-malignant protrusion on the surface of the skin. Diagnosis is established by biopsy of the horn and biopsy of the horn and the underlying skin.

name: addictive substance use
addictive substance use
HP:0033511.def: Chronic compulsive drug seeking and continued use despite harmful consequences.

name: addictive stimulant use
addictive stimulant use
HP:0033512.def: Addiction to a stimulant drug is defined as a drug that typically increases alertness, attention, and energy while also elevating blood pressure, heart rate, and breathing.

name: addictive amphetamine use
addictive amphetamine use
HP:0033514.def: Addiction to amphetamine or dextroamphetamine is a serious concern.

name: paradoxical embolism
paradoxical embolism
HP:0033520.def: Paradoxical embolism describes the passage of a venous or right-sided cardiac thrombus into the arterial or systemic circulation.

name: nasal dryness
nasal dryness
HP:0033521.def: A lack of humidification of the nasal mucosa.

name: cerebral cavernous malformation
cerebral cavernous malformation
HP:0033522.def: A cerebral cavernous malformation (also known as cavernoma, cavernous angioma, cavernous hemangioma) is a collection of structurally abnormal slow-flow capillaries predominantly in the central nervous system. These are multiple mulberry-like distended caverns of dilated thin-walled capillaries without the normal intervening brain parenchymal architecture. Often, individual cavernomas are surrounded by hemosiderin representing remote oozing due to the abnormal capillaries.

name: abnormal sperm principal piece morphology
abnormal sperm principal piece morphology
HP:0033523.def: A structural anomaly of the part of the sperm flagellum that is distal to the sperm midpiece and mitochondrial sheath and which leads into the end piece.

name: abnormal sperm axoneme morphology
abnormal sperm axoneme morphology
HP:0033524.def: Abnormal structure of the sperm axonemal structure which consists of a ring of nine microtubular doublets and a central pair of microtubules, giving the classical 9+2 microtubular arrangement. The axoneme contains a central pair of microtubules (C1 and C2) that are connected by a bridge-like structure forming the central pair complex (CPC). Each of the nine outer doublets is composed of type A and B microtubules and connected by radial spokes to the CPC.

name: absent sperm axoneme central pair complex
absent sperm axoneme central pair complex
HP:0033525.def: Absense of the central pair of microtubules in the sperm axoneme, thereby forming a 9+0 pattern instead of the normal 9+2 pattern.

name: limited ankle dorsiflexion
limited ankle dorsiflexion
HP:0033526.def: Reduced ability to move the foot up toward the shin.

name: decreased gonadotropin - stimulated testosterone - to - androstenedione ratio
decrease gonadotropin - stimulate testosterone - to - androstenedione ratio
HP:0033527.def: A reduced amount of testosterone relative in androstenedione in the blood circulation following administration of hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin).
synonym: decreased plasma testosterone - to - androstenedione ratio
decrease plasma testosterone - to - androstenedione ratio

name: abnormal cardiac output
abnormal cardiac output
HP:0033528.def: A deviation from normal Cardiac output, which is defined as the amount of blood pumped by the heart minute and is the mechanism whereby blood flows around the body, especially providing blood flow to the brain and other vital organs.

name: abnormal cardiac index
abnormal cardiac index
HP:0033529.def: Any deviation from the normal value of the cardiac index, defined as cardiac output divided by body surface area.

name: increased cardiac index
increase cardiac index
HP:0033530.def: An elevated cardiac index, defined as cardiac output divided by body surface area.

name: decreased cardiac index
decrease cardiac index
HP:0033531.def: A reduced cardiac index, defined as cardiac output divided by body surface area.

name: decreased cardiac output
decrease cardiac output
HP:0033532.def: A decreased volume of blood pumped by the left and right ventricle, per unit time. Cardiac output (CO) is the product of the heart rate (HR), i.e. the number of heartbeats per minute (bpm), and the stroke volume (SV), which is the volume of blood pumped from the ventricle per beat.

name: increased cardiac output
increase cardiac output
HP:0033533.def: An increased volume of blood pumped by the left and right ventricle, per unit time. Cardiac output (CO) is the product of the heart rate (HR), i.e. the number of heartbeats per minute (bpm), and the stroke volume (SV), which is the volume of blood pumped from the ventricle per beat.

name: increased circulating brain natriuretic peptide concentration
increase circulate brain natriuretic peptide concentration
HP:0033534.def: An increased concentration of brain natriuretic peptide in the blood circulation.

name: reduced platelet dense granules
reduce platelet dense granule
HP:0033535.def: Decreased number of platelet dense granules, a type of platelet organelle.

name: reduced platelet alpha granules
reduce platelet alpha granule
HP:0033536.def: A reduced number of platelet alpha granules.

name: mosaic pulmonary attenuation pattern
mosaic pulmonary attenuation pattern
HP:0033537.def: Mosaic attenuation refers to heterogeneous areas of differing pulmonary attenuation on CT imaging.

name: aortic annulus calcification
aortic annulus calcification
HP:0033538.def: Pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aortic annulus, a fibrous ring-like structure found at the insertion point of the basal attachments of the aortic valve leaflets within the left ventricular outflow tract.

name: bilateral apical pulmonary fibrosis
bilateral apical pulmonary fibrosis
HP:0033539.def: A reticular pattern of linear or lineonodular densities in apical portions of both the right and left lungs seen initially on high-resolution computed tomography and in case of progression also on standard chest x-ray.

name: reversible airflow obstruction
reversible airflow obstruction
HP:0033540.def: Airflow obstruction with a significant response to a bronchodilator defined as an increase in FEV1 and/or FVC by 12 percent or more and by at least 200 mL.

name: irreversible airflow obstruction
irreversible airflow obstruction
HP:0033541.def: Airflow obstruction without significant response to a bronchodilator defined as an increase in FEV1 and/or FVC by 12 percent or more and by at least 200 mL.

name: bronchial wall thickening
bronchial wall thickening
HP:0033542.def: Radiological appearance of increased density around the walls of a bronchus or large bronchiole. This feature is thought to be related to edema involving the bronchial wall as well as the peribronchial interstitial space. If the cross section of a bronchus is captured in a radiograph or computed tomography image, it is said to have the appearance of a donut because of the central lucency representing the airway of the bronchus surrounded by a circular region of increased density.

name: addictive nicotine use
addictive nicotine use
HP:0033543.def: Nicotine addiction can be defined as a chronic, compulsive craving for nicotine and continued usage despite harmful consequences.

name: mesangial fibril deposition
mesangial fibril deposition
HP:0033544.def: Extracellular mesangial accumulation of slender proteinaceous fibers.

name: mesangial fibrillary deposits
mesangial fibrillary deposit
HP:0033545.def: Extracellular mesangial aggregates composed of randomly arranged, straight, non-branching fibrils that are thicker than amyloid fibrils (average diameter about 20 nm) and are often admixed with smudgy, electron-dense material.

name: mesangial microfibril deposition
mesangial microfibril deposition
HP:0033546.def: Unbranched noncollagenous microfibrils within the mesangial matrix, composed of proteins not present within the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), most notably fibrillin-1, that attach to mesangial cells and GBM structural proteins.

name: mesangial immunotactoid deposits
mesangial immunotactoid deposit
HP:0033547.def: Extracellular mesangial aggregates composed of non-branching fibrils, focally parralel over 30 nM in diameter. The term immunotactoid refers to highly organized immune depositions appearing as rod-like microtubular structures in ultrastructural examination.

name: mesangial amyloid deposition
mesangial amyloid deposition
HP:0033548.def: Extracellular mesangial aggregates composed of fine, randomly oriented, non-branching fibrils 8-12 nm in diameter, often forming a cottony mass.

name: nodular mesangiosclerosis
nodular mesangiosclerosis
HP:0033549.def: Lobular, round to oval mesangial lesions with an acellular hyaline/matrix core surrounded by compressed mesangial nuclei.

name: necrotizing pulmonary granulomatosis
necrotizing pulmonary granulomatosis
HP:0033550.def: A granuloma that is associated with necrotic changes. Caseation necrosis is defined as a region in granulomas with eosinophilic, granular and cheese-like cellular debris with necrosis. The word caseous itself means pertaining or related to cheese, and comes from the Latin word caseus, meaning cheese.

name: non - necrotizing pulmonary granulomatosis
non - necrotizing pulmonary granulomatosis
HP:0033551.def: A granuloma located in the lung that is not associated with necrotic changes.

name: chronic villitis
chronic villitis
HP:0033552.def: Villitis of unknown etiology (synonymous with villitis of unknown aetiology) is a histologic diagnosis and, although it may have a variable distribution, evidence indicates that 3 parenchymal blocks will identify 62% of villitis, reaching an asymptote of 6 and 7 blocks identifying 85% of villitis. Villitis of unknown etiology by definition excludes those cases where an etiology is identified, such as viral or acute infections, and thus is preferred to the term nonspecific chronic villitis. It is usually lymphohistiocytic: although the presence of rare plasma cells does not exclude the diagnosis, thorough evaluation for an infectious etiology, such as cytomegalovirus, is required in a predominantly plasma cell villitis.

name: septic embolism
septic embolism
HP:0033553.def: Embolization of intravascular thrombus containing microorganisms into the distant tissues via arterial system.

name: anti - mi2 antibody positivity
anti - mi2 antibody positivity
HP:0033554.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against the Mi-2 antigen.

name: anti - ro / ss - a antibody positivity
anti - ro / s - a antibody positivity
HP:0033555.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against Ro/SSA autoantigens.

name: anti - nucleoporin 62 antibody positivity
anti - nucleoporin 62 antibody positivity
HP:0033556.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against nucleoporin 62.

name: anti - proteinase 3 antibody positivity
anti - proteinase 3 antibody positivity
HP:0033557.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against proteinase 3. Proteinase 3 (PR3) antigen is a 29-kD serine protease that exists as a protein triplet in human neutrophils

name: anti - histone antibody positivity
anti - histone antibody positivity
HP:0033558.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone antigens.

name: anti - myeloperoxidase antibody positivity
anti - myeloperoxidase antibody positivity
HP:0033559.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against myeloperoxidase.

name: anti - pm - scl antibody positivity
anti - pm - scl antibody positivity
HP:0033560.def: Anti-PM-Scl antibodies target components of RNA-processing exosome complex in the nucleolus. There are ten proteins in this complex and antibodies to eight of them are found at varying frequencies; PM/Scl-100, PM/Scl-75, hRrp4, hRrp42, hRrp46, hCs14, hRrp41, and hRrp40.

name: anti - bactericidal / permeability - increasing protein antibody positivity
anti - bactericidal / permeability - increase protein antibody positivity
HP:0033561.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against bactericidal/permeability-increasing protein (BPI). BPI is an endotoxin-binding host protein with important antibacterial effects against Gram-negative bacteria, such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa. BPI is a 55 kDalton protein that is most abundant in the azurophilic granules of neutrophils. BPI also acts as a target antigen for antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies.

name: anti - glycoprotein - 210 antibody positivity
anti - glycoprotein - 210 antibody positivity
HP:0033562.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against glycoprotein-210.

name: anti - tissue transglutaminase antibody positivity
anti - tissue transglutaminase antibody positivity
HP:0033563.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against tissue transglutaminase.

name: stasis dermatitis
stasis dermatitis
HP:0033564.def: Stasis dermatitis commonly occurs in older age. It is caused by venous hypertension resulting from retrograde flow due to incompetent venous valves, valve destruction, or obstruction of the venous system. Further tissue changes arise from an inflammatory process mediated by metalloproteinases, which are up-regulated by ferric ion from extravasated red blood cells. Stasis dermatitis presents initially as poorly demarcated erythematous plaques of the lower legs bilaterally, classically involving the medial malleolus.

name: anti - epidermal transglutaminase antibody positivity
anti - epidermal transglutaminase antibody positivity
HP:0033565.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against epidermal transglutaminase.
synonym: anti - epidermal transglutaminase ( anti - etg ) antibody
anti - epidermal transglutaminase ( anti - etg ) antibody

name: abnormal ventricular axis
abnormal ventricular axis
HP:0033566.def: Any deviation from the normal direction of the ventricular axis. The left ventricle makes up most of the heart muscle under normal circumstances and therefore generates the most electrical force visible on the EKG. The normal ventricular axis is directed downward and slightly towards the left. The ventricular axis can be determined by analyzing the QRS complex, which represents ventricular depolarization.

name: right axis deviation
right axis deviation
HP:0033567.def: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS axis falls between +90 degrees and 180 degrees, or beyond +100 degrees if the adult range is used.

name: left axis deviation
leave axis deviation
HP:0033568.def: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS axis falls between -30 degrees and -90 degrees.

name: extreme axis deviation
extreme axis deviation
HP:0033569.def: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS axis fall sbetween -90 degrees and 180 degrees. In this case, the ventricular vector is directed upward and to the right.

name: indeterminate ventricular axis
indeterminate ventricular axis
HP:0033570.def: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS complex is isoelectric or equiphasic in all leads with no dominant QRS deflection.

name: peripheral lung neovascularity
peripheral lung neovascularity
HP:0033571.def: The presence of small, tortuous, micronodular, serpiginous intrapulmonary vessels often in the subpleural lung or in proximity to centrilobular arterioles, coursing in directions inconsistent with known arteriolar anatomy.

name: anti - h1 antibody positivity
anti - h1 antibody positivity
HP:0033572.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H1.

name: anti - h4 antibody positivity
anti - h4 antibody positivity
HP:0033573.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H4.

name: anti - h3 antibody positivity
anti - h3 antibody positivity
HP:0033574.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H3.

name: anti - h2a antibody positivity
anti - h2a antibody positivity
HP:0033575.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H2A.

name: anti - h2b antibody positivity
anti - h2b antibody positivity
HP:0033576.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H2B.

name: in situ pulmonary artery thrombosis
in situ pulmonary artery thrombosis
HP:0033577.def: Localized thrombosis in pulmonary arteries frequently found in patients with idiopathic and hereditary pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease.

name: pre - capillary pulmonary hypertension
pre - capillary pulmonary hypertension
HP:0033578.def: Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension is a haemodynamic condition characterised by elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP over 20 mmHg) and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR 3 Wood units or more) accompanied by normal pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP not more than 15 mmHg).

name: decreased growth hormone responses to growth hormone - releasing hormone challenge
decreased growth hormone responses to growth hormone - release hormone challenge
HP:0033579.def: Insufficient growth hormone secretion following administration of growth hormone-releasing hormone.
synonym: impaired growth hormone secretory responses after growth hormone - releasing hormone challenge
impaired growth hormone secretory response after growth hormone - release hormone challenge

name: compound motor action potential abnormality
compound motor action potential abnormality
HP:0033580.def: An abnormal finding in a compound motor action potential measurement in EMG. Nerve conduction studies involve the application of a depolarising square wave electrical pulses to the skin over a peripheral nerve producing: (1) a propagated nerve action potential (NAP) recorded at a distant point over the same nerve: and (2) a compound muscle action potential (CMAP) arising from the activation of muscle fibres in a target muscle supplied by the nerve. In both cases these may be recorded with surface or needle electrodes. The CMAP is a summated voltage response from the individual muscle fibre action potentials. The shortest latency of the CMAP is the time from stimulus artefact to onset of the response and is a biphasic response with an initial upward deflection followed by a smaller downward deflection. The CMAP amplitude is measured from baseline to negative peak (the neurophysiological convention is that negative voltage is demonstrated by an upward deflection) and measured in millivolts (mV).

name: absent peripheral lymph nodes in presence of infection
absent peripheral lymph node in presence of infection
HP:0033581.def: The absence of any palpable lymph nodes in the presence of symptoms suggesting infection in that drainage area should raise suspicion for immunodeficiency diseases.

name: pulmonary interstitial lymphocyte infiltration
pulmonary interstitial lymphocyte infiltration
HP:0033582.def: Abnormal accumulation of lymphocytes in the interstitium of the lung.

name: follicular bronchiolitis
follicular bronchiolitis
HP:0033583.def: Follicular bronchiolitis is a polyclonal hyperplasia of bronchiolar associated lymphoid tissue characterized by the is characterized by the development of lymphoid follicles with germinal centers in walls of the small airways.

name: nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
HP:0033584.def: Temporally uniform (all lesions are in the same stage of evolution) pattern of diffuse inflammatory interstitial process, mostly symmetric over the entire lung, involving mainly the alveolar septa.

name: fibrotic non - specific interstitial pneumonia
fibrotic non - specific interstitial pneumonia
HP:0033585.def: A type of non-specific interstitial pneumonia in which interstitial thickening is due to uniform dense or loose fibrosis and mild chronic inflammation.

name: cellular non - specific interstitial pneumonia
cellular non - specific interstitial pneumonia
HP:0033586.def: A type of non-specific interstitial pneumonia in which interstitial thickening is mainly due to infiltration of inflammatory cells and type II pneumocyte hyperplasia.

name: vulvar abscess
vulvar abscess
HP:0033587.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the vulvar region.

name: labial adhesion
labial adhesion
HP:0033588.def: Synechia vulvae (adhesions of the labia minora) are characterized by a complete or partial fusion of the labia minora in the midline.

name: flatulence
flatulence
HP:0033589.def: Passage of excessive amounts of gas and the feeling of abdominal fullness and bloating.

name: inguinal abscess
inguinal abscess
HP:0033590.def: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the groin (inguinal region).

name: staghorn calculus
staghorn calculus
HP:0033591.def: Large branching stones that fill part of all of the renal pelvis and renal calyces and they can be complete or partial depending on the level of occupancy of the collecting system.

name: anti - h3 - h4 antibody positivity
anti - h3 - h4 antibody positivity
HP:0033592.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against the H3-H4 histone dimer.

name: anti - h2a - h2b antibody positivity
anti - h2a - h2b antibody positivity
HP:0033593.def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against the H2A-H2B histone dimer.

name: elevated urinary 7 - biopterin level
elevate urinary 7 - biopterin level
HP:0033594.def: An abnormally increased amount of 7-biopterin in the urine.

name: elevated circulating globotriaosylceramide concentration
elevate circulate globotriaosylceramide concentration
HP:0033595.def: Increased concentration of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) in the blood circulation. Globotriaosylceramide, also named ceramidetrihexoside, is the primary lipid storage in Fabry disease.

name: elevated urinary 3 - methylcrotonylglycine level
elevate urinary 3 - methylcrotonylglycine level
HP:0033596.def: An abnormally increased amount of 3-methylcrotonylglycine in the urine.

name: decreased mucosal sucrase - isomaltase activity
decrease mucosal sucrase - isomaltase activity
HP:0033597.def: Reduced activity of the linked disaccharidase, sucrase-isomaltase, which is a glycoprotein localized to the brush border membrane of small intestinal villi.

name: fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposits
fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposit
HP:0033598.def: Fibrillar deposits located between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM. This feature is associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

name: glomerular amyloid subepithelial deposits
glomerular amyloid subepithelial deposit
HP:0033599.def: A type of fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by extracellular aggregates composed of fine, randomly oriented, non-branching fibrils 8-12 nm in diameter, often forming a cottony mass. This feature is associated with a prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting an diffuse and relativly uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

name: fibrillary glomerular subepithelial deposits
fibrillary glomerular subepithelial deposit
HP:0033600.def: A type of fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by extracellular aggregates of randomly arranged, straight, non-branching fibrils that are thicker than amyloid fibrils (average diameter about 20 nm) and are often admixed with smudgy, electron-dense material. This feature is associated with a prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting an diffuse and relativly uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

name: glomerular subepithelial immune - complex deposits
glomerular subepithelial immune - complex deposit
HP:0033601.def: A type of glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by finely granular material deposited between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM and corresponding to immunoglobulin and/or complement by immunofluorescence/immunohistochemistry.
