synonym: myxomatous change within arcuate vein intima / media
myxomatous change within arcuate vein intima / medium

name: arcuate vein intima / medial amyloidosis
arcuate vein intima / medial amyloidosis
HP:0033882.def: Amorphous extracellular substance in the inner or middle layer of the arcuate veins of the kidney. Amyloidosis stains Congo-red positive with typically an apple green birerfingence on polarization microscopy, and 8-12 nm fibrils on electron microscopy.
synonym: amyloidosis within arcuate vein intima / media
amyloidosis within arcuate vein intima / medium

name: abnormal cortical radial artery morphology
abnormal cortical radial artery morphology
HP:0033883.def: Any structural anomaly of the radial arteries that branch off at right angles from the arcuate artery and carry blood toward the cortex of the kidney.

name: abnormal cortical radial artery lumen morphology
abnormal cortical radial artery lumen morphology
HP:0033884.def: Abnormal structural characteristics of the interior space of the cortical radial arteries of the kidney.

name: cortical radial artery lumen cholesterol emboli
cortical radial artery lumen cholesterol embolus
HP:0033885.def: Needle-like or slit-like clefts within the interior space of cortical radial arteries (interlobular arteries) of the kidney. Cholesterol emboli are visualized as clear spaces (cholesterol clefts) where the cholesterol crystals have been dissolved by routine processing. Acute lesions can be accompanied by inflammation and fibrin.

name: abnormal arcuate artery intima / media morphology
abnormal arcuate artery intima / medium morphology
HP:0033886.def: Anomalous structure of the inner or middle layer of the arc-shaped arteries located at the border of the renal cortex and renal medulla.
synonym: abnormalities of the arcuate arterial intima / media
abnormality of the arcuate arterial intima / medium

name: cortical radial artery intimal / medial amyloidosis
cortical radial artery intimal / medial amyloidosis
HP:0033887.def: Amorphous extracellular substance in the glomerular, interstitial or vascular compartments of the interlobular arteries of the kidney. Congo-red positive with typically an apple green birerfingence on polarization microscopy, and 8-12 nm fibrils on electron microscopy
synonym: amyloidosis within interlobular arterial intima / media
amyloidosis within interlobular arterial intima / medium

name: abnormal cortical radial artery intima / media morphology
abnormal cortical radial artery intima / medium morphology
HP:0033888.def: Any structural anomaly of the inner or middle layer of the cortical radial arteries (also known as interlobular arteries) of the kidney.
synonym: abnormalities of the interlobular arterial intima / media
abnormality of the interlobular arterial intima / medium

name: abnormal renal arteriole morphology
abnormal renal arteriole morphology
HP:0033889.def: Any structural anomaly of the glomerular arterioles. The interlobar arteries of the kidney branch into arcuate arteries, cortical radiate arteries, and then into afferent arterioles. After passing through the renal corpuscle, the capillaries form the efferent arteriole. The afferent and efferent arterioles are difficult to distinguish histologically and are thus both included in this term and its descendents.

name: abnormal renal arteriole lumen morphology
abnormal renal arteriole lumen morphology
HP:0033890.def: Abnormal structural characteristics of the interior space (lumen) of renal arterioles.

name: renal arteriolar lumen cholesterol emboli
renal arteriolar lumen cholesterol embolus
HP:0033891.def: Needle-like or slit-like clefts within the interior space of arterioles of the kidney. Cholesterol emboli are visualized as clear spaces (cholesterol clefts) where the cholesterol crystals have been dissolved by routine processing. Acute lesions can be accompanied by inflammation and fibrin.
synonym: cholesterol emboli within the arteriolar lumen
cholesterol embolus within the arteriolar lumen

name: abnormal renal arteriole intima / media morphology
abnormal renal arteriole intima / medium morphology
HP:0033892.def: Any structural anomaly located in the inner or middle layer of the arterioles of the kidney.

name: renal arteriolar lumen organized thrombi
renal arteriolar lumen organize thrombus
HP:0033893.def: Thrombi containg fibrous tissue and capillary-like vascular channels located within the lumen of the arterioles of the kidney.

name: renal arteriolar intraluminal thrombi
renal arteriolar intraluminal thrombus
HP:0033894.def: Mixture of fibrin, red blood cells, platelets partly or completely occluding the vascular lumen of the arterioles of the kidney.

name: abnormal renal arteriole endothelium morphology
abnormal renal arteriole endothelium morphology
HP:0033895.def: Any structural anomaly of the lining (endothelium) of the arterioles of the kidney.

name: abnormal arcuate artery lumen morphology
abnormal arcuate artery lumen morphology
HP:0033896.def: Abnormal structural characteristics of the interior space (lumen) of the arcuate artery of the kidney.
synonym: abnormalities of the arcuate arterial lumen
abnormality of the arcuate arterial lumen

name: arcuate artery lumen cholesterol emboli
arcuate artery lumen cholesterol embolus
HP:0033897.def: Needle-like or slit-like clefts within the interior space of arcuate arteries of the kidney. Cholesterol emboli are visualized as clear spaces (cholesterol clefts) where the cholesterol crystals have been dissolved by routine processing. Acute lesions can be accompanied by inflammation and fibrin.
synonym: cholesterol emboli within arcuate arterial lumen
cholesterol embolus within arcuate arterial lumen

name: arcuate artery intraluminal thrombi
arcuate artery intraluminal thrombus
HP:0033898.def: Mixture of fibrin, red blood cells, platelets partly or completely occluding the vascular lumen of the arcuate arteries of the kidney.
synonym: intraluminal thrombi within arcuate arterial lumen
intraluminal thrombus within arcuate arterial lumen

name: arcuate artery lumen organized thrombi
arcuate artery lumen organize thrombus
HP:0033899.def: Thrombi containg fibrous tissue and capillary-like vascular channels located within the lumen of the arcuate arteries of the kidney.
synonym: organised thrombi within arcuate arterial lumen
organise thrombus within arcuate arterial lumen
organized thrombi within arcuate arterial lumen
organize thrombus within arcuate arterial lumen

name: renal arteriole intima / media amyloidosis
renal arteriole intima / medium amyloidosis
HP:0033900.def: Amorphous extracellular substance in the inner or middle layer of renal arterioles. Amyloidosis stains Congo-red positive with typically an apple green birerfingence on polarization microscopy, and 8-12 nm fibrils on electron microscopy.
synonym: amyloidosis within renal arteriolar intima / media
amyloidosis within renal arteriolar intima / medium

name: abnormal arcuate artery endothelium morphology
abnormal arcuate artery endothelium morphology
HP:0033901.def: Any structural anomaly of the lining (endothelium) of the arcuate arteries of the kidney.

name: arcuate artery endotheliosis
arcuate artery endotheliosis
HP:0033902.def: Enlargement of endothelial cells of the arcuate arteries of the kidney because of cytoplasmic swelling.

name: arcuate artery endoarterial hypercellularity
arcuate artery endoarterial hypercellularity
HP:0033903.def: Proliferation of endothelial cells (increased number of cells) of the lining (endothelium) of the arcuate arteries of the kidney.

name: renal arteriole intima / media hyalinosis
renal arteriole intima / medium hyalinosis
HP:0033904.def: Accumulation of amorphous, eosinophilic, glassy, periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)-positive, silver-negative material (hyalinosis) in the inner or middle layer of the renal arterioles. This feature may be accompanied by hypertrophy of the media and intima fibrosis.

name: arcuate artery intima / media arteriosclerosis
arcuate artery intima / medium arteriosclerosis
HP:0033905.def: Thickening of the intima of the arcuate arteries of the kidney with fibrosis and/or duplication of the elastic lamina.
synonym: arteriosclerosis within arcuate arterial intima / media
arteriosclerosis within arcuate arterial intima / medium

name: renal intimal / medial arteriolitis
renal intimal / medial arteriolitis
HP:0033906.def: Inflammation of an arteriole of the kidney, which may involve only the intma or can be transmural.

name: renal arteriole intima / media arteriolosclerosis
renal arteriole intima / medium arteriolosclerosis
HP:0033907.def: Thickening of the intima of renal arterioles with fibrosis and/or duplication of the elastic lamina.

name: renal arteriole medial atrophy
renal arteriole medial atrophy
HP:0033908.def: Atrophy (wasting, decreased thickness) of of the middle layer of the arterioles of the kidney.

name: arcuate vein medial hypertrophy
arcuate vein medial hypertrophy
HP:0033909.def: Increased thickness of middle layer of the arcuate veins of the kidney.

name: arcuate vein medial atrophy
arcuate vein medial atrophy
HP:0033910.def: Atrophy (wasting, decreased thickness) of the middle layer of the arcuate veins of the kidney.

name: cortical radial artery medial hypertrophy
cortical radial artery medial hypertrophy
HP:0033911.def: Increased thickness of the middle layer of the cortical radial arteries (also known as the interlobular arteries) of the kidney.

name: cortical radial artery medial atrophy
cortical radial artery medial atrophy

name: phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor
phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor
HP:0033987.def: A rare, endocrine active tumor that causes severe renal phosphate wasting, which in turn can lead to critical osteomalacia. Phosphaturic mesenchymal tumors (PMTs) are typically small and mostly benign tumors producing fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF-23). FGF-23 lowers the expression of sodium/phosphate cotransporters, which are the primary transport proteins responsible for phosphate reabsorption in the kidneys. The paraneoplastic overproduction of FGF-23 lowers reabsorption of phosphate and causes severe paraneoplastic renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia. FGF-23 also affects vitamin D levels by lowering 25-hydroxyvitamin D 1-alpha-hydroxylase in the proximal renal tubules and by increasing the expression of vitamin D 24-hydroxylase, a mitochondrial enzyme responsible for inactivating vitamin D metabolites.

HP:0034014.def: A type of pericallosal lipoma with a rounded or lobular appearance and a diameter that is usually above 2 cm. They are anteriorly situated and are associated with extensive callosal and often fronto-facial anomalies. A tubulonodular pericallosal lipoma can extend into the choroid plexus or lateral ventricles.

name: cavitating pulmonary nodule
cavitating pulmonary nodule
HP:0034015.def: Thick-walled abnormal gas-filled interstitial nodule within a lung.

anti - hla antibody positivity

anti - class i hla antibody positivity

abnormal circulate gaba concentration

name: elevated circulating sacchoropine concentration
elevate circulate sacchoropine concentration
HP:0034026.def: An increased concentration of saccharopine in the blood circulation. L-saccharopine is the N(6)-(1,3-dicarboxypropan-1-yl) derivative of L-lysine.

name: abnormal urinary non - proteinogenic amino acid level
abnormal urinary non - proteinogenic amino acid level
HP:0034027.def: Any deviation from the normal amount in the urine of an alpha-amino acid which is not a member of the group of 23 proteinogenic amino acids.

name: saccharopinuria
saccharopinuria
HP:0034028.def: Presence of saccharopine in the urine.

name: hepatic foam cells
hepatic foam cell
HP:0034029.def: The presence of foam cells, a type of macrophage that localizes to fatty deposits on blood vessel walls, in the liver.

name: facial cyanosis
facial cyanosis
HP:0034031.def: Bluish discoloration of one or more regions of the face.

name: central cyanosis
central cyanosis
HP:0034032.def: Generalized bluish discoloration of the body and the visible mucous membranes, which occurs due to inadequate oxygenation secondary to conditions that lead to an increase in deoxygenated hemoglobin or presence of abnormal hemoglobin.

name: peripheral cyanosis
peripheral cyanosis
HP:0034033.def: Bluish discoloration of the distal extremities (hands, fingertips, toes), and can sometimes involve circumoral and periorbital areas. Mucous membranes are generally not involved.

name: differential cyanosis
differential cyanosis
HP:0034034.def: Differential degree of bluish discoloration between the upper and lower extremities.

name: pharyngeal exudate
pharyngeal exudate
HP:0034035.def: Fluid exuded from the posterior wall of the pharynx.

name: pseudo - chilblains on toes
pseudo - chilblain on toe
HP:0034036.def: Inflammatory chilblain-like nodules on the feet and/or toes.

name: pseudo - chilblains on fingers
pseudo - chilblain on finger
HP:0034037.def: Inflammatory chilblain-like nodules on the hands and/or fingers.

name: silent hypoxemia
silent hypoxemia
HP:0034038.def: Abnormally low blood oxygen level without the presence of dyspnea.

name: ventricular couplet
ventricular couplet
HP:0034039.def: Two consecutive premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) with no intervening normal beats.

name: bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
HP:0034040.def: Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (BDVT) is a regular ventricular tachyarrhythmia (VT) with two different QRS morphologies alternating at a rate typically between 140 and 180 bpm.

name: ventricular ectopy
ventricular ectopy
HP:0034041.def: Ventricular ectopics, also known as ventricular extrasystoles, premature ventricular contractions or complexes (PVC) and ventricular premature depolarisations (VPD) are beats arising from within the ventricles. When they occur in groupings such as bigeminy, trigeminy, couplets and triplets they are referred to as ventricular ectopy.

name: dorsal hirsutism
dorsal hirsutism
HP:0034042.def: Abnormally increased hair growth in the lskin of the back.

name: increased fecal bile acid
increased fecal bile acid
HP:0034043.def: Elevated amount of bile acids in the feces.

name: trident pelvis
trident pelvis
HP:0034044.def: Spurs at the medial and lateral acetabular margin and in the center of the acetabulum gives rise to shape resembling a three-pronged spear known as trident.

name: angulated muscle fibers
angulated muscle fiber
HP:0034045.def: Normal muscle fibers are polygonal-shaped in cross section, are multinucleated, and have minimal amounts of endomysial connective tissue. In contrast, angulated (also known as angular) muscle fibers have long and narrow vertices (corners) with sharp edges and a pointed tip.

name: mandibular osteolysis
mandibular osteolysis
HP:0034046.def: Osteolysis (destruction of bone through bone resorption with removal or loss of calcium) localized to the mandible.

name: rib osteolysis
rib osteolysis
HP:0034047.def: Osteolysis (destruction of bone through bone resorption with removal or loss of calcium) localized to a rib.

hypoplastic anterior limb of the internal capsule

name: impaired toe - walking ability
impaired toe - walking ability
HP:0034052.def: Difficulty or reduced ability to walk on toes. Toe-walking can be tested as a part of the neurological examination. Foot plantar flexion weakness leads to difficulties in walking on toes.

name: probst bundles
probst bundle

Probst bundles are white matter fibers that normally cross the corpus callosum but (because of the agenesis of the corpus callosum) fail to cross the midline, such that when they reach the corticoseptal boundary, they turn and run parallel to the interhemispheric fissure within the septal leaves, indenting the medial walls of the lateral ventricles.

Whenever there is an interface of structures with different echogenicities, a visible difference in contrast will be apparent on the screen. name: anti - cytosolic - 5 - nucleotidase - 1a antibody positivity
anti - cytosolic - 5 - nucleotidase - 1a antibody positivity
HP:0034153.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against cytosolic-5-nucleotidase-1A (cN1A).

name: anti - ki antibody positivity
anti - ki antibody positivity
HP:0034154.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ki.

name: anti - sp100 antibody positivity
anti - sp100 antibody positivity
HP:0034155.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against sp100. Autoantibodies causing the MND pattern are directed against sp100, sp140, promyelocytic leukemia nuclear body proteins (PML) or ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteins, while in the punctate nuclear envelope pattern, the target antigens are gp210, nucleoporin-62 or laminin B receptor proteins.

name: anti - beta - 2 - glycoprotein i igg antibody positivity
anti - beta - 2 - glycoprotein i igg antibody positivity
HP:0034156.def: Presence of IgG antibodies against beta 2 glycoprotein I in the circulation. Beta-2 glycoprotein I (beta2GPI) is the principal target of autoantibodies in the antiphospholipid syndrome.

name: anti - beta - 2 - glycoprotein i igm antibody positivity
anti - beta - 2 - glycoprotein i igm antibody positivity
HP:0034157.def: Presence of IgM antibodies against beta 2 glycoprotein I in the circulation. Beta-2 glycoprotein I (beta2GPI) is the principal target of autoantibodies in the antiphospholipid syndrome.

name: anti - tyrosine phosphatase region of islet antigen - 2 antibody positivity
anti - tyrosine phosphatase region of islet antigen - 2 antibody positivity
HP:0034158.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the tyrosine phossphatase region of islet antigen 2A (this region is a specific part of IA-2). Usually IA-2A are measured using the intracellular portion of IA-2 (IA-2ic) made up of the protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) and juxtamembrane (JM) regions.

name: paget disease of bone
paget disease of bone
HP:0034159.def: A localized disorder of bone remodeling. Increased numbers of larger than normal osteoclasts initiate the process at affected skeletal sites, and the increase in bone resorption is followed by an increase in new bone formation, altering bone architecture.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 9 concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 9 concentration
HP:0034160.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 9 in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 9 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 9 concentration
HP:0034161.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 9 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 10 concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 10 concentration
HP:0034162.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 10 in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 10 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 10 concentration
HP:0034163.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 10 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 21 concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 21 concentration
HP:0034164.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 21 in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 21 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 21 concentration
HP:0034165.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 21 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 21 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 21 concentration
HP:0034166.def: An abnormally increased concentration of interleukin 21 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 22 concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 22 concentration
HP:0034167.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 22 in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 22 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 22 concentration
HP:0034168.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 22 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 22 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 22 concentration
HP:0034169.def: An abnormally increased concentration of interleukin 22 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 23 concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 23 concentration
HP:0034170.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 23 in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 23 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 23 concentration
HP:0034171.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 23 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 23 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 23 concentration
HP:0034172.def: An abnormally increased concentration of interleukin 23 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 27 concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 27 concentration
HP:0034173.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 27 in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 27 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 27 concentration
HP:0034174.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 27 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 27 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 27 concentration
HP:0034175.def: An abnormally increased concentration of interleukin 27 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating interleukin 17a concentration
abnormal circulate interleukin 17a concentration
HP:0034176.def: Any deviation from the normal range of the concentration of interleukin 17A in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 17a concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 17a concentration
HP:0034177.def: An abnormally decreased concentration of interleukin 17A in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 17a concentration
increase circulate interleukin 17a concentration
HP:0034178.def: An abnormally increased concentration of interleukin 17A in the blood circulation.

name: vertebral artery aneurysm
vertebral artery aneurysm
HP:0034179.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the vertebral artery .

name: fusion of the caudate and putamen
fusion of the caudate and putamen
HP:0034180.def: Abnormal joined appearance of the caudate and putamen with an absence of the anterior limb of the internal capsule.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the liver
aplasia / hypoplasia of the liver
HP:0034181.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the liver.

name: segmental hypoplasia of liver
segmental hypoplasia of liver
HP:0034182.def: Anatomically the liver is divided into right and left lobes based on the attachment of its peritoneal ligaments. This term refers to a developmental anomaly characterzied by the underdevelopment of one of the lobes of the liver. This is a rare and usually asymptomatic anomaly that can be detected incidentally on cross sectional imaging with computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging.

name: spastic triplegia
spastic triplegia
HP:0034183.def: Spastic weakness found in both lower extremities and one upper extremity.

name: increased insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit concentration
increased insulin like growth factor bind protein acid labile subunit concentration
HP:0034184.def: An abnormally elevated concentration of insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit level in the blood circulation.

name: median pseudocleft lip
median pseudocleft lip
HP:0034185.def: A type of mild median cleft lip in which the central tubercle of the upper lip is replaced by a mucosal cleft in the midline.

name: patella alta
patella alta
HP:0034186.def: Patella alta is a patella that rides abnormally high in relation to the femur, the femoral trochlea, or the tibia, with decreased bony stability requiring increased knee flexion angles to engage the trochlea.

name: clavicular pseudarthrosis
clavicular pseudarthrosis
HP:0034187.def: A developmental defect in a the clavicule leading to bending and pathologic fracture, with inability to form a normal bony callus with subsequent fibrous nonunion, leading to the pseudarthrosis (or false joint).

name: midline liver
midline liver
HP:0034188.def: Position of the liver across the middle of the body instead of being in its normal position to the right of the stomach.

name: anti - thyroid - stimulating hormone receptor antibody positivity
anti - thyroid - stimulate hormone receptor antibody positivity
HP:0034189.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against thyroid-stimulating hormone.

name: abnormal fetal cardiovascular physiology
abnormal fetal cardiovascular physiology
HP:0034190.def: Abnormal functionality of the fetal cardiovascular system.

name: elevated fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
elevate fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
HP:0034191.def: Increased peak systolic velocity of the fetal middle cerebral artery (MCA) as evaluated by Doppler ultrasound.

name: pulmonary thromboembolism
pulmonary thromboembolism
HP:0034192.def: Pulmonary embolism is caused by emboli, which have originated from venous thrombi, travelling to and occluding the arteries of the lung.

name: stratum basale cleavage
stratum basale cleavage
HP:0034193.def: Cleavage within the epidermal keratinocytes, which is the innermost layer of the epidermis and consists of proliferating cells that give rise to the outer layers of the epidermis.
synonym: blistering with cleavage within basal keratinocytes
blister with cleavage within basal keratinocytes
cleavage within the basal keratinocyte layer
cleavage within the basal keratinocyte layer

name: suprabasal cleavage
suprabasal cleavage
HP:0034194.def: Cleavage within the suprabasal cell layer of the epidermis, which lies directly above the basal layer and is composed of five to ten layers of cells.

name: triggered by muscle relaxant
trigger by muscle relaxant
HP:0034195.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a muscle relaxant such as suxamethonium and mivacurium.

name: ductus venosus agenesis
ductus venosus agenesis
HP:0034196.def: A developmental defect characterized by lack of formation of the ductus venosus (a shunt that allows oxygenated blood in the umbilical vein to bypass the liver in the fetal circulation).

name: third trimester onset
third trimester onset
HP:0034197.def: This term refers to a phenotypic feature that was first observed prior to birth during the third trimester, which is defined as 28 weeks and zero days (28+0) of gestation and beyond.

name: second trimester onset
second trimester onset
HP:0034198.def: This term refers to a phenotypic feature that was first observed prior to birth during the second trimester, which comprises the range of gestational ages from 14 0/7 weeks to 27 6/7 (inclusive).

name: late first trimester onset
late first trimester onset
HP:0034199.def: This term refers to a phenotypic feature that was first observed prior to birth in the first trimester during the early fetal period, which is defined as 11 0/7 to 13 6/7 weeks of gestation (inclusive).

name: abnormal csf homovanillic acid concentration
abnormal csf homovanillic acid concentration
HP:0034200.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of homovanillic acid (HVA) in the cerebrospinal fluid. HVA is a metabolite of dopamine.

name: increased csf homovanillic acid concentration
increase csf homovanillic acid concentration
HP:0034201.def: Elevated concentration of homovanillic acid (HVA) in the cerebrospinal fluid. HVA is a metabolite of dopamine.

name: decreased iduronate sulfatase level
decrease iduronate sulfatase level
HP:0034203.def: An decreased level of iduronate-2-sulfatase activity in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating c1 - esterase inhibitor concentration
decrease circulate c1 - esterase inhibitor concentration
HP:0034204.def: Decreased concentration of C1-esterase inhibitor (C1INH) in the blood circulation.

name: iniencephaly
iniencephaly
HP:0034205.def: Iniencephaly is a rare neural tube defect involving dysmorphic spine and abnormal fusion of the portion of the occipital skull with the back. It results in extreme fixed head retroflexion.

name: abnormal fetal central nervous system morphology
abnormal fetal central nervous system morphology
HP:0034206.def: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal central nervous system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: abnormal fetal gastrointestinal system morphology
abnormal fetal gastrointestinal system morphology
HP:0034207.def: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal gastrointestinal system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: fetal intracranial hemorrhage
fetal intracranial hemorrhage
HP:0034208.def: Abnormal bleeding inside the skull (cranium) of a fetus.

name: fetal subependymal hemorrhage
fetal subependymal hemorrhage
HP:0034209.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage located in the subependymal germinal matrix below the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles in the caudothalamic notch.

name: fetal intraventricular hemorrhage
fetal intraventricular hemorrhage
HP:0034210.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage with bleeding into the ventricular system of the brain.

name: fetal cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage
fetal cerebral parenchymal hemorrhage
HP:0034211.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage with bleeding into the parenchyma (tissue) of the brain.

name: fetal extra - axial hemorrhage
fetal extra - axial hemorrhage
HP:0034212.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage with bleeding that occurs within the skull but outside of the brain tissue itself (into the epidural, subdural, or arachnoid space).

name: fetal posterior fossa hemorrhage
fetal posterior fossa hemorrhage
HP:0034213.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage that occurs in the posterior cranial fossa, which is the part of the cranial cavity that is located between the foramen magnum and tentorium cerebelli and contains the brainstem and cerebellum.

name: fetal intraventricular hemorrhage without ventriculomegaly
fetal intraventricular hemorrhage without ventriculomegaly
HP:0034214.def: A type of fetal intraventricular hemorrhage characterized by clear hemorrhage spillover to the ventricles filling less than 50% of the lateral ventricle and without ventriculomegaly of greater than 15 mm in the transverse diameter of the lateral ventricular atrium.

name: fetal cerebellar hemisphere hemorrhage
fetal cerebellar hemisphere hemorrhage
HP:0034215.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage that occurs in the hemisphere of the cerebellum.

name: fetal cerebellar vermis hemorrhage
fetal cerebellar vermis hemorrhage
HP:0034216.def: A type of fetal intracranial hemorrhage that occurs in the vermis of the cerebellum.

name: sonographic non - visualized fetal bladder
sonographic non - visualized fetal bladder
HP:0034217.def: Inability to visualize the fetal bladder on targeted prenatal sonography examination. The fetal bladder can be visualized with sonography as a midline, fluid-filled structure in the pelvis as early as 10-12 weeks of gestation. The normal fetus voids at least once an hour but never completely empties the urinary bladder. The fetal bladdder should be consistently imaged after 13 weeks of gestation.

name: fetal intraventricular hemorrhage with ventriculomegaly
fetal intraventricular hemorrhage with ventriculomegaly
HP:0034218.def: A type of fetal intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) characterized by spillover to ventricles with flooding of 50% or more of one or both lateral ventricles accrued accompanying ventriculomegaly, but with no apparent brain parenchymal injury. This type of IVH may be defined as a diameter exceeding 15 mm in the transverse diameter of the lateral ventricular atrium as visualiuzed by prenatal sonography.

name: fetal intraventricular hemorrhage with periventricular hemorrhage
fetal intraventricular hemorrhage with periventricular hemorrhage
HP:0034219.def: A type of fetal intraventricular hemorrhage that additionally includes hemorrhage in a large part of the periventricular parenchyma.

name: temporal lobe megalencephaly
temporal lobe megalencephaly
HP:0034220.def: Expansion of the temporal lobes of the brain along all axes, including rostrocaudal, superoinferior, and mediolateral, resulting in a globular appearance of the brain.

name: abnormal temporal lobe morphology
abnormal temporal lobe morphology
HP:0034221.def: An abnormal strcutural of the zone (lobe) of the cerebral cortex that is located inferior to the lateral fissure on other cerebral hemispheres.

name: temporal lobe dysplasia
temporal lobe dysplasia
HP:0034222.def: A developmental defect of the temporal lobe of the cerebral cortex that is characterized by prominent sulcations and radially directed gyrations.

name: elevated umbilical artery pulsatility
elevated umbilical artery pulsatility
HP:0034223.def: Human umbilical artery (UA) blood flow pulsatility measured by Doppler ultrasound is a widely used biomarker for the detection of elevated placental vascular resistance. Elevated UA pulsatility, which in the most extreme cases manifests as absent or even reversed end-diastolic velocity, is associated with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) and still-birth.

name: absent end - diastolic umbilical artery flow
absent end - diastolic umbilical artery flow
HP:0034224.def: An anomaly that is visualized by umbilical artery Doppler velocimetry. Flow in the umbilical artery should be in the forward direction in normal circumstances. This anomaly is characterized by an absence of flow in the umbilical artery at the end of diastole.

name: reversed end - diastolic umbilical artery flow
reversed end - diastolic umbilical artery flow
HP:0034225.def: An anomaly that is visualized by umbilical artery Doppler velocimetry. Flow in the umbilical artery should be in the forward direction in normal circumstances. This anomaly is characterized by an reversal of flow in the umbilical artery at the end of diastole (i.e., backwards flow).

name: champagne cork sign
champagne cork sign
HP:0034226.def: Characteristic appearance of the chest and abdomen in the sagittal view on prenatal ultrasound when the chest is small and the abdomen protruding.

name: aortic isthmus hypoplasia
aortic isthmus hypoplasia
HP:0034227.def: A type of aortic arch hypoplasia whereby the isthmus (arch between the left subclavian and insertion of the patent ductus arteriosus/ligamentum arteriosum) has a diameter of less than 40% of the diameter of the ascending aorta.

name: proximal aortic arch hypoplasia
proximal aortic arch hypoplasia
HP:0034228.def: A type of aortic arch hypoplasia whereby the proximal aortic arch (arch proximal to the origin of the left subclavian artery) has a diameter of less than 60% of the diameter of the ascending aorta.

name: distal aortic arch hypoplasia
distal aortic arch hypoplasia
HP:0034229.def: A type of aortic arch hypoplasia whereby the distal aortic arch (arch distal to the ductus arteriosus) has a diameter of less than 60% of the diameter of the ascending aorta.

name: inferior crossed fused renal ectopia
inferior cross fuse renal ectopia
HP:0034230.def: A type of cross fused renal ectopia characterized by fusion between the upper pole of the cross-fused ectopic kidney (located more inferiorly relative to the other kidney) and the lower pole of the other orthotopic kidney (located in a more superior position).
synonym: type a cross fused renal ectopia
type a cross fuse renal ectopia

name: sigmoid kidney
sigmoid kidney
HP:0034231.def: A type of cross fused renal ectopia where the normal side kidney is present superiorly and the direction of pelvic is medial, the kidney which crosses positioned inferiorly with direction of pelvic toward the lateral side. As kidneys fuse after complete rotation on the vertical axis, both renal pelves lie in correct orientation.
synonym: type b cross fused renal ectopia
type b cross fuse renal ectopia

name: unilateral lump kidney
unilateral lump kidney
HP:0034232.def: A type of cross fused renal ectopia where fusion occurs over a wide margin, both renal pelves anteriorly directed and placed more inferiorly.
synonym: type c cross fused renal ectopia
type c cross fuse renal ectopia

name: disc kidney
disc kidney
HP:0034233.def: A type of cross fused renal ectopia in which kidneys fuse along their medial borders.
synonym: type d cross fused renal ectopia
type d cross fuse renal ectopia

name: l - shaped kidney
l - shape kidney
HP:0034234.def: A type of cross fused renal ectopia in which the crossed kidney lies inferiorly and transversely, fused with the lower pole of the normal kidney.
synonym: type e cross fused renal ectopia
type e cross fuse renal ectopia

name: superior crossed - fused renal ectopia
superior cross - fuse renal ectopia
HP:0034235.def: A type of cross fused renal ectopia in which the ectopic kidney lies superiorly and its lower pole fuses with the upper pole of the normal kidney. The renal pelvis of both kidneys lies anteriorly.

name: apnea of prematurity
apnea of prematurity
HP:0034236.def: Recurrent episodes of apnea occurring in infants born less than 37 weeks of gestation, defined specifically as a pause of breathing for more than 15-20 s, or accompanied by oxygen desaturation (SpO2 not more than 80% for at least 4 s) and bradycardia (heart rate less than 2/3 of baseline for at least 4 s), in infants born less than 37 weeks of gestation.

name: open neural tube defect
open neural tube defect
HP:0034237.def: A type of neural tube defect that is not covered by skin.

name: closed neural tube defect
closed neural tube defect
HP:0034238.def: A type of neural tube defect that is covered by skin.

name: renal vein thrombosis
renal vein thrombosis
HP:0034239.def: The presence of a thrombus (blood clot) in the major renal veins or its tributaries, generally leading to passive congestion that develops causes the affected kidney to swell and become engorged, leading to degeneration of nephrons and causing symptoms of flank pain, hematuria, and decreased urine output.

name: fetal neck mass
fetal neck mass
HP:0034240.def: An abnormal growth (lump) of tissue in the neck region of a fetus. Masses may be simple cystic,, cystic with a few simple septations (fewer than three septations and less than 3-mm thick), cystic with multiple or thick septations (greater than three septations or septations 3-mm-thick or more), a mass that is than is less than 50% solid, and a mass that is 50% solid or more.

name: prenatal death
prenatal death
HP:0034241.def: Death of a fetus in the uterus.

name: abnormal fetal genitourinary system morphology
abnormal fetal genitourinary system morphology
HP:0034242.def: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal genitourinary system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: abnormal fetal pulmonary morphology
abnormal fetal pulmonary morphology
HP:0034243.def: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal lungs. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

name: gastric pseudomass
gastric pseudomass
HP:0034244.def: At US examination from the second trimester onward, the fetal stomach appears as a uniformly anechoic, sharply circumscribed round structure in the left upper quadrant. However, debris is commonly visualized in the stomach, forming a pseudomass.

name: fetal scalp mass
fetal scalp mass
HP:0034246.def: An abnormal growth (lump) of tissue that projects from the fetal scalp.

name: fetal lower urinary tract obstruction
fetal low urinary tract obstruction
HP:0034247.def: An obstruction in the ureter leading to bladder outlet obstruction. Special criteria are used for lower urinary tract obstruction (LUTO) in the fetus. Prenatal LUTO has classically been suspected on the basis of three ultrasonographic findings: megacystis, dilated posterior urethra (known as the keyhole sign) and hydronephrosis.

name: increased fetal lens echogenicity
increase fetal lens echogenicity
HP:0034248.def: Increased echogenicity (increased brightness in the gray-scale sonography image) of the lens of a fetus.

name: severe influenza infection
severe influenza infection
HP:0034249.def: An unusually severe infection by an influenza virus.

name: fetal nuchal edema
fetal nuchal edema
HP:0034250.def: Nuchal edema is considered present in a fetus at gestational week 14 or more if in the midsagittal plane of the neck, there is subcutaneous edema that produces a characteristic tremor on ballotment of the fetal head. This constitutes the severe end of the spectrum of increased nuchal fold thickness, which is defined as soft-tissue thickening of 6 mm or more, seen in the suboccipitobregmatic view of the fetal head. Nuchal edema may be confined to the neck or it may be generalized, as part of hydrops fetalis.

name: abnormal corneal reflex
abnormal corneal reflex
HP:0034251.def: An anomaly of the corneal reflex that normally induces involuntary blinking of the eyelids following contact of the cornea.

name: absent corneal reflex
absent corneal reflex
HP:0034252.def: Absence of the corneal blinking reflex, which normally induces involuntary blinking of the eyelids following contact of the cornea. The corneal blink reflex is caused by a loop between the trigeminal sensory nerves and the facial motor (VII) nerve innervation of the orbicularis oculi muscles.

name: eosinophil nuclear hypersegmentation
eosinophil nuclear hypersegmentation
HP:0034253.def: An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of eosinophils. Eosinophils with more than two nuclear lobes are commonly regarded as hypersegmented, because seventy to ninety percent of peripheral blood eosinophils have two nuclear lobes.

name: face of the giant panda sign
face of the giant panda sign
HP:0034254.def: The face of the giant panda sign on T2-weighted MRI is characterized by preservation of normal signal intensity in the red nuclei and lateral portion of the pars reticulata of the substantia nigra, high signal in the tegmentum, and hypointensity of the superior colliculus. The findings are said to resemble the face of a giant panda.

name: colovesical fistula
colovesical fistula
HP:0034255.def: An aberrant, pathological communication between the colon and the bladder.

name: absent dermoepidermal hemidesmosomes
absent dermoepidermal hemidesmosomes
HP:0034256.def: Lack of demonstrable hemidesmosomes at the dermoepidermal junction. Hemidesmosomes are the specialized junctional complexes, that contribute to the attachment of epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane in stratified and other complex epithelia, such as the skin.

name: c4 nephritic factor positivity
c4 nephritic factor positivity
HP:0034257.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that recognize C4b2a, the C3 convertase of the classical pathway of complement.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the midbrain
aplasia / hypoplasia of the midbrain
HP:0034258.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the midbrain (mesencephalon).

name: hypoplasia of the midbrain
hypoplasia of the midbrain
HP:0034259.def: A developmental defect characterized by underdevelopment of the mesencephalon.

name: aplastic zygomatic arch
aplastic zygomatic arch
HP:0034260.def: Developmental defect characterized by the absence of the zygomatic arch.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of facial bones
aplasia / hypoplasia of facial bone
HP:0034261.def: A developmental defect characterized by absence or underdevelopment of one or more facial bone.

name: absent lanugo
absent lanugo
HP:0034262.def: Lack of development of lanugo, the fine, soft, unpigmented hair on the body of a fetus or newborn baby.

name: abnormal vaginal bleeding
abnormal vaginal bleeding
HP:0034263.def: Abnormal vaginal bleeding occurs between menstrual periods, after sex, or after menopause. Menstrual periods that are heavier or last longer than usual or last more than seven days also are considered abnormal.

name: postcoital vaginal bleeding
postcoital vaginal bleeding
HP:0034264.def: Postcoital bleeding (PCB) consists of spotting or bleeding after sexual intercourse that is not related to a person's menstrual cycle.

name: pelvic pain
pelvic pain
HP:0034267.def: Pain perceived in the area of the pelvis, the lower part of the abdomen located between the hip bones.

name: abnormal vaginal discharge
abnormal vaginal discharge
HP:0034269.def: Anomalous amount, odor, or consistency of the fluid or mucus that comes from the vagina

name: serrated incisors
serrate incisor
HP:0034270.def: Incisor teeth with irregular edges said to resemble a saw.

name: copper beaten skull
copper beat skull
HP:0034271.def: Diffuse prominent gyral impressions on the inner table of skull vault said to resemble beaten copper.

name: perifoveal hypoautofluorescence
perifoveal hypoautofluorescence
HP:0034272.def: Decreased amount of autofluorescence (emission of fluorescent light from ocular structures in the absence of sodium fluorescein) in the retina in the region surrounding the fovea.

name: premature sagging cheeks
premature sag cheek
HP:0034273.def: Drooping or sinking of tissues of the cheeks more than would be expected at a given age. Sagging can occur due to a relative excess of skin and/or lack of elastic recoil as well as fat accumulation.

name: gastrointestinal ulcer
gastrointestinal ulcer
HP:0034274.def: A deep defect in the esophageal, gastric, duodenal or intestinal wall involving the entire mucosal thickness and penetrating through the muscularis mucosae.

name: verrucous epidermal nevus
verrucous epidermal nevus
HP:0034275.def: A type of epidermal nevus (which represent Blaschkoid hamartomas of the skin that result from mosaic post-zygotic mutations) that appears as skin-colored-to-brown, sharply demarcated, papillomatous papules that coalesce into plaques. The majority of these nevi are either present at birth or occur within the first year of life.

name: elevated circulating thymidine concentration
elevate circulate thymidine concentration
HP:0034276.def: Concentration of thymidine in the blood circulation above the normal range.

name: elevated circulating deoxyuridine concentration
elevate circulate deoxyuridine concentration
HP:0034277.def: Concentration of 2-deoxyuridine in the blood circulation is above the normal range.

name: multinucleated erythroblast
multinucleated erythroblast
HP:0034278.def: Erythroblasts with multiple nuclei. Erythroblasts are nucleated precrusor cells of erythrocytes that are localized to the bone marrow. Normally, erythroblasts have a single nucleus. The abnormal finding of erythrocytes with two or more nuclei may be related to defects in cytokinesis.

name: 2,8 - dihydroxyadenine crystalluria
2,8 - dihydroxyadenine crystalluria
HP:0034279.def: The presence of 2,8-dihydroxyadenine crystals in the urine. The crystals appear as round, yellow-brown crystals.

name: target cells
target cell
HP:0034280.def: Target cells (codocytes) have a centrally located disk of hemoglobin surrounded by an area of pallor with an outer rim of hemoglobin adjacent to the cell membrane giving the cell the appearance of a target.

name: phalangeal cone - shaped epiphyses
phalangeal cone - shaped epiphysis
HP:0034281.def: Cone-shaped epiphyses of the phalanges of the hands or feet. Cone-shaped epiphyses (also known as coned epiphyses) are epiphyses that invaginate into cupped metaphyses. That is, the epiphysis has a cone-shaped distal extension resulting from increased growth of the central portion of the epiphysis relative to its periphery.

name: subcutaneous ossification
subcutaneous ossification
HP:0034282.def: Formation of abnormal, extraskeletal bony tissue in the soft tissue beneath the skin. Subcutaneous ossifications may be observed by radiography or by palpation.

name: increased fecal protoporphyrin concentration
increased fecal protoporphyrin concentration
HP:0034283.def: Abnormally high concentration of protoporphyrin (derivative of porphyrin with propionic acid groups) in feces.

name: recurrent gingivitis
recurrent gingivitis
HP:0034284.def: Repeated occurrences of inflammatory condition of the gums (gingival tissue), most commonly caused by bacterial infection.

name: enteroviral encephalitis
enteroviral encephalitis
HP:0034285.def: Inflamation of the brain related to infection by an enterovirus.

name: pneumocystis carinii pneumonia
pneumocystis carinii pneumonia
HP:0034286.def: Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia is an opportunistic infection that occurs in immunosuppressed populations.

name: afibrinogenemia
afibrinogenemia
HP:0034287.def: Lack of detectable fibrinogen in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating reverse t3 concentration
elevate circulate reverse t3 concentration
HP:0034288.def: Abnormally increased concentration of reverse T3 (3,3',5'-triiodothyronine or rT3) in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating rt3 / t3 ratio
elevate circulate rt3 / t3 ratio
HP:0034289.def: An abnormally increased ratio of the concentrations of reverse T3 to T3 in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating tiglylglycine concentration
elevate circulate tiglylglycine concentration
HP:0034290.def: Concentration of tiglylglycine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating creatine concentration
elevate circulate creatine concentration
HP:0034291.def: An elevation above the normal range of creatine in the blood circulation.

name: reduced circulating creatine concentration
reduce circulate creatine concentration
HP:0034292.def: An reduction below the normal range of creatine in the blood circulation.

name: temporal lobe calcification
temporal lobe calcification
HP:0034293.def: The presence of calcium deposition within the temporal lobe of the brain.

name: ductal bile plugs
ductal bile plug
HP:0034294.def: Bile thrombi that form an obstruction (plug) in a dilated bile duct.

name: reduced cerebral white matter volume
reduced cerebral white matter volume
HP:0034295.def: An abnormally low volume of the white matter of the brain.

name: elevated circulating tetracosanoic acid concentration
elevate circulate tetracosanoic acid concentration
HP:0034297.def: Elevated concentration of tetracosanoic acid (a C24 straight-chain saturated fatty acid) in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating hexacosanoic acid concentration
elevate circulate hexacosanoic acid concentration
HP:0034298.def: Elevated concentration of hexacosanoic acid (a C26 straight-chain saturated fatty acid) in the blood circulation.

name: sertoli cell - only phenotype
sertoli cell - only phenotype
HP:0034299.def: A histological phenotype observed on testicular biopsy in which only Sertoli cells line the seminiferous tubules of the testis.

name: decreased acid sphingomyelinase activity
decrease acid sphingomyelinase activity
HP:0034300.def: Reduced activity of the enzyme acid sphingomyelinase activity in the blood circulation.

name: congenital pouch colon
congenital pouch colon
HP:0034301.def: A malformation of the colon in which a pouch-like dilatation of a varying degree of shortened colon is associated with an anorectal malformation. The pouch usually terminates in a fistulous communication with the genitourinary tract.

name: megalopapilla
megalopapilla
HP:0034302.def: A congenitally anomalous enlarged optic disk (surface area greater than 2.50 square millimeters). It is considered to be a normal variant without physiological defects.

name: notched t wave
notch t wave
HP:0034303.def: A bifid T-wave with a notch duration between the 2 peaks at leasy 0.04 sec and an amplitude at least 0.05 mV.

name: epsilon wave
epsilon wave
HP:0034304.def: An electric signal of depolarization observed between the end of the QRS complex and the beginning of the T wave.

name: 2:1 atrioventricular block
2:1 atrioventricular block
HP:0034305.def: A type of second-degree atrioventricular block in which every other P wave is not conducted through the AV node such that only every other P wave is followed by a QRS complex.

name: ventricular bigeminy
ventricular bigeminy
HP:0034306.def: An electrocardiographic finding of a normal QRS followed by a premature ventricular contraction; a rhythmic pairing of normal and atypical beats originating in the ventricles in a 1-1 ratio such that an ectopic ventricular beat follows each regular heartbeat.

name: elevated left ventricular end - diastolic diameter
elevate leave ventricular end - diastolic diameter
HP:0034307.def: The LV end-diastolic internal diameter was measured from two-dimensional (2D) images in the parasternal long-axis view, timed with mitral valve closure at the level of the mitral valve chordae.

name: prolonged p wave
prolonged p wave
HP:0034308.def: Abnormal increased in the duration of the P wave, which is a marker of delayed inter-atrial conduction.

name: multiflagellar spermatozoa
multiflagellar spermatozoon
HP:0034309.def: Spermatozoa with multiple flagella attached to the sperm head.

name: post - vaccination yellow fever
post - vaccination yellow fever
HP:0034310.def: Infection with the yellow fever virus of the live-attenuated vaccine.

name: hypoplastic optic chiasm
hypoplastic optic chiasm
HP:0034311.def: Developmental defect characterized by undergrowth of the optic chiasm.

name: nocturnal hypoxemia
nocturnal hypoxemia
HP:0034312.def: Abnormally reduced oxyhemoglobin saturation during sleep (nocturnal). Different thresholds are used in the literature, including more than 10 percent of total sleep time below a SpO2 of 90 percent.

name: hyperdynamic left ventricular ejection fraction
hyperdynamic leave ventricular ejection fraction
HP:0034313.def: An abnoramlly increased ejection fraction of the left ventricle, usually defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction greater than 70 percent.

name: abnormal left ventricular ejection fraction
abnormal leave ventricular ejection fraction
HP:0034314.def: Any abnormality of the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which is the fraction of chamber volume ejected in systole (stroke volume) in relation to the volume of the blood in the ventricle at the end of diastole (end-diastolic volume). Stroke volume (SV) is calculated as the difference between end-diastolic volume (EDV) and end-systolic volume (ESV). LVEF is calculated as [SV/EDV] in percent.

name: chronic cough
chronic cough
HP:0034315.def: A persistent cough, defined as a cough lasting longer than eight weeks in adults or longer than four weeks in children.

name: thinning of the substantia nigra pars compacta
thinning of the substantia nigra par compacta
HP:0034316.def: Reduced volume of pars compacta of the substantia nigra.

name: unusual virus reactivation
unusual virus reactivation
HP:0034318.def: Reactivation is the mechanism whereby a latent virus that has infected a host cell switches to a lytic stage, undergoing productive viral replication and allowing the virus to spread. This term refers to reactivation regarded as unusual because of frequency, intensity, location, or nature of the virus, in the sense that the reactivation would not be observed in an immunocompetent host.

name: cns vasculitis with reactivation of varicella - zoster virus
cns vasculitis with reactivation of varicella - zoster virus
HP:0034319.def: A vasculopathy in the central nervous system (CNS) following reactivation of varicella-zoster virus due to a productive viral infection of both large and small cerebral arteries.

name: muscle fiber intracytoplasmic reducing inclusion bodies
muscle fiber intracytoplasmic reduce inclusion body
HP:0034320.def: Intracytoplasmic inclusions in myofibers that reduce nitro-blue tetrazolium (NBT) and thus stain strongly with the menadione-NBT stain.

name: elevated circulating guanidinoacetic acid concentration
elevate circulate guanidinoacetic acid concentration
HP:0034321.def: Concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

name: reduced circulating growth hormone concentration
reduce circulate growth hormone concentration
HP:0034323.def: Concentration of growth hormone in the blood circulation below normal limits.

name: brachiocephalic artery aneurysm
brachiocephalic artery aneurysm
HP:0034324.def: An abnormal widening (dilatation) of the brachiocephalic artery

name: common carotid artery aneurysm
common carotid artery aneurysm
HP:0034325.def: An abnormal widening (dilatation) of the common carotid artery.

name: adenomyosis
adenomyosis
HP:0034326.def: Inappropriate (ectopic) endometrial tissue proliferation within the uterine myometrium, often presenting clinically with painful menses and heavy menstrual bleeding.

name: posterior corneal stroma punctiform multicolored opacities
posterior corneal stroma punctiform multicolored opacity
HP:0034327.def: Thin, punctiform elements of various colors in the posterior stroma of the cornea, immediately anterior to Descemet membrane. The elements are visible to direct and indirect illumination.
synonym: punctiform multicolored opacities in the posterior corneal stroma
punctiform multicolored opacity in the posterior corneal stroma
punctiform multicoloured opacities in the posterior corneal stroma
punctiform multicoloured opacity in the posterior corneal stroma

name: fibro - obliterative bile - duct lesion
fibro - obliterative bile - duct lesion
HP:0034328.def: A condition in which the lumen of a bile duct has been filled by fibrous scar material, in effect replacing the bile duct with a fibrous scar.
synonym: fibro - obliterative loss of bile ducts
fibro - obliterative loss of bile duct

name: dysplastic megalencephaly
dysplastic megalencephaly
HP:0034329.def: A congenital brain malformation characterized by marked overgrowth and dysplasia affecting one or both cerebral hemispheres, and, in some cases, subcortical brain regions as well. The presence of dysplasia in dysplastic megalencephaly distinguishes it from other forms of generalized megalencephaly.

name: regional right ventricular hypokinesis
regional right ventricular hypokinesis
HP:0034330.def: Decreased range of right ventricular motion in a portion of the right ventricle of the heart.

name: mcconnell sign
mcconnell sign
HP:0034331.def: Severe hypokinesia of the mid-free wall of the right ventricle of the heart with a normal contraction of the apical segment of the right ventricle.

name: cognitive regression
cognitive regression
HP:0034332.def: Loss of cognitive developmental skills, as manifested by loss of developmental cognitive milestones.

name: increased circulating hypoxanthine concentration
increase circulate hypoxanthine concentration
HP:0034333.def: Elevated concentration of hypoxanthine in the blood circulation.

name: inheritance qualifier
inheritance qualifier
HP:0034335.def: The terms in this hierarchy can be used to specificy the context in which inheritance of a disease is typically observed.

name: splenic infarction
splenic infarction
HP:0034336.def: Ischemia and necrosis of part or all of the spleen resulting from compromise of blood supply resulting from arterial or venous occlusion.

name: claw hand deformity
claw hand deformity
HP:0034337.def: An abnormality of the hand characterized by metacarpophalangeal (MCP) hyperextension and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) and distal interphalangeal (DIP) flexion. The position of the affected hand is said to resemble a claw.

name: imprinted
imprint
HP:0034338.def: Requires that the abnormal allele be paternal or maternal in origin, depending on the disease-gene relationship. Imprinting refers to a normal developmental process in which either the paternal or maternal allele is inactivated, depending on the specific locus, thus leading to expression from only one copy of the gene. Disease typically manifests when a deleterious variant is inherited from a parent whose copy of the gene would normally be expressed, but not when a deleterious variant is inherited from a parent whose copy of the gene would normally be inactivated.

name: pseudoautosomal inheritance
pseudoautosomal inheritance
HP:0034339.def: A pattern of inheritance observed for alleles in the X-Y identical regions is referred to as pseudoautosomal inheritance, because it resembles the pattern seen for alleles located on autosomes.

name: pseudoautosomal dominant inheritance
pseudoautosomal dominant inheritance
HP:0034340.def: A type of pseudoautosomal inheritance that is dominant and in which heterozygous males and females both manifest a disease phenotype.

name: pseudoautosomal recessive inheritance
pseudoautosomal recessive inheritance
HP:0034341.def: A type of pseudoautosomal inheritance that is recessive and in which biallelic males and females both manifest a disease phenotype.

name: trapezius muscle aplasia
trapezius muscle aplasia
HP:0034342.def: A developmental defect characterized by lack of formation of the trapezius muscle, which is broad superficial muscle that extends from the posterior neck to the posterior part of the trunk (thorax).

name: requires heterozygosity
require heterozygosity
HP:0034343.def: A rarely encountered phenomenon in which condition is most severe in the heterozygous state. Such disorders are rare and currently all are X-linked. Most X-linked recessive conditions manifest if hemizygous in males, or biallelic in females, though may have a mild phenotype in the heterozygous state in females.

name: female - limited expression
female - limited expression
HP:0034344.def: Used to refer to a monogenic trait linked to an autosomal locus in which the phenotypic effects of allelic differences are expressed only in the female sex.

name: mendelian inheritance
mendelian inheritance
HP:0034345.def: A mode of inheritance of diseases whose pathophysiology can be traced back to deleterious variants in a single gene. The inheritance patterns of these single-gene (monogenic) diseases are often referred to as Mendelian in honor of Gregor Mendel.

name: nesidioblastosis
nesidioblastosis
HP:0034346.def: An abnormality of pancreatic beta cells characterized by a proliferation of abnormal beta cells throughout the entire pancreas, with enlarged islet size and number (hypertrophic islets), increased periductular islets, enlarged beta-cell nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm. Occasionally beta cells with pleomorphic nuclei, ductuloinsular complexes, and neoformation of islets from ducts are observed.

name: greater auricular nerve thickening
great auricular nerve thicken
HP:0034347.def: Increase in thickness of the great auricular nerve, a cutaneous nerve of the head. It originates from the cervical plexus, with branches of spinal nerves C2 and C3. Thickening may lead to the nerve being palpable or even visible in this region.

name: subpulmonary stenosis
subpulmonary stenosis
HP:0034348.def: A cardiovascular malformation associated with narrowing of the outflow tract of the right ventricle immediately below the pulmonary valve.

name: supravalvar pulmonary stenosis
supravalvar pulmonary stenosis
HP:0034349.def: A cardiovascular malformation associated with narrowing at the level of the pulmonary sinotubular junction above the pulmonic valve.

name: valvular pulmonary stenosis
valvular pulmonary stenosis
HP:0034350.def: A cardiovascular malformation associated with narrowing of the outflow tract of the right ventricle immediately at the level of the pulmonary valve.

name: neuromyotonia
neuromyotonia
HP:0034351.def: Peripheral nerve hyperexcitability manifesting as spontaneous discharges originating from motor axons or their terminals, lead to overactivity of muscles, typically manifesting as twitches, cramps and stiffness.

name: bile duct polyp
bile duct polyp
HP:0034352.def: An elevated growth from the the mucosa of the bile duct.

name: appendicular spasticity
appendicular spasticity
HP:0034353.def: A type of spasticity that affects one or more limbs (arms or legs).

name: trichoschisis
trichoschisis
HP:0034354.def: Transverse fractures through the hair shafts (trichoschisis). Trichoschisis is characterized by a sharp transverse fracture of the hair shaft.

name: white cerebellum sign
white cerebellum sign
HP:0034355.def: On computed tomography of the brain,the white (or dense) cerebellum sign is seen when the cerebellum appears dense with respect to the cerebral parenchyma. The increase in attenuation of cerebellum is in fact a relative hyperdensity caused by decreased attenutation of the brain. It represents anoxic-ischemic cerebral injury, and has a very poor prognosis.

name: impaired renal tubular reabsorption of low molecular weight protein
impaired renal tubular reabsorption of low molecular weight protein
HP:0034356.def: Increased loss of low-molecular weight proteins by the kidneys, measured in terms of the fractional excretion (FE). The FE of low-molecular-weight proteins such as beta2-microglobulin can be measured in terms of plasma and urine concentrations, since urinary low-molecular-weight protein concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.
synonym: increased low molecular weight protein excretion
increase low molecular weight protein excretion

name: impaired renal tubular reabsorption of glucose
impaired renal tubular reabsorption of glucose
HP:0034357.def: Increased fractional excretion (FE) of glucose in the urine. The FE of glucose is the percentage of the glucose filtered by the kidney which is excreted in the urine. It is measured in terms of plasma and urine glucose, rather than by the interpretation of urinary glucose concentration alone, as urinary glucose concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.

name: impaired renal tubular reabsorption of sodium
impaired renal tubular reabsorption of sodium
HP:0034358.def: Increased fractional excretion (FE) of sodium in the urine. The FE of sodium is the percentage of the sodium filtered by the kidney which is excreted in the urine. It is measured in terms of plasma and urine sodium, rather than by the interpretation of urinary glucose concentration alone, as urinary glucose concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.

name: impaired renal tubular reabsorption of phosphate
impaired renal tubular reabsorption of phosphate
HP:0034359.def: Increased fractional excretion (FE) of glucose in the phosphate. The FE of glucose is the percentage of the phosphate filtered by the kidney which is excreted in the urine. It is measured in terms of plasma and urine phosphate, rather than by the interpretation of urinary phosphate concentration alone, as urinary glucose concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.

name: action myoclonus
action myoclonus
HP:0034360.def: A type of myoclonus (arrhythmic muscular jerking) that is induced by voluntary movement. It is made worse by attempts at precise or coordinated movement (intention myoclonus) and may also be provoked by certain sensory stimuli.

name: redundant umbilical skin
redundant umbilical skin
HP:0034361.def: Greater than normal amount of skin surrounding the umbilicus (belly button) with protrusion of the umbilicus above the plane of the abdomen.

name: dull foveal reflex
dull foveal reflex
HP:0034362.def: Reduced brigthness of the foveal reflex, which normally is a bright pinpoint of light that is observed to move sideways or up and down in response to movement of the opthalmoscope.

name: corneal pterygium
corneal pterygium
HP:0034363.def: Corneal pterygium is an ocular surface disease characterized mainly by a wing-shaped growth of limbal and conjunctival tissue over the adjacent cornea.

name: fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium
fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium
HP:0034364.def: Replacement of the myocardium of the right ventricular free wall by fat and fibrous tissue.

name: elevated circulating alpha - aminoadipic semialdehyde concentration
elevate circulate alpha - aminoadipic semialdehyde concentration
HP:0034365.def: Increased concentration of alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde in the blood circulation.
synonym: elevated circulating piperideine - 6 - carboxylic acid concentration
elevate circulate piperideine - 6 - carboxylic acid concentration

name: fracture blister
fracture blister
HP:0034366.def: Fracture blister is a type of blister that forms following acute bone fractures, typically near the ankle, wrist elbow or foot, where skin adheres tightly to bone with little subcutaneous fat cushioning. The blister that results resembles that of a second degree burn.

name: decreased circulating beta - mannosidase activity
decrease circulate beta - mannosidase activity
HP:0034367.def: Activity of the enzyme beta-mannosidase below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catabolizes oligosaccharides.

name: urolithiasis
urolithiasis
HP:0034368.def: Renal stones are formed within the kidneys, and this is called nephrolithiasis. Urolithiasis is a condition that occurs when these stones exit the renal pelvis and move into the remainder of the urinary collecting system, which includes the ureters, bladder, and urethra.

name: decreased level of coenzyme q10 in skeletal muscle
decrease level of coenzyme q10 in skeletal muscle
HP:0034369.def: Reduced amount of coenzyme Q10,a naturally occurring quinone, in skeletal muscle tissue.

name: reduced circulating prekallikrein concentration
reduce circulate prekallikrein concentration
HP:0034371.def: Reduced concentration of prekallikrein (PK; also known as Fletcher factor) in the blood circulation. PK is the precursor of plasma kallikrein, a serine protease that activates kinins. PK is cleaved to produce kallikrein by activated Factor XII.

name: external tibial torsion
external tibial torsion
HP:0034373.def: External twisting of the tibia resulting in the toes of each foot pointing outward (outtoeing) .

name: trident acetabulum
trident acetabulum
HP:0034374.def: Abnormal appearance of the acetabulum characterized by spurs at the medial and lateral acetabular margin and in the center of the acetabulum, giving rise to shape resembling a three-pronged spear sadi to resemble a trident.

name: spherophakia
spherophakia
HP:0034375.def: Spherophakia is a rare congenital condition that presents with weak zonules around a smaller and more spherical crystalline lens with an increased anteroposterior thickness of the lens, and highly myopic eye. The lens zonules are developmentally hypoplastic and abnormally weak and due to non-attachment of the posterior zonules to the equatorial zone of the lens, the lens changes its normal shape to spherical.

name: atrioventricular valve regurgitation
atrioventricular valve regurgitation
HP:0034376.def: Regurgitation of a heart valve that controls blood flow from a an atrium to a ventricle, including mitral, tricuspid, or, rarely, single atrioventicular valve.

name: single atrioventricular valve regurgitation
single atrioventricular valve regurgitation
HP:0034377.def: Regurgitation of the single atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) in the context of a congenital heart defect with a single ventricle. Roughly three quarters of patients following Fontan procedure display AVVR.

name: urethrovesical occlusion
urethrovesical occlusion
HP:0034378.def: Blockage of the flow of urine from the bladder into the urethra.

name: obsolete vascular granular osmiophilic material deposition
obsolete vascular granular osmiophilic material deposition
HP:0034379.def: Accumulation of granular osmiophilic material in blood vessel walls. Osmiophilic material becomes black upon staining with osmium tetroxide.

name: juvenile type testicular granulosa cell tumor
juvenile type testicular granulosa cell tumor
HP:0034380.def: Juvenile granulosa cell tumor of the testis of neonates and infants is an uncommon lesion frequently associated with abnormal sex chromosome and ambiguous genitalia.

name: central nervous system axonal spheroid
central nervous system axonal spheroid
HP:0034381.def: Axonal spheroids are bubble-like biological features that form on most degenerating axons. During neurodegeneration, bubble-like swellings form along the length of the axon, a primary and early effect of dynamic axonal deformation. These varicosities, spheroids, or swellings have been described as beads on a string and branches bearing fruit, and they frequently appear on degenerating axons. The focal swellings on degenerating axons, axonal spheroids, are often filled with cellular debris such as organelles, pathological proteins, and disorganized cytoskeletal elements.

name: disease remission
disease remission
HP:0034382.def: A decrease in or disappearance of signs and symptoms typically associated with a disease course.

name: elevated circulating biliverdin concentration
elevate circulate biliverdin concentration
HP:0034383.def: Increased concentration of biliverdin, a green tetrapyrrolic bile pigment, in the blood circulation.

name: elevated circulating insulin : c - peptide ratio
elevate circulate insulin : c - peptide ratio
HP:0034384.def: Increased ratio of insulin to C-peptide in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal left ventricular endsystolic diameter
abnormal leave ventricular endsystolic diameter
HP:0034385.def: A deviation from the normal range of the left ventricular endsystolic diameter.

name: reduced left ventricular endsystolic diameter
reduce leave ventricular endsystolic diameter
HP:0034386.def: A lower than normal left ventricular endsystolic diameter.

name: hilar lymph node enlargement
hilar lymph node enlargement
HP:0034388.def: Hilar lymphadenopathy is swelling or enlargement of lymph nodes localised in hila, wedge-shaped anatomical structures containing pulmonary vessels, major bronchi, nerves and lymph nodes. Hilar lymph nodes are not visible on chest X-ray if they are not enlarged. Hilar lymph node enlargement can be caused by benign and malignant conditions and can be symmetrical (bilateral) or asymmetrical (unilateral).

name: pulmonary vein varix
pulmonary vein varix
HP:0034389.def: Pulmonary vein varix (PVV), refers to a localised dilatation of a pulmonary vein. PVV is a rare condition and can be congenital or acquired. PVV typically occur at the confluence of the veins adjacent to the left atrium. PVVs are sometimes classified into three morphological types: saccular, tortuous and confluent.

name: decreased csf glycine concentration
decrease csf glycine concentration
HP:0034390.def: Abnormally decreased levels of glycine in cerebrospinal fluid.

name: elbow contracture
elbow contracture
HP:0034391.def: A limitation in the passive range of motion of the elbow resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.

name: joint contracture
joint contracture
HP:0034392.def: A limitation in the passive range of motion of the elbow resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin. A contracture prevents movement of the associated body part.

name: elbow extension contracture
elbow extension contracture
HP:0034393.def: An elbow contracture that limits the ability of the elbow joint to flex (flexion of the the elbow joint refers to bending the elbow joint to bring the hand closer to the shoulder), meaning that the elbow is fixed in an extended (straight) position.

name: forearm supination contracture
forearm supination contracture
HP:0034394.def: A contracture that limits the ability of the forearm to stabilize the hand in pronation (pronation refers to a rotation of the forearm that causes the palm and forearm to face downwards), meaning that the palm is fixed in a upward orientation. Restriction of supination/pronation can occur at the elbow (radial-humeral joint), at the wrist (radial-ulnar joint), and anywhere in between.

name: forearm pronation contracture
forearm pronation contracture
HP:0034395.def: A contracture that limits the ability of the forearm to stabilize the hand in supiation (supination refers to a rotation of the forearm that causes the palm and forearm to face upwards), meaning that the palm is fixed in a downward orientation. Restriction of supination/pronation can occur at the elbow (radial-humeral joint), at the wrist (radial-ulnar joint), and anywhere in between.

name: hippocampal malrotation
hippocampal malrotation
HP:0034396.def: Hippocampal malrotation, also termed incomplete inversion of the hippocampus or hippocampal malformation, is an increasingly recognized neuroimaging finding of undetermined clinical significance. It is characterized by features including (i) Round or pyramidal shape instead of ovoid shape; (ii) Medial position of the hippocampus on the hippocampal sulcus; (iii) The collateral sulcus is excessively deep or verticalized; (iv) Fimbria located medial to the hippocampus; (v) Small or displaced fornix; (vi) Enlarged temporal horn and empty choroid fissure; (vii) Thickened subiculum; (viii) Reduced upper horizontal portion of the parahippocampal gyrus.

name: claw toe deformity
claw toe deformity
HP:0034397.def: Claw toes are characterized by hyperextension at the metatarsal-phalangeal joints and flexion of the interphalangeal joints.

name: toe deformity
toe deformity
HP:0034398.def: Abnormal positioning of toe phalanges. Deformities of the lesser toes often occur gradually, though they can be brought on by trauma. The main adult sagittal plane deformities consist of claw toes, hammer toes and mallet toes. Axial plane deformities include crossover toes.

name: prolonged central motor conduction time
prolonged central motor conduction time
HP:0034399.def: Increased duration of the central motor conduction time (CMCT). The CMCT estimates the conduction time of corticospinal fibers between motor cortex and spinal (or bulbar) motoneurons. It includes the times for excitation of cortical cells, conduction via the corticobulbar-corticospinal tract and excitation of the motoneuron sufficient to reach its firing threshold. CMCT is calculated by subtracting the peripheral conduction time from the MEP latency recorded after cortical stimulation.

name: circumferential skin creases on extremities
circumferential skin crease on extremity
HP:0034400.def: Ringed creases of the skin of the extremities related to folding of excess skin.

name: atypical teratoid / rhabdoid tumor
atypical teratoid / rhabdoid tumor
HP:0034401.def: An aggressive malignant embryonal neoplasm arising from the central nervous system. It is composed of cells with a large eccentric nucleus, prominent nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm. Mutations of the SMARCB1 gene or very rarely SMARCA4 (BRG1) gene are present. The vast majority of cases occur in childhood. Symptoms include lethargy, vomiting, cranial nerve palsy, headache, and hemiplegia.

name: rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
