HP:0034402.def: A highly aggressive, extremely rare neoplasm of the kidney that is usually seen in children. The term rhabdoid is used because the tumor cells resemble rhabdomyoblasts but lack myogenic markers, and pathologic diagnosis requires familiarity with these microscopic features plus awareness that adult onset is possible. It can be associated with abnormalities of chromosome 22. It is characterized by the presence of cells with a large eccentric nucleus, prominent nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm.
synonym: malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
malignant rhabdoid tumour of the kidney
malignant rhabdoid tumour of the kidney

name: subcutaneous panniculitis - like t - cell lymphoma
subcutaneous panniculitis - like t - cell lymphoma
HP:0034403.def: A form of T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma in which cytotoxic CD8+ T cells infiltrate adipose tissue forming subcutaneous nodules.

name: fungal hyphae in sputum
fungal hypha in sputum
HP:0034404.def: Presence of hyphae (long, branching, filamentous structures produced by fungi) in sputum.

name: enlarged tectum
enlarge tectum
HP:0034405.def: Increasaed size of the tectum, which is the region of the midbrain posterior to the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius. The midbrain is the most superior portion of the brainstem.

name: elevated csf angiotensin - converting enzyme concentration
elevate csf angiotensin - convert enzyme concentration
synonym: angiotensin - converting enzyme ( ace ) high in csf
angiotensin - convert enzyme ( ace ) high in csf
angiotensin - converting enzyme high in csf
angiotensin - convert enzyme high in csf

name: reduced circulating 3 - ketoacyl - coa thiolase concentration
reduce circulate 3 - ketoacyl - coa thiolase concentration
HP:0034407.def: Decreased concentration of 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase in th blood circulation.

name: solitary angiokeratoma
solitary angiokeratoma
HP:0034408.def: A dark, keratotic papule about 2-10 mm in diameter, usually occuring on the lower extremeities. Usually the lesions begin as bright, soft, and nonkeratotic paules which grow larger and change to a firm, blue to black and keratotic stage.

name: fordyce angiokeratoma
fordyce angiokeratoma
HP:0034409.def: A type of angiokeratoma that most commonly occurs on the scrotum of patients who are 40 years old or older. The typical single lesion is a dark red to blue dome-shaped papule 2-4 mm in diameter with a very discrete keratotic surface. Typically, they are multiple and arranged in a line parallel to the raphe mediana of the scrotum. They also occur on the vulva and less commnly on the penis.

name: angiokeratoma circumscriptum naeviforme
angiokeratoma circumscriptum naeviforme
HP:0034410.def: A type of angiokeratoma that typically presents in childhood as a large, mostly linear and unilateral hyperkeratotic plaque which is composed of confluent keratotic papules. The size ranges from a few centimeters up to a major part of the body surface. Initially the lesions present asa multile reddish macules, clinically similar to a nevus flammeus. Within several years they develop into acanthokeratotic papules that agrregate into plaques which may have a hyperkeratotic surface.

name: angiokeratoma of mibelli
angiokeratoma of mibelli
HP:0034411.def: A type of angiokeratoma that typically presents in women on the dorsa of fingers and toes and multiple dark red papules with a slightly verrucous surface, each measuring about 3-5 mm in diameter.

name: laryngeal mass
laryngeal mass
HP:0034412.def: A lump in the region of the larynx. A mass is any lump in the body that can be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes or an immune reaction. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup. Laryngeal masses can be visualized by multiple methods include computed tomography.

name: palate mass
palate mass
HP:0034413.def: A lump in the region of the palate. A mass is any lump in the body that can be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes or an immune reaction. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

name: thick oral frenulum
thick oral frenulum
HP:0034414.def: Increased thickness of an oral frenulum, flaps of mucous membrane that extend from the midline gingiva to the upper or lower lip.

name: tooth avulsion
tooth avulsion
HP:0034415.def: A type of dental trauma characterized by total dislocation of the tooth from its socket.

name: torn oral frenulum
torn oral frenulum
HP:0034416.def: Laceration or tear of an oral frenulum, flaps of mucous membrane that extend from the midline gingiva to the upper or lower lip.

name: intraoral laceration
intraoral laceration
HP:0034417.def: A wound of the mucosa within the oral cavity covering lips, tongue, palate, gingiva, pharynx, or retropharynx.

name: erythematous oral mucosa
erythematous oral mucosa
HP:0034418.def: An erythematous lesion of the oral mucosa may result from a variety of tissue alterations, including inflammation, erythrocyte extravasation, and atrophy or reduced keratinization of the surface epithelium.

name: mitral chordae tendinae rupture
mitral chordae tendinae rupture
HP:0034419.def: Breakage of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve. This can lead to loss of tension of one of the mitral valve leaflets and mitral regurgitation.

name: history of cardiovascular procedure
history of cardiovascular procedure
HP:0034420.def: Indicates that a cardiovascular procedure such as stenting, bypass, catherization was performed on a patient.

name: ejection click
ejection click
HP:0034421.def: A high-pitched sound that occurs at the moment of maximal opening of the aortic or pulmonary valves. They are heard just after the first heart sound. The sounds occur in the presence of a dilated aorta or pulmonary artery or in the presence of a bicuspid or flexible stenotic aortic or pulmonary valve. Ejection clicks may also be called ejection sounds.

name: cryofibrinogenemia
cryofibrinogenemia
HP:0034422.def: Cryofibrinogen is an abnormal protein that forms precipitate only in plasma. consisting of fibrinogen, fibronectin, alpha1-antitrypsin and alpha2-macroglobulin.

name: triggered by allergens
trigger by allergen
HP:0034423.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to allergens.

name: clicking tinnitus
click tinnitus
HP:0034424.def: A type of tinnitus that presents as clicks, resembling the noise made by the snapping together of 2 fingers.

name: reduced hair sulfur content
reduce hair sulfur content
HP:0034425.def: Abnormally low amount of sulfur in hair.

name: purulent eye discharge
purulent eye discharge
HP:0034427.def: Secretion of pus-like (purulent) material from the eye, which may caused the eyelids to be matted together.

name: bacteria in cerebrospinal fluid
bacteria in cerebrospinal fluid
HP:0034429.def: Presence of bacteria in the cerebrospinal fluid, as manifested by visual inspection or bacterial culture results.

name: joint crepitus
joint crepitus
HP:0034431.def: A popping, clicking or crackling sound that accompaniees movement of a joint.

name: intertriginous distribution
intertriginous distribution
HP:0034432.def: Applies to the localization of a skin lesion involving any area of the body where two opposing skin surfaces can touch and rub or chaff.

name: distributed along skin tension lines
distribute along skin tension line
HP:0034433.def: Applies to the localization of a skin lesion that correspond to skin tension lines, which are linear clefts in the skin that indicate the direction of orientation of the underlying collagen fibers. Skin tension lines are also known as Langer's lines or lines of cleavage.

name: abnormal communication
abnormal communication
HP:0034434.def: Presence of any form of communication (e.g., verbal or non-verbal) that does not align with cultural expectations or developmental level.

name: abnormal eye contact
abnormal eye contact
HP:0034435.def: Any abnormality of eye contact behavior. We define eye contact as a form of nonverbal communication between two individuals who are facing each other in which an individual directs the eyes towards the eyes or face of the other individual. Eye contact occurs frequently and voluntarily during face-to-face verbal communication. The duration and frequency of eye contact that is interpreted to be appropriate may follow social and situational norms.

name: gaze avoidance
gaze avoidance
HP:0034436.def: A deliberate avoidance of eye contact.

name: excessive eye contact
excessive eye contact
HP:0034437.def: Tendency to maintain sustained eye contact for an inappropriately long period of time.

name: instep location
instep location
HP:0034439.def: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the arched middle portion of the foot in front of the ankle joint (i.e., instep).

name: ameliorated by ultraviolet light exposure
ameliorate by ultraviolet light exposure
HP:0034440.def: Applies to a skin lesion that is improved or made more bearable by exposure to ultraviolet light (sunshine or phototherapy).

name: decreased circulating aspartic acid concentration
decrease circulate aspartic acid concentration
HP:0034441.def: An reduced concentration of aspartic acid in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal circulating erythropoietin concentration
abnormal circulate erythropoietin concentration
HP:0034442.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of erythropoietin in the blood circulation. Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the peritubular cells of the kidney that stimulates red blood cell production.

name: reduced circulating erythropoietin concentration
reduce circulate erythropoietin concentration
HP:0034443.def: Decreased concentration of erythropoietin in the blood circulation. Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the peritubular cells of the kidney that stimulates red blood cell production.

name: abnormal gamma - glutamyltransferase level
abnormal gamma - glutamyltransferase level
HP:0034444.def: Any deviation from the normal level of the enzyme gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT). GGT is mainly present in kidney, liver, and pancreatic cells, but small amounts are present in other tissues.

name: reduced gamma - glutamyltransferase level
reduce gamma - glutamyltransferase level
HP:0034445.def: Decreased level of the enzyme gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT). GGT is mainly present in kidney, liver, and pancreatic cells, but small amounts are present in other tissues.
synonym: gamma - glutamyl transferase low in blood
gamma - glutamyl transferase low in blood

name: elevated circulating histamine concentration
elevate circulate histamine concentration
HP:0034446.def: Increased concentration of histamine in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 18 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 18 concentration
HP:0034447.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-18 in the blood circulation.

name: abnormal phytanic acid : pristanic acid ratio
abnormal phytanic acid : pristanic acid ratio
HP:0034448.def: Any deviation from the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
synonym: abnormal phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio
abnormal phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio
abnormal phytanic acid / pristanic acid ratio
abnormal phytanic acid / pristanic acid ratio

name: increased phytanic acid : pristanic acid ratio
increase phytanic acid : pristanic acid ratio
HP:0034449.def: An elevation above the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
synonym: phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio high
phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio high

name: decreased phytanic acid : pristanic acid ratio
decrease phytanic acid : pristanic acid ratio
HP:0034450.def: A reduction below the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
synonym: phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio low
phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio low

name: rectovesical fistula
rectovesical fistula
HP:0034451.def: An aberrant, pathological communication between the rectum and the bladder.

name: rectoureteral fistula
rectoureteral fistula
HP:0034452.def: An abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the ureter.

name: arachnoid granulation
arachnoid granulation
HP:0034454.def: Arachnoid granulations (AGs) are tufts of arachnoid membrane invaginated into the dural sinuses through which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) enters the venous system. The lesions are primarily located in the parasagittal region along the superior sagittal sinus, which is occasionally seen at the transverse sinus. Normally dural venous sinus AGs typically range from 2 to 8 mm in size, but may grow enough to expand the dural sinuses, and even the inner table, diploic space and outer table of the skull.

name: increased csf taurine concentration
increase csf taurine concentration
HP:0034455.def: Increased concentration of taurine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: elevated circulating glutathione concentration
elevate circulate glutathione concentration
HP:0034456.def: An abnormally increased level of glutathione in the blood circulation.

name: hawkinsinuria
hawkinsinuria
HP:0034457.def: The concentration of hawkinsin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated urinary phenylpyruvic acid level
elevate urinary phenylpyruvic acid level
HP:0034458.def: An abnormally increased amount of phenylpyruvic acid in the urine.

name: ameliorated by lumbar puncture
ameliorate by lumbar puncture
HP:0034459.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by lumbar puncture.

name: increased csf uracil concentration
increase csf uracil concentration
HP:0034460.def: An increased level of uracil in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: elevated urine kynurenine level
elevate urine kynurenine level
HP:0034461.def: An abnormally increased amount of kynurenine in the urine.

name: increased csf l - alloisoleucine concentration
increase csf l - alloisoleucine concentration
HP:0034462.def: An abnormally increased concentration of L-alloisoleucine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: hydroxylysinemia
hydroxylysinemia
HP:0034463.def: An increased concentration of hydroxylysine in the blood circulation. Hydroxylysine arises from a post-translational hydroxy modification of lysine and is unique to collagen and proteins containing collagen-like sequences. Elevated concentrations of hydroxylysine may indicate increased bone turnover.

name: homocitrullinuria
homocitrullinuria
HP:0034464.def: An increased amount of L-homocitrulline in the urine. L-homocitrulline is an L-lysine derivative that is L-lysine having a carbamoyl group at the N(6)-position. It is found in individuals with urea cycle disorders.

name: 2 - hydroxyadipic aciduria
2 - hydroxyadipic aciduria
HP:0034465.def: An increase in the level of 2-hydroxyadipic acid in the urine.

name: homoargininuria
homoargininuria
HP:0034466.def: An increased amount of homoarginine in the urine. Homoarginine is a nonproteinogenic alpha amino acid.

name: increased urinary cysteine level
increase urinary cysteine level
HP:0034467.def: An increased concentration of cysteine in the urine.

name: gastric xanthoma
gastric xanthoma
HP:0034468.def: Gastric xanthomas (also known as xanthelasmas) are are plaque-like red lesions defined by the presence of histiocytic containing lipids.

name: decreased stool elastase level
decreased stool elastase level
HP:0034469.def: Reduced amount of pancreatic elastase in the stool. This feature may be observed with pancreatic insufficiency.

name: elevated stool chloride content
elevate stool chloride content
HP:0034470.def: Elevated amount of chloride in the stool.

name: increased fecal coproporphyrin iii : coproporphyrin i ratio
increased fecal coproporphyrin iii : coproporphyrin i ratio
HP:0034471.def: Abnormal relative increase in the amount of fecal coproporphyrin III as compared to coproporphyrin I in the feces.
synonym: coproporphyrin isomer iii / i ratio high in stool
coproporphyrin isomer iii / i ratio high in stool

name: increased fecal harderoporphyrin
increased fecal harderoporphyrin
HP:0034472.def: Abnormally high concentration of harderoporphyrin in feces.

name: increased fecal heptacarboxylporphyrin
increased fecal heptacarboxylporphyrin
HP:0034473.def: Abnormally high concentration of heptacarboxylporphyrin in feces.

name: increased fecal pentacarboxylporphyrin
increased fecal pentacarboxylporphyrin
HP:0034474.def: Abnormally high concentration of pentacarboxylporphyrin in feces.

name: increased fecal isocoproporphyrin
increased fecal isocoproporphyrin
HP:0034475.def: Abnormally high concentration of isocoproporphyrin in feces.

name: positive fecal clostridium botulinum test
positive fecal clostridium botulinum test
HP:0034476.def: Identification of Clostridium botulinum toxin in the feces.

name: perihepatic adhesions
perihepatic adhesion
HP:0034477.def: Abnormal union of the membranous surfaces of the liver capsule and the parietal peritoneum due to inflammation or injury. Adhesions may be visualized by laparoscopy and may have a violin string appearance.

name: dilated vas deferens
dilate va deferens
HP:0034478.def: Abnormal increase in diameter (expansion) of the vas deferens.

name: enlarged epididymis
enlarge epididymis
HP:0034479.def: Abnormal increase in the size of the epididymis.

name: atypical gestures
atypical gesture
HP:0034481.def: Spontaneous production of communicative gestures that are perceived as odd or mechanical, or are poorly integrated with other means of communication. This may include inaccurate mimicry of typical gestures.

name: bone marrow vacuolated lymphocytes
bone marrow vacuolated lymphocyte
HP:0034483.def: The presence of lymphocytes with multilple vacuoles (a membrane-bound cell organelle) in the bone marrow.

name: spinal cord calcifications
spinal cord calcification
HP:0034484.def: The presence of calcium deposition in the spinal cord.

name: neuroepithelial cyst
neuroepithelial cyst
HP:0034485.def: A benign epithelial-lined cystic lesion that can occur anywhere in the neuraxis. Neuroepithelial cysts are ependymal or epithelial lined fluid collections of unknown etiology within the central nervous system parenchyma with no obvious ventricular or subarachnoid connection. Most cysts are asymptomatic, however, some present with seizures, mass effect, or rarely with movement disorders. On imaging, they present as CSF-like parenchymal cysts with smooth, rounded borders and minimal or no surrounding signal intensity abnormality.

name: reduced circulating interleukin 7 concentration
reduce circulate interleukin 7 concentration
HP:0034486.def: A diminished concentration of interleukin-7 in the circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 12 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 12 concentration
HP:0034487.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-12 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 13 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 13 concentration
HP:0034488.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-13 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 2 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 2 concentration
HP:0034489.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-2 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 4 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 4 concentration
HP:0034490.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-4 in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating interleukin 5 concentration
increase circulate interleukin 5 concentration
HP:0034491.def: An increased concentration of interleukin-5 in the blood circulation.

name: salpingitis
salpingitis
HP:0034492.def: An inflammation of the fallopian tube.

name: tubo - ovarian abscess
tubo - ovarian abscess
HP:0034493.def: A tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) is a complex infectious mass of the adnexa that forms as a sequela of pelvic inflammatory disease.

name: opacified paranasal sinuses
opacified paranasal sinus
HP:0034494.def: White appearance (radio-opaqueness) of a paranasal sinus on radiography.

name: elevated brain glutamine level by mrs
elevate brain glutamine level by mr
HP:0034495.def: An increased in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: abnormal brain glutamine level by mrs
abnormal brain glutamine level by mr
HP:0034496.def: A deviation from normal in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: increased urinary hexanoic acid level
increase urinary hexanoic acid level
HP:0034497.def: The concentration of hexanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia
hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia
HP:0034498.def: Hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a benign hepatic tumor. FNH develops within hepatic parenchymal tissue that is otherwise histologically normal. Macroscopically, the tumor is characterized by the presence of depressed, grayish-white scar, which is generally (but not always) located at the center of the lesion, with fibrous septa radiating outward, toward the periphery of the tumor. This stellate scar is found in only 50% of all FNH nodules, but its presence is regarded as pathognomonic. The lesion itself is usually lighter in color than the tissue that surrounds it, and it sometimes has a yellowish hue. FNH nodules are generally not capsulated; their margins are well defined, and they are sometimes lobulated.

name: increased bone marrow iron
increase bone marrow iron
HP:0034499.def: An increased amount of iron in the bone marrow.

name: glenoid fracture
glenoid fracture
HP:0034500.def: A fracture of the glenoid fossa, a relatively shallow dish is located on the lateral scapula and is the socket portion of the shoulder joint that meets to articulate the humeral head.

name: widened mediastinum
widen mediastinum
HP:0034501.def: Abnormal increase in the width of the mediastinum, often defined as being greater than 6 to 8 cm.

name: narrow mediastinum
narrow mediastinum
HP:0034502.def: Abnormal decrease in the width of the mediastinum.

name: ovarian torsion
ovarian torsion
HP:0034503.def: Ovarian torsion is a twisting of the ligaments that support the adnexa, cutting off the blood flow to the ovary.

name: septate gallbladder
septate gallbladder
HP:0034504.def: Septate gallbladder is characterized by the presence of a septum that divides the gallbladder in two chambers. When the septum dividing the gallbladder lies longitudinally it is called bilobed gallbladder and when there is a transverse septum separating the fundus from the rest of the gallbladder it is called an hour-glass gallbladder.

name: gallbladder wall thickening
gallbladder wall thickening
HP:0034505.def: Abnormal increased in the thickness of the wall of the gallbladder.

name: gallbladder enlargement
gallbladder enlargement
HP:0034506.def: Abnormal increased in the thickness of the size of the gallbladder.

name: gallbladder mass
gallbladder mass
HP:0034507.def: An abnormal lesion or swelling seen on gallbladder imaging.

name: fingerprint bodies
fingerprint body
HP:0034508.def: Fingerprint bodies are inclusion bodies located at the periphery of the muscle fibers underneath the sarcolemma (subsarcolemmal), consisting of non-membrane-bound packed lamellae arranged in concentric patterns resembling fingerprints.
synonym: muscle biopsy : fingerprint bodies at periphery of muscle fibers
muscle biopsy : fingerprint body at periphery of muscle fiber
muscle biopsy : fingerprint bodies at periphery of muscle fibres
muscle biopsy : fingerprint body at periphery of muscle fibre

name: spheroid bodies
spheroid body
HP:0034509.def: An accumulation of myofilamentous material within individual muscle fibers, forming usually round but occasionally elongated bodies ranging from 2 to 15 pm in size. The so-called spheroid bodies stain green with the modified trichrome preparation and are mainly present in the periphery of type 1 muscle fibers, where they may occupy large sectors sharply demarcated from the remainder of the cross-sectioned muscle fiber.

name: abnormal muscle tissue enzyme activity or level
abnormal muscle tissue enzyme activity or level
HP:0034510.def: Any deviation from the normal activity or histological staining of an enzyme in muscle tissue, usually measured in a muscle biopsy specimen.

name: reduced muscle aconitase activity
reduce muscle aconitase activity
HP:0034511.def: Diminished activity of the enzyne aconitase in muscle tissue.

name: transitional - cell carcinoma of the ureter
transitional - cell carcinoma of the ureter
HP:0034512.def: A cancer of the ureter that most often arises in the distal third of the ureter and is often diagnosed during the sixth and seventh decades of life. The most common presentation is gross hematuria or flank pain.

name: increased circulating interferon - alpha concentration
increase circulate interferon - alpha concentration
HP:0034513.def: An elevation in the concentration of interferon alpha measured in the blood circulation.

name: liver hamartoma
liver hamartoma
HP:0034514.def: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the liver.

name: ameloblastoma
ameloblastoma
HP:0034515.def: Ameloblastoma is a benign odontogenic tumor generally present in the jaw bone. The tumor originates from the residual epithelium of the tooth germ, epithelium of odontogenic cysts stratified squamous epithelium and epithelium of the enamel organ.

name: ameliorated by ketogenic diet
ameliorate by ketogenic diet
HP:0034516.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by following a ketogenic diet.

name: pretibial hyperpigmentation
pretibial hyperpigmentation
HP:0034517.def: Darkening of the area of skin that overlies the shin.

name: muscle fiber fuchsinophilic inclusion bodies
muscle fiber fuchsinophilic inclusion body
HP:0034519.def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells that react positively with acid fuchsin.

name: esophageal myenteric plexus degeneration
esophageal myenteric plexus degeneration
HP:0034520.def: Deterioration of the cells of the myenteric plexus (also known as the Auerbach plexus) located between the layers of the muscular propria of the esophagus.

name: periorificial hyperkeratosis
periorificial hyperkeratosis
HP:0034521.def: Scaling and overgrowth of horny tissue of the skin surrounding body orifices (including peri-auricular, peri-oral, peri-anal areas.

name: eosinophilic lymph node infiltration
eosinophilic lymph node infiltration
HP:0034522.def: Presence of an elevated number of eosinophils in a lymph node (usually as demonstrated by lymph node biopsy).

name: blood parasite
blood parasite
HP:0034523.def: Detection of a parasitic organism in the blood stream. Blood parasites include malaria plasmodia, microfilaria species, trypanosomes (the causative agents of African sleeping sickness and South American Changas disease) and the causative agents of schistosomiasis of the bladder and the intestine.

name: bloodstream trypomastigotes
bloodstream trypomastigotes
HP:0034524.def: Presence of trypomastigote parasites in the blood stream. This finding can be demonstrated by the identification of trypomastigote parasites on peripheral blood smear.

name: adamantinoma
adamantinoma
HP:0034525.def: A primary low-grade, malignant bone tumor that is predominantly located in the mid-portion of the tibia. Histologically, classic adamantinoma is a biphasic tumor characterized by epithelial and osteofibrous components that may be intermingled with each other in various proportions and differentiating patterns.

name: abnormal enzyme activity in muscle tissue
abnormal enzyme activity in muscle tissue
HP:0034526.def: Deviation from the normal activity of an enzyme in muscle tissue.

name: reduced muscle phosphoglycerate kinase activity
reduce muscle phosphoglycerate kinase activity
HP:0034527.def: Reduced activity of phosphoglycerate kinase (PGK) in muscle tissue. PGK is a glycolytic enzyme that catalyses one of the two ATP-producing reactions in the glycolytic pathway, through the conversion of 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to 3-phosphoglycerate.

name: reduced fibroblast type iii procollagen synthesis
reduce fibroblast type iii procollagen synthesis
HP:0034528.def: Diminished production of type III procollagen by cultured skin fibroblasts.
synonym: type iii procollagen synthesis by fibroblasts low
type iii procollagen synthesis by fibroblast low

name: reduced muscle myoadenylate deaminase activity
reduce muscle myoadenylate deaminase activity
HP:0034529.def: Diminished activity of the enzyme myoadenylate deaminase. Myoadenylate deaminase is the muscle isoform of adenosine monophosphate (AMP) deaminase and catalyzes the deamination of AMP to inosine monophosphate and ammonia.

name: bent long bone
bent long bone
HP:0034530.def: A developmental defect of a long bone, such as the femur or the humerus, characterized by a sharply curve deviation located in the metaphysis (shaft) of the bone.

name: tracheal rupture
tracheal rupture
HP:0034531.def: A break or tear in the trachea.

name: increased myocardial glycogen content
increase myocardial glycogen content
HP:0034532.def: Elevated amount of glycogen in the myocardium.

name: triggered by monoamine oxidase inhibitor
trigger by monoamine oxidase inhibitor
HP:0034533.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a monoamine oxidase inhibitor.

name: triggered by serotonin reuptake inhibitor
trigger by serotonin reuptake inhibitor
HP:0034534.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

name: ameliorated by acetazolamide
ameliorate by acetazolamide
HP:0034535.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with acetazolamide.

name: ameliorated by exposure to medication
ameliorate by exposure to medication
HP:0034536.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with a medication. Terms in this subhierarchy are intended to be used for cases in which the fact that a manifestation of a disease responds to a specific treatment can be used in the differential diagnosis.

name: ameliorated by vitamin b12
ameliorate by vitamin b12
HP:0034537.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with vitamin B12.

name: ameliorated by thiamine
ameliorate by thiamine
HP:0034538.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with thiamine.

name: ameliorated by dantrolene
ameliorate by dantrolene
HP:0034539.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with dantrolene.

name: ameliorated by biotin
ameliorate by biotin
HP:0034540.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with biotin.

name: reduced bone - marrow megakaryocyte size
reduce bone - marrow megakaryocyte size
HP:0034541.def: Decreased in average size (diameter) of megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Megakaryocyte diameter can be assessed as using automated cellular imaging systems.

name: hairshafts with longitudinal grooves
hairshafts with longitudinal groove
HP:0034542.def: Long narrow depressions running lengthwise in hairshafts. This feature can be appreciated by scanning electron microsopy.

name: mycobacterium bacteremia
mycobacterium bacteremia
HP:0034543.def: Presence of viable mycobacteria in the blood.

name: decreased delta - aminolevulinate dehydratase activity
decrease delta - aminolevulinate dehydratase activity
HP:0034544.def: Reduced activity of the enzyme delta-aminolevulinate dehydratase. The enzyme is active in erythrocytes.

name: elevated circulating pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor activity
elevate circulate pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor activity
HP:0034545.def: Increased activity of the enzyme pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor in the blood circulation.
synonym: elevated circulating serine protease inhibitor kazal type i
elevate circulate serine protease inhibitor kazal type i

name: presence of uterus in 46 , xy individual
presence of uterus in 46 , xy individual
HP:0034546.def: A developmental anomaly in which an individual with an X chromosome and a Y chromosome (usually 46,XY) has a uterus. The uterus and Fallopian tubes are derived from the Müllerian duct and thus this phenotype is generally also associated with the presence of Fallopian tubes.

name: intraluminal meconium calcification
intraluminal meconium calcification
HP:0034547.def: Deposition of calcium in meconium present in the internal cavity of the fetal bowel. This manifestation may be the result of any distal intestinal obstruction.

name: portal vein hypoplasia
portal vein hypoplasia
HP:0034548.def: A developmental defect characterized by underdevelopment of hte portal vein.

name: adrenal leiomyoma
adrenal leiomyoma
HP:0034549.def: Adrenal leiomyoma is a rare, benign solid tumor that develops from the smooth muscle of the adrenal vein and its tributaries

name: small intestinal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
small intestinal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
HP:0034550.def: Infiltration of the wall of the small intestine by lymphocytes and mature plasma cells.

name: triggered by neuroleptic medication
trigger by neuroleptic medication
HP:0034551.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to neuroleptic (also known as antipsychotic) medication.

name: abnormal peroxisomal morphology
abnormal peroxisomal morphology
HP:0034552.def: Structural anomaly of peroxisomes, which are small, membrane-enclosed metabolic organelles with roles in the metabolism of complex lipids and reactive ionic species.

name: absence of peroxisomes
absence of peroxisomes
HP:0034553.def: Lack of observable peroxisomes. This feature can be observed by immunohistochemical staining of cultured cells (such as fibroblasts) or by electronmicroscopy.

name: paucity of peroxisomes
paucity of peroxisomes
HP:0034554.def: Reduced number of observable peroxisomes per cell. This feature can be observed by immunohistochemical staining of cultured cells (such as fibroblasts) or by electronmicroscopy.

name: reduced sulfide : quinone oxidoreductase activity
reduce sulfide : quinone oxidoreductase activity
HP:0034555.def: Reduced activity of the enzyme sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase, which typically is measured in a biopsy specimen from liver or muscle.

name: deficit at segmental level
deficit at segmental level
HP:0034556.def: Refers to distribution of neurological deficits that corresponds to a deficit of a specific spinal segment and all segments below it.

name: rhabdoid tumor
rhabdoid tumor
HP:0034557.def: Rhabdoid tumors are rare aggressive malignancies in infants and young children with a poor prognosis. The most common anatomic localizations are the central nervous system, the kidneys, and other soft tissues.

name: rhabdoid tumor of the ovary
rhabdoid tumor of the ovary
HP:0034558.def: A highly aggressive, extremely rare neoplasm of the ovary that is usually seen in children. The term rhabdoid is used because the tumor cells resemble rhabdomyoblasts but lack myogenic markers.

name: cardiac rhabdoid tumor
cardiac rhabdoid tumor
HP:0034559.def: A rare and aggressive neoplasms developing mainly in the kidney but also in cerebral and extra-cerebral tissues and rarely in the heart. Histologically, rhabdoid renal and extrarenal tumors share common characteristics. The cells are polygonal, with eccentric, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions. The tumors have an infiltrative growth pattern, necrosis, and high proliferative index. The immunohistochemistry tools of investigation facilitate differential diagnosis by showing loss of INI-1 expression, usually accompanied by germline mutations of the SMARCB1 gene. When INI-1 is still expressed in the affected tissues, a rhabdoid tumor with SMARCA4 mutations should be considered.

name: malignant rhabdoid tumor of the bladder
malignant rhabdoid tumor of the bladder
HP:0034560.def: A rhabdoid tumor (a rare aggressive malignancies in infants and young children with a poor prognosis) originating in the urinary bladder.

name: malignant rhabdoid tumor of liver
malignant rhabdoid tumor of liver
HP:0034561.def: A malginant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) originating in the liver. MRT are best characterized by the presence of round or polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, typical eosinophilic perinuclear inclusions, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemical expression of vimentin and epithelial markers and lack of staining for S-100, myoglobin and desmin are commonly found, but are non-specific.

name: malignant rhabdoid tumor of muscle
malignant rhabdoid tumor of muscle
HP:0034562.def: A malginant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) originating in muscle tissue.

name: neck teratoma
neck teratoma
HP:0034563.def: A teratoma located in the neck.

name: kidney teratoma
kidney teratoma
HP:0034564.def: A teratoma located in a kidney.

name: elevated urinary 5 - amino - 4 - imidazolecarboxamide - riboside level
elevate urinary 5 - amino - 4 - imidazolecarboxamide - riboside level
HP:0034565.def: Increased amount of 5-amino-4-imidazolecarboxamide(AICA)-riboside in the urine. AICA-riboside is the dephosphorylated counterpart of AICAR, an intermediate of de novo purine biosynthesis.

name: aplasia of posterior communicating artery
aplasia of posterior communicating artery
HP:0034566.def: A developmental anomnaly characterized by the lack of development of the posterior communicating artery.
synonym: absence of both posterior communicating arteries
absence of both posterior communicating artery

name: optic pit
optic pit
HP:0034567.def: A developmental anomaloy characterized by congenital excavation of the optic nerve head.

name: ameliorated by naloxone
ameliorate by naloxone
HP:0034568.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with naloxone, an opioid antagonist.

name: ameliorated by pyridoxal phosphate
ameliorate by pyridoxal phosphate
HP:0034569.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingestion of pyridoxal phosphate (activated vitamin B6).

name: thickened intrahepatic portal venules
thicken intrahepatic portal venule
HP:0034570.def: Increased width of the vascular wall of portal venules within the liver.

name: ovarian fibrosis
ovarian fibrosis
HP:0034571.def: Excessive proliferation of fibroblasts and deposition of extracellular matrix within the ovary.

name: pigment incontinence
pigment incontinence
HP:0034572.def: A process in which melanosomes (melanin granules) are deposited in the dermis. The dermal melanosomes are observed to be mainly in macrophages. This phenomenon of pigmentary incontinence usually follows an inflammatory process with the basic feature of basal cell damage, such as in lichen planus, lupus erythematosus, Riehl's melanosis, incontinentia pigmenti (Bloch-Sulzberger), and fixed drug eruption. Incontinence of pigment, or dropping off of epidermal melanin into the dermis, frequently produces a clinically recognizable and characteristic slate-gray pigmentation.

name: reduced epidermal keratin 10 protein expression
reduce epidermal keratin 10 protein expression
HP:0034574.def: Amount of keratin 10 in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

name: reduced epidermal collagen iv protein expression
reduce epidermal collagen iv protein expression
synonym: skin biopsy : collagen iv antibody staining abnormal or absent
skin biopsy : collagen iv antibody stain abnormal or absent

name: reduced epidermal bullous pemphigoid antigen 1 protein expression
reduce epidermal bullous pemphigoid antigen 1 protein expression
HP:0034576.def: Lower than normal amount of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1 (BP230) in the epidermis.
synonym: skin biopsy : bpag1 - e antibody staining abnormal or absent
skin biopsy : bpag1 - e antibody stain abnormal or absent

name: reduced epidermal collagen vii protein expression
reduce epidermal collagen vii protein expression
synonym: skin biopsy : collagen vii antibody staining abnormal or absent

name: bloodstream trypanosoma cruzi
bloodstream trypanosoma cruzi
HP:0034581.def: Presence of Trypanosoma cruzi in the blood stream. Trypanosoma cruzii is the etiological agent of Chagas disease.
synonym: trypanosoma cruzi present on peripheral blood smear
trypanosoma cruzi present on peripheral blood smear

name: abnormal lymph node cell composition
abnormal lymph node cell composition
HP:0034582.def: A deviation from the normal distribution of cell types or their relative proprotions in a lymph node.

name: lipid - laden lymph node macrophages
lipid - laden lymph node macrophage
HP:0034583.def: Lymph node with increased numbers of macrophages heavily laden with lipids.

name: cochlear nerve hypoplasia
cochlear nerve hypoplasia
HP:0034585.def: A developmental defect characterized by underdevelopment of the cochlear nerve.

name: glutathionuria
glutathionuria
HP:0034586.def: Level of glutathione in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

name: nevus psiloliparus
nevus psiloliparus
HP:0034587.def: Nevus psiloliparus is a rare fatty tissue nevus that is a marker for encephalocraniocutaneous lipomatosis, a neurocutaneous syndrome with ocular and central nervous system anomalies. Clinically, nevus psiloliparus is often described as a congenital alopecia and appears as an irregularly shaped, circumscribed area of alopecia on the scalp. Histopathology demonstrates a near-complete absence of mature hair follicles with preservation of arrector pili muscles and mature adipocytes within the dermis.

name: crypt hyperplasia
crypt hyperplasia
HP:0034588.def: Crypt hyperplasia denotes elongation of the length of the crypts of Lieberkuhn, a process that initially precedes villous atrophy. Elongation may be caused by expansion of the lamina propria as a result of the proliferation of stromal cells, an influx of inflammatory cells and tissue remodelling.

name: increased circulating dehydroepiandrosterone - sulfate concentration
increase circulate dehydroepiandrosterone - sulfate concentration
HP:0034589.def: Concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: abnormal circulating thyroxine - binding globulin concentration
abnormal circulate thyroxine - binding globulin concentration
HP:0034590.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) in the blood circulation.

name: decreased circulating thyroxine - binding globulin concentration
decrease circulate thyroxine - binding globulin concentration
HP:0034591.def: A reduction from the normal concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) in the blood circulation.
synonym: thyroxine - binding globulin low in blood
thyroxine - bind globulin low in blood

name: elevated circulating beta - aminoisobutyric acid concentration
elevate circulate beta - aminoisobutyric acid concentration

synonym: beta - aminoisobutyric acid high in blood
beta - aminoisobutyric acid high in blood

name: elevated circulating dihydrouracil concentration
elevate circulate dihydrouracil concentration
HP:0034593.def: An increased concentration of dihydrouracil in the blood circulation. Dihydrouracil is an intermediate in the catabolism of uracil that is also known as 5,6-dihydrouracil.

name: elevated circulating dihydrothymine concentration
elevate circulate dihydrothymine concentration
HP:0034594.def: An increased concentration of dihydrothymine in the blood circulation. Dihydrouracil is an intermediate in the catabolism of thymine.

name: elevated circulating n - carbamyl - beta - alanine concentration
elevate circulate n - carbamyl - beta - alanine concentration

n - carbamyl - beta - aminoisobutyric acid high in blood

decrease csf creatinine concentration

name: decreased circulating biotin concentration
decrease circulate biotin concentration
HP:0034599.def: Concentration of biotin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating thrombopoietin concentration
elevate circulate thrombopoietin concentration
HP:0034600.def: Concentration of thrombopoietin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the liver and kidney that stimulates the production and differentiation of megakaryocytes.

name: decreased circulating c1q concentration
decrease circulate c1q concentration
HP:0034601.def: Concentration or activity of the C1q protein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. C1q is the first component of the classical pathway and is composed of the C1qA chain, C1qB chain, and C1qC chain, which are encoded by C1qA, C1qB, and C1qC genes.

name: decreased circulating apolipoprotein a - ii concentration
decrease circulate apolipoprotein a - ii concentration
HP:0034602.def: Concentration of apolipoprotein A-II below the lower limit of normal.
synonym: apolipoprotein a - ii low in blood
apolipoprotein a - ii low in blood

name: elevated circulating ca19 - 9 concentration
elevate circulate ca19 - 9 concentration
HP:0034603.def: Concentration of CA19-9 above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: elevated circulating sialylated lewis a antigen concentration
elevate circulating sialylated lewis a antigen concentration

name: elevated circulating dopa concentration
elevate circulate dopa concentration
HP:0034604.def: Concentration of DOPA (3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated csf dopa concentration
elevate csf dopa concentration
HP:0034605.def: Concentration of DOPA (3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine) in the cerebrospinal fluid above the upper limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating porphyrin concentration
elevate circulate porphyrin concentration
HP:0034606.def: Concentration of porphyrins or of a specific porphryin above the upper limit of normal. The most commonly tested circulating porphyrins are coproporphyrin, protoporphyrin, and uroporphyrin. Normally protoporphyrin is present in the highest concentration.

name: decreased circulating 17 - hydroxyprogesterone concentration
decrease circulate 17 - hydroxyprogesterone concentration
HP:0034607.def: Concentration of 17-hydroxyprogesterone in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: decreased circulating transcobalamin ii concentration
decrease circulate transcobalamin ii concentration
HP:0034608.def: Concentration of transcobalamin II in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: polychromasia
polychromasia
HP:0034609.def: Increased variation in the color of the erythrocytes (red blood cells), including pale red, normal or dark colors, indicating a highly variable hemoglobin concentration. Typically this indicates the release of immature erythrocytes in states of anemia.

name: decreased circulating myo - inositol concentration
decrease circulate myo - inositol concentration
HP:0034610.def: Concentration of myo-inositol in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: elevated circulating arabitol concentration
elevate circulate arabitol concentration

HP:0034613.def: Amount of erythritol in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0034614.def: Concentration of erythritol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: reduced circulating matrix metalloproteinase 2 concentration
reduce circulate matrix metalloproteinase 2 concentration
HP:0034615.def: Concentration of matrix metalloproteinase 2 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

name: abnormal circulating coenzyme concentration
abnormal circulate coenzyme concentration
HP:0034616.def: Concentration of a coenzyme (an organic molecule that binds to the active sites of an enzyme to promote the catalysis of a reaction) is above or below the limits of normal.

name: elevated circulating s - adenosyl methionine concentration
elevate circulate s - adenosyl methionine concentration
HP:0034617.def: Concentration of S-adenosyl methionine (SAM) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. SAM is a cosubstrate involved in methyl group transfers, transsulfuration, and aminopropylation.

name: abnormal circulating membrane cofactor protein concentration
abnormal circulate membrane cofactor protein concentration
HP:0034618.def: Concentration of membrane cofactor protein in the blood circulation outside the limits of normal. Membrane cofactor protein (MCP, CD46) is a cell surface complement regulatory protein which acts as a cofactor for the factor I-mediated cleavage of the activated complement components C3b/C4b.

name: decreased circulating membrane cofactor protein concentration
decrease circulate membrane cofactor protein concentration
HP:0034619.def: Concentration of membrane cofactor protein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

mcp ( membrane cofactor protein ) low in blood

name: elevated circulating membrane cofactor protein concentration
elevate circulate membrane cofactor protein concentration
HP:0034620.def: Concentration of membrane cofactor protein in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

name: hepatic xanthomatosis
hepatic xanthomatosis
HP:0034621.def: Lipid deposits localized within the liver. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

name: adrenal xanthomatosis
adrenal xanthomatosis
HP:0034622.def: Lipid deposits localized within the adrenal gland. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

name: splenic xanthomatosis
splenic xanthomatosis

spinal cord xanthomatosis

brain xanthomatosis

pulmonary xanthomatosis
HP:0034626.def: Lipid deposits localized within the lung. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

name: bone marrow xanthomatosis
bone marrow xanthomatosis

name: lymph node xanthomatosis
lymph node xanthomatosis
HP:0034628.def: Lipid deposits localized within one or more lymph nodes. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

name: xanthoma of bone
xanthoma of bone
HP:0034629.def: Xanthoma of bone is an exceedingly rare benign primary bone tumor histologically characterized by mononuclear macrophage-like cells, abundant foam cells, and multinucleated giant cells.

name: ameliorated by folinic acid
ameliorate by folinic acid
HP:0034630.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with folinic acid.

name: triggered by succinylcholine anesthetic
trigger by succinylcholine anesthetic
HP:0034631.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a succinylcholine anesthetic such as suxamethonium.

name: exogenous androgen exposure
exogenous androgen exposure
HP:0034632.def: History of having been treated with an exogenous androgen medication.

name: reduced muscle enolase activity
reduce muscle enolase activity
HP:0034633.def: Diminished activity of the enzyme enolase in muscle tissue. The enzyme enolase catalyzes the interconversion of 2-phosphoglycerate and phosphoenolpyruvate. In adult human muscle, over 90% of enolase activity is accounted for by the beta-enolase subunit, the protein product of the ENO3 gene.
synonym: muscle biopsy : beta - enolase activity low
muscle biopsy : beta - enolase activity low

name: dopamine antagonist exposure
dopamine antagonist exposure
HP:0034634.def: History of having been treated with a dopamine antagonist including metaclopramide, phenothiazine; haloperidol, chlorpromazine, promethazine, prochlorperazine, ziprasidone, and quetiapine.

name: muscle fiber granulofilamentous inclusion bodies
muscle fiber granulofilamentous inclusion body
HP:0034635.def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells that contain a mxiture of granules and filaments.

name: bone marrow myeloid vacuolization
bone marrow myeloid vacuolization
HP:0034636.def: Formation of vacuoles (a space within a cell that is empty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in the cytoplasm of myeloid precursors in the bone marrow.
synonym: vacuolization of bone marrow myeloid precursors
vacuolization of bone marrow myeloid precursor

name: pulmonary cylindroma
pulmonary cylindroma
HP:0034637.def: A cylindroma located in the lung. Cylindromas are well-circumscribed, smooth, pale pink nodular tumors, often with arborizing vessels visible. The tumors are slow growing and vary in size from a few millimeters to over 5 mm.

name: colonic fibrinopurulent exudate
colonic fibrinopurulent exudate
HP:0034638.def: Fluid visible on the colonic surface containing fibrin, inflammatory cells, and cellular debris.

name: bloodstream microfilaria
bloodstream microfilaria
HP:0034639.def: Presence of filaria in the blood stream. Filariasis is a common cause of elephantiasis in Coastal Districts of India. The initial manifestations are repeated episodes of fever with chills and rigor, lymphadenopathy which gradually progress to elephantiasis. In India filarial infestation is commonly caused by W. bancrofti and Brugia malayi, the former responsible for almost 98 percent of all cases.

name: skin infectious agent
skin infectious agent
HP:0034640.def: The presence of an infectious agent in the skin.

name: dermal microfilaria
dermal microfilaria
HP:0034641.def: Presence of filariae in the skin.

name: dermal papillary iga deposition
dermal papillary iga deposition
HP:0034642.def: Accumulation of immunoglobulin A (IgA) surrounding dermal papillae, which are specialized cells that support the hair follicle.
synonym: granular iga deposits at the dermal papillae
granular iga deposit at the dermal papilla

name: dermal immune complex deposition
dermal immune complex deposition
HP:0034643.def: Accumulation of antigen-bound antibody in the skin.

abnormal liver metabolite concentration

hepatic polyglucosan accumulation

name: urinary bladder neurofibroma
urinary bladder neurofibroma
HP:0034646.def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) located in the urinary bladder.

synovial granuloma
HP:0034647.def: An aggregation of macrophages (forming in response to chronic inflammation) localized in the lining of a joint (synovium).

elevate urine suberylglycine level

elevate urine phenylpropionylglycine level
HP:0034651.def: Level of phenylpropionylglycine in urine above upper limit of normal.

name: elevated urine octenedioic acid level
elevate urine octenedioic acid level
HP:0034652.def: The concentration of octenedioic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

name: monocarboxylic aciduria
monocarboxylic aciduria
HP:0034653.def: Level of a monocarboxylic acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal. A monocarboxylic acid is an oxoacid containing one carboxy group.

name: elevated urine octanoic acid level
elevate urine octanoic acid level
HP:0034654.def: Amount of octanoic acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

elevate urine glutaconic acid level
HP:0034655.def: The concentration of glutaconic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

elevate urine 3 - hydroxyglutaric level

elevate urine propionylglycine level

elevate urine 4 - hydroxyisovaleric acid level
HP:0034663.def: Amount of 4-hydroxyisovaleric acid in urine above upper limit of normal.

elevate urine 2 - hydroxy - 3 - methylvaleric acid level
HP:0034664.def: Amount of 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal. 2-Hydroxy-3-methylpentanoic acid or 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid (HMVA) is an organic acid generated by L-isoleucine metabolism.

2 - hydroxy - 3 - methylvaleric acid high in urine

name: shoulder contracture
shoulder contracture
HP:0034665.def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the shoulder joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

name: shoulder extension contracture
shoulder extension contracture
HP:0034666.def: Lack of the full expected passive range of flexion of the shoulder joint (Shoulder flexion puts the arms from a resting position at one's sides to straight above the head; thus, with shoulder extension contracture it is not possible to raise the arms above the head fully).

name: thumb extension contracture
thumb extension contracture
HP:0034667.def: Movement in the sagittal plane that increases the angle of the thumb joint (straightens the joint); motion involving posterior bending of the vertebral column or returning to the upright position from a flexed position.

name: tongue myxoma
tongue myxoma
HP:0034668.def: A myxoma (benign soft tissue neoplasm characterized by the presence of spindle and stellate cells, lobulated growth pattern, and myxoid stroma formation) localized in the tongue.

name: abnormal knee morphology
abnormal knee morphology
HP:0034669.def: A structural abnormality of the knee joint or surrounding structures.

name: abnormal knee physiology
abnormal knee physiology
HP:0034670.def: A functional anomaly of the knee joint.

name: knee contracture
knee contracture
HP:0034671.def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the knee joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

name: knee extension contracture
knee extension contracture
HP:0034672.def: A type of knee joint contracture in which the knee lacks full expected flexion, such that the upper and lower leg cannot be brought together.

name: abnormal ankle morphology
abnormal ankle morphology
HP:0034673.def: A structural anomaly of the ankle.

name: abnormal ankle physiology
abnormal ankle physiology
HP:0034674.def: A functional anomaly of the ankle.

name: toe joint contracture
toe joint contracture
HP:0034675.def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of a toe joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

name: extension contracture of toe
extension contracture of toe
HP:0034676.def: A type of toe joint contracture in which the joint lacks full expected flexion, so that the two bony segments on either side of their connecting joint cannot be brought together.

name: finger joint contracture
finger joint contracture
HP:0034681.def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of a finger joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

name: extension contracture of finger
extension contracture of finger
HP:0034682.def: A type of finger joint contracture in which the joint lacks full expected flexion, so that the two bony segments on either side of their connecting joint cannot be brought together.

name: reduced muscle telethonin level
reduce muscle telethonin level
HP:0034683.def: Amount of telethonin protein expression in muscle tissue below lower limit of normal. Telethonin is a 19-kDa sarcomeric protein, localized to the Z-disc of skeletal and cardiac muscles.

muscle biopsy : telethonin low or absent

impaired cerebroside sulfate hydrolysis
