synonym: fusion involving bones of the upper limbs
fusion involve bone of the upper limb

name: synostosis of joints
synostosis of joint
HP:0100240.def: The abnormal fusion of neighboring bones across a joint.

name: ectopic respiratory mucosa
ectopic respiratory mucosa
HP:0100241.def: Ectopic respiratory epithelium presenting as a superficial lesion in the skin usually localised unilateral in the skin of the forearm and associated with ipsilateral hand malformations.

name: sarcoma
sarcoma
HP:0100242.def: A connective tissue neoplasm formed by proliferation of mesodermal cells. Bone and soft tissue sarcomas are the main types of sarcoma. Sarcoma is usually highly malignant.

name: leiomyosarcoma
leiomyosarcoma
HP:0100243.def: A smooth muscle connective tissue tumor, which is rare type of cancer that is a malignant neoplasm of smooth muscle. When such a neoplasm is benign, it is called a leiomyoma.

name: fibrosarcoma
fibrosarcoma
HP:0100244.def: A fibroblastic sarcoma is a malignant tumor derived from fibrous connective tissue and characterized by immature proliferating fibroblasts or undifferentiated anaplastic spindle cells.

name: desmoid tumors
desmoid tumor
HP:0100245.def: Benign, slow-growing tumors without any metastatic potential. Despite their benign nature, they can damage nearby structures causing organ dysfunction. Histologically they resemble low-grade fibrosarcomas, but they are very locally aggressive and tend to recur even after complete resection. There is a tendency for recurrence in the setting of prior surgery and the most common localisation of these tumors is intraabdominal from smooth muscle cells of the instestine.

name: osteoma
osteoma
HP:0100246.def: Osteomas are bony growths found most commonly on the skull and mandible; however, they may occur in any bone of the body. Osteomas do not usually cause clinical problems and do not become malignant.

name: recurrent singultus
recurrent singultus
HP:0100247.def: A contraction of the diaphragm that repeats several times per minute. In humans, the abrupt rush of air into the lungs causes the epiglottis to close, creating a hic sound. Also known as synchronous diaphragmatic flutter (SDF), or singultus, from the Latin singult, the act of catching one's breath while sobbing. The hiccup is an involuntary action involving a reflex arc.

name: hemiballismus
hemiballismus
HP:0100248.def: Hemiballismus is a rare movement disorder that is caused primarily by damage to various areas in the basal ganglia. Hemiballismus is usually characterized by involuntary flinging motions of the extremities. The movements are often violent and have wide amplitudes of motion. They are continuous and random and can involve proximal and/or distal muscles on one side of the body, while some cases even include the facial muscles. The more a patient is active, the more the movements increase. With relaxation comes a decrease in movements.

name: calcification of muscles
calcification of muscle
HP:0100249.def: Deposition of calcium salts in muscle tissue.

name: multiple central nervous system lipomas
multiple central nervous system lipoma
HP:0100251.def: The presence of multiple lipomas located in the central nervous system.
synonym: lipomas of the central nervous system
lipoma of the central nervous system

name: abnormality of the medullary cavity of the long bones
abnormality of the medullary cavity of the long bone
HP:0100253.def: An abnormality of the medullary cavity (medulla, innermost part), which is the central cavity of bone shafts where red bone marrow and/or yellow bone marrow (adipose tissue) is stored.
synonym: abnormality of the marrow cavity of the long bones
abnormality of the marrow cavity of the long bone

name: stenosis of the medullary cavity of the long bones
stenosis of the medullary cavity of the long bone
metaphyseal dysplasia
metaphyseal dysplasia
HP:0100255.def: The presence of dysplastic regions in metaphyseal regions.

name: senile plaques
senile plaque
HP:0100256.def: Senile plaques are extracellular deposits of amyloid in the gray matter of the brain.

name: ectrodactyly
ectrodactyly
HP:0100257.def: A condition in which middle parts of the hands and/or feet (digits and meta-carpals and -tarsals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic 3rd toe/fingers over absent 2nd or 3rd toes/fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands and/or feet.

name: preaxial polydactyly
preaxial polydactyly
HP:0100258.def: A form of polydactyly in which the extra digit or digits are localized on the side of the thumb or great toe.

name: postaxial polydactyly
postaxial polydactyly
HP:0100259.def: A form of polydactyly in which the extra digit or digits are localized on the side of the fifth finger or fifth toe.

name: mesoaxial polydactyly
mesoaxial polydactyly
HP:0100260.def: The presence of a supernumerary finger or toe (not a thumb or hallux) involving the third or fourth metacarpal/tarsal with associated osseous syndactyly.

name: abnormal tendon morphology
abnormal tendon morphology
HP:0100261.def: An abnormality of the structure or form of the tendons, also often called sinews.

name: synostosis of metacarpals / metatarsals
synostosis of metacarpal / metatarsal
synonym: fusion of long bones of hand / long bones of foot
fusion of long bone of hand / long bone of foot

name: synostosis of carpals / tarsals
synostosis of carpal / tarsal
HP:0100266.def: The carpus consists of the scaphoid, lunate, triquetal, pisiform, captitate, hamate, trapezoid, and trapezium bones. The tarsus consists of the talus, calcaneus, cuboid, cuneiform, and navicular bones. This term applies if there is any fusion among the bones of the carpus or tarsus.
synonym: coalescence of carpal and tarsal bones
coalescence of carpal and tarsal bone
fusion of carpal and tarsal bones
fusion of carpal and tarsal bone

name: lip pit
lip pit
HP:0100267.def: A depression located on a lip.

name: upper lip pit
upper lip pit
HP:0100268.def: Depression located on the vermilion of the upper lip, usually paramedian.

name: paramedian lip pit
paramedian lip pit
HP:0100269.def: Depression located paramedially on the vermilion of a lip.

name: abnormality of dorsoventral patterning of the limbs
abnormality of dorsoventral patterning of the limb
HP:0100270.def: An abnormality resulting from a defect or disruption of dorsoventral patterning that normally happens during early development of the limbs. A disruption of the normal development of the dorsoventral axis may lead to a variable spectrum of different phenotypic abnormalities that may affect the nails and or palmar and dorsal side of the hands and/or feet, ultimately changing the normal dorsoventral appearance of the affected limbs.

name: hyponasal speech
hyponasal speech
HP:0100271.def: Hyponasal speech is when there is an abnormally reduced nasal airflow during speech often in a setting of nasal obstruction or congestion.

name: branchial sinus
branchial sinus
HP:0100272.def: A congenital branchial sinus is a remnant of the embryonic branchial arches and their intervening clefts and pouches that has failed to regress completely. Sinuses typically have their external orifice inferior to the ramus of the mandible. They may traverse the parotid gland, and run in close vicinity to the facial nerve in the external auditory canal.

name: gustatory lacrimation
gustatory lacrimation
HP:0100274.def: Gustatory lacrimation results from an aberrant innervation of fibres from the seventh cranial nerve to the pterygopalatine ganglion which are destined originally for the submandibular ganglion. This aberrant innervation leads to uncontrollable tearing while eating or in anticipation of a meal.

name: diffuse cerebellar atrophy
diffuse cerebellar atrophy
HP:0100275.def: Diffuse unlocalised atrophy affecting the cerebellum.

name: skin pit
skin pit
HP:0100276.def: A small, skin-lined tract that leads from the surface to deep within the tissues.

name: periauricular skin pits
periauricular skin pit
HP:0100277.def: Benign congenital lesions of the periauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.

name: ulcerative colitis
ulcerative colitis
HP:0100279.def: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that includes characteristic ulcers, or open sores, in the colon. The main symptom of active disease is usually constant diarrhea mixed with blood, of gradual onset and intermittent periods of exacerbated symptoms contrasting with periods that are relatively symptom-free. In contrast to Crohn's disease this special form of colitis begins in the distal parts of the rectum, spreads continually upwards and affects only mucose and submucose tissue of the colon.

name: crohn 's disease
crohn 's disease
HP:0100280.def: A chronic granulomatous inflammatory disease of the intestines that may affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus, causing a wide variety of symptoms. It primarily causes abdominal pain, diarrhea which may be bloody, vomiting, or weight loss, but may also cause complications outside of the gastrointestinal tract such as skin rashes, arthritis, inflammation of the eye, tiredness, and lack of concentration. Crohn's disease is thought to be an autoimmune disease, in which the body's immune system attacks the gastrointestinal tract, causing inflammation.

name: chronic colitis
chronic colitis
HP:0100281.def: A chronic inflammatory disease of the large intestine (colon, cecum and rectum).

name: acute colitis
acute colitis
HP:0100282.def: An acute and self-limited inflammatory disease of the large intestine (colon, cecum and rectum).

name: emg : continuous motor unit activity at rest
emg : continuous motor unit activity at rest
HP:0100283.def: Continuous electromyographic activity of motor units at rest, i.e., without voluntary movement of the muscles.

name: emg : myotonic discharges
emg : myotonic discharge
HP:0100284.def: High frequency discharges in electromyography (EMG) that vary in amplitude and frequency, waxing and waning continuously with firing frequencies ranging from 150/second down to 20/second and producing a sound that has been referred to as a dive bomber sound.

name: emg : impaired neuromuscular transmission
emg : impaired neuromuscular transmission
HP:0100285.def: An electromyographic finding associated with erratic or absent neuromuscular transmission with erratic, moment-to-moment changes in the shape of the motor unit potential (MUP).

name: emg : slow motor conduction
emg : slow motor conduction
HP:0100287.def: The presence of reduced conduction velocity of motor nerves on electromyography.

name: emg : myokymic discharges
emg : myokymic discharge
HP:0100288.def: The presence of spontaneous bursts of rapidly firing potentials that recur at regular intervals of 2-10 per second and are unaffected by voluntary effort. This is an electromyographic (EMG) finding.

name: abnormality of pattern reversal visual evoked potentials
abnormality of pattern reversal visual evoke potential
abnormality of peripheral somatosensory evoked potentials
abnormality of peripheral somatosensory evoke potential
abnormality of central somatosensory evoked potentials
abnormality of central somatosensory evoke potential
amyloidosis of peripheral nerves
amyloidosis of peripheral nerve
HP:0100292.def: The presence of amyloid deposition in the nerves of the peripheral nervous system.

name: hypertrophied muscle fibers
hypertrophied muscle fiber
HP:0100293.def: The presence of an increased amount of muscle fibers with an increased diameter. This feature can be ascertained by microscopic examination of a muscle biopsy sample. Together with fiber size variation and atrophied muscle fibers, and hypertrophied muscle fibers are commonly found in myopathies.

name: increased endomysial connective tissue
increase endomysial connective tissue
HP:0100297.def: An increased volume of the endomysium, which is a connective tissue sheath that surrounds each muscule fiber. Together, bundles of muscle fibers form a fasciculus, surrounded by another layer of connective tissue called the perimysium.

name: muscle fiber tubular inclusions
muscle fiber tubular inclusion
HP:0100301.def: Unusual regions of densely packed membranous tubules known as tubular aggregates which present as membranous inclusions, derived from membranes of sarcoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, containing miscellaneous proteins with a variety of enzymatic activities.

name: muscle fiber cytoplasmatic inclusion bodies
muscle fiber cytoplasmatic inclusion body
HP:0100303.def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells. Inclusion bodies are aggregates (deposits) or stainable material, usually misfolded proteins.

name: muscle fiber intranuclear inclusion bodies
muscle fiber intranuclear inclusion body
HP:0100304.def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the nucleus of muscle cells. Inclusion bodies are aggregates (deposits) or stainable material, usually misfolded proteins.

name: ring fibers
ring fiber
HP:0100305.def: Ring fibers are formed by a bundle of peripheral myofibrils which are circumferentially oriented such that they encircle the internal portion of the sarcoplasm which is normal in structure and orientation.

name: muscle fiber hyaline bodies
muscle fiber hyaline body
HP:0100306.def: Subsarcolemmal, eosinophilic glass-like regions in the cytoplasm of muscle fibers. Hyaline bodies show significant reactivity to myofibrillar ATPase after acid pre-incubation and with immunohistochemistry, show intense reactivity with only slow myosin heavy chain. Electron microscopy of the affected areas show a lack of myofibrils and a uniform, finely granular matrix, sometimes suggesting a filamentous nature, containing few scattered nuclei and mitochondria.

name: cerebral cortical hemiatrophy
cerebral cortical hemiatrophy
HP:0100308.def: Atrophy of one side of the brain, characterized by findings including thinning of the cerebral cortex, reduced volume of the cerebral white matter with abnormal myelination, and enlargement of the ispilateral fourth ventricle.

name: subdural hemorrhage
subdural hemorrhage
HP:0100309.def: Hemorrhage occurring between the dura mater and the arachnoid mater.

name: epidural hemorrhage
epidural hemorrhage
HP:0100310.def: Hemorrhage occurring between the dura mater and the skull.

name: cerebral ventricular adhesions
cerebral ventricular adhesion
HP:0100311.def: Bands of scar-like tisssue that hve formed within a cerebral ventricle.

name: cerebral germinoma
cerebral germinoma
HP:0100312.def: The presence of a germ cell tumor of the cerebrum.

name: cerebral granulomatosis
cerebral granulomatosis
HP:0100313.def: Cerebral inflammation involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.

name: cerebral inclusion bodies
cerebral inclusion body
HP:0100314.def: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates of stainable substances within cells of the brain.

name: hirano bodies
hirano body
HP:0100316.def: Intracellular aggregates of actin and actin-associated proteins within nerve cells.

name: argyrophilic inclusion bodies
argyrophilic inclusion body
HP:0100317.def: Presence of abundant argyrophilic grains and coiled bodies on microscopic examination of brain tissue.

name: lafora bodies
lafora body
HP:0100318.def: An intraneuronal inclusion body composed of acid mucopolysaccharides.

name: cerebral hyaline bodies
cerebral hyaline body
HP:0100319.def: Cerebral eosinophilic, discrete, intracytoplasmatic inclusions of unknown significance.

name: rosenthal fibers
rosenthal fiber
HP:0100320.def: Thick, elongated, worm-like or corkscrew eosinophilic bundle that are found on H&E staining of the brain in the presence of long standing gliosis, occasional tumors, and some metabolic disorders.

name: abnormal dentate nucleus morphology
abnormal dentate nucleus morphology
HP:0100321.def: An abnormality of the dentate nucleus.

name: juvenile aseptic necrosis
juvenile aseptic necrosis
HP:0100323.def: Juvenile aseptic necrosis comprises a group of orthopedic diseases characterized by interruption of the blood supply of a bone, followed by localized bony necrosis most often of the epiphyses of bones of children or teenagers.

name: scleroderma
scleroderma
HP:0100324.def: A chronic autoimmune phenomenon characterized by fibrosis (or hardening) and vascular alterations of the skin.

name: immunologic hypersensitivity
immunologic hypersensitivity
HP:0100326.def: Immunological states where the immune system produces harmful responses upon reexposure to sensitising antigens.

name: cow milk allergy
cow milk allergy
HP:0100327.def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against cow milk protein.
synonym: immunoglobulin e - mediated cow milk allergy
immunoglobulin e - mediate cow milk allergy

name: carpometacarpal synostosis
carpometacarpal synostosis
HP:0100328.def: Fusion involving carpal and metacarpal bones.
synonym: fused wrist bones and long bones of hand
fuse wrist bone and long bone of hand

name: unilateral cleft lip
unilateral cleft lip
HP:0100333.def: A non-midline cleft of the upper lip on one side only.

name: non - midline cleft lip
non - midline cleft lip
HP:0100335.def: Clefting of the upper lip affecting the lateral portions of the upper lip rather than the midline/median region.
synonym: non - midline cleft of the upper lip
non - midline cleft of the upper lip
paramedian cleft of the upper lip
paramedian cleft of the upper lip

bilateral cleft lip
HP:0100336.def: A non-midline cleft of the upper lip on the left and right sides.

name: bilateral cleft palate
bilateral cleft palate
HP:0100337.def: Nonmidline cleft palate on the left and right sides.

name: abnormality of the os naviculare pedis
abnormality of the o naviculare pedis
contracture of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the 2nd toe
contracture of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the 2nd toe
HP:0100348.def: The proximal interphalangeal joint of the 2nd toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

contracture of the proximal interphalangeal joint of the 3rd toe
HP:0100349.def: The proximal interphalangeal joint of the 3rd toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

name: contractures of the distal interphalangeal joint of the 5th toe
contracture of the distal interphalangeal joint of the 5th toe
HP:0100355.def: The distal interphalangeal joint of the 5th toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

contracture of the outermost hinge joint of the 5th toe

name: contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 2nd toe
contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 2nd toe
HP:0100356.def: The joint between the second metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the 2nd toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

name: contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 3rd toe
contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 3rd toe
HP:0100357.def: The joint between the third metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the third toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

name: contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 4th toe
contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 4th toe
HP:0100358.def: The joint between the fourth metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the fourth toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

name: contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 5th toe
contracture of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the 5th toe
HP:0100359.def: The joint between the fifth metatarsal and the proximal phalanx of the fifth toe cannot be straightened actively or passively.

name: upper - limb joint contracture
upper - limb joint contracture
HP:0100360.def: A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint of the upper limb resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.
synonym: contractures of the joints of the upper limbs

name: erectile dysfunction
erectile dysfunction
HP:0100639.def: A multidimensional but common male sexual dysfunction that involves an alteration in any of the components of the erectile response, including organic, relational and psychological.

name: laryngeal cyst
laryngeal cyst
HP:0100640.def: Presence of a cyst (sac-like structure) located in the larynx.

name: neoplasm of the adrenal cortex
neoplasm of the adrenal cortex
HP:0100641.def: The presence of a neoplasm of the adrenal cortex.

name: neoplasm of the adrenal medulla
neoplasm of the adrenal medulla
HP:0100642.def: The presence of a neoplasm of the adrenal medulla.

name: abnormality of nail color
abnormality of nail color
HP:0100643.def: An anomaly of the color of the nail.

name: melanonychia
melanonychia
HP:0100644.def: Brown or black discoloration of the nails.

name: cystocele
cystocele
HP:0100645.def: Anterior vaginal wall prolapse with bulging of the bladder into the vagina.

name: graves disease
graf disease
HP:0100647.def: An autoimmune disease where the thyroid is overactive, producing an excessive amount of thyroid hormones (a serious metabolic imbalance known as hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis). This is caused by autoantibodies to the TSH-receptor (TSHR-Ab) that activate that TSH-receptor (TSHR), thereby stimulating thyroid hormone synthesis and secretion, and thyroid growth (causing a diffusely enlarged goiter). The resulting state of hyperthyroidism can cause a dramatic constellation of neuropsychological and physical signs and symptoms, which can severely compromise the patients.

name: neoplasm of the tongue
neoplasm of the tongue
HP:0100648.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the tongue.

name: neoplasm of the oral cavity
neoplasm of the oral cavity
HP:0100649.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the oral cavity.

name: vaginal neoplasm
vaginal neoplasm
HP:0100650.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the vagina.

name: type i diabetes mellitus
type i diabetes mellitus
HP:0100651.def: A chronic condition in which the pancreas produces little or no insulin. Type I diabetes mellitus is manifested by the sudden onset of severe hyperglycemia with rapid progression to diabetic ketoacidosis unless treated with insulin.

name: retrobulbar optic neuritis
retrobulbar optic neuritis
HP:0100654.def: Optic neuritis that occurs in the section of the optic nerve located behind the eyeball.

name: thoracoabdominal wall defect
thoracoabdominal wall defect
HP:0100656.def: Failure to close of the chest and abdominal wall likely caused by the failure of the ventral wall to close during week 4 of development.

name: thoracoabdominal eventration
thoracoabdominal eventration
HP:0100657.def: Congenital protrusion of the abdominal or thoracic viscera, usually with a defect of the sternum and ribs as well as of the abdominal walls.

name: cellulitis
cellulitis
HP:0100658.def: A bacterial infection and inflammation of the skin und subcutaneous tissues.

name: abnormal cerebral vascular morphology
abnormal cerebral vascular morphology
HP:0100659.def: An anomaly of the cerebral blood vessels.
synonym: abnormality of the cerebral blood vessels
abnormality of the cerebral blood vessel

name: dyskinesia
dyskinesia
HP:0100660.def: A movement disorder which consists of effects including diminished voluntary movements and the presence of involuntary movements.

name: trigeminal neuralgia
trigeminal neuralgia
HP:0100661.def: A neuropathic disorder characterized by episodes of intense pain in the face, originating from the trigeminal nerve. One, two, or all three branches of the nerve may be affected.

name: synotia
synotia
HP:0100663.def: A congenital malformation characterized by the union or approximation of the ears in front of the neck, often accompanied by the absence or defective development of the lower jaw.

name: angioedema
angioedema
HP:0100665.def: Rapid swelling (edema) of the dermis, subcutaneous tissue, mucosa and submucosal tissues of the skin of the face, normally around the mouth, and the mucosa of the mouth and/or throat, as well as the tongue during a period of minutes to several hours. The swelling can also occur elsewhere, typically in the hands. Angioedema is similar to urticaria, but the swelling is subcutaneous rather than on the epidermis.

name: intestinal duplication
intestinal duplication
HP:0100668.def: A developmental disorder in which there is a duplication the entire intestine or of a portion of the intestine.

name: abnormal pigmentation of the oral mucosa
abnormal pigmentation of the oral mucosa
HP:0100669.def: An abnormality of the pigmentation of the mucosa of the mouth.
synonym: abnormal color of the oral mucosa
abnormal color of the oral mucosa
abnormal colour of the oral mucosa
abnormal colour of the oral mucosa
abnormal pigmentation of oral mucous membrane
abnormal pigmentation of oral mucous membrane
abnormal pigmentation of the oral mucosa / gingivae
abnormal pigmentation of the oral mucosa / gingiva

name: coarse metaphyseal trabecularization
coarse metaphyseal trabecularization
HP:0100670.def: Coarse appearance of the components of the network of osseous tissue that makes up the cancellous structure of a bone, i.e., thickening of the (usually fine) white lines that are produced by trabeculae in radiograms.

name: abnormal trabecular bone morphology
abnormal trabecular bone morphology
HP:0100671.def: Abnormal structure or form of trabecular bone.

name: vaginal hernia
vaginal hernia
HP:0100672.def: The presence of a hernia of the vagina.

name: vaginal hydrocele
vaginal hydrocele
HP:0100673.def: A type of hydrocele testis in which the processus vaginalis remains patent only around the testes, and, as fluid accumulates, it renders the testes impalpable.

name: vulval varicose vein
vulval varicose vein
HP:0100677.def: Varicosity of veins in the vulval region.

name: premature skin wrinkling
premature skin wrinkling
HP:0100678.def: The presence of an increased degree of wrinkling (irregular folds and indentations) of the skin as compared with age-related norms.

name: esophageal duplication
esophageal duplication
HP:0100681.def: A developmental disorder in which there is a duplication of a portion of the muscle and submucosa of the esophagus without epithelial duplication.

name: tracheal atresia
tracheal atresia
HP:0100682.def: A congenital absence or considerable underdevelopment of the trachea such that communication between the larynx proximally and the alveoli of the lungs distally is lacking.

name: salivary gland neoplasm
salivary gland neoplasm
HP:0100684.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of a salivary gland.

name: abnormal sharpey fiber morphology
abnormal sharpey fiber morphology
HP:0100685.def: An abnormality of Sharpey's fibers (bone fibers, or perforating fibers), which are a matrix of connective tissue consisting of bundles of strong collagenous fibres connecting periosteum to bone.

name: polyotia
polyotia
HP:0100687.def: The presence of an extra auricle on one or both sides of the head.

name: decreased corneal thickness
decrease corneal thickness
HP:0100689.def: A decreased anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.

name: abnormality of the curvature of the cornea
abnormality of the curvature of the cornea
increased corneal curvature
increase corneal curvature
HP:0100692.def: An increase in the degree of curvature of the cornea compared to normal.

name: iridodonesis
iridodonesis
HP:0100693.def: Tremulousness of the iris on movement of the eye, occurring in subluxation of the lens.

name: tibial torsion
tibial torsion
HP:0100694.def: Twisted position of the tibia (shin bone) associated with pathological rotation of the leg.

name: lipedema
lipedema
HP:0100695.def: Excess deposit and expansion of adipose tissue in an unusual pattern which cannot be lost through diet and exercise .

name: neurofibrosarcoma
neurofibrosarcoma
HP:0100697.def: A form of malignant cancer of the connective tissue surrounding nerves. Given its origin and behavior, it is classified as a sarcoma.

name: subcutaneous neurofibroma
subcutaneous neurofibroma
HP:0100698.def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the subcutis (subcutaneous region).

name: scarring
scar
HP:0100699.def: A scar refers to a lesion in which wound, burn, or sore has not healed completely and fibrous connective tissue has developed.

name: abnormal arachnoid mater morphology
abnormal arachnoid mater morphology
HP:0100700.def: An abnormality of the Arachnoid mater.

name: abnormal pia mater
abnormal pia mater
HP:0100701.def: An abnormality of the pia mater.

name: arachnoid cyst
arachnoid cyst
HP:0100702.def: An extra-parenchymal and intra-arachnoidal collection of fluid with a composition similar to that of cerebrospinal fluid.
synonym: fluid - filled sac located in membrane surrounding brain or spinal cord
fluid - fill sac locate in membrane surround brain or spinal cord

name: tongue thrusting
tongue thrusting
HP:0100703.def: Pressing forward of the tongue in the mouth, a retained motoric habit from infantile swallowing patterns

name: cerebral visual impairment
cerebral visual impairment
HP:0100704.def: A form of loss of vision caused by damage to the visual cortex rather than a defect in the eye.

name: abnormal glial cell morphology
abnormal glial cell morphology
HP:0100705.def: An abnormality of the glia cell.

name: abnormal oligodendroglia morphology
abnormal oligodendroglia morphology
HP:0100706.def: One of the three types of glia cells that, with the nerve cells, compose the central nervous system and are characterized by sheetlike processes that wrap around individual axons to form the myelin sheath of nerve fibers.

name: abnormal microglia morphology
abnormal microglia morphology
HP:0100708.def: An abnormality of the microglial cells. They are also known as brain-resident macrophages or Hortega cells.

name: impulsivity
impulsivity
HP:0100710.def: Acting on the spur of the moment in response to immediate stimuli; acting on a momentary basis without a plan or consideration of outcomes; having difficulty establishing or following plans; experiencing a sense of urgency and engaging in self-harming behavior when under emotional distress.

name: abnormal thoracic spine morphology
abnormal thoracic spine morphology
HP:0100711.def: An abnormality of the thoracic vertebral column.

name: abnormal lumbar spine morphology
abnormal lumbar spine morphology
HP:0100712.def: Any structural abnormality of the lumbar vertebral column.

name: abnormal cementum morphology
abnormal cementum morphology
HP:0100717.def: Any structural anomaly of the cementum, which is the mineralized connective tissue covering the dental root. The cementum allows anchoring of the fibers of the periodontal ligament. Cementum is secreted by cementoblasts, which may be, later on, embedded in the cementum. Cementum can be acellular (along the two third coronal portion of the root) and cellular (in the apical and interradicular part of the root).

name: lens coloboma
lens coloboma
HP:0100719.def: A sectoral indentation of the crystalline lens, usually due to zonular weakness or absence.

name: mediastinal lymphadenopathy
mediastinal lymphadenopathy
HP:0100721.def: Swelling of lymph nodes within the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavities that contains the heart and the great vessels, the esophagus, and trachea and other structures including lymph nodes.
synonym: swollen lymph nodes in center of chest
swollen lymph node in center of chest
swollen lymph nodes in centre of chest
swollen lymph node in centre of chest

name: hypercoagulability
hypercoagulability
HP:0100724.def: An abnormality of coagulation associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

name: lichenification
lichenification
HP:0100725.def: Thickening and hardening of the epidermis seen with exaggeration of normal skin lines.

name: kaposi 's sarcoma
kaposi 's sarcoma
HP:0100726.def: A systemic disease which can present with cutaneous lesions with or without internal involvement. Tumors are caused by Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV8), also known as Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV).

name: histiocytosis
histiocytosis
HP:0100727.def: An excessive number of histiocytes (tissue macrophages).

name: bronchogenic cyst
bronchogenic cyst
HP:0100730.def: A rare congenital cystic lesion of the lungs in the mediastinum.

name: transverse facial cleft
transverse facial cleft
HP:0100731.def: A horizontal cleft of the face, varying from slight widening of the mouth, to a cleft extending to the ear.

name: neoplasm of the parathyroid gland
neoplasm of the parathyroid gland
HP:0100733.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the parathyroid gland.

name: abnormal vertebral epiphysis morphology
abnormal vertebral epiphysis morphology
HP:0100734.def: An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of one or more vertebrae.
synonym: abnormal shape of the end part of the vertebra bone
abnormal shape of the end part of the vertebra bone

name: abnormal soft palate morphology
abnormal soft palate morphology
HP:0100736.def: An abnormality of the soft palate.

name: abnormal eating behavior
abnormal eat behavior
HP:0100738.def: Abnormal eating habits involve excessive or insufficient consumption of food, or any other abnormal pattern of food consumption.

name: bulimia
bulimia
HP:0100739.def: A form of anomalous eating behavior characterized by binge eating is followed by self-induced vomiting or other compensatory behavior intended to prevent weight gain (purging, fasting or exercising or a combination of these).

name: vascular neoplasm
vascular neoplasm
HP:0100742.def: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) originating in the vascular system.

name: abnormality of the humeroulnar joint
abnormality of the humeroulnar joint
HP:0100745.def: An anomaly of the joint between the trochlear notch of ulna and the trochlea of humerus, which is part of the elbow joint.

name: macrodactyly of finger
macrodactyly of finger
HP:0100746.def: A type of Macrodactyly affecting one or several fingers.

name: macrodactyly of toe
macrodactyly of toe
HP:0100747.def: A type of Macrodactyly affecting one or several toes.

name: chest pain
chest pain
HP:0100749.def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the chest.

name: atelectasis
atelectasis
HP:0100750.def: Collapse of part of a lung associated with absence of inflation (air) of that part.
synonym: partial or complete collapse of part or entire lung
partial or complete collapse of part or entire lung

name: esophageal neoplasm
esophageal neoplasm
HP:0100751.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the esophagus.

name: abnormal liver lobulation
abnormal liver lobulation
HP:0100752.def: Formation of abnormal lobules (small masses of tissue) in the liver.

name: schizophrenia
schizophrenia
HP:0100753.def: A mental disorder characterized by a disintegration of thought processes and emotional responsiveness. It most commonly manifests as auditory hallucinations, paranoid or bizarre delusions, or disorganized speech and thinking. It is accompanied by significant social or occupational dysfunction. The onset of symptoms typically occurs in young adulthood, with a global lifetime prevalence of about 1%. This term is not a helpful parent term to describe abnormal experiences.

name: mania
mania
HP:0100754.def: A state of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.

name: pancreatoblastoma
pancreatoblastoma
HP:0100757.def: A rare pediatric carcinoma of the pancreas.

name: gangrene
gangrene
HP:0100758.def: A serious and potentially life-threatening condition that arises when a considerable mass of body tissue dies (necrosis).
synonym: death of body tissue due to lack of blood flow or infection
death of body tissue due to lack of blood flow or infection

name: clubbing of fingers
clubbing of finger
HP:0100759.def: Terminal broadening of the fingers (distal phalanges of the fingers).

name: clubbing of toes
clubbing of toe
HP:0100760.def: Terminal broadening of the toes (distal phalanges of the toes).

name: abnormality of the lymphatic system
abnormality of the lymphatic system
HP:0100763.def: An anomaly of the lymphatic system, a network of lymphatic vessels that carry a clear fluid called lymph unidirectionally towards either the right lymphatic duct or the thoracic duct, which in turn drain into the right and left subclavian veins respectively.

name: lymphangioma
lymphangioma
HP:0100764.def: Lymphangiomas are rare congenital malformations consisting of focal proliferations of well-differentiated lymphatic tissue in multi cystic or sponge like structures. Lymphangioma is usually asymptomatic due to its soft consistency but compression of adjacent structures can be seen due to the mass effect of a large tumor.

name: abnormal lymphatic vessel morphology
abnormal lymphatic vessel morphology
HP:0100766.def: A structural anomaly of the vessel that contains or conveys lymph fluid.

name: abnormal placenta morphology
abnormal placenta morphology
HP:0100767.def: An abnormality of the placenta, the organ that connects the developing fetus to the uterine wall to enable nutrient uptake, waste elimination, and gas exchange.

name: choriocarcinoma
choriocarcinoma
HP:0100768.def: A malignant, trophoblastic and aggressive cancer, usually of the placenta. It is characterized by early hematogenous spread to the lungs and belongs to the far end of the spectrum of gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD), a subset of germ cell tumors.

name: hyperperistalsis
hyperperistalsis
HP:0100770.def: Excessively active peristalsis (wave of contraction of the tubular organs of the gastrointestinal tract) marked by excessive rapidity of the passage of food through the stomach and intestine.

name: hypoperistalsis
hypoperistalsis
HP:0100771.def: Reduced or inadequate peristalsis, with resultant slow passage of contents through the digestive tract.

name: hyperostosis
hyperostosis
HP:0100774.def: Excessive growth or abnormal thickening of bone tissue.

name: dural ectasia
dural ectasia
HP:0100775.def: A widening or ballooning of the dural sac surrounding the spinal cord usually at the lumbosacral level.

name: recurrent pharyngitis
recurrent pharyngitis
HP:0100776.def: An increased susceptibility to pharyngitis as manifested by a history of recurrent pharyngitis.

name: exostoses
exostosis
HP:0100777.def: An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage, and arises from a bone that develops from cartilage.
synonym: formation of new noncancerous bone on top of existing bone
formation of new noncancerous bone on top of exist bone

name: cryoglobulinemia
cryoglobulinemia
HP:0100778.def: Increased level of cryoglobulins in the blood. Cryoglobulins are abnormal immunoglobulins, especially IGG or IGM, that precipitate spontaneously when serum is cooled below 37 degrees Celsius.

name: urogenital sinus anomaly
urogenital sinus anomaly
HP:0100779.def: A rare birth defect in women where the urethra and vagina both open into a common channel.

name: conjunctival hamartoma
conjunctival hamartoma
HP:0100780.def: A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) of the conjunctiva.

name: abnormal sacroiliac joint morphology
abnormal sacroiliac joint morphology
HP:0100781.def: An anomaly of the sacroiliac joint, which connects the base of the spine (sacrum) to the ilium (a hip bone).

name: breast aplasia
breast aplasia
HP:0100783.def: Failure to develop and congenital absence of the breast.

name: insomnia
insomnia
HP:0100785.def: Persistent difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep.

name: hypersomnia
hypersomnia
HP:0100786.def: Excessive sleepiness or feeling of sleepiness, or difficulty staying awake despite having had adequate sleep, which persists over several days.

name: fused lips
fuse lip
HP:0100788.def: Lack of separation of the upper and lower lips.
synonym: adhesion of upper and lower lips
adhesion of upper and low lip
fusion of upper and lower lips
fusion of upper and low lip

name: torus palatinus
torus palatinus
HP:0100789.def: A bony protrusion present on the midline of the hard palate.

name: acantholysis
acantholysis
HP:0100792.def: The loss of intercellular connections, such as desmosomes, resulting in loss of cohesion between keratinocytes.

name: abnormally straight spine
abnormally straight spine
HP:0100795.def: The absence of the normal curvature of the vertebral column.

name: toenail dysplasia
toenail dysplasia
HP:0100797.def: An abnormality of the development of the toenails.

name: fingernail dysplasia
fingernail dysplasia
HP:0100798.def: An abnormality of the development of the fingernails.

name: neoplasm of the middle ear
neoplasm of the middle ear
HP:0100799.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the middle ear.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the pancreas
aplasia / hypoplasia of the pancreas
HP:0100800.def: A congenital underdevelopment (aplasia or hypoplasia) of the pancreas.

name: malposition of the stomach
malposition of the stomach
HP:0100802.def: Abnormal anatomical location of the stomach. This feature may be due to intestinal malrotation.

name: abnormality of the periungual region
abnormality of the periungual region
HP:0100803.def: An abnormality of the region around the nails of the fingers or toes.

name: ungual fibroma
ungual fibroma
HP:0100804.def: Flesh-colored papule in or around the nail bed. Ungual fibromas may be periungual (arising under the proximal nail fold) or subungual (originating under the nail plate).

name: long fingers
long finger
HP:0100807.def: The middle finger is more than 2 SD above the mean for newborns 27 to 41 weeks EGA or above the 97th centile for children from birth to 16 years of age AND the five digits retain their normal length proportions relative to each other (i.e., it is not the case that the middle finger is the only lengthened digit), or, Fingers that appear disproportionately long compared to the palm of the hand.

name: gastric diverticulum
gastric diverticulum
HP:0100808.def: An outpouching of the gastric wall.

name: scalp tenderness
scalp tenderness
HP:0100809.def: Pain or discomfort of the scalp elicited by palpation.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the colon
aplasia / hypoplasia of the colon
HP:0100811.def: Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the colon.

name: halitosis
halitosis
HP:0100812.def: Noticeably unpleasant odors exhaled in breathing.

name: testicular torsion
testicular torsion
HP:0100813.def: Testicular torsion is when the spermatic cord to a testicle twists, cutting off the blood supply. The most common symptom is acute testicular pain.

name: lip hyperpigmentation
lip hyperpigmentation
synonym: darkening of skin of the lips
darkening of skin of the lip

name: renovascular hypertension
renovascular hypertension
HP:0100817.def: The presence of hypertension related to stenosis of the renal artery.
synonym: hypertension due to renal artery hyperplasia
hypertension due to renal artery hyperplasia

name: long thorax
long thorax
HP:0100818.def: Increased inferior to superior extent of the thorax.

name: intestinal fistula
intestinal fistula
HP:0100819.def: An abnormal connection between the gut and another hollow organ, such as the bladder, urethra, vagina, or other regions of the gastrointestinal tract.

name: glomerulopathy
glomerulopathy
HP:0100820.def: Inflammatory or noninflammatory diseases affecting the glomeruli of the nephron.

name: urethrocele
urethrocele
HP:0100821.def: The prolapse of the female urethra into the vagina.

name: rectocele
rectocele
HP:0100822.def: A Rectocele results from a tear in the rectovaginal septum (which is normally a tough, fibrous, sheet-like divider between the rectum and vagina). Rectal tissue bulges through this tear and into the vagina as a hernia. There are two main causes of this tear: childbirth, and hysterectomy.

name: neoplasm of the nail
neoplasm of the nail
HP:0100826.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the nail.

name: lymphocytosis
lymphocytosis
HP:0100827.def: Increase in the number or proportion of lymphocytes in the blood.

name: increased t cell count
increase t cell count
HP:0100828.def: An abnormal increase in the total number of T cells detected in the blood.

name: galactorrhea
galactorrhea
HP:0100829.def: Spontaneous flow of milk from the breast, unassociated with childbirth or nursing.

name: abnormality of vitamin k metabolism
abnormality of vitamin k metabolism
HP:0100831.def: Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin with a role in promoting the coagulation cascade.

name: vitreous floaters
vitreous floater
HP:0100832.def: Deposits of various size, shape, consistency, refractive index, and motility within the eye's vitreous humour, which is normally transparent.

name: neoplasm of the small intestine
neoplasm of the small intestine
HP:0100833.def: The presence of a neoplasm of the small intestine.

name: neoplasm of the large intestine
neoplasm of the large intestine
HP:0100834.def: The presence of a neoplasm of the large intestine.

name: benign neoplasm of the central nervous system
benign neoplasm of the central nervous system
malignant neoplasm of the central nervous system
malignant neoplasm of the central nervous system
HP:0100836.def: A tumor that originates in the pineal gland, has moderate cellularity and tends to form rosette patterns.

name: atrophodermia vermiculata
atrophodermia vermiculata
HP:0100837.def: Symmetrical vermiform facial atrophy that affects mainly the forehead, the chin, the ear lobes and helices. Atrophodermia vermiculata is characterized by erythema and follicular plugs on the cheeks, developing into painless reticular impressions.

name: recurrent cutaneous abscess formation
recurrent cutaneous abscess formation
HP:0100838.def: An increased susceptibility to cutaneous abscess formation, as manifested by a medical history of recurrent cutaneous abscesses.

name: hepatic agenesis
hepatic agenesis
HP:0100839.def: Absence of the liver owing to a failure of the liver to develop.

name: aplasia / hypoplasia of the eyebrow
aplasia / hypoplasia of the eyebrow
HP:0100840.def: Absence or underdevelopment of the eyebrow.

name: microgastria
microgastria
HP:0100841.def: A developmental anomaly wtih a small tubular or saccular midline stomach.

name: septo - optic dysplasia
septo - optic dysplasia
HP:0100842.def: Underdevelopment of the optic nerve and absence of the septum pellucidum.

name: anaphylactic shock
anaphylactic shock
HP:0100845.def: An acute hypersensitivity reaction due to exposure to a previously encountered antigen.

name: palmoplantar pustulosis
palmoplantar pustulosis
HP:0100847.def: A chronic, relapsing, pustular eruption that is localized to the palms and soles.

name: neoplasm of the male external genitalia
neoplasm of the male external genitalia
HP:0100848.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the male external genitalia.
synonym: neoplasia of the male external genitalia
neoplasia of the male external genitalia

name: neoplasm of the scrotum
neoplasm of the scrotum
HP:0100849.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the scrotum.

name: neoplasm of the penis
neoplasm of the penis
HP:0100850.def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the penis.

name: abnormal emotion
abnormal emotion
HP:0100851.def: Abnormalities in the intensity, frequency, or duration of emotional experiences.

name: abnormal fear - induced behavior
abnormal fear - induced behavior
HP:0100852.def: An abnormal fear-induced behavior includes observable actions. This behavior is characterized by abnormal responses to fear or abnormal fear levels. Examples of such behavior include avoiding fear-inducing situations.

name: hypoplastic areola
hypoplastic areola
HP:0100853.def: Underdevelopment of the areola, the circular area of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple.

name: poorly ossified vertebrae
poorly ossify vertebra
HP:0100856.def: Decreased ossification of the vertebral bodies.

name: dilatation of celiac artery
dilatation of celiac artery
HP:0100858.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the celiac artery.

name: dilatation of superior mesenteric artery
dilatation of superior mesenteric artery
HP:0100859.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the superior mesenteric artery .

name: dilatation of inferior mesenteric artery
dilatation of inferior mesenteric artery
HP:0100860.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the inferior mesenteric artery .

name: sclerotic vertebral body
sclerotic vertebral body
HP:0100861.def: Increase in bone density of the vertebral body.

name: short femoral neck
short femoral neck
HP:0100864.def: An abnormally short femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

name: broad ischia
broad ischia
HP:0100865.def: Increased width of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.

name: duodenal stenosis
duodenal stenosis
HP:0100867.def: The narrowing or partial blockage of a portion of the duodenum.

name: palmar telangiectasia
palmar telangiectasia
HP:0100869.def: The presence of telangiectases on the skin of palm of hand.

name: plantar telangiectasia
plantar telangiectasia
HP:0100870.def: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located on the skin of sole of foot.

name: abnormal palm morphology
abnormal palm morphology
HP:0100871.def: An abnormality of the palm, that is, of the front of the hand.

name: abnormality of the plantar skin of foot
abnormality of the plantar skin of foot
HP:0100872.def: An abnormality of the plantar part of foot, that is of the soles of the feet.

name: thick hair
thick hair
HP:0100874.def: Increased density of hairs, i.e., and elevated number of hairs per unit area.

name: hemimacroglossia
hemimacroglossia
HP:0100875.def: Increased length and width of one half of the tounge.
synonym: hyperplasia of half of the tongue
hyperplasia of half of the tongue
hypertrophy of half of the tongue
hypertrophy of half of the tongue
increased size of half of the tongue
increase size of half of the tongue

name: infra - orbital crease
infra - orbital crease
HP:0100876.def: Skin crease extending from below the inner canthus laterally along the malar process of the maxilla and zygoma.
synonym: crease in skin under the eye
crease in skin under the eye

HP:0500005.def: Pain in and around the anus or rectum (perianal region).

name: iris flocculi
iris flocculi
HP:0500007.def: Multiple cysts along the pupillary margin that appear as spherical or tear-drop-shaped pigmented lesions or wrinkled masses emerging from the pupillary border of the iris.

name: cornea verticillata
cornea verticillata
HP:0500008.def: Golden brown or gray deposits with a clockwise, whorl-like distribution in the inferior interpalpebal portion of the cornea.

name: dysplastic gangliocytoma of the cerebellum
dysplastic gangliocytoma of the cerebellum
HP:0500009.def: It is a rare, slowly growing tumor of the cerebellum, a gangliocytoma sometimes considered to be a hamartoma, characterized by diffuse hypertrophy of the granular layer of the cerebellum.

name: moon facies
moon facies
HP:0500011.def: A rounded, puffy face with fat deposits in the temporal fossa and cheeks, a double chin.

name: abnormal gonadotropin - releasing hormone concentration
abnormal gonadotropin - release hormone concentration
HP:0500012.def: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of the normal gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). Intermittent GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus acts upon its receptor in the anterior pituitary to regulate the production and release of the gonadotropins, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).
synonym: abnormality of gonadotropin - releasing hormone level
abnormality of gonadotropin - release hormone level

name: lack of gonadotropin - releasing hormone pulsatility
lack of gonadotropin - release hormone pulsatility
HP:0500013.def: Secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone that does not occur in a pulsatile fashion.

name: abnormal cardiac test
abnormal cardiac test
HP:0500015.def: Abnormal test result of cardiovascular physiology.

name: abnormal cardiac mri
abnormal cardiac mri
HP:0500016.def: Abnormal results of a MRI for the heart.

name: abnormal cardiac catheterization
abnormal cardiac catheterization
HP:0500017.def: Abnormal results from the diagnostic tests resulting from cardiac catheterization.

name: abnormal cardiac exercise stress test
abnormal cardiac exercise stress test
HP:0500018.def: Abnormal results of exercise on heart function.

name: abnormal resting energy expenditure from metabolic cart test
abnormal rest energy expenditure from metabolic cart test
HP:0500019.def: Resting energy expenditure (REE) can be measured with indirect calorimetry using a metabolic cart, which is used to measure the oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2).

name: abnormal cardiac biomarker test
abnormal cardiac biomarker test
HP:0500020.def: Abnormal blood test results measuring creatine kinase (CK), CK-MB, troponin (TROPI), myoglobin, and/or cardiac enzymes.

name: reduced brain gamma - aminobutyric acid level by mrs
reduce brain gamma - aminobutyric acid level by mr
HP:0500021.def: An decreased level of gamma-aminobutyric acid in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

name: abnormal circulating dehydroepiandrosterone concentration
abnormal circulate dehydroepiandrosterone concentration
HP:0500022.def: A deviation from the normal concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone in the circulation.

name: aplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
aplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
HP:0500024.def: Absence of the musculature of the pelvis.

name: hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
HP:0500026.def: Underdevelopment of the musculature of the pelvis.

name: cotton wool plaques
cotton wool plaque
HP:0500028.def: Deposition of large, diffuse cotton wool amyloid plaques (CWPs) lacking a dense core and associated neuritic changes.

name: abnormal hepatic glycogen storage
abnormal hepatic glycogen storage
HP:0500030.def: Change in normal glycogen storage content.

name: sclerosis of the carpal bones
sclerosis of the carpal bone
HP:0500031.def: An elevation in bone density in one or more carpal bones of the hand.

name: abnormal neuron branching
abnormal neuron branching
HP:0500032.def: Abnormality of the structure and branching of the dendrites of a neuron.

name: abnormal natural killer subset distribution
abnormal natural killer subset distribution
HP:0500033.def: Any abnormality in the proportion natural killer subsets relative to the total number of natural killer cells.

name: nasolacrimal sac granuloma
nasolacrimal sac granuloma
HP:0500035.def: A mass of granulation tissue in response to chronic dacryocystitis as polypoid formations or they follow accidental injury, from probing and as a reaction to retained foreign bodies in the sac.

name: nasolacrimal sac papilloma
nasolacrimal sac papilloma
HP:0500036.def: Benign tumor of the nasolacrimal sac.

name: nasolacrimal sac epithelial papillary carcinoma
nasolacrimal sac epithelial papillary carcinoma
HP:0500037.def: The malignant epithelial neoplasm with papillary growths in the nasolacrimal sac.

name: conjunctival cicatrization
conjunctival cicatrization
HP:0500039.def: An abnormality of the conjuctiva and ocular surface caused by conjunctival inflammation and associated with scarring.

name: dermolipoma of the conjunctiva
dermolipoma of the conjunctiva
HP:0500040.def: A benign tumor composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue usually located near the temporal fornix.

name: myopic astigmatism
myopic astigmatism
HP:0500041.def: A condition where one or both of the two principal meridians focus in the front of the retina when the eye is at rest.

name: latent hypermetropia
latent hypermetropia
HP:0500042.def: A term to describe when farsightedness is masked when the accommodative muscles are used to increase the focusing power of the eye.

name: eyelid retraction
eyelid retraction
HP:0500043.def: With the eyes in primary position, the sclera is visible above the superior corneal limbus.

name: upper eyelid retraction
upper eyelid retraction
HP:0500044.def: An elevation of the eyelid above the normal level in the primary position.

name: collier 's sign
collier 's sign
HP:0500045.def: A unilateral or bilateral eyelid retraction due to midbrain lesions.

name: seborrhoeic blepharitis
seborrhoeic blepharitis
HP:0500046.def: Inflammation of the eyelid due to overactivity of the sebaceous gland.

name: nasolacrimal sac lymphoma
nasolacrimal sac lymphoma
HP:0500047.def: A type of lymphoma that involves the nasolacrimal sac.

name: delayed canalization of nasolacrimal duct
delay canalization of nasolacrimal duct
HP:0500048.def: A very common condition in which the extreme end of the nasolacrimal duct underneath the inferior turbinate fails to complete its canalization in the newborn period.

name: retinopathy of prematurity
retinopathy of prematurity
HP:0500049.def: An avascular or abnormally vascularized retina that occurs in premature infants and can lead to blindness.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 1
retinopathy of prematurity stage 1
HP:0500050.def: The retinal vessels stop and then a linear flat white line is present that usually runs the circumference of the vascular retina.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 2
retinopathy of prematurity stage 2
HP:0500051.def: The accumulating neovascularization thickens and manifests as a linear bump. The neovascularization remains along the surface of the retina and does not extend off the retina into the cortical vitreous.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 3
retinopathy of prematurity stage 3
HP:0500052.def: The neovascularization accumulates at the edge of the vascularized retina and extends into the vitreous (also called extra retinal fibrosis proliferation). In cases of Zone 2 and Zone 3, this may be sausage shaped. In more posterior Zone 1 disease, the stage 3 can appear as a direct extension of the normal retinal vessels but extending tangentially over the avascular retina.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 4
retinopathy of prematurity stage 4
HP:0500053.def: Scar tissue that forms a continuous sheet coming up from the edge of the vascularized retina. This scar tissue can grow toward the vitreous base/posterior lens capsule resulting in traction, distortion, and even detachment.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 4a
retinopathy of prematurity stage 4a
HP:0500054.def: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that does not extend into the macula.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 4b
retinopathy of prematurity stage 4b
HP:0500055.def: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that involves the macula itself. The detachment usually starts in the temporal periphery although can also involve the nasal retina as well.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 5
retinopathy of prematurity stage 5
HP:0500056.def: Funnel detachment from the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 5a
retinopathy of prematurity stage 5a
HP:0500057.def: An open funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

name: retinopathy of prematurity stage 5b
retinopathy of prematurity stage 5b
HP:0500058.def: A closed funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

name: retinopathy of prematurity zone i
retinopathy of prematurity zone i
HP:0500059.def: Retinopathy which extends from the center of the optic disc to twice the distance from the center of the optic disc to the center of the macula.

name: retinopathy of prematurity zone ii
retinopathy of prematurity zone ii
HP:0500060.def: Retinopathy which extends centrifugally from the edge of zone I to the nasal ora serrata.

name: retinopathy of prematurity zone iii
retinopathy of prematurity zone iii
HP:0500061.def: Retinopathy which is a residual crescent of retina anterior to zone II.

name: retinopathy of prematurity plus
retinopathy of prematurity plus
HP:0500062.def: Venous dilatation and arteriolar tortuosity of the posterior retinal vessels and may later increase in severity to include iris vascular engorgement, poor pupillary dilatation (rigid pupil), and vitreous haze. This definition has been further refined in the later clinical trials in which the diagnosis of plus disease could be made if sufficient vascular dilatation and tortuosity are present in at least 2 quadrants of the eye.

name: retinopathy of prematurity pre - plus
retinopathy of prematurity pre - plus
HP:0500063.def: As vascular abnormalities of the posterior pole that are insufficient for the diagnosis of plus disease but that demonstrate more arterial tortuosity and more venous dilatation than normal.

name: retinopathy of prematurity threshold
retinopathy of prematurity threshold
HP:0500064.def: A retinopathy with a 50% likelihood of progressing to retinal detachment. Threshold disease is considered to be present when stage 3 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is present in either zone I or zone II, with at least 5 continuous or 8 total clock hours of disease, and the presence of plus disease.

name: retinopathy of prematurity prethreshold
retinopathy of prematurity prethreshold
HP:0500065.def: High risk patients who were in Zone 1 (no Plus or stage 3) or Zone 2 with Plus or stage 3 but not both.

name: latent myopia
latent myopia
HP:0500066.def: The difference between total and manifest myopia.

name: paralytic ectropion
paralytic ectropion
HP:0500069.def: A type of ectropion associated with orbicularis muscle weakness caused by cranial nerve VII palsy.

name: conjunctival dermolipoma
conjunctival dermolipoma
HP:0500070.def: A conjuctival lesion composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue. Such choristomas of dermal elements are normally found at the outer canthus, and have a gelatinous appearance. Classically, there is an indistinct posterior border (with the lesion frequently extending into the orbit) and a well-demarcated anterior border several millimetres posterior to the limbus.

name: absolute eccentric fixation
absolute eccentric fixation
HP:0500072.def: Eccentric fixation in which the angle of eccentricity equals the objective angle of deviation.

name: abnormal ocular alignment
abnormal ocular alignment
HP:0500073.def: Any deviation from the normal ocular alignment.

name: dissociated vertical deviation
dissociated vertical deviation
HP:0500074.def: An incomitant tendency for an occluded eye to elevate and extort which resolves on uncovering.

name: dissociated horizontal deviation
dissociate horizontal deviation
HP:0500075.def: A change in horizontal ocular alignment, unrelated to accommodation, that is brought about solely by a change in the balance of visual input from the two eyes.

name: alternating hypertropia
alternate hypertropia
HP:0500076.def: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated upwards.

name: alternating hyperphoria
alternate hyperphoria
HP:0500077.def: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates upwards.

name: alternating hypotropia
alternate hypotropia
HP:0500078.def: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated downwards.

name: alternating hypophoria
alternate hypophoria
HP:0500079.def: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards.

name: pseudophakia
pseudophakia
HP:0500081.def: The term pseudophakia refers to having an artificial lens implanted after the natural eye lens has been removed. During cataract surgery the natural cloudy lens is replaced by an pseudophakia intraocular lens (IOL).

name: optic nerve gray crescent
optic nerve gray crescent
HP:0500086.def: Having a characteristic appearance of a slate gray area of pigmentation within the disc margins that commonly appears along the inferotemporal or temporal neuroretinal rim areas.

name: peripapillary atrophy
peripapillary atrophy
HP:0500087.def: Thinning in the layers of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium around the optic nerve.

name: foveal depigmentation
foveal depigmentation
HP:0500088.def: Loss of pigment in the fovea centralis.

name: optic nerve sheath meningioma
optic nerve sheath meningioma
HP:0500089.def: A benign tumor of meningothelial cells of the meninges that usually occurs in middle age. It is typically unilateral and there is an association with neurofibromatosis type 2.

name: periocular capillary hemangioma
periocular capillary hemangioma
HP:0500090.def: A capillary hemangioma surrounding the eyeball but within the orbit.

name: lymphangioma of the orbit
lymphangioma of the orbit
HP:0500091.def: A hamartoma of lymph vessels that usually presents in childhood. It tends to increase in size with head-down posture and with the Valsalva manoeuvre. Superficial lesions are visible as transilluminable cystic spaces of the lid or conjunctiva that may also contain blood. Deep lesions may cause gradual proptosis or present acutely with orbital pain and reduced vision due to haemorrhage.

name: orbital rhabdomyosarcoma
orbital rhabdomyosarcoma
HP:0500092.def: A mesenchymal tumor that is considered to be the commonest primary orbital malignancy in children. Histologically, it may be differentiated into embryonal, alveolar, and pleomorphic types. It is usually intraconal or within the superior orbit.

name: food allergy
food allergy
HP:0500093.def: Primary food allergies primarily occur as a result (most likely) of gastrointestinal sensitization to predominantly stable food allergens (glycoproteins). A secondary food allergy develops after primary sensitization to airborne allergens (e. g., pollen allergens) with subsequent reactions (due to cross-reactivity) to structurally related often labile allergens in (plant) foods.

name: latex allergy
latex allergy
HP:0500094.def: Latex allergy is an IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity response to natural rubber latex (NRL) protein with a variety of clinical signs ranging from contact urticaria, angioedema, asthma, and anaphylaxis.

name: food - induced anaphylaxis
food - induced anaphylaxis
HP:0500095.def: Food-induced anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially fatal, systemic allergic reaction that occurs suddenly after contact with an allergy-causing food.

name: venom - induced anaphylaxis
venom - induced anaphylaxis
HP:0500096.def: A form of anaphylaxis that is triggered by exposure to venom.

name: meconium xenobiotic
meconium xenobiotic
HP:0500098.def: Presence of a xenobiotic in meconium.

name: plasma / serum xenobiotic
plasma / serum xenobiotic
HP:0500100.def: Presence of a xenobiotic in plasma and/or serum.

name: gastric fluid xenobiotic
gastric fluid xenobiotic
HP:0500101.def: Presence of a xenobiotic in gastric fluid.

name: decreased diastolic blood pressure
decrease diastolic blood pressure
HP:0500104.def: Abnormal decrease in diastolic blood pressure.

name: decreased systolic blood pressure
decrease systolic blood pressure
HP:0500105.def: Abnormal decrease in systolic blood pressure.

name: isolated systolic hypertension
isolate systolic hypertension
HP:0500106.def: Elevated systolic blood pressure without an elevated blood pressure.

name: isolated diastolic hypotension
isolate diastolic hypotension
HP:0500107.def: A decrease in diastolic blood pressure (<60 mmHg) without a decrease in systolic blood pressure (> or = to 100 mmHg).

name: positive urine cocaine test
positive urine cocaine test
HP:0500108.def: Detection of cocaine or its major metabolite, benzoylecgonine, in urine.

name: positive urine barbiturate test
positive urine barbiturate test
HP:0500109.def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in urine.

name: positive urine cannabinoid test
positive urine cannabinoid test
HP:0500110.def: Detection of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or other cannabinoid metabolites in urine.

name: positive urine benzodiazepines test
positive urine benzodiazepine test
HP:0500111.def: Detection of benzodiazepine metabolites, primarily nordiazepam, oxazepam, and temazepam, in urine.

name: positive urine amphetamine test
positive urine amphetamine test
HP:0500112.def: Detection of amphetamine or its metabolites in urine.

name: positive urine opioid test
positive urine opioid test
HP:0500113.def: Detection of opioids or opioid metabolites in urine.

name: abnormal stool urobilinogen concentration
abnormal stool urobilinogen concentration
HP:0500114.def: Abnormal concentration of urobilinogen present in the stool.

name: increased stool urobilinogen concentration
increase stool urobilinogen concentration
HP:0500115.def: An increased amount of urobilinogen present in the stool.

name: positive blood barbiturate test
positive blood barbiturate test
HP:0500116.def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in blood.

name: abnormal csf urate concentration
abnormal csf urate concentration
HP:0500117.def: Abnormal concentration of urate in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

name: hypovalinemia
hypovalinemia
HP:0500132.def: A decreased amount of valine in the blood.

name: hypotyrosinemia
hypotyrosinemia
HP:0500133.def: An decreased concentration of tyrosine in the blood.

name: hypertryptophanemia
hypertryptophanemia
HP:0500134.def: An increased amount of tryptophan in the blood.

name: hypotryptophanemia
hypotryptophanemia
HP:0500135.def: A decreased amount of tryptophan in the blood.

name: hypothreoninemia
hypothreoninemia
HP:0500136.def: A decreased amount of threonine in the blood.

name: hyperserinemia
hyperserinemia
HP:0500138.def: An increased amount of serine in the blood.

name: hypoprolinemia
hypoprolinemia
HP:0500139.def: A decreased amount of proline in the blood.

name: decreased circulating hydroxyproline concentration
decrease circulate hydroxyproline concentration
HP:0500140.def: A decreased amount of hydroxyproline in the blood.
synonym: low level of hydroxyproline in the blood
low level of hydroxyproline in the blood

name: hypophenylalaninemia
hypophenylalaninemia
HP:0500141.def: A decreased amount of phenylalanine in the blood.

name: hypolysinemia
hypolysinemia
HP:0500142.def: A decreased amount of lysine in the blood.

name: hypoleucinemia
hypoleucinemia
HP:0500143.def: Decreased amount of leucine in the blood.

name: hypoisoleucinemia
hypoisoleucinemia
HP:0500144.def: A decreased amount of isoleucine in the blood.

name: hypohistidinemia
hypohistidinemia
HP:0500145.def: A decreased amount of histidine in the blood.

name: hypoglutaminemia
hypoglutaminemia
HP:0500147.def: Decreased amount of glutamine in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating glutamate concentration
abnormal circulate glutamate concentration
HP:0500148.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glutamate in the blood circulation.

name: hyperglutamatemia
hyperglutamatemia
HP:0500149.def: Concentration of glutamate in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
synonym: increased level of l - glutamic acid in blood
increase level of l - glutamic acid in blood

name: hypoglutamatemia
hypoglutamatemia
HP:0500150.def: A decreased amount of glutamate in the blood.

name: hypercystinemia
hypercystinemia
HP:0500151.def: An increased amount of cystine in the blood.

name: hypocystinemia
hypocystinemia
HP:0500152.def: A decreased amount of cystine in the blood.

name: hyperargininemia
hyperargininemia
HP:0500153.def: An increased amount of arginine levels in the blood.

name: hypoalaninemia
hypoalaninemia
HP:0500154.def: A decreased amount of alanine in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating asparagine concentration
abnormal circulate asparagine concentration
HP:0500155.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of asparagine in the blood circulation.

name: hyperasparaginemia
hyperasparaginemia
HP:0500156.def: An increased amount of asparagine in the blood.

name: hypoasparaginemia
hypoasparaginemia
HP:0500157.def: A decreased amount of asparagine in the blood.

name: abnormal circulating aspartic acid concentration
abnormal circulate aspartic acid concentration
HP:0500158.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of aspartate in the blood circulation.

name: increased circulating aspartic acid concentration
increase circulate aspartic acid concentration
HP:0500159.def: An increased concentration of aspartic acid in the blood circulation.
synonym: increased level of circulating aspartic acid
increase level of circulate aspartic acid

name: abnormal circulating carnosine concentration
abnormal circulate carnosine concentration
HP:0500160.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of carnosine in the blood circulation.

name: increased level of carnosine in blood
increase level of carnosine in blood
HP:0500161.def: An increased amount of carnosine in the blood.

name: decreased level of carnosine in blood
decrease level of carnosine in blood
HP:0500162.def: A decreased amount of carnosine in bood.

name: hypoornithinemia
hypoornithinemia
HP:0500163.def: An abnormal decrease in ornithine in the blood.

name: abnormal blood carbon dioxide level
abnormal blood carbon dioxide level
HP:0500164.def: An abnormality of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the arterial blood.

name: abnormal blood oxygen level
abnormal blood oxygen level
HP:0500165.def: An abnormality of the partial pressure of oxygen in the arterial blood.

name: abnormal circulating gastrin concentration
abnormal circulate gastrin concentration
HP:0500166.def: An abnormal concentration of gastrin in the blood.

name: hypergastrinemia
hypergastrinemia
HP:0500167.def: An elevated amount of gastrin in the blood.

name: abnormal concentration of acylcarnitine in the urine
abnormal concentration of acylcarnitine in the urine
HP:0500170.def: An abnormal amount of acylcarnitine in the urine.

name: reflex asystolic syncope
reflex asystolic syncope
HP:0500173.def: A loss of consciousness followed by stiffening and brief clonic movements affecting some or all limbs, often misinterpreted as an epileptic seizure.

name: abnormal circulating amino sulfonic acid concentration
abnormal circulate amino sulfonic acid concentration
hypertaurinemia
hypertaurinemia
HP:0500181.def: An increased amount of taurine in the blood.
synonym: increased circulating taurine levels in the blood
increase circulate taurine level in the blood

name: hypotaurinemia
hypotaurinemia
HP:0500182.def: A decreased amount of taurine in the blood.
synonym: reduced taurine levels in the blood
reduce taurine level in the blood

name: abnormal csf carboxylic acid concentration
abnormal csf carboxylic acid concentration
HP:0500183.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carboxylic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid.

name: abnormal csf amino acid concentration
abnormal csf amino acid concentration
HP:0500184.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amino acids in the cerebrospinal fluid.
synonym: abnormal amino acid levels in cerebrospinal fluid
abnormal amino acid level in cerebrospinal fluid
abnormal cerebrospinal fluid amino acid level
abnormal cerebrospinal fluid amino acid level

name: abnormal csf branched chain amino acid concentration
abnormal csf branch chain amino acid concentration
HP:0500185.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of branched-chain amino acids in the cerebrospinal fluid.
synonym: abnormal branched - chain amino acid levels in cerbrospinal fluid
abnormal branch - chain amino acid level in cerbrospinal fluid

name: abnormal csf valine concentration
abnormal csf valine concentration
HP:0500186.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of valine in the cerebrospinal fluid.
synonym: abnormal valine levels in cerebrospinal fluid
abnormal valine level in cerebrospinal fluid

increase csf valine concentration
HP:0500187.def: Any increased amount from normal of valine in the cerebrospinal fluid.

abnormal csf leucine concentration
HP:0500189.def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of leucine in the cerebrospinal fluid.
synonym: abnormal leucine levels in cerebrospinal fluid

decrease csf leucine concentration
HP:0500190.def: Abnormally decreased levels of leucine in the cerebrospinal fluid.

HP:0500191.def: Abnormally increased levels of leucine in cerebrospinal fluid.

abnormal csf glutamine family amino acid concentration
