HP:3000061.def: A structural abnormality of an infra-orbital nerve. The infraorbital nerve arises from the maxillary branch of the trigeminal nerve and normally traverses the orbital floor in the infraorbital canal.

name: abnormal internal carotid artery morphology
abnormal internal carotid artery morphology
HP:3000062.def: An abnormality of an internal carotid artery.

name: abnormality of internal jugular vein
abnormality of internal jugular vein
HP:3000063.def: An abnormality of an internal jugular vein.

name: abnormality of intrinsic muscle of tongue
abnormality of intrinsic muscle of tongue
HP:3000064.def: An abnormality of an intrinsic muscle of tongue.

name: abnormal lacrimal artery morphology
abnormal lacrimal artery morphology
HP:3000065.def: An abnormality of a lacrimal artery.

name: abnormal lacrimal sac morphology
abnormal lacrimal sac morphology
HP:3000066.def: An abnormality of a lacrimal sac.

name: abnormal lateral cricoarytenoid muscle morphology
abnormal lateral cricoarytenoid muscle morphology
HP:3000067.def: Any structural abnormality of a lateral crico-arytenoid muscle, which extends from the lateral cricoid cartilage to the muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage, and can adduct the vocal cords, which closes the rima glottidis and thereby protects the airway.

name: abnormality of lateral pterygoid muscle
abnormality of lateral pterygoid muscle
HP:3000068.def: An abnormality of a lateral pterygoid muscle.

name: abnormality of lateral rectus extra - ocular muscle
abnormality of lateral rectus extra - ocular muscle
HP:3000069.def: An abnormality of a lateral rectus extra-ocular muscle.

name: abnormality of levator anguli oris
abnormality of levator anguli oris
HP:3000070.def: An abnormality of a levator anguli oris.

name: abnormality of levator labii superioris
abnormality of levator labii superioris
HP:3000071.def: An abnormality of a levator labii superioris.

name: abnormal levator palpebrae superioris morphology
abnormal levator palpebrae superioris morphology
HP:3000072.def: An abnormality of a levator palpebrae superioris.

name: abnormality of levator veli palatini muscle
abnormality of levator veli palatini muscle
HP:3000073.def: An abnormality of a levator veli palatini.

name: abnormal lingual artery morphology
abnormal lingual artery morphology
HP:3000074.def: Any structural abnormality of a lingual artery.

name: abnormal lingual nerve morphology
abnormal lingual nerve morphology
HP:3000075.def: Any structural anomaly of a lingual nerve.

name: abnormality of lingual tonsil
abnormality of lingual tonsil
HP:3000076.def: An abnormality of a lingual tonsil.

name: abnormal mandible condylar process morphology
abnormal mandible condylar process morphology
HP:3000077.def: An abnormality of a mandible condylar process.

name: abnormal mandible coronoid process morphology
abnormal mandible coronoid process morphology
HP:3000078.def: An abnormality of a mandible coronoid process.

name: abnormal mandibular symphysis morphology
abnormal mandibular symphysis morphology
HP:3000079.def: A structural abnormality of a mandibular symphysis.

name: abnormal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging finding
abnormal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging find
HP:4000001.def: Abnormal finding by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which uses non-ionizing radiation via a strong magnetic field and radio frequency energy to generate three dimensional images. This term comprises findings that are specific to MRI. Findings such as ventricular spetum defect that can be detected by multiple modalities should be coded separately.

name: elevated myocardial native t2
elevate myocardial native t2
HP:4000003.def: Increased duration of myocardial T2 time without gadolinium contrast. Elevated T2, which can detect myocardial edema.

name: myocardial late gadolinium enhancement
myocardial late gadolinium enhancement
HP:4000004.def: Areas of high signal intensity in magnetic resonance imaging of the heart appearing 10 to 15 minutes after injection of the intercellular contrast agent gadolinium.

name: pericardial late gadolinium enhancement
pericardial late gadolinium enhancement
HP:4000005.def: Areas of high signal intensity in magnetic resonance imaging of the pericardium appearing around 10 minutes after injection of the intercellular contrast agent gadolinium.

name: elevated myocardial native t1
elevate myocardial native t1
HP:4000006.def: Increased duration of myocardial T1 time without gadolinium contrast. T1 mapping consists of quantifying the T1 relaxation time of a tissue by using analytical expressions of image-based signal intensities. A fundamental principle of MR imaging is that the signal intensity of pixels is based on the relaxation of hydrogen nuclei protons in a static magnetic field. The T1 relaxation times between two tissues vary substantially. Edema, fat infiltration, and fibrosis also cause differences in T1 relaxivity.

name: bronchoconstriction
bronchoconstriction
HP:4000007.def: Tightening of smooth muscle surrounding the bronchi and bronchioles with consequent wheezing and shortness of breath.

name: formation of multiple pronuclei during fertilization
formation of multiple pronucleus during fertilization
HP:4000008.def: Pronuclei formation is a critical process during fertilisation. Normally, there are two pronuclei (2PN), including the paternal pronucleus and the maternal pronucleus, in the zygote after fertilisation. It is generally accepted that multiple pronuclei (MPN) formation is due to the abnormal extrusion of the second polar body or to abnormal fertilisation with multiple sperm. The MPN therefore can cause infertility and recurrent failure of IVF/ICSI.

name: kinesiophobia
kinesiophobia
HP:4000009.def: An excessive, irrational, and debilitating fear of carrying out a physical movement due to a feeling of vulnerability to painful injury or reinjury.

name: impaired renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate
impaired renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate
HP:4000010.def: Decreased renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate.

name: history of congenital hpv infection
history of congenital hpv infection
HP:4000011.def: A congenital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection of the newborn. Congential HPV infection can manifest as condyloma cuminata in the newborn.

name: anti - desmoglein - 1 antibody positivity
anti - desmoglein - 1 antibody positivity
HP:4000013.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoglein-1, a dermal cell adhesion molecule.

name: anti - desmoglein - 3 antibody positivity
anti - desmoglein - 3 antibody positivity
HP:4000014.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoglein-3, a dermal cell adhesion molecule.

name: anti - envoplakin antibody positivity
anti - envoplakin antibody positivity
HP:4000015.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against envoplakin, a cytoskeletal linker protein that links intermediate filaments to cellular junctions.

name: anti - periplakin antibody positivity
anti - periplakin antibody positivity
HP:4000016.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against periplakin.

name: anti - desmoplakin i antibody positivity
anti - desmoplakin i antibody positivity
HP:4000017.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoplakin-1.

name: anti - desmoplakin ii antibody positivity
anti - desmoplakin ii antibody positivity
HP:4000018.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoplakin-II.

name: anti - bp230 antibody positivity
anti - bp230 antibody positivity
HP:4000019.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against BP230.

name: anti - bp180 antibody positivity
anti - bp180 antibody positivity
HP:4000020.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against BP180.

name: anti - laminin 332 antibody positivity
anti - laminin 332 antibody positivity
HP:4000021.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin-332.

name: anti - laminin 6 antibody positivity
anti - laminin 6 antibody positivity
HP:4000022.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin-6.

name: anti - laminin gamma1 antibody positivity
anti - laminin gamma1 antibody positivity
HP:4000023.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin gamma-1.

name: anti - laminin antibody positivity
anti - laminin antibody positivity
HP:4000024.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a laminin. Laminins are major components of the basement membrane.

name: anti - integrin antibody positivity
anti - integrin antibody positivity
HP:4000025.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against an integrin. Integrins are a family of cell adhesion molecules with 24 known integrin heterodimers. Integrins transduce mechanical and biochemical signals from fibrotic extracellular matrix into the cell, activate latent TGFbeta, and subsequently modulate fibroblast adhesion, migration, and growth.

name: anti - transglutaminase 6 antibody
anti - transglutaminase 6 antibody
HP:4000026.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against transglutaminase 6.

name: anti - lad - 1 antibody positivity
anti - lad - 1 antibody positivity
HP:4000027.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against LAD-1, which is the soluble 120 kDa ectodomain of BP180.

name: anti - labd97 antibody positivity
anti - labd97 antibody positivity
HP:4000028.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against LABD97, which is structurally identical to a portion of the extracellular domain of BPAg2. BPAg2, a 180 kDa bullous pemphigoid antigen, is a transmembrane protein important for basement membrane cohesion.

name: antigliadin antibody positivity
antigliadin antibody positivity
HP:4000029.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against gliadin.

name: anti - reticulin antibody positivity
anti - reticulin antibody positivity
HP:4000030.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against reticulin.

name: anti - type vii collagen antibody
anti - type vii collagen antibody
HP:4000031.def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against collagen type VII.

name: false perception of self - motion
false perception of self - motion
HP:4000032.def: A perception that one's body is moving or swaying despite lack of motion of the body.

name: non - spinning vertigo
non - spinning vertigo
HP:4000033.def: A perception of unsteadiness of dizziness that is not characterized bythe spinning sensation of classic vertigo, but rather by an oscillatory perception (rocking, bobbing, or swaying despite the fact that the subject is not moving).

name: primary obstructive megaureter
primary obstructive megaureter
HP:4000035.def: Megaurater associated with obstruction or an adynamic ureteral segment in the ureterovesical junction.

name: encysted hydrocele of the cord
encysted hydrocele of the cord
HP:4000036.def: A type of hydrocele testis in which both the proximal and distal portions of processus vaginalis get obliterated while the central portion remains patent and fluid accumulates within it.

name: congenital hydrocele
congenital hydrocele
HP:4000037.def: Congenital hydrocele occurs when processus vaginalis is patent and communicates with the peritoneal cavity. This communication allows the movement of peritoneal fluid but is too small to allow the intra-abdominal contents to herniate through.

name: infantile hydrocele
infantile hydrocele
HP:4000038.def: Infantile Hydrocele is a type pf hydrocele in which the processus vaginalis gets obliterated at the level of the deep inguinal ring. However, the portion distal to it remains patent and allows fluid accumulation.

name: reduced proportion of mucosal - associated invariant t cells
reduce proportion of mucosal - associate invariant t cell
HP:4000039.def: A decreased proportion of circulating mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells relative to total T cell count.

name: puerpural onset
puerpural onset
HP:4000040.def: Onset of a phenotypic abnormality or a disease during childbirth or in the period immediately following.

name: aa amyloidosis
aa amyloidosis
HP:4000041.def: Extracellular tissue deposition of fibrils that are composed of fragments of and/or intact serum amyloid A protein, a hepatic acute phase reactant.

name: fracture type
fracture type
HP:4000042.def: Category of fracture. Terms from this subontology can be used together with terms in the subontology that descends from Bone fracture (HP:0020110).

name: greenstick fracture
greenstick fracture
HP:4000043.def: A type of fracture in which the broken bone is not completely separated.

name: transverse fracture
transverse fracture
HP:4000044.def: A type of fracture in which the break is in a straight line across the bone.

name: spiral fracture
spiral fracture
HP:4000045.def: A type of fracture in which the break spirals around the bone.

name: oblique fracture
oblique fracture
HP:4000046.def: A type of fracture in which there is a diagonal break across the bone.

name: compression fracture
compression fracture
HP:4000047.def: A type of fracture in which the bone is crushed, causing the broken bone to be wider or flatter in appearance.

name: comminuted fracture
comminute fracture
HP:4000048.def: A type of fracture in which the break is in three or more pieces and fragments are present at the fracture site.

name: segmental fracture
segmental fracture
HP:4000049.def: A type of fracture in which the same bone is fractured in two places, so there is a floating segment of bone.

name: open fracture
open fracture
HP:4000050.def: A type of fracture in which there is an open wound or break in the skin near the site of the broken bone.

name: closed fracture
closed fracture
HP:4000051.def: A type of fracture in which the broken bone that does not penetrate the skin.

name: avulsion fracture
avulsion fracture
HP:4000052.def: A type of fracture that is localied near to a a tendon or ligament and a small fragment of bone is separated from the main mass of bone as a result of physical trauma.

name: displaced fracture
displaced fracture
HP:4000053.def: A type of fracture in which the ends of the fractured bone are no longer aligned.

name: intestinal inflammation
intestinal inflammation
HP:4000055.def: A reaction characterizeds by capillary dilatation, leukocytic infiltration, redness, heat, pain, swelling localized to the in the intestinal tract.

name: abnormal apoptosis
abnormal apoptosis
HP:4000056.def: Any abnormality of programmed cell death (apoptosis), which is defined as the orchestrated collapse of a cell characterised by membrane blebbing, cell shrinkage, condensation of chromatin, and fragmentation of DNA followed by rapid engulfment of the corpse by neighbouring cells. Apoptosis is distinguished from death by necrosis by the absence of an associated inflammatory response.

name: decreased fasl - mediated apoptosis
decrease fasl - mediate apoptosis
HP:4000057.def: A reduced amount of programmed cell death upon stimulation of the FAS receptor, which normally induces caspase-8 dependent apoptosis.

name: glomerular proteinuria
glomerular proteinuria
HP:4000058.def: A type of proteinuria characterized by increased permeability of the glomerular capillary wall to macromolecules (particularly albumin), whereby protein excretion can reach 20 g/24 h and consists mainly of albumin.

name: abnormal lung development
abnormal lung development
HP:4000059.def: A structural defect associated with abnormal development of the lung.

name: pancreatic alpha - cell hyperplasia
pancreatic alpha - cell hyperplasia
HP:4000061.def: A diffuse and specific increase in the number of alpha-cells.

name: 3 - 4 metacarpal synostosis
3 - 4 metacarpal synostosis
HP:4000062.def: A congenital hand malformation characterized by the coalescence of the coalescence of third and fourth metacarpals (i.e., those corresponding to the middle and ring fingers).
synonym: middle and ring finger metacarpal synostosis
middle and ring finger metacarpal synostosis
synostosis of third and the fourth metacarpal bones
synostosis of third and the fourth metacarpal bone

name: abnormal iliac artery morphology
abnormal iliac artery morphology
HP:4000066.def: Any structural anomaly of the iliac artery.

name: iliac artery aneurysm
iliac artery aneurysm
HP:4000067.def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the iliac artery.

name: abnormal interest
abnormal interest
HP:4000068.def: Any deviation from normal intensity or subject of a person's interests, which can be defined as a state of giving selective attention to something.

name: persistent preoccupation with parts of objects
persistent preoccupation with part of object
HP:4000069.def: A type of abnormal interest characterized by a persistent and intense focus on parts of a toy/object. For example, affected individuals may spin the wheels on a toy car rather than drive the toy car.
synonym: fixated interest with parts of objects
fixate interest with part of object

name: fixated interests
fixated interest
HP:4000070.def: Highly restricted, fixated interests that are abnormal in intensity or focus (e.g., strong attachment to or preoccupation with unusual objects, excessively circumscribed or perseverative interests).

name: abnormal language feature
abnormal language feature
HP:4000072.def: The presence of any atypical form of expressive language.

name: pronoun reversal
pronoun reversal
HP:4000073.def: Atypical language features characterized by first vs. second or third person pronoun errors such as using 'you' or 'he/she' in place of 'I'.

name: idiosyncratic language
idiosyncratic language
HP:4000074.def: Consistent use of an unusual way of referring to something that is idiosyncratic to the individual.

name: reduced frequency of facial expressions
reduced frequency of facial expression
HP:4000075.def: The number of times facial expressions are produced in a given period is lower than expected given the social and cultural context.

name: use of another person 's body to communicate
use of another person 's body to communicate
HP:4000076.def: Moving another person's hand, body part, or body to communicate a desire, e.g. pushing or pulling someone toward a desired object or placing someone's hand on something.

name: fixated interest with abnormal focus
fixate interest with abnormal focus
HP:4000077.def: A fixated interest in a specific topic that is atypical for the social context of the individual, such as topics of a non-social nature like fossils or vacuum cleaners.

name: fixated interest with abnormal intensity
fixate interest with abnormal intensity
HP:4000078.def: An abnormally intense interest in a topic or object that is not atypical for the social context of the affected person.

name: sensory seeking
sensory seek
HP:4000079.def: Unusual interest in sensory aspects of the environment.

name: reduced production of gestures
reduce production of gesture
HP:4000081.def: Diminished use of typical non-verbal conversational gestures such as shaking the head to indicate no or nodding the head to indicate yes.

name: reduced collaborative play
reduce collaborative play
HP:4000082.def: Impairment in a child's ability to be able to play in a way that involves peer collaboration. Collaborative play involves things such as verbal and non-verbal communication (e.g., self-initiated interactions), turn-taking, sharing, reciprocity, and collaborative problem-solving. It is often contrasted to parallel play, which involves a form of social play in which two children do similar activities near each other and often mimic each other. Typically developing children develop collaborative play between the ages of 4 and 5.

name: ignores peers
ignores peer
HP:4000083.def: Lack of interest in peers of comparable age and social groups is evident when an individual, such as a child, shows more interest in socializing with adults rather than children their own age.

name: reduced sharing of interests
reduce sharing of interest
HP:4000084.def: Decreased sharing of interests with others appropriate to culture and developmental level.

name: reduced object sharing
reduce object sharing
HP:4000085.def: An absence or reduction in object sharing. Object sharing is an early emerging social skill in which a child will share objects with parents or peers during object play. Object sharing typically develops within the first two years of life.

name: abnormal communicative facial expressions
abnormal communicative facial expression
HP:4000087.def: Abnormal expressions (movements or position of muscles of the face that convey the emotional state of an individual to observers during social interactions) comprising abnormalities of quantity, range, context-appropriateness, and quality.

name: facial expressions that do not match the context
facial expression that do not match the context
HP:4000088.def: Production of facial expressions that are misaligned with the social context.

name: abnormal quality of facial expression
abnormal quality of facial expression
HP:4000089.def: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are exaggerated or muted.

name: abnormal gesture use
abnormal gesture use
HP:4000090.def: Abnormality in the use of gestures defined as hand, shoulder, and head movements that convey a shared meaning within a culture that replace or supplement verbal communication.

name: poor conversational reciprocity
poor conversational reciprocity
HP:4000092.def: Reduced ability to conduct a reciprocal (back and forth) conversation, as expected for language level. May be characterized by deficits in the ability to make comments about discussion topics of others, failure to ask questions, and not building a conversation on comments of others. Affected persons may not know what to say next in a conversation, may not notice if others are bored with a given topic, may conduct a one-sided conversation (talking but not listening), or may veer off topic more than is socially acceptable.
synonym: failure of normal back - and - forth conversation
failure of normal back - and - forth conversation

name: ectopic tooth eruption
ectopic tooth eruption
HP:4000093.def: A condition in which the permanent teeth, because of deficiency of growth in the jaw or segment of jaw, assume a path of eruption that intercepts a primary tooth, causes its premature loss and produces a consequent malposition of the permanent tooth.

name: corpus cavernosum hypoplasia
corpus cavernosum hypoplasia
HP:4000094.def: A developmental anomaly characterized by undergrowth of the corpus cavernosum.

name: elevated circulating thymine concentration
elevate circulate thymine concentration
HP:4000095.def: Concentration of the nucleobase thymine in the blood circulation above the normal range.

name: positive lactose hydrogen breath test
positive lactose hydrogen breath test
HP:4000100.def: Elevated hydrogen gas level in exhaled breath following oral administration of lactose. In individuals with lactose intolerance, undigested lactose in the colon will be metabolized by colonic bacteria, releasing hydrogen gas.

name: triggered by exposure to medication
trigger by exposure to medication
HP:4000101.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a medication.

name: triggered by allopurinol
trigger by allopurinol
HP:4000102.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to allopurinol.

name: ameliorated by oral zinc supplementation
ameliorate by oral zinc supplementation
HP:4000103.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by oral zinc supplementation.

name: curved dental root
curve dental root
HP:4000104.def: A root of a tooth that is more rounded than normal.

name: abnormal four chamber view of the fetal heart
abnormal four chamber view of the fetal heart
HP:4000105.def: The four-chamber (4Ch) view of the fetal heart is the most widely used screening examination for the detection of structural cardiac abnormalities during routine fetal ultrasonography. In the healthy normal fetus, the apical 4Ch view demonstrates four well-developed chambers, a concordant atrioventricular (AV) connection, unobstructed AV valves (mitral and tricuspid valves), the foramen ovale flap opening into left atrium (LA), and an intact interventricular septum. Additionally, the pulmonary venous opening can be visualized at the LA wall. Any structural deviations from normal anatomy may lead to congenital heart disease that can be determined by the 4Ch view of the fetal heart's ultrasound imaging.

name: spleen hamartoma
spleen hamartoma
HP:4000106.def: A hamartomatous lesion (benign focal lesions composed of disorganized tissue elements) localized in the spleen.

name: positive lupus band test
positive lupus band test
HP:4000107.def: Deposits of immunoglobulins and complement components along the dermoepidermal junction.

name: bone marrow erythroid vacuolization
bone marrow erythroid vacuolization
HP:4000108.def: Formation of vacuoles (a space within a cell that is empty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in the cytoplasm of erythroid precursors in the bone marrow.

name: triggered by electromagnetic field
trigger by electromagnetic field
HP:4000109.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to an electromagnetic field.

name: exposure history
exposure history
HP:4000110.def: Information about current and past exposure to metals, dust, fibers, fumes, chemicals, biologic hazards, radiation, noise, and/or vibration at work or home.

name: asbestos exposure
asbestos exposure
HP:4000111.def: History of exposure to asbestos, a fibrous mineral with physical and chemical properties that make it resistant to heat and degradation.

name: medication history
medication history
HP:4000112.def: Information about current or past medications taken by an individual.

name: aminoglycoside exposure
aminoglycoside exposure
HP:4000113.def: History of having taken aminoglycoside antibiotics.

name: statin exposure
statin exposure
HP:4000114.def: History of having taken statins, also known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.

name: potassium - sparing diuretic exposure
potassium - spar diuretic exposure
HP:4000115.def: History of having taken a potassium-sparing diuretic exposure such as amiloride, eplerenone, spironolactone, and triamterene.

name: valproate exposure
valproate exposure
HP:4000117.def: History of having taken valproate (valproic acid).

name: calcium channel blocker exposure
calcium channel blocker exposure
HP:4000119.def: History of having taken a calcium channel blocker such as amlodipine, nicardipine, nifedipine, verapamil, or diltiazem.

name: triggered by poison ivy , poson oak , or sumac
trigger by poison ivy , poson oak , or sumac
HP:4000121.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure (cutaneous contact) to poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac. These three plants each contain urushiol. Contact with these plants is the most common causes of clinically diagnosed allergic contact dermatitis.
synonym: contact with poison ivy , poison oak , or sumac
contact with poison ivy , poison oak , or sumac

name: history of exclusive breast feeding
history of exclusive breast feeding
HP:4000122.def: A past medical history of having been fed exclusively by breast feeding.

name: nutrition history
nutrition history
HP:4000123.def: A part of the past medical history consisting of information about the typical food intake of an individual.

name: high dietary oxalate intake
high dietary oxalate intake
HP:4000124.def: A history of ingestion of a relatively high amount of foods containing high levels of oxalate, such as green-leaf vegetables, tea, nuts, chocolate and rhubarb.
synonym: foods high in oxalate , high intake
food high in oxalate , high intake

name: recent honey ingestion
recent honey ingestion
HP:4000125.def: A history of ingestion of honey in recent weeks.

name: raw egg - white ingestion
raw egg - white ingestion
HP:4000126.def: A history of eating raw egg whites.

name: exacerbated by sodium channel blocking agent exposure
exacerbate by sodium channel block agent exposure
HP:4000127.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of sodium channel blocking agents such as phenytoin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine, topiramate, and zonisamide.
synonym: sodium channel blocking drugs aggravate findings
sodium channel block drug aggravate finding

name: addictive nitrous oxide use
addictive nitrous oxide use
HP:4000128.def: Addiction to inhaled nitrous oxide gas (N2O) is a growing concern.

name: recent blood transfusion
recent blood transfusion
HP:4000129.def: A past medical history of a recent blood transfusion.

name: ameliorated by colchicine
ameliorate by colchicine
HP:4000130.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of colchizine.

name: ameliorated by vitamin d
ameliorate by vitamin d
HP:4000131.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of vitamin D.

name: exacerbated by phenytoin exposure
exacerbate by phenytoin exposure
HP:4000132.def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of phenytoin.

name: triggered by angiotensin - converting enzyme inhibitor
trigger by angiotensin - convert enzyme inhibitor
HP:4000133.def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to anngiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, and lisinopril.

name: prostaglandin e1 exposure
prostaglandin e1 exposure
HP:4000134.def: History of having been treateed with prostaglandin E1.

name: 5 - fluorouracil exposure
5 - fluorouracil exposure
HP:4000135.def: History of having been treated with 5-fluorouracil.

name: 6 - mercaptopurine exposure
6 - mercaptopurine exposure
HP:4000136.def: History of having been treateed with 6-mercaptopurine.

name: isoniazid exposure
isoniazid exposure
HP:4000137.def: History of having been treateed with isoniazid.

name: absent cavum septum pellucidum
absent cavum septum pellucidum
HP:4000138.def: The cavum septum pellucidum (CSP) is an important fetal midline forebrain landmark that is normally visible by prenatal sonography. This term refers to the lack of visiblity of the CSP on prenatal sonography. The CSP normally can be visualized between 18 and 37 weeks of gestation. Lack of visualization of the CSP in this time period generally requires follow up and may indicate the presence of underlying malformations such as malformations of the corpus callosum. The lack of CSP before 18 weeks or after 37 weeks of gestation (or postnatally) is considered a normal finding.

name: fetal abdominal cyst
fetal abdominal cyst
HP:4000139.def: Fetal abdominal cysts are usually detected during the second trimester anomaly scan or discovered incidentally at later gestations. However, a definitive diagnosis is often not made until postnatal life. The most common etiologies of fetal abdominal cysts are: ovarian, gastrointestinal cystic duplication, liver and choledochal, meconium pseudocysts, mesenteric and adrenal. Following identification of a cyst, careful morphological assessment allows the prediction of their natural history and importantly, the likelihood of surgical intervention being required postnatally.

name: fetal bowel dilatation
fetal bowel dilatation
HP:4000140.def: Fetal bowel dilatation is characterized by fluid-filled intestinal loops which measure at least fifteen millimeters long or seven millimeters in diameter. Ultrasonographic image of dilated fetal bowel is a sign of intestinal mechanical or functional obstruction and its prevalence will depend on the underlying condition: bowel atresia or stenosis, malrotation with volvulus, meconium ileus, total colonic aganglionosis, and meconium plug syndrome. The etiology of fetal bowel dilatation is a difficult prenatal diagnosis since ultrasound has limited accuracy for bowel evaluation.

name: left ventricular dilatation
leave ventricular dilatation
HP:4000141.def: Enlargement of the chamber of the left heart ventricle.

name: fetal trigonocephaly
fetal trigonocephaly
HP:4000142.def: A fetal ultrasound finding defined by flattening of the occiput with pointing of the frontal bones and brachycephaly with an increased cephalic index. It is characterized by keel shaped deformity of forehead with midline ridge, bilateral fronto temporal constriction with compensatory biparietal expansion, supra orbital and lateral orbital retrusion and hypotelorism. This finding is said to resemble a strawberry.

name: abnormal fetal heart outflow tract
abnormal fetal heart outflow tract
HP:4000143.def: A prenatal anomaly of the outflow tract. Fetal ultrasound may not always be able to easily and accurately describe the outflow anomaly, but can detect abnormal anatomy. Often, follow up with a fetal echo is recommended, but fetal ultrasound is limited.

name: recent past medical history
recent past medical history
HP:4000144.def: History of events that precede the current presenting condition and are thought to be of potential relevance, having occured in the hours, days, or weeks before the current condition.

name: history of recent viral illness
history of recent viral illness
HP:4000145.def: Medical history of a viral illness in recent weeks.

name: history of recent dental procedure
history of recent dental procedure
HP:4000146.def: Medical history of a dental procedure in recent weeks.

name: abnormal hepatic artery morphology
abnormal hepatic artery morphology
HP:4000147.def: Any structural anomaly of the hepatic artery or its branches.

name: hepatic artery hyperplasia
hepatic artery hyperplasia
HP:4000148.def: Abnormal increase in size of the hepatic arteries.

name: lymph node necrosis
lymph node necrosis
HP:4000149.def: Areas of necrotic tissue within a lymph node.

name: multinucleated neuron
multinucleated neuron
HP:4000150.def: Neurons that contain more than one nucleus.

name: history of recent contralateral injury
history of recent contralateral injury
HP:4000151.def: A history of an injury that occurred several hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint and is located on the other side of the body relative to the current presenting complaint.

name: alternating laterality
alternate laterality
HP:4000152.def: Occuring on the left and right in succession. This term can refer to alternating sides of the body (e.g., Alternating hemiplegia) or alternative sides of the visual field (e.g., some migraine auras).

cervical squamous cell papilloma
HP:4000153.def: A benign tumor arising from the epithelial surface of the cervix and usually caused by Human Papillomavirus infection.

name: liver leiomyoma
liver leiomyoma
HP:4000154.def: A benign smooth muscle neoplasm that arises in the liver.

name: typified by high penetrance
typify by high penetrance
HP:4000158.def: Description of conditions in which only an incomplete but relatively high proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for incomplete, but high penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 80 percent but less than 100 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

name: typified by moderate penetrance
typify by moderate penetrance
HP:4000159.def: Description of conditions in which only a moderate proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for moderate penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 20 percent but less than 80 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

name: typified by low penetrance
typify by low penetrance
HP:4000160.def: Description of conditions in which only a low proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for low penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least some but less than 20 percent of carriers would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

name: grandiose delusion
grandiose delusion
HP:5200417.def: False beliefs relating to origin (aristocratic lineage, royal birth, being raised as a foster child), possessions (owning vast estates, castles, etc., which are withheld through intrigue), abilities (being great inventors, discoverers, artists, possessors of special wisdom, gifted with inspiration), and status (adviser to prominent diplomats, the true director of political destinies).

name: folie à deux
folie à deux
HP:5200418.def: Delusional beliefs are transmitted from one individual to another.

name: delusion of control
delusion of control
HP:5200419.def: A false belief that another person, group of people, or external force controls one's general thoughts, feelings, impulses, or behaviors.

name: delusion of love
delusion of love
HP:5200420.def: A delusion is when someone believes they are loved by another person, even though there is no evidence of this, and the person in question denies it.

name: nihilistic delusion
nihilistic delusion
HP:5200421.def: A false belief associated with the nonexistence of the \"self,\

name: cotard delusion
cotard delusion
HP:5200422.def: A false belief that you or your body parts are dead, dying, or do not exist.

name: abnormal experience of reality
abnormal experience of reality
HP:5200423.def: Subjective phenomena or perceptions that deviate from what is considered correct or are outside the range of normal human experiences.

name: delusional perception
delusional perception
HP:5200424.def: A true perception, to which a patient attributes a false meaning, ranges from experiencing some vague meaning to clear, delusional observations, and expresses delusions of reference.

name: hypochondriac delusion
hypochondriac delusion
HP:5200425.def: Bodily preoccupation, disease phobia, and a false fixed conviction of the presence of disease with no response to reassurance.

name: delusions of infestation
delusion of infestation
HP:5200426.def: A persistent belief that a person is infested with living or non-living pathogens, such as parasites, insects, or bugs, when no such infestation is present.

name: delusional atmosphere
delusional atmosphere
HP:5200427.def: Experience everything around them as sinister, portentous, uncanny, and peculiar in an indefinable way. They know that they are personally involved but cannot tell how. They have a feeling of anticipation, sometimes even excitement, that soon all the separate parts of their experience will fit together to reveal something immensely significant.

name: delusional misidentification
delusional misidentification
HP:5200428.def: A group of complex, monothematic delusional phenomena in which subjects hold a belief that the identity of a familiar person, object, location, or self has been altered or replaced.

name: religious delusion
religious delusion
HP:5200429.def: Delusions are characterized by increased conviction and pervasiveness, permeating the individual's entire experience to a greater extent.

name: abnormal psychotic pattern
abnormal psychotic pattern
HP:5200430.def: Any abnormal pattern of psychotic experiences, where an individual has significant disturbances in their thoughts, perceptions, emotions, and behavior, resulting in a loss of touch with reality.

name: incomplete unilateral cleft lip
incomplete unilateral cleft lip
HP:5201000.def: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity.

name: complete unilateral cleft lip
complete unilateral cleft lip
HP:5201001.def: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.

name: microform unilateral cleft lip
microform unilateral cleft lip
HP:5201002.def: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip. Microforms are sometimes associated with disruption of the continuity of the orbicularis oris muscle.

name: complete cleft hard palate
complete cleft hard palate
HP:5201003.def: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the hard palate.

name: incomplete cleft hard palate
incomplete cleft hard palate
HP:5201004.def: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft doe not goes through the entire length of the hard palate.

name: complete cleft soft palate
complete cleft soft palate
HP:5201005.def: Cleft soft palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the soft palate.

name: incomplete cleft soft palate
incomplete cleft soft palate
HP:5201006.def: Cleft soft palate in which the cleft doe not goes through the entire length of the soft palate.

name: incomplete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
incomplete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
HP:5201007.def: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the maxillary alveolar ridge.

name: complete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
complete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
HP:5201008.def: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the maxillary alveolar ridge.

name: complete cleft of the upper lip
complete cleft of the upper lip
HP:5201009.def: Cleft of the upper lip that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.

name: microform cleft of the upper lip
microform cleft of the upper lip
HP:5201010.def: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip.

name: complete bilateral cleft lip
complete bilateral cleft lip
HP:5201011.def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides is complete, i.e. start from the bottom of the upper lip and reach the nasal cavity.

name: incomplete bilateral cleft lip
incomplete bilateral cleft lip
HP:5201012.def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides are incomplete (i.e. start from the bottom of the upper lip but do not reach the nasal cavity), or the cleft lip on one is incomplete and a microform on the other side.

name: microform bilateral cleft lip
microform bilateral cleft lip
HP:5201013.def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides are microform, i.e. a notch, groove, or scar without noticeable rupture of the lip.

name: asymmetric bilateral cleft lip
asymmetric bilateral cleft lip
HP:5201014.def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on one side is complete (i.e. starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity), and the one on the other side is incomplete (i.e. starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity) or microform (i.e. a notch, groove, or scar without noticeable rupture of the lip).
